title: Warnings?
text:
Anise and Fennel essential oils have loads of contraindications associated with them. Anise - Tisserand states that trans-anethole has a weak estrogen-like activity, and it is contraindicated for pregnancy, breastfeeding, endometriosis, any estrogen-related cancers, and children under 5 years of age. Oral doses are not recommended for people taking diabetes medication, diuretic medication, renal insufficiency, and edematous disorders. Also, may interfere with anticoagulant medications or bleeding disorders. When oxidized, it may be skin sensitizing. For topical applications, Tisserand suggests 2.4% dilution.
Sweet Fennel - To be used only for the short term, and at a maximum of 2.5%. Not to be used on children under five. Contraindicated for pregnancy and breastfeeding. Not advisable to use during labor, especially if it is progressing slowly.
Just because these are made from natural ingredients doesn't mean they have no warnings or that they are completely safe.

title: Great, but proceed cautiously
text:
I had read the description and the reviews before getting these weight loss supplements because some people loved them while others said it worked too good. So I decided to go forward with them but to use caution in how many I took at one time. I
The bottle says there are 60 supplements and on the bottom of the bottle it says that there is a one month supply, so I deducted that you were only supposed to take 1 supplement with two different meals to equal 2 supplements a day for 30 days, which would bring you to 60. I started with that number instead of the suggested 2-3 per meal as stated on the bottle under suggested use, I am very glad that I did.
Here is the key, each person's digestive system is different and therefore will differ from person to person. You need to know yourself. For example, I am older and have a slower metabolism and digestive system. I normally need to take fiber pills or colon cleansing pills so I am not constipated. I started with one pill and no extra fiber or colon pills about 20 minutes before my very first meal with these pills. About 15 minutes after I ate I went to the bathroom and then had a normal, soft stool bowel movement.
For a person that doesn't have constipation issues, you may only need one a day. You want to proceed forward slowly to find out if you need to take more or not. One reviewer took the recommended 2 with her first meal and ended up with issues for two plus days. I would also recommend first trying this on a day when you are not working to see how it affects you.
I really like the way these pills are working. The came in date, there was a plastic seal around the lid as well as the tamper free seal under the cap. The supplements were fresh and not sticking together.

title: Awesome travel pillow
text:
We have a long trip in the Jeep planned for later in the year and in the past I have always used the neck pillows with beans in them. Unfortunately, beans will eventually move around and the support for the neck dissipates. Over a long trip, I may have to re-adjust a bean pillow over and over again.

Therefore, I was very happy to see a memory foam travel neck pillow. First off, this thing is bright red and matches the red and black Quadratec seat covers in my Jeep. Not a big deal, but it fits my red and black theme. We tested the neck pillow over an hour long trip over the weekend. Unlike the beans, it supports the neck without needing constant re-adjusting. It is stiffer than the bean filled pillow, but we like that feature. Also, the pillow can make your neck a few degrees warmer than the air temperature when you snap the ends together. My neck gets stiff over a long ride, so I like the fact that it has some warmth to it. If you unsnap the ends, you will get more of the air temperature back in.

The snaps can also make it easy to attach the pillow to the outside of a backpack or suitcase, since it is bulky, which gives the snaps another useful feature. The cover can be removed easily, as well. There is a zipper on the back and you can just unzip it and toss the cover in the wash.

Really, I am not sure what more you can ask for in a neck pillow. I guess it could be a bit more cushiony, but I like the stiffness since I have neck problems and I prefer support over something like a bean filled pillow that loses its shape over time.

text: [[VIDEOID:61c3116a04eb0ca0a0c33e6e7950a6cb]] I like the convenience of having a breath analyzer or blood alcohol content tester with you especially if your husband said he just had couple of beers when in fact he drank 6 packs. Then I drink 1/4 glass of red wine that I bought from costco and immediately I get a reading of 0.19, then next try I got 0.17 reading and on the 3rd try I got a reading of 0.14 with intervals of 1-2 minutes. I'm assuming you have to divide these readings with 100% to get the % BAC because the legal limit of blood alcohol content in your body while driving is usually 0.08%. title: Then the item works great and won't break
text:
I have one of these from a different company (essentially an identical thing). When I first started using it I noticed that trying to stretch jeans more than one inch would make the tube running between the front and the back flex and bow. I could get about an inch and three quarters before it was ready to break. because of the bow you aren't getting full stretch effect.
That's because the center tube is made of hollow plastic. What I had to do to give it enough rigidity was to drill out the hole in the center of the tube segments with a 3/8 inch drill bit and then cut a piece from 3/8 inch aluminum solid round bar stock (you can get them at a hardware store for a few $$) long enough to fit the entire length of the center part.
That stops the flexing and bowing. Then the item works great and won't break. I also use a plant sprayer bottle with water to wet the waistband (I wet both inside and outside to get the waistband soaked) and I leave the pants on the stretcher overnight to allow the waist band to dry.

title: What relief this humidifier was able to offer was cut short by the small tank.
text:
+ Produces steam within 2-3 minutes; steady flow
+ Works well when you are suffering from a head cold or nasal congestion
+ Small unit; doesn’t take up a lot of space
+ Portability and ease of cleaning

± Price seems rather hefty, especially considering the tank size
± 0.5 gallon does not go a long way: works great during woken hours, but does not last 8+ hours at night
± Constructed out of plastic that is relatively “thin”; don’t drop
± Be careful with eucalyptus-based bar if you own pets (more mentioned below)

- No way to control the direction of the steam

------------------------------------------

The first day of use, I filled the tank 3/4th’s of the way. I figured this would last me the whole night, as my cold mist humidifier does fine on even less. I was awoken, however, to a shrill “empty” beeping indicator at 5am. This was a mere 5 hours after first fill - definitely wasn’t happy. No, I was not using the highest setting (depicted by 2 steam lines), so perhaps I’m just an anomaly.

Anyway, I appreciate that the product itself works. Steam was produced within 2-3 minutes, more often within 1, and it was steady enough to where I felt the effects during my congested state. You’re not able to control the direction of the steam though, so this was rather unfortunate.

The product itself is made of plastic with a metal heating plate area. It’s not sturdy material at all, and feels rather delicate. Realistically, this will survive perhaps 3 drops, if even that - I won’t be testing that any time soon though.

Now, this tidbit may or may not be relevant to you, so skip if you don’t own pets. I don’t know if I’m perpetuating a scare either, but I wanted to add this in nonetheless. I was lying in bed with the provided eucalyptus mint bar sitting in the catch tray as the steam rose. As I was laying down, I noticed how strong the scent was, therefore decided to quickly check if it would affect my dogs. Well, it’s a good thing that I confirmed as I discovered that these vapors are known for causing seizures in dogs…

I’m not one to normally believe everything I read online, so I dug a little deeper, where I continued to come across mixed reviews. Most of the reviews favored heavily towards avoiding eucalyptus-based vapor products when around dogs though, so I immediately ceased use.

At $44.99 (on sale), this product does not feel worth it. It only offered 5 hours of relief, so while I may have received a faulty product, it still didn’t perform as long as one would expect. Otherwise, this does produce a nice stream of steam, so does aid with some nasal relief.

title: Game changer!
text: These Lauon Mesh Food Cover Tents are such a game changer, I never even knew these existed! They are very functional & extremely useful for all of us whom incorporate a large portion of our lives to outdoor activities. The tents would make your love of outdoor eating at places such as backyard bbqs, forest preserve gatherings or beach picnics so much easier! You get six 17 X 17 food cover tents in this package, they’re big enough to cover a full size plate, a tall glass of drink, utensils, napkins & even a side salad bowl or corn on the cob holder. They’re extremely roomy enough to fit plenty of food underneath them regardless of width or height as they’re just as tall as they are wide. The possibilities are endless of what these can cover keeping your food safe from insects or even from being knocked over as the large tents are hard to miss. My favorite thing about these mesh tents is how easy & quick they are to operate, you simply pull the string at the top until the plastic notches at the center connects and it pops open. It’s lightweight & lightening quick which is what you need when you’re very busy hosting, preparing & presenting food. Then when you’re finished with them, simply pop the plastic notch off from center and it folds down nice and slim for easy storage. I like the cute lace ruffles underneath the tents, adds a little detail to them. The only flaw in these tents is the mesh itself, it doesn’t appear to be very durable and looks like it could rip quite easily. So these would make great vacation food tents where one would only use them for temporarily. However, if you’re careful with them I’d imagine they would hold up for most of your outdoor gatherings as it’s not everyday we eat outside anyways. At the time of this review the item was unavailable so I’m unable to comment on pricing or whether it’s worth the price point. Overall, I love my Lauon Food Cover tents and would definitely recommend them for everyone whom loves to eat outdoors as much as I do.

I imagine if I used it more often my shower would gleam - but d'oh - I forget too often. My only criticism is more about the seller than the item itself. I was sent the same product, but under a different label. I wanted the Arm & Hammer product specifically, but I was sent something with a different label. title: You've Been Warned -- Avoid SPS
text:
Lasted 18-months before problems began with not taking a full charge, then four (4) months later they were absolutely dead. I even purchased a new battery charger to check if that was the issue -- it wasn't. Message exchange with company (Sigma Power Systems / SPS) garnered the response of the warranty being only one (1) year. No effort made to retain me as a customer i.e. extend even a slight discount to try their product again. It makes me wonder if they know the result would be the same rapid failure.
My original batteries lasted eight (8) years; these should last at least five (5) years; but I got 1-1/2 years. Scooter used indoors so not exposed to extrermes of cold/heat. No drops or damage to the battery cases or the external battry box. All connections secure, and batteries don't move within the box. Used the charger that came with the scooter, and the second charger purchased was an identical 2A triple-protection UL listed dewvice connected to a surge protector on a standard interior home outlet connected to the standard breaker box for the apartment. There have been no electrical issues.
Looking for long-lasting reliable batteries? Look elsewhere.

title: Bought the wrong starch!
text: It has been a long time since I used starch (15 years, harking back to my Marine Corps days). Whenever I ironed some of my clothes back in the day, I would always use heavy starch. I love that crisp look. Recently, I bought Faultless starch and it did rather well. I got the bright idea of trying to buy more of the starch on Amazon instead of having to go to the store. In my infinite wisdom, I ended up buying this Niagara crap, for some reason thinking that that was what I had recently bought. My mistake, not theirs. The very first time I used it, it ended up turning the bottom of my iron brown, which came off on the white shirt I was ironing (I'm in a police academy....lots of expletives occurred at this moment). I ended up cleaning the bottom of my iron as best as I could, and used the rest of my Faultless starch with no problems. Did I learn my lesson? Hell no. I figured maybe I just didn't let it soak in or something (though I used it the same as the Faultless starch), so I ironed a second uniform shirt using the Niagara starch. Again, my mistake. Needless to say, I am never going to buy Niagara starch again.

title: Amazing blanket for the cost
text:
After my wife ranted and raved about her weighted blanket and how it helped with her sleep, aches and pains, I decided to look for one for myself. Being a bigger guy, it was hard to find one sized for me locally that I could try out. So when I saw the Pine & River blanket selling for so cheap, I scanned the reviews and figured, "What could it hurt?"

title: Lifechanging for Eczema
text:
I have patches of eczema on my hands that flare up because I wash my hands frequently, especially in the cooler weather. I alternate between trying to wash my hands less and gloves with prescribed lotion, but this year has been especially bad. I looked into these types of gloves and saw that they really seemed to help other people. I decided to try the finger less option, as I can't put my phone down without it getting lonely.
Putting these on is SO difficult. I have basically resorted to turning them inside out and placing my fingers in one at a time and pushing down the finger part until it's at my palm, then I am able to put the rest of the glove on. It's annoying and sometimes this method doesn't work, with the liner getting stuck to my skin and preventing them from moving into place. (The large, floppy, full gloves are much easier, but have their drawbacks because you can't use your phone.)
Once they are on- they are pretty chilly and weird feeling. That's normal.
They smell pretty strongly but I don't mind the smell. I don't recommend using lotion with these as the smell might make a nasty combination, also the texture of the glove seems like it would be messy with lotion.
I usually put these on when I get home from work and watch an episode of whatever we are watching. After an episode or 2, I take them off - leave them inside out for next time, and put them back in their little bag that they came in. Then, I wash my hands in lukewarm water and dry thoroughly. I haven't hardly needed my rx lotion at all this winter. When I can get them on, these work really well. There is something about this inner lining that is really helpful for your skin, though it also works against you when trying to put them on.

title: Good value for the price. Takes some patience to learn to use.
text:
[[VIDEOID:3e63df19e1b739815ff4cc893254c958]] Like many older cats, mine has some matting close to the skin. My previous method of getting rid of it was to use scissors to cut it out, but I was always afraid that I would accidentally cut the cat. Plus my cat hated the grooming process. So I bought these clippers hoping to be able to get the mats out and clip all of the fur down close, then use the clippers to maintain what I had done. I've been using the clippers for a few weeks now.

QUALITY: The quality of the clippers, including the box they came in, was surprisingly nice. They are sturdy and easy to charge. The plug end of the charger can only go in one way, so the two sides are shaped differently. The guides go on easily if you follow the instructions.

SOUND: The are indeed quiet, as compared to human hair clippers. I was still afraid that the cat would not get used to them. I did have to turn them on and put them next to her food dish while she ate, for about a week. Fortunately her love of food won out. At the end of the week she was sniffing the clippers, then ignoring them.

USE: The next week I started trying to clip her fur with the clippers. My cat's fur is about an inch long. I tried using all 4 sizes of the length guides and I was disappointed to find that I could not use the clippers at all with any of the guides. After a stroke of only 2 inches, the hair completely clogged up the guide and I would have to stop and pull the hair out to go on. I only have a limited time while she is still distracted by her food to use the clippers so that was frustrating.

I ended up taking the guide off and using the clipper that way. It goes very close to the skin without a guide. I'd say it leaves 1/16" of hair. I was somewhat worried about nicks but after 8 or 9 sessions so far and most of her torso fur gone there hasn't been one nick. The clippers are very gentle. At this stage the cat finds the clippers somewhat annoying but she is not at all afraid and lets me go about the process until the food runs out. The clippers are somewhat weak if they encounter any resistance from a hair mat so tackling one of those takes multiple strokes. I am glad that the clippers are so gentle.

For $7.99 these clippers do the job if one is willing to spend the time. For a cat with shorter hair than mine I'm not sure that the guide problem I had would be an issue.

title: "Pet Safe" and Cats - WARNING
text: "Pet Safe" warning for people with cats: Many companies that advertise their products as being "pet safe" do not realize that this can be a very dangerous statement for people who have cats.  Felines are sensitive to an extensive variety of plant oils - several even being extremely toxic.  Even just inhaling certain oils can be harmful to cats (keep this in mind when using oil defusers, aromatherapy oils or sprays). I always apply products away from cats (and all animals), and wash my hands before touching them.  While some oils are safe, I err on the side of caution and keep my cats away from all products except for those I know with absolute certainty are truly non-toxic/non-allergenic/non-irritating to them.  This is not a review of the product as I haven't tried it yet - just information that I hope will help cat owners and their cats. title: Great at nothing, mediocre at everything.
text:
Wrap-A-Nap was an overall pretty disappointing purchase for me given the price tag of $25 and the company's claims that this reduces sound, can be used as a neck pillow for travel, a lumbar support, and blocks out "all light with its patented design". These are pretty lofty claims for the plushy tube of fleece I received filled with flimsy, ill-distributed stuffing. I tried my hardest to adjust to this pillow, using it for a week straight and just hated it.

1. There's not enough loft or volume in the stuffing to use this as a neck pillow or lumbar support. lightly pressing on the wrap-a-nap and it goes completely flat. The modeled photos in the listing should have been red alert for me.

2. They claim noise-reducing effects, but even after tightening this as far as it could go on my head I could still hear even the near-silent hum of my bedroom fan. There was no difference in even ambient noise whether or not I was wearing it.

3. It blocks light...sort of. If you're comfortable with having a pillow covering your eyes and nose, this is right up your alley. However, I enjoy breathing properly when I sleep so this was a no-go for me. Since it's just a big tube of fleece sewn shut, there's no curvature to it that conforms to your cheekbones. To get the most light-blocking out of it I had to secure it as tightly as possible over my eyes/nose, which put uncomfortable pressure on my eyes.

The one claim they made that I feel was factual was the softness of the material. I have a robe with the same color/texture and it is nice and plushy.

I would recommend this as a better than nothing sleep mask if the price were lower, but the design is just awful. I think this idea would have worked out much better if it had been filled with a dense foam that actually blocks sound and was formed to fit a human face instead of a potato.

title: Seems to work, but USE WITH CAUTION.
text:
Ozone is a great thing to have ... in the upper layers of our atmosphere. However, not only laser copiers do bring ozone into our direct vicinity and you may remember the associated issues with that. The EPA even clarifies that: "Manufacturers and vendors of ozone devices often use misleading terms to describe ozone. Terms such as "energized oxygen" or "pure air" suggest that ozone is a healthy kind of oxygen. Ozone is a toxic gas with vastly different chemical and toxicological properties from oxygen."

CAUTION: The EPA notes that direct (excessive) exposure can lead to (a) decreases in lung function, (b) aggravation of asthma, (c) throat irritation and cough, (d) chest pain and shortness of breath, (e) inflammation of lung tissue, and (f) higher susceptibility to respiratory infection. You're free to draw a connection to the current pandemic and its respiratory nature. The car deodorizer even states for humans or pets not to be in the car when using. (Thanks to the EPA statement above, now you know why.) Make sure to execute caution when using this to prevent issues, but it's not just the ozone itself that can be harmful, but also the potentially toxic byproducts of the Ozone reacting with the contamination. That is one reason why institutions like the EPA advise against the use ozone generators.

Anyway, with that out of the way, the design is both elegant and a bit odd. By the latter I mean that even the manufacturer insists on people or pets to not be in the room while using, yet the only power supply is a car adapter and the recommendation is to keep the car running to provide power during cleaning. Environmentalists certainly cringe by now, but the included battery works just fine. It's just that it has to reside in the car when charging. It would be better to have a wall adapter charging the device. That way, the use in rooms (i.e., restroom) would be easier, and the occasional use in a car possible with the battery.

The device turns on with some drama as the countdown counter gives you 10 seconds to leave the area. the Ozone dispensing lasts for 20 minutes, while another 70 minutes should be allowed for the decomposing (chemical reaction) of the contaminants. That translates into 90 minutes of keeping the space unoccupied. Follow with a thorough airing to ensure the remaining ozone is below danger levels.

A side note on the design. It looks nice, and the "wood" ornamentation is really unnecessary. Personally, I find it distracting and does not really add to the looks in a good way. Meanwhile, my concerns are with the usage and potential health hazards. That's amplified by the power supply described above.

Overall, you may remember the smell when using a laser copier extensively. That's a small preview of what this device does when used without proper ventilation. It's not exactly pleasant, but after letting the ozone escape some odors are indeed removed. Note that Ozone attacks rubber and plants, so you really need to use it with caution in addition to the concerns above. But if you do, the occasional use may get some odor relief.

I've tried just about everything, from lotions to creams, ointments, soaks, even tried the PedEgg.  I live in North Carolina and Spring and Summer is sandal-weather, although it would suit me to wear sandals year-round. I've had numerous pedicures and although they feel great, they never really seem to alleviate the problem of tough, cracked skin and calluses for me, although they do soften my feet a bit for a little while.

I received my pedi roll on Saturday, but just got around to using it today, since i kept my grandbabies over the weekend. OH MY GOSH!! This product is unbelievable!! My feet were baby smooth in no time flat! And honestly, after using it, my feet feel better than they do after I've spent money on a professional pedicure. Also, I want to note that this product removes dead skin very fast, so if by some chance you are diabetic and choose to use this product in spite of that, as I did, you may want to keep a check every few seconds. title: Amazing cushion for low back pain
text:
I have a full time work at home desk job and I weigh 300+ lbs. About a year ago I started having low back and tailbone pain. My tailbone would just ache and burn from the pressure of sitting. I have tried multiple chairs, and specialty pillows —all with limited success.

I read a lot of reviews and in desperation for relief decided to splurge on this expensive pillow... WHY DIDNT I DO THIS A YEAR AGO!!!! After almost 2 months of use, my tailbone pain is gone. I am able to sit longer than an hour without being forced to stand and stretch and move around. I still try to get moving hourly for the health benefits but I am no longer forced to do so because of pain.

The cushion is wide enough and does not create any pressure points elsewhere on my legs as some have indicated.

I even take it in the car with me for long road trips because it makes the trip so much easier. My only word of caution—don’t leave it in a hot car. title: They work
text:
Generally, I am satisfied with these insoles, they are ultra thin comparing to other heated insoles that don't leave room for your feet in the shoes, these insoles will fit easily in most of not all the shoes you wear and they do work. They do an excellent job of keeping your feet warm and they warm up quickly too. I own a more expensive pair that take about 15 minutes to get to the right temperature. With these guys you will feel warm within 3 minutes. They also get warmer than my expensive heated insoles but not too hot, just right. The reason why I am giving it only 3 starts is because of 3 issues:
1. It runs on 6 aa batteries that get you about 3 hours of heat at most. I found myself spending too much money on batteries and was not too happy with how long the heat lasted, in the end there is no dial to set the temperature so it's not like you can save some power.
2. There not wireless, the battery pack is strapped to your ankles... I found that okay when wearing sneakers or regular shoes, but boots were too thick to wrap the battery pack around since they cover your ankles, it can be quite uncomfortable.
3. I have used these for nearly 2 months and one of the battery packs stopped working.

In the end, for the price it is totally worth keeping your feet warm when you have to go outside in the cold. The key is to think of them as a temporary solution/seasonal because they will most likely not last you very long.

title: Arrived With Odor
text:
When I received the zeolite rocks I noticed an urine-like odor on the bags that came with them but I thought it would dissipate later. Yet, after a few hours it was stronger, so I removed the rocks from the bags and put them in two cut tee shirt sleeves, it was better than the bags but still smelly. Finally, I put the zeolite in plastic cups which, again, was better but didn't dispel the odor all together. I thought in time the odor would dissappear.

On the second day, I sprinkled about six or seven of the rocks on an unused basement bathroom floor behind the door where one of the original odors I was trying to get rid of was strongest, but after awhile it became unbearable. My nose, throat, face and chest were burning. I collected the rocks and put them away in a drawer. After contacting the company about the odor and receiving no response, I decided to return them.

On the third day, I put them in foam bowls in the sunlight to air out. Even after two hours the odor was still there. I put the zeolite and its bags back into the original packaging. The return was picked up today, the fourth day after I used them.

I considered what could have gone wrong. There were river rocks already in some of these places which I had to remove because the odor from the zeolite clung to them. Also, in two places I had plugin negative ion emitters. But after removing them, the odor grew stronger. I can only conclude that the urine-like smell from the bags was the original problem.

I believe that the zeolite outgassed the odor from the bags that came with it. The odor still has not dissipated from my home though it's not as strong as it was before. I'll have to wait. Hopefully, it’ll be gone soon.
The zeolite did get rid of the odors in the places I placed them in. Even behind the basement bathroom door. But the pain and burning I received in return was, of course, not worth it.

title: Works great as the first mask
text:
This is my very first sleep mask, and I was choosing it carefully. I needed it to be light and breathable and adjustable, so I wouldn't feel something pressing my face or pinching my hair, making it even harder to fall asleep than it already is. I also looked for something pretty cheap because it was just an experiment, I wasn't sure that a mask would really help.
Well, the description is true. This mask is very soft and breathable. All the materials are synthetic but really nice to the touch. I think the same fibers are used in lingerie. It takes a minute to adjust the mask so it doesn't press but doesn't fall off. The soft side of velcro strap is about 5 inches long, so you can adjust it for every head size and desired pressure. Once you chose your size, you may keep the velcro closed forever and put on or remove the mask like a headband. The velcro holds fast, it even held through laundering in a washing mashine. The harsh side of the velcro has extremely small hooks, so it doesn't pinch or tangle your hair.
It doesn't block 100% of the light because of the fit, you still can see a little around your nose. For me it's actually a plus because when I wake up I feel disoriented for a while, and I was worried I would panic if I wake up feeling blind. Seeing this little light helps me to realise I'm wearing a mask, and the mask still provides enough darkness to help me sleep even with open curtains when the sun is up.
What I don't like is there wasn't any washing instructions on the package.

title: Excellent
text:
These are fantastic earplugs!

They are easier to insert into the ear canal than most other foam earplugs. It is easier to compress them and then “un-compress” slowly. You won’t get instant noise reduction because of that, but you only have to wait a few minutes. But when they fully expand, they will be in there well!

This makes them more comfortable, at least for me. I often have sore ear canals from pushing ear plugs in too hard or spending too much time fiddling with them.

The noise reduction is quite significant. If you are looking for ear plugs that enable you to hear quite a bit, like for noisy music environments, these may actually be too much noise reduction for you. For my use, sleeping in a noisy environment, they are fantastic. They do the job better than any other ear plug I have ever used. And they stay in. Five stars plus! High recommended.

title: Great maca
text:
I adore maca. This one is superior and the price is about the same as other brands.

Maca has a toasty almost yeasty taste and smell. I can’t explain it. I happen to love the taste of it. I use it in smoothies and have for years. It’s supposed to be good for you. Can’t attest to that, but I do know that maca seems to give me a little boost without the jitters of caffeine, so that’s great for me as I can not tolerate caffeine.

I particularly love smoothies with a combination of raw cacao and maca. Try them together if you haven’t.

When I first started using maca I remember that I thought it actually smelled like sweaty socks - not dirty socks, but athletic socks that had been worn on clean feet that had been sweating. It’s a very particular odor! Nutritional yeast has that smell. And I thought all maca does, too, but that turns out not to be the case. I don’t get that smell from this brand of maca. I’ll admit that I rather like that smell. I like nutritional yeast and I like maca, but this is quite a bit nicer. It has a strong smell that maca lovers will like. My hubby, whose sense of smell isn’t as strong as mine (according to him) really loves this maca and commented on the good smell when I put it from the re-sealable bag into a glass storage container.

It is noticeably finer ground than other organic brands that I’ve been buying. That means you’ll have a less grainy taste, not that I noticed it before, but I did notice that this was ground very fine indeed.

Good price. Good product. My only complaint is an odd one, and not one that I’ll take away any stars for: I do not like the packaging design. It doesn’t look like the packaging of a food product but more like it would be suitable for office products. Doesn’t matter, as I threw it away. I like keeping products like this in glass containers.

Highly recommended.

title: 99% of the time unresponsive
text:
Pros: easy to install. Keypad works just fine at the door. (Palm over the face to activate, hit the two random numbers, then enter your code) — this is a nice feature bc the first lock we tried, we would have to enter codes a couple times bc we would accidentally hit a number upon waking up the display. Also, the bolt is metal, the last lock we tried felt flimsy but this one feels solid.

Cons: the entire reason we swapped from our original lock to this one was for the apple home integration. This is not reliable at all. In a perfect scenario, when we get home and connect to the WiFi, our phones would ask if we wanted to unlock. Apple home DOES give us the alert, but when we attempt it, lock is unresponsive.

99% of the time, if I open the lock’s app, even if I’m within 10 feet, it cannot connect to the lock. We have 1 gig internet and I don’t think anything in our home aside from the lock itself is the issue here.

If you open the app, close the app, and open again, about 80% of the time it does actually pick up the connection. It’s just annoying to know that it won’t work the first time every time. Defeats the purpose of having a smart device.

Overall, now that I have it, I don’t feel the need to go on another hunt for a lock. However, I would not order this lock if you’re looking for mobile friendly reliable. At the door, it works perfectly fine. The batteries are at 98% after 3 months of use.

I know from experience: when I have used earbud cushions that were too small for my ear opening, I have found the cushions sometimes get lodged inside the ear.

Luckily, I now use bigger earbud cushions, but that one episode was enough to make me the consider the consequences of having some small part dislodge, and the situation with nostrils is no different - if anything, it could prove to be more hazardous. Wear a well-lined mask instead.

title: Reasonably effective neck stretcher
text:
TLDR: works, but lack of adjustability limits effectiveness

I was a gymnast and broke my neck many years ago. I’m paying for it now and am willing to try anything that might help alleviate the constant low level pain. The best I’ve found are a rumble roller and a foam ball, depending on whether I need to stretch or else need focused pressure.

I was really looking forward to using the Kenko neck stretcher, but thus far, am slightly underwhelmed. There are two positions, one of which is slightly more aggressive. But the lack of true adjustability and relatively soft foam limits it’s effectiveness. That said, I t does give a constant and gentle stretch.

I’m going to give this a try for two months, and will change my rating if it is truly effective, but if it doesn’t outperform my rumble roller, I’ll probably just donate it to charity. Still, I give it 4 stars and a conditional recommendation.

title: A Beautiful Choice for Baby
text:
I chose Beatrix Potter for my nursery theme and purchased the GR Gibson Beatrix Pottery Memory Book for my first baby. Since I am not finding out the gender, this baby book is especially appreciated for its gender-neutral appearance in pale cream, soft peach, and green. The soft pastel colours are suitable for a boy or girl, and an excellent showcase for the timeless art of Beatrix Potter.

Thick, sturdy covers promise to stand up to plenty of handling, essential since this book will be revisited several times once the baby comes. The solid pages are different from flimsier, thinner paper found in other baby books. A ballpoint pen works just as well as gel or ink, and none of the ink saturates through the heavier grain. Attaching photographs or keepsakes is much easier with this strong backing.

The memory book separates into pregnancy and post-partum sections. Areas allow details about parents, family tree, and the infant to be recorded. Some purchasers may be put off for the lack of room for all medical information or prenatal visits, but I didn't find this to be a problem. I attached an additional sleeve for the various sonograph photos I received during my pregnancy, as they far exceeded the space provided. I think additional blank pages can be purchased and inserted, though I haven't done so.

The interior artwork is an assortment of Peter Rabbit and other iconic Potter characters, like Jemima Puddleduck and Mrs. Tiggywinkle. Crisp colours and bright illustrations will endure through the years, and make a very sweet counterpoint to the well laid out contents. Achievements, travel and other accomplishments for the first year are spread out across the book. It's easy to document baby's firsts in an attractive format.

I recommend this book to any parent. It makes a fine gift, too!

title: Large heating pad, surely different
text:
This heating pad was certainly not what I expected. First things first, it is big (28"x17", I should have read that...) but the actual heating area is the smaller area in the picture where the stones are (roughly 19"x12"). The whole construction is on the stiffer side, so don't expect to fold it over a shoulder for example - this seems to be thought for use over the whole back, and it works for that purpose. I wouldn't call it appropriate for the neck though, it would take some serious ingenuity to fit it around it.
Now, the instructions say to wait for about 10 minutes for it to heat up, and they are right - you do need to wait for the stones to warm up. Once it is warmed up though, the feeling is really nice, and it feels like it penetrates pretty well.
The first time I used it, it gave off an unpleasant smell reminiscent of burning plastic - this dissipated later though, and there was hardly any smell the second time I used it.
Now, if you read more carefully, this pad claims to be emitting far infrared rays, which supposedly penetrate deeper into the skin to increase circulation. I cannot attest to whether this is true or not, but if this holds, it might be a great complement to the more standard NIR therapy. Worth a try :)

title: Weird, but effective!
text: This is quite possibly the weirdest form of hair removal I've tried to date, and I'm honestly very pleasantly surprised. I didn't have very high hopes for this, because I wasn't sure how rough the material would be, but it's not at all rough; if you run your finger over it, you can't even tell that there's a microscopic almost grid-like surface to it. It's so weird, it's basically sanding your skin until the hair disappears? But I honestly kind of love it? I did it dry; it says to do it after you get your legs wet, but I think the only thing that's different in doing it dry is the layer of dead skin dust that is left after you get done. Which isn't terrible, I just wiped it off, and my legs have literally never been this smooth. The exfoliation is top notch, better than the exfoliating mitt I have, and this gives me as close of a shave as a razor does. I'm not sure if it will be as effective on softer areas, i.e. bikini line or stomach hair, for example, but if you do attempt it, be sure to hold the skin taught to get the most friction possible, as that's really how this works. But again, I want to state how smooth my legs were after this!! I'd definitely buy again; I'm not sure if I will eventually have to replace it, as I'm not sure if the "sanding" part of it will wear down.. it say's it's glass, and I believe it probably is, or something close to it. I'm just not sure about how long it will last, kind of like a razor eventually getting dull.

title: Smaller strong nonflappable attachable bag
text:
Just what I wanted for my sister's power chair. It has straps which keep it tight against the top seat rest, which I think will eliminate strain on the top strap.

I bought her a heavy duty bookbag for more than $20 last year, and used it with only the top strap over her head rest, and it lasted a year. But it was easy for people to get into, because it stuck out like a sore thumb and everyone knows how to get into those things.

I don't expect stuff we put on her chair to last more than a year--nothing ever does, but I like it to look like part of the chair, like it came with the chair, so it doesn't draw too much attention and it looks neater.

I like it to match the wheelchair, to not draw attention. It's not as fun or colorful, but her stuff's always getting stolen, so I like to make it as inconspicuous as possible.

Most thieves don't immediately know how to get into custom wheelchair assessories, so it buys her some time and protection, especially when the bag is on the back of her chair.

Anyway, I also bought it to hold the chair's power charger, so that we wouldn't have to bend all the way down to the bottom of the chair to pull it out of the little compartment they made for that.

So now the charger is stored in this new bag at waist level and it's convenient, accessing it in the top zippered pocket.

There's only two other pockets on the bag, which are both small and face outward. One right one we used to store a small Totes umbrella, and the one on the left we use to store a small case with a folded up emergency poncho.

We use a separate quilted bag that matches her wheelchair that we bought last year for whatever else she has to carry temporarily. That one has a regular tote bag strap and it fits over the head rest easily. She keeps her few valuables in a purse that's attached to a strap around her.

We typically have to replace stuff every year, and I'd love to buy her something frilly and fun, but it's just not worth having her stuff stolen.

Anyway this particular bag is made out of a thin vinyl kind of parachute material it seems, but I'm confident that it will be strong enough to hold her power charger box and cords. The stitching is strong and the zippers look well made, so I'm confident about the chair bag and happy with the purchase price.

I was considered 2 days early and my labor and birth at home went smoothly and quickly (6 hour labor, 10 minutes pushing). Not sure if these were the cause but they definitely didn't hurt. I only got one bottle this pregnancy because I'm sure I'll go into labor before 40 weeks and will still have some leftover during breastfeeding if all goes well. I guess it's a matter preference but the description and photos should definitely be updated to 2 capsules max daily.

title: Love the smooth velcro!! All the function in a smaller package!
text:
I am an avid sleep mask lover and have had my fair share of eye masks. I love how I am able to fall asleep faster and get better quality sleep with eye masks- especially this one! I particularly like this mask for a few reasons: the eye part is contoured and raised off the eyes. The mask is actually slimmer, smaller (narrower) than other masks I have or have owned. The Velcro is a massive improvement over other masks (including every mask I have had)- it is the 'smooth' Velcro that doesn't catch on everything and pull fabric strings. Although this mask doesn't have the contoured nose part that goes over the bridge of the nose- it is comfortable and has enough structure that you will not need to adjust or pull down to block light. With this mask I do not hit my eyelashes, even when side sleeping- awesome! As a bonus this mask set comes with a carrying case and a set of ear plugs per mask. It also includes instructions for those who are new to sleep masks.
Like very mask- there will be tiny bits of lights down by your nostrils which truly isn't an issue unless you take day naps in a bright room. I received this mask at a discount in exchange for my review. My reviews are based on the products I receive and my experience with them. This is a well thought out product and I truly love it.
* Per the CPAP user in my home* This mask is advertised as being able to be used with a Continuous Positive Airway Pressure Therapy Apparatus (CPAP machine)- although that may be true- it is not compatible with every CPAP mask, for example:a full face mask that covers the mouth and nose is not compatible with this sleep mask because of where the CPAP mask sits the eye mask has to be above it or else it does not allow for a good seal on the CPAP mask.

title: Bit expensive for quality, but helpful.
text:
I saw these name badge attachment cards floating around Amazon, and as a nursing student, really wanted to get one for a quick reference when I'm wandering around clinical pretending to know what I'm talking about. I couldn't decide which ones I wanted more, so I ended up buying a pack of five to see how it worked out.

Turns out, I end up using some more than others, but having them all around for a nice reminder where I don't have to carry an extra book around is quite useful. The lab values, titrations, and medications are super helpful, as are the weight conversions (because let's face it, I SUCK at figuring out lbs into kg off the top of my head). I don't necessary need the anatomical direction card, but generally speaking, these are quite helpful in a clinical setting.

You can also take a dry-erase marker to them and it comes right off with alcohol wipes. Spiffy.

Oh, I didn't end up keeping them on the keychain. I cut the plastic part off and added them to my nametag. I tried to just hang them on the keychain, and it was just.. Awkward and heavy. So I let it go, and everything worked out better after that point.

The design is useful as well. It's handle is great when maneuvering the product from place to place, making it easier to carry because the body does get a bit hot around the opening so without this, I wouldn't have understood how to move it around.

It lasts for about 10 minutes, which is how long you should use a product like this on your face. It does get very hot, which is why I advise to not use it more than once a week and not too close to your face. I'm not sure of the benefits with a product like this (I own two) but it's relaxing for me. I keep it about 12 inches away from my face, maybe more and I still feel it. I made the mistake of having it too close to my face before and it was too hot.

Good product. Works as described.

title: Dang me! It works!
text:
I was diagnosed with sleep apnea in 2006 and handed a CPAP machine. While I should have traded it in after 2-3 years, I lost my job in 2008 and lost my health insurance. So it lasted 7 years until a couple weeks ago when the machine burst into flames a minute after putting the mask on. Yeah, that scared the you know what out of me.
Since then, I have been a walking zombie. Cannot afford a new machine. I am so disoriented it feels like I have dementia.
Then a week ago, I tried the Breathe Right strips and it helped. But I had to sleep only on my sides and keep my mouth shut. It helped a bit, but not enough.
I did extensive research before buying this Chinstrap. I saw it had good ratings and crossed my fingers.
I got it today and needed a nap. I figured out how the contraption works without much stress, strapped on a nasal strip, and went to bed.
I slept like the dead.
I was able to sleep on my back, my sides, and over under sideways down.
I think the nasal strip is an important adjunct to the strap.
I am almost too afraid to whisper that it works, but is sure seems to.
The real test will be the next few weeks. I have been taking naps (I'm an old f**t) ever since my CPAP did a fireworks show. And I've been waking up more tired than when I lay down. This is the first nap I woke up from and feel rested.
I did extensive research before I pulled the trigger on this thing.
It works.
Check for follow up.

title: Didn't Realize All Neti-Pot Products Weren't Made by NeilMed
text:
At the recommendation of my Allergist, I've been using the NeilMed Sinus Rinse bottle for years. I primarily use it when I have a cold or sinus infection, as it works wonders in keeping my sinuses clear overnight when used in the evening. My allergist recommended using it year round for allergies.

When I saw this NetiPot Sinus Rinse in a different configuration, I erroneously thought that NetiPot was a product only offered by NeilMed and didn't realize it's a term for a product offered by other manufacturers - in this case Rabuhara.

I received two of the products, but they came with no box or instructions - only the two bottles in a clear cellophane bag. There was no paperwork to even give you direction to where to go to get instructions. Note that I received the product as part of the Vine Program, so perhaps it was shipped before their packaging was complete. I simply didn't feel comfortable using a product for medical purposes without any instructions for fear of doing harm. I left what I thought was a neutral review of 3 stars.

I was really disappointed at my mistake at thinking this was a NeilMed product, which I've got experience using and trust. I mean no disrespect to Rabuharu, but not being familiar with the company or their products, I looked them up online and found nothing about sinus rinses. Without instructions, I have to pass on using the product.

The lids all seem to snap to form a tight seal. The base on all is relatively clear and the lids are all a medium blue. title: Buy it. Comparing 1.2 to 1.8 to 2.0 formulas
text:
I first tried Soylent way back with version 1.2. I have been sold ever since. The idea that I can have nearly complete nutrition for any meal is fantastic. Soylent is very open about their ingredients and choices around them. You can be confident you are drinking something that is as solid a well rounded meal replacement as currently possible.

Recently I have been buying the premade 2.0 version. It best fits my lifestyle. I use it fairly infrequently when I don't have great other meal choices. In those cases I will drink 1-2 bottles of 2.0 to replace a meal.

Getting the chance to try the powder version again with 1.8 was great. It had been some time since I had it and the formula changed quite a bit. The best way to describe the taste is neutral with a slight grain taste to it. It will be similar to other protein drinks but more neutral in flavor. The consistency is a bit thinner (not in a bad way) compared to 2.0. 1.8 is also a bit more neutral tasting than 2.0. Easier to add your own flavors to it. Honestly I would say I don't prefer 1.8 or 2.0 better than the other. Both are solid. Chocolate 2.0 though beats them all.

That said the flexibility of the powder is really a nice change. I can do one scoop for a light snack, two for a heavy snack. Maybe up to 3-4 if I want a heavy meal. It is amazing how it magically makes you feel full after a quick drink. With the premade once you open it, you don't have much time and it is 400 calories, period.

I use a shaker with a good rubber seal to make it and then hand shake it with ice. Mixes very fast and easily compared to old 1.2 formula. Try it, I think you will enjoy it.

title: Tastes great & mixes easily, but pricey
text:
In this review, I'm going to avoid any kind of direct label-comparisons. You can read labels and compare ingredients at different price points. Rather, I want to mention several things about this protein that makes me prefer it as a consumer.

First, it tastes AWESOME for a whey protein. I have used probably half the protein brands on the market. Usually, if they are whey, they have that pungent, condensed milk taste that you have to gag down. Some others are decent if they are mixed with milk, but milk doesn't mix as well and leaves your shaker bottle full of chunks. Or, alternatively, you can mix with water, which makes the pungent whey taste so much worse. This protein, however, tastes great mixed with water and downright AMAZING mixed with milk. The taste, by the way, is kind of a light mocha taste, like a mild jamocha shake from Arby's (remember those?).

Following on that, what really impresses me is that this stuff mixes easily with whole milk in a shaker bottle, without any chunks whatsoever. This matters to me because I always find it is inconvenient to use a blender. Many times I don't want to wake my wife or kids; other times, I just don't want to clean a whole blender. So having a protein that can mix easily in a shaker bottle is often the difference between drinking protein or not.

OK fine, I will say a word or two about the ingredients. As far as I can tell, this protein has all the main ingredients you should look for in a protein. It costs a little more per unit of protein and other ingredients, but it's still a solid mix. And for what it's worth, a typical body can only absorb about 25 grams of protein every twelve hours, so the protein-loading that many options encourage are not really giving you much advantage.

Overall, I give this 5 stars. I deduct one star because I think the price is quite high compared to the competition (over $1.00 per serving). If I check back and the price has fallen, I would definitely raise to 5 stars. This is great stuff. Just hard to buy for this price when there are so many other options that are more affordable.

title: Stylish and Strong toothbrush!
text:
I purchased the Sporzin electric toothbrush (black) to replace my conventional electric toothbrush which uses batteries. This one is charged with a USB port and keeps the charge very well. It gives a fresh feeling to mouth after use. For first time users, the power of the brush may seem a little high, but you get used to it if you start with the lowest power setting and gradually go for higher ones. I loved the preset modes including general cleaning, whitening, refreshing, gum care, and polishing. Once you move along the modes, you will notice the brush head movement direction changes completely.
The brush has a short pause every 30 seconds which reminds you to move to another part of the mouth, so the overall brushing takes about two minutes. Of course, you can extend it if you wish.
I also enjoyed the power of the motor inside the brush, and I showed the strength of the head vibrations in the uploaded video using a cup of water. I think it provides enough force to remove regular debris and stains from the teeth without needing excessive pressure by the user.
Overall, I believe that Sporzin is a very efficient and strong electric toothbrush that is comparable with the popular brands in the market, with a much more affordable price!

As a longtime veteran of working in places that operate around the clock, I'm familiar with most tricks of the trade for succeeding in the unnatural act of staying up all night. During a 12-hour overnight shift, I usually take one of these with a meal about halfway through. Doing so seems to get me over that middle of the night hump. Sometimes I'll take a second just before heading home to share the road with all the "normal" drivers.

title: Not the greatest bang for your buck
text:
I'm a longtime user of protein powders, and I've tried a wide range of collagen and whey powders over the years. title: Solid ingredients, pleasant flavor, annoying bag
text:
I use protein powder on a daily basis for post-workout shakes, and this looked like a solid option so I gave it a try, I like the ingredients list, there's no weird ingredients, no junk filler, and especially no added sugars. I tried the vanilla cold brew flavor, and based on the name I was uncertain if there is cold brew coffee in it, or if the vanilla itself is somehow cold brewed and there is no coffee? The ingredients don't really explain what's going on there.

Upon opening the package, there is a distinct coffee aroma, and when I mixed it with water and ice cubes to test there is a faint coffee flavor. I don't know that I'd call it a coffee flavored powder, it's more a background note, so don't worry about it overpowering other flavors you may add. The flavor in general is mild and not-too-sweet, which is just what I'm after with a protein powder. If I want more excitement I'll mix frozen berries in. The texture is a little grainy, but that comes with the territory for anything made with hemp/rice/pea protein. The color is a slightly weird yellowish-brown, but whatever this isn't a beauty contest, it's a convenient way to get a hit of protein on the way out the door.

My only complaint is the zipper on the bag clogging with powder and refusing to close. I hold the bag closed with a rubber band and am careful not to knock it over on the shelf, but this type of bag is an annoying way to package powders.

In general, this is right in my sweet spot for clean ingredients, good nutritional profile, and good but unobtrusive flavor.

title: Hours Of Fun! A Perfect Activity Kit For Kids And Adults To Make A Bath Time Favorite!
text:
# My Review
This review is for the Sturish Bath Fizzies - DIY STEM Science Kit. Having recently spent numerous days/hours of indoor time with kids who were getting bored over the summer break, this turned out to be a great way to spend a few hours learning, making, and finally trying a bath time fun favorite. That said, when I saw this offering and the way in which it was packaged, produced, and delivered, I just knew it was worth trying with my kid.

First of all, I can’t say enough great things about how this kit is packaged, delivered and presented. The whole presentation is appealing and describes science & fun which draws attention! The kit is packaged in a strong and durable presentation box with the branding, pictures, and wording that gives this product some good shelf presence. Inside the box is everything you need to make these bath fizzies; 4 molds, baking soda, 3 colors (Red, Blue, and Yellow), corn starch, bath salt, and 3 essential oils (Lavender, Appleseed, and Grapeseed), spoons, pipette, and an instruction manual – nothing else needed except for eager kids and adults to get started!

Inside the box you get everything you need to make these bath fizzies (as described in the product description). Making these is supposed to be an exact science where you need to measure, weigh, calculate, clock-watch and have patience! Just steam. I did try different temperatures, and it doesn't matter. The bomb dissolves in about 6-8 minutes (depending on how much water is hitting it) so it lasts long enough; the scent just doesn't fill the area.

The foil out covering is easy to remove, but you do need the little lime green pointy tool to open the inner plastic wrapping. It's easy enough to use when your hands are wet.

This set has a few unique features about it that make it better than some other options, though. For instance, there's some shredded paper at the bottom which makes it seem a little more gift-like. And there's a little sticky-backed hook to hang in your shower to hold the organza bag and opener that comes with the set, and you can fit two bombs in the bag as well. That helps keep your bombs handy.

Summary: I tried the lavender first, and then tried the eucalyptus the next day. Just not enough scent for me. And while I did put the hook up, and hang the bag, 2 bombs, and the opener, I know I'm going to forget to refill the bag. I normally keep all my bombs in a container on the shelf that holds my shampoo and that makes more sense to me. I think hook and the bag are coming down shortly. Better idea in theory than in practice. But again, I've been looking for a year for a shower bomb that truly works the way I want it to and haven't fond it yet. These bombs are in good company! And they really would make a thoughtful gift even though they don't really do much.

title: Passed the skin test on my wrist, but tingled and stung around my eyes. No results.
text:
I tried this cream for 10 days before I decided to discontinue use. When I first got it, I put it on my sensitive wrist skin to check for a reaction. I didn't react or have any issues, so I decided to try it on my face. I used it around my forehead, cheeks, and chin, as well as my chest and tried to avoid my sensitive eye area. It gave my skin a bit of a tingle, but nothing too terrible. I slept it off.

After a couple of uses on my face, I went ahead and applied in my eye area. It began stinging the sensitive skin in the periorbital area, and was too tingly for my comfort. It did dissipate, but I was not keen on it. Thinking it might just be an initial irritation or perhaps too much sun, I have it two more chances at night with similar results.

I haven't noticed any particularly astounding results with hydration or skin brightness, and I wasn't keen on the stinging and tingling around my eye area so I've discontinued use. It could be amazing for someone else, but it isn't for me.

The top ingredients aren't particularly astounding either. I don't find it worth $48 to get the neat container that I can refill. I'd rather pay more or less for a product that won't irritate my skin, and will show some improvement in my dark circles and dry face. The first ingredient is water, the second ingredient is methylpropanediol which is just a surfactant, and the third ingredient is vegetable oil.

Polyglyceryl-3 is supposed to be moisturizing and help with emulsifying. Polyglyceryl-3 is another emulsifier. Betaine is added for moisture, although I didn't see much improvement in my dry areas in the 10 days of use. C6-14 Olefin is another emoliant. It's rated a 1 by Skin Deep in the correct concentrations. Then there is shea butter, which usually leaves my skin soft and moisturized, but perhaps the concentrations are lower in this formula. From there, there's a couple dozen ingredients. I'm not sure which one or which combination irritated my skin, but this isn't one I'll buy again.

Ingredients: Water/Aqua/Eau*, Methylpropanediol, Vegetable Oil*, Polyglyceryl-3 Methylglucose Distearate*, Betaine, Hydrogenated Poly(C6-14 Olefin), Butyrospermum Parkii (Shea) Butter*, Dicaprylyl Ether, Angelica Archangelica Root Water**, 1,2-Hexanediol, Ammonium Acryloyldimethyltaurate/VP Copolymer, Onsen-Sui*, Sodium Hyaluronate*, Bifida Ferment Extract*, Lactobacillus Ferment Lysate*, Lactococcus Ferment Extract*, Glycerin*, Panthenol*, Vaccinium Macrocarpon (Cranberry) Seed Oil*, Rubus Chamaemorus (Arctic Cloudberry) Seed Oil*, Buddleja Davidii Extract*~, Thymus Vulgaris (Thyme) Extract*~, Ethylhexylglycerin, Hydroxyacetophenone, Tocopherol, Citric Acid*, Cetearyl Alcohol*, Sodium Stearoyl Glutamate, Sodium Benzoate, Potassium Sorbate **Component of Icelandic Glacial Water *Natural or naturally derived ~Ecocert

I liked the fact that it was cordless and usb rechargeable.  it seems like everything is these days.  we opened the box and the 1st thing she said was, "y is it only 1 color?  u need to have 2 different colored heads so that u dont use someone else's toothbrush."  strike 1.  she put the toothpaste on and pushed the button.  she said it turns off a little every 30 seconds so that u can change positions.  it runs for 3 minutes, which she said was a very long time. strike 2. if u think about it, its weird that it runs for only 3 minutes u need to do both sides of the inside of ur teeth.  so wouldn't u need 4 minutes?  I guess no one wants to brush that long.  the bottom glows green when its on, and it doesn't make so much noise that its annoying.  once she cranked it up to 5, it did get a little loud and she said that after a while her hand started to feel weird.  strike 3.  we put it in a cup of water to watch the bristle action.  only the top moves, the bottom stays frozen.  strike 4.  she said her teeth felt clean after though.  the instructions that come with this machine are very lacking as well as confusing.  its as if they were translated to English.  the punctuation is all wrong and the words are just incorrect.  so if u r looking for assistance with using it... ur on ur own, but its a toothbrush... haven't we been using them our whole lives... I hope this was helpful.

title: Well-Made But With Some Issues- Still Nice As A Backup Or Liner
text:
These Aneercare washable menstrual pads are okay overall. I haven’t tried any other reusable pads like this so I can’t compare.

So far I have used them as a pad after the 1st and 2nd day of my cycle when it is lighter. I was too nervous to use when I first started this month because I had to work all night and didn’t want to risk having a huge mess on my hands.

They are thick and soft on the grey pad side, and the outer material seems to be made of waterproof fabric with various cute patterns. I find them to be comfortable and and they don’t make any crinkly noise while wearing. I received 6 medium-large size and 1 additional smaller pad (not all shown in my pictures). A cute little waterproof bag is included to store as needed.

Overall, these appear very nice and well made with good stitching. Each one has a snap button in the middle. The buttons work well and don’t come undone, but I will say that the buttons don’t secure them in place as well as I would like. There is a tendency for the pad to slide forward and back or start flipping sideways a bit. Therefore, sometimes frequent adjustments are needed. That is another reason why I’m not sure I would want to use these on heavier days.

They feel thick, well-padded, and seem fairly absorbent, though I have noticed that stuff may appear to sit on top for a little while before sinking in a little more.

They have washed well so far. I always do a nice hand wash before putting in the washing machine.

In the future, I will probably try at least once to use this on heavier days to see if it works, but as of now I think these are nice for using like starting the 3rd day of my cycle. These would also be good as a backup to tampon or cup though I have been trying to just stick to pads lately. My honest gut feeling is that I think I’ll have a mess when I try this on a heavy day. Even if I never use these on heavier days, it is still nice to save money on disposable pads by using these on lighter days- environmentally friendly too!

It would be much better if the company found a way to get the pads to stay in place better without so much sliding. Maybe a second pair of buttons is needed or the waterproof material could have some kind of grip on it.

I’ll be sure to update this review if any other issues arise with regular use. I’ll update when I’m able to test them on a heavier day, but as of now I would recommend them them as a liner on light days if you okay with having to adjust their position every once in awhile. I hope my review was helpful in some way, and if so, I would love to know-thanks!

title: Looks SUPER Cute- But Is Not Without Flaws
text:
This Townley Girl L.O.L. Surprise! Peel- Off Nail Polish Activity Set is only okay. For young kids, this could potentially be fun like maybe 4/5 rating just for the fun of doing nails and that this set looks really cute, but all together including quality I’m only going to say 3/5 stars and I’ll tell you why.

Pros-
-5 cute-looking nail polishes
-240 cute little nail gems organized by type
-Surprise nail stickers
-Adorable little LOL doll bag to store items in
-Kid friendly nail polish set
-Dries fairly quickly
-Peel off (Some may consider this a negative)
-Everything just appears adorable and well-presented. I’m sure any little girl would see this and get excited

Cons-
-Nail polish doesn’t appear as vivid on nails as in bottle. They are pretty transparent (Blue is the worst as you can see from my pictures)
-May dry fairly fast but will require multiple coats to show up well- especially blue. The pink and purple probably show up the best
-They are peel off which can be nice, but are prone to peeling off when you don’t want them to. My daughter went to wash her hands and a few of the nail colors had fallen off. I tried them on myself and they can stay a little while, but kids aren’t so careful.
-Not a huge deal but the rectangular
decorative caps are separate from the actual caps that close the nail polish bottles. You can sit there and twist the rectangular caps forever, but they often just spin around the actual cap. I usually have to take those off first and then unscrew the real cap. They could have just made it all one? I don’t know... seems silly.
-The gems are adorable, but this is actually what frustrates my daughter the most (she is 5). There is no glue or anything specifically to hold the gems in place. I just painted her nails and then added some globs of extra polish to act as glue. NOPE. Fell off in less than a minute even after waiting for them to dry-all of them.... and she was so excited about them and became a little frustrated wondering why I couldn’t get them to stick.
-The bag is cute, but for some reason, the company thought it was a good idea to put some type of adhesive on the back of the bag to connect it to the plastic packaging. Again, not a huge deal, but it won’t come off and you can see it in my picture stuck there with an obvious fold in the bag. I’m not sure why they thought that little adhesive circle was necessary.

In conclusion, is this a fun set for kids? Yes, it can be, unless those kids may become easily frustrated with their freshly painted nails and gems falling off left and right just minutes after they spent time finishing them.

It really is a cute set and my daughter and I had a bit of fun, but we were both still disappointed too which is sad because I was so excited about ordering this for her. I hope my review was helpful in some way, and if so, I would love to know- thanks!

title: Easy formula to absorb, made in USA, third party lab verified
text:
I need to take magnesium due to low bone density issues which is the result of cancer treatment decades ago. I have learned that not all magnesium supplements are created equally and that some forms of magnesium are more readily absorbed than other forms - the National Institute of Health notes "studies have found that magnesium in the aspartate, citrate, lactate, and chloride forms is absorbed more completely and is more bioavailable than magnesium oxide and magnesium sulfate." As a result, I switched from the less expensive magnesium oxide I had been taking to using more absorbable forms of magnesium. My research led me to find that magnesium diglycinate is one of the most readily available forms of magnesium for digestion. One study, entitled Bioavailability of Magnesium Diglycinate vs Magnesium Oxide in Patients with Ileal Resection confirms how much better-absorbed magnesium diglycinate is over the common magnesium oxide. As a result, magnesium diglycinate is one of the best magnesium forms available for absorption.

For a magnesium supplement, this has almost all the positives going for it (the only thing lacking is they are not organic):

Made in the USA
Third-party tested
Vegan capsule
Uses Magnesium Diglycinate
Well-sized and easy to swallow

The only issue I have with this supplement is that to get 420 mg of magnesium requires 3 capsules rather than the daily dosage indicated on the package of 2 capsules. Given the emphasis on the product page and package of 420 mg of magnesium and that the product contains 60 servings, I believed that one serving contained 420 mg of magnesium when the 2 capsule recommended serving contains only 280 mg of magnesium.

title: Difficult setup but easy to sue, clear display w voice, USB powered, useful product for 2 users
text:
[[VIDEOID:dcb83b99b76f4e40016817be9850eac9]] I'm a guy who typically tries to set things up without reading the instructions and found that I had to read the instructions here to figure out how to set it up as the date/time settings were not intuitive to me. Set up was a bit of a pain and I used the single sheet instructions that were printed in LARGE type to do so, but I found that these instructions skipped some setting and the instruction booklet requires me to grab my reading glasses so I haven't sorted that out yet.

Once setup, it is easy to use WITHOUT THE VOICE and the readings are accurate as compared to an OMRON machine my wife uses. That said, this does take a bit longer than the OMRON.

The display is clear and easy to read and stores 99 readings for each of 2 users. It is easy to switch between users.

The device comes with a set of 4 AA batteries but also includes a USB A to C cable that can power the device. I was surprised that when I disconnected the USB cable to move the device from one room to another that my settings were saved so I did not have to go through reprogramming the date and time.

The verbal reading is helpful but with a thick accent. When I turn it off, I'm honestly not sure what the machine is saying - I think "measure over" but I'm not certain. I also find it odd that it reads out systolic and diastolic measurements as "X millimeter or MERcury" - I think just a number or even 106 millimeters but hearing "of MERcury" twice each reading will wear on me. There was some setting for PA which I turned off that gave a reading in some other measurement as well, but that was not useful to me.

Overall, this is easy to use (after setup) and does the job fine. The package includes the device, armband, batteries, a warranty card (12 months), USB cable, and a small carrying case.

I'm happy to recommend this Antrolife blood pressure monitor - it is easy to use, functions properly and the visual and verbal readout are easy to see/hear.

title: ingredients list on package doesn't meet this description on the page.  This is concerning.
text:
I ordered this package of apple cider vinegar gummies understanding that the product was organic, but it does not appear that anything in the ingredients list s organic. I also note that the page shows the ingredients to be "Ginger(root), Cane Sugar, Glucose Syrup, Water, Citrus Pectin, Citric Acid, Sodium Citrate, Natural Flavors" whereas the actual packaging shows the ingredients to be "Cane Sugar, Glucose Syrup (Corn Syrup), Water, Citrus Pectin, Citric Acid, Sodium Citrate, Adipic Acid, Natural Apple Flavor, Black Carrot Extract, Curcumin, Spirulina Extract for Color, Maple Syrup, Chili Pepper." That's a LOT of ingredients on the package that aren't on the list provided on the product page and it seems, given that ingredients lists are typically in the order of prominence, that the most prominent ingredient, per the product page list, is ginger, which it clearly is not as each serving contains 2 mg of ginger but 5 grams of added sugars.

I can't find any reference to anything in here that is organic, other than the listing on the product page proclaiming "Organic AVC Gummies". As someone who typically buys organic whenever given the choice, I'm used to seeing (a) an ingredients list that shows what is organic and (b) a license logo from whoever is certifying the product or its ingredients are organic; both are lacking here.

The fact that the ingredients list on the product page and on the package do not match is of significant concern to me.

As to the product itself, the odor of vinegar is much more prominent here than with other AVC gummies that I've used. While the heavy sugar keeps the vinegar from being too strong, the taste is still there and the gummies themselves are much more grainy than any of the other AVC gummies I have used. While other gummies with the same amount of sugar seem to be more candy-like to me, these are not as easy to chew and swallow.

I'm also confused by the need to take 2 gummies to get one serving; the amount of sugar in each serving is 5 grams and the amount of ACV is 10% of that, meaning if they simply cut the sugar by 10%, the full amount of AVC could get ONE gummy. Perhaps they need the two gummies to split up the vinegar flavor, but the amount of sugar strikes me as very high.

After the issue with the ingredients listing, that is that what is on the package differs materially from the product listing, I have little faith in this product.

title: Wow!  This is PERFECT for travel / weekend trips - 2 packs would be good for eiither 3 or 6 days.
text:
Wow. I'm a transplant recipient coming up on 10 years later this spring.

When I came home from the hospital it was with a GIANT pillbox for a week that was divided into 4 sections per day, and each section had from several to a dozen pills.

Thankfully, things have slowed down and now I'm at taking pills twice a day, and I typically divide them into medicine in one container and supplements in another. My pills/supplements are 18 pills in the morning and 12 at night. I typically split them up into one box each week for medicine and one for supplements.

Thus, this set of two pillboxes is good for me for 3 days of meds, exactly what I need for my travel as I never like a business trip to be longer than that. I use one box for my meds and one for supplements so breaking my pills into AM and PM in each box, that's 3 days of meds.

Each box contains six compartments. The pillbox in place securely to the exterior plastic case, ensuring that the latches inside will not open. The top of the pillbox comes off so it is easy to "load" pills into each box. Each compartment locks solidly in place. Both outside containers are white, with one clear pillbox and one black.

I have zero concern about the boxes opening when they are in my backpack for travel, which is ALWAYS an issue for my regular weekly pillboxes.

title: Works well but required research to make sure I was using correctly
text:
