title: Works with elongated and round toilets and with my bidet installed on an elognated toilet!
text:
My doctor recommended that I use a sitz bath regularly following a medical issue, and I've used the "standard" hard plastic one I purchased at my local medical supply store. The problem I had with that one is that it simply does not fit on an elongated seat, meaning that I'm relegated to one of the many bathrooms in the house to use it.

I saw this listing and decided to give it a try since the page indicated it would work on either type of toilet seat. Not only does it fit on both the elongated and round toilets, but also fits fine on the elongated toilets on which I have installed large bidet attachments!

The sitz bath itself is very nice - it is softer plastic than the one I'd been using. At first, I didn't get the collapsible portion of the bath as I couldn't figure out what purpose it serves. Now that I've used it for a while I remain confused about WHY this is needed - it changes the depth a bit, so it might be easier to fit in a suitcase, but who's traveling with a sitz bath? I guess maybe it makes storage a bit easier, but since mine is used on a daily basis, I'm not collapsing it to store.

The bath itself is a bit wider than the one it is replacing and, thanks to the collapsible portion, a bit deeper as well. Overall, this is a simple product that functions well. I am happy with it.

title: The best thing about them is also the worst - if you remove the sticker they'll stay put in your shoes but can't use in others.
text:
These are soft gels that give some relief to heel pain due to heel spurs. They fit my shoes reasonably well (my size is larger than the recommended size, so that's on me and I did not deduct for that), but their biggest asset is also their biggest detriment.

They come with a sticker on the bottom of the cups. If you don't take the sticker off, they move around in your shoes. If you take the sticker off, the bottom of the cups have a stick substance on them (it seems like the stuff that was on the toys that you'd throw at the wall and watch them slowly crawl down the wall). When the sticker is removed and the sticky stuff hits your shoe, they stay in place very well, which is GREAT. The downside is that if you remove them to put in a different pair of shoes, they will lose their stickiness and not stay well in any of your shoes.

My advice is to put them in one pair of shoes and leave them there. The problem is that this can become expensive if, like me, you want them in all your shoes.

title: Pressure point therapy in a quick and easy format
text:
The first part of The Pressure Point Therapy Kit: The Complete Do-It-Yourself (at Home Treatment Manual) is a pretty comprehensive resource about Pressure Point Therapy and goes through its history, how it works, your wellness, techniques, uses, and tips for application. The remainder goes into the various pressure point to help various ailments with pretty good diagrams. The book also comes with a smaller and somewhat condensed version of the larger book as a sort of handy quick guide. The author has a well-founded background in the ways that conditions and reliefs actually work. If you are already a believer in acupressure, then this is a nice instruction manual. If you are not aware of its uses and applications, the beginning explanation is probably about as good of a concise primer on the subject as can be given. There are probably a lot of larger books that cover the subject, but sometimes just getting to the meat of a subject is all that is necessary to begin a treatment program correctly. It is a somewhat expensive book for the number of pages, but I am a firm believer in quality over quantity, so the fact that relevant info can be imparted in the pages given is more important than lots of pages of useless ramblings and regurgitation of prior studies.
Treatments covered include back and hip, low energy, neck, mid-upper back, lungs, hand, wrist, elbows, sinuses, TMJ, hormonal conditions, digestive problems, shoulder pain, knee pain, and cold and flu symptoms. A look at alternative methods of treatments not usually employed by the Western medical establishment is always a viable option that should be considered.

title: Probiotics!!! They work!

Re: the selling feature that they are a "women's" probiotic is probably just that... a selling tool. title: Useful on more than just appliances
text:
We have a brushed stainless steel refrigerator and have tried a couple of stainless cleaners but were unfailingly displeased with the results - fingerprints cleaned off but oodles and oodles of streaks left, always. We have 4 kids under 12 so our appliances, especially the refrigerator, have layers of fingerprints. Apprehensively, I followed the instructions and sprayed it on a cloth, wiped it on the fridge and buffed it off - with pleasing results! There were some streaks left to be buffed out, but not as many as other products tried. While not ecstatic, I decided to continue using the product.

A few Saturdays later, I came across the cleaner again while digging through products for my least favorite chore, the bathroom. I recalled our faucets are shiny stainless steel and we have some exposed pipes that get pretty gnarly looking, so I and grabbed the bottle. I sprayed it on a rag, rubbed the stainless and was astonished! I could see my reflection perfectly in the shining faucet! I used it all over the bathroom and soon every faucet and pipe shone as never before! I was ecstatic and will use this product from now on.

Summary: 4 of 5 for brushed steel appliances and 5 out of 5 for shiny stainless steel.

title: Wow. 3000mAh battery. Up to 6 hours operating time. Quality design and materials.
text:
This device is a nice upgrade for anf abdominal/lower back/menstrual heating pad. It contains graphene technology for quick and uniform heating (heating and infrared therapy), offering three temperature settings (104ªF - 140ºF). The three temperature settings are indicated by corresponding color lights: Green = Low Setting, Blue = Medium Setting and Red = High Setting. These indicators are found on the battery, which is an integral accessory for the heating pad. It controls the power on/off and access to the three temperature settings.
The battery bank has one button, a series of indicator lights and a port for the pad’s plug. The battery is the only means to powering and controlling the warming pad. So, don't lose it, and you can't replace the power bank with a spare USB power bank. Operation is simple, easy. Theres a power button that cycles through the three temperature settings. As mentioned earlier, the single temperature indicator will change colors respective to the heat level.
Also displayed on the battery bank is the battery status indicator lights: Flashing (0 - 10%), Low (10 - 35%), Mid (35 - 70%), High (70 - 100%). These setting are indicated via the three blue lights (0/blinking lights, and 1 - 3 steady lights for the four instances).
The use of graphene allows for a relatively thin heating pad. This enables a lightweight device, that is conforming to the body’s curves. It fits comfortably, with excellent, consistent contact.
These are all noteworthy features. However, the highlight component is the battery capacity. The battery capacity is rated at 3000mAh. Indeed, to my knowledge, it is the highest capacity battery for the product genre. This generous capacity provides up to 6 hours of operating time. According to the manual, it takes 3 - 4 hours to fully charge a depleted battery.
At the current cost of $28, it seems very reasonably priced, especially considering the battery specs. Factoring in the various features and quality of design, materials and construction, it’s a very good value.
The significant other gives this device a strong favorable nod. Thus, based on these initial impressions, it earns a well deserved 4.5+ star rating, with a high level recommendation.

title: Decent quality/build. Wonky button backlights.
text:
This is a competent red light/near infrared light therapy device. The critical component is the pad that has the therapy LED bulbs embedded, and the controls. It's cogently designed, with clean, minimal aspects. This uncluttered manner also allows it to be easily set up and applied. It comes with various belts and a battery pouch with velcro elements. The top side of the therapy pad has a soft material that secures the velcro counterparts on the belts and pouch. So, it's just a matter of affixing the belt, using the velcro connections on the ends to hold the pad in place.
It comes with two cords, very short and a longer one. The short cable is intended to be used with a USB power bank (not included). As mentioned, there's a fabric pouch to hold the battery, with velcro to affix to the pad. Personally, use of a a usb battery pack is my preferred mode, allowing mobility.
Operation is fairly simple. Plug in the power cable. A long press of the power button powers it on/off. Pressing the M, Mode, button cycles through the four options. Each mode has a corresponding button backlight color. Red = Red Light, Blue = Near InfraRed Light, White = Red Light + Near InfraRed Light, Green = Red Light + Near InfraRed Light, pulsing. The button backlights did not illuminate the buttons properly, with only a noticeable coloring in one side of the M button (see attached photos). While this did not adversely affect operation or performance, it is annoying. And, it's an indication of lack of quality control.
Attached are photos to show real world images, with a series of images noting the button backlight colors per different modes.
Based on initial impressions, this device garners a 4 - 4.25 star rating.

title: Tastes pretty good. Mushroom tea for calming and relaxing.
text:

They're also noted for positively affecting immune systems and cognitive/neurological systems.
The significant other was dealing with taxes, and was obviously stressed out. Between dealing with clients and accountants/taxes, I could see she was more stressed than usual. So, I followed the directions and prepared a cup of this "Unwind" tea. I took a sip, and it has a nice taste, and I recognize the usual mushroom earthiness. But, it has more than a mushroom flavor. There's hints of Chamomile, Passion Flower and Peppermint. Overall, it has a very welcoming taste, and she said it's an enjoyable tea.
There's only 5 calories per serving, with 0g sugar and no added sugars. It uses organic monk fruit extract as the alternative sweetener. So, that's another positive for this product.
The contents of the packet dissolved nicely, and didn't leave any grit on the bottom of the mug. I did add some almond milk, which gave it more a smoothness (she likes her tea and coffee with almond milk). After the cup of this mushroom tea, she said she felt better and not as stressed out. And, said she'd like another one, after she finishes with her last appointment. So, it passes the taste test and seemed to calm her stressed out state.
Based on these initial impressions, this product earns a 4.75 star rating, with a high level recommendation.

title: Excellent sonic cleansing performance. Attractive design. Good value.
text:
I like the overall appearance of this sonic cleansing brush. It has a stylish minimal aesthetic, with easy handling and operation. Of note, it affords an exemplary sonic performance. When powered, even at the lowest setting, your skin can feel the brush head actually vibrating. This is perhaps the best sonic technology cleansing brush that I've encountered.
It comes with three different brush heads, which easily push on/pull off. Two of the brushes have fine nylon bristles, designated as soft and deep cleaning, with the third being a silicone bristle brush head. The brush heads are well made.
The device has three modes. According to the user manual: Level one is Daily Cleaning, Level two is Deep Cleaning, with the third level cycling between the two modes. The user manual does not give specifications for each level. (The product details mentions the two levels as being 9600rpm and 7200rpm.)
The user manual is very brief, with sparse details, specifications. Besides the lack of details regarding the power levels, there is no information on the battery capacity. It does note that it takes 3 hours to charge the battery. And, that it can be used for two months. That's a very vague, ambiguous specification for operating time.
Also, no definitive detail on the waterproof rating. They claim it's waterproof, but clearly mention not to 'soak' the device under water. So, I doubt that it's rated IPX7, which would be true waterproofing. At best, it's IPX6, which means that it's safe to wash/clean under a faucet. title: What a sonic brush should be. Excellent design. Excellent sonic power.
text:
This is one of the better powered facial brushes that I've used, including sonic, rotary or vibrating varieties. It has a nice sleek, minimalist design appearance. There's only one button, for very easy operation. The massage heads merely push on, and pull off, but they don't fall off when in operation. Perhaps the only design flaw is the piece of silicone that holds the cover for the charging port will sometimes interfere with standing it up on a counter. It's generally possible, but I feel it's not very stable. It's a minor issue, though.
Operation is a simple press of the power button, which lights up the ring around the button. Also, the top button lights up, indicating the first power level. Another press advances to the next power level, indicated by the bottom light coming on. Next press activates the third power level, with both lights alight. The next press will power it off.
I was actually surprised by the robust sonic cleansing effect of this brush. You actually feel the brush impacting the face. In fact, I had to take off the brush head to confirm that it wasn't rotating the brush. Prior to this device, I always felt that rotary brushes performed much better at cleansing the face, because I actually felt the brush moving on the face. I got this effect from this sonic cleansing brush.
There is no information regarding the battery capacity, other than the product details stating that it takes 3 hours to charge it, and it lasts 2 months (with the title explicitly stating "continuous use for 2 months"). I think the battery capacity and some semblance of operating time estimate should be provided, especially in the user manual. This absence dings the rating.
Additionally, they state that the device is 'waterproof', without disclosing the waterproof rating. I consider IPX7 to be waterproof, with lower ratings to be water-resistant. This information is also lacking in both the product details and user manual.
The user manual is very brief, with sparse information/specifications. This is the negative aspect of the product.
Overall, I do like this sonic cleansing brush, a lot. Attached are photos to show real world images of the sonic cleansing brush, with a ruler for size reference. Various angles, accessories and close ups are provided for a comprehensive overview of the product.
The missing information/specifications lowers the rating of an otherwise excellent product. It receives a 4.5+ star rating, with a high level recommendation.

title: Quality silicone brush with massage settings and light therapy. Can't select a single light.
text:
This facial brush features quality silicone covering and bristles, with good vibrating massage speeds and a light therapy option. Also, quite appropriately, it is rated IPX7 waterproof. I view this level as being 'true' waterproof, since that rating is based upon no damage or water leakage when submerged up to a meter, for 30 minutes. So, it can be used in the shower or bath, which makes sense for a cleansing brush.
Operation is fairly simple, with one twist. A long press of the power button will activate the vibration massage. Then you can increase or decrease the speed using the respective + and - buttons. The twist comes into play when you want the phototherapy feature. A long press of the - button will engage that feature, and turn off the vibrating massage. If you want to include the massage aspect, merely press the + button to resume the massage (and then use the +/- buttons to achieve the desired massage speed).
The light cycles through it's color spectrum. I could not find a means to select or stop on any specific light color. It seems, you have to use the lighting rotation. Personally, I do not see the sense or value in that strict presentation for the phototherapy.
I like that it has it's own tray/base, which also acts as the wireless charging base. I would exercise caution, though, because the usb port is open/exposed. I would not want to get water in that opening. And definitley use caution if charging in a wet environment.
The silicone covering and bristles are top notch. The vibrating massage seems ample for cleansing and facial massage. The phototherapy is cute, but limited to the color rotation constantly cycling.
The product is a decent and able performer. I don't care for the control aspects involving phototherapy. I would prefer at least an option to select a specific light therapy. Based on these aspects, it receives a 4 - 4.25 star rating.

title: Premium level design and construction. Red Light and Near Infrared Light Wavelenghts.
text:
There seems to be more pen shaped devices offering red light therapy features. And, usually, their offerings are only in that specific red light wavelength spectrum. This product offers both Red Light Therapy and Near InfraRed Light Therapy, 660nm wavelength and 850nm wavelength respectively. The main difference between the two is the depth of penetration of the light therapy. Red Light deals more with aspects closer to the surface of the skin, while Near Infrared Light can affect deeper within the skin to more directly affect muscles and subcutaneous tissue.
Some assembly is required in this instance. The bottom section unscrews to reveal the battery compartment. They supply 1 rechargeable battery. In another clever design move, they made the top section removable, too. This reveals the usb-c charging port. There is a small indicator light near the charging port. While charging it glows red, and then green when fully charged. It takes 4 - 5 hours to fully charge a depleted battery. The defined treatment session is 10 minutes, after which the device will automatically power off. The user manual states that it can be operated up to 12 times on a single charge. So, basically 2 hours of expected operating time.
Besides the usual accessories (protective eyeglasses, drawstring pouch and usb power cable), they include a tripod with flexible legs and an adapter clamp to hold the light therapy pen. This is a smart and clever addition, which allows the user to position the device handsfree. This addition boosts the rating. It's an accessory that I never considered with our other light therapy 'pens'.

title: High Frequency Therapy Device (Neon/Orange). Facial/skin/hair rejuvenation.
text:
In case you're wondering what High Frequency Therapy actually is/does: "High frequency is traditionally referred to as "D'Arsonval high frequency" or the "Tesla current". In the 1970's, European salons discovered the cosmetic and healing benefits of high frequency electrical stimulation on the skin and by 1980, the the technology became widely used in North American by skin care professionals." "High-frequency treatments kill bacteria and reduce inflammation, hence the acne-fighting benefits. High-frequency also increases circulation to stimulate collagen, making the treatment an effective anti-aging and glow-boosting tool. Each electrode has a designated use whether for fighting acne (Argon) or stimulating anti-aging (Neon)." (various online sources)
Studies have shown that high frequency treatments for the skin and hair can boost healthy aspects, eliminating bacteria and enhancing circulation, collagen. You'll find two types of high frequency therapy devices: Argon, which will emit a purplish light and Neon, with an orange hue. "There are 2 types main types of gasses in High frequency wands- Argon and Neon. That is where the glow comes from. The argon gas is purple and is for acne, oily skin, ingrown hairs. The Neon is orange and it's for building collagen and helping with wrinkles."(online source) So, this product, with the Neon/orange light would act to rejuvenate the skin.
The current cost is $28.50, including the 5% discount coupon. When I mentioned the price, the significant other was surprised. She said that to get a high frequency treatment at a spa or skin clinic costs more than that. So, there is already value built into the product.
Operation is simple, easy. Merely push one of the four wands into the cavity receptacle at the top of the handle. Plug in the power plug into a normal AC outlet. There is one dial/knob at the base of the handle. Turning it clockwise powers it on, and as you turn it further, it increases the intensity with corresponding color intensity. Then you apply the functional aspects of the glass wand to the skin or hair. To turn it off, simply turn the knob counter-clockwise until it clicks at the end.
Attached are photos to show real world images of the high frequency therapy device, with a ruler for size reference. Various angles are provided for an overview of the product, including a photo of one wand activated and glowing alit.

title: Decent quality IPL device. Abundant number of flashes. Needs better documentation.
text:
This is an excellent entrant in the IPL market genre. It follows an often used design form, that allows for comfortable handling and application. The operation is deceptively easy, just keep in mind that the light energy is powerful, so use it cautiously and wear the provided protective eyewear.
IPL is Intense Pulses of Light, that is a treatment primarily for 'permanent' hair removal, and also in certain scenarios for skin treatments. In this case, the product is designed for treating hair follicles with the eventual goal of permanent cessation of hair growth. "IPL treatment is administered through a handheld flashgun device that emits pulses of light, which are absorbed by the melanin pigment in hairs. The light turns to heat that is absorbed by the skin, resulting in damage to the follicle effectively removing hair and slowing down regrowth significantly."(online reference). After repeated treatment sessions, the regrowth cycles is disrupted to the point of no further hair renewal.
To be effective, the subject needs to qualify according to skin color and hair color. Basically, light skin color and darker hair color are the ideal combination. This is due to the intense light affecting melanin, the pigment. So, the contrast is necessary, and you want the light energy to affect hair pigmentation, and not skin, obviously.
Operation of this device is straightforward. Plug in the AC power adapter cord. A long press of the power button (with the power icon) will activate the IPL device. The fan will start, and you'll see the display showing the number of flashes remaining, the intensity level (default is set at lowest), fan icon. The display will also indicate if it's in auto or manual mode.
The user manual does a very poor job (actually non-existent) at explaining the manual mode. In this mode, the user actually triggers the flash. The significant other tells me that everyone uses the automatic mode because it's easier and faster. Anyway, the large button above the power button switches between automatic and manual mode.
In automatic mode, when you press the flash window on skin it will trigger the flash. Then you lift it and move it to the next, adjacent target. Lower the flash window, touching the skin, which automatically triggers the flash again. This process is continued until you cover the targeted hair region.
They warn against overlapping and missing areas. I wondered how a user can ensure that there is no overlap and avoid missing areas, when the flash window is not flush with an edge. This is not an issue specific to this product, but to IPL devices in general.
I like the overall presentation and quality of the product. Besides the IPL device, it includes a generic straight edge razor, protective eye wear, AC power adapter/cord and user manual. While the user manual is adequate, I feel it could have been better, more informative.
Based on initial impressions and observations, this is a very competent and capable IPL device. It is exactly as depicted and described in the product details. It earns a 4.5 - 4.75 star rating, with a high level recommendation.

title: Effective performance.  Good construction. 2 channel, 4 outputs.
text:
This is an upgraded version of the usual consumer level TENS/EMS device. It's a very capable device, able to deliver effective electrical signals to effect muscle and nerve stimulation. In fact, the levels of intensity are probably more than ample, with most users finding the lower levels more than adequate.
It seems that the primary upgrade is the addition of an output port for each channel. So, you can actually affix four sets of pads, 2 per both A and B channels, to either form an extensive treatment or to share a 'massage' session simultaneously. Keep in mind that each channel has a set output, and adding pads will share that intensity. So, you may find that you'll increase the intensity levels to accommodate the shared load. Then, if you opt to use just one set of pads per channel, you will need to adjust for that instance (so a lower intensity will feel the same, within your tolerance levels.
I have a slight issue with the two side buttons. It's very difficult to identify them using their markings. Fortunately, it's just two buttons. The top button is the power button, where a long press will turn it on/off. The lower button is the 'lock' button. So, if you get confused and long press the lower button to turn it on, you'll notice nothing happens. Then repeat the long press on the top button, and the display will light up, and you're ready to select your mode, timer and channel intensities.
Operation if fairly simple, especially if you've previously used a consumer TENS/EMS unit. The M button allows the user to select the massage mode. T button cycles at 10 minute increments the timer function (the default is 20 minutes, but you can cycle through and get a 10 minute option).
This device is well equipped with 24 modes and 20 intensity levels. However, the only specification provided regarding the battery is that it takes 2 - 3 hours to charge the battery. And, the product details states that it lasts 20 hours 'Standby Time". I have no idea what 'Standby Time" means, and at what manner of settings it includes. Perhaps, it's 20 hours of just being turned on? This lack of definitive battery capacity rating and operating time dings the rating.
This issue with the battery and operating time specifications is unfortunate. The product displays decent design, materials and manufacture. And the current cost of $32, including a 20% discount, makes it very reasonably priced for it's quality level in the product genre.
