title: Similar to Nuvana, but at double the cost
text: I've been consuming a whole food vitamin from Garden of Life called myKind Organics Men's Once Daily, and in recent months have been trying the competition, including Amazon Elements Organic Whole Food Men's Multi, Nuvana Multifood Whole Food Multivitamin, and the men's and women's varieties of True Grace One Daily 40+ Multivitamin. I've recently tried Truvani Organic Multivitamin, which has a serving size of 3 tablets, similar to the serving size of 3 capsules for Nuvana rather than the serving size of 1 or 2 tablets like the other products I've tried. While Truvani and Nuvana provide different volumes of vitamins and minerals, however, Truvani generally provides less of each. The most drastic example of this is for zinc, of which Nuvana provides 15mg and Truvani provides only 1mg. But is this really a factor of 15 difference? I'm not sure, because the zinc provided by Nuvana is sourced from Saccharomyces cerevisiae, a unicellular fungus, whereas the zinc provided by Truvani is source from an "organic food blend" of 12 ingredients. Another interesting difference in the supplement facts of these two products is the volume of vitamin A provided per serving: Nuvana provides "1500mcg RAE", and Truvani provides 375mcg. So what is "RAE" intended to mean? Before I looked up this term, I did some math using the "DV" (daily value) provided on the label for each. The 1500mcg RAE of Nuvana provides 170% DV, meaning 100% DV is 882mcg, and the 375mcg of Truvani provides 42% DV, meaning 100% is 893mcg. I've noticed in the past that daily values of many supplements aren't standardized, so I've gotten in the habit of ignoring most of this labeling, but in this case I was trying to derive what "RAE" might mean. In this case, it appears there are just some rounding errors, most likely due to what Nuvana claims, but the volumes are virtually identical. From some light research, it looks like "RAE" means "retinol activity equivalents", and generally speaking, this term can be ignored. The RDA ("recommended daily allowance" of vitamin A is reported as RAE to account for the different bioactivities of retinol and provitamin A carotenoids, both of which are converted by the body into retinol. Provitamin A cartenoids are plant pigments that the body converts into vitamin A in the intestine. Now, unlike Nuvana, which doesn't state the type of B12 it provides, Truvani explicitly states that it provides "methylcobalamin" (methyl B12), but unless you have the MTHFR gene mutation, you shouldn't be taking methyl B12. That said, the 12mcg of methyl B12 provided by Truvani is such a trivial amount that it's largely irrelevant: I personally take 3000mcg on a daily basis apart from my daily multivitamins. Combined with the significantly more expensive pricing of Truvani considering serving size and quantity of tablets provided in each bottle, Nuvana and Garden of Life seem to have the edge. I'm still on my journey to better understand the differences between synthetic "isolate" vitamins versus whole food vitamins, but the sudden unavailability of Twinlab Daily One Caps multivitamin I had been taking up until several years ago actually worked out in my favor because it caused me to start taking a closer look at supplement facts.

title: Nonstandard D3 dosage & doesn't provide K2
text: I've tried many D3 and D3+K2 supplements in the past couple years, especially the latter, because I've discovered that it's likely better to take D3 along with K2 due to its promotion of K2-dependent proteins that require K2 to function properly (research is ongoing). While I'm not personally concerned about lack of calcium intake, some competing products include it because D3 and K2 help ensure that it's properly deposited in bones. To compensate for this lack of K2, I had been consuming separate products, such as Complete K from a Norwegian label called Supersmart, which provides both K1 and K2. The math to determine the appropriate ratio of D3:K2 is simple, but it's convenient to consume both from the same product. The standard dosage of D3 is 125mcg (5000 IU), and the standard dosage of K2 is 100mcg. Apart from the absence of K2, the only thing I don't like about this Go Healthy product is 125mcg not being evenly divisible by the 50mcg provided by each tablet. You would need to either break down some tablets in half to provide incremental 25mcg (1000 IU) dosages, or consume a minimum of 5 tablets so that the total of 250mcg is evenly divisible by 125mcg, but this would lead to a 10000 IU megadose you likely won't want to consume on a daily basis. While I have an usually strong immune system relative to other people (other people have expressed anger at me that I don't get sick when I'm surrounded by sick people), I know when I feel even a slight tinge of illness that I need to grab the Colostrum, Vitamin D3+K2, and Vitamin C in order to prevent too much negative impact. I also grab this combination of supplements when I feel especially tired due to a string of long work days, because I know I'm more vulnerable to illness. Don't pay attention to physicians who state that megadoses of D3 shouldn't be taken (some physicians think that the standard 125mcg dosage of D3 is already megadose status). While you should always know your specific body before taking megadoses, physicians generally don't know what they're talking about because the vast majority of them don't understand supplements, generally depending on pharmaceutical companies to train them to prescribe only patented medications. All of this said, I've had a good experience with Go Healthy whole food supplements so far, including the multivitamins it offers for men and women (there are very few differences between these two products). I'm still on my journey to better understand the differences between synthetic "isolate" vitamins versus whole food vitamins, but the sudden unavailability of Twinlab Daily One Caps multivitamin I had been taking up until several years ago actually worked out in my favor because it caused me to start taking a closer look at supplement facts. The D3 provided by this product is sourced solely from organic algae.

title: Good value, but with ingredient discrepancies
text: It's been a few months since I last reviewed an omega 3 fish oil supplement, after having experimented with a variety of brands the past couple years, and this one from Dr Tobias probably provides the most value of the ones I've recently tried. In prior years, I had been a loyal customer of Nordic Naturals Ultimate Omega, and this product from Dr Tobias is a reminder of the existence of many quality alternatives with better price points. A lot of different opinions exist as to how much and at what ratio EPA and DHA should be consumed daily, so fish oil supplements are typically differentiated by these attributes, as well as the types of fish used and how these are processed. The aforementioned Nordic Naturals product uses a 1.44:1 EPA to DHA ratio, and contains other Omega-3s not providing either of these, and this product from Dr Tobias a 1.33:1 EPA to DHA ratio. The product description here discloses the type of fish used as "100% fresh, wild-caught fish", later elaborating that this fish is "herring, anchovy, sardine, salmon and mackerel", but this isn't what the packaging discloses, simply stating that this product "contains fish (anchovies)". Interesting discrepancies, and the only reason I'm rating this product four rather than five stars.

title: Light cooking alternative, but not worth markup
text: This product is the third MCT (medium-chain triglycerides) oil product I've tried out in recent months. While some debate exists as to whether cooking with extra virgin olive oil is a healthy choice, I've used it for many years because it's healthy relative to many of the other available choices, and has a pleasant taste. At least, I personally find it to have a pleasant taste for most foods I typically cook. In recent years, I've also periodically made use of coconut oil, around which debate also exists, but unlike extra virgin olive oil all of the coconut oil products I've seen come in either sprays or solid form, and one of the main reasons I became interested in MCT oil is its being available in liquid form. I've used this Strength Genesis product several times in recent days after trying a similar product from QSTA in recent months, and am fond of both because these provide a very light relative to extra virgin olive oil to the point of having zero taste. The main challenge I've found cooking with these oils is that a non-stick surface isn't created as it is with extra virgin olive oil, although this Strength Genesis product provides a slightly better cooking surface than QSTA. So when making a turkey burger, for example, I need to remind myself to flip frequently, and when making over-easy eggs it's guaranteed that I will end up scraping the pan. The main differences between this Strength Genesis and QSTA is that the former is 60% C8 and 40% C10 in contrast to 100% C10, but the latter also comes at a 50% cost discount. Some might be interested in knowing that a portion of the labeling not provided in the product description here states that this product is a "product of Sri Lanka".

Leaving two stars because the idea of compostable, zero waste floss is cool, but not at the risk of my oral health.

I am addicted to flossing. I floss every single day, with few exceptions. Over the years I have tried many different kinds of floss, and this one is hands down my favorite. It’s thick and textured enough to clean between my teeth better than regular floss, but it’s waxed and can glide through the tighter spaces with zero problems. It doesn’t shred, it doesn’t break, it cleans better than other floss, and it can go straight into the compost bin when I’m done. I love this floss.

The only drawback is that I go through floss pretty quickly, and you get a lot less floss for a lot more money with this stuff. However, both this product and the refills are cheaper on the manufacturer’s website than they are on Amazon. I will be ordering refills directly from Dental Lace. title: Basic but functional with some annoying design decisions
text:
"White Noise Machine Afloia with Breathing Night Light for Sleeping, Sound Machine for Baby and Adult..."

This device accomplishes its primary function, but it's held back by a few strange design choices.

The sound loops are short, and there's an audible sound artifact in the splice between loops on at least some of the tracks. (The join sounds like a distant bird chirp.) It's not really very annoying, but it does come around every 90 seconds.

The speaker quality is so-so. I've definitely heard better from other devices in a similar price range. It can be set fairly loud if you want but stops short of what would be dangerous for young ears I think.

To select the noise loop, you just turn the front knob, and an associated light signals the selected loop. Unfortunately, the loops aren't visually marked on the machine otherwise, so unless you memorize where each loop is, it's kind of meaningless.

Most annoying is that even though you can charge this while using it, the very dumb decision to put the charging port on the bottom of the unit means that you have to flip the machine over onto its back to charge it while using it. This particular design decision is really dumb. Also, the included cable is white but the unit is black, which just looks odd.

I wouldn't recommend this device, but it does work as promised, in a basic, minimal way, which is why I think it deserves two stars.

title: Capable task lamp with two levels of output on a flexible gooseneck
text:
I have been a Verilux user for a long time and thanks to the Amazon Vine program I was able to add this floor lamp to my office very recently. Perhaps because this is not my first, I do not have any problem putting the lamp together. Frankly the amount of work is just average for an assembly-required lamp (try some of the IKEA creations...)

Hardware-wise, the lamp is solidly constructed. The gooseneck gives flexible lamp placement, and the floor stand is sturdy and heavy enough to give you confidence. Overall, it's a high quality item and can easily fit in even for a semi-formal office environment like mine.

The most important part of this lamp, of course, is the light quality of the bulb. Verilux has been in this "natural spectrum" business for very long and they are reputable. Whether their bulbs are "full spectrum" (like natural sunlight) or not is a well-researched topic on the web. I would say that if you like white light, this should not disappoint as long as you understand that this is a task lamp. In other words, the light is focused on a small area and you really need to find another light source for the ambience to reduce the contrast between the lighted area and the environment. (Otherwise, think of the eye strain of staring at a computer monitor in a completely dark room.)

However, given the falling price of cooler LED lamps that are also capable of giving out white light (but perhaps very different spectrum), the heat of the Verilux bulb should not be neglected. I live in the North East and frankly I would not want to get my head too close to this lamp during the summer. YMMV.

title: Good Size Pill Dispenser
text:
I've taken prescribed medication, and carried medication to address acute problems, since high school, and for a while I traveled weekly by plane. So the search for the ideal pill dispenser has been an on-going effort for me.

I like the pill cutter. You're fully protected from the cutter by the plastic design. It cuts pills easily. And it's safely separate from the pill dispensers. If I'm placing too much focus on this, it's because I managed to cut my hand opening an odd-size pill dispenser - odd size because it had the pill cutter inside. I like this one - it's safer.

The two pill dispensers come in two different shades - so you can do the morning in one, evening in another, or prescription in one, vitamins in another, or use just one - but you can tell the dispensers apart, which is a nice benefit. Each pill container closes with a satisfying, and secure, snap.

Each dispenser has seven labelled days, and holds a large number of pills - and not all dispensers achieve these basics, so I view this as a huge plus.

You can't, however, load all pill containers at once. That pretty daisy design makes the lids crash into each other, so you can't have them all open at the same time. If you've got more than two medications to drop into each day of the week, the process of working around the lids is pretty tedious. You can remove all the lids, but replacing them requires pressure, which can cause pills to jump days - which, if you have a lot of meds, is hard to spot. The design there could have been better.

Nice size, nice colors - hard to lose in your luggage - but loading them up every week seems a little daunting.

title: Nope, NOT Designed for Short Hair
text:
I have hair with lots of body, which translates to incredibly rebellious hair that does whatever it wants unless confronted by a professional. Right now, it's short, which means often pieces stick out in the oddest and most annoying way. I have a curling/straightening iron, but it's designed for longer hair. So when I saw this, I was pretty excited - finally, I can get those obnoxious pieces under control.

I was relying on that manufacturer's statement " Q: Will this work for short hair?

A: Yes! Our product is designed to be used on all hair types and all hair length. So It does work perfectly on short hair! "

Well, OK, maybe on someone who has hair longer than three inches from their head. You have to run the heated comb/brush through your hair for it to work. The head of the comb/brush is 1.75" wide (almost 2 inches at the widest point); the "tines," which I assume are designed so as to avoid burns, are an inch deep and unbending.

You have to hold your hair ("and tighten it from the roots" according to the instructions) while running the heated comb/brush through your hair to straighten. This means your hand needs a portion to grasp in addition to the area required to actively comb/brush. With short hair, if you've got, say, 2-3 inches of hair growing from your head thanks to expensive maintenance, that means you've got the comb/brush, your hand, and you're done - no room to actually perform any action.

All credit for having instructions included, a lovely box in which the product was packaged - but I'm really taken aback that the manufacturer would think this product would work with short hair given the size. It may be awesome for long hair (which would have been in 1999, I think, for me) - but I cannot say it works for short hair. At all.

title: Amazing Results
text:
I didn't take a photo, because I was too embarrassed. I'm sorry now I didn't; I should have. I do have the after photo.

I live in the Southern U.S., and I made the mistake of leaving a vintage leather holster in the open air at the top of my master bedroom closet. That closet is one hall from the master bath (think daily shower mist), and has one outdoor wall (think summer humidity). I'm sure at some point I planned to put that holster in a box, but I never did. Out of sight, blissfully out of mind.

Fast forward to 2? 4? years later, a massive closet cleaning, and I find the holster, covered with green stuff. It was gross. Ugh. Well, OK, I'm up for a challenge. On go the rubber gloves. I get some pieces of old bedsheet, and this product. Honestly, I wasn't even sure this product could "clean" - the can isn't exactly covered with instructions - but it was use this product, or toss the holster in the trash can, and I was willing to try (and the vendor says here on the site it does clean, hooray).

And it worked. Not just on the smooth leather, but also on the suede. It was a MIRACLE. I used circular motions, plenty of product on the bedsheet, and the awful looking green stuff is gone - that holster looks as nice as when my grandfather wore it. Nicer, actually.

Hopefully I'll find some box to put it in before I start the whole cycle again. But: for cleaning old leather, it was AMAZING. Haven't used it on anything that wasn't a complete disaster, yet, but if it can take on a 70-year old holster with mold, I'm sure it can cope with a pair of shoes, belt, harness, or jacket. Top notch product. Smelled good, too.

title: Amazing, Moisturizing Product
text:
My "toner" has generally been either a swipe of the latest trial product, or my college favorite of 30 years, which unfortunately contains alcohol but definitely leaves my skin feeling clean and fresh.

The Bio-Hydra Panthenol Toner is a nice combination of those two, minus the toxic alcohol. It feels almost like a serum, rather than a toner, and leaves my skin feeling moist, which is great first thing in the morning. My skin absorbed it quickly and I didn't have the feeling of any sticky residue or tackiness. What I did have was a smooth texture and (here's the best part) no fragrance.

Like 95% of chronic migraine sufferers, I have a hyper-sensitive sense of smell, so any manufactured scent on my face is just not an option - I get instant nausea and migraine. "Scented" lipstick or face creams are the worst. (It wasn't always this way - I used to love perfume, and I still love the smell of creams my aunt used, but I can't wear them). So if something has essential oils, or best case, no fragrance at all, that's a bonus for me.

I also felt comfortable using this product under makeup - I generally hate layering product if I can avoid it - it just feels like I'm slathering on some sort of cement mix, but this is so light, and absorbing, I didn't get that feeling at all. A really impressive product, and a nice price as well.

title: Stops Itch & Swelling...but Scented.
text:
Just about every insect that bites finds me attractive. Habitual biters like mosquitoes, fleas, ticks and chiggers; occasional biters like ants, horse flies, spider wasps (the worst!) and spiders - they've all found me apparently tasty and visited me more than once.

My big issue with these bites is the subsequent itch - apparently I scratch even in my sleep and make the whole experience as long lasting as possible. As a child, people would approach my family asking what was wrong with this poor spotty child. And even now I have a fire ant bite that has itched like, well, fire, for over two weeks.

So I was excited to find this product, and excited to try it. And I'm surprised to say it works! Actually reduces puffiness and redness, and wonder of wonder, stops the itch. I would have forgotten I had the bite entirely if it weren't for the unfortunate (to me) scent of the product. Because the product does have a distinct scent.

The ingredients of the product are Echinacea 30C (coneflower), Apple Cider Vinegar, Bentonite Clay, Coneflower, Lemongrass Essential Oil, Alcohol. That Lemongrass scent is quite strong.

Like 1Billion people (in 2021), of whom 3:1 are women, I suffer from chronic migraine headaches, and like 95% of those, I have a hyper-sensitive sense of smell. Normally essential oils are great, in fact, peppermint and eucalyptus are used to ease migraines, but lemongrass is one of my triggers. I'm lucky that my bites are generally on my legs; provided I use this carefully, I hope to continue using this working (again, seriously amazing) product.

And, perhaps at some point the manufacturer will make an unscented version so I can use it liberally as I need to.

text:
These aren't very good. The texture is what you would expect of a Clif Bar. That's the not quite cooked, chewier than you'd expect brownie texture. If you've had a Clif Bar, and you don't mind that, then don't worry about it. The thing here is the flavor.

This isn't for coffee lovers. And it's certainly not for espresso lovers. This is for the long-distance biker or runner who needs energy on the fly or right after a workout. They will tolerate the taste (maybe). Nobody else will.

Imagine the worst coffee you've ever had. Maybe it was at a gas station on I-80 near Joliet. You know, the kind that's been sitting there for a few too many hours. It wasn't good when it started and it didn't get better. The Clif Bars here aren't this good.

The coffee flavor is stale and overcooked. I think they used real coffee. But they didn't use the good stuff. And they didn't use the mediocre stuff. They went much deeper in the barrel for this stuff.

As you can imagine, I'm not at all thrilled with these. I don't recommend you buy them. And I don't recommend you accept them when your friends offer them to you. They're that bad.

--Brockeim

I keep these handy Green Bay Packers Ziplocs in my car. I fill them with trash. Orange peels. Used Kleenex. Stinky, gross stuff. I zip them tight and the stink stays in. Then, when I toss them out, that green and yellow logo shines bright in the garbage, right where it belongs.

I get that if you count up their record against each other, GB is ahead 96–94–6 through November 12, 2017 (their last meeting as of this writing). That's practically a tie, but OK. Today, it is GB. Remember, we had the class of Walter "Sweetness" Payton, and they had Charles "Too Mean" Martin.

If you are a Packers fan and want to keep your delicates stored in these bags, fine. They'll keep your rose petals, marshmallows, and cat treats as long as can be.

--Brockeim

title: Sticks arrived broken, but they do seem to alleviate drain odors
text:
First, I don't understand how these slender, breakable sticks can last long enough to alleviate the odors of bathroom sink and shower drains, but I've resigned myself to not understanding how most things work.

My goal is to figure out what's causing the odor and work to remediate it. Um, no, we made no progress with that. We use snakes to clear out hair and soap scum, but we have an odd odor of sulphur in one bathroom sink. That seems to have lessened, now that The Man of the House inserted one of these sticks.

The four fragrances seem to vanish once the sticks are in the sink/drain. So they're not "masking" other odors, right? They're actually **working** in other ways: "with just one stick per month" keep your drains clear and odor-free - the stick "stays in the pipe trap to prevent grease or other organic materials from building up" and should "prevent clogged sinks." It's going on a month now, and the slow-draining sinks do seem to run faster now.

I can't say that I "enjoy the smell of fresh bio clean natural fragrance" because I don't smell it at all, and I'm usually the first to detect any new odors in our environment.

"Save time on plumbers and drain snakes as powerful enzymes break down oil and grease to keep drains free and clear." So far, so good. Now to remember to replace these in all the sinks every month. :)

title: Decent enough device with a long list of small flaws
text:
[[VIDEOID:c65b8608abb4071a3a2aa04d5611125d]] TL/DR: This blood pressure monitor does the job, but there are a bunch of little things that need to be changed to make it a five star device.

Pros:
o Very nice display
o Audio readout of results
o Large cuff is *really* large, should fit anyone
o Tote sack

Cons:
o Device forgets time and date if using USB instead of batteries
o Changing users requires entering setup mode
o Memory display does not show date and time.
o Limited to two users
o Can't delete individual readings
o Green/Yellow/Red values don't adjust to age of user
o Time of day only uses 24 hour mode
o Audible output is intrusive when reviewing old readings

My video review for this machine is longer than normal, which is sadly because I found a bunch of things on this machine that are just not quite right.

First, let's get one thing out of the way. It looks like it does a decent job of checking your blood pressure. So it is performing the basic function you bought it for, and that's good. It seems to be consistent in its readings, and when compared to the readings of a name brand unit, it looks like they are in agreement.

One of the nice things about this machine is that it can operate off USB power, so you don't need to always be changing batteries. However, if you don't have batteries installed, it loses all its settings after a few minutes of disconnected time. So in fact, you have to have good batteries in the unit at all times. And since the time and date are not visible on the display, you won't actually know if your batteries are dead or not.

It's really nice to be able to keep track of your readings over time. This unit has a time and date function, so it's kind of puzzling that it doesn't show them when reviewing past readings. Instead, all I get is a number, starting at 1, indicating which reading I am seeing. Not helpful! I need to know the date I took the reading.

And it would also be helpful to be able to delete readings - you might take more than one in a sitting, and you want to only keep the middle reading, but there's no way to delete individual readings.

Having audible readouts of your blood pressure is modestly useful, but the recorded voice has a very strong accent, which is not necessarily great for the US market - a native speaker would have been a lot better. The audible indicator is actually more trouble than it's worth when you are reviewing readings, it starts speaking every reading as you review them, making for a very intrusive experience.

The device supports two users, (and really, is there some reason why it can't be more?), but instead of making it easy to switch between user 1 and user 2, you have to go into setup mode.

To earn five stars on a product you really need better execution than we see here. This unit is okay, but using it will not be free of aggravation, and that's a shame.

I put in a lot of effort to try to help you learn the most important facts about the product. Good luck with your decision, and if you do decide to buy the product, I hope the things you find in this review make it easier to use.

title: The Cadillac of Grabber Tools?
text:
[[VIDEOID:1e3a6843fbf148f24ba0625876c52d8a]] So the basic grabber tool can be found in many variations for a low price. But if you are going to get a grabber tool, and you know the price is low, why not get a nice one? This one is a really great version of the classic tool.

This tool comes in a nifty drawstring bag, and probably its best feature is that it breaks down in two so it can be stashed away in half the space. It locks up nicely when you close it, and when opened it has a secure latch to keep it that way.

The rubberized grabbers and the comfortable pistol grip combine to make this easy to use, and quite capable of gripping just about anything.

I don't use a grabber on a regular basis, but I can honestly say there is one time I need it when it is indispensable: when I drop something behind my dryer. When a sock goes down there, you'd have to have arms the length of Manute Bol to grab it off the floor. You can move the dryer but that's a lot of work, so the grabber comes to the rescue. Other than that, I keep it with my emergency kit, patiently waiting for a hurricane, tornado, or earthquake when I'll use the grabber to get things out of the pile of debris. (No this is not a joke, I have a *very* well-stocked emergency kit.)

title: Decent bath sponges, not great!
text: Since moving from Europe to the US, I have had a hard time procuring bath sponges for my family. Such a basic item in Europe, seems to be a "novelty" in US. I have tried many of the brands/options on Amazon, most from Europe anyway, with very poor results. This set of three sponges is not bad, given the relative low price. Sure, the exfoliating layer is just a bit more firm than the sponge itself, but it is abrasive enough to provide some additional scrubbing power.  Sure, the scrubbing layer will start shrinking and separating from the sponge itself after a month or so of daily use, but it will take a while before making the sponge unusable. In my experience, most of the other sponges on the market do disintegrate or rip in pieces after a few months of use, but not this sponge. So far the sponge itself is holding up well,maybe because of the extra thickness of the material and density. The tight alveolar structure provides probably more strength, but makes the sponge less fluffy and foamy. I have absolutely no use for the attached string and I removed it as I opened the package.

title: A good selection of bath bombs. Content could have to be packaged better. Giftable

The spheres, the macaroons and the heart are individually packaged. The red roses are not, but are beautiful decorations within the package. Because the roses are so delicate and the balls are pretty heavy, they got a little smashed during transportation, which was a pity. There is nothing in the package preventing the various items to move around and bang on each other. The heart bomb also got a little damaged because of this.
The box is nice, but if I had to give this away as a gift, I would transfer the content in something that is a little less cardboard-y. There are so many things in the box that you could even think of making 2 presents and still have a nice presentation.
I like the smell quite a bit as well, but I still have to try the bombs in a bath.

title: You get exactly what you see in the Ad. If you like it go for it.
text:

It's a set of rainbow colored small boxes, one for each day of the week, kept together by a hard plastic base. Each box fits about 4-5 gummy bears and has a single compartment. Therefore you can't organize your pills based on time of day (morning/evening) or differentiate among pills if they look similar and they are not supposed to be taken at the same time. However you get 2 sets of boxes so you could use both for the purpose of not mixing up pills.
You also get a bonus container that I guess can be used for travel (you could use the colored boxes for travel too), which has a blade to split pills when only half dose should be taken at one time.
The only drawback is can think off is that the boxes are made of plastic and the lid might come off eventually as the plastic that keeps it attached to the rest of the body gets consumed by the daily opening and closing. But that's just the nature of the product.
If you like the aesthetic go for it, what you see is what you'll get. Please refer to pictures for dimensions against an adult female hand.

title: Heavy Hair Dryer - can only use one function at a time, settings didn't do much
text:
[[VIDEOID:f310037fe9f7e4560202c12cd59831bd]] The order comes with one ionic hair dryer. The hair dryer is in black and gold color. There are three (3) different type of attachments that you can snap onto the device. The attachments are to be used for different uses. There is a wide-tooth comb, diffuser, and styling concentrator.

The hair dryer has a nice grip but it is pretty heavy. If you are using the hair dryer to dry long and thick hair like mine which takes a long time, it will start to weigh heavier over time. It comes with a black travel bag but I wouldn't take this hair dryer to travel with.

The hair dryer has two settings you can control for temperature and wind speed. There is a LED screen that shows what setting you are on (fan icon shows the wind speed and the degree shows the temperature). You control them but using the + or - button. However, you cannot use both functions at the same time. There is a set temperature if you are trying to control the wind speed and vice versa. I did not feel the temperature nor the wind speed change much even if I increased or decreased the settings, and the range is pretty big. I never had a good experience using it because it ends up taking forever compared to a normal and more afforable hair dryer I use. title: Light, lovely scent :)
text: Happy with this product! It's now the second rose water toner that I've acquired, so I can only compare it to that one other. However, what I've noticed is that while this product does not have as strong an initial smell as my other toner, it consistently smells like light, sweet roses when I spray it. My other toner product has this weird way of smelling strongly like roses right when it's sprayed, but that smell "decays" into smelling like wilted, old petals after a few seconds to a couple of minutes. I don't think that "bad" smell lasts, but I do often notice it with that other product. With this product, I have never noticed any smell other than the initial pretty smell of roses when it's sprayed. I love it because it's like perfume except a lot less strong and cloying, and the smell is so clean and pretty! I also feel like it makes my face feel soft when I spray it on -- and I have found that less is more! I compared this product in terms of price/size to other rose water toners on google "shopping" tab (including what they have at Whole Foods), and this product is nearly equivalent in both aspects to most other rose toners out there. Given I have gotten good results with this (both objectively, and compared to my other toner), I would recommend this product! I am very curious to go to Sephora and compare it to the gorgeous rose hibiscus toner spray that they sell for $32 from the brand Herbivore, and see whether this product lasts as long re: smell, and feels as refreshing. Tbd on that one.

title: Better than vibration style massagers! - Easy to use but hard to read
text:
Positives
-Easy to figure out without reading the manual
-It’s a shiatsu massage style (kneading/rolling) with air compression (inflated air pressure/squeezing). This is better than a vibration massager!
-3 intensity levels
-Relatively quiet
-The fabric liners are removable to wash and clean.
-Spacious for average sized feet: It fits up to size 12 men and 14 women.
-The massage feels nice and relaxing for the whole foot, toes included.
-There are non-slip rubbers at the bottom.

Potential Negatives/Neutrals
-Not easy to see the selections. Designer tries to make it sleek and minimalistic but harder to read instead.
-The buttons are flat and work like a touchscreen. Not a physical/tactile button to press down. I can imagine this being complicated for the visually impaired since it’s harder for them to navigate.
-The printed letters are not backlit. Just an observation, not a big deal to me.
-Heat is weak. Not toasty warm.
-Overall dimension of machine is quite big/bulky. Hard to store.
-The DC power adapter is kind of short. Approximately 6ft long. The cord is removable from the machine but it needs to be plugged into the wall outlet to operate. The plug-in port is on the right side of the massager.

Overall, my mother and I enjoyed the foot massage. It has potential to be better with some minor improvements.

title: Awesome for internal and external use! Mixing it well takes some practice, but once you get the hang of it, it works!
text:
I have been using store bought Hyaluronic products for many years, and while many of them work great, others just don't measure up. One day I was reading an article in a magazine about the benefits of using Hyaluronic Acid for homemade products, so I decided to give Micro Ingredients a try because I absolutely love their products. All I can say is WOW! I love this gooey, gelatin like stuff! I will admit, it is a pain in the rear end to mix. The first time I tried mixing it, it was an epic fail. I had to keep scraping spoon to spoon just to get it into the water so I could drink it. It wasn't really going over that well being added to liquids to drink so I started adding it to my yogurt on a daily basis. That worked out perfect! Not only did I not taste anything, it went down smoothly and I have not had any internal issues.

In terms of using it for beauty products, I have since learned that the measuring spoon used has to be stainless, and it must be completely dry. I tried using a plastic measuring spoon a couple of times and the powder just stuck to the spoon, causing me to have to dig it out each time. Now that I use a fully dried stainless steel measuring spoon, I can easily drop the powder down into the distilled water with ease. Shaking it vigorously afterwards mixes it up pretty good. There will be some chunks, but this is normal. Then you just put it in the refrigerator and wait for the magic to happen! Let me just say that this product used as a serum is the real deal. I have spent $100's of dollars on high-end products and have found that many of them are just fillers. Yes, they contain Hyaluronic Acid, but it is not nearly as potent as this homemade serum. I use this stuff all over my entire body. It makes my skin so supple and smooth! Because Hyaluronic Acid can have the opposite effect by drawing out too much moisture, I make sure I leave some moisture on my skin before I apply it. After my shower, I leave my body slightly wet and apply this homemade serum to the areas that need it most. Then I follow up with my favorite moisturizer. This stuff enhances your moisturizer so well! Those problem areas like your knees and elbows love this stuff! Also remember that it only take a small amount to make your serum. Same goes for the amount you ingest, so this two-pack will last a long time. I was very grateful that Micro Ingredients sent packages that have an expiration date out a couple years or more. This means I will be able to benefit from this package for some time, although I think I am going to make some DIY serum for special friends and family, which means I will need to order more very soon. I am sure they will love it just as much as I do! I really love this product!

title: Caused T:Slim meltdown
text:
I absolutely loved this case when I got it. So much so that I bought a second one. But it caused serious issues with my t:slim & those issues contributed to serious medical emergencies.

After I started using it, I began to have signal problems between my T:Slim & my Dex. I had only been using this technology for about a week when this occurred. Because of being so new to this, I had no idea the case was the source of the problem. Tandem had to swap out my T:Slim 2 times in about 4 weeks & then when it came time to do the 3rd warranty swap, I began to wonder if the silicone case had something to do with the problems. I put that new replacement in the original Tandem hard case with belt clip.... and guess what..... no signal problems. My t:slim also never felt overly warm like it did in the silicone case. If the T:slim is not in a case or is in it's original case, you will see some small dots near the plug cover on the back. Those get covered up when the silicone case is in use. I believe those being covered up are what caused me so many problems. With having gone through so many warranty replacements & now my t:slim is in it's original case with no problems, I have suggested that Tandem Help Desk consider adding a question about the case being used when troubleshooting device problems.

I wish I could swap the silicone cases I bought for insulin vial covers.... but I am past the Amazon return date & it would be unfair to ask this of either Amazon or the manufacturer.

text:
Flying every so often from Hawaii to the East Coast, I have found that the padding in airline seats leaves a great deal to be desired. Some seats are so worn, there's no foam left. After my last trip, enduring nearly 9 hours of torture, I decided to do something about it. The Corflex Medic-Air Seat Cushion worked out perfectly.

With a little trial and error, I found that very little air is needed for comfort. A couple of breaths and you are set to go. The little plug stayed in, and there was no leaks. Prior to landing, I rolled it up, squeezing the air out, and folded it back into its travel case. The case is big enough that you don't have to struggle getting it to fit again, thankfully.

For the price, this little gem should be in everyone's carry-on!

title: Okay for the price, but not as good as the product it is "inspired by"
text:
This is an obvious knock-off of "Baby Foot," and honestly, that's why I bought it. If it would do what Baby Foot did for half the price it would be well worth it. If you've used Baby Foot, there are some differences you should be aware of with this product. It is a liquid, not a gel. So basically, you put your feet in these tissue lined booties and pour in the liquid. (Be careful not to spill, I did.) From there, you can seal them (they tie shut) and slosh the liquid around where you need it. Because it was a liquid, I didn't think it penetrated my skin as well because the active ingredient didn't stay in place. Although the tissue paper inside the booties does get wet, so it holds some of it in place.

So, the result? After a few days my feet peeled, but not the the same horrifying, yet gratifying, way that they did with Baby Foot. I'll probably look for another knock off that has a gel rather than a liquid. And, just FYI, most of the packaging is in Japanese. There are very limited English instructions on the box.

I'm now a couple of weeks post-surgery and off the antibiotics, and this recovery has been the easiest, digestion-wise, that I have ever had. Elimination is easy, clean, and comfortable. title: NECESSITY for Colonoscopy Prep
text:
I discovered this cleansing lotion when I had my first colonoscopy. I had been warned that the prep was the worst part. And my mom warned me to lay in a supply of this lotion when tidying up after the prep stuff did its thing. I was skeptical. Lotion? For my BUM?! Turns out, that's a very definite YES.

If you've had a colonoscopy, you know that after you drink that concoction of vileness that they call the "prep drink," you're going to poop in much the same way that Vesuvius erupts. Trip after trip to the loo, right? Right. Oh, you thought you were done and could have a little lie-down to recover? Haha. NOPE! Why don't you just bring in War and Peace and sit here the rest of the day?

So after a few trips to the throne room, your bum feels a bit sore. Even the softest toilet tissue feels like 80-grit sandpaper rasping all the skin off your most delicate bits. And you can't stop going to the loo, because that death-potion you had to drink is ripping through you like a wildfire through a summer-dry grassland. In fact, your bum feels like it might BE on fire.

That's where this lotion stuff comes in. After gently patting the worst of the debris off your bum, you take a fresh piece of toilet roll and put a bit of this stuff on it. Use that to clean up the rest of you. The relief is instant, like a cup of ice-water after a mid-day hike through Death Valley in mid-August. And it does seem to make the cleanup more effective.

I imagine people with chronic digestive issues would also find this useful, and I know that on days when my "girl thing" is happening, it's a relief to clean up using this product. But if you're slated for a colonoscopy, you should most definitely lay in a supply of this stuff. You're gonna need it!

title: Myself, my wife, and my dog. All 3 of us are taking this!
text:
The thing about supplements is they are hard to prove or disprove. So many factors. Was your body already in the healing stage? Did you stop sitting on a certain couch that was causing it? Did it really work?
I'm a realist. Unless I can say with 100% proof positive conclusion; I'm not saying either way.
I got these for myself, my wife, and our dog. All 3 of us are experiencing joint issues. Have they cured any of us? No. Have we been on them for months? No. Do they work? unsure. Is it worth a try? YES!!! Does pain hurt??? YES!!!
unless I can prove something doesn't work I rate it 5 stars. Because I don't want to smear any brand's good name.

So the best anyone can do is the following:
1) limit sitting time! Sitting for too long can cause these same issues. Your body needs exercise, and until you give it said exercise, expect to continue hurting. Of course there are exceptions, but that's just my findings. In times (like during snow storms) when I find myself watching a lot of TV or playing a lot of video games, I experience pain in the joints. Its conclusive. The 2 go hand in hand.
2) Use a cain to get up if necessary, and exercise WISELY. Don't over do it. But don't do nothing either! A good steady walk down my local main street at night enjoying the lights seems to help.
3) Research any remedy. The ingredients on this look promising. Its exactly what my research suggested I needed, so I'm taking it. Time will tell.
4) For the pooches the same rules apply. They're just like us only covered in fur.
Hope this helped somehow.

It says there are 2 nozzles, 1 adult , 1 kid but it actually comes with 3. One is already on the bottle when you open the box. So I’m not sure if this is supposed to be used? I would assume so. The package also contains a thermometer but doesn’t say where to stick it (no pun intended :o) I would assume you put it on the bottle as it has a 3m sticky on the back, but I would think you can’t get it wet? Or do you just hold it on the bottle to see if it has reached the ideal temp.
The one upgrade I would do to the actual bottle is the make the button with rounded edges. You have to push and hold the button to release the water and after holding it for a bit, the rough edges aren’t that comfortable on your finger. It is nice that the water flows for you with the button , unlike the neti pot where you just have to tip your head to get it to come out the other side.

There's also a hint of salt to keep things lively in the taste bud department and to give it a balanced taste.  They only downside is that these are extremely "moreish" and you'll want to practice good self control to stop having a 2nd or 3rd one if you're hungry.  Even though there's 210 calories per bar, there's 6G of protein and the bars are also certified organic.  I just wish they had a GF version.

So far I do like this supplement even though it seems pretty pricey for what it is. After a week of use I can say that this supplements aids in a healthy metabolism which results in better energy day to day. It’s difficult to accurately say it helps with my immune system. text:

In faint white print on the back of the package, it says to “double the daily amount for the first 3 weeks”. My dogs weigh about 32-33# which means I need to give them 4 chews a day for the first 3 weeks and then 2 chews a day afterward. The package contains 60 chews making a package last only one month with the maintenance dose and for the first 3 weeks lasting only 1/2 month. At $19.99 a package, it is quite expensive.

The packaging list “cautions” which one is giving the treat with food or right after to avoid GI upset. It also lists warnings to keep away from children and animals and if there is an overdose to get medical care immediately.

I like the fact that they are made in the USA but then it list it is manufacted for Kenn & Kit which has a Singapore address. Humm…not sure what to make of that.

I received this product in August, 2021 and the “Best By” date is 5/2024 so they have a nice length of time before expiring.

title: Limited Use and Poor Manual Guidance Hinder Product's Full Potential
text:
After a few weeks of using Fidac's IPL hair removal device as directed, I haven't noticed much of a change in the amount of hair that grows back in a given area but the overall texture of said hair is much softer now. From the research I've done regarding IPL machines, hair removal is accomplished in stages and diminishing of hair coarseness is indicative of the IPL mechanism doing it's job successfully.

The operability of this IPL device by Fidac is fairly easy to grasp, without much effort needing to be pursued but attempting to follow the provided user manual is pointless and confusing. I wound up watching a "How To" video to effectively master the proper steps in IPL and it was easier to understand because visual supports were provided. There is the added convenience of choosing the laser's energy level according to your preference, which is important because choosing the wrong level can lead to some major skin irritation and pain. As much as I wanted to love this product, I wasn't made aware of the multiple places on your body you cannot use the IPL device on, which I felt the company should disclose initially, as to not deceive customers and create an issue that could've been prevented.

If there is anything you MUST do correctly, PLEASE follow all safety protocol in place and wear the provided protective eye-wear because those intense light emissions can cause retina damage. Due to the company failing to inform customers about areas to not use this device on before purchasing, in conjunction with a poorly written user's manual that should guide customers, I deducted 2 stars. Complete product disclosure and effective instructional guides should always be prevalent when selling a product to the masses, it's just good business and facilitates trustworthiness/

title: Favorite cloth diapers
text: I have tried six brands of cloth diapers including these. Five of them have been pocket diapers, and these have by far been my favorite brand. I have a 18-month-old heavy wetter and have had leaking issues with all the other brands I've tried due to the legs not fitting properly. With the Wink diapers, the fit doesn't have to be perfect, since there is elastic around the legs to keep them from leaking (FAVORITE feature, and a very unique one from what I've found.) I also really like that the inserts load in the front and that the overlapping flap is so wide, so it doesn't flip up like some of the other brands. The microfiber inserts that come with them are nice and thick. I had to use two inserts with the other brands, but the inserts for these are absorbent enough that I've mostly been able to get away with just the one. These diapers are also just really well-made, sturdy diapers. The difference in quality is noticeable, and worth the extra expense. I got rid of all of my other diapers to switch to these.

title: 4 1/2*  Stronger Cherry Flavor Would Have Been Better
text:
INTRODUCTION
I would rate this higher except for the fairly weak cherry flavor. YOu can taste it, but you have to search. The texture is excellent, and it tastes good, if not great. It's neither overly sweet nor ruined by strange aftertastes.

NUTRITIONAL VALUE: ASK AN EXPERT
I'm not a nutritionist, and it would be wise to analyze nutrition against your own physiology and need for this product, but here are a few lay observations. Total fat(4 grams) and carbohydrates(45 grams, including 18 grams of sugar from cane juice syrup and other sources) are basically comparable to many other similar products. These levels may be fine given how and when you use of the product (e.g., perhaps you practice "carbohydrate loading") Again, those who rely these for workout energy should seek the advise of a professional. You get a fairly good dose of nutrients with the added vitamins and minerals, although I don't know how absorbable they may be. Though probably not as healthy as fresh oats, rice, apples, raisins, soy beans, fruits, etc., this is probably better for you than several doughnuts or skipping a meal altogether.

INGREDIENTS
Please see list above.
Vitamins and Minerals: Vitamin C (Ascorbic Acid), Vitamin E Acetate, Vitamin B3 (Niacin), Pantothenic Acid (Calcium Pantothenate), Vitamin B6 (Pyridoxine Hydrochloride), Vitamin B2 (Riboflavin), Vitamin B1 (Thiamin Mononitrate), Folic Acid, Biotin, and Vitamin B12. Calcium Phosphate, Magnesium Carbonate, ZInc Glutonate, Iron (Ferrous Fumarate), Copper Gluconate.

NUTRITIONAL ANALYSIS
Calories, 240; Calories from fat, 35; Total Fat, 4g; Saturated Fat, 0.5 g; Cholesterol, 0 g; Sodium, 80 mg; Total Carbohydrates, 45g; Fiber, 4g; Sugars 18g; Protein, 7g; Vitamin C and Vitamin E: 100% each; Thiamine, Riboflavin, Niacin, Vitamin B6, Folate, Vitamin B12, Biotin, and Pantothenic Acid: 50% each; Phosphorus, Magnesium, Zinc, and Copper: 15% each; Vitamin A, 0%.

COMPARISON
The Clif "Chocolate Peanut Butter Cup" contains:
Calories 220, Fat Calories 20, Total Fat, 2.5grams; Sat. Fat, 0g; Cholesterol, 0; Sodium, 90mg, Potassium, 280mg; Total Carbs, 43g; Dietary Fiber, 5g; Sugars, 21g; Proteins, 8g.

SUMMARY
From a flavor standpoint, this is fairly good. While you get none of the unpleasant aftertastes, off-flavors, or bland taste of similar products, the cherry flavor was not strong enough. However, I enjoyed the coating of rolled oats and rice crips-it's crunchy, yes, but not so firm that your jaw aches afterwards. It also doesn't leave you incredibly thirsy like some other nutritional snacks. For those who like apple pie, the apple crisp in this line tastes better.

The heating feature is controlled by a 4-foot usb-c / remote control cord. There is no wall charger, so you need to use one from another device (phone charger) or use a battery bank.

The mask is made of a soft fabric throughout and can also be used as a standard eye mask. There are three settings for the heating element on the mask; low, medium and high. I like the medium setting the best since the other two are not comfortable to me. The mask doesn't have a sleep mode, so you need to be careful not to fall asleep or it will drain your battery bank.

My only complaint is that the 4-ft cord is too short. If you use a wall charger, it will greatly limit your movement and I found myself tugging the cord out of the socket.

title: My eye pressure dropped 40%
text:
I have the beginning stages of glaucoma and I've been doing Lumigan eye drops for over a year and had laser treatments, but my eye pressure was still too high, according to my ophthalmologist. It was all theoretical until one day I was able to see the blind spot on a simple piece of paper with a white grid on a black background. I did three things: 1) Stopped drinking coffee or any caffeine. 2) Started taking another eye drop prescribed by my doctor. 3) Prayed for healing 4) Started taking two pills of Life Extension Eye Pressure Support per day. At my next eye appointment my doctor was surprised to see my pressure had dropped 40% and was well below the marker she had been shooting for! She measured the pressure an extra time to be sure. She said "whatever you're doing, keep it up!" True, I don't know which of my new tactics actually helped but I'm going to continue doing all four!

Note, like most supplements, the bottle is 10 times larger than needed for the contents. I opened both bottles and combined them and still had plenty of space. Somehow this seems disingenuous at best. No stars taken off, but I feel better after having said that!

+Mask is comfortable with cut-out wells for eyes
+Strap is elasticized but soft and flexible with velcro adjustment
+Good instructions that are clearly written, with hint to wait 5 minutes after wearing mask before jumping up too quickly, since sudden changes in heat and light can cause eye discomfort and headache

MINUS

title: Nature’s Edge Q-Gel has a 3x Higher Absorbtion Rate. Good for those Over Age 30.
text:
I’ve used Nature’s Edge products for the past year and have been impressed: good products, good price, and I feel good after using this for several months.

Their version of coenzyme Q 10 is known as Q-Gel. This is ubiquione, also known as ubidecarenone. These are different names for the same substance: CoQ10.

Co-Q10 is made naturally in the body. We also get it from some of the foods we eat. It’s an important element in the creation of cellular energy. Since your heart (and your kidneys, liver, brain, etc.) is a hard working organ requiring a lot of that cellular energy, you’ll find a lot of Co-Q10 in heart tissue.

Age has a lot to do with the type of Co-Q10 supplement you should consider. There are two forms of Co-Q10: Ubiquinone (most popular version) and Ubiquinol. Ubiquinone is the standard, oxidized form of Co-Q10. Prior to age 30, your body can generally absorb and convert ubiquinone to ubiquinol without any problem. However, as we age, our body becomes less efficient at making this conversion.

Since this is Ubiquione, it’s generally going to be a better option for those under the age of 30. The difference with Nature’s Edge is that their QGel has been studied to prove a 3x higher absorption rate. This is good news for those OVER 30 and want to use the product.

Of course, as with any supplement, always check with your doctor for their recommendation and to make sure it won't conflict with any medications you might be on.

title: This will save your puppies life.
text: We had a liter of French bulldog puppies and one of them had extremely labored breathing. We monitor their weight and feeding activity and while she was the runt we noticed she wasn’t eating anymore, she was distant from her brothers and sisters. We called the vet and got her on some antibiotics. The vet said if she didn’t start eating their was a small chance of her surviving so we got one of these and started slow just giving her 5-6 ml per feed( 3 hours apart.) She had went from weighing 15.3 oz to 13.1 oz throughout the course of about a day and a half before this had arrived. She wasn’t able to suck on her own at all. She is now weighing over 1 lb and is able to feed off mama again although We still supplement using this tube feeding system. She is night and day healthier because of this and I have no doubt she would not have made it without this. This product is literally life saving and it is well built. The tube fits snugly on the end, your not getting it off after you put it on. A good thing as you don’t want it leaking, or coming off while feeding. To clean I just heat water to boil in microwave and clean the syringe and tube out. Leave it open to dry out and store in plastic bag until next use. I do wish that they sold multiple different size syringes with the same small French tube. The FR 5 is the perfect size for small breeds. We used it on a 8 day old French bulldog that weighed 13oz with zero issues at all. Just got slow and ensure to study up on how to administer this. It can and will save your puppies life when the puppy cannot eat on its own.

title: Good idea but ineffective
text:
I already had a smart scale prior to this one, one that was much cheaper even. The first thing I noticed when stepping on the Aria was that my weight was up by 2 pounds (128 vs 126). It also calculated my body fat at 28%. I definitely, under no circumstances, am 28% body fat. I've had that tested with old-fashioned calipers by a doctor and my other scale seems to correctly figure out that I'm at about 20.2%--huge margin of error. This doesn't seem to be a matter of retaining water--the Aria consistently reports these high numbers.

It is cool that it auto-reports these numbers to FitBit but the integration also seems kind of clunky, buggy, and awkward. It's not clear in the UX on the app how to access the scale (it's through a settings tab). And also, it's not particularly useful if the data is not accurate since it uses that data to establish your basal metabolic rate to determine how many calories you need to eat/burn that day.

If you're thinking about buying this, I'd suggest waiting for the next version of it when they've hopefully refined it some.

Works perfectly, just like you hoped, as others reviewers have said. I just adore this stuff! Not gunky or gooey on the face at all--in fact leaves no residue whatsover. I have some thin, thin rimless frames that not just slide, but go flying off my face--a BIG PITA! I ordered Nerdwax along side Wedgees, and have since sent the Wedgees back; yes Wedgees are highly rated and loved, but they are such an eye-sore for those of us that are fashion hounds that care about how our eyeglass frames look--I mean "fins" of neoprene?! Yecch! I MUCH prefer putting invisible coats of Nerdwax on the nose pads/bridge...!

IME, Nerdwax really kicks in after a few base coats are applied. I recommend cleaning your pads/bridge with Q-tips and alcohol and then apply a few good coats of the wax--maybe a coat every hour for the first few hours. It then works really well, and stays on, even after washing with soap (I wash my glasses daily). I only have to touch up with single coats every 3-4 days now.

Love this Nerdwax and I HIGHLY recommend it!

title: Good basic peroxide cleaner, better out there....!
text:
Good basic peroxide cleaner--and a good choice for those that do not want to rub their lenses and have no issues with comfort or lack of crystal clear lenses over their wearing period while using it.

And you should have learned by now, as a contact lens wearer, that "no rubbing" is a myth, and you should be rubbing! Particularly with silicone hydrogel lenses!

But if you're vision freak like myself, and want the cleanest and clearest vision possible, check out another peroxide based cleaner/disinfectant--OXYSEPT. It's only available online, and requires a separate cleaner that you rub your lenses with (miraflow.com or Lobob SOF/PRO 2), and then rinse with saline before putting into the Oxysept peroxide solution overnight. But the results are far, far superior than what Clear Care can offer. The Oxysept product also adds a ophthalmic lubricant to your lenses which makes them comfortable all day--something Clear Care does not.

Remember with Clear Care the bubbling is just show--with a new lens case the bubbling can be so intense so quickly that the neutralization of the peroxide can happen in as quickly as 20 minutes--barely giving them time to get clean and disinfected,

title: Cord free is AWESOME!!
text:
[[VIDEOID:a7fa6b1224f5f426f6defcf1361a9f89]] I had a hard time getting the hang of this iron at first. After watching a few tutorials on youtube, I love it! I was looking for something cordless and I had wanted to try one like this, so it was a good combination. I attached a few photos and a video. Here are some key things to know about the iron

- the battery lasted long enough to do my full head of hair.
- to change the function, you have to push the stop button to scroll through the different options including the direction of the curl, the temperature, and how long you want the countdown to be. Once the option you want is flashing, you use the up arrow to change it.
- Put the iron UNDER the piece of hair you want to curl, with the slit up
-Make sure your hair is to the side of the inner barrel, and that you start at the root of your hair
-If your hair starts to twist, STOP, pull it out and try again. Even if it doesn't pull your hair, you will get a weird curl.
-To curl your hair away from your face, set the curler to Right when you are doing your left side, and Left when you are doing your right.
-It also works on natural curl! I used it when my hair was slightly damp in the picture that you see my hair curly! All my natural curl likes to go left, so it was nice to be able to turn it the other direction without using the direct head of a curling iron.

It’s been about two months and my husband uses on a daily basis for his vitamins and I'm afraid it went from “Hey! i want a matching one!” to “i need to shop for something a little bit more sturdy.”

To start off with, their was a lot residue caked on left over not only in just the crusher but pretty much everywhere.

The cup for water seeped through but with vitamin residue everywhere, he really didn’t want to use the cup for water.

The splitter didn’t work from the start. Was really hard to use. Didn’t split evenly even with it directly on the indent of the vitamin meant to mark the middle of it.

The the top half - grinder, splitter and cup, stopped snapping together with the bottom half - the storage, after a month. Their isn’t a way to keep the whole product together once that happens.

My husband only used for crushing the pill but like I’ve mentioned, it’s been two months and some of the.. well, I'm not sure what to call them so ima call them “spikes” are severely worn down and close to the plastic which causes the crush up vitamins to NOT be finely grounded up anymore and leaves a lot of “rocks.”

He still uses out of the kindness of his heart to store his vitamins but I feel bad that this product did not make it for the long run. It’s a great idea but could have been made a lot more sturdy & maybe better than plastic to last longer than two months.

title: Great supplement with lots of uses
text:
I have a fructose intolerance that prevents me from eating a large amount of fruits and some veggies without extreme discomfort. I have discovered super food type powders as a way to get all the things I have been missing by having to cut so much out of my diet. I have tried many different powders with varied amounts of success. For me sometimes the good ingredients are less important than the unnecessary additives, and I will pick supplements based on what is not in them.

FeelGood Organic Superfood Powder has no additives at all. The ingredients are just a list of actual organic foods. No need to go online and look up all of the things that I cannot pronounce. For me that is really important. I can use this powder in whatever I want without adding a bunch of things that I do not want or need to put in my body.

I have used this powder in soups, stews, smoothies, blended coffee, casseroles, spaghetti sauce, lasagna, taco meat, and several rice dishes. So far I have not noticed any real difference in flavor, except for the coffee, so I add less to that type of drink. There is a slight, for lack of a better word, earthy(?) flavor. A bit like an all natural wheat grass tea maybe. I personally like the taste but, if it is too strong for you that is easily fixed by adjusting how much you add.

I have tried other powders with a bit more nutritional value, but I really like this one. It blends in quickly and does not take over the flavor of what it is added to. It has a long list of amazing ingredients, and is less expensive than most of the others I have tried. My overall opinion of FeelGood Organic Superfood Powder is positive, and it is a product I will continue to use and recommend to others.

title: Quick and convenient
text:
This spinach powder is great! It is quick and convenient and really easy to use. I have mixed into soup, stew, smoothies, and gravy. I have sprinkled it on different dishes for extra flavor and nutrition. My wife and I are on a diet that requires specific amounts of color groups of food like greens (spinach, kale), reds {berries, beets) and it can be tough to eat the required amounts of each color group. Having a powdered supplement like this makes it so much easier to meet our goals.

As far as the taste, it tastes like spinach. There is no bitter aftertaste and in smaller amounts it does not change the flavor of the soups, stews and smoothies I have added it to. It has a stronger flavor when sprinkled onto foods, but like I said it tastes like spinach, which I don't have a problem with, so it works great for me. It mixes in quickly and easily, and so far I have not had a problem with it clumping up even when mixed with cold things or just sprinkled on.

My overall opinion of this spinach powder is positive, and I will continue to use it as an ingredient and as a supplement to my diet. I have already recommended it to some friends, most of whom enjoy it as well.

title: No brush as shown in pictures. Very poorly made and poor design
text:
I almost exclusively use a dish wand for dishes when doing them in the sink and thought this would be good to replace my old one. I was wrong. It's made in China, and made cheaply. I really have nothing positive to say about it.

The sponges attach by Velcro-type hook and loop. They even have the ones on backwards that they put together in China. The fill port is terribly designed and is difficult to seal again after pulling it open. One cannot put much dish soap in the wand. The handle, shown detached as well, is deceptive in that I thought perhaps that would be part of the holding for the dish soap. It is not comfortable to hold. The sponge took forever to get any soap to it and this is after adding water to the reservoir per the suggestion in the instructions. Even after waiting for a few hours, very little soapy substances came out of the thing. I've never added water to my old one. The sponges are not stout at all; they just collapse. This comes with two hooks that you can peel and stick somewhere. The thing itself is 10.5 inches long and will not fit hanging in a sink and I have no clue who would want to hang a soap/water soaked dish wand anywhere but where it can drain into the sink. I don't think a company should show pictures of this wand with a brush attached in the advertisements and not include one. No, the written description doesn't mention a brush, but this is still deceptive. I'm glad I did not waste much Dawn to try this thing, especially after mixing it with water. Steer clear of this dish wand.

title: Did someone make a massive mistake at the company?
text:
I’ve been using Oral-B electric toothbrushes for decades and have purchased numerous models over that time and never have Oral-B ever sold them without a brush or two included in the package. However, this very expensive AutoBrush package doesn’t contain the very item that allows you to do what is intended, namely, the brush head (see my photo). The question should be, if you’re selling a toothbrush, can you still call it that if you don’t actually include the brush head?

What you’re paying for is the body of the toothbrush, the charger, the charging adaptor, and its cable. The side of the box says that the brush heads are not included. However, the listing says otherwise - “Brush Head Included”. But it’s not. Not only that but you can’t even buy the brush head on Amazon! You have to go do that on their website directly. They’re $10 each.

Not having the brush heads means that I can’t really test the efficacy of the brush and their stated claim that it works better than normal brushing. But, after turning on the unit and grabbing the metal prong where it connects with the brush head to feel the vibration, I have to say that it feels extraordinarily weak. I fail to see how these micro-vibrations will do anything to remove plaque. The power put out by Oral-B or Sonicare is 10 times stronger.

In summary, this all seems “too good to be true”. First, they don’t include a brush head in their kit – even though they say that they do. Then, the weak vibrations from the motorized body feel like my iPhone vibrations. How can that possibly clean your teeth?!

title: It is working well for my dog's wound
text:
I purchased this unit in 2015 and put it aside until 3 days ago (now May 2017).

The first day after we arrived Hong Kong last year, my 2 dogs started suffering from skin allergy, very itchy. They have to wear the protective collars 24/7.

Three days ago, after feeding my dogs with drinking water, I went to the kitchen and forgot to put the collar back on to my 4 year old 7 pound Maltese. When I came back to my bedroom after 30 minutes, I found the chin and neck of my dog were bleeding with blood here and there on her pillow. When I was cleaning her wound, which was pretty massive, I saw her wound no longer had any hair left, and the kind of dark red flesh was exposed, very horrible. On the right side of her hairless bleeding neck, a lump in the size of a cherry was still swelling. I think my dog must have scratched through her skin and damaged the lymph around her neck.

At that moment, I suddenly remembered the silver water generator that I had taken with me when I came to Hong Kong.

I took the generator out, cleaned it, set it up and finished making the silver water all in a total of 30 minutes. Immediately, I sprayed my dog's wound with the silver water, and pumped 0.8 ml silver water into her mouth the first time, and 0.5 ml after 2 hours. That night, I sprayed her wound with the silver water 3 times.

The following morning, my dog's wound had shown significant recovery, no longer in dark red color, the swollen cherry sized lump disappeared, and no more swelling neck. I pumped 0.5 ml silver water to her mouth two times, and sprayed her wound 3 times the 2nd day.

Today, her wound is in light color, and recovering well, no trace of inflammation at all. I sprayed her wound 3 times and gave her 0.5 ml, 1 time only.

Instead of using the silver wires that came with the device, I used 10mm silver wires to shorten the processing time. I used 17 minutes to process the silver water for my dog's wound without doing the ppm reading, so I still don't know what ppm the silver water got in 17 minutes with the 10mm silver wires, but the result is amazing.

Seeing my dog's quick improvement, my sisters were amazed by the silver water and asked me to make each of them a glass of silver water.

title: Great for heavy periods, heat-sealed seams are EXTREMELY weak.
text:
I have heavy flow during the first 2-3 days of my period. I got tired of washing (destaining) blood-stained clothes so I got these vinyl pull on under pants. Since I usually wear a size 8/Med in clothes, I got a size Med. Boy, they're huge! The elastics are not that uncomfortable but the vinyl is super roomy. It balloons out as if your tummy and hip are supposed to be fluffy airy bread/marshmallow. It doesn't matter though. They're under my clothes (pants/shorts/skirt/dress). As long as the blood stays inside the vinyl, what does it matter what it looks like?

I do a 3-layer protection during heavy days - overnight pads (or 2 overlapping heavy pads for a really long overnight pad) worn in snug panties + vinyl under pants + a waterproof incontinence mattress pad. The vinyl under pants catch leakage/spillover. The mattress pad is just there in case the vinyl under pants fail (but that hasn't happened yet). These are vinyl so you're going to perspire a bit under it. But, I only wear these for 2-3 days per months so it's not that big of a deal. I don't know how comfortable/uncomfortable this would be if I have to wear these 24/7.

There's less to wash for me now during my heavy days - just underwear, no pants/shorts/skirt/dress. I only hand wash these vinyl under pants and then hang them to dry.

Update 10/25/2015:

What others have said is true. The seams are really very weak. After a few uses, the seams come undone. Downgraded to 2 stars. What I did to fix it was to use a soldering iron very lightly and over a PTFE cloth (oven liners) so the soldering iron will not stick to the vinyl. Be very careful when you do this. You only need a light tough otherwise your iron will melt the vinyl through.

If you don't want the hassle of using a soldering iron, just apply heavy duty shipping/packaging clear tape. It doesn't look as neat as hot sealing but it's underneath your clothes. Who cares what it looks like?

Another option is to use vinyl adhesive - e.g., PVC cement (the kind used in plumbing) or Loctite vinyl/fabric/plastic flexible adhesive. Apply with a cotton bud. A good preemptive step is to reinforce the seams by adhering the seam with vinyl adhesive so that it doesn't come apart when the hot seal eventually fails (and it will fail). The PVC cement is very strong so use just a small amount and spread evenly over the seam surface.

Has a mild, pleasant smell, is thick and applies easily, leaves a mild to moderate oily film for a while if you're over-generous (I tend towards that, myself), but no worse than most others I've used. title: I Think Best for Light to Moderate Cleaning
text: This spray mop is okay for light to moderate cleaning.  I like it because it's easy to put together plus I can use my own cleaning solution (50% vinegar and 50% water).  The mop head, which is a large flat pad that attaches to the bottom of the mop, is large about 15.5 inches in width.  This comes with 3 mop heads.  An interesting feature is a plastic comb-like tool that attaches firmly on the mop handle for cleaning the mop head or, as suggested, cleaning tough spots on the floor.  To be honest, I use a mop so hopefully I don't have to bend over and clean much on the floor.  On my floor, which was quite dirty, I did have some spots that I cleaned using another scrubbing item I already have which is why I state this is mop works best for light to moderate cleaning.  The cleaning solution bottle is easy to use.  It just pulls out where it fits in a position that to me seems upside down.  The bottom is a small plastic lid which twists off.  When filled with the desired solution, it just goes back on the mop handle.  I found it does take a small push to get it properly fitted into place.  To spray the solution when mopping, there's a trigger-type lever on the top part of the mop handle.  The solution sprays out several inches in front of the mop so care is needed if one doesn't want to get woodwork, doors, and such wet.  My rating is 3 stars for this is not cleaning as effectively as I hoped for especially with the roughness of the pads which should have helped with 'scrubbing.'

When I apply this cream, it does have a cooling effect and my muscles do feel more relaxed after a few minutes.  I haven't felt any warming.  The smell is pungent - it's not bad, but the smell is certainly strong.  The active ingredients are camphor 2% and menthol 6%.  Clove bud oil, eucalyptus oil, peppermint oil, and sweet birch oil are included in the inactive ingredients.  Since this cream is effective and it gives me relief, my rating is 5 stars.
