title: Extra virgin? More like extra bland.
text:
There's nothing special about this extra virgin olive oil at all, and it's rather expensive compared to better olive oil you could get in a grocery store. The bottle design is awful - the plastic packaging is unremarkable, and pouring oil directly out of the bottle ALWAYS causes dripping onto the top of the bottle. And the oil itself is so flavorless that it could essentially be a neutral oil, not extra virgin olive oil. Considering the price, there's absolutely no reason to buy this oil since you can get better (and cheaper) at a regular store.

To characterize flavor, I compared it to another common brand of olive oil as a reference (photo shows GreenIVe on the left, other oil on the right). The GreenIVe olive oil is a shade lighter in color and considerably thinner/less viscous. Flavor-wise, the GreenIVe oil has no particular distinguishing flavors rather than notes of plastic and maybe a hint of olive. No aftertaste - it essentially goes away with no lingering flavor. It really does taste like almost nothing. Comparatively, the oil I compared it to was robust, flavorful, and had a spicy aftertaste. There's basically no reason to use the GreenIVe olive oil to make something taste good, i.e. making a salad dressing or finishing a dish. Its best use is coating a pan for light sauteeing, where it's essentially a thin neutral oil.

title: No phone support! Setup explained poorly. Health WARNINGS not listed.
text:
1) Phone support number says no phone support, 877-623-4997.
2) Device setup is explained very poorly at the official website.

First of all, the setup wants you to either use a Laptop with WIFI or a mobile phone. A desktop computer without a wifi card will not work.
During setup the scale acts as its own access point, and your Laptop / phone has to connect to it. That is why a desktop computer can't be used.
So I tried first setting up on my desktop, clueless in how it worked. Setup failed and because my desktop doesn't have wifi.

Then I tried to setup the device on my mobile phone, a Samsung Galaxy Note. I thought it was working, the phone connected to the scales temporary access point from the mobile setup webpage. But the mobile site then failed, stopped at a screen saying trying to connect.

I then got my laptop, installed the same software that failed on my desktop and reset the scale by removing one battery. The software found my access point and I saved my wifi password to the scale. So I am all setup now.

If your reading this before setting up your own, just use your Windows laptop on wifi for best setup results.

3) I have to create separate accounts for everyone in my family. Why can't we just have 1 account?
4) And the final issue, official FAQ says
"I am pregnant. Can I use the Fitbit Aria?" "Yes, the Aria is safe for pregnant women to use, but the body fat % and BMI measurements may not be accurate for you."

But the piece of paper that is included with the scale says "WARNINGS Do not use this product if you have a pacemaker or other internal medical device, or are pregnant. This product is not intended for use by children under 10 years of age. Always consult your physician to determine what is most ideal for you"

So what is it?pregnant YES or pregnant NO. Should I risk zapping my unborn baby? Why does the company say two different things?

5) Why can't my other kids who are under 10 use the scale?
6) Why can't two people use different measurements. I want to graph lbs, but my wife is used to kg. The website forces us to use the same measurement system for some weird reason - even though we were forced to create separate accounts.

7) Will give an updated review in a few days once we get some data recorded. I emailed the company about the pregnant issue, will report back.

title: Great Suction. Helps you Relax
text:
The jet have enough power to push the water around on a large tub. I set it up for my wife and also setup her Kindle to stream the movie "About Time" which show a run time of 2 hours and 3 minutes. She actually watched the whole movie with this product on and running and the suction held up well even after the water has been drained.

I believe that the complain about the suction is due to improper installation. One of the suction was also folded a little when I first got it out of the box same as some of the comments I have read from other reviewers but it did not give me any problem after I have it installed in the tub.

Tip to have a strong suction.

1. Make sure that the surface is flat and clean.
2. Wet the wall and the suction prior to installing.
3. Push the suction flat into the tub wall making sure that there was no air inside the suction cup. If properly installed, the suction cup should be flat and not cone shaped. If there is air inside the suction cup then it will give up with the weight of the product or when the jet turned on.

Note: When you have a properly installed suction, you will not be able to just pull the jet spa from the wall. The only way to remove the suction is to peel the suction cup 1 at a time.

This jet spa keeps the foam from the foam bath that my wife added in the water. I did not see any difference between the jet stream mode and the bubble mode. It seem to just push the water around at the same rate. We have it set to bubble so I guess that is what keeps the foam from the foam bath soap working the whole time but it could be the same if we leave it at jet stream mode.

I did not see any cleaning procedure on the manual but after my wife's use, I clean this by filling one of my kids bucket with clean water and submerge the bottom part of this product letting it suck the clean water from the bucket and spit it out to the tub. I did this about 4 or 5 times.

I left the product hanging on the wall for more than 24 hours to make sure that all the water have dripped and the filter dried up before putting it back in the box for storage. 2 of the suction was still holding up after over 24 hours of the product just hanging on the tub wall so I could say that it is built to hold the device during use.

text:
This little gadget first and foremost is very difficult to use. Starting with charging. It’s difficult to get the plug in. Once it’s charged you can easily power it on and select one of three settings. But to actually USE the product you have to keep your fingers on the metal edges. I did finally discover that contrary to the instructions you can also keep them on the small V at the base…basically you just need to have two fingers on the metal to complete the current loop. (That alone worries me! I have another device that it’s similar and it doesn’t require sending a charge through my body.) Once your fingers are on the base you have to figure out how to move this across your face while keeping your fingers in constant contact. It is thoroughly awkward! I also found it to be too wide to move along all the surfaces of my face. It fit okay on my neck but was tough to lay against my face because the curve was greater than the area I was moving over.

The settings don’t make sense. The first one “cleans”. Sure, whatever…how does a different colored light clean? The second setting is the one I was interested in. The IPL setting. Based on how junky it was I don’t think it’s anything more than a different colored light. The third setting is suppose to be warm. It was barely perceptibly warm in a couple tiny spots. Don’t expect the entire surface to warm up. Again the similar product I have gets really warm is is super soothing. This one you probably wouldn’t recognize as warm if you didn’t know that’s what it was set too. And as for the sonic vibration is more of a clattering and rumble. Again does nothing but makes a bunch of weird noises.

Lastly the cover does not stay on at all. Not even a tiny bit. It wasn’t even designed with a lip or groove or tab or anything to realistically expect it would stay attached to a smooth plastic surface. Save your money and skip this item.

title: Worth it for the committed Fitbit user
text:
I've had and used a Fitbit One for two years now, and I love it, but I balked at spending money on the matching scale when I had a scale that already worked. Then the body fat percentage calculator, which had always been a little wonky, on my old scale died and I decided to take the Aria plunge.

Pros:
- Reads quickly
- Accurate (reads the same as the mechanical scale at my hospital)
- Consistent (gives the same reading when re-checked in a short span of time)
- Attractive design
- Durable and easy to maintain
- Motivating and simple to use

Cons:
- Price
- Does require some setup
- Privacy concern- will store readings for anyone who uses it, not just the programmed users

I found the setup pretty straightforward, but it does require the user to be comfortable with using consumer electronics and following instructions. If you can order on Amazon, you can probably handle this setup, but, say, my 88-year-old grandma probably would find it confusing. Once setup, it's good to go, however- the user simply steps on the scale and the reading is displayed, then sent to the Fitbit account wirelessly.

The scale will store readings for anyone who uses it. These are easy to delete from your Fitbit account, but guests and non-Fitbit family members may not be excited to find that using a scale in the privacy of the bathroom has broadcast their weight and body fat % to others.

The quality of the product is excellent- we had a fairly high-end scale to begin with, but it didn't compare to the design or execution of the Aria. I also love that it's easy to wipe clean- it looks so much nicer on a daily basis than our old scale, which had rubber components, did. I also love that it's so straightforward to use- some scales I've owned required knowing which buttons to press to access different functions, or required the user to step on them lightly and then wait before stepping all the way on, or required the user to select their own profile before use. With Aria, you literally just step on and off.

Finally, I love that it's so motivating. I'm sure this varies from person to person, but if you respond well to using a Fitbit in the first place, I think there's a good chance you'll respond well to the Aria. I like seeing the data pile up in my account, and making a daily weigh-in part of my routine keeps me conscious of my movement and food choices throughout the day. I only intermittently tracked my weight and body fat before the Aria, but now track it every day that I'm home, and I'm finding the data useful and the daily practice keeps me mindful. And you get new badges, which, again, not everyone may find worthwhile, but I find motivating.

Overall, I am extremely pleased with my Aria after one month. I've seen slow but steady weight loss and I plan to keep making it part of my routine for the future. It's not cheap, but if like me, you're a dedicated Fitbit user who struggled to stay consistent with weigh-ins, it may well be worth the price.

title: Good to prevent muscle soreness; made in U.K.
text:
The Science in Sport Go Electrolyte drink works by replacing things you loose when you sweat. If you ever get crampy or sore in your muscles, something like this or Powerade or Gatorade will cut that right out. It's an essential home remedy. Even just a hot sweaty summer can deplete salts out of you, and these sports drinks will stop the muscle soreness.

This sports drink is right now about twice as much as Gatorade. It's not crazy, but I can't figure out how they are trying to stand out. This is labeled vegan, but Gatorade and Powerade are also vegan. This Science in Sport drink mix is made in the United Kingdom and that's the most unique thing about it. It works fine, but I see it as just another option and I would buy on price.

The 17.6 oz powder makes 6 liters total, which is 12 servings of 150 calories each, if used according to instructions. I found it too sweet, and did half as thick. (I also do this with Gatorade powder - half thick.)

Most calories in this are from maltodextrin, which is a carb but not a sugar. It's sweetened with a little fructose by mostly aspartame. I found it a little more tart than most sports drink. I had lemon lime flavor. It's a much finer powder than other sports drink mixes and is about like a dust.

title: The Good, the Bad and the Unusable
text:
This BAIBB Water Flosser/Electric Toothbrush Combo is both good and bad.

The good part is the toothbrush. Small, compact yet relatively heavy for its size, the power unit has an attractive semi-matte black finish that’s easy to grip with wet hands. One button turns it on, switches among Clean, White and Sense modes.(the tiny Operating Instructions manual explains the modes) and turns it off. Simple. It comes with four identical brush heads (it would have been a nice touch to number or color-code them for different users) and a USB charging cable with a nonstandard plug that interfaces with the base of the power unit.

The bad part is the water flosser. It’s HUGE! It’s way too big, heavy and unwieldy to even hold in the hand, let alone maneuver it to and fro, up and down, in and out, in order to floss. I don’t see how any manufacturer could think this is a good design, but I’ve seen a few other water flossers that are similar, and I can’t use any of them. Why not a reservoir-pump unit that sits on the sink with a flexible tube connected to the flossing head? Maybe there are sound engineering reasons for this design, but I’m at a loss to explain it. In any event, the unit comes with seven flossing heads of three different types, a USB charging cable (again with a nonstandard interface) and a tiny instruction manual, so if this is your kind of appliance, you’ve got everything you need. But mine will sit under the sink unused.

My three-star rating is an average of five stars for the toothbrush and one star for the flosser.

title: A Good TENS Machine Choice
text:
This POHAKU Dual Channel TENS Muscle Stimulator arrived with the tiny control unit almost fully charged. The USB charger and cable, the electrode pads and wires, as well as a drawstring carrying bag, were all in a box that seemed too small to hold it all, but did.

This unit applies strong electrical impulses to the body, so I RTFM’ed before I tried it. The User Manual is relatively well translated from Chinese; it’s a treat from the norm of literally translated manuals that make no sense at all. It covers the unit’s features, safety precautions, operation, care and maintenance (plus info on TENS theory and techniques and some troubleshooting steps), and complements the largely self-explanatory control unit screen and buttons. Several tiny drawings show where the electrodes go on the body for various purposes; you’ll have to experiment to find the right configuration and the most effective of the 24 operating modes.

After reading the User Manual, I plugged in the wires, stuck two of the incredibly sticky pads to my arm and turned the unit on. The startup impulse intensity is zero, so I used the control button to ramp it up, and—wow!

The strength of the impulses even at about half intensity, which is as far as I went in my test, was impressive. I expected to not feel much, but I was wrong. This little thing packs a big punch!

My long-standing doubts about “fad” health treatments tempered my initial positive reaction to this device, which I tested just enough to write this review. It works very well, but only time will tell if it’ll really relieve aches and pains, none of which I happened to have at the time. If you’re into electrical muscle stimulation as an alternative health treatment, this thoughtfully designed, high-quality powerhouse puts out more than enough juice to do the job. I enthusiastically rate it at five stars; whether it works for you or not is left as an exercise for the reader.

title: Helps with my family's stomach issues

I learned that patients who have heartburn, peptic ulcer disease, or gastritis find great relief from DGL. My husband found that DGL helped him.
When I had the opportunity to try this DGL Licorice 500 mg at a discount for my review, I of course seized the opportunity to try another brand. I was pleasantly surprised that this DGL is in capsule form as I've only had chewables before. Some days, the licorice taste is not always pleasant so capsules are wonderful. These DGL capsules worked very well and just as quickly as the chewable form.
My son, who is being treated for Lyme disease, has nasty stomach issues due to the Lyme. He too has found that this DGL really helps to relieve his stomach distress so he is better able to eat.

title: IT MELTS! DO NOT BUY IF YOU WANT FOR YOUR CAR & LIVE IN A WARM CLIMATE/INCOMPLETE PRODUCT DESCRIPTION
text:
PROs: It's comfortable and you can wash the cover.

CONs:
IT MELTS! If you want this for your car, forget it.
1. Incomplete and ridiculous product description: If you live in a climate where the temperature would kill a child or dog left in a car, even with the windows cracked, don't buy this product. There is absolutely no mention in the description or details online stating "Be careful when leaving your Purple cushion in the car when it's hot. Like the Wicked Witch of the West, it can MELT (my emphasis) under the wrong circumstances. If your seat cushion gets above 105F, do not sit on it or move it. This could permanently damage your seat cushion! Wait until the Purple is below 105F (up to 30 minutes) before moving or sitting on it. Placing your seat cushion in the shade on the car floor or under the seat should keep it from getting too hot." They take the time to mention "no more seat sweat" but make no mention of the PROBABILITY of melting. Unbelievable. This warning, however, is included in the package. See the pictures.

I'm not joking about dogs and children. It happens a lot. Even one child (or dog) is too much. Just do a search on "internal car temperature chart" and you'll see how quickly temps rise in cars.

Here's some problems with their solution to put the cushion in the shade on the car floor:
a. Direct sunlight doesn't matter for temperature in Florida and other hot climates.
b. It rains a lot in Florida. Even if I did move it off the seat, I'd have to move it back to sit on it. In a car, it's so much easier to do that when you're not sitting in the seat you want to put the cushion. Easy enough when it's not pouring rain. In south Florida, it seems to rain every day in the afternoon from May through November. That means you get in the car as fast as you can. June - September are the hottest months. Add the melting, the rain, and the hot months, and this was a worthless purchase. I bought the cushion to use in the car.

2. Lousy Customer Service
Dealing with 1a and 1b, I debated with myself for quite some time, do I want to carry this cushion in to work with me every day? I'd have to carry it in with my purse, lunch, and laptop. The cushion would then make 4 things I'm lugging, and it's quite a distance...in the hottest months, often in the rain, so add an umbrella. I ultimately decided it wasn't worth it. When I decided to return it, I discovered I was two days past the return date. I wasn't home when it was delivered. They probably thought it was great that it was delivered early, but I don't, Evidently, they count the 30 days starting from the day of delivery. They delivered it almost 2 weeks early. When I ordered it on 1/12, I was told it would be delivered between 1/26 - 2/5, which was perfect. Turns out it was shipped on 1/15 and it was delivered 1/19. I requested a refund on 2/20 via Amazon's site and was denied because I was a day outside the 30 days. It didn't matter that they didn't completely describe their product. We went back and forth over several days. It didn't matter that they actually delivered it too early (that's usually a good thing, right?). Nothing mattered. They didn't offer any resolution. Perhaps their portable product? Perhaps even thanking me for pointing out the incomplete product description and a commitment to fix it. They offered NOTHING. They held to their 30 day return requirement, even though they failed to do the right thing with a complete description.

Their product description does mention "seat sweat" and their product description mentions "swamp butt." But they can't give key information about melting. Their legal disclaimer says, :Actual product packaging and materials may contain more and different information than what is shown on our website. We recommend that you do not rely solely on the information presented and that you always read labels, warnings, and directions before using or consuming a product. Please see our full disclaimer below." Well, Purple, if you can talk about seat sweat and swamp butt, you can talk about melting at 105F on your sales page.

So, I'm following through on my commitment to them with a review of their product description and customer service, complaint to Amazon, and any other appropriate venue. I don't expect Purple to do anything at this time, but if one person in a hot climate who wanted to use it for a car sees this and is now fully informed about what the downside of this product is, then that's one less person that is disappointed that it won't serve their purpose.

I apologize if the pictures are rotated incorrectly - the system won't let me adjust it.

title: Great for your skin and better for the environment!
text:
I use a lot of cotton rounds. Every day, I use them to remove makeup and to apply toner and softeners. I use at least 2, sometimes more a day. Cotton rounds are cheap, so it doesn't cost much to use them like I do. But it's wasteful.

These bamboo cotton reusable rounds are much less wasteful and so soft on your skin! They absorb my makeup remover just fine, and take off my makeup with little issue. I find they work better than the cotton pads for toners and softener because they don't hold onto the liquid quite as much. I wash them immediately after use and leave them on a table to dry. At the end of the week, I put them all in the included mesh laundry bag and toss them into the washing machine with the rest of my laundry. They always emerge perfectly clean.

I give it four stars instead of five because of the container. I adore this brand, and have a couple of their metal containers. This one is plain bamboo, which gives a nice sophisticated but understated look. But I don't like using it in areas that might get wet or damp, like the bathroom, because I don't want the bamboo to warp or get damp. Also, there's a cutout in the box so you can see how many rounds you have left. I understand the idea, but I don't like these type of items to be open to the air and dust when I'm going to be applying them to my face. The top comes off easily enough, which is useful when you're using it every day, but not amenable to the entire thing being packed in a travel bag.

title: Small but mighty cotton balls
text: I always think cotton balls I buy are too large, and I usually pull them in half before I use them.  That's why I like these.  They're small cotton balls that don't skimp on the cotton, and the perfect size for me to use.  It seems like they recognize this too, because usually packs of cotton balls come in 100, but this one comes in a pack of 200.  It's the same size bag as well, so it does seems as if each cotton ball is half the size of a normal cotton ball.  I haven't had any issue with usage either - it takes off nail polish with nail polish remover pretty easily and also doesn't painfully stick to scrapes and cuts when applying medication.  Small but mighty cotton balls indeed.

title: Pretty gift bag for small to medium sized gift
text: The gift bags are pretty without being over the top.  I chose the gold gift bags and were worried the glitter would fall off, but the sheen isn't from glitter that would shed everywhere.  The paper quality is decently thick, and they come with a cardboard insert for the bottom for addiitonal support.  The bags also come with ribbon handles that you have to insert and tie off yourself.  It's a nice touch for 6 bags, but I'd get tired of having to assemble them pretty quickly if I needed to make a lot of them.  Also, it makes me concerned about the weight that the bag can handle.  I do wish that the bag didn't say "Thank You" on it, and maybe just had a removeable tag wit hteh same sentiment, because while I give gifts relatively often, I rarely give thank you gifts.  These are very pretty gift bags that are limited in versatility but look great for the right occasion.

title: Good but small hot water bottle

Like other traditional hot water bottles, you have to dry it by turning it upside down and leaving it in the sun to dry.  It comes with a cheap fleece cover that doesn't have a zipper or buttons or any other way of getting the hot water bottle in it except through the narrow top.  You have to fold the empty hot water bottle and slide it in, and do the same to get it out.  Although the idea of a cover is good to prevent too-hot contact with your skin, it should really be easier to get it in and out of the cover.

title: Thicker than the Dr. Scholl's liners, perfect for slightly too-big shoes
text:
I waited for the Dr. Scholl's liners to arrive so I could compare the two. This set comes with four pairs, all nude. They adhere very well to the back of my heels, and are comfortable, so they fix the problem they're meant to - the heels of my shoes no longer dig into the backs of my feet and pain me.

But part of the comfort comes from the thickness of the liners. These are definitely thicker than the Dr. Scholl's ones, which makes for comfortable feet, but only if you had enough space in your shoes to begin with. That means they work best with shoes that were already about a half-size too large. A shoe that fits perfectly before the liner will be too small with the liner in. I don't have that many shoes that were too-large to begin with, so these won't be particularly useful except with those select shoes.

title: Definitely worth the value!
text:
I bought this facial brush years ago and I still love it. It's easy to clean and works great in helping to cleanse and exfoliate my skin without doing damage. I don't usually use the "massager" side with the larger silicone bristles, but the smaller silicone bristles do a really good job at removing makeup and then working the cleanser into my face. I can feel a real difference in the softness of my skin on days I use the brush compared to the days I don't use it.

It also has an incredible battery life. I use it every other day, and have honestly only charged the brush a handful of times since I bought it literally years ago. Note that the charger is a USB charger, so you'll have to use a different plug or a USB outlet, but I don't find that to be a problem. The charger cable is also pretty short, so it's difficult to charge in the bathroom. However, I usually charge it by plugging it into my laptop. Even though that's a slower charge, it only takes about 1 hour for it to fully recharge, and then I'm good on charging for a few months.

text: I really like the idea of this product, but it just doesn't work. title: Weak Suction, Incorrigible Water Tank, and Very Flimsy During Use
text:
Hi, it’s Glamorous Gem, hope you all are having a wonderful day,

Anyway, I have been into pore vacuums for a while because besides scrubs, it had to be some way to get out those stubborn black heads around my upper cheeks and nose. Rather than covering them up with makeup, I have tried a measure of different devices. This one sadly isn’t that much better.

This unlike others I have tried, does have a water tank built in for storing water for cleaning out your pores during suction. So, it has an ample design that is very unique. Not super large, but not super small either. It even has an illuminating blue light during use. It’s a very beautiful device.

What I immediately didn’t like about this product is, ITS SUPER HARD TO OPEN. It took me quite a while to try to bust it open because of its tightness. I came to look back at the product page for instructions to do so, because it didn’t have any. But, ALL YOU HAVE TO DO IS GRIP THE DEVICE AND TURN IT RIGHT UNTIL IT OPENS.

It popped opened after a while of harsh effort. Thank god, I didn’t break it immediately, BUT after the tank came off, it is super hard to keep it back in place without it trying to FALL OFF DURING USE. Nothing is broken about it’s sealing, but the water makes the tank so slippery, I have to hold it towards the middle not to have water spilling over myself during use. First, the tank wouldn’t come off, now it plainly won’t stay connected properly.

Though, that’s one part of this equation. This device comes with five heads, two silicone, and three plastic. It also has three modes, oiliness, dryness, and neutral. It sucks, it really does.

I feeling like it’s sucking/vacuuming is very weak, though. I have to turn it up to oiliness just to feel any real suction. Even then, it doesn’t feel as targeted as it should be. It goes between being harsh to gentle which is inconsistent. I don’t feel like this cleans as properly as it should. I didn’t get the results I would expect in the least from this.

Last but not least, there’s no indicators what so ever. Every time I have to put back on the tank. There is no indicator saying where what side anything should be on. It only shows the water dropping on the opposite side. Even my water pik has indicators (dirty water/clean water) for what each side does. It seems however you put it on is just how the tank is gonna be. Which is super awkward.

I think if you like gentle sucking, this would be okay. But, it’s still a bit flimsy and it leaks even straight up. So, there are clearly some issues they still need to work out about this product.

PS: No matter the nature, I only write honest, unbiased, and authentic reviews. Thanks for reading. 🥰🥰

title: Quite large
text:
Cloth Face Mask 4ply Washable Reusable,Adjustable Earloop Unisex Adult Dust-Proof Face Mask,Navy,2PCS

These masks are much larger than I expected. They completely cover my face below my eyes. They extend well below he chin and almost to my ears on either side. The mask seems very well put together. I noticed no loose or skipped threads. The straps are quite thin. They really just thin, cloth covered elastic, and that might be one of the weak points about this mask. The adjusters were easy to pull on, making the mask easy to adjust. I needed to pull the strap adjusters very close to the mask so that it didn't just flop around on my face. These do not come with a nose wire but because of their shape, it's not that big a deal.

Once adjusted, it does a decent job. It is a very thick mask, but that doesn't seem to interfere too much with normal breathing. The large filter pocket accepts the standard sized PM2.5 filters that are so readily available on Amazon. The product came with four of these filters. They were easy to insert and remove.

The biggest problem that I have with these masks is that they do not seal against the side of my face or at the bottom, under my chin, making them less effective at keeping the bad stuff in and out. We wear these masks during COVID to protect both ourselves and others. If air is leaking in or out, they're not as useful. I have a normal sized face and I think that these are just too large for me. I think that these would be better on someone with a larger face that could fill them out better.

These are decent masks. They're thick and cover the face. There is two masks and four filters in the package. For the price, this represents a good deal. If they fit you well, they will serve you well. I can tell that they were made to take a beating and that they'll last through many washings. They just didn't work out for me because they were simply too large.

title: Great masks that come with extras
text:
Mamlyn 3 Ply Breathable Cloth Face Mask, Reusable Washable Adjustable for Men and Women, Mask Wash Bag, and Pouch to Store The Mask

These are actually pretty standard masks. They have adjustable straps, a nose bridge wire and a filter pocket. They are a bit thin though as far as I can tell, they do have three layers as described in the product information.

For the price, there are two individually wrapped masks included. What sets this product apart from the huge number of masks that have shown up on Amazon in the last few months is the extras. They include a mesh bag to wash the masks in a washing machine (delicate cycle only) and a carrying bag. And the mesh bag is actually good quality and large enough to fit more than a few masks in.

Though the masks have a filter pocket, they do not include filters. They take the standard PM2.5 filters that are more and more available on Amazon. The filters slide in easily and stay put.

The instructions on the back of the mask package are kind of silly. They were obviously written by someone who doesn't have English as a first language. They are hard to understand, to the point of being nonsensical, and even use the word poison. By poison, I think that they mean any contaminants that are picked up while you're out and about. Anyway, it's a mask. Wash it like you normally would.

For the price, this is a great deal. Especially with the extras.

I never knew that there was so much to an eyeglass repair kit. This kit has every kind of screw and screwdriver imaginable, all packed into a nice, compact case. There are tons of different screws and numerous screwdriver bits. There are tweezers and ear hooks and nose pads. It comes with a cleaning cloth and a decent screwdriver for all of those bits. It even has a tool for magnetizing and de-magnetizing the screwdriver bits! The screwdriver is much larger than the ones in those little kits that can be picked up at a pharmacy or grocery store. I'm happy about that because the tiny screwdrivers in those grocery store kits are difficult to use and are just really cheap quality. Now I can go through my junk drawer and toss all of them in the trash. This easily replaces all of them.

My one complaint is that the screwdriver is kept separate from the rest of the kit. It doesn't look like there's any way to fit it in there with all of the other stuff. A slightly larger case would have accommodated all of the pieces of the kit. It seems like a miss.

Still, it's not a big enough complaint for me to give this amazing kit anything less than five stars.

title: These make wearing a mask easier
text:
Homesprit Strap Extender 12 PCS Reusable 3D Face Nose Mouth Bracket to Increase Space and 50 PCS Adjustable Strap Extender Non-Slip Ear Saver Strap Extension Ear Hook

Nobody likes wearing masks. They're either too loose, or they press uncomfortably against the face and get all sweaty over time. This right here is the solution to those problems.

Since the start of the pandemic, I have gotten all kinds of masks. These are most beneficial for masks that are a bit loose because they take up some of the room and make them much less likely to fall down. I am not able to use them on tighter masks because the masks smash the bracket against my face, but that makes sense. With the right size mask, these are perfect.

Pros:
- They keep masks from touching my face. It makes wearing a mask for longer than a few minutes much more comfortable.
- They have made masks that were too large usable. I have masks that have gotten no use because they were too large, but now I can use them comfortably.
- One frustrating aspect of masks is how they act with facial hair. Facial hair pulls masks down when talking. These brackets keep that from happening.
- In addition to the 12 brackets, they include a bunch of strap extenders and a couple of lanyards. The lanyards can be used to keep track of masks or glasses and are very useful.

For the price, this is a complete win.

Cons:
- When used with a mask that's regularly tight, the brackets can leave facial marks if they're worn too long. It's kind of like bedhead, but for the face. The marks go away pretty quickly.

Unknowns:
- Each bracket has a clip on the left and right sides. I cannot figure out what it is for. It doesn't affect anything, but I am curious about it.

For the price, this is a complete win. There are enough brackets and strap extenders for a large family.

title: The perfect bamboo pad
text:
I reviewed these a year ago, but my review has disappeared. I want to preface my current review by saying that I have used this particular set of bamboo rounds for over a year (including machine laundering and ironing) and they are good as new (although not as white as when they were new). No holes have developed, the edging hasn't come apart. They are wonderful a year later! Here is my original review:

I have not found anything I like as much as these. The main reason for this is because these pads consist of a woven texture that are both gentle and exfoliating. Because they are woven, they hold their shape very well and don't roll up. The other types of bamboo pads I've tried are a knit-type and they have a terry-like texture. I find this type to be too thin to use efficiently and they just don't feel as nice on my skin. If I wanted terry, I'd just use a washcloth. The particular kind of pad in this review is my absolute favorite. It uses a bit more product than the terry texture, but it's a much sturdier and efficient pad. I absolutely love these.

These pads are terrific! I use only micellar water to take my makeup off, so I just saturate one of these pads and wipe my face slowly to remove the makeup. Unlike cotton pads, they don't shrink or roll up once I've dirtied them. Because they are bamboo, I can then rinse out the pad and go over my face again with just water (or toner) to remove any residue. These pads aren't terribly soft, but that's a good thing, because that second wipe allows me to exfoliate gently without irritating my skin and without the pad falling apart. There is no strap across one of the pads' faces, so it doesn't matter which side you use.

Each pad has a fabric edging that keeps the pad from falling apart or fraying-- they are very well made. They come with a little mesh bag and I keep mine on a hook on the back of the bathroom door and as I use a pad, I rinse it and toss it in the little bag until the next laundry day (don't use fabric softener on these!). The pads come in a tasteful, decorative canister that is not only pretty, but also a very sanitary way to store these pads. I can't speak for their longevity once they start seeing a lot of washing, but they do seem like they will hold up very well with some care.

title: Horrible flavor, gross texture
text: While I like the the purported amount of biotin in these gummies, they are undoubtedly the worst supplemental gummies I've ever had. They taste rancid-- there is no flavor at all besides a rancid taste, as if they've gone bad. They are stuck together in a clump and have a weird mouthfeel-- they don't dissolve as quickly as other gummies, so that horrible taste lingers even longer. Maybe my jar was part of a bad batch, but I am also discouraged by the carelessness with the label copy-- typos (zine? do you mean zinc?), weird spacing, and incomplete claims like "no flavors" (but fruit juice is in the list of ingredients) and "no gmo" (no gmo what?), "no artificial color" (where in the world does that blue come from?) really make this product look unprofessional and all the protective plastic and foil in the world will not make me take this product as seriously as someone who took the time to carefully proofread their label to ensure everything makes sense. Add the terrible flavor and unpleasant texture and this is a big "do not recommend" from me. There are plenty of vegan gummies out there with a better taste, texture, and accurate information on the label. I know this is the product of a home industry, but I would not have put this on the market yet.

title: Smells great.... but not to the bugs...
text:
I bought this product on the recommendation of my coworkers. This summer has been ridiculous with the rain and overabundance of mosquitoes. Every time I go outside at work or to exercise I end up getting eaten up. For whatever reason, I just must really smell good to mosquitoes! I got to the point where I was afraid to leave the house because the bites were becoming more numerous and the itching was severe. I initially purchased an "Off" brand product, containing DEET, which works really well- but boy does it stink! I did not like smelling like that all day and was desperate to find something else. I gave the Avon product a try and am very pleased with the results. This smells more like sunscreen and is not strong in the least. As long as I put it on, it has protected me from the mosquitoes and my number of bites has drastically decreased. Since it is a lotion, it is much easier to apply to specific areas such as arms or neck without getting it everywhere- and you are not inhaling half of it like with the spray on products. Really, the only downside is that you seem to have to apply this more frequently than the DEET containing products. About every 4 hours if you are going to be outside in mosquito rich areas. I believe the directions say about every 2 hours, but I found you can go to 4 as long as you are not swimming or getting wet.
Highly recommend for anyone that seems to be a delightful dish to a mosquito. The sunscreen is just a bonus. It is easy to use and once it dries you don't feel oily or greasy. Thank you Avon!

title: Not impressed overall, but they seem to mean well
text: When I look at essential oils, I look at them through the lens of an organization like Dr. Pappas' Essential Oils University, which has a very pragmatic and realistic view of essential oils. In short, these oils contain chemical compounds from plants, so whatever those compounds can do to the human body, these oils can do, and their effectiveness is determined by their concentration, dosage, and the presence of other compounds that can diminish them or harm the user. Some compounds can have a physical effect through inhalation, most can't, so in the case of MONQ oils (which stands for Modified Observation of Natural Qualia, according to their website), where their main method of recommended application is through inhalation (with some, like this, being topical application), I look at how effective those compounds likely are when applied that way. In the case of this particular blend, the oils seem to be mostly meant to have a psychosomatic effect by triggering the relaxing mental effect a forest can have on a brain, rather than a direct physical effect. Ergo, this is essentially just a placebo that relies on your own personal experiences to help you relax. Given that the company has Qualia in the name, it makes sense that they'd go for such a blend of scents. This company was started by an MD who prefers to talk philosophy when he describes the products, rather than hard chemistry, but I'm not very concerned with what a company says its oils are meant for, I care what they are. I want to know where and how the source plants were grown and by whom. I want to know the distillation protocols and methods. I want to know the details of their quality control. I want transparency before I use a product like this or put it near or on my body. MONQ reveals none of that. I have no idea if the plants they use come from the grocery store or if they're grown where they're indigenous. I can't find any information about their distillation practices, or if they have any sort of post-refinement process to doctor their oils. In short, I have nothing telling me to trust MONQ, and a lot telling me to doubt them. They talk about GC/MS testing, but provide no transparency beyond that. They're not as bad as, say, Young Living, where their claims both ordinary and extraordinary have been proven to be outright lies, but they don't seem to be terribly concerned with anything except making their oils smell good. That's a huge set of red flags for me. I can't recommend this company or this oil, but I also can't say there's anything terribly bad about it. It's really only meant for smelling, and I doubt it'll do any harm to my skin when I roll it on, but I want more from my oils. I don't want just aromatherapy. I also don't trust any company that uses the CYA strategy of saying "only for external use", because if the oils truly are straight from the plants and have nothing added or done to them, there should be no reason you can't ingest them in a safe dosage, and no reason the company can't stand behind that kind of usage. Covering your legal bases is one thing, but if a truly pure essential oil is for external use only, I have to wonder what else is in it. Poison? Other compounds used in the extraction process that the company wants to hide or avoid liability from? I can't say MONQ oils have other stuff in them, but I can say they don't want you using the oils internally, and that's a red flag. For this price, just get some RMO oils instead.

title: Solid solution for packing lunches
text:
I’ve started to cook more and bring lunch to work. While I’ve typically relied on cheaper plastic food containers, I wanted to try something more “solid” and longer-lasting. Hence, I decided to give these a try:

• Contents and Size: This is an 18-pack box, which contains six 3-packs inside. As noted, these are designed to hold 24fl oz, consisting of a larger (16fl oz) compartment and a smaller (8fl oz) compartment. In reality, this is perfectly portioned for lunches that consist of one entrée and one side dish. Although I typically prefer boxier shapes to be able to pack in more food, I did find the volume to be adequate

• Preservability: I was a little concerned at first as the lid does not fully “snap” shut, and instead tends to slide shut. That said, I can confirm that there were not issues with preserving food in the fridge for at least 3-4 days at a time.

• Wash: I often find it very frustrating and difficult to wash plastic containers, particularly cheaper ones. Although some of those elements remain here, I appreciated the little touches like the “gripped” bottom of each container. And in general, these are easier to wash grease off than the cheaper alternatives.

In summary, I’m a fan of these containers and will continue to use these going forward. It does take a little longer to wash grease off from plastic containers, but overall these is a nice efficient solution for packing lunches. Recommend!

title: Great hot water treatment for general soreness
text:
I’ve been experiencing more and more leg soreness after long runs, particularly in my quads. I’ve tried different hot and cold therapies, but true to my Asian roots, decided that it was finally time to try using a rubber water bag. Here are some thoughts:

• Size/Design: The water bag is appropriately-sized to cover a large area of the body. I have a fairly large hot water kettle that I use for this bag (about one kettle fills one water bag). The exterior cloth is both comfortable and aesthetically pleasing. I also appreciate the buttons, as it allows me to peel the cloth bag to avoid getting the cloth wet when pouring the hot water into or out of the bag.

• Ease of Use and Effectiveness: As noted, this holds a good amount of water. The rubber design is nice and flexible, allowing for good contortion to the body. I actually don’t think you have to fill the water all the way, as it helps to “slosh” the water a bit to get a bit more heat. Be careful at first, however, as I found that the water bag was a bit too hot in the first few minutes of use. It may be good to take some breaks here and there, as I had some noticeable red marks on my quads afterwards. Overall, I found that the bag stayed well-heated for over an hour (if not closer to one and half hours).

• Leakage: This is well-made with a screwable top that prevents water from leaking out.

In summary, I’m happy with rubber water bag and will continue to use this to treat general soreness. My only concern is that this water bag can get a tad hot in the beginning and may leave some redness, but as long as you are cognizant of these factors then I think this is a great addition to the home. Recommend!

title: Met my low expectations, but already starting to wear down
text:
I needed new nail clippers as my other clippers is very clumsy. I came across these relatively inexpensive nail clippers and decided to give them a shot. Here are some thoughts:

• Look/Feel: I like the fact that these come as a pair, with a larger pair for toenails and a smaller pair for fingernails. They feel normal, but one thing that I would have preferred was a nail file on the back side of each clipper.

• Effectiveness: Given how inexpensive these are, I wasn’t expecting all that much. That being said, I did feel like I had to press down harder to clip the nails (and it’s not as if I have nails that are thicker than normal). The biggest issue, however, is that the clippers are already beginning to show some wear after just one use. This is particularly evident on the smaller pair, where one edge of the cutter is showing noticeable indentations. I think it’ll be only a matter of time before these clippers become dull.

• Case: One positive that I’d note is that the clippers come in a very nice case. This makes it easier to keep the nail clippers together and conveniently tucked away in the drawer.

In summary, this was a fair purchase of something that I had very low expectations on. The clippers worked fine, but the noticeable fraying of the edges confirms my initial thoughts that this will probably not last that long. If you need a backup pair or are in a pinch then go for it, but otherwise I’d get something that is a bit higher quality.

title: A waste of money. I would give it a minus were that option available
text: I was abroad on business and with mere hours to go before my departing flight  I succumbed to temptation and purchased several pairs of a designer shoe, utterly gorgeous which had caught my eye several days previously.  I did not even have the time to try them on. Even the clerk's doubtful glances at my American size 8B feet failed to deter me. When I got home I had a formal event to attend and one of the shoes--as I thought it would--matched perfectly a gown I had decided to wear. Suffice to say that I had a bleeding heel at the end of the evening because I  had misread the Italian size charts.  The wound would not heal and was so sore it would wake me up at night. My dermatologist was on vacation but she had prescribed a self-adhesive foam dressing that  I used  up while she was away-- so I went on Amazon and using "self adhesive foam dressing" as my search term I came across this product. It specifically states it is for the heel so, expensive though it is, I bought it. It came promptly but even before I had tried it I had misplaced it  so I bought another.  Pardon this lengthy opening statement: I found the first box and took out the first sheet of the product---each dressing is sandwiched between two clean sheets of a plastic type material. I pulled out the first and removed the material protecting the adhesive, applied it to me heel and IT FELL OFF! There was no adhesive, none, nada zilch. I tried every dressing in the box and they were all the same--no adhesive! I then opened the second box and there was no adhesive on any of them.  I had spent $120 on nothing. A friend told me that the two boxes had different batch numbers so this is no isolated event (I had thrown the boxes away--my friend fished them out of the trash and told me about the batch numbers) Please do not buy this product.

title: I really like these, but I can't comment on longevity and ...
text:
I really like these, but I can't comment on longevity and it came slightly blemished and wet.

CASE
These come in a nice leather (faux?) case that zippers open and closed. The case has a nice velvet like slip that fits in the middle of both scissors to prevent them from clanking against each other. On each side are little elastic bands that are to hold the scissors to the side of each case. I really like this case because it will keep the scissors safe, together and help prevent me from misplacing them.

WRAPPINGS
The scissors come in a plastic wrapper that are shaped like the scissors. These were really flimsy but I don't think (and don't hope) they were meant to last because they were really flimsy. I just threw these out cause they were so thin. If it didn't come with the nice case I would have knocked off a star but I do think they were just for the packing purposes.

QUALITY
I can't complain. They are sturdy and have a good weight to them.

THEY WORK
The scissors do a good and very quick job of cutting hair. It's really sharp and quick. There's a sturdiness to them and there's these small plastic/foam balls between the parts that your fingers hold. It prevents you from snapping the scissors too hard when you close them. It makes for a really nice cutting expereiences, very smooth.

The thinning shears do exactly that. I love the combo together.

WET?
I don't know why but the scissors were slightly wet? Is it some kind of oil? No idea but thought I'd put that out there cause it was weird.

BLEMISHES
I had to take out a star for this. There were blemishes, kind of like old metal makrs, but these seem new so I'm a bit confused. They don't look rusty or anything though so not too big a deal, but hey you're buying something new. Should be mint condition.

OVERALL
I'd buy these again as they are functional and I REALLY like the case.

Note: I got these at a discounted cost in exchange for an honest and unbiased review. That discount has no sway in what I say!

Wish it could focus on just one spot, but it's clear a drive screw that makes it go up and down is also the part that drives the rotation of the massager. So impossible by design. Hey it's for your car.
In short, should you buy it? If you need it, yes, you aren't going to find a better one on amazon that works (CLEARLY) in the car.

title: This Travel Iron works great and is small and compact plus I love the zippered carrying bag and clips
text: I have long, wavy hair and during the summer I love the tousled, beachy look but I still want to be able to get that sleek, polished look for nights on the town.  I was really surprised to see how nice this flat iron was when it arrived, and the presentation was also impressive.  The Xtava Travel Flat Iron comes in a sturdy black box that opens from the top and inside the Travel iron was in a nice carrying bag and even included hair clips.  The heating element on the iron is 3 1/4" in length and an inch wide and that works fine for my needs but if you have thicker hair you may not get the same results.  The iron heats up quickly and I love the bag is insulated so that you can place the still warm iron into it without any worries.  Another great thing about this iron is how lightweight it is, definitely great for air travel plus they even included a set of bonus alligator clips which I thought was pretty great.  Overall I am really pleased with this product, I usually tend to pack the bare minimum, especially on weekend getaways but this iron is small and light enough for me to toss into my bag and go, in fact, it's compact enough to fit in a large purse for after work touch ups.  This item was supplied to me at no cost during a promotion by the seller in order to evaluate and share my experience. All opinions are 100% my own and they reflect my honest & unbiased opinion. One may or may not have the same results as myself when using it. title: Nice looking but underperforms.
text:
This is to help heat a small room which is always pretty cool.

The packaging made it very difficult to get the fan itself out. Once I got it out I was happy with the ease of assembly. Unfortunately mine would not clip and stay in the base. (I’m not sure if others have the same issue.)

I initially turned it on in my living room and it started blowing heat fairly quickly. Unfortunately it was not close to hot as is typical of my other, similar ceramic space heaters. (I have a much smaller version I bought for $20 to sit on my desk that I have to constantly turn down.) The remote and controls do require you to read the instructions to understand their functions. Unfortunately the remote interferred with my smart lights, by causing them to dim and flicker when using the remote.

If you’re interested in an actual space type heater this is not for you. It will warm but not heat. I have one that is temperature controlled (remote or direct) and less than half the cost that I use in my camper on Hi, it can drive you out of the camper. Not to mention no part of my current heater gets hot as the top of this can. The value in ceramic heaters is they stay cool and safe. The top of this can get hot.

NOTE:
In general I've found you need a 1500W minimum to actually heat. This is only 1450W to 1480. The heat output does not feel like my other 1500W units. When you combine that with the Hi Fan setting required to distribute that heat, you actually loose heat. (The fan is better suited for just that, a fan, not heat distribution.) The HEPA filter is moot to me since there is no way to really measure that efficiently... heat is what people are generally after.

This simply does not live up to the posted features, durability or usability. That combined with the interference with smart lights makes this only a 3 star product.

If they could address the stability issue with the top and base I encountered, the smart light interference I experienced and reduce the price some, this could go to 4 stars.

I was not happy with the flavor though, and who really cares about the other benefits if the taste is just not that good. It tastes like artificially sweetened International House of Coffee, or like those espresso drink machines at gas stations. I was really hoping for that "good cup of coffee" flavor that was mentioned in the product description. The artificial sweetener taste is just overpowering and there's not enough real coffee flavor. Luckily, I got to try it for free in exchange for this review. Otherwise – first of all I'd never have even considered purchasing it for $70 for 20 servings, and second, even if I paid $20 I'd be extremely disappointed in this product. Two stars for having potentially healthy benefits, and that's it.

CLR would have handled the water stains under the dish rack with ease. The one pot that it did do well on has a polished surface and it was able to remove some light water stains from that. title: Comfortable, easier to talk & breath with these!
text:
Awesome!

PROS: Lightweight, flexible enough to slip inside the pocket of home made double layer masks & washable. There are holes to secure the mask frame in place if you choose to do so. We personally chose to not attach them but leave them loose for cleaning / sanitizing purposes because we have to switch masks multiple times a day during long shifts. These are so comfortable & they actually keep the cloth away from your mouth & nose area so lipstick doesn't get smeared everywhere making it so much easier to breath without the mask getting sucked into your nose & mouth! Several of us work in management at healthcare facilities & have long shifts during which these exceeded our expectations. Another key thing we noticed is that it's easier to talk to people & have them understand you when compared to wearing a mask without the frame!
Update 1/12/2021: I officially love these even more as I have become lazy & started washing these in a linen bag in the washer with my masks in hot water & then hanging them to dry, lol. I ended up buying more so I had enough to allow one frame for each day of the week for each household member with a few extra for washing days. Basically once a week I throw a few large linen bags in the wash with them & our masks instead of having to wash them all every day or every few days all week long & they are just as good as the day I bought them!

CONS: The only con we found is that it is almost impossible to slip the mask down under your chin without touching the parts of the mask you aren't suppose to. We solved this by just temporarily unhooking & dropping one ear loop so that it left the mask hanging off of one ear if needed & then all we had to do was use the ear loop to reapply without touching the yucky face of the mask.

UPDATE: 8/29/2020
We are expirementing with attachment & so far like loosely tacking the mask frame on with several stitches, after removing the tab portion that sticks up a bit, for a more permanent application on masks with no pockets. For a less permanent attachment we have been using small cloth or elastic loops shaped like a U attached at 2 points in the appropriate place marked on the mask after mock fitting. The last method is better for washing, removal & possible adjustments but it is also a bit more involved in creating the pockets / loops. Both methods work for an entire shift & they are still comfortable sitting on the face. It will be your personal preference as to whether or not you want the frame covered with cloth in a 2 layer pocket style mask or attached or not etc.

Overall this is a good product thus far. I will update if things change. Please see pics with my review for reference. I did receive this product for free but that has in no way influenced my review. title: Not A Fan
text:
I’m not confident in the legitimacy of the company that makes this product. It’s a little sketchy that the QR codes on the package either lead to a dead page (404 error) or the one that goes to their website it just a single splash page with a 8 bullet list of marketing points. So much for that “Free User Guide” they promote, or the “Get your next bottle free!” Promotion. I tried doing additional research on Gods Greens and came up with very little. I’m hoping they may just have poor marketing, but for any product that I put in my body, I want to know that I can trust the company making the product, and that all of the claims they make are legitimate.

What I DO like about this product is that it’s manufactured in an FDA-registered facility, made in the USA, and 3rd party verified. It’s also good that the product contains black pepper, because turmeric studies have proven it’s more effective in conjunction with pepper. However, I’m not sure if they have enough black pepper for the ratio of turmeric. The youtheory brand I’ve been using for the past year has 10mg of black pepper for every 1,000mg of turmeric. The Gods Greens brand only has 15mg of pepper for every 2,100mg of turmeric.

Of the claims on the bottle, one that I’m not too sure about is the bottle’s label states “Certified Organic by Organic Certifiers”. In doing some research, you’ll find that a lot of times organic products slip through the cracks. I tried to contact Gods Greens at the phone number they listed to understand the process of being organic certified, but got an answering machine. Granted, it is a Sunday, but it could be like that all the time. Didn’t help my suspicion with the legitimacy of the company.

Lastly, I was excited at the high-volume of turmeric in these (2,250mg) as listed on the front of the bottle, but in flipping over and reading the back - the serving size is THREE capsules!! That was NOT clear in the product description or from looking at the packaging. What I thought at first was a great value of for this product quickly changed when I realized I had to divide that by 3 to get the true cost for “1 serving” of these.

In short, I am disappointed by misleading marketing, serving size, and have concerns about the trustworthiness of the company that makes these. I will be going back to purchasing my turmeric supplements from youtheory, and/or keeping my eye open for a different brand (nothing wrong with youtheory, just a little pricey).

title: All that up and down causes hose to want to pull down which can be annoying not to mention having to pull them back up ...
text: I work at a big box retail store and am on my feet 6 - 8 hrs a day on concrete.  At the age of 53 the concrete was causing my legs to severely ache.  Then I remembered something about how nurses often wear support hose to help with their legs.  With my job, there is a lot of squatting, kneeling and sometimes sitting on the floor.  All that up and down causes hose to want to pull down which can be annoying not to mention having to pull them back up every time you go to the rest room; which can be quite a task during the summer months.  So I got on amazon and started looking for something better and found the compression socks.  I had forgotten about them.  These work great.  The compression is just enough to keep my legs from aching (only from the knee down ached -- not my thighs).  They are not hard to get on, but it can be a little difficult pulling them off.  But once you've worn them a couple times they start to loosen up and pull off easier.  I usually wear them under my regular socks -- especially during winter to keep my legs from getting cold.  In my work environment you don't wear dresses, so the knee high compression socks are perfect.  I am constantly on the move, in the store, and they do not slip down.  I have more trouble with keeping the regular socks up.  Compression helps with my legs -- absolutely no more ache.  A lot of people will not consider compression hose or socks because they associate that with old age.  But hey, I am old, and I choose not to suffer unnecessary discomfort.  I have a lot of energy and have always moved at a quick pace; these socks help me to enjoy my job and maintain the high energy life I am used to.

title: Not Nearly as Much Fun as Red Wine
text:
I first heard about resveratrol when Dr. Oz mentioned that it was a benefit of red wine. The resveratrol in red wine comes from the skin of grapes used to make wine. Because red wine is fermented with grape skins longer than white wine, red wine contains more resveratrol. Researchers believe that resveratrol activates the SIRT1 gene. That gene is believed to protect the body against the effects of obesity and the diseases of aging.

My wife and I started drinking red wine and probably felt that if a little is good, a lot is better. We are finding out during the pandemic that you can have too much of a good thing. This seems to be a good alternative.

We have been taking this for a week with no side effects. It is hard to tell the benefits so far. Research does suggest it might help protect you against heart disease,cancer, diabetes and Alzheimer's.

The price is very reasonable, and these capsules are easy to swallow. We take them daily, but we still feel like it is a good idea to occasionally supplement them with a glass of red wine just in case.

title: Plastic tensioner tabs broke off right away.  But worked anyway.
text:
Got a package with three of these toothpaste tube squeezers.
It was easy to insert the bottom of the tube into the twist key and then push that into the base. My tube was pretty full, so I only got a partial wrap, but it seemed to be working good.
The base can be used to sit the tube upright on the counter and that worked.

Two days later I was able to get another half twist out of the key. Then one of the plastic tabs on bottom of unit broke. Then I just thought I would try to twist it just a bit and the other tab broke off.
In case it was just one defective unit I tried another one and it broke also. If they are breaking off with only one wrap of tube, there is no way this can work for even half a tube.

I then just tried pushing on the tension tabs with my finger to see how much flex they had. The answer is almost none. There is no way these tabs will not break off.

However, I kept using this and to my surprise it worked anyway. I didn't think the wrapped tube would fit in the space, but it did. So I am adding a picture with tube wrapped up and almost empty. So I bumped this up from 1 to 3 stars. With all the tensioner taps all breaking off, I don't think I should rate it any higher.

title: Good alternative if you do not wear glasses
text:
This is a plastic full face covering that you wear like glasses.

It comes with 5 stick on plastic lenses. I was not sure how you were supposed to stick them on (no instructions). It seems you can put them on inside or outside of frame. I think inside looks better, but less surface to stick it to due to square holes in frame. Seems to stick well though on both sides. So you choose.

It does not steam up on me! Even with mask on also! That is a big plus.

Vision does not seem more distorted than most safety glasses.

Only issue I see is that I don't see how they would work on top of glasses.

I think these are the best way to protect yourself besides offering a little more droplet broadcasting protection for others than mask alone and way more than nothing.

Here is a big plus over a mask...you can see peoples expressions. This on top of some distancing could reduce virus transmission most likely than distancing alone and allow for facial expression. It is not in the news much, but I have heard scientist say that droplets in the eye are a path of infection and I am not talking about from your hands. I am referring to people talking right into your face which is what people tend to do.

Unfortunately most people will be laughing at me for wearing this in public. I will wear it around my parents where I distance >10 feet and still want them to see my face. I don't want to give them the virus. I want them to enjoy what they want out of life which is not what they have been getting these last 9 months sitting at home with people visiting with masks. This product will provide people with an alternative they can decide how to use in places where there are not other conflicting rules.

title: too loud for baby
text:
So disappointed. It has a way to adjust the volume but even the lowest doesn't create a soft sound that you could let drift in to the background. I ran it in a room with an Ac unit (which runs at 90 decibels when you are right in front of it) just to see which was louder. You can hear it over the Ac unit when I'm sitting in front of the Ac unit and the sound machine is in the opposite corner. I was looking for something like the Ac unit fan but quieter to make soft white noise for my baby when we don't need the Ac unit to run. Well this is louder then that so it wakes her. The white noise sound sounds like old analogue tv static not soft fan sounds. It's terrible. I even tried putting it on the other side of her door, no still sounds terrible and too load. To top it off you have to use a forward and back button to even try the other sounds, which are at different volume levels so cycling throug them while trying to put a baby to bed is counter productive. Last thing, even if you try the nice soft rain track it's got some lovely rolling thunder to wake you dosing infant. Even the lullabies are too load. Very disappointed this thing.Returning. Replacing it with a small 10 in fan, which make a nice soft sounds to which my infant has now passed out to after being woken up by and not being able fall asleep with this dbpower machine.
Waste my time and money on the one.

Update: I have been contacted by the seller/maker. They share that they did a lot of research before making this product. They report that many people wanted a louder machine to fully block out external noise. That's fine and well, but it's also advertised for babies room with special tracks just for baby. So that said, I still stand by my original statement that its too loud for that purpose. Most recommendations say in babies rooms prolonged noises should not exceed 60 decibels. This is over that. After exchanging emails with the company, sighed by Bella (who ever that is within the company , no title or position was listed) I do believe this company wants to make a quality machine and make customers happy. My return was a breeze and money returned with in 24 hours of the item being picked up with no further action needed by me. They also offered me a free item as an apology (and a request to update my negative review) but I didn't take it. I didn't write my review to get free things, just to express how my expense was compare to my expectation based on the item description. They asked me if I will test the next generation which I will. I'd love to see a version that meets the original claim.(and maybe a few other improvements) It could be a great machine if it's improved. I'll hold out hope for that. I'd really like to have a better version of this. I really wanted to like it.

title: Actually tastes good AND got me ready for sleep
text:
I'm pretty impressed with these little packets of Unwind tea. Here's what I noticed about them...

** FLAVOR **
This is probably the most important factor for me, since I already know I can take mushroom-based supplements as pills, and I already know there are calming bedtime teas that are tasty. So if you're going to combine them, you'd better not mess up the flavor.

Thankfully, this tea is actually pretty good! It has a rich, dark flavor that stands up well on its own. I did try adding a splash of milk to it too, but I actually preferred it plain.

I'm not saying it's my new favorite tea, but it's absolutely enjoyable as hot drink before bed.

** CONVENIENCE **
Obviously it's packaged into individual packets, which is convenient. However, I was more concerned about how well it would dissolve into water. Thankfully, it was easy! I poured the powder into a cup of hot water, and it immediately started dissolving into the liquid. I gave it a good stir, and it was done. No need to keep stirring it; no leftover bits on the bottom of the cup. Easy peasy.

** EFFECTIVENESS **
I made my drink around 8:30pm, as I was just getting ready to put my kids to bed. I sipped it for the next hour or so as I got things ready, and I could feel myself getting into a more restful state as I went along. I wouldn't say I was getting drowsy, but just more relaxed and calm. I also slept pretty hard that night. I'm sure it will work better or worse depending on other factors going on during the day, but in general it does seem to help ease my body on toward sleep.

If you're curious, here's the complete list of ingredients from the side of the package:
- Organic Reishi Fruiting Body Extract
- Organic Chaga Fruiting Body Extract
- Albion® Magnesium Bisgylcinate Chelate
- Organic Chamomile Flower Extract
- Organic Peppermint Leaf Extract
- L-Theanine
- Organic Passion Flower Extract
- Organic Monk Fruit Extract

title: Really good basic white noise
text: I am somewhat of a white noise junkie. I have tried fans, electronic machines and even a nebulizer to achieve deeper uninterrupted sleep. I discovered this machine when I was visiting my sister's house and needed to put my baby down in the other room. She told me this machine had worked really well for she and her husband and so I bought one. My little one did really well with it running, and did not hear the mayhem of my neices's fourteen year old birthday party. It is a really basic machine. It has an on/off switch and twists to adjust the loudness of the noise. What I really like about it, although it can't be turned up as high as some of the electronic machines, is that the white noise is really truly white noise. I don't know if you have ever noticed but on some of the machines that allow you to choose a variety of noises, the white noise setting is on a sound loop and if you are lying awake and listening closely you can hear it. This is just good pure white noise. Not a recording of it. It is a great machine. It works for my baby and it works for me, and its not too big to throw in the suitcase for travel. Will be using this from now on. If you just need good basic white noise, this is the machine for you.

title: It is ok.  But, have many reservations
text:
For a multivitamin the cost is pretty high. It comes out at $13 a month. Well, there is your Netflix subscription right there. At $156 a year for just a multi, that's pretty expensive.

Also, the combination of the B complex is rather weird. Some Bs are at 100 times daily requirements (for B12), some others at just 1.5 times daily requirements (Niacin). That is actually common among multivitamins. And, when you compare them their relative dosage for the Bs are completely different. There is no convergence among brands. It is kind of a random function.

Along the same lines, some minerals that are pretty important for nerve functions and electrolyte balance are extremely underpowered including Calcium, Potassium and Magnesium all coming at 3% or less of daily requirements. Why bother. You are practically not ingesting any of those three key minerals to make any impact on your health. I gather it is enough for this multi to put those three key minerals within the ingredients. Don't be fooled, they may as well be at 0% of daily requirements, it would not make any difference.

In view of the above, well I would keep your Netflix subscription. It is a far better value. I would probably recommend a very basic multi that has just 100% of daily requirements of the basic vitamins. And, if you feel you do need Calcium, Magnesium, or Potassium, well spend the money on earmarked dedicated supplement for each. You will get far more (at times a 100 x more) of what you really need. You may spend a bit more money at the end. But, you will get an intake of minerals micronutrients that could make a material difference to your health.

title: Excellent reading lamp.
text:
I don't find this to be the most aesthetically pleasing of lamps nor the brightest, but the light it gives off provides cool, even, low-power, long life LED reading performance. It's also quite sleek, so it fits well behind couches or in corners. It's stable and sufficiently well constructed.

The structure is easily adjusted via the bendable armature that holds the lamp. The armature is covered in a bendable plastic sheath to prevent pinching. The sheath is flexible and durable. The light can alternate between 2 brightness modes via a switch on the underside. I could barely distinguish between the levels of brightness, and the switch itself could use some tactile feedback to let you know which is the brightest setting -- there's only visual icons on the switch itself to provide feedback.

The base/stand is actually a bit bulky. It comes up about 2.5 inches high on the front, dips down in the middle and pops up to about 3.5 inches on the back end. Fitting it under a couch may be problematic depending on the couch. And trying to squeeze it behind a couch sitting right up against a wall will probably require at least 4 inches of comfort. However, it would be fairly ideal sitting in the corner of a room that had a rounded sofa there.

The light is intended to be for reading, for which it works great. It won't likely disturb others nearby. It's a cool light and even. Glare on glossy pages is kept to a minimum, and the lower brightness setting also helps for that.

The creme color will stand out in a room that has white trim, so it's a shame there's no white lamp. Other than that, it's a fairly excellent product that does what it does well.
