The big LCD screen is easy to read. It uses a color coded green, yellow, or red to indicate if your pressure is a good or a concern--it's best to know what the numbers mean and not rely on the colors, though. It runs on 4 AA batteries, or you can use the included USB cord to power it--a nice convenience. There is a memory feature if you want preserve a reading for your records, and it has a calendar/clock to record the date/time of the readings. The size is compact and is light weight. There is no carrying case, just a little bag. For the price, this is a good value and works well enough to be trusted.

I will update if I ever get bit by anything so see if this product helps.

title: Pear scented toilet spray
text: I could smell this right out of the package. In fact my hand smelled like it for a while. I think the bottle leaked slightly as the pump looked wet but the box was dry. I shook the bottle and sprayed it twice into the toilet. I couldn't really smell the scent at that point. I've tried this with formed stools which don't really smell in first place. Then I tried it with soft stool/ diarrhea and it masked the smell but not completely. Maybe if I sprayed more into the toilet it would've completely masked the smell but I didn't want to go through the whole bottle so quickly. Overall I think it works for the most part.

title: Nice sized shaver but lacking some desirable features
text: This rechargeable electric razor does look and feel cheap as others have mentioned. I do like the shape of it as it is easy to hold. I wish there was some texture on the body to provide a better grip. I used this to shave the bikini area and I thought it did a great job. The size of the shaver head was perfect for me for that area (much easier to maneuver compared to my old battery standard sized shaver head which I'd been using for years). I didn't experience any snagging of the hair as others have mentioned. The hair was pretty long but I just went over it with a light hand until it got short and then I got a close shave. I like that one side of the blade is curved for the under arms and bikini area (although I did those areas just fine with the straight side too). I think the biggest thing that I don't like is the way the blade/ foil is removed in order to clean. Mine was a mess inside because there was some kind of lubricant/vaseline type substance in there and the hairs were all stuck. I had to wipe all that gunk out. It wasn't the easiest the clean compared to my old shaver. I feel like this new one is not really meant to be cleaned or it would've had a better design to open up the shaver head. Another issue is that this is not to be used in or around water which is kind of inconvenient. I think the only thing I would put under water is the blade/foil once it's removed from the body. I wouldn't trust rinsing it under water while attached to the body like they show in the product video. On my unit when the blade/ foil is removed, I see a little piece of sponge/ foam in the center and underneath that it looks like it's opened into the handle. Definitely don't want to get water in there. I wish there was an included protective cover like my other shaver. I like that it is rechargeable by using the included micro USB cord. The handle glows red when it's charging and turns off when it's done. There is more to be desired but it gets the job done so it's not a total waste. I also don't know why the box says 'epilator' because it is not.

title: Longer reach grabber with light source
text: This is a long reach grabber that's 10 inches longer than a regular reach grabber. I was excited to stumble across this because I have 30-32 inch grabbers and always said "only if it was just a little bit longer". The handle is easy to grip and squeeze. The grabber folds in half for easy storage. The grabber has a light source which is a nice feature but it's not something that I need. It came with a small screw driver and 3 button cell batteries  that you would have to install yourself. There is an on & off switch located near the battery door located where the grabber arms are. It also has a magnetic pickup built into one of the arms. It did take some effort to extend the grabber fully for the first time. There is an attached velcro strap to keep the grabber folded in half. The grabber arms can be rotated if needed.

title: Large thicker masks with adjustable ear loops and filter pocket
text: This is a thicker mask with adjustable ear loops and filter pocket. It is also a larger mask. On my smaller face, the fabric practically reaches ear to ear on me and I have to make the ear loops very small. With that being said, this mask should fit a wide range of face sizes. I do wish it had an adjustable nose piece which is important if you wear glasses because it helps lessens the fogging by creating a tighter seal. This set comes with 2 identical masks and 4 disposable filters.

title: Cute looking silicone facial brush with rotating massaging beads
text: This is a massaging silicone facial brush that not only vibrates but there's also 4 magnetic beads that rotate in the center which makes it different than most silicone vibrating brushes. It is waterproof to an extent and it recharges with its proprietary USB charging cord. I do wish it was a standard micro USB or a USB-C cord instead. The device is easy to hold and because of the cute flower design, a "petal" can easily reach the sides of nose, above my upper lip area, temple areas and chin. The device will automatically turn off in 90 seconds and when you turn it back on, it goes back to the mode where you left off. There are 4 modes and I like to use the first 2 modes (gentle or deep cleaning both with magnetic bead massage). I noticed that my face felt soft & smooth after use. I do find the power button which doubles as the mode button is really small and could be difficult to press. To plug the charging cord in, there is a tiny slit in the silicone that covers the opening and I did find that I had to gently wiggle the plug around to find the correct spot internally to actually plug into the device (instead of jamming it in and risk damaging it). Device also comes with a drawstring storage / travel bag which was a nice surprise.

title: Cordless travel friendly hair straightener/ curler
text: This is a cute little flat iron that can straighten and curl your hair. It was smaller than expected but larger than my other mini flat iron. The best part of this one is that it is cordless. I've always found cords on hot styling tools quite annoying, even if they swivel, the cord always somehow gets tangled and in the way. This cordless flat iron charges by a micro USB cable which is included. It doesn't have a lock to keep the plates closed but it did come with a silicone ring that slides on around it to keep it closed. The only thing I wish it had was a safety lock so the power switch didn't turn on accidentally. It's a slide switch so if you were traveling with this, there is a very good possibility that the switch would slide to the on position if it was put in a bag or purse. The outside of the straightener doesn't get terribly hot to the touch even at the highest temperature setting but that is still a safety hazard. I don't use this to straighten my hair since I have naturally straight hair already but I use it to curl my hair which works well. My curls were still there when I woke up. My hair never got stuck when using it. There is a comb on the straightener which helps keep your hair smooth. This would be great if it came in a full size version. I knocked one star only because of the potential safety hazard with the power switch. I like the portability of this and it being cordless.

title: A great rose quartz facial roller & Gua Sha gift set
text: This rose quartz facial roller and Gua Sha stone arrived undamaged because it was nicely packaged in multiple layers (open the outside descriptive packaging and the plastic refrigerator box was surrounded by padding. Then you when you opened the plastic box, there was more padding on the bottom & sides of that box. Inside the box was the travel case and inside the travel case was the roller and a microfiber cleaning cloth. The Gua Sha stone was underneath the travel case on top of the padding). The facial roller rolls smoothly & quietly. The stone feels smooth and cool to the touch. The handle does not appear to be stone, it just looks like pink plastic so I think that would've been better if it was a stone handle like my other rose quartz & jade rollers. The Gua Sha tool is small compared to my other ones. One side is smoother than the other but I understand that a natural stone would have some imperfections. That side just doesn't look or feel as polished but it doesn't feel rough. The roller feels nice on my skin and it's relaxing to use. Everything arrived as pictured. This would make a great gift set for someone and for yourself (we all need a little self-pampering sometimes)!

title: Good quality pleated face masks with adjustable nose piece
text: These pleated masks look like the disposable ones but it is indeed fabric. The cotton feels soft. It washes and dries nicely. There is an adjustable nose piece. The ear loops are a little big so the mask is a bit loose on my small face but I tied a knot at the end of each loop and that helped with the fit. This would been better if it already came with adjustable ear loops. The mask should fit fine for the average adult face. There is no filter pocket but that doesn't bother me. These masks came nicely packaged- wrapped in tissue paper and placed in a zip lock bag.

title: Great deal for these standard face masks
text: These came sealed in a plastic bag and came in a box. This is a good value for 50 masks @ $8.99. I have not seen this price at a local store. I have a small face so the mask is a little big but all I do is tie a little knot at the end of the elastic and that makes a difference and it fits perfectly (I don't like twisting the ear loop because it leaves gaps on the side of my face), by making a knot at the end of the loop, it fits snug like how a mask should fit. The nose piece is essentially a twist tie but it holds it's shape. I'm used to the medical grade masks where the nose piece is an actual flat piece of metal (I work in healthcare so we don't purchase masks outside of medical supply places - there is a difference in the level of protection, that's why most masks that the general public can purchase at the stores say "not for medical use"- these masks say the same). You can't go wrong with these, it's a great deal so there's no excuse. Wear a mask (cover your mouth AND nose at all times in public), wash your hands frequently for 20 seconds, social distance of 6 ft and be safe!

title: A cute looking mask but not the best fit if you have a small face
text: These masks are cute but they were too big on my face (I do have a smaller face so I tend to have that problem with masks). I had to modify the mask by making the ear loops smaller and then the mask fit much better and more snug on my face. It doesn't have a wire on the nose for a better fit and it doesn't have a filter pocket. The ear loops were not adjustable due to how it's made, it's not an elastic so those small silicone beads that you see on the adjustable masks would not fit on these masks (these ear loops are made from the same material as the edging on the mask, like on cotton underwear). If you have a larger face these should fit fine. But once the ear loops get stretched out from normal wear, these masks will be useless unless you get crafty (I tied some thread around the end of the ear loops to make it smaller or you could also fold some of it & sew it smaller). It's hard to tell which way to wear the mask without the adjustable nose piece (the shape of the mask is not entirely symmetrical from the nose to chin area). There is a tag inside the mask so for my masks, as long as I have the tag on the left side, I feel that the mask is on my face properly.  While the mask is not bad, it did miss the mark in some areas as mentioned above. There are better masks out there that offer a more customized fit (if the mask doesn't fit properly then you're not protecting others from yourself).

title: Super soft cloths for your face

The cloth is like the size of a large pot holder. I like that it included small round ones that are perfect for around the eyes. I'm not wearing much makeup these days since all this mask wearing but I did wash my face with it. It feels nice and gentle on my skin. I first tried it with just water but I felt my skin was still felt a little bit oily so I used a little bit of cleanser with it and my face felt a lot cleaner. The cloth absorbs a lot of water. I would recommend if you're looking to try something like this.

title: Flavor is spot on!
text:

The flavor is great, albeit not very sour. The gummy bear flavor is there though, and it's actually quite nice compared to many that I've tried in the past. It does a good job of covering up the chemical flavor of the various stimulants without coming off as overly fake or sweet. The color doesn't match the flavor, but I really don't care much: it's just something to know.
The only complaint I have is the price to product ratio, 14 servings of this costs as much as 30 servings of other products. That being said, if you're really into this sort of thing, I'm sure some people will find a good value here.

Overall, I recommend this pre workout! It gives clean energy without too many tingles, and the flavor is honestly the best I've ever tried. It's a bit pricey, but worth the money.

title: Professional quality nail trimmers
text:
Disclaimer: I received this product for free through the Vine program.

I used to use professional nail trimmers for patients with thickened, mycotic nails, in the medical clinic where I worked. These trimmers have similar high quality, with the only difference being that they have plastic covers over the handles. They are just as sharp and are curved to follow the contour of the nail. In use, these trimmers easily and accurately cut through thickened nails and are far superior to a standard toenail clipper.

The trimmers have double springs which can be flipped out from the handle to automatically open the trimmers when your grip is relaxed after cutting a nail. The double springs provide a significant amount of resistance, and you can also use just a single spring if you prefer less resistance and a smaller opening when relaxing your grip. If you prefer opening and closing the trimmer yourself, you can use the trimmers without the spring. It's nice to have the choice of operating modes.

These are excellent nail trimmers to have if you deal with thickened, malformed, or mycotic nails.

Anything after that and you are shaving for a while (going over the same areas) I would recommend this product to anyone looking for an affordable shaver that they can use in the shower quickly and whose battery lasts for a while. Of the 3 shavers I have rotated between over the last few years, this one is definitely my favorite. I've only had the shaver for 1 month so I will update here if I find that changing the blade in the future, once it gets worn out, is a hassle.

Overall 9.5/10

The box is labeled as a toothbrush without the seemingly obvious usage as a tartar remover highlighted. Much worse, the instructions are totally lacking in guidance for the instrument’s usage. While the toothbrush is pretty self-explanatory, I’m hesitant to stick vibrating metal into my mouth , between my teeth and near my gums without specific instructions and warnings. For that reason, I doubt that I’ll use it, and have posted a low rating.

title: Compact toothbrush with versatile modes
text: This is a nicely styled sonic, rechargeable toothbrush. I like that it has two separate buttons for power and mode, as opposed to a single button that cycles modes with multiple presses. On the negative side, it charges via an outdated micro USB connection, and doesn’t include a stand or travel case. The charging port is at the base of the handle, covered by a removable rubber plug, so you must lay it down when charging. That removable plug is destined to get lost since it’s not tethered, likely violating the water resistance of the handle. Lastly, like almost all unknown brands, getting additional brushes may be challenging. It’s probably best to consider this disposable after a couple years.

title: Excellent design for travel
text:
I’ve used several water flossers and this has a unique design that makes it perfect for travel while not detracting from using it at home. The clear plastic water tank removes both for filling and to invert and place over the device’s body for travel. When packing it into a compact size, a second small cap covers the siphon hose. Thoughtfully, there’s a compartment that holds 2 jet tips inside the handle and a drawstring bag also is included.

Though dim, the digital display conveys battery level and operating mode. Four pressure settings each are available for standard and pulse modes. When started, it oddly revs up for a couple seconds. Just don’t start moving it across your teeth until it’s up to speed. Included are 6 jet tips and a nasal tip.

The only concern I have is the longevity of the small nubs that latch the tank to the body. Since the tank must be removed for filling, these small protrusions must survive lots of cycles. Maybe they will, but maybe they won’t. It’s too early to tell.

title: It does what it says it will do
text:
This item arrived with the protective case cracked. Stuff happens, so I won't judge to harshly as this was not a high-value purchase. But I will suggest that if you're going to ship your material in a bag, a little bubble wrap goes a long way. The cleaner itself was undamaged so (again) not a huge deal.
As for the cleaner itself, it does work effectively in cleaning the fingerprints and smudges off your screen. Not sure I'd consider this a necessary item to carry around in my pocket, but it is small and portable so perhaps in the glove box or center console of the vehicle? The integrated spray bottle is very creative but it goes beyond being a novelty as you're going to want to spray "something" on your screen before using this cleaner. Otherwise, you're just going to spread the smudges making the screen look exponentially worse. Having the spray bottle solves the dilemma of finding a fluid (besides spit) to apply to the screen.
Can you get the same clean from a cleaning cloth? Sure. But the fluid and cleaning block together provide an all-in-one solution in a compact design, without breaking the bank.

title: Softer than the regular non-lotion kleenex, but more expensive
text:
I decided to compare regular name-brand Kleenex with these newer soothing lotion coconut oil and aloe Kleenex tissues. In conclusion, the lotion tissues were better in most cases. In a side by side comparison the lotion tissues were noticeably softer, and surprisingly, without the annoying oiliness and strong smell of other lotion products.

My biggest gripe is with the small decorative boxes, which are 65 tissues per box opposed to 160 to 230 count in a regular box. The upright box, perhaps in a car or other tight location, can be convenient. The tissues themselves are still full size at 8.2x8.4 inches. On the other hand, for serious nose blowers they are 3-ply instead of the usual two-ply, so ideally a single tissue takes you a little bit further.

The size is good for someone who does not use copious amounts of tissues on a daily basis, otherwise, I'd suggest looking for a larger box with a lower per tissue price.

title: If you go through a lot...
text:

The expiration date is about 20 months out from when I received the product, however, I'd expect you'll have no problem using the product past that date. It smells and feels just like the brand name product.

The large opening on each container has its plusses and minuses -- great if you need a lot else when sticking your fingers in, otherwise, they'll get quite greasy fast. A squeeze bottle format is sometimes handier. I've lately been putting the jelly on my wrists during our "cold" California winters to keep them from cracking and drying out, much like I use a lip balm on my mouth during these days, and this product fits the bill.

For a few bucks a piece versus the more expensive name brand, I don't hesitate to recommend if you need a large container and a lot of them at the same time.

title: Great non-medicated option
text:
I'm a daily user of Flonase/Fluticasone propionate to control my allergies. However, there are three circumstances when I stop using it because it dries out my nose: if I have a cold, I'm going on a long haul flight, or somehow have a bloody nose due to other environmental factors. This is where saline spray/drops come in handy to moisten the nasal cavities. I know others who use it for similar purposes and it's basically a non-medicated item (water, salt, and some preservatives) so safe for those who are worried about side effects or drug interactions.

It is made by Perrigo (but branded GoodSense), which is one of the largest manufacturers of the generic over-the-counter drugs in the United States -- so Perrigo likely produces this same exact product for your local grocery or drugstore in their generic brand. This listing is for a 72 pack, which means you use a lot of the stuff or have multiple household members that do, but for most users, it's probably too much. Mine had an expiration date about 16 months away, but I'm not sure how critical expiration date is on salt water. Five stars for the product and its use.

Update: No longer is the version with D3 or 33% smaller and is now from a new vendor HBKDirect (this page used to be for Fresh and Fast, which it still is in my Order History). This is no longer a good deal at all at this price without those features.

I have tried taking this, stopping it, given it to others... unanimously... THIS WORKS!

When my wife was working at a retail pharmacy, all the patients used to tell her that the various chondrotin formulas did nothing for them, but that this one, and specificialy the Triple Strength, really worked for them. When I fell and ruptured a disk, I had so much pain and nothing helped. I started taking this and felt so much better. I was able to put off surgery for 12 years (only additional falls forced me to have it). Since then, I've given it to many friends with chronic back pain and sciatica and they say they love it and they now take it every day. Recently though, I thought maybe I did not need it anymore.

I was on neurontin/gabapentin for neurological pain and it was helping, so I thought, maybe I don't need the Osteo anymore. So, I stopped taking it. I didn't really think much about it and, in the following weeks, I was really distressed by all the neck pain (had a fusion there too) and back pain and the leg and hip pain I was having. One day, it dawned on me, could it be the Osteo? I went back to taking it. In about a week or so... pain gone. Dang. I will never stop taking this again!

Really, try it, it will make your life so much better. But, give it time. It can take a couple weeks or even a month to really kick in (it has to build up in your joints). You can take a loading dose (double up on the dose for the first bit to make it help more quickly), but discuss that with your pharmacist or doctor, as everyone is different and this may be unwise for you in particular. This is also now helping my wife with her arthritis, though I will say it seems less effective there... it helps, but it is not the kind of miracle it has been with my back.

title: Time release capsules don't work
text:
I've recently done a fairly broad comparison (about 10) of leading Probiotic options on the market, so I feel like I have a good point of reference on this.

The Intestinal Fortitude 11 Billion CFU capsules are on the middle of my list. Here's why:
1) NO prebiotics included. Prebiotics are often extremely high in FODMAPS and can trigger symptoms in IBS users. This product has none.
2) Great tolerance - I found I was able to tolerance these perfectly well with no side effects. I can't say the same with some other Probiotics
3) No gimmicks. No exaggerated claims or extraneous additives like soil based organisms which many other products do

However there are some issues namely:
The time release capsules are not effective. They can, and very often do, go right through the GI track unopened. As an alternative, all is not lost, it's easy to open the capsule and empty the contents and take it directly on the tongue.

The other issue is that this is marketed by a relatively small company and most likely manufactured by some other vendor. There isn't much transparency on what lab is really producing this. The good news is that they appear to be manufactured in the US.

title: Great Entry Robotic Vacuum from Hoover!
text:
Hoover's BH70700 Quest 700 Bluetooth Enabled Robot Vacuum Cleaner for Carpet and Hard Floors is a member of Hoover's Fall 2016 new product release.

Hoover is a special brand in the vacuum industry. Indeed, in the United Kingdom, vacuuming is referred to as "hoovering." They are a pioneer of the industry.

Hoover's latest products aim to get them back as a premium brand in the space. Over the years, Hoover's products had been driven towards a race to be a more affordable option. While many of those options still exist, Hoover is now attempting to take on premiums brands such as Roomba and Dyson with some of its latest products.

This robot vacuum clearly takes on iRobot's Roomba brand. I have owned a Roomba for nearly five years, therefore, I was excited to check out Hoover's offering. Many of the features on this Hoover compare beautifully to my similarly priced Roomba. Automatic docking station, virtual wall, fantastic side brush, and bumper are features that make the two units very similar and perform nicely. In addition, this Hoover includes a remote control and bluetooth, features I do not have on my Roomba. The battery run time of up to 90 minute is also vastly superior to my Roomba.

Overall, operating the unit, I see similar performance to my Roomba, though the long battery runtime of this Hoover seems to make it more capable from the first use. I felt my Roomba always worked best on a super clean floor, the Hoover doesn't suffer as much if you have a corner or spot under some furniture that has been neglected a couple weeks. The Roomba would tend to get filled up or clogged up easier if you didn't start with a super clean room. Once the Roomba had been operating, automatically, several weeks, it was great.

The bluetooth and remote are handy, though a scheduled vacuuming is ideal. Running the unit in the same room or rooms 2-3x per week keeps the carpet looking oh so fresh. There really is no match for regular multiple times per week vacuuming. That would be a chore with a heavy, large upright vacuum. However, with the Quest 700 from Hoover, the robot does the work for you, which makes the multiple times per week vacuuming that leaves your carpet so fluffy, comfortable, and clean, easy to achieve. That is my favorite feature of robot vacuums, unlike people who might keep putting off the chore, the robot won't. You truly see over the first couple weeks, your carpet gets nicer and nicer. A 15 minute upright cleaning just can't match multiple, robotic vacuum sessions throughout the week.

My least favorite feature of these vacuums is cleaning out the bin, keeping the brushes clean, etc. It's a rather dirty job. That's why, again, it's best to start with a clean carpet and use these units for maintenance, that will keep down the maintenance you have to do on the robot!

I would also caution they are best to use in rooms and a home without cables, shoes, or other objects in their way. Otherwise, the robots are going to drag these objects around your room. You want a rather clear room for the robot. Furniture is fine, it will gently bump into it and change direction, but movable objects or cables are not so great.

Overall, Hoover has a very competent entry level machine with the Quest 700. I prefer it to my nearly five year old entry level Roomba. It's a great introduction to robotic vacuuming. Should my budget allow in the future, I would like to see if the features and performance of the higher end Hoover Quests might impress me even more. Still, this unit is a sweet spot. You get a lot of convenience and features at an affordable price.

I certainly recommend this Hoover Quest 700. I am excited to have this in my home!

title: Good Idea, Bad Execution
text:
I've had severe low-frequency hearing loss in one ear since early childhood, but the high-frequency hearing in that ear is sharp. I have very sharp, full-spectrum hearing in my other ear. Overall, the combination gives adequate hearing and I've never felt the need for a hearing aid. Still, I wondered what improvements might be possible if I boosted the low-frequency sound in my bad ear.

This product looked like a great and relatively low-cost way to see what improvement might be had by boosting the low frequencies in my bad ear. It is claimed that this hearing aid has four spectral modes: mode 1 gives uniform amplification, mode 2 boosts high frequencies, mode 3 boosts medium frequencies, and mode 4 boosts low frequencies. Mode 4 was of interest to me. It is also claimed that this hearing aid has six different volume (amplification) levels.

I was eager to see what this product could do for me. I inserted one of the pair of this hearing aid in my bad ear and wore it for a couple of evenings around the house, doing mundane house chores and chatting with my wife. I have these observations:

1. There seems to be very little difference among the four spectral modes. They all sound essentially the same to me.

2. In all spectral modes, including mode 4, high frequencies were WAY TOO LOUD! This was unpleasant and even painful at times. This was true even though I set the unit at the lowest of its six volume levels. (And there wasn't much difference I could hear between the six volume levels.)

3. I heard a distinct and annoying artificial background hiss continuously. This hiss probably would have been substantially less if I could have turned down the volume further, to a level appropriate for my ear. Also, this hiss might have been less if mode 4 worked better to amplify just low-frequencies and not high-frequencies as well.

4. I heard instances of fuzzy distortion on speech, and my own speech sounded very loud.

5. Here are some of the sounds that were jarring, unpleasant, and even painful in my hearing-aid-boosted ear: the sound of my fork hitting my plate, the sound of the door latch as I closed the utility room door, the sound of the washing machine lid as I closed it, and the sound of my wife's normally pleasant laugh from a distance of three feet.

After two evenings experimenting with this product, I don't ever want to put it in my ear again. Given that, I can't justify awarding it more than one star.

title: The almost-perfect tool kit for eye and sun glass repairs
text:
My wife and I both wear glasses, and without fail, whether it is our eye or sunglasses, a screw comes loose, a nose pad falls off, or the screws fall out completely, and we are left using tape or super glue to temporarily fix them. I have purchased small kits in the past, the kinds with usually two - four screws and the screwdriver is concealed in a small tube that connects to your key ring. If not on the key ring, they always get lost, and trying to get the screws in with just that little screwdriver is a bugger for my hands. I wanted a cape that had tweezers to help stabilize the screws while inserting into the respecting holes in my glasses, and I wanted a longer screwdriver with variable heads that could help me efficiently install the screws and make my repairs. I have several pairs of tweezers, but they are more cosmetic styled and not really suited for the fine point work needed for holding the screws.

This case has it all, and more! There is a small, portable screwdriver you can keep in your pocket or purse, and the screwdriver kit is long, contains easily changeable heads, and it is ergonomic. I haven’t carried it around with me in my pocket, but it could be used for EDC and leveraged for many different tasks if needed. The end stopper doesn’t stay inserted into the main body of the handle, though, and does require you to secure it frequently while in use. For this reason, I would just stick with my leatherman-style multi tool for EDC. But, this is for eyeglass repairs, and it pairs well with the XSIATO kit.

The tweezers are easy to grip, and the long, fine tip allows convenient and precise control over the tiny screws. This tool can also be used for many other tasks, but I am keeping it dedicated to this repair kit. The magnetizing piece performs without fail for me when I am trying to magnetize or demagnetize the tip of the screwdriver heads, which helps in screw retention while in use. I have not had to use the nose pad repair tool, yet, but I have practiced with it. It was new to me, but easy to figure out, and will be convenient to have, although many of my glasses are new just coming with a built-in silicone nose pad on each side of the glasses.

Next, the screws: there are tons of them! That is the good, along with the fact that there are (14) - (15) different sizes and types. The problem I have with them, though, is that there are so many options, yet they are grouped and packaged together into four different packages. This has been a little frustrating, as I would have preferred them to be better separated and organized. When I need a particular type of screw, I was able to locate it, and its pair, but it did take a while searching through the rest of the bag from which the first was located. I like to have order and be more organized, especially with such fine things like these screws, so I would have liked to see the case be built to allow more slots in for more size options and separations.

Finally, there is one more item that bugs me, probably the most, even more than the screw issue: the long, blue screwdriver and tweezers do not fit in the case. It is deceiving because both are no longer than the overall length of the case, which has a decent latch for keeping it closed, but there is a compartment or slor for the nose pieces or pads that shortens the length of the inner, longer slot where they could fit. Fortunately, the slots are structured by removable plastic inserts, which allows the two tools to fit. The problem, with this, however, is that now you can’t get the magnetizer tool to fit! Maybe everything fits, and this is just operator error, and I’m failing at my Jenga skills. To even get close to making them fit, though, now the eye pad pieces will have to be mixed in with another supply slot. So, I use another case to keep all of these items contained. This isn’t the end of the world, but as per the products marketing slogan on the packaging of ‘Efficient’ and ‘Convenient’, they could have improved this repair tool kit and made it a five star rating. Nonetheless, the supplies are solid, and have helped me fix two pairs of sunglasses, one pair of shooting glasses, and my wife’s favorite pair of glasses. You won’t go wrong with this kit, but just keep the organizational points in consideration.

title: Excellent Safety Kit for Any Emergency
text: In retirement, I am a full-time grandmother, meaning that on days my granddaughters are not in school and every day during the summer, I have them full-time. I always had a first aid kit in my car until I was rear-ended last summer which caused my car to catch on fire and burn completely - including all the contents. I knew I needed a replacement first-aid kit, and I wanted to be sure to get one which would cover any situation I could think of for active children. This one from Protect Life meets all my expectations. It has 200 pieces of anything you would need for an accident like a small cut or a large scrape. There are emergency supplies like a light stick and a rain poncho. I have eye pads and triangular bandages in case either girl ever needs an arm sling. In other words, I have more than I will ever need - hopefully. That is the beauty of this fully packed kit. I may need to cut a small piece of moleskin for a blister someday; I hopefully will never need a mouth-to-mouth resuscitation device. However, if either of these things is ever needed, I know where it will be - safely packed in the little red case in my car. The very reasonable price for this is a small price to pay for peace of mind where safety is concerned.

title: I love these pads.  My old ones are 20 years old and still good.  Just bought more!
text:
​As I was doing my floors I thought I would tell you about these pads that I use for my aluminum mop.

I have many different kinds of pads and have basically tried them all. I find the "blue" ones tend to smear and not pick up all the wetness if you are using a damp map. I think they are more polyester. These green ones are finer than the blue ones and more absorbent, more like a cotton-poly blend. As a result they are a little harder to push when wet because they make kind of a "firmer", more clinging, contact with the floor when wet, which is what make the floor super clean.

They are billed as dust mop heads and are great for that, but they are backed by an absorbent pad which makes them ideal for damp mopping. They are the only ones that don't smear the dried dog drool marks on my floor and they clean them off with one or two swipes, whereas I have to scrub with the blue ones. Plus they leave the floor nearly dry and the floor then dries in less than 5 minutes.

I highly recommend these.

title: Very firm, oily, and expensive
text:
This BodyMed Premium Hand Therapy Putty is surprisingly firm. I did select the firm one, but I didn’t expect it to be the hard. I can see how this would be helpful in improving grip strength and dexterity, but at the same time, I would be concerned of the negative effects of misusing this and arthritis; there are no directions or suggested exercises to give it more credibility, so you wouldn’t be able to tell the difference between this and any other putty like the kids toys. The price is quite steep in my opinion and it would be difficult to justify the cost without the benefits. Also, although the label states it is dry, there is definitely an oily solution on it which I don’t t necessarily find uncomfortable and is probably necessary to keep it from hardening even more, but would be nice to know what it is and if it is meant to be on there.

Overall this product isn’t bad; however, the price makes it more unappealing and the lack of information/labels/facts give it little credibility. Be sure to select the firmness appropriately as the this green one is a lot firmer than you would think putty would be. If you are looking for an alternative way to rehabilitate your finders/hands/forearms, and don’t mind the stew price, and believe this might work better for you than it did for me, then this might be the one for you.

title: Too bitter and not very effective
text:
First impressions were great, the concept is fantastic and the presentations is pretty good; however, the product itself fails to deliver greatness.

The first thing that hits once you spray this stuff in your mouth is the bitterness. Then comes a burst of not great flavor and very mild sweetness. I guess my expectation was that this product would be very sweet and flavorful rather than bitter. Getting through a couple of sprays is rough, but 5 sprays is a bit of torture unless you enjoy bitter things that don’t taste well. I gave the product a try a few times to properly review the effect on my energy levels, but I can’t say I felt much of a difference. Perhaps there was some increase in energy, but it must have been very mild; nothing like what you would get from an energy drink or an energy shot, and you still have to endure the bitter bad flavor and aftertaste.

This did not work for me in any level; however, that is not to say that it might not work for you, since these types of products affect people differently and it also depends on your sensitivity, so you might get the bursts of energy this product claims, but it just wasn’t my experience therefore I can’t really recommend this product. My recommendation to the manufacturer would be that they lower the bitterness and increase the sweetness and scent so it is a more pleasant experience.

title: Might be good for the slim and fit, but not if you are on the heavier side.
text:

Not much to be expected at the price point. The packaging was simple and ergonomic, though some maybe refer to it as cheap. Quality overall is okay for discounted price.

I’ve used the product for over a week now, and it could be the lack of instructions or simply my body type, but it is very uncomfortable to use. It does a good job at keeping your posture in check, but at the price of the straps digging into my armpits to the point that your armpits hurt after use.

The instructions for where the added pads needed to be added was nowhere to be found so there is a little guessing with a little common sense required, but the pads don’t provide much additional padding or support.

Overall, I would not recommend this product for the heavier set body types; but I feel that it would work great for someone with the physic of the people in the product pictures. I think it serves its purpose to keep your posture straight; it is just not for me, because the benefit of a straighter posture does not outweigh the discomfort/pain of using the product.

title: Easy to use with large lettering... As long you don't need settings or change user profiles.
text:
[[VIDEOID:12240cee47b83cc78b8ec6776437086b]] Pros:
• Works off batteries or plugged in with usb-c. It includes the batteries too!
• Buttons and numbers are large and clear, making it easy for people to use and read who may otherwise have difficulty.
• Blood pressure seems to be fairly accurate when comparing to my manual blood pressure cuff and my typical normal pressures.
• The base function is simple to use. Just press the center button and it turns on and starts getting a blood pressure.

Cons:
• Any complex functions are very confusing to use. These include going through settings or changing between user 1 and user 2. I consider myself very tech literate, work with medical tech frequently as part of my job, and was referring to the instruction manual. Its not easy to change between user 1 and 2 at all.

Overall:
• I think this is a fantastic blood pressure cuff with the large well lit font and the fact that it takes a simple button to start the blood pressure and turn it on. The device is solid, the cuff itself is solid, and it includes (almost) everything you need to use it either plugged into an outlet or battery powered. In general I don't think most people will need to change any settings so the biggest downfall is if you want to use the two separate user profiles as it is very complex to navigate. I would recommend if several people want to use the cuff in a household to just keep it on one user profile and just having them write the results into a notebook for themselves. That would keep this super simple and great for elderly family members.

title: smells fantastic but definitely only for moderately slow drains
text:
My condo is in an older building (built 1908) and though the plumbing has been updating, there are still years of crud and sludge in the pipes. Every month or so I am tasked with unclogging my bathroom and kitchen sinks, and having an eco-friendly drain opener has been my preferred choice over the chemical-laden products. I was eager to try this Enzyme Drain Cleaner, hoping it would be my go-to product. Here are my impressions:

PROS
* smells incredible and does a great job deodorizing sinks
* I have the liquid version, which is convenient and easy to use
* price per use is about $.50, which is reasonable for an eco-friendly drain cleaner
* multi-purpose is nice, not requiring separate solutions for toilet, sink, tub, etc

NEUTRAL
* works, to a degree. I tested it on a slow-ish, but not fully clogged, drain and it did open up the flow, though to not as much as expected

CONS
* given the lack of real strength, this product could be cost-prohibitive, as it requires more than one "serving" to fully flush out your system

VERDICT
Eco-friendly and deodorizing are a plus, but weak formula could be costly. Recommended only if you have been unsuccessful with other brands and want something new.

title: Won't recommend
text:
7I cannot say for certain this product caused my issues, but this is the only different thing I'd done. Here's my story:

I had a deep cleaning done at the dentist in September. I've waited about two months since having that done and continued with my thorough dental hygiene routine. I wanted to try to keep my teeth nice and white like after a dental cleaning so I decided to try out these Moon strips.

They are all the same, top and bottom. I find them to be a little small. The instructions say to use twice a day for two weeks. I find the twice a day to be a bit of a hassle. I tried doing it about 30 minutes after brushing in the morning and evening. The strips are pretty sticky in your mouth, but start dissolving pretty quickly. It does leave a bit of a film on your teeth once it's gone. The flavor is fine.

After 3 days of use, I noticed some discomfort along my bottom gumline. Upon further inspection, the gums at one of my bottom front teeth is now receding. I immediately have stopped using the strips and no longer feel the discomfort but my gums haven't gone back. I didn't notice my teeth looking any whiter after just 3 days. I have another dentist appointment now for December.

So, be weary trying these. Even without the issues, I don't think I'd recommend these strips anyway because of the instructions, tedious and inconvenient.

title: Concern over Evening Primrose Oil
text:
For safety's sake- READ LABEL for ingredients before purchasing, and research the ingredients. (I wish I had) One ingredient of concern is Evening Primrose Oil! This ingredient has contraindications with certain disorders and medications. From what I read : Evening primrose oil should not be taken if you have a history of seizures or schizophrenia- there have been reports of increased seizure activity when taking evening primrose oil. There have been drug interactions with evening primrose oil and anti-convulsants. I also read that there have been interactions with several psychiatric medications. I found anecdotal reports of increased risk of mania in bipolar disorder.

As always consult your doctor (and do your own research) before taking anything new. It also contains the following ingredients: Evening primrose oil, Black Currant Oil, Pumpkin seed Oil, Canola Oil, and Flax seed. If you've already researched omegas in general you already know that any omega 3's are a blood thinner.

NOTE to VEGETARIANS and Vegans- I can see how this might possibly be a good alternative source for omegas for people who do not eat fish, however it does contain gelatin without specifying if the gelatin is from an animal source.

ALLERGIES- although it does NOT contain yeast, wheat, gluten, soy, milk, egg, fish, or shellfish, it IS produced in a facility that processes other ingredients containing these allergens.

If the ingredients are safe for you to take, I encourage you to also read other reviews before purchasing so that you are aware of the type of Omega 3's in this compared to other options, to be sure this product meets your needs. And when comparing products for the sake of price you need to compare the numbers on the supplement facts and the serving size to do an accurate comparison, don't just look at price and number of gels. I will go back to taking :

What I will tell you, with certainty, is that as a result of those previous alignments by a great chiropractor and the continued use of this pillow, I only visit the my chiro Dr. about once every 3 months or so...just for maintenance adjustments!

I kid you not...if you are in the market for a good, supportive, cervical, orthopedically-correct pillow, and at a very fair price...look no further! I'm hooked on it, I've got my boyfriend hooked on it, and I just couldn't recommend the Core Products Tri-Core Full Size #200 highly enough!

Give it a try...follow the instructions, get used to it (use for about 2 weeks before making a decision), and I hope you love it like I do. BTW, this is in no way a fluffed up compensated review. title: From my experience with these types of devices, this one does not work.
text:
I've had experience with actual negative ion generators, and this one does not work at all.

It does not create a soft sizzling noise and create a soft flow of air from the graphite bristles.

Although the bristles do seem to be referenced to the mains voltage, the circuitry does not produce sufficient stepped-up voltage in order to produce the negative ion generation.

===============
Updated review:

After taking this device apart, I found that it is just a 120VAC to 5V-DC power supply for LEDs. One of the 5V outputs (in the picture marked "LED102" on the circuit board) is connected to the potted supposed high voltage multiplier circuits.

I de-potted the supposed high voltage multiplier circuit, and the circuit board is not populated with any electronic components like it should be (see first photo showing locations for some kind of component, but none have been installed). Additionally, the circuit board is just a straight through connection to the carbon fiber emitters (see the picture of the blue side of the circuit board with traces that go straight from the 5V input to the carbon fiber emitters).

This device is complete BS. The carbon fiber emitters are not fed with high voltage low amperage power. It is just supplying 5V to the carbon fiber emitters. There is no ionization taking place at that low of a voltage.

Total rip-off.

text:
Just about everybody in my family has hand issues ranging from arthritic joints to carpal tunnel.

Treatments in the past have ranged from hot wax dips (a mess if you’ve never tried one) to hot and cold compresses and the occasional (yet amazingly expensive) medical injection.

So, I decided to give this a try (or, more accurately, relatives gave it a try). It seems to combine the purported effects of hot and cold compresses without the mess and bother.

This is essentially a large plastic box with an included rechargeable battery and controls on the top for heat/cold, timer, etc. Just for the sake of simplicity, you get 3 modes and the ability to turn the heat on or off. No need to worry about complicated codes or button pushing.

Expecting something possibly miraculous, I was surprised to take a close look at the internals and discover it’s a modified blood pressure cuff. or an inflatable wrap if you so desire.

And here’s another surprise - you had better not have big hands. This works if your hand is small or not swollen with arthritic joints. Great if your hand is petite, but the fit might be a bit much for larger hands.

However, for the average person this might be just the ticket. Using alternating pressure cycles (inflate, deflate, inflate, deflate....) this unit provides a firm, yet comfortable, massaging action.

Oh, and by the way, if you're looking for something portable, this isn't it. It's larger than most tablets in surface area and several inches thick.

text:
My daughter loves to create characters through her theater skills and through her make-up and costume design skills. As a home school mother, I like to foster her gifts so every once in awhile I will purchase something for her that allows her to grow her skills. That was my thinking when I purchased the Kangaroo Professional Grade Liquid Latex Make-up for my 16 year old daughter. I had no idea how crazy things would get after it arrived. . .

Just about every day, I sneak out for some exercise at the gym, leaving my 16 year old daughter and 10 year old son to do school work. Lately, returning home I have found all manner of creatures instead of my children including a zombie and a ghost with a slit throat. Of course it doesn’t faze me because we are home schoolers and that is just normal.

WHAT IS IN THE BOX: One 4 ounce bottle of liquid latex. No applicators are included. The bottle looks nothing like the larger version in the picture on this listing as of the date of my review.

WHAT I LIKE: This is real latex. I know because my youngest has a latex allergy. I returned home to find my kids quickly scrubbing his chest one time when they decided to create a wound for him. They forgot. (Fortunately his skin just turns red temporarily and itches.)

Despite my son’s latex allergy, his reaction has so far been mild. In fact my kids want to recreate their wounds and head to Wal Mart. (Not going to happen.)

Realistic special effects can be created without any other special tools.

It dries quickly.

My kids love this stuff!

WHAT I DON’T LIKE: I love the product but I hate my son’s latex allergy.

PICTURES: I am including some of the effects my daughter created with this product plus some fake blood.

My kids have had a great deal of fun with this product and I would definitely recommend it to anyone who is interested in this sort of thing.

If you put a purse or anything in the bag that has a little weight in it, it makes the walker top heavy and you will be going head over heels. If I had known about the severe issues with walkers like this, I would have purchased another walker.
The wheels don’t glide over small rocks or uneven surfaces. You will make a sudden stop and be on the ground. If there is no handicapped access ramp and you have to go over a curb (it doesn’t matter how short or tall it is, even with help from someone), the short wheel base makes the walker flip. You will end up on the ground, with maybe nothing but a scrape or two. Maybe a trip to the ER for stitches after you crack your head open on said curb. Or worse with a broken neck or hip. So, if you want to live dangerously, this walker is for all you adventurers.

title: Beautiful urn, holds adult remains securely
text:
I purchased this urn for my son's girlfriend, whose father passed away far too young. It was a very painful time, made more difficult with tight finances. This urn was perfect. . . So attractive and peaceful. Family really loved the turquoise color and doves on the front - very ethereal and calming. And the price. . . Wow. The cremation office sold urns in the $200-300 range. How perfect it was to get this one and a small urn necklace for under $100.

On the issue of size: I read some reviews which caution about the size of the urn needed to accommodate adult ashes. That has to do with the weight of the deceased, so larger loved ones will need bigger urn, small urn for smaller person. Some urns give specs on pre-cremation weight... eg "will accommodate ashed of 180 pound person." That's helpful if you know the weight. But how does one ask this delicate question of a grieving child whose parent had dramatic weight loss during final weeks of life? We did not know the weight of the deceased, but he was an adult male over 6 feet tall, was stocky prior to illness. This urn was suitable in size and held the entirety of his ashes, no problem.

When looking at the pictures online, I was not certain whether the metal accents were gold, silver, bronze. In case you're wondering, it is a lovely silver trim.

text: So I picked this up mainly out of curiosity. I did a YouTube video experiment (Phreakwar PC Custom Builds is also my YouTube channel name if you wanna search for the video). Search for "Using a Lydsto breathalyzer to find my drinking limits". I did an initial check, slammed down some seltzers every 10 minutes and took readings. I noticed a bit of fluctuation in readings .vs my alcohol consumption, so not quite sure on the accuracy of the product. Might have just been my body so I am not going to claim it was the device. But anyways, through my own pseudo-experimenting, I figured 4 is my limit, 6 or 7 drinks I am impaired 100%. I'm gonna call this a not so 100% accurate, but VERY RELIABLE if that makes sense.. device for judging yourself or other's impairment levels. While I don't feel the readings it takes are a true representation, I think one might be drunker than what the readings will show, I think that for what it DOES pick up, it can easily say right on the spot if you should not be driving. Would advise if you are using this to judge party guests, if it goes into the "CAUTION" zone, you advise that person, if they are to be driving, to STOP their consumption. You don't wanna really go PAST that caution zone and risk it, so I think this meter is PERFECT for letting one know when they have reached that point and I can honestly recommend it for that use. For 100% accuracy though, it loses 1 star, but AGAIN, I DO RECOMMEND THIS PRODUCT.

title: Formula and Size Definitely Changed from the Original
text:
They definitely changed the formula for the better. I purchased this from a big chain store that was not Amazon. I suspect they are using less neem oil, which is a very strong off-putting oil originating from India.

Neem oil is known for its special healing/beneficial properties, but I always try to avoid shampoos, conditioners and lotions with it because the smell is just that pungent. The product still has a herbal/medicinal smell to it, but the smell is pleasant now. It is 1000% more tolerable now.

Before, I would only use this if I had no plans of going outside and interacting with other people. The smell would get in my sheets, even after I wiped off most of it, and I could smell the lingering smell of neem oil for days in my apartment.

I agree, the texture of product is different. It is a lot lighter than it was before, and the container is noticeably smaller. But, I prefer the change. It is still moisturizing and softening, and it smells so much better.

I am rarely ever affected by smell, but the smell of neem oil makes me nauseated. It is a shame, because Neem oil has such amazing properties.

title: as the Aveeno moisturizer I use during the day has sunblock in it (and there's no need to waste that at night)
text: This is an incredibly high quality night cream. I have fairly sensitive skin and needed something specifically to put on at night, as the Aveeno moisturizer I use during the day has sunblock in it (and there's no need to waste that at night). Rose-scented products can be nauseating so I was relieved to note that this is not too highly scented, just pleasant. It's a rich cream, but feels very light going on, absorbs quickly without feeling greasy, and leaves skin soft and supple by the morning. Compared to the night cream I recently tried at a salon during a facial (which was $60!), this is about an equal product at a fraction of the price. Highly recommended.

title: Large German Woman Taking Out Her Anger On You
text: This is by far the worst gift I have ever purchased. I ordered this for my 85 year old grandmother who often suffers from a stiff neck and tight shoulders. The idea is great, being able to determine how deep the massage is by pulling on the straps, easy to use, and it looks nice in the pictures. I read reviews, watched videos, and after my research, I believed I was buying the IT gift of the year...except it wasn't like that. I am so glad I tested this before leaving my Gram's house, because it was quite literally a reindeer wanting to run over my Grandma. It punched my mom in the head while she was trying to put it over her shoulders. My sturdy uncle tried it out, and he winced in pain. This is the worse massage anyone in the room had ever had. It feels like someone POUNDING into you, and it is relentless. The buttons are confusing even after reading the instructions, and the box says "Massage Blet" rather than "belt". If you are looking for this type of massage, and enjoy a good beat down, I would buy this. If you are hoping to bring your grandmother some relief, buy her a back scratcher and a nice blanket to match her sofa set. So thank you Viktor for the laugh, and I hope I can steer anyone who bruises away from this torture device!

title: put allergen information on the bottle
text:
If you want me to try a new probiotic, please put allergen information on the bottle. I take probiotics daily, and the bottle on my preferred Garden of Life brand, (Prostate+ variety) clearly states: Gluten Free, Dairy Free, Soy Free. These ADDOT WellLife Probiotic Capsules ARE NOT so-labelled. In my experience, the vast majority of probiotic supplements don’t make the non-dairy claim, and many explicitly say they contain milk. Because milk is typically the medium on which the lactobacillus active ingredients in the probiotic are grown. That raised my suspicion, and that’s not a good thing when I’m trying a new product that I’m putting in my stomach. Because I’m allergic to dairy and gluten. They both make me sick for a period of weeks, and they take down my sinuses and other parts of my immune system and potentiate sinus infections and other respiratory ailments. I get severe fatigue and headaches for weeks. I’m not lactose-intolerant, so I don’t get indigestion with dairy. After digestion, it gets into my bloodstream and cleansing it takes time.

In choosing to order these ADDOT WellLife Probiotic Capsules, I looked carefully to ensure they were non-dairy and gluten-free. And under the 4th bullet down under About This Item on the Amazon product page, we’re assured that they’re, “Free of gluten, wheat, dairy, sugar, soy, yeast, preservatives, and unnecessary additives.” BUT THERE’S NOTHING ON THE BOTTLE TO INDICATE THIS. There is a disclaimer on the Amazon product page, (below the Reviews section) that basically says the actual product may contain different ingredients than what’s on the product page. And to always read the label before consuming a product. I’m paraphrasing this disclaimer, so if you’re interested, please refer to it on the product page. Good advice, it seems.

Also, the product page headline banner says they have 1800 Billion CFUs. Seems odd that’s not stated as 1.3 Trillion. But the rest of the product page says it’s 60 Billion, but you have to read the fine print ON THE PHOTO of the label to see that’s per serving size of (3) capsules. With a serving size of (3) caps, 90 caps makes 30 servings and 30 times 60 Billion makes 1800 Billion (1.8 Trillion). But the TOTAL QUANTITY of CFUs IN THE BOTTLE is not usually the way probiotics state their content. It’s typically per serving, and if it’s the sum of CFUs for the whole bottle, they say that. Not a big deal, there’s not room in the headline banner description to qualify it. But when I’m talking about earning my trust, making me do math until I get the right formula for the stated CFU quantity isn’t your best pitch.

That said, I opened the bottle and took a capsule to honestly review this product. And I had more sinus inflammation than usual the next couple of days. The increased sinus inflammation may or may not have been related to taking one capsule of this probiotic. But given the dearth of allergen information on the bottle, I don’t expect to continue testing this brand. They didn’t gain my trust. I can’t recommend them.

title: This is for bangers, not bongs :)
text:
If you are planning on buying this product to clean your water pipe, look elsewhere. This product CAN be used for that, but it is much better suited for cleaning your quartz banger after a dab. This product will keep your quartz bangers crystal clear for probably 500+ dabs.

HOW TO USE :
I bought a bunch of dropper bottles from ebay (15ml) for like $4 and I fill those with the dark crystal and then drip it into my banger right after a dab. Be careful not to let it bubble up and over the nail (I wait about 30 seconds), because then when you torch that stuff that bubbled over on the outside it will get burnt on and will never come off, so just keep it on the inside and you're golden. Then take a Q-tip and rub it around with about 10 drops of dark crystal and it will lift up all of the left over oils and clean your banger like it's brand new.

You can also use this stuff and some steel wool to restore a gunked up old quartz banger, just take a microwavable container that fits your quartz banger nicely and fill it will the dark crystal, then microwave it until it is nice and warm. This will speed up the process. I do this about 5 times over the course of a day and once I feel like I have soaked it enough then I take some tweezers and a little bit of steel wool and jimmy rig a sort of "Steel Wool Q-Tip" to scrape the crusties off my old nast banger, and then after about 3 minutes it will look good as new!

title: Great scooter. One issue. No instructions to unlock front wheels.
text: This is my first mobility scooter. I was very disappointed over the turning radius. It was horrible. Guess what? You have to unlock the front wheels. I had three different people plus myself read the instructions. No where does it say anything about unlocking the front wheels. There is a small knob at the front of the scooter at the bottom of the steering wheel column that you have to pull out on and turn. LOL. Scooter is great. Has plenty of power. Looks very nice. The headlight is bright. I would recommend reflective tape and additional lights if used at night. The wheels are solid rubber, so the ride is a bit bumpy, but you cannot get a flat using it outside. It is sluggish on grassy areas, but I expected that. I have a very steep driveway and it handled it perfectly. It comes with a five year extended warranty. Is it the quality of a scooter costing several thousand? No. For under a thousand with free delivery, this was a Godsend for someone living on a budget. I would recommend this to anyone wanting to get a bit more freedom.

title: Disposable, loosely woven, facial wipes that do not absorb a lot of product.
text:
The wipes work great for distributing skin care products across the skin. They have a lot of surface area due to their loosely woven cloth, but at the same time, they do not actually absorb a lot of product so you use less and more of the product ends up on your skin. We use them for facial cleansers and toners. You get a lot of these wipes, 200 of them so they will last awhile. They are lint free which is nice and they do not generate dust. They come in simple packaging so we transferred them into a glass jar for storage. We use facial cloths like this all the time in the small salon in our wellness center.

Summary: 4/5 stars for fulfilling item description of being disposable, loosely woven, facial wipes that do not absorb a lot of product.

I purchased these facial wipes at a discount in exchange for my honest and unbiased review. As a matter of routine, I give items that meet their descriptions a rating of 4 stars, and 5 stars if they exceed my expectations. title: ABSOLUTELY AMAZING!! NO-BRAINER PURCHASE!!
text: Bought this after reading a review elsewhere from a professional detailer. Figured it would be just like goo-gone and not work any better, but we were desperate. I tried goo-gone on the old decal glue on the truck and it did nothing whatsoever. Not even with a magic eraser. Opened this bottle of Rapid Remover and it smells just like goo-gone. Uh-oh! Well, I can assure you it is NOT goo-gone. Sprayed RAPID REMOVER on the old glue residue and in less than 5 minutes the truck door was as clean as a whistle. You'll definitely want a plastic razor to scrape the stuff. We bought one of those rubber wheels thinking we'd need to use that, too, but NOPE!! This stuff really is amazing. It took me longer to get the red rubber stopper out of the bottle than it did to remove 4 lines of decals on the side of one truck door!! Spray on, wait 1 to 1-1/2 minutes, scrape off (SLICK!!!), grab a rag and spray a little on the rag, wipe up any leftover residue, grab a spray bottle of water, rinse the door and you're done! Some spots we had to spray a little more on, probably didn't give it quite enough time to do it's thing. Seriously, though, this was a GREAT PURCHASE. On hindsight, I would have purchased a much, much smaller bottle. We probably didn't use even 2 ounces to do two truck doors!! title: Makes it like that bag of Doritos at 2am never even happened ...
text:
Probably the greatest thing about being a grown-up is that at 2am I can drive myself to the convenience store, buy myself a whole family size bag of Doritos and a full container of French Onion dip, and make a decision- void of all logic and reason – that I don’t have to answer for – about whether to eat them there in the parking lot or to bring them home and eat them standing in front of the TV in the kitchen. The second best thing about being a grown-up is that I can afford to buy myself little things that effectively hide the fact that at 2am I’m scarfing full bags of Doritos in the parking lot of the Stop-N-Go. These great compression arm sleeves are my favorite way to make it seem like the Doritos never even happened.

The Presadee Compression Arm Sleeves have made a huge difference for me – in how I look, how I shop for dresses, and how I feel. title: Letizia Mattiacci has published a beautiful Italian cookbook
text:
Letizia Mattiacci has published a beautiful Italian cookbook. The book is broken down by season, and weights are conveniently given in both volume and metric weight.

The book is not only overflowing with recipes but photographs of the beautiful countryside and dishes as well as stories of Italian life including a piece entitled How to Make and Drink Coffee Like an Italian.

Letizia starts us off with Food Processor Pasta Dough and includes recipes for Gluten Free Dough and many other pasta variations such as Kamut Flour Cappelletti, Stringozzi and Maltagliati. Breads and pizza are covered as well. The recipes and instructions (including step-by-step photographs) are wonderful for porchetta. And the desserts — Salted Almond Praline Gelato, Lemon Profiterole Delights, Limoncello Melon Panna Cotta and Grazia’s Chantilly Cream – all looks tempting. The book is chock full of delicious Italian creations.

I made the Umbrian Style Chicken Alla Cacciatoria from the book and it tastes heavenly - the sauce was incredible. Great instructions, wonderful flavors and not overly complicated.

This is a gorgeous book and one I will turn to again and again. Letizia teaches us that Italian food can be light and fresh and very accessible to everyone.

text: I honestly didn't know what to expect from using one of these reusable dental floss variants. But I did know I hated using my fingers/hands to floss and it's what put me off from regularly doing it as I should. Enter the eco-friendly Lessmore dental floss set. It comes with a very appropriately sized floss holder (it looked too big on first impression, but upon using it's actually great), a base for which the floss holder can stand in, and a spare roll of (mediocre) floss that can be stored in the base. I like the design and utility provided by the floss holder and the base. I am disappointed with the supplied floss and I immediately switched it out for my own Glide floss. Which brings me to another point; the base and the floss holder work with your own floss! It's an easy and convenient tool to keep up with flossing. I usually set it up again after using it so it remains ready and reminds me to floss. The final setup can be a little large/space-consuming (in my opinion, for a flossing tool), but that keeps it noticeable to prompt me to floss.

title: A Roll of Disappointment
text:
UPDATE: It's been less than a month, the roller has already changed colors, and does not stick at all anymore. I am kind of glad this happened before the 30day return policy as I will now be returning this. Very disappointed!

===============================Original Post=================================
We have a short haired Pitbull and have had many issues with her shedding. The traditional lint roller just doesnt cut it, we go through one roll every other week and it doesn’t even clean that much. So when I saw this product I was pretty excited, we had one of these in the 90s and as I recall it worked wonders!

However, compared to the ones in the 90s, this particular model, while working better than most lint rollers on the market, it still isn’t the best, and if compared to the original ones in the 80s, this is far less effective on picking up hair.

The gel on the roller is very thin, which makes it harder to stick and pick things up, it only works on certain surfaces so it’s a hit or miss with whatever you’re trying to use it on. I find that it is the easiest to clean the roller under hot water, and dry it with a microfiber towel (if you are trying to reuse it within minutes as it doesn’t pick up everything in one setting). As far as not having my drain clogged, I bought one of these drainshrooms which picks up the mess and prevents everything going down the drain and clogging your drain later.

Overall, it is an okay product that’s better than most but not the best, and if I could find anything better I wouldve returned this.

title: Really great pouch for a great price
text:
I have a lot of attention to detail so I can usually find a few problems with most bags, but this is one of the best designed bags that I've ever bought so I couldn't find any issues with it. Great stitch work, attached MOLLE straps, a small handle at the top which can be hidden under the velcro between the pouch and the flat backing with the MOLLE straps. It has a cinch strap on the back which you can unbuckle and flip around the front if you want to compress the bag to save space, but if you fully stock it then you won't need it so I plan on removing it. There's also a vecro strap at the top of the pouch, the only two things that I think it could be used for are to slow small children from getting in the pack or more likely if you were to use it in a combat situation you could close it with this strap instead of using the zippers which would save a few seconds. I'll probably remove this also but some people might want it so I see why they included it.
But once you open the bag is when you can see how great the design is, there's a zippered pocket which hinges out, the middle section which is the main compartment, and then the top compartment which swings out from the body. When I started loading the pouch up I realized that left to right starting with the pouch on the left side the pouch can be used as a three section first aid kit which can be used chronologically- the zippered pouch can hold saline wipes, insect sting wipes, bandaids, alcohol pads (for very small wounds, or when you have nothing else, but saline wipes are better for wounds), burn pads, and anything else you may need for small issues. The second compartment is for more serious issues, you can put sterilized gloves, quick clot (gauze with impregnated activated charcoal I think it is to slow bleeding), sterilized pads, an Israeli bandage, or anything else that you need for moderate issues. The final compartment can be used for really serious issues, I put large absorbent pads, large burn pads, large gauze, and the scissors here- if you look at the picture the two pockets have a velcro strap to hold them shut and there are three MOLLE style elastic loops to hold the scissors which are included, tweezers, a small scalpel, etc.
Really great pouch for a great price, I was really impressed with everything about it but especially the design and build quality.

title: Don't buy a bucket before this arrives
text: It is what it is - a toilet seat you put on a bucket to make a camp toilet. They claim it will fit on any 3 to 6 gallon bucket, which is true, more or less. It doesn't fit tightly - or securely - on a "pickle bucket" I got from a fast food place; but it does work. I advise you get this first, then find a bucket at Lowe's Hardware or Home Depot that it will securely snap onto, and buy that. I weigh around 230 to 240 pounds, a friend who also tried it out weighs around 300 pounds; it is comfortable to use and sturdy enough to support either of us. I like having it for those late night or early morning "calls of nature", so I don't have to go out in the dark to find either a bathroom or a safe spot to go. I'm in the process of setting up a "permanent" campsite, and this will be part of the gear I use there, for inclimate weather and such. You can buy those bags that gell the waste, or use small trash bags, or just put a layer of cheap kitty litter in the bottom and add more after each go - any of those options or a mix of them will help control odors and make cleaning it out easier. A mix of sawdust, kitty litter and baking soda works too, absorbing liquids and smells. For the price, it's fine.

text:

If some people do as I often do and fail to read the directions they might be missing an important step. I happened to find a u-shaped plastic piece in the box. Reading the directions, for once, I found that it is supposed to go over the hole on the back wall inside the unit. If it is not in place and the unit is overfilled or you slosh around the wax too much, the wax most certainly will go onto your countertop or wherever you keep your unit.

I made a living working outside in all seasons. The extreme cold caused my fingertips to crack and bleed. The warmth soothed my cold, aching hands when I got home from work and the paraffin softened my hands. Now that I am retired, it gives me relief from arthritis and an affliction in one hand called Reflex Sympathetic Dystrophy.

Buy the unit. You won't regret it.

title: Good idea, bad execution
text:
I had used plexus Slim several years ago, and liked the original formula. Once they changed it, however - it wasn't a good product. Omni Health has developed a name for itself for making decent copies of other brand name diet formulas - so when I saw this, I decided to give it a try. Omni advertises Slim Stix "as compared to Plexus Slim" on its packaging - so that got my attention. They are not skirting around the comparison what so ever.
Indeed, the ingredients look very similar to the Plexus Slim from about 2 years ago. It comes in the same single serving sachets, and contains roughly the same amount of calories per serving. That is where the similarities stop however. Smell-wise, the Slim Stix have a chocolate-y odor. They actually smell pleasant. It reminds me of the Plexus Slim 'tootsie roll batch'.
However, taste is where it fell apart. I could only manage to drink 2 mouthfuls. The drink was revolting. Once mixed with water, the chocolate scent disappeared, and it tasted like I was trying to drink perfume. Just couldn't do it. Now, maybe it gets it's appetite suppressant properties from making you nauseous. I have no idea, but you are a bigger person than I if you can manage to drink this.. I wanted to like it because I would love to have a product that worked like the original Plexus Slim, but sadly, this isn't it.
