title: Subtle but effective!
text:
This review was composed over the course of 7 hours, to demonstrate its effectiveness of this product on this reviewer

I read various reviews before I bought a "shot" and was mixed on whether or not to try it for myself. This past weekend was Daylight Savings coming into effect and I've been dragging my face on the ground at the office all week so far, so when I saw it at the checkout when I bought gas this afternoon, I bought one.

It sat on my desk for about 1/2 an hour until I couldn't take my lagging anymore and thought, "even if it doesn't work, it won't do me any harm," so I opened it and consumed the tonic in the little plastic bottle.

Ugh, I must say, it tasted like liquefied chewable baby asprins, a flavor I will never forget remembering how much I hated it intensely when I was a child. I was not disappointed for long, though. At first I felt somewhat relaxed, probably from swinging my head back so quickly to guzzle it down, I was experiencing a head-rush. Then, I could feel a slight awakedness I haven't felt all week. And now, about a half hour later, I don't feel "buzzed" like I have from those energy drinks, but I do feel awake. Not bouncing, not hyper, not doped-up, just alert. What a great feeling!

[An hour and a half later note]: Still feeling good.

[2 hours later]: The same, cool!

[3 hours later]: I can't recall how tired I was this past week, I still feel great after consuming this 5-Hour Energy shot, glad the earlier part of this week is a distant memory, nothing like trying to function when you're tired and out of sorts. This stuff did the trick.

[5 hours later]: Still not tired like I was, but I think it is starting to wear off. But - NO JITTERS! And no cravings for more, like I've experienced with the energy drinks.

[6 hours later]: No crash. Thanks goodness, that's something I dreaded.

[7 hours later]: Not tired, but also not quite as awake as I was a few hours ago. However, if I had used an energy drink, I'd probably be reaching for another one after the usual crash. They say those energy drinks are non-addictive, but anyone who's ever experienced that "can't cope-need more" feeling is addicted, which I had and was to the RB for a whole summer last year. It took me weeks to get over the hump of those cravings, not because I loved the taste, but because my initial tiredness went to a whole new level where no matter what I did with sleeping more, eating better, etc., nothing seemed to perk me up anymore as it had before I ever tried RB. After about 6 weeks I finally felt normal again where fresh foods and the occasional coffee gave me a boost when I felt tired from working all day.

I am glad to know the 5-Hour Energy shot works for me. I suppose if someone is an excessive coffee drinker it might not work, or if someone has a slower metabolism, perhaps it might not take full effect. I say to anyone (except to sufferers of any heart conditions, etc, as noted on the label) to give this stuff a try when all you really need is to just "snap out of it" and wake up - not when you're cramming for an exam, leave it to those energy drinks and stuff for that sort of thing. For someone looking to just take the edge off of feeling dragged down, I think this is the best thing out there right now; two thumbs up from me!

title: Quick Horse Hair
text:
The middle of the road with this product.

I bought this for my daughter as she was interested in it and she also kept using my hot air round brush. She said the Apalus brush hair straightener made her hair look "fried", so I thought I'd give it a try myself before returning it.

One thing I really love is that it straightens my dry hair in about 15 minutes. As opposed to using my round hot air brush which took a good hour with damp hair. I have quite a bit of thick, curly long hair, like Amy Irving or Dee Snider from Twisted Sister, which means it takes a very long time to straighten. So the quickness of straightening dry hair is a real plus.

However, after using the Apalus, my hair did look "fried" after it was straightened, like the texture of a horses mane/tail. Not smooth and shiny but dry and frizzy and stick looking.

It helped somewhat when I put some gel and frizz serum through my hair and then put my hair in a twisted bun for about an hour to compress the strands and give it some shine. I also used my In-Styler to get it to compress and look silkier.

I definitely prefer the look and feel of my hair after drying it with my round brush dryer over the Apalus, but as I mentioned my round brush dryer takes an hour because I have to section it into very small pieces and it just takes forever plus I developed tennis elbow, even though I did it every other washing or less.

The speed of the time straightening of the Apalus just really appeals to me, so I will keep it for that reason, but it's not something I can do right before I leave the house unless I want to have that "horse hair" look or walk out with a twisted bun. I am just really amazed at how quickly it does the job, it's just too bad that the results aren't smooth and shiny like my round hot brush or the Instyler, which both take so much longer.

title: Perfect for my salad dressings (and other things)!
text:
I have been using MCT oil since 2015 – and I use it every day. Mostly I use in it my salad dressing, which started out as being avocado, MCT oil, sea salt, turmeric (powder) and pepper. I started using it to make raspberry vinaigrette, which is delicious. And now recently began to incorporate dulse, garlic, cilantro, fresh turmeric, fresh ginger and apple cider vinegar to make it even healthier. Of course, I could use other oils, like a walnut or macadamia nut oil, but MCT oil is processed very differently in the body, which is why I continue to use it daily.

This particular MCT oil from Strength Genesis comes in a clear bottle and is the most beautiful bottle of MCT oil that I have seen! It is tall and sleek – and actually made it onto my counter top! It even comes with a lid/cork, which serves to seal off the MCT oil once you are done pouring it. I actually have one of those green salad dressing bottles that I pour my MCT oil into (because most bottles are quite large), but I don’t have to do that with this brand.

I appreciate that the company informs you of the quantities of C8 and C10 in the oil (on the back of the bottle). If you are new to MCT, I recommend that you work your way up to a tablespoon. If you go straight to using one tablespoon, you may end up with gastric upset, so it’s best to start with 1 teaspoon and see how that goes. Most say the taste is imperceptible, but I always feel like MCT oil has sort of a nutty taste. I love it!

If you want to give some weight and smoothness to your shake, you can add some MCT oil. It’s tasty right out of the bottle (yes, I consume it straight for a kick of energy) or in any salad dressing! The limitation with MCT oil is that you cannot cook with it because of its low smoke point, so keep that in mind.

I went to their website and you can see that their company is focused on wellness – and I love this mission. They sell a range of wellness items and even have some delicious-looking recipes (ahem, “Avocado Breakfast Bowl”) to try. I do recommend this MCT oil because the quality of the oil is superb and the company’s mission for wellness is something I am completely on board with!

title: Definitely helps streamline my focus!
text:
I love checking out products like this, and the best time to test them is when my mind is jumping from task to task! I have used a wide range of nootropics (note that is product is called “Nitropics”), and each of them has a different mechanism of action. Some ingredients in some of these supplements actually make me sleepy! This one does not.

What I like about this product is that it contains vitamins and herbs (among other ingredients), so I am familiar with nearly everything on the label. I decided to try it on the days when I felt that my mind was surveying all of the tasks without concentrating on a single one. Clearly, many mornings, I just have so many things I am trying to do before a client call, and I feel like I am going in circles between feeding the cats and dogs, preparing my morning shake, getting ready, etc.

I did feel like this helped me streamline my focus. I suppose that much of the time I am looking at the overview of everything that must be completed either before I can actually start my day, and then also at my task list once the day is underway. Apparently this creates overwhelm for me – and that’s in spite of my morning meditation!

I tend to take this on the days when I need to have laser focus to get a large number of things done, or when I notice that I am jumping around from task to task and start to feel frazzled. This product has helped me concentrate on the task at hand as opposed to doing something for 60 seconds and jumping to something else, leaving the other task incomplete.

This product is non-GMO and caffeine-free, both of which I appreciate because another supplement I use already has caffeine. The suggested use is from 1 to 3 capsules, but the serving size for the ingredients listed is 3 capsules. Because I take other supplements that contain caffeine, I split up the dose, taking 2 capsules two hours after taking the caffeinated supplement and 1 capsule later in the day. This avoids one product potentiating the other.

Overall, I absolutely recommend this product. It provides quite a number of ingredients, many of which I have researched, so I know the research supports the intended outcome. If you often feel like your “task list” creates overwhelm (perhaps you are an entrepreneur?!), then find a program that helps you organize your tasks and take a product like this to help you achieve levels of focus to complete those items that you might not otherwise achieve.

title: Nearly impossible to apply, so how do you know it works?!
text:
I had been using Dermacrine and thought I had hit the jackpot with this product having similar ingredients. The problem is that applying it is incredibly difficult if not almost impossible. It is liquid without any type of viscosity (maybe one step up from water) and goes everywhere if you aren't careful. It is incredibly difficult to even wash off the of the sink and if you get it on your hands, you have to wash your hands (maybe scrub?) several times with Dial soap to remove it. I had read in a forum somewhere that using a syringe to measure it would be useful since the syringe that comes with it is completely useless, and the reality is that a syringe is the ONLY way to achieve any kind of specific dosage. However, you are still squirting the liquid from the syringe and if you miss the palm of your hand, your poor aim might end up land on the wall or the bathroom door! (This depends on how "new" your syringe is.) After a few days of using the syringe, it has to be thrown out because since the liquid is tough to clean, you can forget about cleaning out the syringe thoroughly for the next use. This makes the plunger difficult to press down going forward, rendering the syringe useless.

I really had high hopes for this product, and actually dread putting it on, hence it is collecting dust in the bathroom cabinet. I ditched using the syringe and now just pour a dime sized portion in the palm of my hand when I use it and hope for the best. They seriously need to return to the drawing board on this one, but I think they have heard this same feedback multiple times. I think the ingredients are the right ones, and I don't doubt the line-up, but it doesn't do you much good sitting in the cabinet.

title: The Pros and Cons As I Feel ‘Em!
text:
I had wanted this cushion for some time and was delighted when I received it as a gift. I had wanted this largest-of-all the Purple Cushions because it most closely matched the dimensions of the chair I had earmarked to use it with.

When I first sat on it I was thought I may have made a mistake in wishing for this cushion. It felt rather odd.
I did adjust well to it though and have now used it for several months. We all need/want cushions for different reasons. For me, after two spinal surgeries, I was hoping to mitigate the chronic pain I have, and hoped to add some comfort to the chair I use for sewing. From my point of view here re the pros and cons as I “feel” ‘em:

The Pros:
1. I do think that the gridded construction of the material does help disperse heat. My sewing area is in a loft with a very low ceiling and in the summer it gets SO hot! I have been able to spend a bit more time up there this summer because my derriere feels a bit more comfortable with this cushion.
2. It IS supportive.

The Cons:
1. The “non-slip” cover is not very non slip. I have tried it on a variety of chairs and it it slips on them all. I feel that the fabric used for the cover should be: a) more substantial (while it is a nice, stretchy, knit it is a bit thin) and b) have a much beefier, much more ‘non slip’ fabric on the bottom of the cover. I may make a new cover for I myself. I also think that a sturdier cover would increase the comfort factor since it would minimize the feeling of the gridded purple material. In home dec sewing some cushions are first wrapped in polyester first to add support for the cushioning material and, imho, that would not be a bad thing.

Other than that I DO find it to be a comfortable, helpful, cushion. I am older, and relatively petite and perhaps the Purple Royal or Double would have been a better choice for me. For larger people this would be great. I can really see it making a big difference, in a positive way, for truckers and those who spend a lot of time in their cars.

I thought perhaps I should have gotten a foam type alternative, but that would not have helped disperse the heat at all! I thunk my decision to get this cushion was good in long run….

title: There's Good & There's Bad
text:
After reading a lot about this cushion both on Amazon and on the company's website I decided to give it a try. I read all of the reviews too - both the good and the bad. My review of this cushion is neither all 5 starr nor all 2-3 stars.

There are some 5 stars qualities about this cushion:

1. The comfort. I have had 2 back surgeries and wanted a cushion for my desk chair and also to take along with me on art related retreats. The comfort level of this cushion is excellent. I can see where you could sit on this for a long time and remain comfortable. The gel itself is also a bit cooling which I really like. NOT cold - just cool. I would definitely recommend this cushion for it's comfort - and that a big thing- and it's the main reason that I decided to try this particular cushion. I can have my foot tucked under my butt and my foot remains comfortable and doesn;t go to sleep. That's an excellent plus!
2. The cover. This model comes with a nylon cover that will be easy to remove and wash. It fits very well, works great and looks good too.

The 3 stars of what's good:
1. The weight. I don't know exactly what it was that I thought this would be like but it IS heavier than I had expected. It's in the gel of course, and it makes perfect sense that it would not be aslight as either regular foam or memory foam. It's no bother to me and the weight would not be at all prohibitive for any but the frailest.

The 1-2 stars of what is NOT so good about this cushion:
1. I am not a very large person - neither heavy nor stick thin -, but this cushion is, indeed, a bit smaller than I would have liked it to be - especially for the price! It does not quite fit my aging office chair all the way around. My butt hangs off just a bit in the back and the cushion ends mid thigh ( I do have short legs). The size of this cushion could be deal breaker for some people I think.

I can really see where larger people, or people who are using these cushions in their big rigs or larger car seats would find it a bit inadequate in size. It's really too bad because the cofort is there - but the size is a bit frustrating.

I like it, but I think I will return it and try something else that will be a bit larger... I'm sad - I really like the comfort -- but I wanted to be able to 'sink' into this cushion the way you might i na generous chair and the size is just not here to allow that to happen. If this had been larger I would have bought a second one rather than make a return.

title: Best sleep mask EVER...
text:
Caution: I am going to gush about this sleeping mask!

I have been in search of the perfect sleeping mask for 20 years. I’ve found ones that I liked using at the time I purchased them - but looking back, they were more decorative than functional. They were better than nothing, but there was a light of light creeping through. For quite a long time, silk outer, cotton-ish flat sleep masks were all that seemed available.

Masks then became available with newer, more elastic fabrics like this mask began to be produced. The masks also seemed to get bigger at that time, especially when compared to the flimsy decorative silk masks. I liked my first mask of the “new generation" very much. It barely let any light in at all. But it also came with such a large band that even though it had a velcro adjuster for size, it was way too big. I added in a very small safety pin to tighten it up. Never quite got there. The mask was also a flat front - which these new thicker masks made quite warm. It had it’s good and bad points.

Then I tried this mask and I knew that my search was over. That does sound dramatic, I know, but I love this mask! It functions literally like a blindfold, as advertised. It has much the same fabric and thickness of my previous mask, but the way that the eye covers are 3D contoured is EVERYTHING. I hadn’t realized just how miserable and warm I had been during my long search until I came across this mask that makes no contact with my eyes. It doesn’t cause any unwelcome warmth in the mask area. I use it all the time and can’t imagine using another mask. It has the same type of around the back of the head with velcro band, but this band and it’s velcro are thoughtfully sized.

I’ve recommended this mask to all my friends who use masks and purchased others for my mother and my sister. The price point is quite reasonable and allowed me to send them as “thinking of you,” gifts. All that have tried it in my circle love as much as I do. I give it my highest recommendation.

title: Works for me...
text:
I find cleaning products, in general, a gigantic, dollar-sucking hassle. If we we all go along with a custom cleaning product for everything we clean around our homes - we’d need to make serious room for grout cleaner, toilet cleaner, surface cleaner, etc., etc., There’s a “best” in class cleaning product for just about everything - if that’s what we choose to believe. I gravitate to products like this hydrogen peroxide to take care of my cleaning needs.

HP is a known chemical that comes with no surprises. It cleans and disinfects quite well given the chance. I read through a few reviews and found some to be a little harsh on the price. It doesn’t surprise me that it’s $25. for the gallon (where’d the $40. price come from?). Buying ANY liquid online and having it shipped is going to cost extra. It’s heavy and it could leak, so packaging is important. It’s pretty cheap when buying it in person, but through the web - there’s ALWAYS a markup. It’s a given.

The GreenFist product has worked well for me in the applications I’ve tried it on. But my favorite “before and after” was on the cream colored grout in my guest bathroom. I had a couple of nieces living with me for a few years and they managed to make some sections of the grout go a yucky brown. My niece took a crack at it with grout cleaner. No improvement. I tried the same cleaner with a serious scrub brush and a lot more shoulder into it. No progress. I used this hydrogen peroxide with a wash cloth and not much muscle and the brown was gone in a minute (with an extra few minutes of drying time). There was no “film” on the floor from the grout cleaner I had to deal with the first go arounds. It worked.

This is the type of cleaning solution that works great for me - it’s versatile and has no scary chemistry in it. The HP emits a nice orange scent as I use it, not the smell of serious chemicals. It’s perfect for me. Recommend!

title: Decent bath bombs with very light scent
text:
I spent several nights trying out these bath bombs. There are two of each scent and they are on the smaller side in comparison to many other bath bombs on the market today, so I ended up using two bath bombs for each bath in my somewhat larger tub. On the plus side, they are long-lasting and take awhile to completely dissolve, meaning that the scent and oils keep getting added into the water as you're in the bath. The scents are very light though - it was pretty faint the first time I tried them, and then I couldn't smell the next scent the next two times unless I literally held the bomb right up under my nose. It's too bad, as what I could smell was very nice. The other thing that puzzled me was that there was no description of the scents included on or in the box itself, so there's no way to tell which bombs you are using. I had to go and look at the picture in the listing to figure out the scents.

Overall, if you like very light floral scents and have a smaller tub, these will probably work. If you have a larger tub and prefer a stronger scent, these may not work.

title: Some things to consider before you buy.
text:
For the most part, these insoles are pretty much what you’d expect by looking at the pictures, so I won’t restate what’s obvious and stated in many other reviews. But I will list below some things that might NOT be quite so obvious, and that you should think about if you are considering purchasing this item:

The insoles themselves really don’t offer much (arguably, none, in my opinion) arch support by themselves. You’d have to add the little sponge pads to the insole in order to get any significant amount of arch support. Note that these insoles DO NOT have a built-in hard plastic arch support like many other insoles and orthotics do. In my personal opinion, if what you seek is a very firm, high arch support, the ones having the built-in hard plastic piece under the arch may be a better option for you.

Insofar as the sponge pads that you can stick on, that sounded like an attractive feature to me initially, because I could customize the support/padding to my personal preference. But I feel there are a few downsides to this that you should consider:

It can (and probably will) take several trial-and-error adjustments to get a pad positioned “just right” so that it feels perfect. Doing this requires you to stick the pad on, put it into the shoe, and walk on it. But then you have to remove the pad, move it a little, and stick it back on, and walk on it again. Still not perfect? Do it again! Because you’re removing and reapplying that pad, the glue is likely becoming less sticky with each removal. Meaning, the pad becomes more likely to later lose its grip on the insole and slide out of position while you’re walking long distances, especially if the insole gets warm/sweaty or wet for long periods due to water leaking into the shoe, or even just perspiration..

Even if you manage to stick a pad on in the perfect position the first time and never remove it, I am still concerned that the adhesive will eventually give way and with the addition of friction between the pad and the shoe itself, the pad may slide out of position over time. And then it will become uncomfortable and not provide the desired support. Consider how annoyed you might get if that happens. Would you be annoyed? (be honest!) Would you consider it to be wasted money? If so, perhaps you might not want to take the risk and maybe a one-piece insole would be a better option for you.

The insole relies on the use of the stick-on pads not only for arch support, but for heel and forefoot padding as well (if you want that). So on my insole, I have a pad under the forefoot, a pad under the heel, and two pads stacked under the arch. While some might love to have that level of customization, I actually find it rather overcomplicated and kind of Macgyvered to “make it work”, if you know what I mean. And not very visually sleek in my opinion (not that this matters much, given that it’s on the bottom of the insole). I find that I’d much rather just have a one-piece insole that comes with good heel and forefoot padding built in, and a hard plastic (and high) arch support. Something that I can use right out of the box, and be happy with. Yes, it takes some trial and error to find the perfect model for my foot, but once I find it, I will likely just keep buying the same one for each new pair of shoes and not have to spend time on trial-and-error fitting anymore.

title: Ideal Food Storage Containers
text:
AmazonBasics (Solimo) food storage containers are lidded, plastic, reusable containers.
Ideal for storing leftovers, microwave heating of any number of food items (microwave safe) or gifting of food items.
An affordable alternative to the name-brand containers and just as good (and in some cases, better) quality. Includes snap-on lids that "lock" and hold well.
A good quality product that can always come in handy.
You can use these containers to store foods in the refrigerator or freezer and then go directly to the microwave to reheat. (Make sure the food has cooled to about room temperature before refrigerating/freezing.)
Can also be used to hold/store small items; tacks, nails, paper clips, almost anything dry, that fits. (Short-term storage of liquids or wet items should be OK, but bacteria can still grow, so beware.)
The set I received are rectangular tapered (with rounded corners) and hold up to 24 ounces (approximately three cups.
They feature textured grips, sure-seal "snap" closure and they are generally thin, but thicker where they need to be. Also, these have a non-slip, textured base.
The containers feature three measurement makings, on two sides; one in ounces, the other, in milliliters. They are made from BPA-free recyclable plastic (type 5). They are packaged in sleeves of five (containers and lids.)

title: Extend The Life of Alkaline Batteries
text:
Alkaline batteries are great, except for one aspect. Manufacturers tell you to dispose of the batteries when they are worn down. Now, the Alkaline Recharger will allow you to recharge worn alkaline batteries. Some, up to 10 times. Typically, it takes about five hours for this charger to charge a depleted battery, It really works. Sometimes the charger doesn't realize a battery is incapable of holding a charge until it has tried to charge it for several hours. That is one of the only shortcomings of this product.
There is a warning for this charger; only charge alkaline batteries. It is not intended for rechargeable batteries, nor standard or long-life cells. It can charge AAA, AA, C or D cells. It would have been nice if it could handle 9 volt batteries, but what can you do?
This charger can save you some money and help reduce some waste too. A really handy tool.

title: Extremely soft, different from other traditionally "soft" toothbrushes

The bristles on these toothbrushes are extremely soft, somewhat short, and very tightly packed, so they don't really move back and forth or get between your teeth as well as other toothbrushes. The feel of the bristles honestly reminded more of a makeup brush than any other toothbrush I've tried before. I think if you have extremely sensitive teeth or gums, and even traditional "soft" toothbrushes are too rough for you, these might be a good alternative, but if you are used to more traditional "soft" toothbrushes, you might also find these to be too soft. While the front surfaces of my teeth felt pretty clean after using this toothbrush, I felt like it was a lot more difficult to brush the backs of my teeth and I also didn't think they really got in between my teeth very well. If you're an extremely good flosser, that might be okay, but I prefer the bristles on my toothbrush to move a bit better and help get in between my teeth as well.

title: Works great!
text: Works perfectly with my Audeo Marvel M90- and 2018 LG TV via optical connection.  Allows for both the TV external speakers and the optical audio to this device at  the same time.  No lag at all in the audio.  Once initially connected to the hearing aids the box will automatically connect every time the TV is on and you are in range (in the same room).  When you walk away out of range,  your hearing aids will chime as the signal drops out.  When walking in range they will connect with no indication.  Actually wish I could turn off the chiming.  If you walk in and out of the room a lot with the tv on it can be a bit annoying but other than that I’m very happy with the device.  My new hearing aids are a great improvement over my 6 year old previous hearing aids  and I’ve been able to get away from using closed captioning.  The LG TV also has a “clear voice” setting which also helps a lot.  But this is icing on the cake, for perfect audio.

So I was holding this minky diaper just marveling at how soft it is and I was staring at the red "stains". title: Lots of money saved.
text:
I originally ordered aprox. 30 of these batteries right before my daughters birth to power all the toys we were given for her. I have used these in everything around the house from; wii remotes to remote control cars, baby swings, lamps and flash lights even used a couple to power my potato gun. These batteries have done fine. They typically don't last as long regular disposable batteries. I am able to put these batteries into my daughter vibrating singing toy on the end of her crib and these usually last 1.5 to 2 days while running continuously throughout the night. WII remotes typically last about 10 to 15 days with a good amount of usage throughout the day before running out. We typically always have a set on the recharger while using others are in use. I did have to buy a better recharger than the one sanyo sends, one that has slots for more than 2 batteries. With my improved charger i purchased i received some extensions that allow me to use the AA bateries as C's or D batteries. Have used them a couple times when in a jam as a C or D battery and they do not power the toys very well at all. However it is useful when i am out of these larger size batteries and my daughter is screaming because her swing doesn't work.
Have been cycling through the same 30 batteries for the almost a year now and they seem to have kept the same charge time as when they where brand new. They work good as long as you don't mind replacing them a little bit more often than you would typical disposable ones. Would definitely recommend this product to a good friend. However make sure you purchase enough to always keep some on a charge while your using others.

title: Would recommend.
text:
My hair is usually very very much straight. I am not used to using a curling wand or iron on my hair, so keep that in mind when reading this review.

Temperature settings: I love this part. It actually tells you what temperature you are choosing, instead of just high/low. It's very easy to select or change the temperature.

Heat up time: Pretty quick! Not the fastest I have seen but also not slow.

Easy to use: it took me a few tries to really get it down. It does what it says, which makes soft curls/waves and doesnt tangle. I cant imagine using this on shorter hair. I think it would be really hard to use on shorter hair. I start with the brush toward the roots, then while holding the tip of my hair, I brush down toward the tips of my hair and then start to roll my hair up in it at a vertical angle. You can also press the lever to release the brush part, and use it as a wand(you have to hold the lever down the whole time but it's not awkward). That part isnt so easy for me to do.

How the curls look: So, you wont get super tight ringlets with this tool, as the barrel is bigger and just the over all function of the tool wont really allow it. I think the brush part does a great job of eliminating any frizz on the curl. It gives a more natural look, which is what I am going for. On my long, thick, straight hair(virgin hair), that I rarely use heat on, the curls dont last long at all unless you use a hair spray. On my hair, the curls probably last a couple hours before going completely flat(without the hair spray). I cant speak to using it to brush through and straighten the hair because my hair is already pretty straight.

Quality: it's not the best quality, but it's still quite nice. I'd say its in between drug store and professional quality but leaning more towards drug store. The barrel isnt anything fancy but it's not cheap quality.

Overall, I am happy with the purchase! Knowing what I know now about it, I would buy it again.

I couldn’t find where it said that it would cut grease and that’s what I would use it for the most so I went straight to my dirty, greasy stove with it. It says spray and let it sit for a few minutes but I don’t have time for all that. I mixed the powder up with hot water and a 5 drops of lemon grass essential oil in a spray bottle and sprayed it on my stovetop. Then I immediately wiped it down intentionally being very easy when I wiped. I was giving this spray a hard time to see if it actually worked and let me tell you it WORKED without even waiting a few minutes before wiping. This is an excellent value for the price because you get 3 packages that make 17-24 ounces. I honestly don’t know how big of a sprayer mine is. I believe I got it at one of the dollar stores and it doesn’t have a size on it but I must have mixed it just right. If I figure out the size I will update my post. The solution didn’t bother my hands at all and I didn’t wear gloves while spraying or wiping. If you are concerned about that just wear disposable gloves or reusable gloves. This is also environmentally friendly because you use the same sprayer instead of throwing away a sprayer every time it runs out. This eye mask seems to be well made but the first thing I noticed, besides lack of instructions, was how much it made my face sweat. That being said, now that my mother and sister both have glasses, we're so pleased to have this repair kit in case anything else goes wrong. text:
Now one of my favorite cleaning products. I am not the type that likes spraying chemicals all over the place (or paying for them). These "Magic Erasers" are great for some of the most annoying cleaning... specifically I keep one in the shower stall to wipe down the glass door, chrome(plastic) around valve, and the walls. I find just running it over these surfaces about once a week until "smooth" feeling pretty much keeps the soap scum from being there - glass is clear etc. Very quick to do, no bad chemicals, and the eraser lasts a very long time so I'm confident cost is minimal.

Also good on painted walls (kids fingerprints etc) and removed quite the buildup of dog nose prints on the glass door to back yard...

Did not work well for me on inside of oven door (perhaps too many oils on that?) Oh well, can't be perfect.

title: More fits than you think
text:
Got this for youth sports coach's. When I first opened it I thought it was going to be too small.

Here is a list of what it holds (and I could probably squeeze smaller stuff into it):

2 - Roll Up Splints
2 - 4" Ace Wraps
2 - 2" Ace Wraps
4 - 2" rolls elastic wrap/tape
2 - 1" rolls sports/medical tape
15 - 3x3" Gauze pads
1 - quick clot gauze pack
1 - Shoulder sling
5 - Misc finger splints
Approx 10 nitryl gloves
Bandage Shears
6 - 6" square break and shake ice packs
Bottle of Bactine
Bag of misc bandaids
Approx 25 packets antibiotic gel

It keeps that well organized in three zipper pockets. The larger middle one has a soft velcro divider that works well enough and is sized well for the rolled goods to stack neatly.

After the season I'll keep it in car to supplement that first aid kit. The splints, slings and wraps are what I hope the kids never need. But having seen an unprepared coach deal with getting an obviously broken wrist stable enough to take to ER I feel much more prepared.

title: A man trimmer
text:
I dislike shaving, and over the past 2 years have not had to shave much. But after 3-4 days am looking a bit shaggy. I do have a corded trimmer, but was looking for something that didn't require as much unpacking, plugging in... And this seems to fit the bill.

It is a smaller cordless trimmer. It is not like the big kits with 10 different size guides and able to cut hair to all kinds of different lengths. This has 3 guides, one come installed on the trimmer, and the other two are in the box. Also comes with a charging cord and little bottle of oil for the blades.

It appears to be well made for home use. I know the person who cuts my hair says that she goes through a set every year or so, so she must buy the expensive ones that will hold up to her heavy use for a year. These, for her, probably would not last more than a few months, but for home use, one person, should last for several years. From experience a bit of oil on the blades is really important, and will keep them operating smoothly.

I am not looking for a hair cutting trimmer, just taking off the excess facial hair, and maybe the back of my neck between hair cuts. Should work perfect for that. Runs smooth, battery charge seems to last well, and no complaints. Seems to be a very good product.

title: works, must be plugged in
text:
I have a dog who has become anxious over the past few months. I am guessing that anxious is the right word. He wants to be near someone all the time. Honestly it is annoying. Started with him pacing back and forth outside our bedroom at night, and then he would cry. Thinking he needed to go out, we would get up and bring him out. Back in, 10 minutes later same thing. We put up gates to keep him away from our door, and he pushed those out of the way to get to our door. Finally, desperate to get some sleep, we let him stay in the room. He is noisy, it is horrible! He does this lip smacking thing, sometimes ending with throwing up. He gets up, walks across the room and then flops, loudly, on the other end. 20 minute later he is back to his previous spot. One night we got the idea to turn on the window AC. We usually do not run it at night, but just put it on fan for the noise. Either he was quieter or we just didn't hear him as much. Realizing we live in New England, and running the window AC, or even having it in your winter, is crazy come fall, I bought this. One of the fan sounds is like our AC. Still hear the loud stuff, but now can get a solid 45-60 minutes sometimes, before he wakes us up.

This one has a volume knob. Many newer units have a volume up or down button, so if you don't like any of the 8, 10, 12 set volumes, you are out of luck. This does run off a USB C cord, and must be plugged in. I have a USB outlet next to by bed, so can leave that plugged in without any problem. Sits on my night stand where I can reach over, and flip it on when needed. If he is strangely quiet, as he has been a night or two since he started this, we don't have to turn it on, but when he starts, especially with the mouth noises, on it goes.

Works for us now, also found then when my spouse and I are working in the house together, I will sometimes flip it on. I usually can not hear what she is saying, but can hear her talking, which distracts me. Perfect for that purpose also.

title: Disgusting, inedible amounts of stevia
text:
EDIT: A few helpful people let me know Stevia is not in this formula to improve the taste, but to bust up biofilms. Thanks! In that case I can't recommend this unless you're going to put it in capsules because it's nearly impossible to drink.

EDIT #2: Samsara contacted me in the comments of this review to offer me a refund and say they're going to reduce the amount of stevia. I found the powder was effective once I put it in capsules so I'm not going to take the refund, but I appreciate their offer and I have continued to buy Samsara products.

--

I got this for bartonella because it was cheaper than buying the individual ingredients. If it ends up being helpful, I'll update my review to three stars at most.

But I just had my first scoop of this in water and it is BEYOND nasty! The levels of stevia in this are INSANE. So sickly sweet that even one scoop heavily diluted in THREE CUPS of water took me half an hour to drink.

I am never, ever drinking it again. I almost threw up several times and I am not super sensitive to gross tastes.

After realizing how impossible it was going to be to consume this stuff, I immediately used a size 000 capsule filler to put the powder into big capsules; one scoop is roughly 2 to 3 size 000 capsules. I will take those and see if they help.

But honestly after this I will just spend the extra money to buy the ingredients separately because this was so nasty and inconvenient.

title: This is a simple and easy to follow portion control program

This is a simple and easy to follow portion control program. The leaflet gives you clear directions for any caloric intake needs as well as menu plan ideas to get you started. The containers seal tight and when storing nest into 2 neat stacks. It is a tool more for measuring than for on the go containers. The system requires multiple boxes of the same color through out the day. So do not think that you can pack your day into the set and just have everything ready to take with you on the go. But it is easy to measure out into these and then move to a larger container for taking meals with you. The collapsible silicone cup is a nice added item. Good for on the go.
Pros
~Color coded
~Seals tight
~Dishwasher safe
~BPA free
~Easy to follow system
~Nests for easy storage

Cons
~Multiples of the larger containers or a single larger container which could also hold the other containers in storage would be a nice feature to add to the set and would make the system just that much easier to follow

title: Solid Probiotic for Solid Poo
text:
Floranex is a trusted brand name for probiotics in the healthcare field. As a nurse, I see a lot of patients taking this brand of probiotics.

I started taking probiotics a few years back due to GI issues, and I continue to take them because of that and increasing research showing ties between gut health and mental health. These Floranex One capsules are as easy to take as any others I've tried before. I'd never tried Saccharomyces boulardii supplements before, but they seemed to work just as well as my Lactobacillus and Bacillus coagulans (my personal favorite) supplements. If you have really bad GI problems, these may do the trick if the other probiotic strains haven't worked. Saccharomyces boulardii is a yeast (fungus), not a bacterium like the others, so it has very different cellular properties.

title: Great for Relaxation
text:
I LOVE magnesium for sleep. It's a guaranteed relaxation aid for me. I've historically used Natural Vitality Calm, which you can get here or at Costco, but I thought this would be fun to try since it's a low effort way to get my fix.

Aside from the difficulty of pulling the pods apart, these were everything I'd hoped for. The flavor is decent, and the relaxing effect is quick. Just a squirt under the tongue, and it's sweet dreams 30 minutes later.

As with all magnesium supplements, I caution all buyers about the potentials of softer or more frequent bowel movements. But, hey, at least you won't be constipated.

title: Works well for me
text:
I received my bracelet a couple of days ago and am pleased with it. It fits well, is obviously a medical ID bracelet that all medical personnel will instantly recognize, and the built-in software is basic, but serviceable.

Downsides: If you are a large person with a bigger than normal wrist, this bracelet might be too small for you. I am a 210-pound male and it fits me perfectly. However, I know some people with bigger wrists who might have problems.

The included software is a bit basic but seems to do the job. It has no built-in printing capability but I found it is easy to print: take a screenshot and print that. That takes a second or two and it works well. I'd prefer built-in printing, but this work around is simple and suffices. I suspect that all medical personnel and most everyone else can figure it out in a second or two. Then again, there isn't all THAT much information. I'm not sure anyone will really need to print it.

I also copied a text file to the jump drive called EMERGENCY - READ ME.TXT that duplicates most of the information I entered into the bracelet's ID and then I added quite a bit more info besides. I gave the names and phone numbers of several next of kin, in case the two listed in the bracelet's software were both unavailable. I also added information about my medical insurance, car insurance (I am guessing this could be useful after an auto accident) and everything else I could think of. The EMERGENCY - READ ME.TXT file is easily printed.

I am keeping the bracelet and plan to wear it all the time.

title: Labor-saving!
text:
Once I understood how to use the settings, this was much faster to use than a traditional wand or curling iron and feels much safer (no burns!). I’m NOT an expert user and I have fairly short hair which is just brushing my shoulders now; as you can see, I was able to get some nice soft curls to frame my face after just one proper use. Its really easy to change the temperature, styling time, and left-right direction. It’s quite lightweight so I could see myself taking it on travel.

Cons: battery life is short, just enough to do one head of hair (just), so if you have a lot of hair, this tool may not meet your needs. The winding mechanism runs too long for my shorter hair but there is no way to shorten the winding time; that would save battery life for me right now until my hair gets longer. While actually curling, it beeps each second; I’m just not a huge fan of the constant noise. The 2 short beeps to let you know to remove it would have been enough for me. Also allow time to read the instructions which appear to be translated by a non-native speaker.
At this price point it’s pretty good value though; I would probably have given this product 5 stars except for the battery life. We’ll see how durable it is.

text:
Some how, in my absentmindedness I found myself sucked into purchasing the Hydroderm Age Defying Anti Wrinkle Reducer- after 4 months of using twice per day I have had zero improvement.

The only lesson learned, is that aggressive internet marketing will make someone wealthy. I don't mind that part, but if you got the hype, at least back it up with something that actually works.

On a positive note, the product did not harm my skin- was comfortable to wear, was not inundated with needless scents, and did not cause me more wrinkles, just an annoying monthly ding of $82.00 on my credit card bill!

Keep in mind, there is no such thing as a free sample- once you receive it, you have to cancel asap or you will be knee high in monthly shipments.

Oh and one more thing- I do not mind spending money on cosmetic products if they work- here's a funny antidote. Ponds dry skin cream works as good if not better then any expensive cream I have used in the present or past. I think a 10.1 oz jar costs about $9.00.

The key to healthy skin is to eat healthy, drink plenty of water, watch sun exposure and last but not least, good genetics.

title: The very best product for a serious safety issue (or snoring spouse)
text:
If you are routinely subjected to noise that is loud enough to damage your hearing you should buy these. After trying dozens of earplugs through the years I can state unequivocally that Moldex Softie 6600 ear plugs are the best product available. They are extremely comfortable and easy to insert and remove. If placed properly they will attenuate all sound adequately up to and include large caliber rifles.

I would strongly advocate that anyone who is serious about shooting and who goes to the range frequently, wear double hearing protection. In other words a pair of Moldex Softies and a muff along the lines of the Peltor 10. I have always been obsessive about wearing hearing protection my whole life but still have significant hearing loss due to target practice. I only learned of the double protection technique when I attended a prominent shooting school and the instructors all wore double protection eschewing the trendy electronic muffs with microphones and noise gates. Shooters, RocknRollers or Jack Hammer Operators. Protect your ears and enjoy the music for long, long time.

PS This is a bit TMI but the best way to put these in is to roll them between you thumb and forefinger along the long axis until they are compressed as much as is possible. Holding the compressed plug tight to keep it from expanding to soon, wet the end of it with your tongue and then ease the plug into your ear canal. If you have them in correctly as they expand you will hear something very reminiscent of a Hollywood sound effect when the sound is suddenly vacuumed out of the room. (Dude Warning: Ear hair is a problem and is probably making your special person a bit ill. Get rid of it.)

title: Great product, Second (edited) review
text:
I have been shaving with soaps/creams for over a year now. I will leave my initial review intact for new DE shavers to reference. My initial product rating was 3 stars.
**Initial review:
I was disappointed at how difficult it was to make a good lather, but it's probably due to my inexperience. I love Taylor's tub of shave cream - lathers great and I thought this would be similar, but the lather I produce with this soap leaves my face nicked and razor burned quite a bit. I give it three stars b/c the lather doesn't seem to protect that well and the bowl only works with Taylor's refills - if I had known that, I would have bought a separate bowl and less expensive soap; on the other hand, the bowl is very attractive and the soap smells great. I recommend sticking with the cream though. **End of initial review.

After having much more experience with this shaving soap I have to say that I have come to love it. The technique for obtaining a good lather from a hard soap and a cream are different and it was my own inexperience that produced unsatisfactory results. As a matter of fact, even the cheap (less than $5 soaps) will produce a good lather if done properly. That said, this product has lasted for a long time, smells great and produces a smooth easy shave. It truly does produce a rich, thick lather and if it does not for you, than you are not doing it right (just look at my initial review). It does not dry my face out like the less expensive soaps tend to do. All in all, a great product and I will continue to purchase it.

title: Have had great results, but newer model didn't quite compare
text:
Product update: After six months of beneficial use, the belt stopped working. We think the problem lies in the recharging cord, but for whatever reason, the belt is not heating up. This is the second belt we've had; the first one performed extremely well with heavy use for several years. If this is the "new, improved" variety, we're not quite so impressed. I wrote the following review based on our previous, very positive experience with this product. I won't change our general assessment, but would urge some careful research since there are now, apparently, "up-graded" models, including rechargeable battery packs, different types of disks (we have the jade ones), etc., and we just don't have experience with all of them. It's not an inexpensive product, so one hopes for long-term performance. Our second purchase just didn't compare in this regard.

Earlier review: My husband has been using this heating belt for his chronic lower back problems for several years and he's found it to be the most helpful device he's tried. He's now on his second belt after wearing out the first one from frequent use. The jade stone disks retain the heat well and yet they are not too hot to be uncomfortable (however, he does wear the belt over a light t-shirt when using it). The belts we have purchased use electricity to warm up to the target temperature and an indicator light goes from red to green when ready to use. (I understand there's a battery pack variety also available, but we have no personal experience with that model). It doesn't take long to charge the belt -- the new belt charges in under 5 minutes (the previous iteration took a little longer). The wide velcro ends allow for a comfortable, easily adjustable fit. All in all, this is an excellent and effective product. Highly recommended.

title: Hard to dissolve and, to me, tastes terrible beyond words.
text:
According to an article published by the National Insititute of Health, “hypomagnesemia is common in hospitalized patients, especially in the elderly with coronary artery disease (CAD) and/or those with chronic heart failure. Hypomagnesemia is associated with an increased incidence of diabetes mellitus, metabolic syndrome, mortality rate from CAD and all causes. Magnesium supplementation improves myocardial metabolism, inhibits calcium accumulation and myocardial cell death; it improves vascular tone, peripheral vascular resistance, afterload and cardiac output, reduces cardiac arrhythmias and improves lipid metabolism. Magnesium also reduces vulnerability to oxygen-derived free radicals, improves human endothelial function and inhibits platelet function, including platelet aggregation and adhesion, which potentially gives magnesium physiologic and natural effects similar to adenosine-diphosphate inhibitors such as clopidogrel. The data regarding its use in patients with acute myocardial infarction (AMI) is conflicting. Although some previous, relatively small randomized clinical trials demonstrated a remarkable reduction in mortality when administered to relatively high risk AMI patients, two recently published large-scale randomized clinical trials (the Fourth International Study of Infarct Survival and Magnesium in Coronaries) failed to show any advantage of intravenous magnesium over placebo. Nevertheless, there are theoretical potential benefits of magnesium supplementation as a cardioprotective agent in CAD patients, as well as promising results from previous work in animal and humans. These studies are cost effective, easy to handle and are relatively free of adverse effects, which gives magnesium a role in treating CAD patients, especially high-risk groups such as CAD patients with heart failure, the elderly and hospitalized patients with hypomagnesemia. Furthermore, magnesium therapy is indicated in life-threatening ventricular arrhythmias such as Torsades de Pointes and intractable ventricular tachycardia.”

In addition to what magnesium I normally ingest as part of my diet, I take 350mg of elemental magnesium daily (Natural Vitality Calm Magnesium Citrate) and have for a number of years. Because of my pragmatic use of magnesium supplements, I accepted the opportunity to review this formulation.

One test of the bioavailability of any essential mineral supplement is to measure its concentration in the blood. Magnesium requires an acidic environment for optimum absorption (best to take on an empty stomach to maximize HCL concentration in the gut).

This formulation does not readily dissolve in any liquid I tried. My greatest success was achieved by placing it in a blender for five minutes in warm water. OK, no big deal. However, drinking this stuff was impossible for me: IT TASTES HORRIBLE!!! I tried a few fruit drinks, various make-your-own-carbonated-drink mixtures, and gobs of sugar. Without getting too graphic, it honestly reminds me of putrefaction.

For my health in particular, adequate magnesium levels are essential. If I had to rely on this stuff I would die. Because of its difficulty in dissolving and its taste, I cannot recommend this product.

title: Superb Everyday Lip Balm
text:
Because this old man has used lip balms since age 11, I can, at least, claim to be experienced. My use of lip balms serves a singular purpose: to prevent my lips from drying out and cracking (like many whose finger tips around the nails will crack, especially in the winter, if one does not keep the hands well lubricated).

To me there are three types of lip balms by texture: waxy - the traditional Chap Stick made by Wyeth; oily or greasy - Lypsyl, especially the versions distributed in Canada and Europe made by Lornamead; and those variously in between - e.g. Chap-Ice made by Oralabs. To me each has a place: waxy - maximum retention; oily - best for billing and cooing (youngsters may have to ask their grandparents about that one); and everyday use.

Apart from the texture, a second equally important characteristic is flavoring which yields, of course, flavored an unflavored (essentially) products. One question (or its variants) always on my mind is, "Do I want to use an exquisite Pinot Noir as a chaser for my lip balm?" No! Because I use lip balms round the clock, I tend to avoid flavored products that will contribute to the flavor of food and drink.

A third characteristic of lip balms is whether or not they are medicated; specifically, do they contain camphor, menthol, phenol, (e.g., Blistex, Carmex.) or, in the case of sunscreens, octyl methoxycinnamate (perhaps the most widely used sunscreen ingredient today, replacing PABA). I do not care about this characteristic one way or another except as it contributes to texture and flavoring as noted above.

I tried Chap-Ice because of its cost: at $0.64 per 0.15 oz tube it is the least expensive I have found. If "1" is greasy or oily and "10" is waxy, I would classify Chap-Ice at about a "6." The Beeswax Lip Balm variety that I purchased (about which this review refers) contains: Sunflower Oil, Beeswax, Coconut Oil, Sweet Almond Oil, Castor Oil, "N&A Flavors," and Corn Oil. It also contains butylated hydroxytoluene (BHT) which is a fat preservative. When smelled or first applied, there is an aroma - a flavor - that dissipates very quickly; it also imparts a slight warm sensation.

In a word, I like Chap-Ice. It has enough body (no so greasy) so that it lasts a reasonable length of time for me; the aroma/flavoring and sensation of warmth dissipate quickly so as not to contaminate food or drink, or otherwise be on my mind; and, at $0.64 a tube, it is an exceptional buy (after it arrived and I tried it, I went back to Amazon and purchased their remaining stock; no fear, however, they immediately posted that they would have a new supply in 3 days).

Nonetheless mindful that one person's food is another's poison, I think lip balm users will find Chap-Ice a most satisfactory, everyday lip balm. Given that it is not entirely waxy, I suspect that it would serve nicely for protracted billing and cooing; sadlly, I have no one my immediate circle with whom to test my theory.

title: I thought it would be a nice addition to the supplies I take
text:
I purchased this first aid kit to put in my trailer that I take to craft shows with my embroidery machine. I thought it would be a nice addition to the supplies I take. I liked the idea that it was supposed to be for 25 people, was separated into sections for usage, and came in a hard case. I thought it would also be good to take with us when we go camping.

First, it appears that this item is as advertised. It is a basic first aid kit to "clean, treat, and protect" in case of accident or emergency. This is why I am giving them five stars.

When I received this item, I was a bit disappointed in how the box is organized. The way it is separated is by a six-section re-closable plastic pouch that is marked with what you are supposed to use each of the sections for. This is a decent idea, but you cannot separate the sections (I guess I could cut them apart), so I can’t organize them the way I would like to. They are re-closable, but the way it is accomplished is by a sticky strip on the face of the pack that the flap sticks to. In my opinion, six separate, zip-closable sections would be better, or section off the case.
The supplies provided are basic first-aid supplies. In my opinion, fabric bandages would be better than plastic ones, as they stay in place better, but that’s just personal preference. I have not had an opportunity to use any of the supplies yet, so I’m not sure of their quality. They seem to be the typical, basic ones provided in all first-aid kits.
I think it would be an OK starter kit. I was expecting a bit more from a “25-person”, “ANSI/ISEA Z308.1-2015 Class A Type III” first-aid kit, especially when it is said to be suitable for office, work, industry, home, auto, and all-purpose. I guess I was just thinking that there would be a bit more in it.
I received this item at a reduced priced in exchange for an unbiased review.

title: After a month of use. . .Update
text:
Update (050719): I have since received another unit from customer service and also purchased another unit from a different vendor. When using the flosser I now place the rubber plug into the charging port after learning my lesson with this unit. I gave this one to my sister to try and advised her to place the small rubber adapter into the charging port when using it. I noticed after using the unit that calcium deposits developed inside the charging port. I cleaned it out, but it did not help my situation. The unit would not power on.

Today, I received correspondence from customer service:

Hello dear.

Sorry for disturbing again.

According to our technical team, the water flosser stop working probably because it get wet. But our water flosser are IPX7 waterproof. It wouldn't get wet even using it while taking shower. Could you check that whether you plug the cover for charging interface? Please remember to plug the cover while using.

By the way, your review is really important for us. We would be grateful if you can remove it at your earliest convenience.

Looking forward to your response.

Sincerely
CSmile service team

After the email, I upgraded my review to reflect 4 stars instead of 3. However, I am still not sure if the unit was defective or stopped working because of me using it without the adapter inside the charging port. I advised customer service they need to update their instructions on the site and those with the unit to state to place the small adapter inside the charging port when in use.

I will not be removing my review because it was my honest experience of using the unit. As I advised customer service I will update the review, but not remove it. I think it would be dishonest to do so because I was sent another unit. I am still not sure if the unit wasn't defective or if it failed because of the charging port not being protected. I mean this thing is supposed to be waterproof, right?

Previous review: This water flosser works as described. If you haven't used one of these before, it is quite a different feeling against your gum line. It fits well in your hand, but you can't effectively use it without mistakenly hitting the power or pressure mode buttons. Most of the time, I have to hold it on the bottom (by its base) because otherwise being able to maneuver it around can be frustrating because of the sensitivity of the pressure mode and power buttons before you can get it into your mouth.

I cannot describe how many times I've had to wipe down my mirror and walls because I accidentally pressed the power button before I could get it into my mouth. Holding it at the base is the best way to use it.

For two days I have not been able to use the water flosser because it stopped working. It has a full battery but yet will not turn on. I filled it with water and made sure the water tank was attached correctly...nothing. I placed it on my sink and walked away. I returned and could hear a noise of some sort. Upon investigation, the water flosser had come on and was squirting water onto the ceiling and light fixture in my bathroom. Crazy! I tried my darnedest to make sure it was off before leaving it alone, but it wouldn't come on. I assumed it would be another day of not working. However, it started working and sprayed my ceiling and light fixture before I could turn it off.

I'm not clear why it is now working intermittently. It's not one that I would recommend because if it is waterlogged then I would have to question if it is really waterproof. Because I am not careful with the amount of water that gets on the flosser because I thought it would not be a problem. The water issue is about the only thing that I can imagine could have made it stop working or working on its own.

**Update: I reached out to the seller regarding the issues with this device. The seller was very nice about replacing it. I was sent another one with no problems. Customer service is excellent and aims to please. They are very serious about making your purchasing and user experience pleasant. They will do what it takes to make you a satisfied customer.

title: Contents not as advertised and no response from support team
text:
Ordered a Solo Basic directly from MyMedic. I did an inventory of the Solo kit received comparing it to the contents listed on the website and found the following discrepancies.

Missing: Tylenol, 2 Caplets, 500 mg each
Missing: Advil, 2 Coated Tablets, 200 mg each
Missing: Benadryl, 2 Tablets, 25 mg each
Missing: Safetec P.A.W.S. Handwipe

Included, but not listed: Sunscreen Lotion
Included, but not listed: Ibuprofen (x2)
Included, but not listed: SannyTize Hand Sanitizer
Included, but not listed: Medique Diphen
Included, but not listed: Medique Diotame
Included, but not listed: Medique Extra Strength APAP

I suspect that some of the items included are intended as substitutions for items that were missing, but in the case of the three Medique items, the print on the packages is too small to be read without a magnifying glass. Seriously, blame it on my old eyes, but I absolutely cannot read the print on those packages because it is just to small. Additionally, the names Diphen, Diotame, and APAP are meaningless to me. While I could use Google to find out what they are intended for, I wouldn't remember that out in the field. Consequently, the safest course of action is for me to dispose of the Medique packets and replace them with something equivalent where I would recognize the purpose out in the field.

Additionally, I sent this information to support at MyMedic five days ago, but I have yet to hear anything back.

A quality product produced and apparently well-known in Germany. I have been suffering from gallbladder issues off/on for over 20yrs! My first ultrasound showed no gallstones, but HIDA scan was at around 19-20%. My doctor at the time said he thought it was sludgy. He left it up to me if I wanted to have gallbladder removal surgery or not. I opted not to have the surgery, as everyone I know that has had it can no longer enjoy certain foods and are often left running straight to the restroom if they do. One of my relatives told me she could no longer eat any kind of fresh salads or lettuce. The idea of surgery not only scared me, but also just the thoughts of having an organ one's body needs removed certainly did not sit well either.

Fast forward to three years ago when I had another attack (upper right flank & back pain). Once again, my ultrasound showed no gallstones, but this time the HIDA scan was at 90%, which is over-active. Many doctor's don't consider over-active to be a problem, even though it's obviously not functioning properly. I was in a lot of pain and didn't want to have to resort to surgery if I could avoid it. The pain eventually subsided and went away, until a year or so ago. It came back again, so I started taking a daily milk thistle supplement. The milk thistle had a soothing effect and the pain finally disappeared. A couple of weeks ago the old familiar pain returned. I'm still taking my milk thistle, but this time I decided to add dandelion capsules, along with the Rowachol. I'm feeling much better, so hoping this will pull me through yet once again.

In the past year I have started having a really hard time falling asleep, staying asleep, and sleeping soundly- at all. It was getting to the point of me having mood swings and not having any energy, although I am at a healthy weight and work out and do cardio daily. My diet is good, and I have no other health issues, which frustrated me further, because I didn't understand why I couldn't sleep- I cut out caffeine and alcohol completely, gave up the refined whites, and exercised so I should be tired and sleep soundly.

At first I didn't see a change in my sleeping patterns. It really wasn't until about week 3 that I noticed that I fell asleep easily. Then soon after I slept through the night, and woke up well rested. I love being able to sleep- and with only taking a natural sleep aide! I was so afraid of the possibility of having to take a medication that may knock me out, leave me feeling groggy, or who knows what else. With Govivo's Natural Sleep Aide I sleep just like a baby- and wake up well rested without any sort of 'hang over'.

Also, the thread slips out of the hook very easily so you spend a lot of time re-threading. To make matters worse, because you have to pull so hard to get it to go thru the material, it frequently cuts the thread. It's too bad, because you have the feeling that with a little better quality control it should work. Better off sticking with regular needles and getting a needle threader.

title: Improved Circulation: Check
text:
I’ll admit I had low expectations for this foot rest. By logic, propping one’s feet up further should make one feel more cramped, not less, particularly on an airplane where the opportunity to stretch one’s limbs is rare. Still, I travel frequently for work and figured it was worth a try, given Amazon’s liberal return policy, so I bought the “separated” version before a nonstop flight from Montreal to Cancun, approximately 5 hours.

The Pros:
-The footrest is light and takes up very little room in my carry on. This was very important to me.
-It’s fairly stable once secured to the tray table (pro tip: make sure to pull it down as far as possible towards the seat in front of you when securing).
-It’s efficient when the tray table is in use or in the upright/latched position (both).
-It isn’t in the way of me or anyone walking through my row.
-Unlike the reviews for the nonseparated footrest, each foot remained nestled snugly in its home and my feet never felt cramped or as if they were competing for space (note: I used the footrest with flip flops and shoeless (taboo, I know). I’m not sure there would be enough room for tennis shoes, let alone boots).
-It works! My legs feel significantly less stiff and swollen after the flight, and I was able to fall asleep using the rest!

The Cons:
-I got some stares (no comments, just stares). It was probably envy.
-I’m 5’5, so while this worked for me, I’m not sure it would work for (say) my 6’6 husband. (Note to self: experiment with husband).
-Most international flights won’t allow you to plug electronics in prior to reaching a safe altitude. While no one mentioned the footrest, I’m sure a true international flight would require this to be stowed until then.
-It doesn’t work miracles. The space between you and the seat ahead of you remains the same, the footrest simply allows your feet and legs to “swing,” ensuring good circulation and a bit more flexibility.

Overall, I’d recommend this for air travel. I have not tested it in any other setting, but I imagine for an individual with restless leg syndrome, this could be quite handy in multiple settings. I found it did everything I needed it to, and the adjustable straps were convenient and simple to use.

text: The packaging was very clean and professional.  When I opened it I noticed the product felt very cheap compared to models I had seen and tested in person. I've had recurring back pain, and when I tried one of these devices two weeks ago in person at a trade show, I had relief for several hours.  I had no such relief from this device. It just didn't feel or work the same.  Also, the settings are pretty confusing.  There are two insert pamphlets. One somewhat tells you what each setting is (they provide a list of the settings, I assume it's in order of how the display scrolls).  There is a separate insert in Chinese and English that is an acupuncture chart.  There is also one photograph in the first pamphlet that shows "recommended" placement (shoulders, lower back, etc) The images on the device are odd, one shows hands (ok, that's massage), the next one shows pinching, next what looks like a stomach (the organ, not the abs), a head with the brain showing, feet, and ears.  No explanation about why these images are the ones used (is the stomach setting supposed to do something for your GI?  No telling).  Bottom line, it felt like Chinese cheap junk, the stimulation was more like zapping the muscles than massage, and the intensity settings were inconsistent.  At one point I had to quickly turn the unit off because the leap between two intensities was so significant (from barely anything to pain in one setting change). As a woman, I will also say my facial skin has become clearer, and I started noticing this about half way through the bottle. I usually take about 1/2 teaspoon of this a day in the morning straight. Thing is, when you take supplements, you can't be sure at first, and I have always taken a host of supplements such as MSM, Krill, K2, Vit D, Magnesium, and you wonder if its just been a good week, hitting all the bases on the food list (salmon, veggies, etc.). title: A good series, but a little long
text:
In honor of Halloween, I decided to dust off an old witch series and do a review of the entire series. There are 15 books in the Sweep series by Cate Tiernan. I started reading the Sweep series probably about 6 or 7 years ago (before my blog) when my Borders was going out of business. They had the first three bind up volumes for next to nothing so I grabbed books #1-9 (there are 3 books in each bind up) for I think $5-6 total. Once I started reading I really got into the witchy atmosphere and elemental vibe of the magic in Sweep, so I went back to Borders and grabbed the rest of the books that were out. Books 10-15 I had to get individual novels because their bind up wasn't out yet, and consequently my series doesn't match, which makes me kind of mad.

The Sweep series started out really strong. I read the first 4 books in no time at all and I couldn't get enough of them. I read them all back to back, which I find myself doing more and more when I have a bind up. I will read the whole massive tome as if it were one super long story. Morgan, Cal, and Hunter completely drew me in. I think the first 4 or so books were close to 4.5 or 5 star reads for me, but then as I hit book 5 and beyond, I started to lose interest.

The characters started to annoy me in rotation, and the plots started to drag on. I think this was a case of the series going on too long for my liking. The later books started focusing more on side characters, and that didn't really do anything for me. Especially since we were right in the middle of the overall story arc, so the side stories (books 11, 14) were distractors from me and I would have preferred them to come after the series was done, or put in as novellas. Looking back on my notes from books 11-14 they all centered around the same thing- not enough Morgan and Hunter. Here is my snippet of what I thought of book 13 when I was reading it.

"This book was a side storyline from the main characters, and personally I don't enjoy those as much. Morgan and Hunter were barely in the book at all. Alisa was the focus of this installment and we got to learn about her family. It was a good story but with only two books left in the series I had hoped to have more about Morgan and Hunter."

In book 14 we finally got back to the main storyline and I liked that more. It dealt with a growing discontentment with the council, which was something that I was waiting for the entire series. It was the one plotline that I was hoping would turn up more and a main reason I stuck with the series. My sticking point with the series, other than the side plots that were literally full books long, were the fact that Morgan and Hunter have not really developed as a couple. They started out with a lot of character growth but for the past 3 or 4 books they have kind of been stuck in the same place.

Overall Series: this series is very long and it has a lot of highs and lows. Some of the books are really great, and others were a total snoozefest for me. The magic and the council elements were really well done and they were the highlight. Read the Sweep series if you love all things wiccan and witches and cann't get enough books about them. You can probably get some pretty good reals on the bindups. But in my opinion this series was only average overall, and got worse as it went on. It picked up at the very end (books 14 and 15), but it took too long to get there.

*Disclaimer- I bought these books from Borders (remember borders??) And I am not compensated for my thoughts.

title: Works fine for tablets, not so much for gel caps
text:
I bought this to replace another popper that had seen better days. After a couple of years of struggling to pill my cat daily with about a 75% success rate (and a lot of angst for both of us) I found that putting his half-pill into a #2 gel cap, smearing it and the tip of the popper with GNC High Calorie Booster Gel, and plunging it into his mouth had a 99.9% success rate on the first plunge and created a lot less angst.

This didnt work at all for me with this particular popper, though. I did some test runs (sans kitty) with both tip sizes to no avail. The tips are too soft and the plunger is too pointy, so when the plunger hits the capsule it slips around the sides of it (I did it without smearing the capsule with the booster gel, so that wasn't the issue). The capsule got stuck in the tip and I had to do a lot of poking to dislodge it.

What I found, however, is that the soft tips pretty much eliminate the need for the gel caps. I popped the half pill into the small tip, smeared the outside of the tip with the booster gel (avoiding the opening), and it went down without a hitch.

It might work with sturdier gels caps -- mine are vegetarian caps that I bought in bulk and they're admittedly a bit fragile -- but I did note that a few others had the same comment so just keep that in mind.

This came with no instructions, but I found the best way to use this is to push the soft tip onto the end of the unit as far up as you can get it -- it takes a bit of finagling -- then push the pill into the tip so that it sits right at the opening. The rubber end keeps it from falling out; it's better if it's kind of a tight fit so try both size tips. BEFORE you insert the popper into your pet's mouth push the plunger slowly until it's touching the pill -- that way all you need to do is a quick pop once you get your pet involved.

Long review, but I hope it was somewhat helpful.

Update 12/6/16: Three of the tips have split, so I wouldn't buy these again.
