Sigg of Switzerland water bottles are very high quality, made of light aluminum on the outside, slightly insulated, and covered with a special powder coat on the inside that prevents any leaching whatsoever, unlike plastic and polycarbonate water bottles. They are light, durable, and perfect for any activity. Well water tastes spectacular in these bottles, just like from the tap.

Sigg bottles come with several different types of tops. I bought the screw top because I don't like sports tops, and I don't mind unscrewing the top when I want a drink. You can buy Siggs in alternative sizes too, such as .75L, .4L (for kids), .6L, .5L. You can occasionally find this bottle in the 1.5L size, also. Search Amazon for the perfect size.

Pick a style and pattern you like, as this bottle is a personal accessory, and should reflect your style. The colors are vibrant and even prettier than they seem in the pictures on Amazon.

They are expensive, but they are so durable that you can plan on them lasting many years. I consider them both an accessory and an investment in my health, so they are well worth it value-wise for me.

title: CAMU CAMU: MY ANALYSIS OF ITS CLAIMS OF EXCELLENCE
text:
I have always been a strong supporter of the daily health benefits of consuming Vitamin C, and learned long ago that oranges are an inferior product for Vitamin C. With my magnifying glass, I was able to discern that Camu Camu comes from Peru and Brazil. The manufacturer claims it has 7 times more Vitamin C than an orange. It is a light orange color and is a very, very fine powder.

I like the fact Camu Camu comes from plants which grow in Amazonian Rain Forests in Peru and Brazil, but packed into a sturdy plastic container with a screw on lid and shipped from some place in California, but the size of the container is so small (4 oz.) and so the print (even if you use a strong magnifying glass, is largely illegible). But I find it is expensive, comes only in a 4 oz. size, and at the rate of 1 tsp. daily, is rapidly used up providing only 39 days of consumption. With my magnifying glass, I can read that this source is reported to be the highest source for Vitamin C anywhere. Is that true? The label is telling us nothing meaningful.

Yes I am glad to have this product as part of my extensive Ayurveda products from places that are not in the USA. All this said, there is one other resource available for Vitamin C within the USA and available from Trader Joe's which is a company I really trust for the quality of their products, and which comes in a 16 oz. size and requires only 1/4th tsp whereas Camu Camu requires 1 tsp. and provides only 39 days covers, and does not verify it claim it provides the greatest source of Vitamin C. Whereas, Trader Joe's clearly states their product at 1/4 tsp. (1,000 mg) of ascorbic acid provides 1,667% of the daily requirement for Vitamin C as well as 454 days for its inexpensive Vitamin C product. This means, Trader Joe's Vitamin C consumption provides almost 12 times more days of coverage than Camu Camu's. Which one does anyone think I'm going to continue to purchase?

Camu Camu should use larger print, a slightly larger container, and verify its claim of how much Vitamin C is provided per 1 tsp. But, since this product manufacturer says 1 tsp. of this product has 7 times more Vitamin C than an orange, I'll now see how much Vitamin C is in an average orange. Here is what Google has to say. So, will I purchase it again? It is operating just as the fake news does in the USA, and not tell us the truth.

Google reports "Just one orange has about 100 mg of vitamin C, which is 130 percent of that daily recommended intake.Jun 17, 2016"

title: Not Appropriate for Use in a Car - Shape Cuts into Your Legs BADLY
text:
This is not appropriate for a car. Its not shaped like a "wedge" with one side tapered, which I believe would have made it work.

As is, I could see this being fine for an office chair. But car seats are already shaped so as to slope. So the addition of the Purple's edge sticking up brought great pain to my legs, where it hit them. I was in such pain after only driving 20 minutes, that I needed to do a lot of stretching and it took over 24 hours to heal.

Because I have sciatica (which is why I bought this), the exacerbation of that was frustrating to say the least.

title: Pretty customizable
text:
I never used insoles like these before, closest thing would be those gel ball of foot comfort pads or the heel liners from Dr Scholls over the counter. I am 31, athletic build with bad knee pain and so my physical therapist suggest insoles among many other treatments. I like that these have lines in the back side so you can use them as markings.

They come with these semi- customizable arch pads with a sticky back to stick onto the back side of the insoles. You can choose small, medium, large and soft support or regular support (6 pairs total). Additionally, you can also choose where to put these arch pads on the insoles, that's where the lines come in handy. You can also cut these down to size to fit your shoes, and the lines help with that too.

I can see how insoles would be a challenge for some shoes, I found the Ugg boots easiest to work with because they are so cushy with so much fur you can smush down. Sports shoes would be ok but you would have to remove the existing insoles.

When you first wear these, it takes time getting used to. First time I wore these to walk my dogs, and I was already tired within 5 minutes. Probably want you want to do is slowly introduce it into your life and wear it for 30 mins a day, and gradually increase the time instead of what I did which was walk my dogs and then wore the same boots to work.

Edit: 2/19/21
I have chronic knee pain and got this because the sports doctor and my physical therapist told me to get insoles. At first my feet got tired after only a few minutes. I have been wearing these daily for a while now, and 5 days a week I am taking at least 12,000 steps. I am wearing Uggs, because these are too thick for my sports shoes. I have felt some relief and improvements in my knees and no longer have tired feet now that I am used to these. I wish these are harder with less flex, but they are really good beginner insoles. I will soon be moving on from these to more intermediate, form fitted ones that are prescribed. I am very happy that I tried these, I never had insoles before.

title: Decent electric toothbrush but without the charger base
text: [[VIDEOID:f7dcba259a612417362fc513b8916088]] The electric toothbrushes reduce dental plaque by 30% more than the manual ones. With time, unfortunately, they develop a strange coating around their charging base. After each use the water drips down and wet surface allows bacteria to grow mold. Luckily, this particular toothbrush doesn't have the charging base; instead it is being held by the support attached to the wall. This allows the water to drip down and let the toothbrush to dry out and prevent bacteria accumulation at the bottom. The charging is still done through the bottom by connecting a USB cable, but you only need to do it once in 4-5 days (duration will vary depending on your dental habits). The nice thing is that it comes with 8 brushes so you don't have to rush to the store every 3-4 months to buy a replacement. The downside is that these brushes are not standard so I doubt you'll find a replacement in CVS or Target. I also found that they sometimes come off easily during brushing, but perhaps it was the exception rather than a rule. Taken together, I'd say it deserves 4 stars.

title: Easy Reach Lotion Applicator
text:
I bought this Easy Reach applicator by Active Forever as a replacement for the commonly sold one with sponge refill, ribbed end. I picked this one over the type with the floating balls, which you fill with lotion, because I wanted control over how much lotion was dispensed. My objection to the sponge type was that after a few days of applying lotion with it, the sponge became saturated causing the adhesive to loosen and the sponge to fall off. I had bought the sponge refills at a store for about $2 a piece so having one last less than a week was not acceptable. My Easy Reach applicator is superior to the sponge type in all aspects except one. I prefer the feel of the sponge on my skin to this plastic cover, but this plastic is certainly okay. The upsides to this applicator versus the sponge type are:

1. This applicator is about 19 inches long - about 5 inches longer than the other - which is important for the hard to reach parts of the back.
2. Having a non-absorbent applicator means all lotion/ointment gets rubbed into the skin rather than have some fill a sponge.
3. In addition to the handle being longer, the application surface itself is about 5 times bigger and therefore covers a much larger area.
4. It's far cheaper in the long run than continually having to replace the sponge refill.

I find this a better applicator for those 4 reasons. And after using it for several weeks, I am very satisfied with it.

title: Call it "Pro*Kool", not Kold.
text:
Eight years ago I purchased this product from the same company, then known as Dura Kold. Both the inserts and the sleeve worked splendidly until this past summer when the velcro on the sleeve would no longer hold. Since I've been icing more frequently, I decided to reward the company for their great product and buy TWO new units, each with a sleeve and two inserts.

Unfortunately, this is no longer the same product. It should now be called Pro*Kool, as the inserts do not get cold enough to have any impact. The inserts only get about as cold as the original after it has already been in use for about thirty minutes. In other words, not cold. I've gone back to using my two remaining eight year old inserts, because they still get cold enough to matter.

What really jerks my chain is that the company did not even bother to respond to my correspondence outlining the problem. But that's not all. The original sleeve held up well, with the velcro getting unusable only after many years of use. (Which is why I bought new ones.) The new sleeves ALREADY will not stay in place as the velcro will not adhere. I don't know if it's the newer micro fiber material that they are using, or the hook side of the equation, but after only a few months, the velcro will no longer hold.

This was a waste of money, pure and simple.

Bubbles stop after a few uses due to a poor design. The tiny air pump has no ability to overcome any obstruction in the air lines (which are far to large in diameter) There are no check valves or mechanisms to keep water from migrating into the air lines, which is the cause of the bubble failure.

Removing the lower cover (9 screws on bottom) reveals the air pump. A quick blast of air (blow hard with your mouth) into the intake of the running pump will open the airway and return the unit to bubbling. For longer term use you could remove the bottom vent shutters so you can gain access to the pump without removing the bottom part of the unit each time this happens. Additionally, storing the unit upside down and/or with the front of the unit pointing down may help keep water from draining into the air lines in the future. See photos for a better understanding of what's going on here.

text: I already own 2 clarisonics and am not ready to fork out another $100 for a Foreo, so after looking around in the knock-off fields I decided to give this one a try, which had 9 reviews when I ordered and that is too few to be reliable even if it's all 5 star reviews. I have enough experiences with both genuine name brands and knock-offs and honestly i'd not expect them to perform at same level. It's a matter of reaching the right balance in terms of value. Say if a knock-off performs at 60% of the brand name product but only cost 1/3 or less of the latter, I would call it a good buy. Since I am used to clarisonic cleaning, this facial cleanser was way too gentle/soft for me when i tried the first time, I was convinced that this was useless and i was gonna return it, but then once i finished washing my face with it, I had to say it definitely felt much cleaner than a simple towel wash! So it was doing some sonic cleansing job after all even though the vibration was very mild comparing to Clarisonic. The weak link of this product is its charging base. Even after a few days of using it a couple of times a day between washing and massaging, the unit would only charge for one minute and then stop charging. I contacted the customer service, who is very responsive and told me that the product arrives charged and the charging indicator light will turn off when it's fully charged. So it's a bit hard to tell if my unit has a defective charging base and will find out if it holds a steady charge once its power significantly drained. Also it takes some practice/nudging to find a secure charging contact point with the charging base, the unit is probably not waterproof but water resistant as it's not seamless, there is a fine slit line at the bottom. I think it's safe to use in the shower but as instructed do not soak in water. All in all, this is a good product if the charging base turns out okay which I will update in due time. I wouldn't know if it performs just as well as a genuine Foreo as I don't own a Foreo but it does complement with Clarisonic brush which is not meant to use daily.

title: Perfect for measuring out oral doses of CBD oil
text:
We recently got a batch of pure CBD oil for oral and external use. The oil from a distillation or extraction is very thick. We were advised to use ethanol to dilute and make it easier to mix and dose. We used Everclear (95% ethanol), but lesser liquors (almost always 40% ethanol) did NOT work (the other 60% is water). We diluted the CBD oil to provide a CBD concentration of 50mg per ml.
We used these syringes to administer our oral dosages. Dosage is calculated by body weight, usually 0.10 to 0.25 mg of CBD per day. These syringes, without needles, are perfect for small oral dosage like ours (0.3 to 0.6 ml per day).
One thing you must be aware of with these syringes: they have a Luer-Slip nozzle, and a small extension of the plunger extends into the nozzle. Careful: the measurement is taken from the FLAT part of the plunger, NOT at the end of the extension. See photo attached.

title: Contact Cleaning Magic! Thumbs Up!
text: This product is amazing!!!!! I use saline rewetting drops with my contacts they leave a pretty gunky residual on them very quickly. I have been wearing these contacts a little over a month now(bad I know, but they are really expensive now). I used this product as the instructions directed and it removed all of the gunk that was built up. My contacts look and feel like I just opened them. The solution composition is 3% hydrogen peroxide. In the bottom of the cleansing case is a neutralization disk. According to the box, you must leave your contacts in this container for six hours so the disk can fully neutralize the solution and prevent eye irritation. If you do this, you can take the contacts straight out of the cleansing case and put them in your eyes without the need to rinse with saline. I personally rinse them anyway, but that's my preference. The only information I wish I had known is that you are supposed to replace the cleansing case after you finish one bottle of the solution. So, I would recommend buying either the set of one bottle and one case, or they do make a set that comes with two bottles and two cases. Both of these items are also sold by amazon. I feel like this product will extend the life of my contacts better and keep my contacts clear. I highly recommend this product.

text:
Overall this scale performs very well. Weight and body fat measurements work as expected. Results are posted and tracked through Fitbit. Generally, the technology (specifically the user interface) is relatively new. Fitbit does an admiral job of making the product friendly, however, because of the changing landscape of technology, it seems to be just off the bullseye, but I want to reiterate, this is a very good product. Normally, I would give it 4 starts because it isn't "perfect", however, because of the quality of Fitbit's customer service, I'm throwing in an extra star. Recently (last month) my scale died. I've owned the scale for two years. The display no long shows text or icons. When I step on the scale the backlight comes on. That's all.

To make a longer story short, I contacted customer support. I emailed my receipt. My scale was within the warranty period. Fitbit fully replaced my scale with no charges. No service fee, no charge for shipping, nothing out of pocket. I couldn't be more pleased. Thanks for great service.

title: Leaves skin feeling great with a clean, subtle scent
text:
I ordered this to replace my old shave soap that had been good enough to get my by but was otherwise totally unremarkable. I'm quite happy I made this decision. The Taylor of Old Bond Street Lavender shave soap is a great way to improve your shaving routine, whether you're using a multi-blade cartridge, a double-edge razor, or even a straight razor.

The scent is very subtle and clean. It is not overwhelming and, rest assured, it does not smell like a bouquet of flowers whenever you walk in a room. The choice of a scent is personal and some may not prefer lavender, but I personally feel that the scent is not strong enough to dissuade anyone.

The soap produces a nice, thick lather that makes for a great shave and leaves your face feeling smooth and healthy. Of course, a great brush is a useful tool, but changing to this soap with my old brush made a huge improvement.

The wood bowl is much larger than I expected and it is an attractive way to store and protect your soap. When you are ready for more soap, you can simply purchase refills and reuse the bowl.

For those interested, I received a Potassium Stearate formula in late 2011, so it is indeed available, but may vary by seller.

title: Vibrating button is easy to activate and easy to remove. Batteries not included.
text: I ordered the vibrating pillow for a child on the spectrum that loves squishy, minky pillows and plushies. The item arrived vacuumed sealed inside a box. There is a small zippered pouch that holds the vibration button. You will need 2 AA batteries for operation. Once assembled, the pillow plumps quickly and the vibration button seems quite sensitive to activate through hugging or pressing the pillow from any direction. The minky exterior is textured. The pillow itself is quite fluffy. My only real concern with the pillow is how easy it is to unzip and retrieve the vibrating button. If you intend to give the pillow to young people, they could easily lose that piece or get to the batteries, which could be very dangerous. A better design would be to attached the button to the pillow or make the zipper less accessible.  Also, the description read “purple” but on my device the picture looked pink. The pillow is light and bright purple in real life.

title: If you've never bought these before...
text:
I'm writing this for people like me who don't have experience buying these kinds of pose-able mannequins.

These are NOT pose-able like you might think. You can't really bend the joints in the arms or legs beyond 5 or 10 degrees; you can bend them more by hand but they are held together with springs that pull everything straight again immediately upon release. The hips also don't bend accurately; the legs can therefore only swing directly forward or backwards. The result is a mannequin suitable ONLY for poses standing straight with straight arms or lying straight with straight arms.

Really this is not going to be useful for someone who wants to create a variety of realistic poses for drawing or other artistic purposes; the mannequins sold here appear to be a gimmick for people who think this sort of thing is required for art school or similar. Sorry to disappoint, but you're not going to get a useful mannequin here.

Let me know if this helped you!

title: Better than attaching a cylindrical adapter
text:
I had a Lensmate adapter on my last camera, a Canon s90, which has no other option for attaching a filter, other than holding one in front of the lens with your other hand. My current camera, a G16, dispenses with the innovative and useful large adjustment ring around the lens (its function is taken over by a small toothed wheel above and to the side), replacing it with a removable cover and mounting system. Canon and several third-party vendors sell a cylindrical adapter that allows you to attach a filter to the camera.

This appealed to me as it didn't require making any changes to the camera, but once I tried this method, the drawbacks were immediately obvious. The G16 is not a tiny camera; it measures around 105 x 75 x 40 mm and barely fits in a shirt pocket. This comes out to a volume of a little over 300 cubic centimeters. The cylindrical adapter is 62 mm wide and must be at least 50 mm deep so the lens will not hit it when the camera is on (the one I have has two parts; you can remove the front section and make it a little shorter as long as you only shoot at wide-angle where the lens does not stick out as far). This cylinder is around 150 cubic centimeters - so it makes the camera 50% larger, and in the most inconvenient way possible, changing the form factor from a block to what amounts to a "bridge" or "super-zoom" profile. What was barely pocketable is now impossible - just to gain the ability to attach filters.

I now have the Lensmate bayonet mount on the G16, which adds barely anything to the size, and allows filters to be attached much more easily than having to thread them on. It also uses smaller 52 mm filters. Until Canon decides to add conventional threads to this camera line, Lensmate offers the only workable system for attaching filters.

title: They work
text:
I was diagnosed with neuropathy earlier this year and was told there was NO treatment for it, the symptoms would not improve, and the feeling would never return. One of my symptoms, which I hate more than anything, is the feeling that I have something thick and stiff strapped to my feet. If nothing else, I hoped for improvement for this alone, anything else would be an added benefit.

I received these right before I left on vacation, tried them out for a couple of days, three treatments a day, but it was nowhere near enough time. When I returned, I started daily treatments, shooting for three times a day every day, however I have missed weekends a lot and had a few days where I did not get all my treatments in. I have felt the "thick sensation" for so long I can barely recall a time when I have not felt it. This morning, I took my dogs out and while walking down the stairs noticed my feet felt different (I do not think this was an overnight, flip the switch, they suddenly felt different, just the first time I noticed). The sensation of a what I guess you could call leather, or to me sometimes it feels like I have plywood in my feet, is changing.

I still feel like something is there, but today, for the first time, I noticed it feels lighter, more flexible. Is it a huge difference? No, I would say subtle, but a definite improvement all the same. If this trend continues, I will be overjoyed, if this is best result - it is still enough difference to make my feet feel better and make the treatments worthwhile.

I went into this believing I was stuck, and these might help. Are they a miracle? No. Are they helping? Yes. Would I recommend you try them? I would. Am I hopeful for more progress? Certainly am. I will grant, they are not cheap, but improvement in my experience usually comes at a price. If you try them, you must give them time and you have to be willing to commit to using them, but if you do I hope you feel what I have.

title: You will be PREPARED with this kit!!!
text:
Excellent first aid kit put together by Accumed! This is a great emergency first aid kit to have in your home, vehicle, office, off road vehicle, or hiking (although to me it is a little large to bring hiking). I can not stress enough the importance of having a complete emergency kits such as this by Accumed to have with you at all times, you should always be prepared!!

Recently, I purchased a few first aid kits- one for hiking, one for my truck, and one for my off road UTV Side X Side. Originally, I had desifgnated this for my truck; however, after assessing the quality and how complete this kit is, I decided to keep this in my UTV.
Accumed did such a thorough job creating this, that I trust having this in situations where I will be out in the middle of nowhere, miles and miles from civilization and without cell service. Under these circumstances, I really have to be prepared and have emergency supplies that I can trust.

This first aid kit has everything you find in a standard kit, plus more! There are quite a few unique items that will be very handy in a time of need, such as a compass, whistle, glow stick, emergency blanket, cold pack, etc.... Every item inside is placed in an organized fashion, which makes it easy to find what uou need and easy to put back. Everything is high quality and sterile items are in appropriate sterile packaging. Scissors are sharp and cut smoothly. I am very happy with every item inside.

The kit is within a soft bag, which allows for easy storage, it will fit in most places easily. Also, the bag is tough and durable, it will hold its own without falling apart on you. Inside, there is extra room in case you want to add few extra items, such as an epi pen, hydrocortisone, triple antibiotic cream, benadryl, etc... The kit closes with double zippers that zip easily and will not jam, especially in a time of need.

When purchasing an emergency first aid kit, you must make sure you know how to use it and be sure that it is made of good quality because this is what you will have to keep you and/or a loved one safe in a time of need. I go out exploring, hiking, biking with my husband and dogs very often. I completely trust Accumed first aid kit in an emergency/ time of medical need. I would highly recommend this product to every person.

I received this product at a discounted price for an honest and unbiased review.

title: Lightweight, rechargeable sonic toothbrush
text:
I've used an electric toothbrush for years, although I mostly pickup one of the inexpensive Oral B models sold at the grocery store for under $10. Rechargeable models with very fast vibrations are usually much more expensive and can be almost $100. I was attracted to the features and affordability of this toothbrush.

This sleek, lightweight toothbrush is charged over USB and lasts a month or so on a single charge. It has multiple modes/speeds from a normal brush to polishing and buildup removal. The higher modes have a pulsing sensation rather than just vibrating at one speed. It comes with 6 brush heads so you can replace one every two months for a year's worth of brushing. While you're brushing, the toothbrush signals every 30 seconds to change to a different quadrant of your mouth so that you use it for the full 2 minutes that dentists and the manufacturer recommend.

When you use this type of sonic toothbrush for the first time, the vibrations can be either pleasantly stimulating or somewhat irritating depending on your gums, but you become used to it over time. I'm not sure how much better this brush cleans than a manual toothbrush or one whose vibrations aren't quite as fast, but it certainly leaves your teeth feeling very clean and fresh.

Also, if you're going to a new country, you don't always know what to expect or if you'll be able to grab a snack somewhere. So, I can't say a lot from a diet/ exercise perspective (I run most days, I used to be a competitive athlete, and I have in general a good diet, but I don't consider myself some super knowledgeable work out person). text:
• Cute packaging

• Very easy to use

• Doesn’t break easily
• Comes w/ clear instructions
• Works w/ or w/o mascara use
• Curls abit better than regular curlers w/o mascara
• Holds the curl quite a bit longer than a traditional eyelash curler w/ mascara.

This is my second attempt buying a heated eyelash curler. The first was; battery operated, a cheaper price but cheaper made aswell, a pain in the ass to set up, weirdly shaped which that made it harder to use, and worst of all it broke after a few days!
This is a huge step up, glad I didn’t give up on electronic eyelash curlers!

I curl my eyelashes with a traditional eyelash curler, apply a clear drugstore mascara, separate my eyelashes with the eyelash comb and then use this curler right on top as the mascara dries. I found this is the best method if you want your curl to last several hours longer than it would if you just curled your lashes with a traditional curler twice.

If you have straight eyelashes like me your lashes WILL still droop a little as the day goes on so you’ll need to touch them up a little bit around midday, so I recommend carrying this with you. Touching up will take less time than initial curling though.

I haven’t tried it with regular (Black) mascara, expensive mascara nor a waterproof mascara. If you use regular mascara, with a higher price point, and is waterproof your curl will probably last quite a bit longer since those kinds of formulas tend to ‘hold’ your lashes in place a bit longer.

Very happy with this product thus far. If it doesn’t start to lose power or break soon then it’s DEFINITELY worth the price.

I like that it comes with a makeup brush and a eyelash comb/eyebrow brush. It’s a nice bonus.

title: OMG! Incredible results on my special needs skin!
text: I've finally discovered a miraculous skin elixir in Gold Bond Strength and Resilience lotion. At 56, my skin (especially my face) has met a lifetime of challenges: Southern summers, sensitive/acne-prone skin, and lastly, aging. Over the years I have have collected a literal graveyard of creams, lotions and "cures" for my complexion. (My more recent battle with menopausal cystic acne has been nothing short of a nightmare.) Finally, after myriad acne products prescribed by dermatologists, I've found two extremely effective non-prescription cures--Differin gel, followed by GB Strength and Resilience lotion. I apply Differin one hour before bedtime, then wash my face in the morning with Noxzema and apply GBS&R lotion afterwards. The difference in my skin texture and appearance has been nothing short of miraculous! GB lotion not only soothes my face from the irritation of Differin but has also healed my acne scars. Honestly, my face has not appeared this fresh and clear since I was twelve years old! Admittedly, I'm also taking 100mg of Spironlactone daily (the ONLY prescription that has worked), but I am so tickled with my Differin/Noxzema/Gold BondS&R cure that I had to write a review. I've also noticed amazing results using GB on my arms, neck and legs. I love that this lotion is non-scented, rich and creamy, but most importantly, NOT GREASY (extremely important when dealing with acne). It goes directly into my skin and retains my skin's moisture for hours on end. Everyone's commenting now on how "good" and "healthy" I look. Thank you Gold Bond! The toiletry graveyard is gone and you have a loyal friend forever!

title: It just works
text:
I've been struggling with low back pain from facet arthritis. Can't afford a chiropractor or physical therapist right now, so I thought "what do they do that I don't." Obviously, I can't adjust my back like a chiropractor would, but truthfully physical therapy helps just as much. What was the ONE THING they did that I couldn't do at home? TRACTION. Stretching. I searched and this item came up. I saw the reviews. I thought, okay, for less than $30, we'll give it a try.
I am a fairly out-of-shape 62 year old woman who was diagnosed with osteoarthritis at age 30. It's been a long, painful road. The last few weeks have seen me walking tipped forward, with acute spasms. I was doing all my exercises and nothing was getting better.
This beautiful item arrived Saturday. I used it Saturday evening, twice a day on Sunday and Monday, and once so far today.And.....
I can stand up straight! My lumbar muscles actually feel RELAXED!
I am 100% sold on this baby. I just have to think of a name for him (yes, I named my heating pad and ice pack, too).
My only recommendation is to get up very slowly and gently afterwards. You don't want to undo the good you just did. I ease onto my side, then onto my stomach for a minute or two. Come up into child's pose, then some cat/cow stretches.

text: Many people are disappointed about the updated version in which the sheets are a bit smaller and some say it tears more easily.  I have been purchasing the older version for quite some time and am happy with that but I must say that this updated version is better.  Although the sheets are a bit smaller, I feel that the size is perfect and makes it not wasteful.  I recently saw on the news that sewage companies have been complaining about these so called "flushable" wipes clogging up the sewage system so it is possible that Pampers had to make the sheets a bit thinner so it doesn't back up the sewage system.  For that matter maybe most of the wipes will eventually have to be thinner or "weaker" in some way.  These wipes need to break apart in water and when I tested the old wipes, it did not do that too well but these newer ones seem to break apart more easily.  I did not notice these new sheets being any thinner but I do remember the old version being very thick which is why many people like the old version.  I like these new wipes just as much as the old ones and if being a bit thinner is what it takes to keep these wipes coming and not have it banned for clogging up sewage systems, then I am all for that. title: Screening & Grounding
text:
I have personally met Clint Ober and Dr. James Oschman and tried out the grounding sheets. I noticed the mixed comments left here, some had seen great improvements some have seen none. I have to tell you about some of my own discoveries:

I sleep with a grounded metal screen underneath my bed since the late 1970s, after my mother had a dowser check her bedroom and where the dowser found a crossing of `water veins' (but could also be the Hartmann or Curry grids, discovered by physicians Dr. Ernst Hartmann and Dr. Manfred Curry) underneath the bed of my father who passed away due to stomach cancer in 1974. Since then I became interested in the subject dowsing. After meeting Clint Ober and Dr. James Oschman about 10 years ago, who promotes sleeping grounded, I experimented with batteries that I connected into the grounding circuit. When the negative pole was connected to the screen (or grounding mattress pad) and the positive pole of the batteries connected to ground, I, and a friend of mine who replicated my experiment, had severe nightmares. But with the positive pole connected to the screen or pad there was no ill effect and for us indistinguishable from just being grounded without any batteries.

Very recently, a friend of mine asked me to shield his bed because he could not sleep. After putting aluminum fly mesh underneath his mattress and connecting a single 9 V battery, with the positive pole to the screen and the negative pole connected to the safety ground of the power outlet, he slept fine. He also experimented with the shielding and grounding. He unplugged the ground from the power plug, he removed the battery but kept the power plug in the socket so the aluminum screen was directly connected to the safety ground of the power plug, but only the combination with the battery gave him his needed sleep. I installed a screen at a bed of an elderly woman who has severe insomnia. Although this did not solve her insomnia, she reported that she felt like being inside a cocoon when she slept (using sleeping pills) with the screen (plus the 9 V battery and grounding). She also has a small grounding pad that she uses in addition to the screen but which is connected to the screen.

So my recommendation here is to use this metal mesh shield (aluminum fly screen from Home Depot, for example) as described with a single 9 V battery in the ground loop TOGETHER with the grounding pad. But connect the grounding pad to the screen, so both are connected to the plus pole of the battery and the negative pole connected to the safety ground of the power plug (or into moist soil.)

title: DOES THE JOB NICELY. Nice piece after removing chain and  re-attaching ring!
text:
Replacing an older lost leather snap cock ring-Medium to heavy duty. Took time to wear into comfortable. So I am liking this one a lot so far with the pros/cons below. you decide which is which.

The leather is light/medium - so wear comfortable from go. But quite suitable for leading.. and does EMPHASISE a command or direction with a firm to hard pull when needed. Believe me the wearer feels it!!!
I did modify this ring upon receiving it. The chain is an annoyance more than a benefit. It is attached by a small ring and ball-loop rivet to the leather in a good place.. But that means you have a 12 inch, pretty thin, chain hanging with a quarter sized ring swinging between your legs if you get up to walk anywhere. Or it, as I learned from a similar "toy", can also be quite painful if it swings too wildly mistakenly turning to fast etc. It is breakable-dangerous to painful to anything and anyone within 12 inches!!!!!!
My modification:
The metal rings are NOT welded. So with gentle effort and a pair of large, long nosed-needle nose plyers, I opened the bigger ring (Where you would hook the leash I guess) and spread it open enough to slip the chain out.
(Now you can either open the small ring first to remove the chain from it, or just use wire cutters to clip a link of the chain at either side, on either step, now or last step.)
Then I inserted the small ring into the larger rings opening, and closed the larger ring with a vice. Turn the ring to ensure a tight fit. *You may also choose to add some gorilla glue or JB weld when closing the ring as I did. This is to help ensure smoothing edges, and it doesn't open later during play, as my lover has a tendency to get very aggressive at times. (Wipe excess glue/epoxy off very very well or you will have to sand it down later with a nail file.)
If you have not already removed the chain from the small ring, you can do it here. "Clip".

Finished product will have the larger ring- to still attach ANY leash to.. But you will not have the rings in the way, OR 12 inches of chain dangling between your legs even when "off leash"! Busting stuff up including your own family jewels.

Only took off 1 star on thickness - due to the chain. The leather and all other aspects were a perfect fit.

I also went to my local SUPERSTORE's hobby/sewing section and bough the same size snap (female) covers, to snap on the un-used -exposed "male" snaps. Finishes the look and makes it more comfortable.

Bottom line- Does it work? Let me answer that with a question. How big of an idiot are you? No, seriously. Like, are you big enough of an idiot that in your excitement of getting your smartwatch in the mail, you wore it in spite of the fact that you were working with roofing materials and metal flashing without any regard for the glass of said watch, only finding out later what you hath wrought? This is a purely hypothetical question.

The kit itself come with multiple ways to understand how to use it, and points out that you may get frustrated with the effort and time needed and to take breaks. Great advice. If you have scratched watch crystal, I have no doubt in my mind that this will work AND impress you. If you've managed to etch canyons formed over millions of years of erosion into the surface of your watch, like, hypothetically, then temper your expectations.

The photo I have posted is the result of using, in sessions, ALL of the included materials plus a buffing pad on a dremel (Be mindful of heating a smartwatch surface if you go that route) and a couple hours of work. Is it perfect? good lord no. did it impress me? Hell yes. it was difficult to photograph the scratches after the effort. the scratches are on a scale of gone to much smoother but noticeable. It has improved the clarity and the feel of the watch.

Is it worth the 18 bucks or whatever? Yes. Just be patient. And don't be an idiot. I'm giving this 4 stars because I'm selfishly keeping a star for me as a consolation for being an idiot.

title: I'm keeping it
text:
It's hard to write this review, because it might be too good to be true.
My husband has had severe, and I mean severe, back pain for seven years, ever since he was a young teen. We could only just manage the pain, not alleviate it. It kept us from doing so many things we wanted to do.
Then we bought this pillow. It was comfy. I made him use it, just to keep him comfy.
Three weeks after we bought it, he woke up in no pain.
Guys.
No. Pain.
If you know anyone with chronic issues, you know this is a big deal.
Like I said earlier, it was too good to be true, so we waited. It's been months, and he's only had a few recurrences after a lot of exertion.
I'm not a doctor, and I do believe in miracles, so draw your own conclusions. As for me, I'm a happy camper, and I'm keeping this pillow.

title: Cornerstone of my healthy lifestyle change
text:
I love this scale. It has been 5 months since I purchased it. I wanted to make sure it held up before rating. This has truly changed how I approach my health and weight. Most of that change comes from within, but this has been the cornerstone of my change in habits. Obviously the wi-fi connection is the standout feature, but just as important is the Fitbit software that the measurements are sync'd to. With my weight (and my wife and 2 kid's weight) automatically sync'ing with every use, it's hard to make excuses, and it's easy to see progress that encourages you to keep going.

I have also been entering everything I eat and drink into the Fitbit website, which establishes what calorie deficit is needed to reach your goal and in what time. You get a badge for every 5 pounds you lose, and see dials and graphs showing your progress. I feel all of this has helped me stick with it for 5 months, and will keep me going into the future.

I do not track steps with a Fitbit band, but have been hand entering runs from my Suunto GPS watch to track calories burned above and beyond my basic metabolism. I also linked up Fitbit with Microsoft Healthvault to marry up other health information.

title: Not that useful or secure
text:
I found this basket to be less than satisfactory. It has a very small base so larger items will not fit well (like my 64oz growler water bottle). I have a Knee Rover All Terrain Quad, but am tall so I have the handlebars on the last hole from the bottom to make them high enough for me. This means that the recommended placement of below the adjustment knob is not workable as it is awkward to reach (too low) and it interferes with using the folding mechanism. Consequently, I put it on the upper part of the handlebars. As the post there is thinner, it was less secure even with the extra grip pads provided (it moves or slips down). The single attachment ring just is not enough if you need to hold somewhat heavier items like a full water bottle.

My husband installed my Wald rectangular bicycle basket instead that I have used on a seated knee scooter for years (purchased here on Amazon). It had two attachment points on the handlebars around the center post and a third bracket the basket fits into. It is far more secure and holds much more given its wider flat bottom than the cheaper made Knee Rover model.

I would not recommend this basket unless you do not have much to carry or are short enough to attach the basket on the lower Knee Rover post. Even then, I still think it would interfere too much with the folding knob. I returned mine for a refund.

title: Actually does what it claims :)
text:
I bought this because my dentist was telling me that I was bordering on the line of gum disease. I've taken it for 6 months and recently had my cleaning appt. Although they didn't verbally tell me anything, like whether my teeth were improved or not, I could tell they barely had to do any scraping. Just a lil' bit between the teeth. I'd say that's a DEFINITE improvement.

This is what my routine is like: I take 1 pill in the morning and 1 pill in the afternoon. I floss everytime I brush, and on top of that I add a drop of tea tree oil to the toothpaste. Once a day (at night) I rinse with ACT mouthwash. It might sound like a pain, but really the only additive in the normal oral hygiene regimen is taking the pills and adding the oil to the paste.

I also reccomend to take the pills with milk or some other flavored beverage. It masks the taste of the actual pill. If I just take it with water I can taste it... and if you burp afterwards you taste it again. LOL

title: SUPPORT + COMFORT (yes, they are two different things)
text:
I purchased this directly from purple when I saw the "egg test" mattress add on you tube.
I have a herniated disc between L4/L5 and get lower back pain after sitting for more than 20 min or so. Most lumbar pillows I have tried are both too firm and too bulky, which forces you forward in the chair (they work but are awkward). This is great because it gives the support without "the bulk". It still has great support but doesn't force you forward in the chair because it absorbs the pressure much better than other pillows, even better than the memory foam lumbar pillows I have tried.

The only negative in my opinion is also the greatest thing about the pillow... the gel like 'floppyness' of the pillow. This is a double edge sword because it allows for excellent comfort, but you need to hold it in the correct spot when first sitting down otherwise it will fold/flop and or droop with gravity... In other words you can't leave it in "the perfect spot" on the chair and have it stay because it will droop. There is another factor related to this... on the back there are two loops in the cover that I assume are for a strap that will attach it to the chair? there are no instructions for this and no strap included so that is just a guess. Even with a strap I don't see that working because of the floppyness of the pillow and the stretchy characteristic of the cover.

As an FYI, the packaging suggests that this can double as a travel pillow to sleep on... I tried using it as a pillow one night and was not impressed. It would be better than nothing but I slept pretty poorly that night due to the discomfort.

The 5 star rating is for EXCELLENT lumbar support and EXCELLENT comfort in the same pillow.

title: Could work during these WFH times
text:
Upon wearing it, there was a noticable difference in sitting upright. Good quality straps that don't seem like it will loosen soon, and the back part is a rubber/semi-matte-plastic material that pushes your muscles up. Out of the box, there was a slight smell that probably can be rid off by tossing it in the good ol washer.

From an anatomy perspective, the reason why we have the desk slouch, or "potato chip" slouch is due to overdeveloped lats, and underdeveloped rhomboids. If you sit up straight, and feel the back of shoulder blades connect to each other, that part of the muscle is usually the weak muscle developed from being a desk warrior. (Imagine if that muscle was really strong, you couldn't even slouch if you wanted to)

This helps in that it pushes and engages some part of this muscle, but I also suspect that I can only work with a good exercise routine that trains that specific part. The shoulder strap keeps you upright, engaging that lazy muscle that we grow accustomed to relaxing, but we would also need to give it some gym time such that overtime it becomes strong on its on. Personally, I also think this should be eased-in when wearing, such that you don't develop aches or muscle injury from something too drastic.

Search up "How To Fix Rounded Shoulders FAST (10 Minute Science-Based Corrective Routine)" on YouTube, there's more details in there that can perhaps complement this device well.

*** I am not a doctor, or licensed practitioner, all thoughts above are my opinions only and cannot be construed as advice. Please see your doctor or licensed physical therapist for any personal issues. ***

title: Decent Knife for the Price!
text:
[[VIDEOID:f3fa5de8670896c64418ab7516df3326]] A sharp knife is one of the best tools in the kitchen. Unfortunately, good knives can cost hundreds of dollars.
This knife is made of good Cro-Moly high carbon steel. Although it is a bit rough around the edges, it is a good solid design with good balance and hand feel. My only complaint is that the back edge of the knife isn't completely straight. While most of the time you don't cut with that back edge, it is important for the back edge to be straight so that the entire blade makes contact with the cutting board when you bring the knife down. I have to take off a whole star for this.

Overall I think it is a decent knife for the price and I think I may have just gotten one that wasn't quite as good as others. If it weren't for that curve at the back I would give it a full 5 stars.

Pros:
+ Made of High Carbon Chromium Steel
+ Good Grinding on the Blade Edge
+ Wooden Handle that is Weighted Properly
+ Finger Guard
+ Balanced Quite Well

Cons:
- Overall a Rough Around the Edges
- Back of Blade is not Completely Straight

Watch This Video in Full HD Over on My YouTube Channel: GadgetClass
This knife was provided to GadgetClass for Testing and Review

text:
So, first, I have taken Krill Oil before, it does alot for me. For instance, it decreases PMS for me, alleviates joint pain that I get occasionally or if I've had a minor injury, and I find sleep better when taking it. So, I looked online for a krill oil to start taking again. I found this one here and it seemed to be of good quality. I have read the reviews stating that the omega 3's and epa levels were not high enough. In my opinion and experience I have not needed those higher doses to get the medicinal effects of it. This theory was put to the test recently with trying the DailyNutra Neptune Krill Oil.

So, after taking for a while I noticed a huge reduction with the PMS again! I am sleeping better. I am calmer in situations that I haven't been lately. And, some joint pain I was having is gone again. During the day I definitely noticed more energy. I am a big believer in Krill Oil and COQ10 and this brand does not disappoint. I am so satisfied with results that I will be a repeat buyer. The pills are small and you take two, simple. No smell but do have a mildly sweet vanilla taste. I actually like the taste, different from the other krill that I took.

I can recommend this brand of krill oil with no doubts. It has worked for me.

Neptune Krill Oil (NKO) is known for its unique fatty acid (FA) profile, as well as for its rich antioxidant content. NKO's balanced fatty acid content includes not only EPA and DHA, the crucial Omega-3 , but Omega-9 and phospholipids, as well. NKO is a rich source of Astaxanthin, a powerful immune-supporting antioxidant. Clinical studies have shown that NKO can support joint comfort, healthy blood lipid levels, and may reduce symptoms of pre-menstrual syndrome.

KRILL OIL VS FISH OIL: Krill oil is an omega-3 nutrient and is an alternative source of omega-3 than fish oil. Some folks prefer krill oil over fish oil because they believe it has increased bioavailability and better absorption than fish oil, and contains the additional nutrients, Astaxanthin and Phospholipids. In fact, this is correct. Krill oil has better bioavailability and absorption than fish oil and contains Astaxanthin and Phospholipids, neither of which are contained in fish oil.

ASTAXANTHIN: Astaxanthin is a powerful anti-oxidant and anti-inflammatory. It is a red-pink substance found in various seafoods such as salmon, trout, krill, lobster and cooked shrimp. It is responsible for the red color of salmon meat, cooked shellfish and flamingo feathers. It is present in krill oil but not in fish oil.

The presence of astaxanthin in krill oil, combined with other naturally occurring antioxidants in the oil (Vitamins E and A), provides protection against oxidation of the oil, making it stable for a long time. It also protects the body against free radical attacks which can cause aging of the cells. Antioxidants are usually added in fish oil to prevent the oil from oxidizing as they do not have any on their own.

title: My Redneck* Jacuzzi
text:
(*I'm actually the farthest from a redneck you'll ever meet. I live in Minneapolis and I wear clothing from Talbots. I drive a Toyota Camry.There's a support group for people like me.)

God made two things that secured my happiness in this world: Marshmallows and bubbles. This is a review about the latter and a device that promises to be a "spa-like" experience. (Marshmallows in a bathtub might be delicious, but it's weird. And gross.)

Like me, you stumbled across this device and thought: "Now, I no longer have to make my own bath bubbles." (Don't ask.) It looks magical, and comfortable. The product description boasts, "Soothing bath bubbles. Variable speeds. Heat maintenance." Upon the unboxing, I saw a very long cord, a machine that makes bubbles and a bathmat that looked like it was something Lady Gaga wore on tour. You place the long cord into the wall outlet, and you connect the hose-thing to the Lady Gaga thing. Then you turn it on and it makes BUBBLES. Truthfully, it does make bubbles. But it doesn't stick to the bottom of any textured bathtub. This is where s*** got real.

I'm not one to give up easily, so I sat on the bubble mat, which was not nearly as graceful as you might think. Because the suction cups are made of non-suction-y stuff, (purely the scientific term,) they will not work with bathtubs that are not 100% smooth. This means you have to actually clean your tub with each use, and it has to not be a "bath-fitter" tub, or any tub with texture.

Instead of a peaceful bathing experience, the mat will find you with its evil bubble tentacles and hunt you down in a way that can only be described as, "Bathtub assault." The mat came up as my delicate body tried to hold it down, and unfortunately the Lady Gaga-like structure won. It mocked me with the, "gel-filled padding," and it's, "tri-bubble speeds." It made bubbles clearly, but I had to sit through arduous torture to have the bubbles. It was like college.

Keep in mind the warranty is a Homedics warranty. One year? If I had a single Homedics device that worked after the 2nd week of use, it'd be a miracle. Homedics is like that time you were short on cash so you ordered the crappy Tequila instead of the top shelf tequila. You paid with your evening and the puking. (You promised yourself, "Oh! Never again!" But alas, they get you with their photos of women in a zen-like state on the box, or being pure and not being able to afford a REAL jacuzzi tub. Whatever.) Additionally, Homedics keeps Bed Bath & Beyond in business, which is unfortunately where I picked up this gem. The horror continues.

Skip it. Don't try it thinking it'll be different for you. (Oh, but your bathtub has a shiny surface and it's so shiny that you could brush your hair whilst gazing into its white, porcelain beauty? The suction cups will fail you, bathtub-gazer.) You can still win if you hit your back button and buy yourself some marshmallows instead. Those never fail me.

title: Permanent addition to my beauty routine
text:
I am not a dermatologist, and these statements have not been evaluated by the FDA. This is based off of my personal experience. What works for me may not work for you.

A friend was raving about konjac sponges so I decided to give them a shot. I've never tried to use this type of sponge before. My facial routine is pretty minimal. Wow. My skin is so happy I added these in to my routine!It's very smooth to the touch and doesn't feel like it's really doing much, but it sure is working! The string through the sponge is brilliant, I love that it has an included hook to keep it handy on the mirror or in the shower. I keep mine on my mirror by the sink. They dry pretty quickly considering they're a sponge, I use it once a day and it's always dry when I go to use it again.

I have psoriasis and the patches are annoying. It's good to exfoliate my psoriasis patches to keep them smoother but it's hard to get myself to do because most other ways I've tried were painful for me. Not with this sponge. It did a good job of removing the scales and it didn't hurt at all. I didn't notice an addition of pain even days after. I've been using the charcoal sponge in the shower on my psoriasis patches. It's a great way for me to get a little relief from the itching. Combining this with an intense moisturizing routine has helped me immensely.

The packaging of the sponges is nice and I wouldn't mind giving it as a gift. It would be a great addition to a health and beauty themed gift basket. The sponges work well with facial washes and They are pretty easy to rinse clean when you've finished. This will be a permanent addition to my beauty routine.

title: These are hard for me to put a fair review on.
text:
I've had leg swelling due to blood clots from a factor five clotting issue. I was prescribed 30-40mmHg socks, and I was fitted for Medi Size - V socks at a local medical supply shop, but I paid $100 for the pair locally. I only need the left one so I figured these being non L/R specific - unlike the Medi version that I simply turn the right one inside out - and cheaper were worth a try.

They're not for me.

Despite the fact they're not for me I'm going to give them a passing but not glowing review. They do the job. The reason they're not for me is I'm built weird, I'm slightly outside the normal human range for muscle mass - and not just developed muscle mass, but in general. I don't have a double muscle mutation, but I'm just out of range and I have trouble getting a lot of things to fit. The size of this sock that accommodates my leg thickness is meant for someone quite a bit taller than myself, as a result they don't fit me well, they have a tendency to roll up and chap the back side of my knee. They also cut off some circulation at the top as a result. I'm giving this issue a pass since I recognize I'm a freak.

The reason I'm giving these a three star instead of a four or five is the fact the elastic isn't the greatest, after a few washings (but no dryer) some of the elastic is coming loose and popping out through the fabric like an over-worn old pair of tighty-whities. I'm no longer going to buy this brand and I'm going to stick with the Medi brand since they fit better and I can get them much cheaper here on Amazon, even though they do cost more than these.

If these fit you well go for it, I don't see anything that screams "do not buy". At this price even if they do wear out quicker than Medi (which may or may not fit you well) the lower cost could balance that out.

text: It is obviously a well-made and well-thought-out product, but here's the problem: although the manual is pretty much comprehensible, getting this thing to pull sound out of a TV and then wirelessly send it to the earbuds proved to be almost impossible. In the end I had to use the analog (red & white) leads and hook them up to the cable box - which means that only programming that originates with cable TV is delivered through the device. Well, I'd like it to feed all the sound which relates to the TV, but none of the analog ports from the TV produced sound in these earbuds. So, for example, when I'm streaming something and the sound does come from the TV it still doesn't feed this device. Believe me, I tried all the plugs. If anyone can tell me why this is and what to do about it I would greatly appreciate the guidance. Furthermore, the extra functions that this hearing enhancer offers are pretty much not on my list of needs - but there they are and I have to pay for them too. Why doesn't this company make a device that is specifically for TV sound, and then explain that it is not going to work except when hooked up to the cable box. Lastly, the earbuds that came with it are supposed to be mute-able, but that does not work. So I have to listen to the ads or take the buds out of my ears. Something very GOOD about this device is that I can walk away from the TV and around the corner and work in the kitchen and the sound from the TV comes with me. title: Works great on stainless steel
text:
Been using this product for more than a year now and worked great always for me. Most of my dishes are stainless steel and often some of them gets dirty because of grease and oils.

I finally got into a situation where one of my dishes are too greasy and messy. This cleaner and polisher saved me time and money and it brought back life to my dishes again.

As you can see in the pictures I attached, there is lot of grease and dirt in my pan and applied about 2-3 squeezes of the bottle. After the squeezes, scrub the cleaner around the pan and wait for few minutes. The manufacturer label says 30secs, But I would recommend giving 2-5mins for tougher stains like these.

In the first round of cleaning, the grease did not go from the pans all the way. More than 70% of the grease was gone. I had to apply another round of cleaner, as the grease was tougher.

After second round of cleaning, the grease was totally removed, and the pan got cleaner like new condition.

Overall, very satisfied with this product and worked great for my dishes. As I mentioned, for tougher stains give it few more mins and try scrubbing and it should work.

title: Great wax, Easy on/off, Great for Black cars. Think of it as Rain-X for paint
text:
I bought mine at WalMart. The wax behaves like Rain-X for paint, with it's beading action. It does provide a deep shine on a black car and it's application is very easy. Wax On and wax off. But seriously the application is indeed easy, no need to buff. Just spread a thin layer with the applicator sponge, then after about 30 seconds or less, follow it up with the microfiber cloth to remove it. That's it. No elbow grease necessary.
Now for better shine, I would clay the car before applying the wax. Claying is also very easy thing to do and you only have to do it once or twice a year.
So anyhow here is my procedure of doing things.
1) grab a plastic baggy and place your finger in it, then rub your finger across the paint. If you feel any bumps then clay the car before waxing.
2) Do a quick wash of the car, no buffing, high pressure wash and rinse.
3) Spray Iron-X all over the car, let it stand for 4 minutes (don't let it dry). This will remove any micro metalic particles that might have inbeded in the paint while driving (break dust from other cars etc).
4) perform a good water rinse of the car (with water)
5) Clay the car
6) Perform a good wash now (with cloth, etc)
7)Apply Extreme Shield Wax.

The only negative thing of the shield wax is that it does not last too long. It will last at most 2 months or 2 mechanical car washes.
Also, IT"S NOT A WAX! It's a Sealant. I would recommend that folks read differences between the two at autogeek dot net

Iron X: http://www.amazon.com/Carpro-Iron-Remover-500-Ml/dp/B004UM6DLE/ref=sr_1_1?ie=UTF8&qid=1403211895&sr=8-1&keywords=iron+x
P.S.
I learned this the hard way. No matter what the picture shows, the Shield Wax is NOT BULLET PROOF!

title: Much more effective on my psoriasis than Cortaid (topical steroid)
text:
I really don't want to write this review. Like you, I have a million other things to do. But this cream has worked so well for me that I feel a responsibility to write this review. I suffer from psoriatic arthritis, and have had small patches of psoriasis on my skin for decades. Topical steroids (like Cortaid) have kept these patches somewhat under control, by eliminating cracking and bleeding. But this minimal relief requires taking the maximum dosage, and I wonder what effect this chronic use of topical steroids has had on my body.

After talking with a sales rep at Whole Foods (in Framingham, MA. Hi! Thank you!), I decided to give this cream a try. I was highly skeptical, especially considering the price (I'm a guy), but I figured that I had little to lose. And WOW!, was I pleasantly surprised!

I applied the cream on average about 4 times/day for a month, and my psoriasis has COMPLETELY disappeared! Completely. I now have normal skin on my knuckles. It's taking some getting used to.

So I cannot recommend this cream highly enough. My wife has noticed and is using it on her split cuticles. It's working for her as well.

And DON'T WORRY ABOUT THE PRICE. What is healthy skin worth? The cream also goes a very long way. I was using it 4 times/day on four knuckles, and at that rate I wouldn't have gone through a container in a year. I have now cut back slightly.

You don't have to suffer anymore. Best wishes for success.

title: Actually, pretty good!
text:
These are actually some of the best of the cheaper ear plugs I've bought (haven't bought any expensive ones yet, so I can't compare).

I like foam plugs but they hurt my ears, so I got these. If comfort if your problem, try the blue pair, (all 4 have different comfort and noise reduction levels). The blue ones are definitely the easiest on my ears (as the directions even state, but I'll vouch for this). They really hit the sweet spot (for me at least) since you can adjust it (in a way) for different levels of noise reduction and keep taking them in/out, without hurting your ears.

The grey pair are also good because they're pretty comfortable but don't block so much noise that you can hear your breathing, heart rate, etc. (like the blue and orange pair seem to do). The directions also say this, but I'll also vouch for this too. They aren't as comfortable as the blue pair, but moreso than the orange pair.

Also, I almost forgot -- I live in an area where if you fall asleep without earplugs you WILL be woken up, so I really wanted something that was cheap, for extended use (so I can wear them all the time and not forget to put them in before falling asleep), but that could be repurchased economically if needed. I didn't want to drop $30 for a pair of almost-the-same-thing, so this saved me ~$19.

The directions are actually pretty good, also, but they should state how removing them too quickly can damage your eardrums (a lot of people don't know this). Only other recommendation I would make to them is to switch the white pair with foam plugs, since I'll never use the pure white kind, but might use a pair of foam plugs if they happened to come with it. Or just make another set with foam plugs added and sell it for $1-2 more than this set. That way you'll have every type/kind and not need to buy other brands.

Just wanted to write this since they were a pretty good purchase, and glad I found them since they saved me from buying a bunch of different kinds.

Edit: You CAN cut the blue ones down to size to make sleeping in them easier, but you may not be able to get them out of your ear then. Had this happen twice, but it's not their fault. They should say that, though, maybe, just to sound honest.

title: I did my own comparison
text:
To be fair, I have been taking a very good supplement for quit some time, Andrew Lessman's Essential 1, this is a multivitamin, and I take B-12, D, C, Co-q10, vein and circulation support, which are all separately and sold within his line of nutritional products. I've only had one complaint, they are all in capsule form, and even though not hard to swallow, I'm just tired of popping pills everyday. My brother had been urging me to try this Tangy Tangerine. So I finally broke down and ordered some.
I want to add that I had a Gastric Bypass 10 years ago, so I do not absorb vitamins and minerals like the average person, infact recently I have had D, B-12 and Iron deficiencies, which caused some big problems. Mostly, lack of Iron, but I have also been taking Andrew's Iron supplement everyday that has helped greatly. (I forgot to mention that above ) when this happened, it was a wake up call, so I got on supplements and take them religiously now.
As I mentioned above, vitamin absorbsion is a big problem with me, so the idea of a supplement drink made sense to me.
I have taken pictures of the Supplement Facts label of both products for comparison. The first picture is Andrew Lessman's label, and the second and third are Tangy Tangerine. As you can see, there are higher levels of everything in Tangy Tangerine. I am guessing it's because in capsule form, you may be limited, as compared to drinking the supplement. There are also important enzymes you need like Co-Q10 in TangyTangerine, that you have to buy separately in Andrew's line. And a big one for me, Potassium is in Tangy Tangerine, not in the supplement I was taking. Glucosamine and Chondrotin, is in this, not in Andrew's, again, you have to purchase separately.
Then there is the price to consider, and good vitamins and minerals do not come cheaply. I was spending on the average, about 100.00 a bottle for each supplement, although, that was a 1 year supply of each. So, actually, when I spent 60.00 for Tangy Tangerine, the breakdown is about 720.00 per year, with all the supplements you could ever need in the product. Whereas for Andrew's I was spending about 600.00 per year. I was not getting the levels in Andrew's that I am getting in Tangy Tangerine. So I say price wise, it's a toss up.
I have just started Tangy Tanderine, so I may have to update this review as to long term results. As far as taste, it's tolerable, just like the label says it tastes like tangy tangerine. I did not feel the extreme energy boost after the first drink like others have reported, but then I have already been on some very good supplements for a long time, so I may not be a good example. Someone who is not taking anything may feel an energy kick, I don't doubt that. I was not really clear on how much water to mix this with, so I took a bottle of crystal geiser bottled water, put it in the blender, added the powder and it blended up ok. I've read others saying they use half a cup to 8 oz of water or juice. I am now using 6 to 8 oz of water with a few ice cubes in the blender, and it actually tastes better with less water. The only sweetner I see in this product is stevia, and I do not mind that, but that is a choice you'll have to make.

title: Spend extra $’s To deter rust and sharp edges: DIY improvements
text:
I guarantee This device will rust the way I use it, so I applied Rustoleum (inside & out). The paint will probably also smooth out any sharp metal edges that would destroy fabric during wash agitation. I took extra precaution to remove sharp edges by applying epoxy before applying primer and paint (as suggested by another reviewer,)
I prepped for paint with DAWN dish soap to remove any potential machine oils, then lightly sanded reachable surfaces I could reach to give paint something to hold on to.
To paint the inside where I cannot reach with a brush, a taped up the very top holes with strips of duct tape, poured primer paint inside device, and rolled washer around to cover all inside surfaces, then removed tape to drain excess paint into paint bucket.
I hang painted surfaces that will touch fabric, but was careful not to leave bumpy thick drops of paint that might damage fabric from repeated washing sessions.
I also bought a larger wood handle from a hardware store.
I like the feel of this metal washing device compared to competitor’s plastic versions, but rust is a deal breaker, so without applying paint, I’d stick to plastic, which I modified with a taller handle.

title: Big 33.8fl oz bottle of Swedish bitters
text:
This 3.38fl oz bottle of Swedish Bitters Elixer is claimed to be prepared according to a centuries-old recipe to provide the benefits of bitter foods often missing from the modern western diet.

Compared to a natural human diet, modern western diets tend to be sugar- and salt-rich to make the food more addictive and tasty. This product is particularly useful for maintaining good, balanced digestive function especially if you sometimes have to eat on-the-run and don't have the time to prepare `proper food,' and most especially if you have any kind of impaired liver function.

Swedish bitters are also claimed by sufferers to help with all kinds of other conditions, from fibromyalgia to viral illnesses to acne. The manufacturer however promotes no such claims, and it's best to consult with your doctor or herbalist prior to having high cure-expectations; though it needs to be emphasised that the product is safe with no cautions or counter-indications, so swallowing the liquid poses no health risk.

The squared-off bottle is of thick brown glass, with a plastic screw-top. It's very secure and robust. You only need a teaspoonful at a time and don't usually need to take it every day, so the content can last some weeks. The elixir itself is watery in consistency, with a pale brown color. It dissolves in a glass of water if you want to take it that way.

title: Smell - It smells like wax? Quite similar to bedhead wax stick that ...

I don't really see why there are so many negative reviews for this product. I have used one complete tube now for a couple months so I feel I can give a decent long term review.

Smell - It smells like wax? Quite similar to bedhead wax stick that I use also... it's not a bad smell but its not really what a person would say smells awesome.

Texture - It's a bit softer than skateboard/surf wax but still has some heft at room temp.

Longevity - I apply the product to my glasses (Oakley Survo) and it lasts about 8 hours at full grip and drops of quite quickly from there. This may be due to having very oily skin in my case.

Ease of use - I mean there is a video... I apply it like the video in about 30 - 45 seconds. I clean the wax off nightly. Id say its pretty easy but it does not apply or clean itself...

Value - It lasts a long time... I apply a very generous amount one time a day and the tube lasted nearly 3 months.

Conclusion - This is MILES better than other options I used prior to Nerdwax. My glasses actually stay on my head and don't slip at all for the 8+ hours the products lasts, even after it still prevents slipping significantly over not having the product applied. Overall this is a winner and I am repurchasing (this time the 3 pack) as there is NO better solution.

text:
I was shopping for a durable set of earplugs that didn't just muffle all sound. I have dealt with tinnitus and some hearing loss for years now and do all I can to keep it from getting any worse. My tinnitus and hearing loss is all of my own making in my wild teens and twenties youth of working with power equipment and tools for years at my then job, and also doing loud things like flying airplanes and riding motorcycles on my off time, all without ever even at least stuffing cotton in my ears. So I'm paying for it now with that always and constant whistle tone.
These "DownBeats" turned out work great, easy to insert, I wanted the long stem for that, and to take out, also easy to keep clean too. And most importantly, they reduce the sounds without totally blocking it all. I really like the metal carrying case too, I keep these with me all the time now since I'd rather have them with me and not necessarily need them than need them and not have them! I will buy them again if I need to, an inexpensive investment that I now wish had been more easily available back in the 70s and 80s.

title: Still a bit too big
text:
I ordered this travel jewelry organizer because my small old one is starting to show some wear and after looking at numerous options I decided on this one from Conair.

While I really like the padded exterior as well as the interior design and organization of this travel case - it will hold plenty of jewelry - I felt that in the end it was a bit too big and bulky for me to take along on trips. I think though that it is very dependent on what type of travel you do. It should work perfectly for road trips and even short air travel, especially for those among us who love to bring a lot of their favorite pieces when going somewhere. However, for longer or intercontinental flights I find that it takes up too much room in my carry-on tote, especially because jewelry should always be placed in one's carry-on and not the checked luggage (with checked luggage being routinely opened in this post-9/11 world). Since my tote usually contains a neck pillow, a travel blanket, Kindle, and a bunch of other personal items such as reading glasses, earphones, moisturizers etc., my tote is already too full to be able to comfortably fit this case in as well.

Overall, this is a good-quality case with plenty of thought-out organizational features but I would like it better if it were about half the size because of the limited space I have, and because I usually only take just a few select pieces with me for which a smaller case would be sufficient. I recommend the case, but primarily for people for whom space isn't an issue.
