title: DO NOT BUY THIS!
text:
I'm still having problems trusting this to support my weight; it just seems too flimsy to do it. I'm 265 lbs. and this cane is rated for 300, but I'm skeptical if it really would support that weight. It's a plastic shell of a handle that houses the batteries and electronics and I can feel it flexing and making small crunching noises under my hand. Time will tell I suppose, I just hope I don't wind up on the ground. Other than that, I like the flashlight and blinking red light. They help quite a bit when I walk down my drive and out into the road to my mailbox at night. I wish there were a way to toggle them individually though. Sometimes I don't need the white light (full moon) but would like to have the red on for safety but that isn't an option. The first push of the button turns on the white light, the second adds the red to that, the third shuts them both off. It would be an improvement if the third turned off the white but left the red on, then the fourth shut them all off.

The alarm function, while I'm sure it has its uses, really isn't loud enough to help much, and my cats hate it. Oh well, it may come in handy at conventions... "Gangway! Old-fart coming through!" WeeeeeWeeeeeWeeee!

Update: So I got this on February 26th, and today is April 15th. 48 days. Still on the first set of batteries. That's how long it took to break. One side of the hinge on the battery door seems to have snapped, and the door no longer stays closed properly, causing the lights to flicker and go out when you least expect it. The plastic handle is also starting to split apart when I put my weight on the cane, causing it to pinch my fingers now and then. I'd send it back but it's just now worth the expense of the shipping and the cost of getting it to the post office to send it. (My truck gets 11 MPG and the post office is 25 miles round trip) It's a good idea, and I'd love it if it were better made, but I have to be able to trust it and it's not up to that.

Update July 26: I knew I should have gotten rid of this thing. I got lazy tonight, and instead of walking back to my office for my regular cane I grabbed this one in the garage to use taking the trash cans down to the street for pickup tomorrow. The thrice blasted thing broke on me as I was going down our steep driveway and I fell, banging myself up pretty good in the process. The handle snapped clean in two on it, right at the seam, and down I went. Batteries went one way, cane went another. I've got a nice gash on my hand where the plastic cut me that took a few stitches to close and I had to crawl on my hands and knees back up the driveway to the house. Took me about half an hour to do that with my bad knees and arthritis. I have half a mind to call my lawyer and sue, but I blame myself for not throwing this piece of junk away a long time ago.

title: Good product that suits my purposes
text: My doctor recommended Inositol to me as a natural alternative to taking prescription antidepressant drugs.  I did not feel that I was ready to go the route of prescription drugs--I avoid drugs as much as possible in my life.  But I needed a little help in dealing with stress and its effects on my health.  So I tried Inositol.  I take about a teaspoon in filtered water twice a day.  I feel it has really helped me to calm my sometimes stressful or chaotic thoughts and to approach my busy day with more mental clarity and less pressure.  The Inositol product I first tried was only available in a small bottle and very expensive.  Since I go through it fairly quickly I looked for more of a bulk supply and found Liftmode on Amazon.  I also tried an Inositol from another manufacturer.  The Liftmode product is far superior because it is less granular or gritty, and dissolves better (though not completely) in water.  I find the Liftmode product to be much more pleasant to take, easier to swallow than the grittier brands, and it continues to seem to help me deal with the stress in my life.  I have ordered and used at least three of these large jars now and plan to continue ordering in the future.  I also started taking Vitamin B12 about the same time as Inositol, to help my stress and keep my mental functioning at its best.  So I am not certain which of the two products helps me the most but I am content to keep using both, because I think they both help and provide me with something that was missing in my nutrition before I started using them.  The only downside to this product is that it is rather expensive, although not as much as prescription drugs, probably, and it is worth the cost for the good it seems to do.  Also, Inositol in general does not dissolve well in water.  As I said, this brand is better dissolving than others.  I put the powder into a little bit of water and just keep swirling it in the glass between sips, so that I can drink it quickly before the powder settles to the bottom.  If there is some left in the glass, I just keep adding a bit more water until I get it all down.  It is not unpleasant tasting.  It tastes like mildly sweet sugar water as I drink it.  My understanding is that Inositol is a sugar alcohol, so it is sweet tasting, but has no calories.  Also, in case you are wondering, it does not make me intoxicated!  ;)

title: This is the sleep mask I've been looking for
text:
I have a couple different sleep masks that are designed to fully cover the face, which is great because they block out 100% of all light. But the trade off is they have large straps that connect via velcro in the back, and that can be uncomfortable when sleeping on my back. I can feel the strap on the back of my head and it's annoying. I've been trying to find a more minimalist design and this sleep mask fits my needs perfectly.
First, it's very comfortable on the face. Nice smooth silky feel that is lightweight and doesn't rub. Second, the strap is very thing. So thin I don't feel it between my head and pillow when sleeping on my back. So important! The strap is easily adjustable. The mask does a great job at blocking out light. I will say it doesn't block out 100%, but about 95%. If I open my eyes with the mask on I do get a very little amount of light bleed on the sides, but when my eyes are closed I can't tell at all, and that's the important thing.
I will say I did need to experiment between the tightness of the mask vs. comfort. I found I don't want to wear this too tight (almost loose I would say) because the straps connect at the sides of the mask right, and if the mask is too tight it will cause annoying pressure on my eyes because they will pull the mask towards my face right where the mask crosses my eyes. So I need to wear it pretty loose so I don't get that pressure on my eyes. But I'm finding even when it is loose it still stays on, blocks the necessary amount of light and is very comfortable. I'll be using this for many years to come and my search is finally over!

title: Installation and configuration is Troublesome Regardless of method and no phone support!

Installation and configuration is Troublesome Regardless of method and no phone support!
I repeated the setup procedure multiple times on a MacBook and an iOS device (iPhone 5s).
Changing the the Routers configuration to accept b and g, seemed to solve part of the problem. Using the iOS device and not the MacBook with the "Fitbit Wi-Fi Scale Setup.app" seemed to solve another problem.

Put simply the "Fitbit Wi-Fi Scale Setup.app" didn't work at all using my MacBook (Retina latest OS version).

The iOS (iPhone 5s latest version) configuration using safari worked after changing my routers (Airport extreme) configuration to accept b and g as well as N.

As this is the default configuration on all routers those using an iOS device may not have any problems at all.

Fitbit has no phone support!

::This Konjac Sponge does exactly as described above! It's non abrasive so it doesn't leave your skin feeling scratched and raw but it does clean your pores like a pro! BIGGER, BETTER, UNIQUE DESIGN: Our Premium Konjac Sponge is longer, wider, and thicker than most other sponges, giving you more control, a longer life span, and a higher quality product. No more crunching up your circular sponge to get into the tight areas
::The shape of the sponge is perfect! The rounded edges are perfect for your cheeks, chin and forehead while the smaller end is the perfect size for your nose and eyes. My eyes looked brighter and my skin felt so smooth!

::When you open the package, the sponges are hard and dry. They kind of look like rocks and feel like a dried up loofah. All you have to do is soak the sponge in some warm water and you'll see it expand.It gets a little more than double the size and feels so soft. Rinse or cleanse your face with water or your normal facial cleanser. The warm water will open your pores which makes for better dirt removal with the Konjac Sponge. Then place the sponge in your palms and press together to remove the excess water. DO NOT squeeze or ring out like you would normally do with a dish sponge. I can only describe the way the sponge feels as rubbing a wet marshmallow on my face. I know that sounds weird but it's the only way I can describe the feel right now. When I finish cleaning my face, I place the sponge back in the bowl and rinse my face with cold water to close my pores. You will see the water in the bowl turn from clear to cloudy as the sponge expels all of the dead skin and dirt. Then again, gently press the water out of the sponge and rinse it under running warm water. Press again and hang to dry. Be sure to hang it in a well ventilated area. You don't want it getting moldy. It is made from a plant after all. Once it's all used up, you can simply throw it in the compost bin.

title: Nice big bath sponges
text:
[[VIDEOID:2bf0962d8847845cf50a903742bc7b5e]] I have to be honest and say, I really was not sure I would like these sponges for bathing with, I am more of a netting loofa kind of person, I figured if they were not my cup of tea, I could pop them in a gift basket here and there or they would make great stocking stuffers.

Well. I am beginning to think I AM a a bath sponge person. A true test for me is when I use my hand made soap with a loofa or in this case a sponge as to how well the soap suds on it. We have really hard water here and that can be quite the nemesis of hand made soap. I was super happy with how many suds were in the bowl after running it over the soap bar a few times and giving it a couple of squeezes.

You get 3 sponges in your pack, they are individually wrapped, all in a tear drop shape and they have a waffling pattern in the outer surface of the foam, it reminded me of the surface of a sea sponge. My yellow sponge has a slightly different pattern and feels a touch denser than the pink and orange ones. Each sponge has a white cotton corded handle to hang it by or pop over your wrist while using.

I can just picture bath time with little ones and these sponges and how much fun time in the tub could be. I found since they are over sized that they are easy to hold onto.

I will note that none of my sponges had any weird smells as rubber products often can, they are just a set a bright cheery sponges ready for you to enjoy.

title: Be prepared for the sheets to get stuck!
text: Seems my Central Vac pipes are very coated on the inside, probably due to the high humidity in our area. I first used a shop back to suction out any debris, and a lot came out.  Then, when I put one sheet in the closest inlet to the motor, and it got stuck.  Using a Shop Vac would not suck it back out. I had to cut the central line pipe to get the sheet out, and when I did I also removed "junk" totaling about the volume of a grapefruit. I resealed the pipe and put more sheets in from the 1st outlet and eventually "junk" about the volume of several grapefruit was in my central vac canister (I had cleaned the canister 1st).  I ordered a T PVC pipe fitting so I can add a clean-out along the central line pipe.  I did not want to start on the next outlet until I had build-in easy clean-out point. I then bought a 25' flexible plumber fish, and ran it into each inlet, starting with the closest to the canister with the vacuum on; wow, a lot more came out into the canister. Then I ran these sheets thru a few times from each inlet. Bottom line, these sheets will help a lot, but I had too much build-up inside my pipes for them to work initially. Now I will use them every so often so I don't have to go thru this again.

title: Amazing Deep Massages!
text:
Bought this with my own money, no sample given. I wanted to wait a bit to actually get some real usage in before reviewing this so as to have an accurate perspective. I do own a trigger point roller as well (the black one, densest they have) and this raw roller definitely gives it a run for it's money.

The truth is in the PVC piping they use, and it's REALLY dense. Compared to the trigger point, this thing has some heft for sure. It's still extremely portable though and is definitely not too heavy to carry (they even include a nice carrying bag, but the quality of the bag was sub-par, there's already a rip occurring near the straps). The foam that they use to coat the PVC pipe is very thin, but comfortable enough that there is a bit of cushion between your body and the roller. I'd say it's the bare minimum between comfort and discomfort, which is GREAT! You can definitely feel the deep massage in your muscles with this thing. The trigger point does give adequate massages as well, but if you really want to get DEEP, this roller is the way to go.

I also got a follow up email with cute pictures of the owner's dog in some spiffy shades with the roller next to it, so that was kinda cool. If you're looking for the next best thing to a PVC pipe, this is it!

title: At 29db These Only REDUCE Noise NOT Cancel
text:
I bought these to get me by, I have custom made (muscian's)earplugs that have removable/replaceable filters that went missing the 1st week of December. The cost of those was$165.00 so my hope was I would find them.
I ordered these as interim protection, I tune/repair pianos for a living & a piano when played loud is 120db. OSHA says anything over 90db should have hearing protection. These were very good except I have deep ear canals, I could put them in with my fingers. To remove them I have a small forceps (tweezers)that I had to use to remove them. Understand that 29db is NOT a lot of protection, it's enough for me for my work so I could still hear the piano. At 29db you can hear normal conversation, when YOU talk you will be VERY loud in your own head. 29db will protect you from some noise but Not seriously loud noise. If you coupled these withearmuff style hearing protection that would improve your hearing safety. In my shop around machinery I use shooters earmuffs, battery powered microphone for conversation, any noise louder than 80db INSTANTANEOUS SILENCE! For quieter machines I have 32db earmuff style hearing protection. Hearing is my business, so I am careful & try to be as knowledgeable as possible.

title: disappointing massage
text:
[[VIDEOID:6ce45d8875feadd039bda06437caad5a]] This review is for Back Massager with Heart and 8 Deep Tissue Massage
I was a little disappointed in this product.

There are two buttons on and change rotation. You have to push the on/off button a few times to switch the modes and then to finally turn it fully off. The modes are: slow rotation with heat, fast rotation with heat, slow rotation no heat and fast rotation with no heat) With either slow or fast it only changes the rotation speed. When it is on heat mode you will see it light up to a orangish/red.

Pros: it has a strap you can wrap around a chair to help hold it in place. There is a button to reverse the directions of the rotation. Good for back massage or calf massage. It comes with a plug for the car (but I don’t have a car so I can’t speak to how it does).

Cons: It is not very strong, I think the massage balls sit back in too far personally. I don’t feel any heat from it. There is no on/off for heat setting. Not good for arm or neck massage.
The cord is really short, maybe 2-3 feet so you have to be sitting VERY close to the plug for it to work, or use an extension cord. It doesn’t come with any carrying case which would come in handy if you were transporting it to-from car or even within the house and storage.
The heat is also a very dull heat. I let it go for over 10 min and didn’t notice too much heat production.

Overall, I’m sad to say I wouldn’t recommend this product. I think there would be others out there with a bit better feature to make it a nicer product.
My husband has used it and called it just a relaxing massage and he’ll be happy to put it on his office chair.

title: Attractive Design and a Quality Feel
text:
This Wrinkle removal device has a beautiful ergonomic design that is very appealing. I’ve been using it for about three weeks, and dang it, I still have a turkey neck. Thanks, mom. Some things are just genetic. Anyway, I love the gentle heat and vibration the device gives. I don’t know about the other two settings; they don’t seem to do much more than vibrate. When I first used it, I would not vibrate, but then I realized I had failed to remove the white plastic protective cover. The device will not vibrate until the metal sensor on the head touches your skin. The vibrations feel as if they serve a functional purpose.

It is rechargeable and uses a USB-C cord that you will need to plug into one of your 5V phone chargers. A faint red flashing light lets you know it’s charging. I usually charge it after each use, so I don’t know how many ten-minute sessions you get with one charge cycle.

text: The jelly jungle of orange marmalade  that white folks nostalgically recall growing up in Cumberland has been penetrated by the grim reality that blacks faced growing up in what was at one time Maryland's second largest city. Although a Facebook Page Growing Up In Cumberland, Maryland, with over 4,000 members who are predominantly white, has its elder members gush over the movie theatres, restaurants and swimming pools that once adorned this town when it was a thriving city, overlooked are the roadblocks that blacks faced when they would want to attend a movie, or go swimming, or enjoy a soda at a drugstore. Thank goodness Lynn Bowman did some extensive research and the result is this marvelous book, which pulls no punches. History cannot be ignored or smoothed over and events buried like they never existed. Living A Lie brings out things that most people didn't realize happened...and I highly recommend it.

text: Ok, actually, I'm glad such things are available because I really need the support. However, I'm sorely disappointed that the description says "fully adjustable" and the Best Cradle is NOT at all fully adjustable. It would have been easy and inexpensive for the manufacturers to make it so, but they didn't bother. The band that does most of the support; the wide one that fits under the belly, has a hook and eye closure. There are only three sets of eyes, spaced quite far apart. Right now, 2 of them are WAY too loose and do nothing, and one of them is really too tight, and hurts. There should be more options here. There could be more sets of eyes, an adjustable bra-type tightener, additional bands that wrap around the hips at the sides (like the last, simpler belly band I had that my belly outgrew), or better yet, velcro, which can be adjusted to any degree, as needed, and as your belly grows. What a shame that something so expensive fell short in so needless a way. If I hadn't gotten a decent discount, I'd return it. As it is, I guess I have to make some alterations myself. So annoyed.

title: This style works much better for me than the traditional armpit crutches
text:
This style of crutches doesn't rub my armpits, allows me to open doors more easily, and are more manuverable. This particular product works well for me. The adjustments are easy, the directions on where the handles and forearm pieces should be after adjustment are clear, and they seem sturdy. After a week or so of usage, there is a bit of a squeaky noise from the joint that allows the half-circle forearm pieces to rotate up, but that's pretty minor.

There are only two pieces of advice I'd give for someone buying these crutches. If you have arm hair (like me), you might want to wear a long-sleeved shirt or sheathe the forearm pieces in cloth. They are rubberized to reduce slippage, and this is uncomfortable on bare forearms since it ends up pulling hair. Also, if you are worried about having your forearm come out of the opening, holding the handles a bit further away from the crutch and bracing my elbow against the back of the crutch seems to be a bit more stable.

title: Good in theory, but not practical enough to use in the field. TP is still easier.
text:
I purchased this as a lightweight backpacking solution. In theory, it is! But I haven't used it in the field for a number of reasons:
(1) It just seems like an awkward thing to carry because the attachment doesn't fit neatly into the bottle (it rattles around). You should be able to screw the nozzle back into the bottle in reverse so everything's self contained. I'm not sure how to carry the attachment (I don't want it touching my gear and don't want to carry something extra just to protect the glass.
(2) Glass - why? It seems fragile and I don't want to break it in a heavy pack.
(3) It should come with an extra cap for the bottle so you can carry water inside the bottle (then when you need it, the water is ready to go and you don't need to grab your hydration system to fill it). If you're in a rush, I can't imagine this being a quick process.
(4) Carrying the extra water it requires to use is heavier than a roll of TP.
(5) Cleaning the device when backpacking seems like a mess all by itself

I'll give this 2 stars because it's a decent idea, but need to subtract a few stars because it isn't practical enough for real-life use. Not to mention it's way over-priced for what it is. It's still in the package, collecting dust. I can't return it because the product isn't available anymore and the company has no online presence anymore.

title: Very nice trimmers
text:
I have been using 0-gapped trimmers on my own head for about 25 years now, and this trimmer cuts closer and nicer than any I have used in that time. I wasn't expecting much from this device given the design, the price, and the fact that there are so many other trimmers available on Amazon that look almost exactly the same. However, I was really surprised by the closeness of the cut, the quality of the materials, and just how quiet it is.

This trimmer has a nice wide head, which makes trimming a little faster than some of the narrower ones I have used in the past. It also has some heft to it. It is not heavy enough to be uncomfortable, but it definitely lets you know it is a well-made trimmer with a metal body. It only comes with a few combs, but I don't use the combs and they are pretty up-front about that... so I really can't take any stars away for that. The protective pieces and the included brush are nice, though. It took me longer than it should have to figure out where the clear protective piece goes. I probably looked pretty funny. FYI - it goes under the trimming head and protects the spinning mechanism. The included user manual is pretty minimal, so don't expect a lot of detailed info from it. But this is a trimmer... there isn't a lot you need to know.

Aside from the sparse user manual, this is a high-quality trimmer and I can't even believe the price for what you get. Definitely worth it. I would buy another one when needed, for sure, but I don't anticipate this one giving out for a very long time. If you are looking for a 0-gapped trimmer and don't need a lot of combs, stop looking... this is the one.

title: Use a chair if your door is low or you are tall
text:
I pinched a nerve in my shoulder or neck at the end of last ski season, and even though PT helped, there are pain flareups that the PT exercises didn't entirely remedy.

From the photos on the Amazon page, I thought you would pull to provide traction, but the pull only sets the length of the strap and then you can let go. I found that sitting in a chair facing the door gave the best traction as I could lean back slightly to increase traction, or lean forward slightly to release it. I'm 6'1" (185cm) and the doors where I use it are only a few inches more. I could let go of the handle once I got a length I liked. Most of the pull was under the chin with the back of the head strap providing stability. 15 minutes or so and the pain was reduced quite a bit.

I have no problem with the tensioner buckle so far, but if it breaks as in some of the negative reviews, I'll replace it with a 2" O ring or climbing carabineer so as to provide direct traction by pulling down. (The strap would slide through it and not be held by the buckle).

If you have trouble figuring out how to assemble, there is a short video on the Amazon sales page with the photos. My wife suggested that I install an "O" ring screw in my office ceiling so I could provide traction while sitting at the computer. This might be a future option but not yet as I'd probably pull down the ceiling if I didn't get it into a joist.

title: Better than a scale & a measuring tape, not as user friendly as bioimpedence scales. Meant for professionals.
text:
I was initially very excited to get this product after reading about it in 4 Hour Body by Tim Ferriss.

However after using it for about 8 months, I've noticed that it suffers from the same potential flaws as calipers & bioimpedance scales. If you don't use the proper amount of gel, hold it at the same angle as last time, move at the proper speed, at the same exact location, then you might get a wild variance of readings.

In fact the algorithm takes this into account and you have to take a minimum of 3 readings at each site, and then it averages the 3 readings ... if the ranges have too much variance, you will be required to take 2 more readings. I often have to take more than 3 readings.

What this does that no other device will do is actually show you the size and amount of muscle over time on a given body part... although you really need to know how to read the ultrasonic scan to tell.

I think this is meant moreso for professionals who have training in this field. I got this for personal use to get more accurate readings than my Omron or Fitbit Aria ... and while I DO get more accurate readings than those devices, I'm not sure if it's worth the price because I lack the training to effectively use it :\

I must say the support you get with this is TOP NOTCH. The creator is a very smart guy. The software that this runs on is a bit out dated though, and the technology (USB) could be updated.

title: intriguing product
text:
Since few reviews can be found, here are some initial observations. I purchased this based on lots of online research of the bewildering number of products and advice out there. I just finished mixing and spraying 5 one-gallon solutions of Komodo on exterior decking using my 1 gallon pump up sprayer.

The company customer service via email and phone was responsive and helpful. The product arrived very quickly. Application instructions are mostly via scanning a QR code and watching two short videos which were marginally useful. Detailed written instructions with photos would be better, imho. The 5 lb bag is not ziplocked and has no measurement devices, so I weighed out 1 lb using a household scale and banded the remaining bag shut. I am an experienced sprayer and my sprayer was clean prior to use. I mixed the solution thoroughly but still found the spraying to be annoying in that the spray tip periodically clogged up with some sort of debris or substance in the mix. Aside from that, the spray went on well onto my old redwood deck and fir subframing. I felt it was odorless and non-irritating. Once dried it left the expected hint of whitish speckled residue, which I used for a guide for where I have gone. Overspray was not a concern given its lack of toxicity but I rinsed patio walls/concrete off with water anyway. Given the relative ease of use, I will probably buy more.
The biggest question mark with this (and any fire retardant application) is whether or not it "works." I wish there was a good way to test the effectiveness of my application. For me it is almost an act of faith, and it also makes me feel like I did "something" to deal with the wildfire season upon us. Any guidance on home testing is appreciated. I have not yet sprayed any dead vegetation. I will update as needed.

title: Comfortable and effective light blocking
text:
I tend to not sleep well with visual stimulation... including light through closed eyelids. So, I always keep my bedroom very dark.

But there are times this doesn't work. My wife might not be able to sleep and is looking at her cell phone screen. Or I'm on a long flight. Or in a hotel with some item... a thermostat panel, or an LED on a smoke detector, or lights from outside shining past the blinds... which causes issues.

I have been buying the "Good Night sleep mask" from Magellan's for all this time, after trying, and discarding, quite a few others. The Magellan mask is neoprene rubber... think "like a SCUBA suit"... cover with soft cloth bonded to the rubber. What makes them so good is that the rubber is formed, so there is a "domed" cavity over each eye, and even while wearing them, you can have your eyes open, blind, and so on, with no sensation of contact with your eyes or eyelashes.

Their drawback, however, is that the fabric inevitably debonds from the rubber. A set, if well cared for, may last a year of continuous usage.

So, seeing these, I wanted to give them a try.

Generally, I like them. They're very comfortable to wear, block light effectively, and seem likely to last longer than my long-time favorites.

But they don't QUITE clear my eyelashes. Opening or closing my eyes with this on results in a "tickling" of my eyelashes.

If these were a bit more "domed" over the eyes, but identical in every other way, they would be PERFECT.

As it is, they still work quite well, and if you have short eyelashes or deep eye sockets this quibble of mine might not be a concern for you, anyway.

But for me, opening my eyes and still being in pitch blackness without any sensation of contact? That's a huge selling point. The Magellan ones accomplish that. These don't, for me.

So, while I'm keeping these and will use them, I'm not ready to abandon my favorites for them just yet. I'll keep both types around for now.

But a set like these, with the around-eye "pillows" and well-sewn construction, but with those domed eye cavities? That would be a vast improvement over either type. If someone made a set like those, it would be all I'd ever buy again.

title: Feels like an untested, unfinished product
text:
I'm always very tired in the mornings and have trouble waking up. The Sleeptracker is supposed to find an "almost-awake" moment to wake you up, feeling refreshed. I really wakted it to work. It didn't.

The first night I tried it it didn't monitor my sleep at all and it didn't wake me up. The next night I tried it it woke me up but I certainly didn't feel refreshed. The following mornings it woke me up sometimes and sometimes not. The alarm is very quiet, according to the manifacturer because it doesn't need to be louder because it wakes you up when you're almost awake anyway. Problem is, if it doesn't find one of those "almost awake" moments, it rings at the time you set, no matter how deep you sleep. And it only rings once. If you miss it, you better have another alarm clock set or you won't wake up. I overslept twice in the first week I tried the Sleeptracker Pro. It also has a vibrating alarm but it's very weak.

Before going to bed you're supposed to set a "to bed" time. The easiest way to do this is to press the "Down" button when the watch is in "to bed" mode and it automatically sets the "to bed" time at thirty minutes later. This would be very easy if the "down" button had worked. Unfortunately it only works sometimes. I've had to press it up to ten times before it sets the time and it's just as frustrating every time. And getting pissed off about an alarm clock doesn't make it easier to fall asleep.

Another problem is the software that lets you track your sleep history. You connect the Sleeptracker with a USB cable to the computer and upload the data (the watch can only store one night's data for some unexplicable reason so you'll have to do this every day or lose data). Here you can see your almost awake moments and when the alarm went off. You can also click to see your best and worst sleep sessions, but there's no explanation of what makes a sleep session good or bad. I haven't noticed any pattern. Occasionally I get the error message "Sleeptracker not found". I emailed the support and asked about it and they told me there was some weird bug that gives that error message on Sundays and told me to uninstall and download the software from their website. Looks like they haven't been beta testing the software.

And this is the feeling I get for the product as a whole: that it hasn't been tested. It's hard to believe the Sleeptracker Pro is an improved version of the original Sleeptracker, because there are so many little flaws that would easily have been found and fixed if they had done any testing at all before marketing it. As it is, the Sleeptracker Pro feels like an unfinished product. If it was as sophisticated and effective as it claims, it would have been a great product, but it's not. In its current state it's really just a novelty item that might have been fun for a tenth of the price, but there's nothing to justify paying $180 for a product that is impractical to use and doesn't do what it's supposed to do. I really wanted this to work but I returned it to get a refund.

title: throwing rocks
text:
The title, Grass Doesn't Work...the Rocks Do!, is taken from a short anecdote at the beginning of the book. An old man trying to get a boy to stop stealing his apples realizes that talking or throwing grass at him doesn't work, but hitting him with rocks gets his point across. Bradlee Dean takes this analogy and applies it to america and christianity, decrying an overemphasis on God's love without an equal emphasis on God's wrath and hatred of sin. This book is Dean's equivalent of throwing rocks in his attempt to wake people up to the fact that everyone is a sinner deserving of hell, and therefore desperately needs to accept Jesus' payment for sin on the cross.

This book is written at a very popular level, a "street ministry" level, which Dean is involved with (from what I can gather). You won't find any intricate philosophical arguments, or detailed apologetics; his emphasis is conviction of sin.

He covers everything from alcohol, drugs, and promiscuity, to evolution, television, and government corruption. He actually prints out the articles of amendment to the constitution in the back of the book, in his section covering his views of limited government.

I can't say that Dean is a great writer, or that the book flows smoothly. His practice of embedding the definitions of difficult words right in the text (with parentheses) was annoying to me. He basically just hops around from one topic to the next, telling short stories and making analogies to drive home his points. However, he also puts a ton of scripture in his book too, even to the extent of entire chapters at times.

I can see how this book could be really helpful to certain individuals, and how Dean could use this profitably in his ministry. There was nothing I disagreed with in the book, but nothing that stuck out to me as eye-opening or profound, although I did enjoy reading the amount of scripture that he included, which is always profitable.

title: Finally Something I can Believe In!!!
text:
Up to this point in my life, nothing meant very much to me. I believed nothing. I mostly did nothing, too. I could see nothing wrong with this attitude, though.

And Amazon, don't get me started about amazon. I WOULD probably be a big fan of amazon, except that I am always finding SOMETHING to buy. Believe me, I've spent many, many useless hours searching for nothing at all. All I've ever been able to find up to this point, was a whole lot of SOMETHINGS. Not only that, but I have spent hundreds, nay, thousands of dollars on this website purchasing things, things, and more things.

What does it all mean? I wish I knew! It's so hard for me to express the depth of my feelings about nothing; my vocabulary is so limited that I have to use circumlocution to try to say what I mean. I mean nothing is worth all this. And more. Nothing could make me happier. Than Nihilist Mints, that is. Finally something that is basically nothing. Something I can believe in, because it is nothing at all really. No taste, no calories, no color; nothing!

This may seem ironic, but, that's OK, because irony is the basis of everything. Everything that I have experienced so far, that is. And apparently, it is the basis of nothing, too. This really pleases me. There is nothing that I feel stronger about. Well, except maybe apathy. Thank-you, amazon, for offering Nihilist Mints, a (no)thing I can really believe in!

As far as inserting this vibrator, it is rather small – maybe the diameter of a quarter at the largest point. It’s also pretty short as seen in my pictures. This one will definitely be making repeat appearances in our bedroom.

Bottom line: smooth, sleek, powerful… rechargeable! This is a nice vibrator and is replacing some of our older ones. The wife LOVES it!

title: Provisionally positive results from this skeptic
text:
I'm an open minded skeptic about supplements. I'll try just about anything. Few of them do anything. This one seems to work. It's the first supplement related to ecdysterone or turkesterone I've tried that really does seem to offer some benefits. I didn't get that benefit from the bulk packages of powdered turkesterone from another reputable vendor -- three months of using that seemed to have little or no benefit.

Most positive reviews about supplements appear to be misguided (see the revised recommendations to avoid excessive antioxidants) or placebo effect (hey, nothing wrong with the power of positive thinking -- but why pay extra for it in a gel capsule?). That includes most antioxidants, remedies for bone health, joints and cartilage, and most supplements marketed to athletes and physically active people for energy and better performance. Tried 'em. Most seem to do nothing.

The few exceptions include creatine (well documented and non-controversial), niacin (blood flow), and l-arginine (the latter helps the body produce nitric oxide on the fly as needed, especially in daylight).

I've been an on/off serious amateur athlete since my teens, now in my early 60s, including amateur boxing, long bike rides and occasional races when I was in my teens and early 20s. Like most healthy folks, in my youth all I needed was a healthy diet, good training program and rest. As I got older, well... not so much.

After my thyroid failed a couple of years ago my energy dropped to nil. I went from vigorous bike rides several times a week to barely being able to get out of bed. My endocrinologist and other doctors didn't seem concerned. As far as they were concerned my lab tests looked normal. So other than levothyroxine, the common thyroid replacement, they didn't offer any solutions or suggestions. And, nope, my health care plan doesn't include fountain of youth prescriptions (PEDs, if you're competing in sanctioned events, which I'm not doing). They even cut back on testosterone patches for anyone without a medically indicated need such as double orchiectomy. They used to prescribe those for active men who just felt more tired with age. But not any more.

So for the past year I've tried everything I can find over the counter, including DHEA and pregnenolone. After trying several brands I found one brand of DHEA that seemed to offer some benefit, but I couldn't be sure it wasn't placebo effect. It seemed like my endurance was improving. My short term energy bursts -- sprints and short steep hill climbs -- were already improving from creatine, and maybe from l-arginine. But not my endurance. I still faded after 20 miles on fast solo and group rides.

But the effect of the S5 beta-ecdysterone was almost immediately noticeable. Within a few days I noticed a distinct improvement in my bicycling endurance. My interval training sessions were more vigorous and I had enough energy afterward for full body workouts. And my endurance on longer sustained effort rides improved significantly. I'm pushing bigger gears, including on climbs, without my quads and calves burning. Friends who follow me on Strava commented on my recent speed boost, consistently 1-2 mph faster on the usual 20-40 mile training routes. A few months ago I couldn't even finish those rides. Now on good days I'm able to keep up with the A-group rides with guys much younger than I, whereas a couple of years ago when my thyroid failed I struggled to keep up with the B-group, and even with some stronger casual riders on social rides.

I'm not looking to get bigger, just stronger. Unlike creatine, which is good for short duration high intensity exercise, this stuff seems to help with sustained effort.

I'm still skeptical. S5 hasn't published any lab results and I don't see any independent lab tests. It's pretty well documented that many supplements marketed to athletes surreptitiously contain stimulants like caffeine and ephedra to give an energy boost that makes it feel like it's doing something. And some even sneak in other banned substances. So I don't know for certain how or why the S5 Labs beta-ecdysterone is working.

But I just ordered another bottle, something I rarely do if I have doubts about whether a supplement works.

title: It's Cheap and Adequate Given the Price
text:
This product is NOT precise, and I would not call it "professional" grade, but it is probably as good or as bad as all the other cheap pill cutters. However, it can be adequate if you modify your cutting technique.

The results I got on the first few pills I cut were abysmal. I thought that the blade was either mounted off center or was flexing. However, on investigation, I found the blade was mounted true and was very ridged. The problem is that the plastic is slick, and the pills slide around when cutting, resulting in off-center cuts. The design could be improved to overcome this but changing your cutting technique can overcome this design flaw. (Almost all the hinged pill cutters use this same design!)

To improve cutting accuracy, do the following:
1. Carefully place the pill in the V-shaped slot.
2. Tilt the device slightly so that gravity pushes the pill into the V-slot. This will help prevent the pill from sliding out from under the blade and improves the accuracy of the cut.
3. Now, push firmly, but slowly down on the lever to cut the pill.

You will NOT get accurate cuts every time and for the tiny chalky pills I'm cutting a little debris will result, but it mostly cuts arcuately. I can be more accurate with a single blade safety razor with pills that have a score line. However, for the tiny, unscored pills I am cutting, this pill cutter works adequately given the price.

It doesn't make you smell like anything - don't worry. You have to add things to this oil or use perfume after to have a smell. I swear by this stuff and use it every night. I put a few drops on my ends and a few in my hands and distribute evenly. Then use a water based leave in conditioner (Mystic Divine from Sally's) or it makes me look like I stuck my head in cooking oil. Minimal drying time and I get dressed right after with no issues of staining clothing. The pump is great right by the shower for quick application and delivery into smaller containers for other uses/mixtures. title: Great as a straightedge, but Sharp Edges.
text:
4.5 Stars. Well made. Thin enough to use as a bookmark and very slightly flexible but feels sturdy. I use it to draw straight lines and underline text in my textbooks (the book's pages are slightly curved, so a little flexibility is good). The edge is perfectly straight.

Only issue is that the edges are sharp. This actually helps you draw straight lines as, if you angle the ruler against the page it's sharp enough to grip the paper and hold still while you drag a pencil/pen over it. Also doesn't leave any gap between the ruler and the page, which is good if you wanted to use it with a marker I guess. But it is seriously sharp, as in, airport security would confiscate this sharp. I actually coated one side with a strip of black electrical tape so I can grip the thing without fear that it's going to cut me (which I think it would if you gripped it hard enough). Again, I don't really consider this a con because it serves my purposes, but I wouldn't get this for kids or if you plan to handle it a lot and need to use it as a ruler and see both sides (because my electrical tape trick covers one side). If you just need a really good straight edge, this is pretty great for that.

title: Amazing for sensitive skin!
text:
I have tried numerous natural deodorants over the years. Crystals, homemade recipes, name brands, off brands, boutique brands, Shark Tank brands... Every single deodorant has triggered some sort of reaction after prolonged use. Whether it's terrible rashes or painfully swollen lymph nodes, my body just doesn't seem to appreciate natural deodorants. On top of that, few actually keep the odor away all day.

Enter Ethique Natural Deodorant. I am on month three of using Ethique and NO skin reactions! 100% normal lymph nodes! No stinky pits! It's miraculous!!

As with the majority of truly natural deodorants, application takes a moment longer than traditional antiperspirants. In cold weather, the bar must be warmed a bit to soften it for ease of application. This might be by simply keeping it close to a steamy shower or holding it against your skin for a few moments. Easy enough to do. It goes on creamy and smooth, much easier than a lot of brands I've tried. If you use too much, just rub the excess into the skin with bare fingers and it disappears.

Typically doesn't show on clothing but I have had some incidents where I applied too much and it rubbed off on my clothes (a little goes a long way). Unlike the antiperspirants I used years ago, Ethique washes out easily. No pit stains.

Can't say enough good things about Ethique Natural Deodorant. It's simply the best out of dozens of brands I've tried.

I'm not very tech-y, so that could have been just user error.  However, I did google it and found a video that suggested using your cell phone to set it up (basically takes you through temporarily changing networks from your own to a "fitbit" one during setup).  Was really easy to do and worked great.  That's the only little stumble I've had.  Features/Use: The Aria is easy to use.  My husband and I are both set up on it. It automatically logs the weight and body fat to the correct Fitbit account.  If by chance it gets confused, you can reassign or delete readings from your Fitbit online account.  My husband doesn't use any other Fitbit device, but he was so intrigued by the scale that he setup a Fitbit account and weighs himself on the Aria.  Fitbit has a great standalone website, and the integration of their devices such as Ultra and Aria make the experience FUN.  I have lost 40 lbs since purchasing the Ultra in June.  Fitbit is not the sole reason for my weightloss (diet and exercise!) but it has helped me be more focused and motivated.  The Aria is a great extension of the Fitbit program and continues to make it easier and fun.  For anyone trying to keep motivation in their health journey, or those who are already serious about it, I recommend the entire Fitbit system, including the Aria.  I do not regret the $$ I spent on the Ultra or Aria.  Love them!

title: Handy weekly pill container set
text:
I liked this enough to buy another, 6 months after I bought the first one. (Apologies if a partial review got posted before this one, my computer crashed while I was writing it.) The individual day slots are big enough to hold a lot of pills, or a couple of big ones (I'm looking at *you*, fish oil). If you're going away for the weekend, you can take out just a few days and toss them in your bag.

A couple of things could be better:
1. Would be nice to have the name of the day printed on the other side of the box. I could memorize which color goes with which day, but somehow I haven't gotten around to that yet.
2. The ink has worn away on a couple of them. I don't know if it's because I got oil on the cases, or what. I've included a couple pictures.
3. The surface of the plastic on the individual day containers is very slick & slippery. When carrying one or a couple of the day boxes on top of a stack of papers or a box or some other thing I'm moving from one place to another, more times than I'd like the pill case just slides right off and lands on the floor. Usually no pills spilled, but it's annoying. Maybe I should take some sandpaper to the boxes. But less slippery would be good.

I note that this item is "currently unavailable". Because of how useful they are for someone who takes a lot of pills (or some big ones), I hope it returns, with or without improvements.

title: This little blood pressure cuff is great!! I've been concerned about my blood pressure ...
text: This little blood pressure cuff is great!!  I've been concerned about my blood pressure lately while being in grad school and under so much stress.  This has given me a very convenient way of monitoring it for my own piece of mind.  A lot of the blood pressure cuffs I've used in the past pump up super tight to the point where your arm feels like it's going to fall off, but this one isn't bad at all.  It has a memory for 2 different users so you don't have to worry about which pressure was yours, you simply change user 1 or user 2 when you turn the unit on so that it logs it for you.  It's definitely a neat little feature to check trends in your pressure.  It also has a display area for the heart rate and time.  The colors are very attractive and easy on the eye.  It has a back lit screen which makes it easy to read in the dark.  It also color codes your blood pressure and will notify you if your heart rhythm was abnormal which is nice.  This is a very helpful feature for people who may go in and out of afib and want to know if they converted or not.  It won't tell you the rhythm, just whether or not it's abnormal.  Then on the left hand side it will give you green which is good, yellow which means it's a little high, and red which is high.  So it gives people with no medical background a sense of what is okay and where they should be with their pressures.  I've been in the medical field for years, but I still enjoy this little cuff.  It helps to keep me on track and working on lowering my pressure.  I did receive this at a discount in exchange for my honest review.  I do highly recommend it for anyone who is curious about their pressure at home.  It's a great price for such a convenient product to give you a piece of mind.

Is this working? I have no clue. Prior to this, I always bought Source of Life's vitamins -- always felt noticeably more energetic with those. title: It works. There isn't a better alternative than the Sleep Nora
text:
Purchased Smart Nora after seeing several IG ads.

It was $300, came with a 30-day guarantee, so it felt relatively low risk.

Background, I snore, and have mild sleep apnea. I tried a few devices, first a mouth guard, then a chin strap, and neither worked. The mouth guard helped but left me with a sore jaw, and the chin strap just made me look like a tool.

I immediately noticed a difference after the first night. I've run a few experiments, using it, and not using it. It's pretty conclusive, when I do not use the Smart Nora, my wife will wake me up from snoring.

The Smart Nora doesn't stop you from snoring, and instead gently adjusts your head to re-engage your soft palette muscles. It has an ambient noise sensor, and triggers when the noise reaches a certain threshold. The adjustments work by inflating a small baffle which changes the shape of your pillow, then slowly deflating it returning your head back to the previous position.

As a user you can configure both the noise sensitivity threshold, and set three levels for adjustment. There is also a delay timer which will start the Smart Nora after 30 minutes.

Over all the product feels well made, and comes self contained in a traveling case.

It was easy to setup and get started using, and the supplied cables are all plenty long.

For downsides, there are a couple:

The baffle has a tendency to get shifted on the pillow. I've tried with both the cloth cover, and without, and it will often shift towards the back. If there was a way to secure it to the pillow, it would be perfect.

Second, as noted, there are a few cables: power cable, the air hose which attaches to the baffle, and a USB charging cable. It can add unnecessary clutter next to your bed.

Overall, if you are looking for alleviate snoring, either for yourself, or any adult who shares your bed, this product works wonders.

Finally, it should be noted that this is not a cure nor is it treatment for sleep apnea. You should seek out your doctor for options on how to best deal with Sleep Apnea.

For snoring, I don't know if there is a better alternative than the Sleep Nora

title: Sticker Alert ... and a little Warped
text:
Nice box ... nice size (fits well on a shelf). I would have given this a five star review, but for two things.

1. This had a good size sticker on the front of the box. It is not the worst I've ever had to deal with, but when I have to stop what I'm doing, sit down and work a damn sticker off that serves no function then I start to get irritated. Some stickers come off easily once you get a corner up ... and the companies that use this type of sticker have my gratitude and business. This sticker makes you think it is going to easily come off but it only looks that way. You do have to work at it to get it off and then you're left wish some small scratches and sticky smudges to deal with.

I just happen to be a person who takes care of my possessions. If you take care of things they can last a life time ... but I don't want to look a product that has been marred by sticker removal for a lifetime.

2. A smaller issue is the tray inside the box is warped. Not so bad it can't be used ... however I'll probably recycle the tray and just use the box without it. Or, maybe I'll just donate the thing and start over.

If I could, I would return it. However, I'm dealing with a recent death and a bad fall that has me black and blue and cut up. So I'm not in my usual good humor. However, I've very grateful ... because it could have been much worse. And, my neighbor is lucky that I'm not the suing type.

So, if you hate damn stickers and having to invest valuable time into removing them then definitely move on!

title: A real perk for those like me that try to avoid harsh chemicals is that ...
text:
Magic erasers are my salvation and saving grace. I had scuffs and stains all over my apartment where I've lived for ten years that I thought were things i'd have to live with till I moved out. Now, my white countertops gleam again, wall stains where my pets have repeatedly love-rubbed against the wall are a thing of the past, light switches and door jams don't have that slightly tan or grey haze....a real facelift for anything looking dingy or old due to regular-use staining. I had a haze in my stainless steel sink from pouring out leftover coffee day after day that cream scrub and/or bleach solution didn't quite touch. Magic eraser finished the job with flying colors!

A real perk for those like me that try to avoid harsh chemicals is that Magic Erasers are very effective without any heavy/offensive odor or chemicals. It's all about the texture! They are abrasive, so you'll want to consider wearing kitchen gloves to save your hands if you'll be using them extensively.

I buy the extra power kind since the only drawback to Magic Erasers is that they tend to wear down fast....especially if you go on a cleaning spree.

title: No Wire Nose Bridge, Fogged Glasses, Filters Do Not Fit
text:
Based on the tremendous number of positive reviews that I do not understand we purchased this mask. Let me go through the con's first because if any of these issues are a problem for you like they were for me, the pro's won't offset the cons.

Cons:
1) No wire bridge to make the mask form-fitting around the nose. These are essential and part of any high-end mask, especially for glass wearers. Without the wire bridge, your glasses will fog up.
2) Filter far too small for this type of mask had to use two filters vertically instead of horizontally to ensure appropriate coverage.
3) After 30 minutes the fabric becomes wet from your exhaling. Because you have to wear the mask so tightly to avoid fogging glasses, the inside becomes damp from your breathing.
4) Customer service - awful; when asked why no wire bridge was provided, they sent me to a link to make another purchase on Amazon. Absurd; why would I pay more for an enhancement to a mask I already overpaid for at this price point. Outrageous and sellers of masks should be ashamed for selling these as such a high price point for an inferior mask.

Pros:
The only pro is that this is one of the only masks on the market with the adjustable ear straps built into the mask that allows you to adjust very well, and it serves as a holder around your neck when you need to take your mask off. Seems anyone with a quality mask could add this feature and hope they do.

We do not recommend purchasing this item and can not understand why there are so many 5 star reviews, which is another red flag.

title: Has the sustained power, heat and strength to provide awesome relief to body pain and touch hunger.....a wonderful item.
text:
OK....I've had mine for several years. I paid $2000 for it used and don't regret a penny. I bought it with my inheritance and its
the only thing I bought from that money that I will probably have the rest of my life. If you have TOUCH HUNGER (a spouse
that isn't very affectionate), or live alone, or need more massage or caring, this can be the lifesaver of your life. Set one of the many modes of the massage patterns, lie back with some nice music and candle light (safely set up of course), and let it "fill your cup."
There was a study done in the 60's by scientists at Stanford I believe with newborn monkeys. They took them away from their mothers and gave them two choices.... a bottle wired in the proper position to nurse, and a piece of terrycloth rag, about the size of a mother monkey. The babies one and all, clung to the terry cloth rag, and only briefly left it to suckle, again and again returning to any semblance of mother's warmth and touch. It was earthshaking in the scientific world...and if you've not heard of it before, its time to hear of it now. Let this be your deal maker....if you've got the dough, get this thing.
I have it set up in my bedroom and relax before bed. It gets ride of the kinks in my lower back, neck, up and down my spine, along my legs and thighs, buttocks, the works.
There are numerous jade balls inside and it has heat. It also has FAR INFARED ....look that up for its amazing healing qualities.
The only thing I do that doesn't come standard with the bed is add padding. You can buy a thick foam pad, like those things you put on the top of a mattress....but I've found a yoga mat that has many gussets which works perfectly. Then I cover that with a comfortable quilt. Sometimes I use it with an eye mask, others not. Sometimes I cover with a blanket, others not.
When friends have back aches, I offer them a "ride on my bed." They always come out smiling!
Obviously if you have a serious back condition it may not help that much or even cause harm. I am not guaranteeing it would
work for all people, all the time. If you are really curious, check on line for a dealer or store that sells these things (its on the internet), and give it a try in the shop.
The top and bottom mattress pieces with Jade balls, come apart. The frame sets up easily. I have moved mine in the
back of an SUV without difficulty. There are a couple of wires to hook up, but its not complicated. Schematics are available on the internet, if you don't have your booklet. These come from Korea and its the best export I think they've every made. (I'm not into Kimchee!).
When I get on it, my pets sit on me too. Everyone seems to love the up and down wave motion of this amazing Migun bed.
I know that I come off my session, calm, relaxed, and out of pain. Its a true life saver In this busy world of stress and pressure.
I don't know any time I've spent $2000 and been happier with it, over time, year after year. I've had mine 5 years so far.
If I had a holistic shop, I would also consider offering "rides" on the bed for a fee. That's how I first got acquainted....was in
a Migun bed shop....and I drove about 25 miles a day each way just to use it during a period of severe back pain until I got my own.
Feel free to ask questions if this is not a thorough enough review. I will happily answer them for you. It has a strong vinyl
cover which doesn't tear or pull. This is a quality made piece of health equipment....medical quality in my view. Nothing tacky
or flimsy on this unit.
There are numerous patterns you can choose (they are numbered). You just put the code into the little piece sticking up by the side of the bed, and put in the pattern you prefer, given whats going on with your body. I've never found one I didn't like.
The patterns are intermittent, move slowly enough to really center into a pain spot, the jade balls are rolling beneath your back, you are sometimes lifted, sometimes eased down.....a genius of workmanship. Its not like a massage chair with just a bit
of tingles. This is a REAL massage....quite equivalent, even superior to a good professional masseur. As I have had some training
in massage....I know that what this bed offers that a live therapist can't is CONTINUED strength and pressure, sustained over time.
None of us are that strong to continue on for 30 minutes or more in the pressure level and exactitude this provides. They are in different leagues. I still go to live massage therapists from time to time, but when I don't have the time or the money, this is an excellent provider of body health and comfort.

title: Big and lightweight. Would give it 5 stars if it had a nose wire and toggles on the neck strap.
text: I live in Japan, and I'm a big guy with a full beard. It has been a real struggle to find masks of any kind that fit me. even ones labelled as XL are laughably small.  I bought the XL version of this mask as a trial, and after wearing it for a couple of days, I immediately ordered 10 more., so I don't have to wash a single mask every night.  It is big enough to cover the entire lower half of my face, and rests comfortably under my jawline, containing my manly beard with ease haha. It is wide enough to reach my ears, and thanks to how the neck strap is designed, it makes the mask adjustable, so it can be tightened or loosened as needed. It is very soft  and double layered, with the inner layer acting as a filter pocket for extra protection if you want. But it doesn't feel heavy or restrictive to me. I only have two minor "complaints" First, as a glasses wearer, a nose wire would have been great to help keep my specs from fogging up occasionally. Though obviously that's not a problem for those with 20/20 vision. And second, a couple of small toggles (like those found on drawstring bags) to help keep the neck strap from loosening over time, would be great. Not a problem for general daily use, but I'm pretty active in my job, and had to tighten up the neck strap from time to time, to keep it as snug as I like. title: Will stick with empty soda bottle
text:
I grew up sleeping with hot water bottle, so when we made decision not to turn the heat on at winter time here in Arizona, i figured this would be a good alternative to warm up those cold sheets before bed.

The good point of this hot water bottle was it's price and what you get for the money. Growing up in Europe, we never had covers for them, so i thought these covers are a nice touch, and they were the reason why i decided to purchase this model over some others.

Sadly, as cute these covers are, once put on, they diminish the heat factor to the point of uselessness. They simply don't work.

In Europe we used to boil water on the stove, pour it in, and put the bottle in bed, so they would heat through the night. This hot water bottle instructions suggest hot tap water, but due to thickness of the rubber, this just doesn't warm up nowhere enough to do any good. And if on top, you slip one of the covers on, you will get no use from it.

So i used it for couple of nights without covers, with hot tap water. After going to bed and getting greeted by cold sheets, i went back to our traditional, proven method: an empty soda bottle.

Soda bottle, filled with hot tap water, heats up tremendously, and holds heat quite long, so we just continued doing that. not to mention that this method is completely free.I am not sure what my daughter ended up doing with this hot water bottle, but i haven't seen it in months.

The smell didn't bother me, these are prone to strong rubber smells, and i am quite used it.

title: This is the trauma shears you are looking for!
text:
(A) This is an update to (B), which has been issued prior. During my last visit to the wound doctor I took these scissors with me and asked him to cut my Unna boot off with my scissors. He was tremendously impressed, just as I knew he would be. While using mine he switched to the scissors they use and it was a struggle using them because the blades separated just enough to make cutting tedious. His comments were excellent and asked I if would send the information to him because he was going to purchase 4 of these scissors for his practice. Knowing him as well as I do I had a printout of this shears from Amazon and gave it to him. He said he will be ordering at least 4 pair. (I reminded him that they are with PRIME).

(B) During my wife's home care we told the nurse we needed some good shears. I had a pair but while cutting thick wrappings from my wife' legs daily the cutting part would separate and not cut. At our request nurse purchased shears for us which we paid for. I used them one or two times and they too separated. Since my wife's passing April 2012 I am currently wearing an Unna boot which I change by myself weekly between doctor office visits. I saw the Princess Care here at Amazon and was awed by so many good reviews by nurses, trauma and emergency room personnel. I purchased a pair and have been used them several times. (I must add at this point that the shears the home nurse used did not cut anywhere near and effortlessly as the Princess Care.) This week I was at the doctor and he was cutting the Unna boot from my foot and leg. I told him about these shears. His advise was to buy the more expensive shears because the lesser costing shears just are not worth the aggravation they yield. Watching him cutting I told him how easily my new shears cut. He did point out that cutting the wrapping from the bottom to the top is much easier because you are cutting with the wrapping - not against it like I must. When he said that I instantly liked my Princess Care shears even more because cutting against the wrapping is now very easy, no blade separation and defiantly no aggravation. I want to thank the medical personnel who took the time to issue their reviews because they helped me choose shears that allow me to remove my Unna boots effortlessly and without struggling while cutting in a very awkward position.

Therefore, I can honestly say that the 5-star reviews are accurate.

title: Powerful Rechargeable Sound Machine
text:
[[VIDEOID:49c45055eab93cc80353b85a006cff4a]] So, I purchased this Sound Machine because I have permanent Tinnitus (ear ringing) from a TBI and need background noise at night to help drown out the high-pitch ringing in my right ear. I currently have an Echo Show 5 on my nightstand, however, if there is a power/internet outage, then I will not have a backup. Which is why I purchased this as it isn't reliant on the internet and is rechargeable with a 7-hour battery and timer options (pro). Below, are some pros and cons for this device.

Pros
-Rechargeable 7-hour battery with 2.5 hour full charge time
-Not reliant on the internet
-3 different timer options
-Light with 7 different color options and 3 different modes (always on, breathing light (I like this as I suffer from Anxiety), and off.
-Adjustable volume gets pretty loud.
-Headset jack.
-29 sound options (15 Nature sounds and music box; 7 White Noise; 7 Fan sounds); each category have their own button with a sound notification when you reach the end of the list.
-Actually includes a wall adapter along with the USB cable.

Cons
-Not Voice-activated like my Echo devices; I have to manually power on and activate/change the options.
-Of the 29 sound options, I will only use the Nature Sounds category minus the music box sounds (creepy). The White Noise sounds, to me at least, are a bit distracting/annoying and the Fan sounds are more like a generator than a fan.
-Although not really a con for me, but it is a bit bigger than the Echo Dot devices.
-It states that it comes with a "Travel Pouch", but there were not any included in the box, unless they consider the paper-thin, styrofoam packing material to be a travel pouch.

I have included pictures and a video of the device for sound and light reference.

title: Fabulous for so many reasons and uses.
text:
I bought these as I was tired of always having to buy (and throw away) cotton rounds. They have the softness and texture of a high quality baby towel. Very soft.
Initially, the rather large tag is annoying, but as you wash them, they become more flexible and less “invasive” when you’re using them. We also use the tags to hook them for use when they’re clean.
I do not recommend putting all of them in the bag to clean and dry at the same time. They don’t have enough room in the bag to get properly cleaned or dried. What we do instead is hang the clean ones on a hook and as we use them, put them in the bag that is hanging on a hook next to it. When the bag is about half full, then I tie off the bag like starting to tie my shoes, but not finishing. It’s stays shut. Then I chuck it in the wash and forget it until it comes out of the dryer. Hang the clean ones and hang the bag for the used ones, lather, rinse, repeat.
I use mine with the Micellar water for makeup but use the oil free eye makeup remover (Up and Up).
I had read a review where someone said it removes waterproof makeup with just water. Maybe face makeup, but no way with eye makeup.
Only thing I absolutely would not recommend using these for (unless you buy some completely separate and for this purpose - which I will be) is for nail polish remover. The risk of that not washing out all the way and getting into eyes is too great for my liking.
Also, using fabric softener will affect absorbency.
Will buy again and recommend.

title: I was super skeptical!
text: I'll start by saying his gets five stars, even though it's not a perfect product, because of the results it delivered. I'm almost embarrassed to admit I bought this back in November because I had a crush on this amazing guy. We had been going out on and off for months but he hadn't as much as tried to hold my hand. I put on a somewhat heavy coat of this before going out on a date (mini golf and then decorating for Christmas with him, which if you know me is basically my perfect date). I tend to like more floral or citrus-y smells and I'll admit I don't much like the smell of this product, it's very sweet and candy-like. As well the consistency is about as viscous as olive oil, maybe a little less thick. While I haven't put it to the test I imagine it could stain clothing. However, back at his apartment in the light of the newly-hung Christmas lights, he finally admitted that he had a crush on me too and we may have gone at it three times. This was TEN MONTHS after our first date. I put the perfume on a book case and forgot it existed until I was deep cleaning the other day. As the same guy was coming over that night, I thought I'd put it to the test again and see if he behaved any differently. He commented on the scent, describing it as vanilla mixed with air freshener. Again, not a scent I would review with five stars if it hadn't been for the absolutely mind blowing sex that followed shortly after. As we've been dating for 8 months we've had plenty of sex and, while always satisfying, it can be somewhat routine when you're both tired from work. But holy crap, wearing this seemed to spark something and, without going into too much detail, it was a very, very good night. So, to sum it up, it's a bit too thick and sweet smelling for my taste and I will be buying this to trick my boyfriend into loving me for the rest of my life.

Plus, the puma (hole) where you sip from is so so so small
Only about 1/2", and square shape.
The best puka are a bit bigger, and NOT square shaped, more wider at lip than inside (see photos).
Plus, the nose thing
I don't like to have my nose tickled, or in this case, punched, when I try to drink my morning liquid caffeinated petrol.
If I had a small nose, it would be fine. Or maybe if I was a boxer in my former life…
How bad is the nose hit issue?
Well, our favorite mugs (Starbuck ones) and this one have about a 30 degree difference in the angle you can lift the mug up to drink before the lid hits your nose.
That's a lot!
Plus, with the small puka for the drinking of coffee from, it makes it worse!
Designers, WAKE UP!!!!
I love the look of the mug!
Best one we have seen.
Coffee did not heat up outside like my old favorite mugs.
Didn't leak when I turned it upside down
This is a must for us. All our mugs have to pass this test.
It must not leak if turn upside down.

Plus, the small opening made it hard to pour the coffee into it.
I use a french press, and a gold filter to do a more fine strain to coffee when I pour it into the mug
With the 2" opening, I could NOT put the filter/screen in to pour coffee.
I had to pour into another glass/cup and then pour into this one.

I returned it.
I wanted to like it
Design is flawed, a really bad design for us "big nose" people.

Check out the photos, to see the differences between the silver Bubba, and our old faithful Starbucks blue one.

Gregg Hutchings
Editor/Publisher
Model Cars Magazine
Slot Cars Magazine

title: Works OK... Great idea but
text: Most golf shoes are OK but not as comfortable  in warm weather or as breathable as a good running shoe . So i tried this product on a barely worn but good as new pair of Asics Kayano 25. It takes some force force to screw them in. If you have one of those ratchet type screw driver it works better than what is included. The first time I played in them I lost 2 cleats. So I screwed in 2 more and next time I played I lost 4, two on each shoe. I lost the 2 on each shoe at the toe (front) of the shoe. I put a lot of pressure on the front of my shoe when I hit the ball so that seemed logical. But I don't want to keep losing cleats. Next time I screwed them back in but first added some gorilla glue to help hold them. I haven't played in them yet to see the results but I think it should work (for a while)  . In summary I like the concept . it's a great idea. I like playing in my light , cushioned running shoe. Second even with the glue I know I'm going to be changing a lot of cleats. What I would like to see is a box of just replacement cleats at about $15.  I don't need a screwdriver I don't use so cut the cost deleting that. The first time  I saw this product was on shark tank and they were selling them for $28. I purchased from amazon for about $35. I think they are overpriced and should sell for about $18 or $20. Like i said, the concept is genius , they don't work as well as advertised and they are overpriced. BUT I like playing in my overpriced good quality running shoe.
