title: Works ok
text: This hair dryer works ok. I wouldn't suggest using it on freshly washed hair that is still fully damp. I suggest very lightly misting your hair and then using this dryer. I had heavily misted my hair with water and then used this dryer but it still didn't really style or give my hair the volume I needed. It's possible that maybe it was cause the air was humid. Also I didn't want to leave the heating element close to my hair for too long and cause damage. It did for the most part smooth out the cowlicks in my hair but just minus the volume. Aside from that, the dryer was very easy to use. I was able to brush it through my hair very easily without pulling or tangling (I have straight hair). Its also quite light so my hand and arm didn't get fatigued using it. Overall a decent unit but don't expect dramatic styling/volume capabilities.

title: Easy to use and hair doesn't stick
text: Heats up fast and there's a temperature window that counts up as it heats up. You just press and hold to power on/off the unit. You also know the unit is on when the center of the brush turns red. Two additional buttons on the handle to increase or decrease the temperature. The instructions do indicate the best temperature per hair type and recommend using a heat protectant spray on your hair. So basically same care instructions as a flat iron but this is so much easier to use and doesn't leave your hair fully flat with and with an indent near the scalp of your hair like a flat iron does. Since this is shaped like a brush, I was able to get slightly more body into my hair rather than completely flat which is what happened with a flat iron. Also the bristles are not meant to comb your hair with but they are meant to hold your hair in place like a brush as you run the unit through your hair. You're supposed to brush out and detangle your hair first before using this straightener so don't use it like a hair brush.  I really love this design so much better though. It also came with a heat protectant glove for the other hand that is holding your hair in place as you're running the unit through your hair sections but I found I didn't need it. Also unlike a flat iron, I wasn't pinching or pulling my hair on this nor was I applying any heated weight to it, all good things in my opinion. My only suggestion is that the buttons should be placed elsewhere because having them on the handle, I ended up changing the temperature by accident while maneuvering the device. But that's not enough of an issue for me to be deterred from recommending this device. It's very nice! I'll be using this in the mornings now when I decide to wear my hair down. I have crazy cowlicks on the back of my head and I was able to smooth that out quickly with this device today. Also I wanted to mention this is really easy to store and isn't a huge device either. Since it's like like your traditional flat iron, it doesn't flop open like pair of tongs so storage isn't awkward and would be easy to travel with. Mine also came with a storage pouch as well.

title: Great alternative to plastics
text:
Our son (almost 3YO) is demolishing plastic toothbrushes at a frightening rate and we thought bamboo would either slow him down or be a more affordable and environmentally friendly alternative.

However, I'm testing them out first to make sure they're ok (will update review later if our little one has any issues with them).

My experience has been mostly positive: soft bristles are good if you're heavy handed (like me). Bristles are long and feel like they're getting in between teeth and along gum line. It forces me to slow down and pay attention to how I'm brushing my teeth, so I feel like I'm being more thorough.

Negatives are that, coming from a small headed Oral-B electric, I feel like the physically larger head prevents me getting good access to my back teeth. Also, the bamboo material sometimes looks dried out and I see possible micro splinters along the handle. So far, none have pierced my hand or mouth and the larger ones I just pull off.

I kinda feel like, as with a bamboo cutting board, maintaining the handle and head with a food safe oil might extend the product life..

Overall though, happy with these brushes and our little one should be trying them out after he finishes mauling his current plastic toothbrush to death. Will update review with his perspective and any issues.

As for loins mane itself, its no cure for any issues but i found it very helpful. It takes a week or 3 to notice anything. Maybe even a month for some people. For me i had clinical depression and it effected my brain function and my memory. This helped to improve my short term memory a little and it helped me with having a little more clarity of thought. I picked an alarm that goes around his arm because I thought having the alarm/vibrator close to his ear as possible would be better.  This device worked as fast as the second night. We called about this and we were told this was normal & to just keep the switch up until pushed down on his underwear.  It continues to work great!!  My son is now on week 2 of staying dry throughout night.  Keeping it on for at least a month to be sure we are done with bed-wetting!! title: Two nights in, and it is working so far...
text: I'm only two days into this, so if it ends up doing the trick, I will be back to update the review. If you are as desperate as we are to help your child with bedwetting, I would love to help advise. My daughter was diagnosed with an over-active bladder when she was about four years old. Potty training had been no problem, but then she began getting UTIs and had constant urgency. We took her to the Urodynamic Lab at Morgan Stanley Children's Hospital for months, where they monitored her using ultrasound - and it cost an arm and a leg and didn't seem to be going anywhere. She was on the same medication that older women with incontinence take - it was not making a difference. So, we've lived with it, keeping her in pullups overnight, and just trying to make her use the bathroom consistently during the day. She is a very happy, confident kid - she is 10 now, about to go to Middle School, and I feel that we have not done everything we can do to help her to control her bladder. So - two nights in, and she is getting up and using the bathroom when the alarm goes off. She does pee a bit, but I'm assuming this is going to improve as we continue to use the alarm, and perhaps the deep sleep she enjoys at night will become light enough so that she can get up instead of just letting the pee fly. I hate to ruin a great sleeper. I just don't know what else to do. So - the sensor is a little hard to turn off once it starts beeping, but we're managing and I'm sure she'll get better at it. She's being a great sport. I am hopeful.

title: Good basic Foot Spa
text:
I picked mine up at Bed, Bath & Beyond for the same shelf price. Mine was cheaper with the BBB coupon. I filled mine up with partly warm water and it maintained the heat for 30 minutes. I was under no illusions about the bubbles, vibration or massagers being worth anything. The bubbles and the vibration are both loud even though I have the unit on carpet. I keep expecting DH to tell me to do it elsewhere while we watch tv at night. I find the pointy foot rollers more irritating than anything else. There is too short a placement so you feet must sit in practically the same spot every time. Good for you if you like them. Larger smooth rollers or none would feel better to me. The first time I used the bubbles it took several minutes to start up and then it worked right off each time. You do have to use either the bubbles or the vibration if you want the heater to work.

It's a far cry from a professional pedicure station, but just being able to soak my feet in a foot shaped tub was worth it for me. I do use the vibration and bubbles to help agitate the water and possibly loosen up the dirt that was in my horribly cracked heels. After one 30 minute soak they looked 100% better. I use epsom salts that I dissolved in the first pitcher of water I pour into it. Since it is summer I am enjoying a cool soak for my feet now. They show one of the 4 attachments that you can put on the center piece. You'd have to be a lot more coordinated than I am to use it right there. I do like the attachments which are handy to have right there. It's kind of awkward to carry so I fill it while it is on the floor and dump the water out into a bucket rather than try carrying it across the room.

Bottom line, I am glad I got it but wish the rollers were removable and it would be nice if the cord were removable, too so I don't have to worry about tripping on it while I carry it if water is still in it..

title: Perfectly acceptable, Good flavor, except Gingersnap
text:
Look, it's my total daily fiber and 20 grams of protein in a completely allergen-friendly bar. That's practically impossible. I'm gluten, dairy, and egg-free, so finding a protein bar that has both fiber and protein was a miracle for me. I struggle to get my daily fiber in, so I usually have 1/2 to 1 of these a day. I'm not vegan, so I also eat the grass-fed beef collagen bars in their Paleo Line.

Here's my personal opinion and breakdown of the PEGAN bars:
*Sweet Sunflower: BEST TEXTURE and flavor. Closest to peanut butter, soft and chewy straight out of the wrapper, easy to overdo it and get sick of.
*Chocolate Lava: 7-10 seconds in the microwave (this is actually recommended) makes this soft and chewy and *almost* brownie-like. It's a little sticky, but decent chocolate flavor. Without the microwave, it's a little dry-sticky, kind of like a two-day-old brownie, but still totally palatable, just have a beverage nearby.
*Vanilla Cinnamon Bun and Cinnamon Raisin Bun: These are actually really good. I don't even think I've tried nuking them. The flavor is spot on and the texture is on the medium-dry side, kind of like a day-old cinnamon bun without icing. A little crumbly, but not fall-apart. Also not something that is going to leave you gasping for hydration.
*Gingersnap: I just can't. These are so disgusting, I'm so glad I got it in a variety pack and only had to waste 1 or 2 of them. Even my hubby, who can eat just about everything couldn't stomach it. I asked him if it was just me. His response is "What is wrong with this one???" It's full chemical flavor. I'm not the only critic. There are other reviewers who agree. I don't know where they went wrong. Just throw some ginger and a touch of cinnamon in there and you'll be fine, but somehow it went sideways. DON'T torture yourself, it's not you, it's them. Send them back, ask for a refund or throw them out. It's poison.

PALEO Grass-fed Beef Collagen Bars (these fit my allergen-friendly diet):
*Chocolate Mint: I'm a chocolate-mint person, so I like it. It's a decent mint flavor, it's kind of like the chocolate lava ones, but I don't have these very often and I have to be in the mood for the flavor. Sometimes I'll have half of one for a "dessert. Not overwhelmingly amazing, but not terrible.
*Almond Fudge: Meh, I've kind of moved over to the Paleo bars, but these are also not bad on flavor and texture. These bars lend themselves well to a few seconds in the microwave.
*Vanilla Pudding: I'm not a huge vanilla fan, but these aren't bad. Not too chemically, decent texture, from what I remember. I didn't want to leave these out of the review, but it's been awhile since I ate these. I don't have any yuck memories, just not over the top awesome memories either.

UPDATE: Heard back from Fitbit with a quick (almost instant) email exchange. They finally stated, "Unfortunately you router is not compatible with the Fitbit Aria. As a last option please contact to your internet provider, if there is any chance to change the Connection." SO, I am still VERY impressed with Fitbit CS. Very fast. They just need to get their scale up to par with their CS and other products. Still love my Charge HR!!!

title: Pretty darn good, for the price!
text: I bought and used these with my FuzziBunz diapers. They were a little bit cheaper than some of the other brands, so I figured I would try them and see. Wow...clean up is GREAT!! My son poops, I pull the liner away from his butt (it does stick there), and take it to the toilet to flush it. There is hardly any leftover poop on my cloth diaper and the pee goes right through. No more toilet swishing, which is great news for me!! The only reason I did give it 4 instead of 5 stars is because the liner is quite large width ways, so it needs to be folded, but not in half, because then it wouldn't cover the whole diaper. So that is a little anoying to get it folded just right, but it's really only a few extra seconds. I started lining all of my clean diapers when I fold them and put them into the changing table this way it's ready to go when I need it. And the second reason is because the liner sticks to the baby after they have pooped, so you really can't wait too long before changing them. So when my son poops overnight and the liner has been stuck to his butt for a number of hours, his poor behind is a little red once I change him. It's never been real bad, and I've heard most liners do stick, so maybe it is just a small price to pay for the ease of clean-up. I say if you're using them and changing the diaper as soon, or soon after, they've pooped, it wouldn't be a problem with rashes at all. It could just be my kid though too; he has very sensitive skin, which is why I started using cloth to begin with.

title: Very good value.  But don't use soap.
text:
Reviews of similar bath spa products mention problems with noise, suction cups, and cleaning.
These issues exist, but I believe they are minimal when comparing cost with product.
I find this to be a very good value.
I was impressed at how strong the jets really are. I was expecting much less power from this mat that seems more like a pool toy than a "spa".
The pressure was surprisingly strong and massaging.
In fact, my nearby book (which I had intended to read while soaking) went untouched as the only thing I wanted to do while using the spa was close my eyes.
All of the suction cups do not stay in place, this is true -- but I found it was only a minor inconvenience.
I had no problems with the cleaning -- as you need only to spend an extra minute pooling the water near a hole and turning the blower on. This takes no strength, not much time, and really should be expected of any product like this.
Regarding noise. Yes... it is noisy. But so is being in a real jacuzzi tub. In fact, if you had a jacuzzi tub in your home you would be dealing with even more noise.
These things are not quiet.
My biggest single complaint is that you are not supposed to use any kind product in the bath water.
No soap, oils, salts, or gels of any kind should be used.
This means you are not going to be cleaning or moisterizing at the same time you are "spa-ing".
Therefore, you might end up bathing twice in an evening.
That is a pretty big inconvenience.... but... all in all I think [$$$]or such a powerful at-home jacuzzi experience is an excellent deal.

title: A Fantastic Extractor Kit!
text:
There is NO reason to be tempted to use your fingers to pick or squeeze a pimple or blackhead if you have this handy kit. You do your skin a world of good to give up poking and prodding your acne with your fingers (even if you washed your hands first, just don’t do it). The key is in addition to a good cleansing and exfoliating routine to reduce acne, invest in a good set of extractor tools when pesky acne crops up, which can happen no matter how much you do to keep your skin clean.

Ideally, one should topically medicate a pimple and ride it out. But, that is easier said than done. If you just CAN’T wait for a pimple to resolve on its’ own, extractors get the job done without introducing bacteria into the open area or damaging the skin. This means less redness in the area, no marks or swelling. I have used blackhead extractors for years and also started using long loops in the last couple years. Some extractors are plastic, which is not sturdy enough to apply enough force to get the job done, but is strong enough to damage capillaries. When choosing an extractor, whenever possible, invest in quality stainless steel. It lasts longer, it is durable, and it is more sanitary. This kit is an excellent investment, especially for this great price.

ABOUT THIS KIT:

I like this kit specifically because it is a nice high quality, surgical grade stainless steel, they are easy to hold and handle with grip grids on the tools themselves, and for about the price of one tool from a well-known popular brand name, you can get multiple high quality tools in this kit. It comes in a small zippered case with ample space to hold the tools securely. I like that the tools come in this enclosed case so they are not exposed to open air and stay more sanitary. The loops are large enough and sturdy enough to clean well and therefore can last for years.

The one downside I see to this kit is the lack of instructions, which is fine with me to get instructions elsewhere, or if you are someone who knows already how to use these tools, but someone who has not used such tools should review how to use these tools to remove a pimple or blackhead before use.

This is an absolutely amazing kit at an amazing price!

title: If you want to know about Magnesium......
text:
As many now know, magnesium is need for hundreds of chemical processes in the human body. Most people buy it for muscle relaxation, sleep or to relieve muscle cramps at night, but there many other positives to taking magnesium. Almost everyone is low in Mg, unless they supplement. But here's the KEY, all Mg is not created equal.
The lowest quality, least soluble form is Magnesium Oxide. This is basically useless and is actually the "rust" or oxidated form of magnesium. This is also the cheapest and most magnesium supplements use only this form.
The next up the chain, with a little better absorption and a little more expensive is Magnesium Citrate.
The magnesium forms that are considered top tier, with best absorption is a class called chelated Magnesium. They included Magnesium Malate, Mg Theonate, Mg glycinate and bisglycinate and a few others. These are the forms that are the most soluble and the best quality......BUT they also cost the most.
This Magnesium uses a chelated form, which is one of the best. "Bisglycinate Chelate" is the form used in this supplement.
This supplement uses a superior form of magnesium, is more absorbable and more bioavailable. I personally take this and also recommend this to my patients.
Side note:. Too much magnesium, taken too frequently, will cause diarrhea, but you can work up the dose slowly to avoid this.

I can't really understand why the one VHS copy available is over $200.00, that's just crazy. title: Would be great, with just a few changes
text: Overall, this appears to be a good product.  It's not fool-proof, but I wanted to present my mom with something that would be as similar as possible to the pillbox she was using, but would remind her which pills to take and when, as she had double-dosed and missed doses. As others have noted, there's nothing in the way of instructions, which you have to look up online.  I had no trouble setting the alarms initially, but ended up messing them up while trying to demonstrate the alarm to my 94-year-old mom who has dementia.  The arrow, which indicates which side of the pillbox the alarm is for, is very tiny and difficult for my mom to see.  (Actually, I didn't see the arrow either at first, hence the reason I messed up the alarm and assigned the a.m. alarm to the p.m. boxes and vice versa.) She wants to know which side of the box her next pills are going to be on, so this is a problem.  A bigger arrow and a lighted LED screen would have been helpful.  Also, it would have been nice if one side of the boxes had some kind of marker to differentiate them.  I'm going to get some little dot stickers or something to put on her p.m. boxes so she can easily see which ones are which.  We've only had this pillbox for less than a week, but I think she'll get the hang of it eventually.  She gets her days and nights mixed up pretty often and calls me to tell me that the alarm didn't go off (at 7:30 p.m.--because it's supposed to go off at 7:30 a.m.), but other than that, she seems to understand that she has to hit the "Next Alert" button to turn off the alarm.  With a few improvements, this would be a 5-star product.

title: Replacement filters are no good.
text:
Update: 10/11/2019: The water was starting to smell and taste a bit off this week. Finally took a TDS reading. Turns out that the TDS has jumped from 0004 to 0032. The input municipal tap water's TDS is stable at 0285 PPM.
The original assembly which I replaced this with lasted around 6 months. It took the original assembly 6 months for the TDS to increase this much when I replaced it. I don't think I've drawn even a 100 gallons.
I'm disappointed. I'll have to buy something better.

Filters arrived in only 3 or 4 days. The filters are really good and all you need is a pair of pliers to unscrew the L shaped quick connect connectors.
Per the instructions on the box you need tools which are not supplied plus Teflon tape which is not needed since it's got silicone o rings on all the connectors which are quick connect too.
I was initially frustrated when I read the instructions but it's actually quite simple.
Just connect them in the following order ensuring that they are not reversed. There are arrows on the filters too indicate the flow.
1. Sub micron sediment filter.
2. First carbon filter to remove chlorine.
3. Membrane
4. DI resin.
5. Coconut charcoal filter.

I wish the seller would provide a few blue pull tabs for the quick connectors because they tend to slip out of fingers and fly out.

My only complaint is that the RO filter casing is screwed on too tight and the supplied tool slips a lot. What you really need is a strap wrench.

title: Critical design flaw leads to failure; parts unavailable
text:
The bad: the threads holding the base to the lamp's neck stripped on mine, just like it has for other reviewers. These threads are made from soft metal, and are only about an inch in height. They don't need much coaxing to fail catastrophically. When they do, this relatively heavy lamp can flop over, threatening anything within its path.

If you frequently push this lamp aside, in a way that makes the neck rotate, I promise you, yours will also fail. It ain't no swing lamp!

Verilux won't sell you replacement parts on this, their most expensive lamp. Their Customer Service comment:

"Unfortunately we do not sell separate parts for this lamp, but advice I can offer is trying teflon tape, also known as plumber's tape and wrapping that around the threads to help make a tighter connection. . . "

This advice is dubious. Teflon tape is a lubricant, and a very, very thin product. I gamely tried the tape, and it was a waste of time. Worse, the threads are attached to the base very securely; I couldn't figure a way to remove them, despite a healthy collection of tools.

What has worked for me, at least temporarily: the old Christmas Tree Stand approach. I drilled and tapped three holes arranged around the base of the neck, and screwed three half-inch, #10x24 stove bolts through both the neck and the stripped threads. IMPORTANTLY, I attached nuts to the bolts to help limit how far the bolts go into the thread/neck assembly. The bolts should not penetrate to where they put pressure on the lamp cord (which passes through the neck, duh).

Yes, the result is rather inelegant. It looks like a Red Green Show hack. But it is not that noticeable, with the lamp in use. And it seems sturdier than the original product.

WARNING: if you try this, you must be very careful not to penetrate the insulation on the lamp cord!!! Be sure to check it visually and by feel, once you've drilled your holes. If you damage the cord, I strongly suggest you discard the lamp. If you perform this repair, you should periodically check the lamp cord, to be certain that the bolts are not abrading it.

Another bad: if you buy a Verilux, you've committed yourself to their proprietary replacement bulbs. There are comparable fluorescent bulbs available at your local hardware store, but Verilux has designed plastic tabs into their products, simply to make the competing bulbs incompatible. Yes, some generic bulbs may be cheaper and/or brighter.

The good: the Verilux Heritage Deluxe floor lamp is otherwise, an attractive, reasonably bright, and otherwise seemingly durable product.

title: I love this plug!
text:
Ok, so my eyes might have been bigger than my...well you know. The 3 is pretty big (1.48 inches in diameter). I put this in the first time and knew the Snug Plug was the best plug I had ever used. The thin neck allows my backdoor muscles to relax while it is in. The base, which I think they call a handle, allows for easy removal, but also rests nicely between my cheeks when the plug is in. I tried plugs with round bases that didn't feel good at all. The silicone base on these is elongated and thin, but substantial enough to keep the plug from going inside.

Back to my original statement, the 3 is large! Please, work your way up to it! I have since ordered a Snug Plug 2 (1.2 inch diameter) and will be wearing that for several weeks before I use the 3 again. I am excited about the size of the 3 and I look forward to getting back to using it as soon as it feels appropriate.

Having now worn the Snug Plug 2 and 3, other than the obvious size difference, the only other real difference between the two is that I cannot feel the weights move around in the 2 like I could with the 3. It makes sense, given the smaller size of the 2. Otherwise, both feel fantastic inside.

I will be enjoying these for some time, but I might also have to check out what other products b-Vibe has to offer since these are so well made and feel so good.

title: Very Nice!
text:
~Better Quality~
They are very big and soft and well.. poufy. I really like them. I feel like I am covering more area with these than I was with my older ones which felt less denser which in turn made them squish smaller while holding them. I'm not really sure if that will make sense to anyone besides me so let me explain. The other ones that I use to have must have been made out of something else or made differently. They were just as big if you compare them side by side to these, but when I would grip the other ones in my hand they would shrink to at least half the size as if the insides were mostly just air. These stay just about the same size in my hands as they are out of my hands as if they use more material when they make them. Anyway, since they stay bigger that means that I get done quicker because I cover more area at a time and I worry less about missing any spots.

~For Bathing~
The only thing is that when I use them to bath they don't exfoliate like the scrubbies I use do, so I only use these now for when I'm having a more relaxing soak or when I'm in a hurry. Part of me wishes that they did exfoliate so that I can use them all of the time, but the other part of me doesn't wish that because I love how soft they are and how relaxing it is to use them. I really like that it came with three because I really really don't like using the same thing for some of the same parts of my body. For example, I have one designated as just for my face, so that I don't use the same pouf on my face as the one that I use for my feet. Is that crazy or do other people feel that way as well?

~For Washing The Car~
When they first came in, something had gotten on my brand new car and these were at my finger tips so I used one to get it off really quick. Well, I liked it so much for cleaning my car that I bought another set. They are big and hold a lot of soap and water making them perfect for car washing. My step dad loves them for that reason as well (and I'm pretty sure that he stole one). He came over while I was using one and said that they would be better than what he was currently using for his truck (which he is obsessed with) and he kept on talking about it like he was hinting for me to give him one (I didn't because I was just going to buy him is own set). Next thing I know, one was missing and a few days later when my mom was over, she saw one and said something about how I was using the same thing that my step dad uses. AH HA! So, apparently these are so good that people are willing to steal them. lol

~If There Is A Reason To Update I Will~
I can't talk about how long they last because I haven't been using them for all that long, but if it's a significant amount of time I usually update my reviews. For example, I had a pair of shoes that lasted me way longer than the suggested length of time to use them and I update the review with pictures of how well the shoes still looked after all of that time even though I abused them pretty badly. And I updated a review of something that fell apart much sooner than it was supposed to even though I had barely gotten any use out of it. So, if you don't see an update to this review in the future, it is most likely because these poufs lasted just as long as expected.

title: Check Your Multiple Vitamin - You May or May Not Need This!
text:
I thought these Mega Minerals would give me some extra minerals that my multiple vitamin (Nature's Way ALIVE Women's 50 Plus) was lacking, but I see now that I was mistaken. A side-by-side comparison confirms that almost everything contained in the Mega Minerals bottle I am already getting in my multiple vitamin, and my multiple gives me even more good ingredients! However, I also see that the Mega Mineral does give me additional calcium and magnesium in conjunction with additional Vitamin D, needed for absorption. My ALIVE vitamins only give me 200 mg of calcium and 100 mg of magnesium, and 1,000 I.U.'s of Vitamin D.

According to the National Osteoporosis Foundation ("NOF") women under age 50 need 1,000 mg of calcium from all sources daily and women age 50 and older need 1,200 mg. For men, the NOF recommends 1,000 mg of calcium daily for those age 70 and younger and 1,200 mg for men age 71 and older. For women and men under age 50, the NOF recommends 400-800 I.U.'s of vitamin D and 800-1,000 I.U.'s for women and men age 50 and older. So in my particular case, I will search for a calcium / magnesium supplement to give me the extra 1,000 mg I need a day.

I try to be very careful about not doubling up on my vitamin milligrams, as I take other supplements which also include other ingredients that I haven't purchased the product specifically for. An extra few milligrams of this and that add up to a daily cocktail, which may be too potent and deliver unanticipated consequences. I haven't done it yet, but I am thinking of putting together a spreadsheet of all my supplement vitamins and their milligrams, so I don't cause harm in the pursuit of health!

In fairness, I am giving this 4 stars, as it appears to be a good product for those who may be taking a less potent multiple vitamin that does not include all of the minerals that I am already getting in my multiple vitamin. Please note for full disclosure that I purchased this for a penny in exchange for writing an honest review.

title: Works well but make sure this is all you need
text:
For several months this chair worked well for my husband who has PD. As a matter of fact a bath chair is an absolute must for the elderly and infirm. Not a platitude. Falls in the shower are responsible for too many deaths.
This a sturdy seat and we are pleased with it.
At the time I looked at transfer seats and thought they were more than we needed and too complicated but I'm sorry that we didn't purchase one instead of this seat. It was just a matter of months before my husband's condition escalated. He's still safe getting into the tub with a bath support bar and the back of this seat but my back is killing me.
Consider the possibilities for the future and if the situation (for which you need a seat in the first place) is subject to escalating, look at transfer seats. Buying more than one bath seat is an unnecessary expense when you'll probably by buying several bathroom aids.
That said my husband was relieved when I put the seat in the tub/shower and has been enjoying the security it provides. In the last few weeks since he has needed assistance, it has become apparent that I should have upgraded before making this purchase.

title: Very impressive glasses for this price range.
text: These are very nice glasses.  They come in a sturdy case that includes a mini-screwdriver for keeping the screws tight, and a cleaning cloth.  The glasses are classic aviator type and very stylish looking.  They have metal frames with rubberized bows that will expand outward a bit for those with big heads. The feel is quality all the way and they could easily be mistaken for much more expensive glasses.  They are intended primarily for night driving and do a good job of reducing the glare of oncoming headlights and streetlights without obstructing vision.  They also work well on overcast, cloudy days and in the rain.  They can be worn in sunlight and do block UV rays although probably not as effectively as darker lenses.  The lenses do have a photochromatic feature and darken a bit in the sunlight but not to the extent of glasses designed for that specific purpose.  The yellow, polarized lenses have the effect in the daytime, of making everything look clearer and colors sharper.  They work well for outside sports such as golf.  If you're looking for glasses to wear exclusively on very bright sunny days these might not be for you, but if you need quality night driving glasses that will also work during certain daytime situations I highly recommend these glasses.

title: Warning - new formula dangerous
text:
I took the old formula for a couple of years. It worked well to lower my triglycerides significantly. The new formula is dangerous.

The new formula to include Black Cumin Seed Oil. Within a week of starting taking this new formula I ended up in urgent care who sent me right to ER. I had a lot of blood in my urine and not from any infection. The lab results also showed my kidney was in distress (BUN & Creatine were elevated - not in the normal range though a physical the month before showed them in the middle of the normal range). I take blood thinners and my INR reading was in my desired range.

In reviewing what had changed that might be causing the bleeding and doing some internet searches, I found out that Black Cumin Seed Oil, when taken by someone who is on NSAIDs or a blood thinner, can increase bleeding. I stopped this product that night and the bleeding was gone the next morning.

If you are not on blood thinners, taking this product will cause the same issues as being on blood thinners. The problems are severe and can include death from things you would not think twice of if you were not on blood thinners. This is why blood thinners are carefully monitored. So having internal bleeding going on without knowing - very dangerous!!!

If you are on blood thinners, this "increases" the effect significantly. Enough said, you know what that means.

I called the company thinking they would care about this information, that they would put a warning on their labels, etc.
Nope, no caring at all, just a lot of excuses and side stepping.
Their technical rep basically said they were not responsible for telling you this information above (or the other situations it is very harmful for, like pregnancy). He said:
They are fully aware their product is sold on Amazon and other locations (without these fact sheets), YOUR FAULT you bought it there.
Only Drs are supposed to be giving out/selling their products, the other people that sell it like the ones on Amazon are putting aliases on their forms (e.g. they never check if the person applying to sell their product is a Dr or not). He said the Drs who sell the product have access to fact sheets no one else sees, but when I asked if the fact sheet said taking with blood thinners / NSAIDs can cause bleeding, he avoided answering that question. title: Cleans better than anything else out there!
text: We do a lot of white towels, linen napkins and linen/cotton duvet and sheets and pillowcases, plus shams, blanket covers, etc.  (I like a great looking and feeling bed! - Yes I indulge myself in good sheets, a LOT of them!)  Sending out pricey linens can be dangerous. Commercial laundries are far too rough on them and have destroyed a set or two. So I do them at home in a Miele Washer and use ONLY Persil Powder, hot water, and the long cycle with extra rinses.  They come out spotless, stains never are a problem (and I’ve spilled espresso in bed in the morning a few times.) With the Persil, it comes out. Period. Not a shadow of a stain left.  The machine can heat it’s own water up to 200 degrees, and that temp, plenty of time, and good detergent is AMAZING.  Persil is the BEST. I prefer their powder formulas for whites and use the Mega-Pearls Powder for colors.  The Persil is so concentrated that two tablespoons is sufficient to do a full load of whites. No bleach (ever) and no additives. Just soap, hot water, and time!  Just like great grandma’s maids did the sheets when they’d boil them in copper tubs every Monday back in the 1920s.  I inherited her table linen collection and have Hand Woven Irish Linen Damask tablecloths and napkins that are easily 100 years old or older. Yet they are blindly bright white. Still after all this time.

title: Very configurable; excellent support team
text:
This works for me and my wife loves it. The device is configurable in two important ways. The snore detector can be set to be more or less sensitive. It is worth taking the time to find the right sensitivity. If the device is too sensitive, then even small irrelevant noises can trigger the device. I inadvertently did this two days ago and I got terrible sleep. But when the device was set on medium sensitivity it works well.

In addition to this, the amount of air pumped into the balloon expander can be configured. Because I am a deep sleeper, I think I need it set to maximum which causes the pillow to rise the highest it can. I set it on the lowest setting and it did not even register with me. My wife said that I snored as I normally do, so I don't think the lowest setting works for me.

Over time, the white plastic sleeve that surrounds the balloon expander broke and was no longer effective (the hard plastic slats inside it would slide around). Smart Nora support promptly offered to send me a replacement (at no cost). I am glad to have it working again. I can't say enough about how responsive the support team was and how quickly they got me working again.

This really is made for shorter people or to pick up items about six inches or so off of the ground. title: Great for very short hair
text:
I've got a 1-inch iron that was fabulous for adding smooth curves to my short bob, but when I cut my hair super short it became a lot harder to use. I wanted to add some wispy little curls, going this way and that. The big 1-inch barrel wasn't working for me. This little iron has been terrific, making it easy to add a curl wherever I want, even on my baby bangs. It only takes 1 second to make a curl. Honest, I counted! "One thousand one"... and boom, curl! Now it needs to be noted that I'm not trying to curl large sections, just individual curls. And my hair is fine and curls easily. YMMV. The rounded barrel makes it easy to draw the curl through the iron, giving a great shape without crimping.

Some reviewers complain that the on-off switch is difficult to access without getting burned, but I've had no problems. I've got normal fingers, not overly thin, and keep my nails sport length, not long. The switch is located about a half inch back from the heat plates, which seems to allow plenty of room. At least, it is for me.

With it's short length and small barrel, this little iron is perfect for my very short hair. It only needs a swivel cord to be perfect, but at the price, I'm willing to overlook that flaw.

title: High quality, lightweight, and packable. Perfect for anything outdoors!
text:
Honestly, I haven't used a hammock in over 30 years. I tried the old style ones and really didn't like them. I remember trying a two-person size hammock with my best friend. It was almost impossible for us to crawl our way out of it after being squeezed in like sausages. That was then, this is now. Now that I have a couple big trees nearby, I wanted to give hammocks another shot. I'm glad I did.
This is NOT the old style woven hammock that acts like a Venus Flytrap. This is a hammock that, even at 50 years old, I can get into and out of easily. Yes, you still have to do the whole "twist-around" maneuver in order to get in and out, but I didn't feel like it was trying to either grab me or buck me out!
I was also impressed with the parachute style material. Although it is very thin and breathable, you don't feel like it is going to tear apart, dropping you to the ground. The seams are all well done, especially around the ends where the rope goes through. It was nice that they give you the rope needed!
When I was done, I was actually able to get the hammock packed back inside itself! You have to roll it up just like it came out, but it will work! I know this will be going with me in the RV! So lightweight, I could even take it backpacking, fishing, hunting, picnicking, you name it.
I was given one of these hammocks in exchange for my honest review. I rely on these reviews just like you do, so these are my honest opinions. I am now sold on hammocks. I would recommend the Swift-n-Snug hammock to anyone.

title: Quality Massager (NOT)
text:
I used to own a model of this massager which was acquired in the 1970s, but it was small and I decided to get a larger one. I purchased a Dolphin massager, but it stopped working after about 9 months. I then decided to purchase a new Wahl massager which is now larger and decided upon the professional model because it appeared to be more solid in build. I was disappointed that it came with only three attachments but decided that better quality was still the best route to follow. I am very pleased with the unit and find that it is solidly built, that it has plenty of power, and that I can get by fine with the three attachments. I have problems with my lower back and find that it is easy to position in the right places. Although it is not a thumper, it still gets the job done.
UPDATE 9-1-2015
Since I purchased my Wahl Professional massager on December 2, 2013, I have used it occasionally to relieve muscle trauma. I tried using it today and it ran fine for a couple of minutes and then stopped vibrating in its normal way. Now, it will vibrate at a very low level which I can stop with the slight press of my finger. I tried contacting Wahl to see if it could be repaired or replaced, but their website does not have a customer support page or a contact link that works. It is now worthless to me, and I am very disappointed in the present quality of Wahl products. I have now reverted back to the use of a Wahl massager that I inherited from my parents that is about 40 years old. The reason I have now given the massager a score of two stars instead of one is because it worked well while it worked.
Update 9-30-15
I decided to take the massager apart and see what caused it to stop working and discovered that the metal piece that vibrates had cracked at the point where it attaches to the motor. Because I was not able to find a way to communicate with Wahl customer service and, perhaps, obtain a new part, I took the broken part down to a machine shop and they welded the part that cracked. It now works like new. It appears that the quality of the Wahl massager is not be as good as their massagers used to be.

title: A perfect 10
text:
Every now and again there is a product that stands above the crowd. The daylight24 Booklight is such an item.

I have looked at various book lights from the two major producers: MightyBright and Zelco. Most current offerings by them are LED based lights. I have been less satisfied with these for a variety of reasons. I might have considered the incandescent itty bitty light from Zelco but many reviewers have warned of quality control issues. I have owned the Lightwedge but it is cumbersome to keep moving it and it scratches easily, leaving it unpleasant and annoying to use.

Design: The clamp/battery base holds 3 AA batteries. This may add bulk and weight (an advantage, see below) but this leads to a longer battery life. There is a convenient on/off switch on top the base. The bottom has two pieces that slide out to the sides to form a stable base so this light may be set on a table instead of only attached to a book. The base also has rubber feet to hold it in place. The extra batteries in the base give it the necessary support. The goose neck that holds the lamps comes out of the front not the top as in most other similar designs. This design allows you to move the light in a much broader way, nearer the book. The light itself is long and narrow which allows the light to cover an entire book with absolutely no hot spots. The illumination is even over the entire book. The quality of the light from the cold cathode tube is... perfect. Unlike LED lamps, it is very white but not too bright while it maintains true color palette.

Quality: Top notch. The base of the daylight24 is not at all flimsy like those made by its rivals. It has a high quality metal (yes, that's right, metal) toggle on off switch that is very unlikely to break. The quality of the goose neck, which is important to keep the light steady, is only approached by those on the Zelcos. However, it is the length of this one that sets it apart from them. This goose neck makes those on the MightyBrights seem like horrible toys. The light fixture appears to be a high quality plastic on top with protective glass covering the bulb.

Feature set: The daylight24 remarkably comes with an ac adaptor and batteries unlike most others. It has its own padded carrying pouch that has two compartments, one for the adaptor and one for the light.

Value: At $16 this light is a tremendous bargain. No other book light comes close.

I applaud the manufacturer for making this product and Amazon for making it so affordable. It, therefore, receives my highest rating and recommendation.

title: Great shaver, Excellent Customer Service
text:
Long-term Update (after 1 year of use) - Great customer service and very good product!!
I have been using the Bald Eagle Pro for over a year now. Just about when the one-year was going to be over, the battery started losing power. I called Skull Shaver and they sent a replacement battery. As it turned out, the replacement kept turning off after about 30 seconds. I called Skull Shaver again and they said they would send another replacement. After a couple of days when the replacement did not arrive, I called again. This time they sent a COMPLETE box with everything! I was very pleased with the customer service. The shaver works very well and it is very easy to use. Takes only a couple of minutes each time. Now I use it dry. I only had to replace the blades once so far. Overall, a good product and great customer service. A+++++

OLD REVIEW
Power to the baldies! I mean, electric power delivered via a rechargeable battery that rotate circular thingies that cut hair pretty well. For the layman, a shaver that works as described. To make a short story long, I was tired to forking $15 bucks each time I went to my local Great Clips for a 'haircut' that required driving, some waiting, and at times praying that the haircutter would not nick an artery. Well, I ordered the Bald Eagle Pro based on reviews and it fits well for my needs. Instead of waiting a month to go to the hairdresser, I can now easily shave my head every week. I read reviews from some folks who complain about stubble. Well, I am on the other end of the complaint, in that I wish it would leave more stubble. I actually like to have a hint of hair. I mean, I don't want the ladies to think I am going completely bald. (That's a joke, by the way for those who don't get these things). In any case, the shaver works as I expected. I actually prefer to grip it with the battery and kind of press it down on my held as I make the motions all over. At my second try I was better, and I think it works better with shaving foam. Obviously that reduces friction and allows for smoother motion on the head. The battery seems to hold the charge well, and the entire unit is pretty compact and handy. The construction is well done and so far I have no complaints. I think the unit is pricey, and the company would probably attract more buyers if they lowered the price, but that's not my problem. Good luck to Skull Shaver as they do have a good product, but hopefully they figure out a good pricing model that works for both sides.

Update: I have been using the Bald Eagle Pro for about 3 weeks and I am quite pleased overall. The unit has worked without any issues, and shaving my head is a breeze. I first apply shaving foam (NO GEL), and that makes shaving easy. Compared to your typical electric razor (like the ones hairdressers use), this is so much better and convenient, and faster. Initially I was missing a few areas around my ears, but now I do a few more passes. The shaving is quite painless and worry-free. I shave once a week and it works great for my needs.

title: A gentle "foot grinder"
text:
Let me start out by saying this product is worth every penny they charge for it. The first time I used it I had excellent results and will continue to use it to keep my feet callous free.

I have what I consider heavy callouses on the heals of my feet. They are hard and scratchy and just ugly to look at. I bought this tool because the battery operated ones had complaints of the wheel stopping if too much pressure is applied. It turns out the this tool also will stop if too much pressure is applied but this is a safety feature and not a flaw. The product works by spinning a rough cylinder that literally grinds callouses away. If it didn't stop when you pressed hard you would risk damaging the softer skin around and underneath the callous.

To properly use this product I would simply sit on a tile floor and gently rub the tool over the calloused areas using just enough pressure to slow the cylinder down slightly. you can hear this by a change in pitch from the motor. At this pressure and speed it is safe to use and will not damage your skin. Just keep it moving over the calloused area and the callous will slowly disappear.

What you will leave behind is nice soft skin a pile of skin dust. I kept my vacuum cleaner near by and used it to clean up the mess and then clean up the tool when I was done.

I would suggest this tool to anyone. As a side note I bought the extra course cylinders and used them first. They worked fine and weren't too rough.

Well, they work, and will stick into your shoe, as long as you avoid too much contact with your fingers AND get it placed perfectly into your shoe on the first try. Otherwise, the adhesion is GONE. I didn't even make it out the door with the first pair I tried. It turned into a strip of clear rubber. Not even a tiny bit tacky. Then, I tried again (trial and error), removing the backing and sticking it to my shoes like applying a bandaid. BOOM! Worked great, and stayed in all evening. I don't wear heels everyday, so it's stayed in those same shoes for a couple outings (dinner... I didn't sweat or dance in them yet). For casual use, I can say they do the job for sure. title: Love it! Comfortable and Lightweight!
text:
The ComfyCloud was something that interested me because I have really bad Arthritis and back pain, which is a big issue seeing that I am only in my 30’s. So sitting in a spot for awhile and then trying to twisting sideways to get out of an office chair or the car is very painful anything that helps even a little is a huge deal and the Comfycloud seat is great.

The seat itself is made out of foam top of a plastic base that spins 360 degrees. This means you can use it in any direction. On the bottom of the base is a grip pad, this is wonderful because you can use it on all chair types and not worry about it moving around. The top is actually a gray cover that is really soft and plush. The cover has an elastic type band around it holding it around the foam edges. The cover itself can be removed and washed. title: Works when taken as prescribed
text: I believe this product really works. You have to take it as prescribed, however. It works to essentially dissolve unwanted grit in the joints (for lack of a more scientific explanation), but it has to to be taken on an empty stomach or the product will work on breaking down food instead. I've been on and off of this product, and I definitely feel a difference (better) when I'm using it regularly. The trick for me is remembering to take it right when I get up, before my shower and my daily coffee or morning smoothie. A full half hour or more on an empty stomach is best. It doesn't work like an NSAID which you take to deal with inflammation in the moment. This is only effective when taken over time and on a regular basis. Give it sufficient time (a few weeks at least) and take care to take it as prescribed in order to experience a decrease in overall body joint pain. I'm not crazy about spending the money every month to stay active on it, but my body feels better when I do.

title: Good tape, take care when applying...
text:
I’m an older (in my 40’s) BMX freestyle rider and have been using Kinesiology tape on and off for about 4 years for various injuries. This past February, I developed a horrible case of tennis elbow that made riding my bike insanely painful. I could barely lift the front end which is critical for many tricks. I also lift weights 4 times a week, which made matters worse. I thought rest would do the trick, but found that active rehab, message and ice was the key. And to offset the pain, kinesiology tape. I was buying tape at the local drug store and it was kinda getting expensive at $12 - $15 a roll, when I realized good ‘ol Amazon should have a less expensive version. I can get 3 rolls for the price of one.

I am really happy with this tape, although I would recommend oil free skin and maybe a heating pad to heat the adhesive on. I’ve showered with it as a test, and it stayed on without issue.

When I cut it, I round off the corners, but if you rub and accidentally roll off ends of the tape, it won’t restick very well. Meaning, take care when applying it and don’t allow the ends to roll off.

In certain creases of the body, it may come off some at the ends, but the meat of the tape will stay. I know this because removing it feels like removing duct tape. I’m pretty hairless, but for you hairy folks, take caution, or shave.

Colors and designs are fantastic and bold. I really like mixing them up.

Good tape for the price. Great colors, just needs a bit of attention when applying.

title: Good electrolyte powder!
text:
I love the fact that there's zero calories and zero sugar. I also like the fact that there's a minimal amount of salt. Both of those are hard to find in most electrolyte powders. The taste is subtle and not overpowering when mixed at the recommended dose. If you don't like plain water this will help offset the taste and provide nutrients as opposed to most sugar-laden drink mixes.

As for actual usage, I wish it mixed a bit better in water. Every time I use Junp it leaves a decent amount of "sediment" at the bottom because it doesn't mix in very well. So far the best way I've found is to mix Junp in a water bottle and shake it every single time before taking a drink, yet there is always a tiny bit of granules leftover when the water is gone. It's not a huge problem, but it definitely doesn't mix perfectly with water.

The scoop is interesting because it has a super long handle and a tiny scoop at the end. The long handle would help when the container is nearly empty, but until that time, the only way to store the scoop is to insert it upside down and push until it clears the cap. I completely understand why they did it this way, but it's really awkward to store the scoop. It's not a deal breaker, just weird.

I think the price is a bit high for what is actually included in the product, even though it does appear cheaper than similar electrolyte products. This would be a no brainer at <$15, but over $20 starts to be questionable.

title: I think I already wrote a review but there is MORE!!!
text:
I had bought this to go with my Fitbit that I love. I am going to Hawaii and was trying to lose 10 pounds before I went.

When using the Aria the first few days I was impressed with how great is was to step on a scale and see progress even though setting it up was tough. I have love how it can tell the difference between me and my husband. I love not having to read the scale before I can see, I can just step on then go get my coffee and wake up.

But this is where this thing is AMAZING. For the past few weeks I have been taking over 10,000 steps in a day, exercising and eating right. By right I mean nothing processed, high protein, low carb. If it wasn't for this scale I would of given up (probably). My scale has not moved in almost THREE weeks. I have gone hiking, taken the stairs as often as possible, been to the gym, cut down on beer and junk food. I was not really losing ANYTHING!!! I would of lost my MIND before.

But with this scale I was able to see a steady drop in body fat every SINGLE week. A LOT. So even though in 3 weeks I haven't lost ANY weight I have consistently dropped in body fat by about 3% total in 3 weeks. That means I have been gaining MUSCLE which is the whole point of exercising and eating like I used too when I was super fit.

This scale is GREAT!!! LOVE IT!!! Would recommend to ANYONE trying to lose a few pounds. If you are getting this to improve your health and fitness go for it!!

title: the best decision I've made in a long time
text:
I have back, knee, and hip problems and they've been really flaring up lately, making it hard to do a lot in the kitchen. I was having trouble even putting groceries away or finding something in the fridge. Finally, I had the idea to get an adjustable stool for the kitchen and I cannot believe I never thought about that until now. I can't stop raving to my friends about what a genius I am. I sit comfortably while I rearrange stuff in my fridge instead of crouching awkwardly and then making dying wildebeest noises when I try to stand up again. When I'm between steps in cooking something, I just sit down and relax instead of letting my low back tense up and my knees get inflamed from just standing there like an idiot who forgot that sitting is a thing that can be done anywhere. If my back starts to get sore while doing dishes, I sit down for a minute. It's not actually great for doing dishes, as it puts you at more or less little kid height and it's not that convenient but for a few minutes it's a nice relief. It's great for loading the dishwasher at least.

The chair itself is sturdy, doesn't take up too much room, and the height is adjustable so I can be equally comfortable hanging out at the counter and rummaging in the vegetable drawer at the bottom of the fridge. I genuinely feel stupid for not doing this before now. My only qualm is that it feels just a little unstable, like my weight is all on that center support and not spread out evenly. I'm just getting used to that, as I'm told that that's just how it is with this type of stool. Apart from that, I'm in love.

title: Nice little pill holder - a little on the heavy side...
text:
I got this as a gift and was really pretty annoyed at the small storage area. I was really wondering why people only carry like 4 tylenol in such a big container.. why is it so heavy? Why didn't they drill all the way down to the bottom!?

Well, the short answer is that I was pretty stupid and didn't figure out until 3 months later that it's actually two distinct pill holders in one. Yeah...
If you didn't buy this or see pictures of it before, you would never guess that the bottom ribbed portion was actually another section. Mine was screwed together so tight that the seam looked like it was just a design element like the ribs on the bottom.

After learning that it was two parts, i was able to fit about 16 lactase pills (each about the size of an extra strength tylenol capsule) in this. That's two doses for me :(

So, after learning about the secret compartment (I call it that to make myself feel better) this pill holder is pretty awesome. It's got just enough storage for most people and it's small enough to fit in your pocket without making it look like you're really excited to see the person standing in front of you.

The best part about this pill holder? The rubber gaskets. They make this holder waterproof. Yay!

title: Essential for Percussion Ensemble Practice
text:
I'm the glockenspiel player in my school's percussion ensemble, these are essential at every practice. They cut out 18 db; this is great for concerts and practices, but not so great for things that require heavy-duty ear protection.

PROS:
The little metal case is wonderful, these things are so tiny I'm sure I'd lose them in an instant. It has a thick plastic lining so the plugs don't rattle around.
Fit is good, better than the Etymotics for me (but your results may vary).
A lot smaller so not as visible as the Etymotics, more discreet for sure.
Clarity of sound is good. More than the volume changes if I'm not wearing them, but they're miles better than foam earplugs at limiting sound evenly.

CONS:
They do get uncomfortable after a couple hours, but that is to be expected of any earplugs.

Overall, 5 stars. They do what they need to do and the price is right.

title: Good for transition lens
text: Is the corrective aspect for far-sightedness on your transition lens seemingly weak? In other words, when trying to read through the bottom of the lens, is the letters soft? It might just be that your lens is not positioned correctly on your face. To test this, read like you would normally do. Then, slowly push up the glasses while still reading. Do things become more clear? If they do, then, you need these pushups. For those with glasses with large lenses, these pushups work the best, as the corrective part for reading is at the bottom of the lens, and these pads are needed to elevate the glasses so that the reading part of the lens is easier to access. I have RayBan 5184's, which saw much improvement in reading with these pads. However, for me, the clear silicone pads would look better on these particular RayBans. Ordered the clear.

title: Camallanus killer when combined with levemosole
text:
I used this in conjunction with levamisole to eradicate camallanus worms in my 60 gallon livebearer tank. The directions on the container says to mix with 4oz of food per packet but I couldnt see my tiny fish eating so much in 3 days so I scaled it down with the aid of a cheap $10 jeweler's scale. I mixed the powder with frozen blood worms and seachem focus to try making it adhere to the food better. Then fed them as much as they could eat in about 3 minutes. No signs of any worms since.

If you're looking for levimasole you won't find it pure on amazon, but you can find it on pure ebay. If you are trying to kill camallanus worms know that they may be resistant to this medication and for best results get your fish to eat it. Using 2 medications at once will guarantee better results.

No fish fatalities. I don't keep inverts.

title: You get what you pay for. Get this if you are looking for a cheap scale that will give you a ballpark weight average.
text: First, the scale is actually smaller than your average scale. Second, this scale gives me a different weight half the time so I usually have to do a best out of 3 or 5. I also tested this scale using a 35lb plate and every time it would do the same thing so its not like my bodies center of gravity is causing the difference. Third, I would go through the motions of storing it in the cabinet then pulling it back out instantly and the dang scale wouldn't even be "zeroed" anymore so if you get this, make sure its staying in the same spot and never being moved. Either stick to using the precise scale at the gym or spend more money and get a digital one. Yes I could have gotten a digital one but I mainly needed this so I could pick my dog up and weight the both of us since hes a bigger dog that is on a diet,  the digital ones just instantly error out since I'm moving slightly the entire time holding onto a 90lb dog. If you just need a ballpark of what your weight is, then sure get this but if you are actually serious about losing or gaining weight, then DO NOT rely on this. It will give you false hope lol.

title: Great item....but...cold bubbles
text:
I really searched hard to find some sort of bathtub insert. The house that we just bought has updated bathrooms, but only one bathroom has a tub. The previous owners told us they wanted to put in a jetted tub, but due to the layout of the bathroom it was impossible to install one. I knew my hopes of having a jetted tub were over when he told us that.

I decided to buy this insert for all of us as a Christmas gift. Overall it is really a nice product. I HATE taking baths, but I love jacuzzi's, therefore this gives me the bubbles in the tub that I really want. The bubbles do come out fast, however you will not have that relaxing feeling of a jet pounding into your sore muscles. You will have a nice, calm, relaxing bath experience.

The main issue that we have with this item though is that the air that produces the bubbles is COLD. Therefore the bath water becomes cold very quickly. If you decide to purchase this I would recommend filling the tub 3/4 full with water and then add hot water 1/2 through your bath. Even when the water is warm you can still feel that the bubbles coming out are cool.

Even knowing about the cold bubbles I would purchase this product again, only because I had taking a bath when the water is still.

title: great product, works within minutes
text:
I usually take magnesium at night to help me fall asleep. I thought I would give this a try after reading about it. It does help relieve pain, and it also --for me---provides a nice, drowsy-relaxed feeling. I like taking magnesium so there is no hangover effect the next morning so I can still wake up for work with no problems. Initially, I was having what I guess was restless-leg issues. Just an uncomfortable feeling in my legs/ calves where they sort of twitch and just won't relax to let you sleep. One pump of this spread on both calves solved that problem COMPLETELY. I put it on other areas like if my hip or lower back is aching, and it helps me fall asleep by relieving the pain in that area. Also, works great if you over-did it from exercise so have achy muscles. I have used it on my neck, shoulders, upper arms, trigger thumb joint pain, low back, hip, legs and feet. No problems whatsoever----besides the drowsiness effect on me. (I would say you could probably gauge if you will feel drowsy/sleepy vs. just relaxed and pain-free based on the effect any other magnesium supplement you have tried has affected you. I just happen to be super-sensitive to it.)

I recently bought this product that also contains MSM after reading about the pain relieving effects of MSM on joints. My foot had started hurting mainly under the big toe after wearing some new shoes and doing a lot of walking that day. Anyway, using the cream has also been helpful in that regard, putting it on at night (again because it happens to cause me drowsiness).

This does have a rust smell because it is a mineral. I typically wear vinyl or nitrile latex-free examination-type gloves to apply the cream since I do not want that smell on my hands. The smell does go away after a while if you do not want to use gloves. ( Also, I re-use the gloves.)

Also, I have learned that this product with just the magnesium lotion is a bit stickier and smellier than the one which contains MSM, but that is because the one with MSM has 25mg magnesium per pump whereas this product contains only magnesium at 40mg per pump. Both lotions do absorb, but this one, at first, will have a bit of a sticky feel. The stickiness and odor both go away after maybe 10 minutes.

Additionally, it is true this lotion does not have any effect on your bowel movements. Some can take magnesium during the day with no problems, but this magnesium though a lotion, affects me just like a pill supplement in that it causes me to feel drowsy. (Again, I only add this because I am super-sensitive and want to make sure anybody who is sensitive is aware you might not want to use this for the first time right before going to work. Also, even if you are sensitive to a magnesium-drowsy effect, it may not create that feeling for you with only one pump. )

Bottom line: I think this is a great alternative to taking NSAIDs on a consistent basis which I have read is not good for the liver or stomach lining over time.

title: If anything, a really good multi-vitamin product.
text:
Who doesn't want thicker, fuller hair? I know I do! As someone who suffers from Hypothyroidism, hair loss is a daily frustration, so when I had the opportunity to receive this product at no cost in exchange for an honest review, I was extremely happy to give them a try!

So....what did I think?

If anything, Will’s General Super Hair Growth vitamins are a really good multi-vitamin product. If you look at the label, there isn't any magical ingredient that would cause the hair to grow super fast.

The smell is not too bad and the pills are easy to swallow in my opinion. During my evaluation of this product, I did not experience any bad side effects.

I will continue to use these vitamins until my supply runs out in order to see if hair growth is noticeable. As of right now, just normal growth has occurred. This product is full of the good nutrients I need anyway, so I will continue to use this product until it's gone, if for anything, my daily multi-vitamin.

*Update 6/11/15* After taking 2 bottles of these vitamins, I will have to report that there was not a bit of SUPER hair growth obtained by taking this supplement. If you are looking for a good multi-vitamin, then this is a good choice. If you are looking for a product that claims to grow your hair super fast, look elsewhere......this product does not live up to it's claim.

title: mmm like pina colada mix! also reviews of all the syntrax nectar flavors.
text:
Caribbean Cooler is awesome. I love the taste. I put 4 ounces of frozen pineapple juice, and a little water and some ice in the blender along with my calcium powder and its like drinking a virgin pina colada. Makes getting my daily protein requirement in very nice.

I ordered a sample pack directly from Syntrax and decided to review all the flavors here.

Strawberry Mousse :
I really liked this a lot. Mixed with 1% milk in a blender. Would probably be good with almond milk also. Nice Strawberry aroma when opening the package. The flavor reminded me of a strawberry shortcake ice cream bar. Pleasant and no weird aftertaste. Much better than Premier Protein strawberry flavor which I find pretty nasty. I will be adding this to my pantry.
4.5 out of 5 stars.
I think this would be good with fresh frozen strawberries added in a blender.

Crystal sky: I loved the packaging. Blue with pictures of fruit all over it. Pineapples, watermelon,kiwi, grapes, strawberries. I had high hopes. Opened the package and the smell of Juicy Fruit gum hit my nostrils. (Do they even make Juicy Fruit Gum anymore?)
Gag. But I soldiered on. Mixed with chopped ice and cold water. I'm sure that helped. Looked like a blue slushy but no it did not taste like one. I managed to consume it like a good RNY patient trying to be comply with her protein requirements.
Unless you like Juicy Fruit gum I cannot recommend this flavor in any way shape or form. Ick. Hold your nose and swallow.
1 star out of 5

Lattes Cappucino:
This one I had heard so many good things about and it did not disappoint. Smelled like coffee ice cream upon opening the envelope.
Mixed it with cold 1% milk. Very very good! This flavor is outstanding. Someone here previously stated that they drank this hot and yes I think that would be excellent. I also was thinking if you chopped up frozen milk cubes in the blender and then mixed a small bit of cold milk and the powder it would be a coffee frappe!
Definitely will order this!
4.75 stars out of 5!

Roadside Lemonade: didn't smell that lemony when I opened the envelope. (I drink a lot of sugar free Wylers lemonade so I was looking for that sort of flavor maybe?)
Mixed with cold water.
Eh. Not good but not undrinkable either. You have to wonder why they didn't add more ascorbic acid to the recipe for a proper lemony tang.....
Not impressed enough to order.
3 stars out of 5

Chocolate truffle:
Smelled like brownie mix when I opened the package. Mixed with cold 1% milk. Eh. Frankly not chocolately enough. Premier Protein chocolate is better. Not bad, just lackluster.
3.5 out of 5 stars.

Vanilla Bean:
It was very good. When i opened it, reminded me of the smell of vanilla pudding. I mixed this with 1% milk. Nice flavor and has the possibilities of adding other flavors (almond extract) or using a blender with frozen fruit
This one would also be good with almond milk I think. I don't know about mixing straight with water.
Overall very palatable and I will probably buy a container since it has a lot of other flavor options for creative cooks like myself.
4.75 stars out of 5

Cherry:
Smelled like a cherry lollypop upon opening the package. Mixed with chopped ice and water in my blender.
The actual flavor kind of reminded me of a Luden's cough drop when drinking it. I don't think I could drink this every day.
2.5 stars out of 5. I won't be adding this flavor to my pantry.

Fuzzy Navel:
I have never actually had a Fuzzy Navel cocktail. I suspect this flavor does not come close, BUT I enjoyed it very much. Although I gather its supposed to be peach and orange flavor, I thought it reminded me much more of a mango.
I mixed it with cold water. I suspect it would be very good with frozen banana, strawberries, or mango.
I would definitely order this one.
4.5 stars out of 5

Cookies and Cream:
mixed it with 1%milk
I found it very palatable. It was actually pretty good.
I think it would be good with almond milk too. Don't know about mixing it with water.
Definitely would order this flavor
4.5 out of 5 stars

Green Apple- mixed it with plain cold water.
It seems to be going for a jolly rancher kind of flavor. But the whey protein is distracting. I don't think I could drink this often.
2.5 stars out of 5

Wild Grape - mixed it with plain cold water. I was a little afraid of this one. Generally I do not like grape flavored products.
This one smells like Fanta Grape Soda which I actually do like. And its not bad. But its not really good either. I kept wishing for fizzy bubbles and that whey protein thing kept sneaking through. I don't think I'll be ordering this flavor.
3 stars out of 5

title: A Great Whey Protein But better mixed with Medical Unflavored Protein
text:
If I follow the directions using 8 to 12 oz of water, this has a strong, artificial peach flavor and a stevia-like aftertaste that I don't love, but grew accustomed to after a few days. By doubling the liquid the taste and aftertaste were improved, but I felt bloated. I just purchased the Nectar unflavored medical protein and by mixing equal parts peach and unflavored (using the smaller scoop that comes with the unflavored) with 8-12 oz of water it has more of a natural peach flavor and the aftertaste is reduced dramatically. And no more bloated feeling!

I don't really crave sweets, so perhaps others would find the above option too bland, but it's hard for me to imagine.

Mixing the peach flavored (and the fruit punch) is much easier in room temperature water. I then add ice to cool it down. If I mix it using cold water, or in a blender bottle with ice, it ends up having clumps of sticky goo throughout that stick to the bottle and are hard to clean off. It only tastes good cold, but mixing first then adding ice is the way to go.

Compared to other whey proteins I've tried over the years, this is tastier and easier to use. I'll buy this again as it has no sugar and is relatively easy to mix. Less versatile than the Unflavored Medical Protein though. If you like the flavor of peach, give this a shot!

these are the many uses of cinnamon in your diet
Lower Cholesterol
Studies have shown that just 1/2 teaspoon of cinnamon per day can lower LDL cholesterol.
Blood Sugar Regulation
Several studies suggest that cinnamon may have a regulatory effect on blood sugar, making it especially beneficial for people with Type 2 diabetes.
Yeast Infection Help
In some studies, cinnamon has shown an amazing ability to stop medication-resistant yeast infections.
Cancer Prevention
In a study published by researchers at the U.S. Department of Agriculture in Maryland, cinnamon reduced the proliferation of leukemia and lymphoma cancer cells.
Anti-Clotting
It has an anti-clotting effect on the blood.
Arthritis Relief
In a study at Copenhagen University, patients given half a teaspoon of cinnamon powder combined with one tablespoon of honey every morning before breakfast had significant relief in arthritis pain after one week and could walk without pain within one month.
Anti-Bacterial
When added to food, it inhibits bacterial growth and food spoilage, making it a natural food preservative.
Brain Health
One study found that smelling cinnamon boosts cognitive function and memory.
E. Coli Fighter
Researchers at Kansas State University found that cinnamon fights the E. coli bacteria in unpasteurized juices.
High in Nutrients
It is a great source of manganese, fiber, iron, and calcium.
