title: Great Ionic Facial Steamer with an Anther Box for Essential Oil Treatments
text:
I am always interested in trying new beauty products to pamper myself, and I have been trying to be more diligent in keeping my pores clear lately, so I've taken to steaming my face over the stove top using a pot of boiling water and a towel before using blemish extraction tools, and while that's certainly a method that works, it leaves a lot to be desired, so I was eager to try out this facial steamer.

This facial steamer comes with the steamer itself (which is white and gold plastic), as well as a power cord and a set of very detailed, and very easy to understand instructions. The steamer is lightweight, and 8.5 x 5.5 x 4 inches in size, so it's a bit smaller than most water kettles, and doesn't take up too much counter space. There is a handle on the top so you can move it around when it's hot (or in the process of cooling down).

With this facial steamer you can moisturize your skin not only with distilled water or purified water, but also with milk or essential oil. While I don't necessarily see myself as someone interested in trying the milk approach, I was quite pleased with how well it worked with both distilled water as well as distilled water with a bit of essential oil using the anther box (lavender oil was quite lovely!).

The facial steamer was quite easy to set up. You simply remove a small compartment on the back and fill it with your liquid of choice, then you screw the cap back on and replace the reservoir and plug the unit in. At that point there will be a red LED light on the front which designates that the steamer has power, but is not powered on. From there you simply turn it on using the power button on the front, and the the LED light will turn blue. It took about a minute for mine to heat up, at which point steam will start to be emitted from the nozzle of the steam outlet.

The steam will last for between 8 and 10 minutes, and initially you're recommended to only use this type of treatment a maximum of 2-3 times per week as you become used to it. The closer you are to the steamer, the hotter it will be, so feel free to stay back a little ways if it feels too hot or uncomfortable.

On top of the nozzle is a small sphere called the anther box. To use it, you simply pull the halves apart and place anther or essential oil on a cotton pad and then put the two halves back together so that the steam will be forced through the pad when it is in use. This approach works quite well, and keeps your essential oils away from the delicate components inside of the steamer.

This worked really well for my skincare routine, and so much better than opening my pores over a pot of boiling water! I usually wash my face first, then use this to help open my pores, remove blemishes, and then wash it again and apply a moisturizer for maximum absorption, and this facial steamer has definitely been an improvement to my routine.

All-in-all, I love this ionic facial steamer, and would definitely recommend it if you're considering adding one to your own health and beauty routine. Just be mindful that you read the directions and use it properly so that you don't inadvertently burn yourself or damage your skin.

title: Nice Case Fits Up to Ten 5ml, 10ml, or 15ml Bottles of Essential Oil, But Not as Snugly as Some
text:
I'm a huge fan of essential oils, and I'm always lookout to try new cases and find better ways to organize my ever-growing collection.

This essential oil carrying case fits up to ten 5ml, 10ml, or 15ml bottles of essential oil. The bottles are not included with the set, but are merely shown to illustrate what the set would look like when filled. The case is 6 x 4 x 2.5 inches in size and includes prominent branding on both sides of the zippered bag. I purchased the "purple" version of this case, which appears to be quite color-accurate to the product photos.

The case is soft, but has a small amount of padding on either side. I like that the pockets are black vinyl mesh so that you can see through to read what type of oil is in each bottle. The only problem is that since the openings accommodate 5ml, 10ml, or 15ml bottles, unless you're using the largest size, they have quite a bit of wiggle room. I would highly suggest the manufacturer consider making the edging that runs across the bottles out of elastic so that the bottles, especially smaller bottles, are better held in place, regardless of their size. There is also no padding between the bottles.

On the whole, I like this case, and would recommend it if you're considering a nice way to store up to ten of your favorite essential oils. Just keep in mind that it is not as padded as some other options out there.

This little device has made my mouth feel squeaky clean before even brushing my teeth. I should note that I did not use the toothbrush attachment, nor plan to, as I already own a top of the line electric toothbrush that is admittedly more powerful per the manufacturer.  The docking station holds an adequate amount of water for a couple of uses, and the cord management is very good. It is tidy since it’s rechargeable and doesn’t always have a cord attached to it. I like having the 3 speed settings (high, low and pulse), and the 2 time settings (1 min. and 2.5 min) for maximum personalization. The high setting works well with constant pressure and isn’t too powerful if you floss regularly, however the low setting seems to pulsate a little irregularly. Also be forewarned that the hose needs to be attached to the water flosser handle when there is water in the tank; otherwise the water dribbles out of the hose. These are minor shortcomings for the gentle and effective flossing action it provides

title: I found an easy fix to keep them from slipping off my arms
text: I'm using one of these in conjunction with the iWalk knee crutch, which has turned out to be the perfect combination for me! They feel like they are very solid construction, with adjustments for both the lower leg and the upper arm. The only issue I had with these forearm crutches is that they would slip off my arms because the cuffs are a little too big for me. I tried several ways to push on the cuffs to get them to be smaller, but they always just sprang right back. I like that the cuffs are covered in a sort of rubbery plastic, because that helps them grip a little better. To keep them from slipping off my arms when I let go of the handles, I just wrapped a thick hair band around the ends of the cuffs, and this has worked perfectly. It's not so tight that it digs into my arms, but has just enough resistance to keep the crutch from falling. I happened to have the hair bands on hand, but you can get them at just about any type of drug store - they are near the hair brushes and combs. I also really like the little threaded metal bands that tighten the outer tube against the inner tube, and this makes the crutch completely noise free. I also added a little WD-40 to the bolts that attach the cuffs to the poles, and this made them move a lot easier with my arm movements.

title: There's no cheating with the Aria!
text:
I decided to purchase the Aria to use in conjunction with my FitBit for my fitness improvement. I had a little trouble installing the scale. I am a senior but reasonably computer savvy. Finally I used an alternate installation route suggested and that worked. Of course it measures your weight, but also BMI and body fat %. And it all syncs automatically to your PC. I'm looking forward to FitBit getting an app for my Windows phone.

I decided to add some additional info about the setup after reading some of the other reviews. I am a 74 year old senior and as I said reasonably computer savvy. I did use Geek Squad to install my WiFi two years but didn't think I would have any problems as I have installed other programs. Well I have no idea what Ethernet is, and wasnt about to pull out cables from my computer if I could figure out which cable to pull out! But after trying for about 30 minutes I decided to use the alternate method suggested with my iPad (I have a windows phone so couldn't go that route). After a couple of false starts I was able to get connected. I had the scale on my desk next to the PC (my floors are carpeted) and after I connected I took it upstairs to the master bath and it works great. I figure if this 74 year old can do it anyone can. I figure all this computer work is keeping my brain young, and hopefully I'll be able to keep up with my 6 year old grandson!

One other note: I was a little concerned about the body fat % as it seemed high to me. BMI was normal. Anyhow I went on line and found a chart that was age adjusted and that was normal. So even though I know this isn't the most accurate way to measure body fat it still was a relief to know that I wasn't out of line.

4. Wash your sock aids once in a while.

I HAVE seen comments here on assembling this item, specifically the top part where the rubber gaskets go for the metal loop. I have no idea why that's a challenge for some people, but if you find that hard to figure out, then the problem isn't really the unit or instructions.

You simply remove the cotter pin from the bolt, slide the bolt out of the loop, put the rubber washers in the recesses at the top of the unit, slide the loop over the washers (it fits perfectly, then slide the bolt back through the loop. Then you replace the cotter pin, making sure it's bent out enough that it won't slip out of the bolt.

Very, very, very basic stuff.

title: Typical benefits of MSM are just as good as internal.
text: I purchased MSM for it's healing benefits, specifically it's ability to spped production of collagen in skin. I deal with hormonal acne & my skin marks very easily. I can heal any breakouts quickly but the resullting post inflammatory erythema & hyperpigmentation is my long term issue. Vit C, niacinimide, licorice root, alpha arbutin, & other things I've tried have all been beneficial but Im always looking for a better option. Microneedling, chemical peels, etc. have all been used, then I read about MSM. Applied tropically it can stimulate collagen production & cell turnover, replacing the inflammation damaged tissue with healthy clear skin. I add a scoop of MSM & a scoop of zinc oxide (for it's antibacterial & anti-inflammatory benefits along with it's other benefits) & dissolve it in aloe. I use a pure aloe liquid with only 1 other ingredient, a preservative. I apply the resulting paste over any red marking left from my breakouts. I find they heal much quicker when I use this mix. Applied to #11s or other tiny fine lines this can also be beneficial. My only issue with the MSM is that it does not dissolve as well as I wanted it to. For being water soluable, I expected it to do better in aloe, but just to make sure it wasn't the aloe, I have used water also. I had the same issue of just a grainy texture left after mixing. Even with that graininess though, I just dab the mix on any spots I have & they are visibly less red the next day. This mix, especially if you add the zinc oxide, is going to be white & won't absorb fully, so this isn't an "under your makeup" type of thing. I put it on at night & sleep with it on, wash it off in the morn. I often add a drop of Rosehip seed oil & Black Cumin seed oil to futher help with the healing process. If you deal with breakouts & the post inflammatory erythema/hyperpigmentation they leave behind & have tried all the typical treatments without a lot of benefit, then try using MSM. Taking it orally can also be beneficial, but applying topically will ensure that your skin actually sees the benefits. While so many products exist for hyperpigmentation, melasma & dark spots & they are effective; there is just not the corresponding same amt for red marks, erythema, so many deal with. Many of the ingredients that help hyperpigmentation by inhibiting melanin production, just do nothing for redness. Erythema, caused by tiny broken blood vessels under the skin done by inflammation, benefits from very few things other than time. Because MSM is anti-inflammatory it can help decrease swelling & help heal those red marks. MSM contains the building blocks skin needs to make collagen. Increasing production allows new cells to replace damaged cells faster. Because acne can cause pitting & indented scars, the increase of collagen productionn can help to fill them in. So while I specifically wanted to try using MSM for my red marking, if you also deal with rolling, boxcar or icepick scars; you may find benefits with MSM. It took maybe 2 weeks of use to see any results but cell turnover takes 28+ days, so your always want to continue a new skincare product for at least a month before passing judgement unless you experience irritation or other issues from it. So far, I've seen good benefits from using MSM. I'm hoping to see continued benefits for the foreseeable future.

title: Easy to see why this is so highly rated!
text:
After doing the usual read every review check every product on Amazon, I decided on this one for my Airbnb apartment rental. And then I took it with me to Burning Man. For those with compliance needs, it's clearly marked ANSI/ISEA Z308. 1=2015 Class A Type III. Whatever all that means. I just wanted something to ensure that whomever might show up in my apartment would have ready access to immediate resources in case of an incident. Here's why this kit is so good. It's divided into six pouches, one of which includes a Red Cross Emergency First Aid Guide. Each pouch is clearly marked with what it's for and what's in it: e.g. 1-Small Cuts & Burns (Antiseptic, Adhesive Bandage 1 x 3 in. Burn Treatment 1/32 oz. 2-Medium Cuts & Scratches (Sterile Pad 3 x 3 in. Eye/Skin Wash 1 fl oz total... etc) So.... when you actually need the kit, it's going to be under some level of urgent or at least pressing circumstances. You simply unfold the accordion pouches and quickly choose the right one for what you need. At this price, no home should be without this kit. A few of my guests have already used it and said they would order one for themselves.
Didn't have to use it at Burning Man thank goodness! But is is reassuring to know you have everything ready and accessible just in case.

I gave it 4 stars only because it didn't come with instructions but after watching a YouTube video, I was able to use it with no problem. Each person is different but this is what worked for me:

I used the size medium pink curlers instead of the rods. I have short straight Asian eyelashes that even after using a curler or whatever to curl my lashes, they are as straight as a stick again. I felt the large wasn't going to do anything and that the smalls were going to curl my lashes over each other's so I used the medium and they were a perfect fit! I did cut it to fit my eyes as I tried to use them as is and even after glueing them on my lids, the bottom piece would still stick out over my lashes. After cutting them to fit, I was able to eliminate that problem. Make sure when glueing your lashes that you keep each lashes as separately as possible since how you glue them on will be what they look like once permed. For
Solution A and B, I left both on for 20 mins. Then clean with solution C. Solution D I left on for 6 minutes. Once done with solution D, I used solution C to help clean off the glue I had on my lids and lashes using Q tips. Do not use water!!!

I do wish that there was more of Solution C instead of just two small bottles of them but other than that, I'm pretty please with the results. The picture is without mascara or anything else on but you can definitely see the curls 😍

title: Even more convenient than before.  :D
text:
Machine-Washable Foot-Warmer and Heating-Pad

I have to say, in winter time, these warmers are fantastic. I don't like a house that's too warm (plus overheating the air just burns out all the moisture and you get electrocuted by static just moving around).

But when you're not moving, eg, watching teevee, reading, working on computers, etc., your feet can get rather cold. Mine especially, because once I'm home, I walk around barefooty.

So I've gotten a few warmers where I usually stay. By my computer desk, near the couch, and even at the foot of the bed when I'm reading or doing puzzles. They're loose and not constricting like socks, let me shift foot positions easily, and are warm even if not powered up.

So these latest warmers are just as fantastic as the others I have. It's double-sided so you get heat from both top and bottom, has a nice thermostat and timer to let you adjust the heat and time before it shuts off, and has nice heating that's even more even than the others. Plus, the grippy rubbery surface helps it "stick" to hard floors without sliding around, which is a really nice touch.

The control is very nice and easy to use, too. The dial twists around to set the temperature you want, from barely warm to scorching hot. Buttons are for on/off and to set the automatic timer. That's all there is to it... simple.

Being able to be easily washed is a must for me, because anything I have gets covered in cat-hair almost instantly, haha. And even the "old fashioned" way of sliding out the heaters and tossing the rest into the machine is sooooooo simple and easy. But convenience got easier by being able to toss the entire warmer into the wash!

All in all, I love these heaters, and will probably get more.

As mentioned, this new one is actually machine-washable. The older design was easy to remove the outer layer from the heating elements and wash the former while keeping the latter, but machine-washable design is even easier. Just pop the warmer into the washer, let it go, and out comes a spotlessly clean warmer with minimal muss or fuss.

Convenience increases, and I can wash off errant cat-hair so much more easily.

I've really gotten to like these warmers! :D

I am in a loose loose situation, There are no options to contact the manufacturer, Amazon will not allow a return or replacement. title: Make sure you have a LOT of clearance under your roof racks or keep looking
text:
Ok. they are affordable. BUT
One of the hardware packs was missing 1/2 the washers. I could let that go for the price. (What's a few washers cost?)
However, installation is a pain. The bottom bracket is too narrow (small radius) to mate nicely with my 4runner's stock roof rack. (Yes. they match the dimensions that the product calls out). It works but not cleanly. It would mate better if the bottom radius was the same as the top bracket radius. The REAL negative is that the 2 bolts that tighten the brackets to the roof rack are so long that there is not enough room between the room and the bolt to to install. Well, you CAN if you back the bolt out of the frame but then you have to monkey with trying to get the carriage head into the frame again, with the stuff on the end but you can turn the bolt...I'm not doing it justice as to the difficultly. I installed just the tightening nut (the nut embedded in a knob) and I could get it pretty tight, but after a short trip, they were getting loose as expected. Even if I could get every thing on, there is essentially no room for my hand to turn the tightening knobs. This is compounded by the other 4 bolts used to put the frames together being longer than necessary (~10mm extra sticking out below the nuts). It isn't like a 4 runner is a tiny vehicle and the roof racks are cosmetic. The straps are okay. I can see where others have had issues with them letting loose. I can make racks work with some modifications, but that's my time and money. Save yours and keep on shopping.

title: Good For Those Who Need A Longer Shoehorn And It Passes Security
text:
Purchased this shoehorn for travel. At home I use a single piece 31-inch shoehorn similar to the HOUNDSBAY 31.5" Extra Long Handled Metal Shoehorn. I tried going on a cruise with it and was sent to security. In a room with other people being inspected, they opened my suitcase and took out the shoehorn. They asked me what it was. I told them an extra-long shoehorn. They called a supervisor over and he just laughed at them and waved me through. They thought it was a sword or weapon of some kind. I never tried to carry it anywhere again.

I saw this telescoping shoehorn. Collapsed, it’s short and does not appear to be a weapon. Took it on a cruise and no questions asked. This is now my travel shoehorn. It’s somewhat compact, about 14 inches, but extends to over 36 inches. The only issue I have is it’s a bit thick on the horn part. The one piece is thin metal all the way down and is much easier to get my foot into a shoe. But I can live with this minor deficiency.

When I first saw it, I thought it looked very familiar. The shaft looked exactly like my Velbon monopod. Exact same twisting motion to unlock and lock it. Even the white dots on the sections looked identical to the Velbon. It has the same feel to it too. Maybe it’s from the same manufacturing company. I’ve used the monopod for over 10 years and it’s still a solid performer. I have no doubt this will also last me a long time.

Highly recommend this for people who love to travel and can use a longer shoehorn.

title: This takes stealth vaping to a whole new level.

I'm not a cloud chaser but I still exhale a decent amount of vapor, 0.2 ohm coil at 45watts on a dual battery mod. Some vapor will escape the device a tiny bit when you pull it away from your mouth but it is a very small amount and dissipates almost immediately, majority of the vapor goes into the device and disappears. After a few times using it you'll get some condensation drops on the outside of the filter but it's easy to wipe up or leave the lid off to let it dry on it's own. If you need to stealth vape in a bathroom at work, a hotel or public place you'll find this thing super handy.

Tip: Both end caps need to be off for it to work. I'm not always a smart woman, it took me a couple puffs to figure out both caps have to come off this thing. At first I thought it was impossible to blow through it.

title: If you have leaky gut....
text:
I was informally diagnosed early last year with leaky gut based on a blood allergy test. I had no IgE reactions, but a broad range of IgG sensitivities. I really don't have any other lower abdominal problems, thankfully. No IBS, Chron's, etc... I do have chronic constipation, which can be a sign of leaky gut, as well. Many things can cause constipation, one of them being hypothyroidism, which I do have. It appears that my doctor caught the leaky gut early in that I don't have other horrible symptoms. I intend to be vigilant about healing my gut.

This testing all came about because of some upper GI issues. I started having troublesome throat symptoms, choking episodes, ear pain, and upper chest pain. I've been told I have LPR (laryngopharyngeal reflux, very different from GERD.) In the midst of this LPR, my Dr. ran blood and stool tests. The results revealed, in addition to suspected leaky gut, that I had intestinal parasites and candida overgrowth. Fortunately no bacterial issues.

My troublesome symptoms are the LPR, I don't know if repair of my lower gut issues will have a long term impact on my LPR symptoms, but I can't believe that it's not all related, since it's all part of the GI Tract. I am definitely doing much better with the LPR than I was a year ago. The parasites and candida most certainly compromise the integrity of the gut lining. Parasites bore holes all through the intestines, allowing large particles of food to escape into your bloodstream, and your body consequently labels them as foreign invaders, resulting in the broad IgG food sensitivities.

My alternative doctor (with permission from my regular doctor) has me on an intense antimicrobial regimen intended to kill the little critters that don't belong. The antimicrobial treatment itself isn't a long term cure. Permanent diet change plays a huge part in this, and will continue to do so, as I assume I'll be susceptible to yeast long term.

I've cut out all grains, dairy, sugars, fruit, and starchy vegetables while I'm on this treatment program for the next 8 weeks, Basically just meat, non-starchy veggies, nuts, lemon, lime, tomato, goat cheese and goat butter (these contain enzymes that cause the goat products to digest their own sugars.) I hope to add back some low glycemic fruits and veggies, but I'm pretty sure I'm headed in the grain free, dairy free direction permanently.

Anyhow, I have taken many things over the course of this past year, and I'm not sure what's working the most, but this RepairVite is well regarded, and my alternative doctor highly approved the prescribing of it by my regular doctor.

It contains L-Glutamine, a handful of herbal ingredients I don't know much about, and several that I do (slippery elm, aloe vera extract, and DGL), all of which I was taking separately until I was given this Repairvite. It's not cheap, but then again, I was spending quite a bit on products with the individual ingredients. As far as the taste, it does have a decent caramel flavor. By itself, I find the taste just fine. I'm tougher than the average Jane in that I don't have a huge problem taking disgusting tasting supplements. Not that this Repairvite is disgusting, but I do mix it with several other supplements at the same time to get it all over with. I usually mix a scoop of Repairvite, a couple tablespoons of George's Aloe Vera Juice, some powdered probiotics, half a teaspoon of liquid vitamin B complex, and 3 droppers full of my antimicrobial defense together in a small shaker with enough water to blend it all together. Shake vigorously, and bottoms up.

A word of caution that's not on the bottle. Do not take this at the same time as any prescription medications, as it can interfere with proper absorption. Wait at least an hour or so after meds to take this.

For anyone who might be interested, I've taken some suggestions from the Gut and Psychology Syndrome book and cookbook for healing my gut. In addition to my daily Repairvite cocktail, I also make my own bone broth and typically drink a cup or so before breakfast and dinner. This is supposed to help seal the intestinal lining, especially when you don't skim the fat. I also take George's Aloe Vera before each meal use probiotics twice a day. Regarding constipation, I've heard that warm lemon juice first thing in the morning is very helpful. I wasn't that crazy about taking it warm, but I do squeeze fresh lemons, add cold water, stevia, and ice, and I drink a big cup of lemonade twice a day. This seems to be helping with regularity. If you have leaky compromised gut health, constipation is your enemy, trust me. You need to get that resolved.

Give this RepairVite a try. If you're taking it because of lower abdominal symptoms, I suppose you'll notice whether this is helping or not based on whether your symptoms improve. Since I wasn't having lower abdominal symptoms, I'll have to wait until the next blood and stool tests to see if my IgG allergies have lessened, and whether the parasites and fungus have been either reduced or eradicated. In any event, by LPR has improved since this all hit me suddenly a year ago. Again, it's all part of the same system.

I encourage anyone with gut issues that there's no magic bullet for your health. Avoid prescription meds if possible. They mask the symptoms, cause more side effects, and don't get at the root cause of the problem. Find a doctor or alternative practitioner who won't just prescribe pharmaceuticals. Be willing to thoroughly investigate everything, and most importantly, prepare yourself for big diet and lifestyle change. You're guaranteed to be stuck on drugs if you want to have your cake (literally) and eat it too. Start taking steps to repair your gut naturally. What's the old saying...a journey of a thousand miles starts with a single step. Your health won't improve with a silver bullet solution. But small, consistent steps taken over a long period of time will pay big dividends in the long run. Be faithful today to make wise choices and small steps in the right direction. This will compound over time and get you headed in the right direction. And one last thing...if you need encouragement to stick with the "slow but steady wins the race" concept in your health, and all other aspects of your life, read The Slight Edge by Jeff Olson. Great encouragement contained therein to plug along like the tortoise in Aesop's fable. Slow but steady wins the race. This book helped me to stick with small daily steps to improve my health. Like the principle of compounded interest, you might not see immediate gains in the daily minutia of yet another dose of Reparivite, probiotics, clean eating, etc..., but over time you will see the tide turn in the right direction!

title: This scale is not accurate by design
text:
I have not read any other review so if someone has already said the following, sorry.

I bought a One Tracker and thought it was such a good idea that I decided to try the FITBIT scale. The first one I received totally quit working within one hour. Amazon sent a replacement.

I followed the instructions and set the scale up and the WI-FI worked and connected the scale to my online account (dashboard).

I set the scale on my wood floor, took off my shoes and socks and weighed myself.
The first weight was 68 lbs (I weigh 205.5, according to my doctor's scale).
I chalked this up to the machine calibrating itself.

I waited 10 minutes and weighed myself three times, pausing between each weighing.

The weights given were:

205.9
204.2
205.1

I contacted FITBIT and gave them the results.

I was told that the scale gives a "unique" weight each time you weigh and this can fluctuate if you move any at all when you're weighing yourself.
I was also told the scale has an accuracy of +- 2 lbs. I thought this meant that the weight it gives will be within 2 lbs of the "true" weight as measured by a doctor's scale or other high end scale.
In other words, it's fine so long as it gives the same weight if I weigh myself three times in a row.

Apparently, that's not what it means.

If I weigh myself three times in a row I may get three different weights, within 2 LBs of the "true" weight.

For example, I weigh myself today and I'm at, say, 205.
I lose 1 LB which brings me to 204.
The next day I weigh myself.
The scale may report the weight as anywhere between 202 and 206 ( 204 +- 2LBS).

This may(!) be very discouraging to anyone on a diet who is trying very hard to lose weight.
A lower number at weigh-in time is a great incentive to keep going.
But if the scale is unable to record the loss, and may actually show a gain this might lead one to say "What's the use. I tried hard and still gained weight."

title: This is a great little high quality IFAK pouch.
text:
This is a great little high quality IFAK pouch. Big enough for the things you need without being to big to mount in areas that will limit how you move or sit. Quality is on par with 5.11 or Maxpedition.

Materials and build quality

Stitching is consistent and well done. The zipper is high quality and the pulls are easy to us The hook and loop (velcro) used throughout is a good high quality and seems like it will last well even with hard use.

Layout and size

The IFAK has plenty of room for essentials. I was able to fit a combat gauze, OPA, small trauma shears, and a full booboo kit in the pack. You would have a hard time fitting a large full size trauma compress in the pack with everything else, but it could be done. I prefer a IFAK will a little room that I can get into ( like the booboo kit ) that forces me to inventory things regularly. They elastic layout on the inside is well thought out and provides good retention for large and small items. You’ll need to experiment a little to get everything to fit how you want it. There is room under the external elastics at the hinge of the pack for a tourniquet but it's snug- not a bad thing. One of my older style TQ’s also fit well in the retention strap that doubly secures the IFAK to the velcro backing.

Negatives

Really very minor stuff. The IFAK out of the package is meant for a horizontal orientation out of the package, and there's no provision for mounting it vertically. A couple of vertical MOLLE straps added to the back would be great for taking up less real estate on a belt or vest.

I don’t lose a lot of sleep about all my gear color matching, and the black is a great option, but adding a brown or gray seems like a great choice for future changes to this well thought out little pack.

Conclusion

Really impressed with this little pack. For someone that needs a IFAK that can carry a pretty good load, yet not get in the way this is a good option.

On the hood I noticed that the little bit of bird droppings on the vehicle just weren’t breaking down as well as with other products. Additionally after the wash there were two big streaks of dust that had become more tacky and clung to the clear coat. I used on another vehicle that is garaged and not a daily driver that gets a weekly wash and the soap did well but the car didn’t really have anything on it so it is hard to mess that up. Because of the results I had and the price of this soap I do not think it is a very good deal for the price. Durability wise it is a soap that foams up and removes most of the light dirt but it all depends on your driving conditions.  The product is a foam cannon soap so I don’t know how it can be super versatile. I feel like this is a soap I would feel comfortable using on a vehicle with clear coat or paint damage but based on my cliental those aren’t situations I encounter regularly.

title: Useful supplement to your regular flossing routine
text:
I really love the size of this water floss. It's versatile and small enough to bring with you when traveling. Let me say this... it will NOT replace your regular dental floss. The water stream power is not strong enough to dislodge every food particle between your teeth. However, for someone with deep pockets between their gums from previous dental work, it can be an addition to regular floss as the water will go deeper than the threads without injuring your gum line.

I tried all modes and liked the pulsating mode in its highest setting the best. Oh! Make sure you read the instruction before trying it for the first time. Although it's very simple to operate, you may be lost without the instructions. My only complaint is that the water compartment is very small. It doesn't hold enough water for your entire mouth, so you will have to fill the small chamber a few times. It also takes a while to charge it for the first time, but the battery lasts for a while.

I believe this floss is better suited for someone with very sensitive gums who cannot use the large powerful water floss machines out there, or someone who just wants to add an extra boost to their regular flossing routine.

title: Perfect for sensitive ears
text:

I have sensitive hearing - concerts, movie theaters, fireworks, bars - they are all cause significant discomfort due to the high volume of surrounding noise. They are small and ribbed so they don't slide out of the ear canal, and have an unobtrusive stem to help get them deeper in the ear - and to aid in pulling them out. They are rated to reduce noise by 18 decibels while maintaining the integrity of the sound (not only high or low sounds are reduced, but the full range of noise at an even level).

They are clear, which makes them inconspicuous - I can wear them in public places without my company feeling embarrassed about my sensitive hearing (in very loud places, I often need to excuse myself to to a quiet area occasionally, or if there is nowhere quieter to go, I have to cover my ears for a few moments to alleviate the discomfort).

No more! I can go anywhere now and I don't have to worry about loud volume. These come in a stainless steel keychain small enough to store with your car keys or in your pockets.

title: Extreme Disappointment
text: My objective was to give members of my family a bottle of Mangosteen Juice due to healthy issues that this juice has a reputation of helping. I ordered this product with 1 identified ingredient on the label; 1) Organic Certified Mangosteen Juice and fruit from the Whole Garcinia Mangostana L. (See attached picture) To my surprise when  the product arrived and I gave some to my extended family, the ingredients identified on the bottle were not the same as ordered. The bottles received had ingredients such as Mangosteen Puree with Pericarp, filtered water and citric acid. I hope this was an accident and not a strategic attempt to advertise one product and ingredients and replace it with a product with the same label, but different ingredients. Within the  manufacturing process, when the juice and fruit processing is done, and the real juice is extracted, the by-products left over is the pulp; which when added with water and other ingredients is called a Puree. Unfortunately, the Puree product has significantly less health benefit and the added ingredients tend not to be organic; however, this puree version produces higher margins and profitability for companies as compared to producing the real juice. Please send me what I ordered; that the label states and it has only one ingredient. Also, if you can enclose shipping labels so I can put the other stuff in the box and send it back. I hope this was just a mistake and you actually don't have 2 different products under the same product label.

title: Great at diffusing oils!
text:
My first diffuser purchase and remains my favorite after purchasing a second, more expensive one!
Pros:
Easy to use, just fill, add a few drops of oils, replace cap, and turn on
Diffuses the scent throughout a mid sized room well
VERY quiet motor! Although I wasn't aware that all diffusers made a water dripping noise constantly... it's annoying until you get used to it. It sounds like a leaky faucet! Now I can just ignore it into background noise.
It can be set to different lengths of time 30, 60, 90, and 180 minutes.

All said, it's a great little diffuser. It's not very pretty, doesn't run for a long time, but it's functional and it works. Plus the price is great!

Neutral:
The colored lights (they do not change automatically as others do) The color function is not necessary for me at all though, so it's a moot point.
The light is fairly bright (even on the dimmer setting) (it would be too bright for me to sleep to, although it may work well as a night light if your little one wouldn't mind it shutting off in 3 hours)
The lights change from white to dim white, red to dim red, green to dim green and blue to dim blue, then off

Cons:
The dripping noise (which seems unavoidable, but still a nuisance)
It's a little difficult to figure out how to put the lid back on
The cord comes out of where the buttons are pressed, which is annoying because I want the cord to be in the back of the machine, not coming out of the front...
It will only run for 3 hours at a time but the water in it could last for 6+ hours
It's not very pretty... It just looks, industrial...

title: If you are thinking about buying an Air Filter, this the one you should get.
text: I had been looking at Air Filters for over a decade.  Remember the Smarter Image electrostatic units.  I went to my local Smarter Image and looked over the 3 demos they had in the store.  But the thing that struck me the most was the air passing through was so gentle.  And all I remember thinking is how could one of these ever do very much.  I seen the commercials where the cigarette smoke disappeared in a sealed small chamber, but I don't smoke. And I didn't live in twelve cubit feet. I lived in an apartment, about 900 sq. ft. at the time.  And units were kind of expensive too, about $300. So, buying two or three of those things were not feasible.  Then new Air Filters started coming out, and each new Air Filter was clearly improved over the older unit.  Then suddenly it seemed there were lots and lots of Air Filters on the market, all claiming to be better than the last, but each new one was plagued by one fault, they were ugly.  And the prices ranged from $75 to $500, but how did I know if they worked.  Then a friend of mine, who had a lot more money than me, showed me his storage unit in his apartment building, with about a half dozen vacuum cleaners, and nearly a dozen Air Filters.  According to him, all of these did not work the way he wanted them too, neither the vacuums or the Air Filters.  But one of the really cool things about Amazon is the customer reviews.  Because if you thinking about buying something, you can find out what other people think about it, before you buy it.  I only mention all of this, because I have never actually owned an Air Filter before. And my friend convinced me I never would because of all the units he had in storage unit.  But I was able to surmise from everyone elses reviewing of Rabbit Air that this unit would actually work.  So, I bought one, and it does work. It works really well.  In silent mode it actually is silent just like the Smarter Image unit. But it also passes a lot of air, because you can feel it coming out of exhaust vent upwards. It actually is automatic, or you can set it to be manual and fixed in its function with a remote. What could be cooler.  And it works.  It works really well.  I have only 500 sq. ft. currently.  I'm retired.  This one unit actually removes the odor from my apartment. Odor which I had gotten use too.  And it even pointed out to me that I needed to clean the inside of most of my kitchen cabinets.  And since I live in the equivalent of Tiny House, 500 sq. ft. or less.  It cleans the air in my entire apartment, just one unit. Rabbit Air claims it will clean 700 sq. ft., but I don't know if that is true, having less than 700 sq. ft. But I know that the rest of their claims are true. And finally, it is not ugly. I have it sitting in my living room, proudly. I'm very happy with my purchase. And too people who think that $500 is too much, I remind you of my friend who had thousands of dollars invested in air filters, none of which really worked the way he wanted them too.

title: Be very careful-i suffered a chemical burn on my eye
text: I have used this cleaner for my contacts for a long time.  They used to include two of the neutralizing containers.  Since there is now only one I assumed it was safe to use with both bottles of Clear Care  However, with about 1/3 of the second bottle left the container quit neutralizing the solution.  When I went to put my contact in my eye I had immediate and intense burning.  I immediately removed my contact and rinsed my eye with saline. The burning was so severe that it was hard for me to open my eye enough to rinse it but I knew that's what I needed to do. The burning continued so I called my optometrist.  She had me come in and examined my eye.  I suffered a chemical burn.  She gave me two prescriptions and my eye was healed enough to wear contacts in about 3 days.  So proceed with caution as it isn't a gradual process but rather the neutralizer works one day and the next you will have excruciating pain and a possible eye injury.

title: No More Clumping!  Best Brand of Three Tried.
text:
This was my second purchase and I'm happy to report that the company has started adding one of those little dessicant packets so the problem with product clumping is a thing of the past. I'm serious about my Vitamin C, so I purchased three different brands of freeze-dried organic acerola cherry powder. Terrasoul's is hands down the absolute best. There is nothing added to it and you can tell that right away. Of the three brands I tried, Terrasoul's is the darkest in color, and it tastes and smells the best.
I don't want to disparage the other two brands in a review of this product, but I DO want those reading this review to know I did my homework, so here's the scoop without the brand names. One of the other brands has "organic non-GMO maltodextrin in it"; that's not something I want and I find it suspicious that the claim is it has more C in it even though it's been thinned out with this other product. Rank that number two of the three. I do really like that brand's non-fortified nutritional yeast a whole bunch, though. The third brand I purchased claimed it had nothing added but was suspiciously light in color--waay lighter than the other two--and it didn't taste good. After trying it, I threw it out. I can't think of a reason it should have looked so light without something added to it.

title: Grossly overpriced. Versatile and compact.
text:
The ComforTrac Wave Cervical Traction Neck Support helps to stretch my neck in the correct, ergonomic direction to assist with headache reduction. It is one solid unit and very lightweight. I couldn’t find the exact materials this device is made of, but it feels like a rubberized plastic with soft’ish’ lighter colored foam insets. I only notice the very slightest ‘give’ to the shape when I press hard enough on it with body weight. So, I’m not entirely certain it has ‘give’ at all with just the weight of my head on it.

It’s fairly compact measuring 8.5”Wx7.0”Dx4.75”H so it’s easy to store. It will even slide right under a bed assuming the bed is standard height or taller.

The materials look to be very durable so this device should have a long life. It is really easy to clean and disinfect due to the hardened feel of the material. It doesn’t have an unpleasant odor. In fact, it just smells very lightly of rubber.

I wasn’t impressed with the instructions but found a way to lay my neck over it that was comfortable enough anyway. I ordered this product with hopes that regular use, along with chiropractic and physical therapy, could help restore some of the natural curve back to my cervical spine as well as reduce pain due to herniated discs, pinched nerves, and chronic muscle spasms.

There’s no special rubber bottom for traction on the floor but it seems to hold very well without it. It doesn’t slip when I position my neck over it. I can’t get my head to hang backwards over it like advertisement photos demonstrate due to my neck curvature issues, but that’s the goal. I realize achieving the goal will take time and regular use so I wasn’t unrealistically expecting immediate pain relief.

I also use the raised upper ledge of the device to roll the muscles across as a type of mini massage. It’s also good for applying targeted pressure for trigger point therapy with the same technique of utilizing the raised areas.

It has not eliminated pain. I think that will be a long time coming, if ever, but it does help to reduce headaches for short periods of time with the trigger point work.

It is definitely, grossly overpriced. Other products are available on Amazon that are nearly identical to this one for half the price. Otherwise, I’d give it 5 stars. Hopefully, the seller catches on and does a reasonable price adjustment.

title: Stops running and lcd lights blinking crazy
text:
[[VIDEOID:3b85ff538f2fce07059a9b386550f24b]] Edit 5/25/22:
This hair dryer was honestly the best hair dryer I used in my entire life, until it wasn’t. It just won’t continue running. The first hair dryer I received started only blowing cold air, even though it was on the hot air setting. But before that happened, the lcd display screen had started wigging out and blinking like crazy. The numbers would be randomly, and partially, missing. The seller sent a replacement promptly and assured me this was nothing they had experienced before. The replacement worked during first use, but the numbers were wigging out and blinking. It went completely rogue on the second use. It decided to stop blowing any air at all (cold or hot), after a few seconds of use, with the lcd screen still showing numbers like it was on and running. If I unplug the hair dryer and wait awhile, it will run again for about 15 seconds and then do the same thing; no air but still displaying numbers (wigging out and blinking). I’ve reached out to support again but haven’t heard back yet. As much as I loved this hair dryer, when it did run, I have to advise you to look somewhere else. This one has serious electrical issues.

Original:
The ENISECA 1875 Watt Negative Ionic Hair
Dryer is the best hair dryer I have ever used… in my life. Hands down, a curly girl’s dream dryer. Where to start….

First off, it’s a bit different in that you hear it blowing (quite loud) and you feel some air (kind of) but it’s like almost nothing but heat comes out. I’ve been using old school dryers with the huge toothy diffusers forever and didn’t know this technology existed!

There is a handy LCD screen on the side to tell you if you are in hot or cool mode and at what temperature it is set. Unfortunately, it shows only Celsius with no option to change to Fahrenheit. It starts at 50C by default every time you turn it on. I took it to 75C and my hair was nearly completely dry in 3 minutes time. It goes to 99C but I wasn’t using heat protectant so wasn’t feeling that brave.

The instructions leave a little to be desired. While they definitely make a noble attempt at thorough, a lot was lost in translation. Literally. Some really rough translation from Chinese to English is going on in there. With the dryer in your hand (plugged in to put it in use), and doing your best with directions, you can figure it out pretty quick. The first seven pages of the twelve page booklet are safety warnings. Plus, there’s a short maintenance/troubleshooting section on the last page. There’s no support contact info. If you have issues beyond the provided troubleshooting, you’ll have to reach out through Amazon.

Function: It’s worth noting, the air speed does not change. The temp does. The air speed on my dryer was constant and only the degree of temperature changed with the +/- buttons. The instructions imply temp, as well as ‘wind’ speed, change with +/- buttons. So I don’t know if mine is faulty by not changing air speed or not. Either way, my dryer performed like a rockstar and I wouldn’t change a thing … except maybe being able to see Fahrenheit as opposed to Celsius. LoL

There’s a cool setting and heat setting as well as a large range of heat. Press and hold the power button three seconds to turn it on/off. The hair dryer starts automatically at 50 degrees Celsius by default. You will tap the plus button to increase temperature and minus button to decrease temperature as needed. Tapping the power button twice, quick clicks, while it’s in use will switch to cool mode and the LCD will read 99C with the fan emblem. Tapping the power button again one time switches back to heat and back to the 50C default. Note: You’ll know you are in cool mode by the little fan emblem on the LCD screen. Video attached for reference.

I absolutely love that it is push button and not a slide lever. Often times I couldn’t turn my old dryer off without grabbing a hand towel for traction. Hair product on the hands made them too slippery for the slide lever. That’s no longer an issue with this dryer! Also, this dryer is incredibly lightweight and fairly compact compared to traditional hair dryers that aren’t specifically compact for travel . It has a very classy look in matte black with gold trim.

It arrived with a large storage bag, a gold colored 1 inch round brush, and three attachments: the diffuser, a smoothing nozzle (already attached upon arrival), and a third nozzle with really short teeth which is not described in the manual. You change out the nozzles by simply popping them off and on. They have a tight grip so don’t be afraid. You’ll think you are going to break something, but you won’t.

About the noise … yeah, it is loud. Quite loud in my opinion. I’d say it’s twice as loud as my old hair dryer. It is definitely NOT the low noise variety as advertised. But, I’ll follow that with, the noise level is definitely not worth overlooking this dryer. My curls are crazy bouncy and not one frizzy, belligerent hair is out of place.

The heat…. It is definitely hot. Depending on the setting you choose , hotter than hot!! If you were not using heat protectant already, you will definitely want it with this one. At just 75C, it was nearly too hot for my hand that was scrunching the hair as it dried.

Overall, I’m giving this hair dryer 5 stars but would give 10 if I could. There’s only one other product I’ve found in the last five years that I’ve been this excited about and I found it here on Amazon too! But that’s in another review, and non-hair related. I highly recommend you grab some heat protectant and this dryer, especially if you are a curly girl/guy, and you will be as excessively pleased as I am.

title: Very interesting but frustrating and not the best quality out there for these devices
text:
The AotBlcer Ear Cleaner Camera 1920P FHD compatible with iOS and Android works well and is very fascinating. There are other brands I would recommend first due to their better lighting and camera image quality.

Charge before attempting to connect through WiFi (not Bluetooth) to your device because it won’t show up on the WiFi device list until it is able to be turned on. It does not arrive charged. I read the instructions but I automatically gravitate toward the bluetooth list when connecting wireless devices so thought it wasn’t working at all until I realized I was in bluetooth not WiFi. So, be sure to thoroughly read the instructions for connecting the device and have them handy while connecting. It creates it’s own WiFi connection. It does not connect to your home WiFi. The included user manual is detailed with step by step instructions for setup and has a QR code to scan so you can easily find and download the compatible app. A small troubleshooting section is included in the manual but it provides no point of contact should your troubleshooting efforts fail.

This kit does NOT come with a convenient carry case to keep all the components together in one place. It does have a small plastic container with an easy, and securely fitting, push/pull on/off lid big enough only to hold all the plastic ear spoon attachments that go on the end of the scope. The ear cleaning tools are a lightweight metal and come in a small cellophane baggie with the adhesive strip to reseal (until the adhesive wears out or the thin cellophane bag tears, which won’t take long, and no longer holds anything). The scope itself is very lightweight and does have a nice matching lid to slide over the scope wand. You can always place the kit back into the original box but it too is not going to hold up to regular use over time. You might want to look into finding a small pouch to keep it all together, as I will. It charges by a very, very short (about 6 inches long) USB type C cord. No wall charger port is included, just the USB cord is. A red indicator light comes on when connected to power for charging but goes off on it’s own after a couple minutes so it’s hard to know if it’s still charging or not. There’s no information provided in the user manual about how long to charge the device or what the lights mean while it is charging with exception of one line in the troubleshooting guide that says red light means charge the product. I charged the otoscope for 2 hours prior to first use. No other indicator light appeared to show if the device was fully charged or not.

Press and hold the on/off button a couple seconds to turn on. Just clicking it won’t turn it on but does turn it off. You will know it’s on when the light comes on in the end of the scope. Additionally, the LED power light blinks a lavender color while awaiting the WiFi connection. The scope will automatically shut off at 10 minutes of non-use.

The plastic spoon tips for the scope have different curvatures at the end. They easily slide on/off the metal end of the scope. It’s definitely possible that the spoon tip could come off inside the ear if you are using much pressure to scrape in the ear so be cautious. There are several metal ear cleaning tools provided which you would use much like a cotton swab but not while using the otoscope.

In use: The otoscope is fascinating. Within the app, where you will be watching live on the otoscope camera, be sure to change between right ear and left ear to get the best camera angle. I can’t stress enough how easily it will be to damage your eardrums with this device. You WILL see your eardrums. Very fascinating. But….sneeze or cough, bump your arm, twitch the wrong way, eardrum wrecked. You will want to cough or sneeze while the otoscope is inside your ear disturbing all the little hairs. Again, strong, strong caution is advised. I kept the scope very shallow to avoid the eardrum but could still see it very clearly. Also worth mentioning, the magnification is great so what is actually a very minuscule amount of earwax will look like a massive glob. You can use the attached plastic spoon to scrape using the camera to guide you but the angles are awkward and you will find yourself trying to tilt your phone to adjust the camera angle instead of moving the otoscope. This was frustrating but funny at the same time. It will take some practice getting used to it. The inside of the ear is incredibly sensitive so scraping with any of the plastic spoons or included metal devices is very uncomfortable and only took a couple minutes for it to become painful for me after only 5 minutes inside each ear. There’s no cleaning cloth included as with similar devices by other brands, but the instructions clearly tell you to clean with alcohol after use, prior to storing so no cloth is really not that big of a deal to me.

There are several other functions within the app such as taking photos and videos. Unfortunately, due to how sensitive my ears were, I will have to use the device several more times to try these other functions out. Honestly, I’m not in a huge hurry to make my ears that sore again yet but I’ll come back to let you know how it goes.

title: Excellent hydration assist device
text:
This little gadget has been a hydration life-saver. This flash is very bright and eye catching even if you aren’t looking at the bottle. The flash grabs your peripheral vision. It flashes every 30 minutes. It will reset the flash time interval to 30 minutes again when the bottle is tipped as if your drinking. So, keeping it set on a flat surface is important for accurate timing. It does not flash constantly after the 30 minute time. It flashes for as minute or two then resets again. This is handy for when you’re sleeping and protects the battery life.

For best results, keep the device facing you so your peripheral vision will catch the flash. It’s safe to be placed in the fridge if you’re going to be leaving it in your bottle while you leave the house or go to bed. Not freezer safe. The silicone band is very accommodating to bottle size and shrinks back to shape quickly when coming off a larger bottle and going back to a smaller one.

I wish it also gave audible cues but it has turned out to be more effective than I thought it would be just with the flash. Highly recommended for anyone who struggles with adequate hydration.

title: Great product! 4C natural hair
text: I have used this product twice.  I have 4c textured natural hair.  Have never used a hair straightener.  Used it at 370 degrees F.  Straightened relatively medium-sized sections of my hair in 2 passes.  Took me 20 minutes to finish my head.  Passes through so easily afterwards that I passed it through all my hair as I would with a regular hairbrush.  This is not recommended by the manufacturer btw, but I wanted to try it anyways.  Hair still has bounce afterwards and my ends are not stringy.  Look at this temp was between a blowout and flat hair straightener finish.  Heats up quickly (takes 5 minutes to fully get to temp).  You can feel the heat emanate from the brush as it heats to temp, but the black spokes do not get hot (only the ceramic portions).  Comes with 2 alligator clips that have amazing hold!  Did not need the glove provided to hold the product.  My only complaint is that the brush is hard to clean thoroughly when product in my hair materialized on the brush.  I had to use my pressurized keyboard cleaner to clean the crevices for my next use.  If the product came with a soft bristle brush with bristles long enough to reach the bottom of the brush, I would be completely satisfied with my product and give it 5 stars.  Would definitely recommend for straightening natural black hair.

title: Wow! Amazing!
text: I have cervical radiculopathy from a bulging disc in my neck and it contributes to my migraines. I was hopeful this would help, but had no idea just how great it would be. It not only massages and has great variation in intensity, but it also gets hot! It felt so great, I took it on my vacation to Kauai and used it on the flight. Really helpful device! Make sure you wet the electrodes and your neck. If you put it on dry, you will feel nothing. I had turned the signal up quite high thinking it wasn't working or wasn't very effective, took it off, used a wet washcloth to wet the electrodes and my neck, put it back on while it was cranked up high and my spine was shaking for hours later! WOW....it is powerful! Definitely adjust the intensity slowly and NOT until you have prepared the electrodes and neck and it's on your neck. I can handle a 4 intensity, 5 if my neck is really bad. And the high heat isn't going to burn you, but it can get uncomfortably hot after a little while.

title: Not the cheapest out there, but worked well for me
text: Four stars vs five simply based on price.  I've had rheumatoid arthritis for 20+ years, and it is now pretty severe.  I take weekly injectible medicine to help manage it.  For years I also took NSAIDs (prescription) twice a day to manage the inflammation and pain, until they finally caused an ulcer.  I've tried all sorts of things over the years to help manage the pain and stiffness I experience.  I'm always looking for non-medicinal options as well, as I don't like to take more medicine than necessary.  I had read a lot about turmeric as an anti-inflammatory over the years, and decided to give it a go.  I took two of these capsules in the morning, and two in the evening every day for a month.  Within the first week I started noticing a difference.  I wasn't having to take my NSAID prescription at all - the turmeric was helping my morning stiffness enough by itself.  That's not saying it miraculously eliminated all pain - but it was enough that I could back all the way off of the NSAIDs.  It's been a month now and I haven't taken the NSAID once!  Again, you need to have realistic expectations of an herbal supplement...it won't cure you.  It won't eliminate all pain.  But for me it was enough of a noticeable difference that I was able to stop taking a drug that was tearing up my stomach.  My RA doc said it was safe to take and he had no problems with me taking the turmeric  - he said if it worked for my pain, then I should take it.  He said some of his patients have great results with turmeric, while others notice no improvement.  I think every person's body is different, and the causes of inflammation/pain are different.  So will it work for you?  Only one way to find out.  Try it.  It worked for me.  But as you can see in the other review, it didn't work for that reviewer.  I liked that this formulation had a high MG count compared to others, and was certified organic.  I may have to switch to other brands over time due to price, but for now this is a staple in my daily supplement list.

title: Not easy to put together and a bit finicky
text:
We had a much older version of this chair that recently broke. Not willing to live without we ordered a slightly different one than this in the same brand, but when it didn't show up we were refunded and this was all that was in stock. Having had good luck with the brand previously we went for it even though it was quite a bit more expensive.

The truth is, it's hard to put together. The arms did not want to fit no matter what I did. In the end, as a 6'4" 220 pound man I had to push as hard as I could on one side while two members of my family pushed on the other in a particular direction in order to mount each arm. Even then it took a while to get it in place and we were all soaked in sweat. After each armrest was in place it was pretty easy, but there absolutely no way I could have pulled it off on my own.

Once we got it up and running, it would get stuck in it's "sensing" mode where it determines your body size and shape. It would go for 20 minutes and then start over for 20 more minutes. We were convinced it was broken for about a day. What we discovered is that you have to sit dead center with your legs in a certain position and stay pretty still, but after we figured that out it usually only goes into sensing mode for about the first 30-90 seconds after you turn it on.

So, all of that said, why is it still a 4*? Because it's straight up magic once it gets going. I wish it had each of the modes that my old one had, and honestly, the "stretch" mode is pretty weird the way it contorts your body, but the rest of the auto modes that are there hit all the right spots, with variable pressure, temperature and time through the menu, and the speakers are a nice upgrade from our old one.

If this one lasts as long as our last one did it'll be a worthy investment.

title: This is one POWERFUL hair dryer!
text:
This is the closest thing I’ve ever had to a “professional” hair dryer. After years of using low-powered, less-expensive models, this is really like moving up to the big leagues (aka “a salon”). The unit feels very sturdily built, and its 2000 watts of power produce an amazingly strong air flow. One of my favorite features is the multiple combination of settings — cool, warm and hot air PLUS high and low airflow settings. (A lot of models in this price range have only cool, hot/high and hot/low, with no warm setting. To avoid over-drying my hair, I like the warm setting!) There is also a “cool” button which you can press at any time, but you have to keep it pressed, so I find it’s much easier just to change the heat setting.

The concentrator attachment is fantastic. It stays firmly attached to the nozzle and can be adjusted to whatever angle works best for you; it really helps to focus the airflow exactly where you want it. I have short hair, so I’ll probably never use the diffuser or the comb, but for the sake of thoroughness, I had a friend try test them, and the report was that both attachments were study and worked exactly as they should. The comb attachment dried long hair quickly and smoothly.

Another really nice feature is the removable filter. My old dryers didn’t have that, so periodically I would have to clean all the hair and general airborne dust from the air-intake grate with a dry toothbrush. That’s not the hardest chore in the world, but having a removable filter is so much more convenient, and it gets the filter much cleaner so there are fewer tiny dust particles blowing around.

The main reason I ordered this model was because I wanted to try out the ionic feature. I *think* it helps tame those annoying flyaway hairs a little bit, but to be honest, I don’t think those negative ions live up to all the hype. Still, the dryer works incredibly well, so whatever small improvement the ionic feature might produce is icing on an already great cake.

One thing to keep in mind: this is not a small or lightweight hair dryer, so it might be a bit cumbersome or heavy for young kids or elderly folks. For everyone else, though, I think this dryer is an excellent choice, and the price ($49.99 at time of order) is quite reasonable compared to other brands with less power and fewer features.

5 stars!

title: Avoid This Fingerprint Magnet with a Streaky Plastic Top!
text:
FOUR-HOUR UPDATE:
I have never updated a product review after only a few hours to lower my rating, but felt honor-bound to do so in this case. What I thought was just an "average" quality product (3-4 stars) turned out to have a truly annoying flaw: the plastic on the lid is a major fingerprint magnet and, to make matters worse, the plastic itself has built-in distortions/defects that make it look really grimy. (I didn't notice the issue when I first unboxed the item during the day, but when I turned the lights on after dark, the plastic top looked like it had been passed around by a bunch of 4-year-olds who didn't wash their hands after eating birthday cake.)

It's hard to capture in photos, but I gave it a shot. Do you see that set of "tire tracks" on the left side of the lid? Those marks are distortions *in* the plastic; they literally cannot be cleaned off from either side. And all those smears and fingerprints on the rest of the lid? Those were left *after* I thoroughly cleaned the inside and outside of the lid with soapy water and a soft dish towel!

If you hate grimy-looking plastic (as I do), you should definitely avoid this product. I'm off to shop for a pill organizer with a textured, matte-plastic lid that won't show every finger mark!
---------------------------
ORIGINAL REVIEW:

Flexible large pill organizer, but nothing special

This is a generous-sized pill organizer with three interior boxes which can be used in a variety of ways.
However, since there are only 7 separate compartments in total, this would *not* be a good pill organizer for people who need to take different pills at different times of day.

Overall Quality: The plastic and the construction quality are slightly above average.

Price ($16.99 at time of order): Comparable to other large pill organizers

Size: I really like the overall size. It holds a lot of pills, but the overall footprint is small enough to be relatively unobtrusive on your bathroom counter or tucked into your top drawer.

Hinges: Like most pill organizers, there are no actual hinges on the main box or the interior mini-boxes; the plastic at the back of each box simply bends when you open and close it. The plastic seems to be good-quality, so I would expect it to last a long time before wearing out.

Open/Close Function: The compartments on the interior mini-boxes have little tabs to make opening them easier, and they have a decent click when you close them. The two clasps on the main box are average quality, close fairly securely and are easy to operate. I doubt the box will pop open unexpectedly.

Not Waterproof: The product description claims this pill box is waterproof. It is not. The main box has a one-piece silicone gasket which sits in a recess around the edge of the box. Submerging it for only 3 seconds resulted in plenty of water in the main compartment and also in a few of the interior boxes. This shouldn't be a major concern since most people don't intentionally submerge their pill box, but the "waterproof" claim is clearly a major exaggeration.

Bottom Line: This pill organizer does not stand out as above average, but if you like the overall size and interior configuration of the smaller containers, the product should last a reasonably long time.

title: Amazing charger. Really.
text:
This charger is amazing. It has recovered 2 old 7200 extended batteries for me. And when it charges it give them a solid trickle charge. Meaning: when you turn on your phone it is at 100% and stays there for about 2 hours, even after restarting. The phone is on all day and only gets down to 65 - 84% depending on use. Meaning: it takes a long time to charge a battery. Sometimes a whole day.
When you plug it in, the light will be pink (if you have the pins on the battery connected to the pins on the charger). Otherwise the light will be blue and you need to connect it properly so it is Pink. Now just let it charge as long as it needs to until it turns blue. It may take all day and night the first time. Note: This charger is for people who have 2 or more batteries. Otherwise it takes to long to charge 1 battery. However, you can charge a single battery over night and use it with whatever charge it reached in the morning. I am sure it will be enough for the day on an extended battery.

title: You get what you pay for (it's good and bad)
text:
The alternative of the leader loss that Braun (Oral B) offers, at $30, it's rather ridiculous and for me, with these generic replacement heads, impossible to go wrong.

Out of the 4 heads I received, the very first one snapped a little plastic ring inside the casing so it was useless in just one use. Maybe I pulled the thing too hard when changing heads, I don't know, nor do I care. Why? At this price I can afford to buy 9 more packs (36 brush heads in total!) and still save over the original, overpriced, similar nylon/plastic heads that Braun wants to overcharge me. This is a simple to manufacture, plastic and nylon bristle heads with a tiny plastic shaft inside. Why charge over $10 (nearly half what the whole electric brush, batteries AND head costs) for such a cheap to make item, it’s ridiculous. I figure it costs some 0.20 cents to make, and then Braun adds a surcharge of 9.80 for marketing and branding hype costs.

This replacement heads are the equivalent of forgoing expensive OEM inkjet ink cartridges with cheaper refill bottles at 1/10th of the cost. Sure, it's not the same quality and blah-blah-blah. But at this savings I don't care to pay that obscene extra to get the "real" deal.

I used to buy the original replacement heads, and they were so expensive, that they made me difficult to throw them away at the recommended intervals, which was not so good for my teeth, the latter should be main objective here.

My verdict? Get these. No doubt about it. Buy a bunch of packs and toss them on a monthly basis before they get a bit worn-out from proper use. Your teeth will thank you for the hygienic rotation, and your pocket will be glad too.

title: Great Felt Liner for Sorel Caribou Boots
text: I wanted a pair of good quality felt liners to replace the ones that came with my Sorel Caribou Pac Boots.  I didn't like the faux fur snow cuffs on the original liners.  It was hard to fit my pant cuffs down over the bulky snow cuffs, and I didn't like having to wear my pants tucked into the boots.  I checked with Sorel, to see if they had a replacement liner without the snow cuff.  They do offer a replacement, but is a combination wool/synthetic fiber material, and I only wanted wool.  These new liners are high quality, well made with good quality material. Stitching is excellent.  These liners are 8mm thick vs 9mm for the originals.  That doesn't seem to make a significant difference in how they fit on your feet, and they fit into your boots as easily as the originals.  I measured my foot per the instructions provided and used the sizing chart to pick the right size.  The size recommended on chart seemed a little small compared to my normal shoe size, but I read many reviews that said to go with the size on the chart, so that's what I did.  When I received the new liners, I compared them to the originals, and they are "exactly the same length and width."  Note: these liners are 10 inches high.  They exactly match the height of the original liners, "including the snow cuffs", so they stick up out of the boot about 2 inches.  That doesn't bother me, but if you want them to match the height of your boot, you should measure the height of your original liners, and order that height.  Believe they offer these liners in both 8 and10 inch heights.  A good quality liner at a fair price.  Received them quickly.  Very satisfied.

title: How to rid your Shrimp tank of Hydra
text:
Two different ways to do it, used both. For those that bought the packets and do not have a syringe, use a pinch for every 10 gallons. I used that method first, stirring the powder into a little aquarium water. Product will not dissolve, you will end up with stuff floating around coating everything. First dose, did nothing, next day Hydra fine, Shrimp mating in front of me, babies everywhere. Next day did second dose without a water change. Still nothing. If you want to be more exact, divide the packet into ten equal parts, each part is for a 10 gallon tank.

Next method, the better of the two but you will need a syringe. I did a 25% water change before using this method. Take 100ml of aquarium water, dump in one full packet and stir. 1ml per 10 gallon, repeat every 12hrs till Hydra gone. This way you get more of a dissolved solution. One dose seemed to do it. In my tank I had various kinds of shrimp and babies, rabbit, mystery, mts, and nerite snails, dwarf crayfish, guppy, various live plants. All did well. If they return I still have my solution ready.

Day five, no water change since the last dose, snails are showing signs of stress. Hydra gone, shrimp are fine. Will do a 30% water change and add new snails, I moved the others to another tank to bounce back.

Oh, watch for pH and Ammonia spikes, it may cause a mini cycle or spikes and a water change will be needed. I used Stress Zyme before using product and after water change.

text:
The circular geometry (ok, heptagon) is a much more compact shape for sliding into a pocket. Furthermore, the fact that the compartment door opening tabs are on the more protected inside of the heptagon oculus is a great solution because it greatly reduces the chance of accidental opening in the pocket (or purse). Furthermore, since the hinge material is along the longer side of the compartment lid on the outside edge, it should last a lot longer than if it were on the shorter side.

The days of the week do wear off, however, from bouncing around in my pocket. I don't particularly care, but others might. I just use the compartments sequentially and fill them on the same day each week. Since I use a daily alarm timer on my phone to remind me to take my pills, I find the system perfectly acceptable and will re-order them when the hinges finally do wear out. Since 3 of them came in the order, I don't expect that to happen any time soon.
