text: okay so I ordered this chair off of amazon from the cavilier store in Duluth ga.  extremely skeptical due to the co's extremely poor reviews both on amazon and the bbb. the company is very difficult to return contact and did have to go through amazon for response. however I received product in said time through R+L carriers, who were great to work with. okay the chair. size! I live in a very old house where the doors are smaller 32". front door. I had maybe 1/4 inch (with chair out of the box). trying to get it into my preferred room was almost a no go bc of the trim in the doorway, however after placing 2 towels on each side we were able to slide it ever so gently through the doorway. Easy to assemble, just 3 foot rest connections, the power cord and remote cord. powered on and cycled through. the remote is a bit confusing but you will figure it out.  Okay size - I am 5'7" 170lbs I would not recommend this for any larger of a person. it actually fits me like a glove, like custom made. air bags can be a bit intense but any less and ppl would be c/o it not being strong enough. you can adjust this pressure. the foot rest extends manually with out much effort, just push with your feet. only down fall with the foot rollers is they are stationary and remain in the central portion of your foot vs going all the way to your toes. the SL track goes from top of neck all the way down past your buttocks to upper leg, the heat works well. the blue tooth connects easily to my smart phone, however the audio isnt the greatest (its not a polk or bose system) but its a nice feature. for incoming or outgoing calls I can hear them but they can not hear me. possibly that is a feature I havent figured out yet and there is nothing in the owners manual touching on this subject.  it does have a control panel on the chair itself which is convenient.  the chair is comfortable, looks good, has a clean new smell to it. but its not real leather (but I wasnt expecting it would be). all and all for the all the functions and the price, its a nice chair. it had all the features I wanted for a affordable price. title: Powerful Natural Laxative!
text:
Do you research and don't over-do it!!

Generally used for people with IBS (Irritable Bowel Syndrome) or before a colonoscopy to help you eliminate your bowels within a time frame of 10-12 hours. Typically this process takes 24-48 hours to "clear" yourself.

My personal review of this product is, Woah! this is some powerful stuff. Senna's active constituents are Sennosides which act as a powerful natural laxative. I took this stuff before work the night before and oh boy what a mistake! While this stuff works and if completely effective, brace yourself if you take anything more than less than a half of a tablespoon. I didn't do this. I put it into a green smoothie and used about 2 tablespoons. I was in pain the next day using the bathroom probably 8 times and while the pain would subside for about an hour in between, the second I had some water, the pain would come right back. Besides all the pain, I can't deny that this stuff works. The taste by itself is super bitter but when mixed into my smoothie, I couldn't even taste it. All in all, I would recommend this product and buy it again but seeing as how I bought a pound of it, with how little the serving size it, it's going to take me quite a while to go through it.

title: Misleading Description, Poor Quality, Small and NOT Hypoallergenic!
text:
I was desperate to find a less expensive bandage. I've been spending more than half my monthly income (yes, half) on bandages for the last month and something has to give here, so I took a chance on these. What a disappointment!

Yes, the bandage is 2 x 3, but the pad area is about 1 x 1, much smaller than a name brand's pad normally is. The only thing that the package says is latex-free. There is nothing that says gentle or hypoallergenic the way that name brands, or even store brands do.

I've learned over the years the hard way that being just latex-free isn't enough. I am very allergic to most adhesives and only bandages marked gentle will not break me out.

I can use a store or no-name brand as long as they say they are gentle or hypoallergenic.

I took a chance and put one on my arm to see if it would bother me. I wasn't about to put it anywhere near my already-sensitive wound. About 10 minutes after I put it on, I started to itch.

Yes, they are cheap, with good reason. I should have been suspicious when the company didn't bother to show a photograph of the individual bandages.

The pad is ludicrously small in comparison to the adhesive area. There is no reason I can imagine to have it be that small.

When the price seems too good to be true, apparently it is. Now I have to go through the hassle of returning them. Amazon will pay for the return, but I have to find a way to get downtown to the UPS store to do it and wait to get my money back.

Shame on this company for misrepresenting this inferior product!!!

title: Very Strong Tooth Powder Could Also Be Used For Drawing Poultices Travel Size Container is 2 3/4 x 1 3/4
text:
It's going to be a little difficult to rate this product because there were some complications with it. I love the idea and that is why I rated it with 3 stars. The things in it are so good and important and needed for good oral health so when it was offered at a Discount for a thorough review I wanted to try it right away.

It wasn't sealed for some reason or another (it might have fallen en route somewhere) and that's just not something we're used to in the US we have PSA's telling us not to use anything that isn't sealed for safety. Then, when I went to open it and it fell out on me like flour the camphor and menthol was so strong that I had pulmonary issues and started coughing. I am admittedly sensitive to anything that is strong and I just hadn't imagined it being that amount. I would have been very happy with it if it was sealed and the density of essential oils had been titrated lower. Some may find this wonderful and love it because they don't have those sensitivities so I can totally appreciate the differences there. Doing everything all over again I would say that perhaps more could have been explained on the page about what it is and what it is not. There should be a warning on the label for people who have pulmonary issues or maybe hay fever or anything with allergies because it was just too potent for me. It's a difficult situation to be in because most places would barely put enough of something while this company put maybe a little too much, but that is subjective for me ... One can always double-up and add more powder to one's brush but if the powder is so strong already that it causes other issues then it's a little too far the other way maybe?

Because of what is in it and and what it does it would be great for so many other things, which is another reason why I got it. I'm sure it would help with a bug bite to draw it out like with a mosquito bite or a bee sting...

Pros:
Great list of items all together
Strong recipe (almost too strong for my allergies, but maybe perfect and generous for people without them).
Bamboo Charcoal is a real bonus, it has so many great properties
Small container is easily portable and wouldn't be counted at TSA in the infamous tiny baggies and is 2 3/4 H x 1 3/4 W
Breath Freshener
Clay and Charcoal are natural detoxifiers and i use them already
Kills bacteria, would leave the mouth fresh
Natural ingredients.
Charcoal isn't black in appearance so if it gets on you or your stuff it isn't hard to get off, doesn't stain.
Charcoal has a whitening effect on teeth.

Cons/Tips:
Not organic, but it is natural.
Oils are too strong/powerful for people with allergies, if you have strong sensitivities or MCS I'd say to avoid.
Redundant seal on the inside would have helped a lot.
Could mix this with baking soda or other charcoal to cut the power of it down and make it last longer perhaps
May want to use another natural product to help spread it around the mouth more easily, perhaps coconut oil.
An ingredient warning might be advisable on the label to advise users for those who may be sensitive or have loved ones who are.

title: Tried & true basic soap
text: Obviously I'm a fan of this soap, since I bought the 12 pack. This isn't a fancy or luxurious soap. It's a basic white lemon-scented puck in a cheap cardboard box. For reference, I'm a woman that shaves daily, and I live in a city with hard water. I shave in the shower, so I drop the puck into my enameled metal mug, set my brush on top, fill with hot water & let it soak for 5-15 minutes while I brush my teeth & do other stuff, until I'm ready to shave. Pour the water off, shake off the brush and go to town. I load the brush & skin lather. I get billows of slick lather, and this soap doesn't irritate my skin or dry it out. If you want to make a thicker lather, or if you've had trouble with Williams lather dissipating, try adding a tiny squirt (like 1/2 tsp.) of Dr. Bronner's liquid shave soap (the lemongrass lime compliments the Williams scent nicely) on top of your Williams puck & lather away. I don't care for Dr. Bronner's shave soap as a standalone product, but in trying to finish off my tube discovered this trick and I believe it does help stabilize the Williams lather. I also think Williams benefits greatly from a stiffer boar brush. I've actually had great luck with some of my cheapest, stiffest Burma Shave brushes. Williams is affordable, doesn't irritate my skin, and does what I need it to. I go through this faster than a man would, so I'm not sure how long this 12 pack will last me, but I will be repurchasing whenever I run out.

title: Effective and comfortable
text:
This is a very comprehensive kit; you get everything you might need to treat your teeth. Included are the whitening strips, a tube of pretty blue desensitizing gel, a toothbrush and cleaning powder.
I have to say that the strips are probably the most comfortable ones I have used - I was almost forgetting I had them on when my timer would remind me that the 30 minutes were up. I can’t tell you how truly effective these are at bleaching, because my teeth are light to begin with, but my I feel that the overall appearance is noticeably brighter and the surface of the teeth feels cleaner.

I truly love the toothbrush that comes with the kit! Even though I am a devout user of a sonic toothbrush, I’ve been reaching for this one daily. The bristles are thick and comfortable, but I wish the handle were a little longer.

I’m not crazy about the cleaning powder. I like how my teeth look and feel after having used it, but it is so messy! I find it very annoying that the surface of my countertop is always covered in white powder whenever I open the container. Btw, the best way to use the powder is to either wet your toothbrush first, or after you have applied a strip of your toothpaste, and then dip into the powder.

Overall, I like this whitening kit a lot, and I appreciate the thoughtfulness that went into creating this set. That said, it is on a more expensive side, which may deter some customers.

title: Very soft, ergonomic beard brush.
text:
This brush is (almost) perfect. The cruelty-free horsehair bristles are very soft, and don't scratch or irritate my relatively sensitive skin. The size is ideal: small enough to fit easily in the hand, but large enough to spread beard oil and balm quickly throughout a moderate goatee.

Because of the softness of the bristles, it's hard to tell if they makes enough contact UNDER THE BEARD to be effective at light exfoliation, or provide sufficient penetration through beard hairs to fully coat hairs below the top layer. I'm not saying it does or doesn't; just that it's really hard to tell because I can't feel the soft bristles on the skin underneath my beard. This isn't really a negative for me, but your mileage may vary.

Overall, if you have sensitive skin or a relatively soft beard, this is probably one of the best beard brushes on the market. It’s also very effective at spreading the brand’s dry oils without getting residue on my hands. The protective travel tin that it comes with is definitely an added bonus, too. I highly recommend this brush!

title: Tasty Candy. Hard not to eat too much
text:
The taste, at first, is great. However, if you have a sweet tooth, and havnt had any real sugar in a long time, you may be tempted to over indulge. I could easily have eaten a whole tube at a sitting. This would be a mistake on 2 levels.

There is some magical balance, where you can eat more than their specified serving and have no ill effects. However, if you have one too many, bam, your going to have some digestive tract issues that you may not enjoy. A few times I managed to tip over that balance, since i bought all 3 flavors. Speaking of which, I found that their various flavors are not terribly distinctive from each other.

The second level of mistake is that as you have more the flavor begins to wear on you. My wife ate too many right out of the chute, and now cannot stand the smell of these things. It took me about 2 tubes over a couple to get to that point where I felt obligated to eat them, having paid good money for them, but didnt really want them anymore. I like candy, so I would eat them again, were the presented. But its going to be a while before I would actively go buy any again.

I received the seat and the back one day and tried them out in my computer chair at home and was very uncomfortable.  The next day I tried them together in my car seat and in addition to the seat adjustments I had to make for the extra height and thickness, I was in more pain after my drive to work WITH the cushions, than without them.  I returned them both the very next day, and bought a 2" memory-foam dining chair cushion for $13.00 which works better for my pain. title: Rusty charcoal after a week's use? No!
text:
Hmmm... Charcoal shouldn't "rust." I boiled these koins/pieces as per the instructions. I placed 3 in my 17oz S'well bottle for travel. Over a week's time, I used the bottle & Kuro-Bo off/on. When not in use, I made sure the bottle was empty & tipped the bottle on its side so the charcoal could spread out & dry inside the opened bottle. On my trip home, I filled the bottle at an airport filling station; took a sip immediately & it tasted like iron. I thought it was an improper filter on the filling station, but didn't have time to empty & fill elsewhere, so I just didn't drink the water. When I got home & took out the charcoal koins, they were rusted! See photos.

No wonder my water tasted like iron. But how does charcoal have the ability to oxidize & rust? That isn't possible for true charcoal.

I boiled these 3 pieces to see if it was just a weird coating. Nothing changed. The photo shows the rusted pieces after a re-boil. I returned this product because rusty charcoal isn't safe at all!

And it ruined my S'well bottle. I've used bicarbonate +vinegar, and then just soaked in vinegar for 2 wks, but the bottle's stainless steel interior has permanent marks. Not scratches, but like corrosion. Oh, my!

title: Fabulous for giving Tramadol to a small dog!!
text: I've always been able to give meds to my animals up to and including cats until my very senior dachshund needed Tramadol.  It seriously must be the most bitter medication in the world.  We couldn't hide it in cheese, steak, or canned dog food.  Dachshunds are known for their sense of smell and they can smell these pills no matter what you try to hide them in.  Bless him, he is now deceased (at almost 19 yrs old) but he had teeth from the front all the way to his tail!  He never would bite us but he wouldn't open those jaws to save his live.  I ended up giving it transdermally on his ear until he died.  Now I have his 18 yrs old son requiring the med.  I guess when you live to be that old, you're entitled.  I never thought he'd be an issue as he ate everything.  Ha! Was I ever wrong.  He had the same great teeth as his dad and was just as stubborn.  During my reading on Amazon, I discovered these little jewels and man are they a life saver!!!  I take one of those pills, but it in half length length-wise and then put it in one of these capsules twice a day in a spoonful of canned dog food and zip it gets snarfed up.  He never even thinks about smelling, biting or tasting that pill.  If you have a small dog that is difficult to pill, these are the best thing since slice bread.  I bought a pill popper and haven't had to use it because these work so well.  The pill pockets he bit into so I plan on using these as long as he needs the Tramadol!

title: Antrolife BPM Worked Great Right Out Of The Box!
text:
I've had the arm cuff blood pressure monitors over the years due to my inheriting the genetics for high blood pressure so I like to check my overall blood pressure on a fairly regular basis even though I've been on high blood pressure meds for most of my adult life.
Here's what I like the most about this Antrolife Blood Pressure Monitor:
They really need to highlight in their description (not just in one of their many pictures that this device will operate in dual power modes, with the batteries or without batteries when you plug in the supplied USB type A/C power cord to the monitor and a charging port (either in you home or in your car) or as I did to test it out I plugged into my PC while writing this review.
I purchased a name brand (Omron) BPM years ago and the first thing I found out was that the cuff was on the small to medium size so I had to purchase their separate large cuff. So this was a big deal to me since with the Antrolife cuff it is considered a universal fit with the arm's circumferences ranging from 8.66" (22cm) to 16.54" (42cm) which runs from small to large. So for the people with larger arms you may want to measure prior to ordering but this cuff will fit the majority of individuals.
Their are some discrepancies between their user manual and Amazon webpage for their warranty and number of available readings you can store in memory so here they are: although their User Manual states that they have a 1 Year Worry-Free Warranty and any problems within 12 months result in a replacement or refund (they also have a folded insert in the box which makes it a little more confusing by stating a Mfg. Warranty of 1 year and an Extended Warranty of 3 years). Their Amazon page states that they provide a Worry Free Warranty of 36 month and in another location on the webpage it states an extended 36-month warranty (so I'm really confused by all of this change in wording) which covers almost anything (malfunction, measurement inaccuracy, mechanical damage, and much more) so if you meet their criteria then just contact them at by addressing your email to "support at Antrolife dot com". "You can get a free replacement or refund quickly and easily, just contact us", also with your warranty claim remember that you will need a copy of your Amazon order invoice and Amazon Order I.D..
As for the number of stored individual readings that can be stored in this monitor the manual states 2 x 90 the Amazon webpage states that it will hold up to 99 for each of the two individuals tracked on this monitor so it appears that the manual is just out of date vs their current sales literature and actually each of the contradictions have been improved upon between the User Manual and the Amazon webpage which is another Plus for picking this up. Also the soft storage carrying bag although a nice thought really needs to be a little bit larger to comfortably hold the device, the cuff, the usb type C power cord and the manuals (I like to keep everything together).
I also checked its' accuracy against another recent BPM that I acquired and both are within 2 digits apart from each other so I consider that very accurate for this BPM since it's hard to take 2 measurements with the same device and come up with the same exact numbers, it just doesn't happen that often.
Setting up the User as No. 1 or 2 and setting the Date, Time, Voice (On or Off) which uses someone with a female Chinese accent (personally I would have used a voice with a neutral accent but that is just me) and Unit of Measure went well although their instructions leave out a few details but it is easily figured out once you get started. The biggest drawback I can see with this device and honestly I don't understand is why you're asked to input the date and time into the device if they aren't displayed on their monitor either while taking your measurement or when you're thumbing through your past Memory listing (they do list them in numerical order starting with 1). Although I think they've got a great BPM device I would really like to know the day and time of each memory stored in this device so for me, although not an issue for everyone, had they included that information showing somewhere on the device I would have rated this with 5 Stars but I consider this a pretty big deal so that's why I removed one Star from my rating...
Would I still buy this, the answer is "Yes", mainly due to the dual power modes that makes it so very flexible to take on my trips and not worry about the batteries dying on me...

title: Very quiet, moves a lot of air
text:
This air purifier moves a lot of air. Setting it on auto adjusts the fan speed based on how 'dirty' the air is in the room. I'm not sure how the sensor works to determine air quality, but in my room it always shows around 10 and so it keeps the fan on setting one. I always forget that it's even running, plus the lights shut off after a few seconds making it even harder to tell if it's running. For me personally, I can't tell a difference in the air quality with it compared to without it. So is it actually doing anything? Well it is pulling air through the filter so it must be doing something. It's extremely lightweight and very easy to accidentally knock it over and the plastic does seem like it's cheap. I've also added lots of essential oil to the pad on top, but I can never smell it.

Pros-
It has to be filtering the air, at least somewhat.
Super quiet and lightweight.
Particle sensor to auto adjust the fan speed.
Comes with a filter.
Lights shut off after a few seconds, making it ideal for a bedroom.

Cons-
Feels cheap for the price.
Essential oil pad seems pointless, the bottom is solid plastic and I don't see how air would pass over it.
Either the particle sensor is a gimmick, or I just have really clean air in my entire home. I'm not sure on that one.

Overall for the price I can't really recommend this unit. There are much cheaper options that do the same as this unit just without the sensor and auto adjust function.

title: Beautiful Diffuser
text:
This is probably the most elegant diffuser you will ever buy. It is entirely made of glass - which is very unusual. It's heavy, and the top attaches by resting on the base. All the parts (including the inner section which is made of plastic) appear to be of very high quality.

If you have other diffusers you'll notice the absence of the LED light option. The only LED lights this unit has are on the button, but they do indicate what setting the unit is on, and I think that's very handy.

The diffuser puts off a nice stead stream of mist and the scent is good. I've noticed that scent doesn't last long or it's not very strong with some diffusers, and this is not the case with this one. It does have a constant or intermittent option.

The diffuser doesn't hold very much water compared to others, but it seems to last a very long time considering. I have mine in my living room which is large and open, but I think it might be better suited for a bedroom or smaller more enclosed room - this is not a flaw with this particular diffuser, it's a general rule with small ml capacity units.

I received this at a discount for my honest review, and it is probably the most expensive diffuser I've seen - especially for the size it is. BUT it's a higher quality item and made of higher quality materials. I do think it's worth the cost especially if you're looking for a gift to give someone. Diffusers tend to look like weird gourds made of cheap plastic, and this one absolutely doesn't. I would very much recommend this diffuser.

title: This is a very useful tool for communication if someone is on a ventilator.
text: I liked that the pictures were large and easy to see, applicable for patients on ventilators in the ICU, and covered with a laminate plastic that it is easy to sterilize. We ordered one for a loved one that went into septic shock from viral pneumonia who had to be intubated in the ICU. Viral Pneumonia will not respond to any modern medicine and the only thing to do is provide support. I am so grateful to the doctors and nurses in the ICU for providing that support and for the family and friends that prayed for our beloved patient. We chose this version of the chart based on the recommendation of a speech therapist office. Being able to communicate helps a patient to feel valued and safe because they can express their needs and interact with caregivers such as medical staff and family. The actual item did not arrive in time, and the hospital provided print outs of the images that were quite helpful. Our family was covered in prayer and God was very gracious, moving in observably powerful ways to our great relief and to the amazement of the attending doctors and nurses. His condition changed overnight in miraculous ways to the gratitude and suprise of his medical staff. We praise God in gratitude for His mercy and grace that our loved one recovered to quickly. We also donated the communication chart to the ICU after the patient recovered. I searched for an acrylic bed rail hanger to donate as well, but I was unsuccessful in locating one similar to the one in the picture or one that would do a similar job. I am very grateful for the images that assisted us in our time of need. I hope that the donated board will assist another family in their time of need so that we may share love with others in the way that God loves us. Thank you, and God bless you!

title: Works great to prevent slipping.
text:
I love Vibram soles, because the product is very durable and slip resistant. So many women's heels have slippery soles, and these are perfect for this problem. I glued them on with professional strength shoe adhesive. These do not have any glue/adhesive pre-approved. The extra step is well worth it though. The color of these are perfect for shoes with red bottoms. If you don't mind, they can be used on other colors, as it is not so noticable when you trim the excess off. When walking, it is not seen anyway. I had seen Vibram in other colors, but hard to find pre cut half soles for women's heels. These are a good price in comparison to other non slip soles. I have purchased lesser priced versions that have adhesives, and those tend to be temporary and fall off. The other types are less quality too. The Vibram soles are very strong and lasts longer. They do not wear down easily, so over the long run, are a good value. You can find many YouTube videos on how to properly add half soles to shoes. Just make sure you give yourself enough time to allow these to cure and dry. I do not recommend expecting these to be a quick solution to add at the last minute before an event. You will not have your shoes ready if you expect these to be a rush application. These are professional quality, and as said before require the right adhesive and drying time. You will not be disappointed if you followed the how to instructions on videos. Also, make sure you have the tools before trying to apply these,
because once glued, can damage the product if you have to take off and proposition or flatten the surface . If you don't feel confident with applying yourself, bring them to a cobbler to apply.

What is amazing about this is that it would normally take him a month or more to finish a project because he is easily side-tracked.

title: A good, comprehensive set...
text:
This little manicure pedicure makeup set is adorable. It's been in heavy rotation since the moment it arrived. I'll start with the nail portion, since that's where my polish-obsessed heart lies.

First, I was surprised by how solid and well-made the tools are. These aren't the cheap nail tools you sometimes find, that are warped or have rough edges. These are perfectly shaped and highly polished to a smooth finish.

Everyone in the house has used at least one set of the clippers. They both work well for a nice, clean cut on the first try. The set includes an ear pick, which I'd never use on my ear, because I don't trust that I'm coordinated enough not to hurt myself. It does, however, make a great tool for cleaning under the nails, as well as putting on rhinestones. There's also an acne needle, for which I feel similarly unqualified to use. It does, however, have a blackhead tool on the other end that I'd consider using.

I've used everything in the set, and my favorites are the scissors and the cuticle pusher. I reach for those most often. The scissors are sharp, and allow for precision in cutting hangnails, as well as decals and stickers. The cuticle pusher lays flat against the nail, so I can get a clean push back without lifting up the cuticle.

Now, the brushes were an exception, and I had an issue with them. They have soft bristles that feel good on the face. The problem I had was that all of them had stray and unruly bristles. That made for streaky application. I decided to take a chance and trim them, which helped tremendously. I still prefer round brushes to flat ones like these, for applying makeup, but, after my bit of doctoring, they provide easy even application of powder, shadow, and blush.

Overall, this is a nice set, and it looks really cute in my nail area. It includes lots of useful tools. Even though I had to do a little tweaking, it turned out well. It would be a great gift for any makeup lover.

I received this manicure and makeup set free to evaluate in exchange for my honest review. Any opinion I've expressed is purely mine and based on my own personal experience using this set.

title: Excellent but a few issues to be addressed
text:
Below are my likes and dislikes. Feel free to comment.

Likes:
1. Pistol is heavy duty and well made.
2. Weight is very close to a Glock 17.
3. Red and green lasers are pinpoint and brighter than I expected
4. Trigger is "close" to a Glock and adjustable but read the instructions first.
5. Magazine release is the extended version.
6. Weighted nonfunctional magazine is very close in weight to an actual full one (10 rounds).
6. Very addicting to practice with.

Dislikes:
1. Sights are black with NO white outline like factory Glock sights (this is a big problem).
2. The supplied magazine and factory Glock magazines fit a little sloppy in the grip.
3. Taking the top slide off is a pain... one pin was very stubborn coming out (quality control issue).
4. The pistol does not fit my Glock 17 holster made by Comp-Tac. Slide is slightly too wide. Fits the
Comp-Tac Glock 9mm "slide" version the best.
5. Trigger doesn't have the safety (2 triggers) like actual Glocks (no big deal).
6. The grip doesn't feel Glockish without the Glock SIDE checkering. It is smooth with recessed words SIRT on it.
7. No detailed instructions came with the pistol. There is a PDF file you can download but I had to search for it.

I immediately changed out the sights with factory ones. The rear sight on the SIRT can be pushed out with your fingers and the factory sights slid on the same way. NO TOOL or VISE is needed. May need glue to secure.

For the front sight replacement, you have to remove the top red slide by pushing out the 2 pins that hold the slide on. The front sight is glued on. There is NO NUT to unscrew. There is only hard RTV you have to scrape off on the underside then gently tap the sight out. Now you can install the factory Glock front sight with the small nut that comes with it. You can easily tighten the nut with a small needle nose pliers. YOU DO NOT NEED A GLOCK FRONT SIGHT TOOL. You only need the nut snug as there is no recoil. The nut has a self locking feature and won't back off. That's all there is to it!

Before you purchase this training pistol, read the "Customer Questions & Answers" below the Amazon reviews. You will see other customers as well as my questions and answers I posted earlier.

Bottom line... I really like this trainer pistol and wish the manufacturer would address the issues I noted above. Price is kind of steep to recommend to others. Maybe a cheaper version with the metal slide and only a red laser is in order?

title: Power Pearl Probiotic Brand Pros & Cons
text:
Pros:
+ Made in the USA
+ Vegetarian, Sugar Free, Preservative Free, GMO free, Nut free, wheat free, gluten free, Lactose free*, Chemical Free, Yeast Free, Soy Free, Iron Free, Artificial Color & Flavor Free.
+ Includes Prebiotics as well
+ Small “pearl” pills, easy to swallow
+ No refrigeration necessary
+ Small serving size for maintenance – only 1 per day
+ Tasteless & Odorless when swallowed

Cons:
- Not Indicated as from an FDA Registered/Certified Facility
- Not Indicated as from an NSF & GMP (Good Manufacturing Practice) Certified Facility
- *May Contain Trace Amounts of the Milk Protein Casein

Neutral:
~Probiotic Content (5 billion per pearl at time of manufacture)
~ Fair Price

I’ve been taking probiotic supplements daily for many years, so I can’t truly say that I’ve noticed any additional functional benefits from taking this brand over the other brands. However, I think this is a really great product for all of the above listed “Pros.” Not all brands also include prebiotics, and I think this is an important addition to probiotic supplementation. I love the small spherical pills, as the only other brands I have tried either come in larger capsule/powder or gummy form (tasty but more expensive, and lots of added sugars). I also love the smaller serving size for maintenance, as the previous brands I have used usually call for 3 per day (powder capsules) or 2 per day (gummies). The smaller "pearl" shaped pills are also a nice feature, for easy swallowing. For some reason I imagined a soft-gel type pearl, however, these are more of a hard round tablet. This brand is also a fair price, comparatively. Currently retailing on Amazon at just under $22 for a 2-month supply, compared to the $26 for a 2-month supply of the Probiotic Gummies I was previously taking. However, the powdered capsule brand I used to buy is as low as $7.19 for 200 pills. Regarding the probiotic content, this brand contains 5 billion per pearl at time of manufacture. I’ve seen this number as low as 500 million, to as high as 50 billion with other brands.

title: My physical therapist has this prone pillow. I love it.
text: My physical therapist has this exact product, which is why I wanted it.  It is very comfortable on the face, puts my neck into a neutral position that relieves pain, and I can breathe well.  Some reviewers have commented that they do not like the foam part by the chest, but I personally really like it.  It's like a cushion for my female chest and I think it's very comfortable.  Both cushions attach with velcro.  At physical therapy, I'm there for neck issues, so after doing the training program and exercises, they will put heat or ice on my neck with a TENS unit or comparable device.  Lying on my stomach instead of sitting up in a chair helps my muscles relax and get the full benefits of the modality.  Now I can do it at home after I complete physical therapy with my own ice pack and TENS unit.  I like to put my arms up on the sides by my head.  It's very comfortable, but I wouldn't want to lie on my face for any extended periods of time because of the pressure on my forehead.  You really start to feel it no matter what your face is in after 15 to 20 minutes.

I do believe people that are more average thin skinned, will find happiness with this mat.

title: Exactly what I was looking for.
text:
I've been wanting a simple solution for meals that doesn't require me to cook (because I'm lazy and hate grocery shopping) and has all the nutrients I need (because I tend to skip the veggies). I've tried Factor75 and Freshly but I found that I got tired of the meals after a few months and ended up wasting the meals AND DoorDashing way too often. Not economically friendly for a broke student. I also have a terrible habit of not eating all day (because I don't like breakfast and don't want anything in particular) until late evening, which results in me binge eating something unhealthy for dinner.

I've only had this for a few days, but it's helping break bad habits already. I'm not good at having meals at proper times, but now I just have Soylent whenever I wake up (unless I order coffee, then I'll have it afterwards). Honestly, it tastes like Bisquick pancake mix but thinner which is definitely not yummy but it's not as bad as many artificially flavored protein powders I've tried. (Gainful has been the best flavorless protein powder.)

I sleep too long to really schedule 3 meals a day, so I typically will only have this once and then have dinner. I honestly might try having Soylent twice a day and a light lunch/snack in between to avoid large meals altogether. I would only go to such an extreme because I am barely active at all since the pandemic started and I'm at my heaviest weight ever (I've always been overweight regardless but otherwise healthy). I'll update with any weight/loss, physiology changes if I notice any.

A second person tested this, and did notice a difference in her perfumes that had the same formula base, where some were made with and without glycerine.  So its very good for that.  Just be careful how it mixes in your perfume or you could get separation.

title: Best cleaner ever!
text:
I’ve been living in Japan since 2016, so when I came back and heard they stopped making the Cherry Blossom Pomegranate Lysol, I was upset. Pretty much everywhere you look, Cherry Blossom is everywhere in Japan. It’s very difficult trying to find anything Cherry Blossom scented in the United States. Even Japanese Cherry Blossom from BBW doesn’t really smell like Cherry Blossoms to me. I also love the Lilac scents that Glade, Mrs. Meyers, and Febreze have out. I don’t like that most floral scents have to be limited edition and seasonal scents. Great Value has a Japanese Cherry blossom spray that smells like cherry blossom 🌸 and similar to this cleaner. I doubt it’ll be our yearly, I’ve only seen it this Spring.

I ordered 3 bottles of this spray and all were packaged very well.
However, unfortunately some had spilled into the box. All 3 were not completely filled and there was some cleaner spilled in the box. I paid $30 for 3 bottles…that’s $10 a bottle. I think it’s worth it being they don’t sell this anymore anywhere, but they aren’t full bottles.
The original bottles I had were full. I still have an old bottle from 2015 and it had more cleaner than these came with. I keep hoping they bring these back, but for now I’m just going to hope and pray my husband is okay with me spending $30 on these again when I run out. 😬
I’m going to add water to help make it last longer because the bottles arrived half empty. It could also be due to the spray nozzle and when you overfill them, it can cause spillage.
I haven’t used them yet, so I’ll measure them on a scale before I use them and take photos of how much is in the bottles. If I remember, I’ll post more photos when I do.
I may just have to place an order once a month so I can stock up on it. I’ll be using it often anyways. It smells exactly like the original one, so I believe it’s the real deal. I understand the price is only high because they don’t make it anymore.

title: WORKS ON CAT PEE!!
text:
My female cat started marking/scenting on our laundry, I threw away a lot of clothes, sheets, towels, and blankets because I just couldn't get the horrible smell out...and if I made the mistake of washing the items that had cat pee on them with other clothes, the scent would transfer onto every item in the load! I had to throw a lot of items away and it was costing me a lot of money. I'm able to get the smell out now! I have a remarkably strong sense of smell. I can smell in layers...I swear I must've been a bloodhound in a past life, lol. I'm not able to pick up even a tiny trace of the scent now! If you've been wondering what could possibly work, this has been my method:
1. I do my best to locate the pee spot (using a black light if I have to) and spray it with Rocco & Roxie Professional Strength Stain & Odor Eliminator. I saturate the spot and let it sit for at least 15-20 mins.
2. I use Tide pods (2-3), a half scoop of Biz, a scoop of OxiClean, 3-4 scent pods (or a cap of scent beads), and 1/2 - 1 cup of Nature's Miracle Laundry Booster all together for one load.
(I know that sounds like a lot, but this is war and cast pee is a powerful enemy...nuke that stench!)
3. When the load is finished, sniff. Sniff it real good and deep. If it has even the tiniest hint of yucky cat pee, DON'T DRY!
You will need to wash again.
I was able to get the smell out of clothes that marinated in the pee for weeks. They smell so good now!
Good luck!

title: Most Effective Creatine Product, Excellent Value
text:
After trying several different supplements over the past two decades, I have been most pleased with the Body Fortress High Performance Creatine because of its efficacy and its price. Within a few days after starting to take this product, I am able to squeeze out a few additional reps to my heaviest upper body free weight sets. The effect appears disappear within a few days of ceasing to take the recommended daily serving. The only downside to this product (or any other creatine product for that matter) is that is does increase bodyweight by 1-2% almost immediately, presumably through the addition of water weight.

Unlike pure creatine alternatives, Body Fortress High Performance Creatine contains carbohydrates so each suggested serving will contain about 150 calories. Some nutritionists feel that carbohydrates provide a transport vehicle for the creatine molecule. While I have no way of scientifically verifying this, the product sure seems to work better than pure creatine. Additionally, it tastes far superior than pure creatine alternatives which effectively taste like sand. I find the product nice to take in the morning because of sweetness and the stimulant effect of taurine (i.e. key ingredient in Red Bull), which it also contains.

What is especially great about Body Fortress High Performance Creatine product is its extremely reasonable price at approximately $13 per giant container (~two month supply). You can get it at discount retailers such as Target or Wal-Mart for 1/3 the price of similar products at GNC or health clubs. Unfortunately, there doesn't appear to be much of an online retail channel at this time, except for eBay.

In short, this is the best value in creatine supplements if you can accept the additional calories.

title: Wipes: use them, but don't flush them.
text:
It's important for consumers to know that there is no US federal standard for "flushable". The manufactures set /guidelines/, but they are voluntary. The FTC and water quality groups don't believe the guidelines are clear enough and that definition should be a /standard/ (mandatory, not voluntary).
The result: some wipes marketed as flushable are very good, whereas others may clog your plumbing and damage septic or sewer systems.
When in doubt, put the used wipe in the trash.

Baby, facial, hand, and surface cleaning wipes are NEVER flushable- they are a different material

title: Great Lenses
text:
I wanted a pair of glasses weaker than my reading glasses to wear at the computer. I usually wear +1.25 for reading, so I went with +.50 for computer glasses, hoping they would be strong enough for my laptop which is fairly close, but weak enough to be able to also wear at my desktop computer which has a monitor that's further away. The strength worked out well for both purposes.

The lenses seem to be pretty good quality for the price I paid. The anti-reflective coating is the kind with the purple reflection, not the green reflection that expensive prescription eyeglasses have, but I expected that. Basically you want to be careful cleaning these because they will scratch more easily than non-coated lenses. There is a very slight tint to the lenses it's not bad though, it doesn't interfere with color, it just tones down bright whites. You might not even notice they're tinted without doing a side by side comparison with something white. I first tested these while sitting outdoors on an overcast day doing some paperwork and when I occasionally took them off I realized how harshly bright all my papers suddenly seemed. I've been testing these out all afternoon and evening with paperwork, for laptop use and now; sitting at my desk with a larger monitor, and there's definitely less eyestrain with them on in all cases. The +.50 strength (for me) is perfect to magnify ever so slightly to reduce tension but also weak enough that I can glance away from the computer without getting woozy from the blur.

The frames themselves, well, I have mixed thoughts on the frames. On the plus side, they're lightweight. They also have spring-hinge temples which is great if you tend to remove your glasses with one hand so they don't get bent out of shape. The color however, is so much worse than I was expecting and I'm really not very picky with glasses. I chose the yellow frames, primarily because I dislike seeing dark frames in my peripheral view. But my impression was that they were a matt, semi-translucent mellow yellow color. But they are not translucent at all and they are definitely not a mellow shade. They are a solid, pastel "Easter yellow" which when combined with the thick frames look totally absurd on my face. Not in a "cute nerdy" way either, but an exaggerated, costume, clown sort of way; with my eyes close to the bridge of the glasses giving an almost crossed-eyed appearance.

That being said, I plan to keep them because I live alone and plan to wear these at my home computer where no one ever sees me, and the lenses themselves are great, especially for the price. Oh, perhaps the best part of this purchase is the fantastic case they came in; it's a semi-hard zippered case which is exactly as pictured, along with a cleaning cloth. The case alone was worth what I paid, although I noticed the price on these glasses has increased since I ordered them. So despite looking like a clown in them, the lenses are great for computer use so they'll work out for my purposes.

title: Fabulous styler for flippy happy hair
text:
My white hair is delicate and easily scorched so I’m super careful with styling tools. Even my stylist singed my hair with a flat iron. That little mistake right by my face took a year to grow out.

When I say I have virtually every type of styling tool I’m not exaggerating but since I’m often changing my style I’ve accumulated things over many years.

This tool is fabulous. First, I would never use it on wet hair. In my opinion it is not designed to dry but to style. After rough drying my hair with just a dime size dab of smoothing cream I brush through, lightly spritz with a heat protectant and section my hair into 6 sections. The beauty of this brush is the curved shape. You must use the glove that comes with it or you’ll for certain burn your helping hand. Use reasonable size pieces at a time, too much and it will tangle. Position the brush close to your scalp and use your free hand to keep tension on the hair. Pull through to smooth and then again to flip it any way you want. You will not get pin straight hair with this like you would a flat iron. If you are looking for body with a bit of volume this is simply fabulous. I really like that there is a low heat setting which is perfect for my hair type.

I’m tempted to buy another to have a spare. Wish I had kept the receipt from the paddle style one I’d bought at a big box store so I could return as it’s inferior to this one.

I survived a massive stroke! I can walk again (with difficulty) and after 2+ years still have no use of my left hand and arm... and there are thousands of us!!! Some with the more common partial left side paralysis - and the rest with partial right side paralysis.
The throttle/braking system is strictly for use with the right hand, and the turn signals are strictly for use with the left hand - THE FULL CONTROLS CANNOT BE MODIFIED STRICTLY FOR USE BY A PERSON WITH THE FULL USE OF ONLY ONE HAND!!!

I would gladly pay a service fee for these necessary options/modifications; but the proof is in the pudding. These common sense options simply don't exist! If they did have these options, I would purchase one asap; but as it stands, I give it only one star and they have lost a potential customer.

title: Not worth the price, but good information.
text:
I purchased this DVD along with some cups from Amazon. I am a Massage Therapist looking to add cupping therapy to my current practice. This DVD provides the viewer with great tips including contraindications and specific conditions that benefit from massage cupping. The therapist demonstrates various techniques on each area of the body, which is very helpful to the beginner. However, I found that the majority of these techniques were instinctual to me; they made sense and they are exactly what I would have done anyway without even watching the video. I have been a massage therapist for 5 years, which is really not that long, but perhaps that is why the movements and techniques were common sense to me. For a beginner though, I could see the demonstrations being useful.

Overall I enjoy the video and its presentation. My biggest complaint, and the reason I didn't give it 5 stars, is that it is ridiculously expensive considering its content. I would recommend it for beginners who need the visual aid, but for others I suggest researching online for tips and techniques. Much cheaper that way!

text: I own 2 pairs of these; one with the brown lenses and one with the gray lenses.  I like them because they fit and look like "NORMAL" sunglasses.  I can wear them anywhere without feeling self-conscious, as they are NOT AT ALL like the goggle-type fit overs that make a person look like the cartoon character "Mr. Magoo"!!!  My friends have told me that they can't tell that these sunglasses are fit overs.  I also like them because they are lightweight and the side stems are thin enough so I have adequate peripheral vision while driving and changing lanes.  I've tried on a variety of other brands of fit over sunglasses.  Some I tried on at local stores.  And I ordered a few from Amazon (and promptly returned them because of the Mr. Magoo effect).  I tried the following brands:  Cocoons, Vistana, Fitovers, Jonathan Paul, SA106, and JuicyOrange.  None of them fit me and my driving needs as well as these fit overs that I bought from Florida Glasses.... AND they are a reasonable price to boot!!  They'd be nigh on perfect if the lenses would be a teensy bit darker.  While driving towards that eye-blasting setting sun, a person would want a really dark pair, ... but if they were THAT dark, they might then be too dark for regular sunny days.  (I do think the gray lenses have a tad darker effect than the brown).  Because these fit overs are the best I've found, I'm leaning toward purchasing a 3rd pair, ... just in case I lose a pair.  Yes, I recommend them!!  I like them a lot!!!

title: Works great for us as a couple. Very convenient.
text:
My girlfriend and I take a lot of supplements, and being busy working professionals, we welcomed the chance to save time in setting them out each day. This pill case is perfect for that. Since we take all our supplements once a day, the two sided design served more as a "his and hers" than night and morning, but either way, it's good to have. The compartments are large enough to fit many large capsules, as you see in the picture. The lids of them fit tight, and are a little hard to open at first, but I didn't consider that a drawback. The case seems to be of good quality material, and does not have a smell when it comes out of the packaging.

The pill cutter has a nice safety feature where it locks when not in use. This is particularly good if you have small kids, because the blade of it is very sharp, and the locking feature would prevent any accidents with fingers. When I first attempted to cut a medium sized Magnesium capsule, just to test it out, the top part of the pill cutter separated from the bottom part and flew across my kitchen. I'm not sure if it just wasn't secured tightly enough, or if it was operator error, but I put it back together (not difficult), and it successfully cut the capsule on the second try.

I was given this product at a discount in return for an honest review. In all, this bundle is a good deal, and I recommend it. Great for couples, anyone who takes supplements, or even older kids or teens who are capable of administering their own medication with some minor assistance.

title: Back on the Seventh Generation Band Wagon
text:
I really love these diapers. I have been purchasing chlorine free diapers for all three of my children since birth. I have had a love hate relationship with the traditional Seventh Generation diapers. They worked well for infants, but were a real disaster for toddlers, and for the price you may as well purchase their competitors diapers, and I have tried them all (Earth's Best, Nurtured by Nature, Naty, Honest Co.). Along came the Touch of Cloth, and I am back on the Seventh Generation band wagon. The review below is just for newborn and size 1.

Pros
-chlorine and fragrance free
-Made in USA
-great fit. Not bulky like Natty and similar and maybe even slimmer than Nurtured by Nature and Earth's Best
-Good fastners. Better than Nurtured by Nature, but maybe not as good as Honest or Naty. Traditional seventh generation diaper soften fell off once my kids were crawling.
-no leaks (so far only tested on newborn, but feel very similar to Naty which were great in all sizes for absorption). This was a real problem with the traditional Seventh Generation diapers once my kids were on the move.
-price compared to other chlorine free brands. Hopefully price stays competitive on Amazon subscribe and save. More recently we have been using Nurtured by Nature for the last year for my kids, but they had a huge price hike recently which prompted me to switch

Cons
-none yet, but waiting on my toddlers diapers to arrive, so I will review again once we try out size 4 and 5.

title: Lack of 5GHz Wifi support and Died before 6 months
text:
Overall it's a good scale but there are a couple things folks should be aware when purchasing this product:
1) The version I have (not sure if they have improved since) only supports 2.4GHz Wifi network. I had to figure out where my 2.4GHz can hit and unfortunately my bathroom is out of the range. I didn't want to by a Wifi extender just for this scale and I don't want to place it in the livingroom where the wifi router is. It's tricky.

2) After 5.5 months, the scale started to show "ERR" after you step off and after the "THINKING". I've searched online and noticed it's a very common problem. I contacted Fitbit support and after a few troubleshooting cycles, they decided to send me a new one. From other people say online, this is what happened to them, too. Fitbit just sends the replacement for this problem and they can't seem to find out why yet.

[NEW UPDATE] After 2 years, the device stopped syncing with my WIFI even if I tried several times to reset it. At the last step of pairing, it continues to say "WIFI ERR" even if my wifi is 2.4GHz and supports 802.1.b/g/n. I give up. Time for Bluetooth scale.

title: NOT as heavy-duty as implied -- good for light duty use only.
text:
The description claims "Strong enough to tolerate all residential household garbage and commercial waste." We bought these to bag up clean, dry cans to be recycled -- a school project. The clear feature was appealing for the end-of-year photo of all the cans that had been collected from the school cafeteria through the year, to be recycled in June.
We've done it in past years, and had no issues with the opaque bags we used for bagging up the cans to stack in a huge pyramid, take a photo, then transport to the recycling center. This year, switching to these clear ones has been a hair-tearing experience. Once loaded with cans, the bags start tearing with any handling at all. Because they're very large, they take some effort to hoist around, and almost every one started tearing open at some place when moved. Damage control has included double-bagging some, and use of packaging tape on others, just to keep the bags solid enough to make the final transfer to the recycling center. It's been a total pain, and these were not cheap. :(

title: Short hose, cheap quality, but great for arthritis sufferers
text:
Wow, why don't they market things like this in the US? Sure, we can buy them on Amazon, but I'd feel a little more comfortable buying them from a recognized brand, you know? That said, I've never used a better enema/douching system in my life. A pump! Finally a douche/enema system for those of us with arthritis! No more squeezing those tiny rubbery bulbs for me!

The materials are pretty cheap. The highest quality parts appear to be the nozzles, which are actually very comfortable for any sized adult orifice. Including three means fun for the whole family! (Or is that "hole family"?) The water flows well with each pump. The 600mL container holds way more than you'll probably ever want to pump into a single orifice at a time, but that's better than having to refill it 2 or 3 times. I was a bit disappointed by the pump top, which works ok but gives the impression that it will be the first part to die.

The most disappointing thing for me was the length of the hose. With the nozzle "installed" in back, the hose is too short to place the bottle in front when lying on my side, so I have to set it on my hip. The device appears to use standard medical-use plastic tubing, such as for nebulizers and oxygen tanks, but the end that connects to the pump bottle is square, not round, making it impossible to simply replace with off-the-shelf medical tubing. I'm looking into adding a coupling and another extension of hose to make it easier to use, but haven't done so at this point.

In the end (get it?) there's not really much else to say. It works well, all things considered, but the length of the hose means 1 star deducted. And the quality of the item makes me think it really will not hold up for a long time if used regularly. For that reason, I deduct another 1/2 star, with a final rating of 3.5 stars, rounded to 4.

title: A More Peaceful Sleep
text:
I work nights so when I'm trying to sleep during the day there are lots of daytime noises that keep me awake, or wake me up mid-sleep even in my relatively quiet neighborhood - trash trucks, dogs, lawnmowers, obnoxiously cheerful birds...that sort of stuff. This unit was recommend my several of my fellow vampire coworkers (all nurses). I was a bit hesitant because of the price - I had tried several digital white noise and nature sound machines, several apps on my phone, a window AC unit, and an oscillating fan. I can't get to sleep with the digital machines and the apps because they typically rely on a loop of noise that I always end up hearing where it's seamed together which then drives me crazy. The window AC actually works great, but it's not practical unless it's hot outside, and the fan was useless. So after a string of sleepless nights I finally bit the bullet and pick up the Dohm and am extremely glad I did.

The unit is very customizable to whatever volume and pitch of noise you need. By rotating the two different sets of slits you can change the pitch, tone, and volume of air the flows through the machine until you find what's exactly what's right for you. Because the noise is generated mechanically, there's no looping of sound files and low quality samples output through phone speakers. There is a dual-speed option out there for a little more money, but from my own research and talking to the nurses that had recommended the unit there's very little need for the lower speed that is available with the more expensive unit. None of the other users or reviewers found any need to make the unit any quieter than what could be customized on this single speed unit. In short, the Dohm has drastically improved my quality of sleep and made me a happier person.

title: Perfect for me
text:
Quite simply, this product works very well for an apartment dweller, person who enjoys quiet or a grad student. If you enjoy or need white noise or the sound of a fan to focus, but you lack a proper sound system and a fan would be too chilly in the winter--try this product.

I recently moved into a very old apartment building where the walls and windows are extremely thin. I listened to my neighbors shout and others manage to sound like a full-on zombie chorus until I could not take it anymore. I was rescued from the chaos of the cafeteria, shopping mall and frat party to relax in TRANQUILITY at last, for $40!
-------------------------------------------------------
My personal experiences in detail:

What the Dohm-SS does not drown out:
My neighbor's noisy truck or its beeping sound, neighbor tramping up the stairs, slamming doors, sirens (obviously and fortunately!)

What the Dohm-SS DOES drown out:
outdoor voices, indoor voices, outdoor college parties 1200 yards away, my downstairs neighbor's techno music, most construction sounds

Keep in mind that I can hear everything that my neighbors do, especially if it involves the stairs, but at least now their ruckus is silent or muffled.

If I were to purchase 3 of of these they would totally block out all noise, if that were my objective. As it is, one Dohm-SS is sufficient to provide solace for a moderate sized bedroom. I position the Dohm as far away from me as possible at night, either near the door or the window. I am a fan of peace and quiet and now I've a much better option that wearing ear plugs--hooray!

-------------------------------------------------------------
Good for: dorms, apartment dwellers, people sensitive to noise, students, test taking, privacy, people with attention difficulties

It's easy to set up. Plug it in and adjust the holes on the top so that the sound is pleasing to your ear.

In short, I do not regret spending my hard earned cash on this sound conditioner. Enjoy the wave of tranquility it brings and kiss goodbye the majority of the discordant shrieks, moans and raucous noise of your neighbors!

title: Not perfect
text: Prior to this purchase, I've been using a soft-bristle Colgate brush - which has stayed in good shape for so long that at this point I feel like it might be eternal and I just need to switch already. I figured that switching to something more environmentally-friendly is a good idea, and this was my first pick because the handle seems more comfortable than some other wooden brushes (it's more rounded on the sides). However, since I'm switching to this from a toothbrush that I thought was amazing in every way besides it being made from plastic, my toothbrush expectations are pretty high now. I've read some comments that said it takes some time to get used to a wooden brush and I think it's because wooden brushes are shaped slightly differently (more flat, more rectangular). It might be a bit weird for some people, but also not that big of a deal. However, the wooden part could've been better in this version if it was smoothed out just a tiny bit more. I mean, I don't think I'd get a splinter from using this brush, but there is quite a bit of room for improvement in this regard. The more important aspect are the actual bristles. They're just not as soft as the ones on my old brush. And when you look at them you can see that some weren't even cut like they were supposed to in order to get that soft effect. The bristles themselves might also be a bit thicker. So overall, the brush works, and this pack has a whole 10 of them so it will last me a while, but I hope to find something better next time I'm purchasing brushes.

title: Magic Wands are NOT Real!
text:
If Amega Global, or any wand developer, has discovered nothing more than a way to detect and measure zero point energy it would be a Nobel Prize worthy accomplishment. The ability to harness and control zero point energy, let alone all the profound benefits attributed to it, would be tantamount to harnessing and controlling gravity. It would be the single greatest scientific breakthrough in human history. And there would be at least one double-blinded, clinical study to validate it.

According to Amega and other wand producers, ZPE somehow promotes cellular repair by "reminding" our cells to "return to source". That is, their original, undamaged, pristine state. This begs the question, why does Zero Point Energy only contribute to repairing cells we can't see? Why doesn't zero point energy repair skin cells of burn victims or those with eczema, psoriasis or acne? Why doesn't it reverse cataracts, or return the scalp cells of balding men back to "source"? In fact, the only demonstrations we are ever presented are subjective, where the subject rates their pain from 1 to 10, and the injury is internal where we must only assume "cellular repair" actually took place. This is somewhat similar to charlatans like Peter Popoff and Benny Hinn who routinely heal trick hips and bad backs, but who can never seem to find any clinically blind, quadriplegic or stage-4 cancer patients in their audience, in spite of the hundreds that attended.

Instead of demonstrating the miraculous powers of these wands on citrus fruits, old dogs or people with a headache, as you will find all over YouTube, why don't they send free wands to stage four cancer sufferers who are under hospice care and have ceased all anti-cancer treatment? That way there would be no doubt what caused their cancer to go into remission, they could save thousands of lives and end tremendous suffering, and these wand purveyors would heroically be front page news all over the world. And there would be a multi-billion dollar bidding war among pharmaceutical companies for the rights to this technology, and hundreds of new jobs created to dig the ten mile deep hole for them to bury it in.

For the record, I have performed extensive research into ZPE wands, specifically Amega Global's AMWand, including blind field testing. You can read the results in the Alert section of our website (which you'll have to search for as URLs external to Amazon are not allowed here).

Len Clements
Founder & CEO
MarketWave, Inc.

title: I'd like to give it zero stars.
text:
Totally inadequate. Falling apart. It comes with no directions, so the first night after it arrived, I was struggling with it, trying to figure out which strap goes where, and how to put it on. I couldn't quite figure it out, so decided to put it aside, and try again in the morning. Then when I looked at the chin strap in the morning, I noticed that it was already falling apart, because of the stretching when I tried to put it on the first time. It had begun to rip near the seam in the part that goes directly under the chin. And on both sides of that seam, the cloth which had originally been glued to a foam rubber material on both sides, had now become detached on both sides.

The general design, the way the straps wrap around the head to secure the chin, seems good. But this device needs to be made of far more robust materials, so that it is not easily destroyed by just a little bit of stretching.
----------------------------------------------
Addendum, Jan 7, 2018: After buying and trying out a more robust chin strap that follows this general design, with one strap going over the top of the head and the other wrapping around behind the head, I am now of the strong opinion that none of these anti-snore chin straps are likely to work well, because the whole idea of the design is wrong to begin with. The fatal flaw is that they all pull your chin in the general direction of your ears. And that's where the hinge of your jaw is. This hinge is the TMJ (temporomandibular joint), and it is right in front of your ear canal. If the strap pulls your chin in this direction, it will produce no torque whatsoever to close your jaw. In order to produce any torque that would help keep your mouth closed, the force exerted on the chin should be tilted further up toward the nose.

I have also explained all this in a review I posted yesterday for that more robust chin strap that I just mentioned. Here's a link to that review:
Why anti-snore chin straps don't work

title: WORTH A TRY! IF YOU GIVE IT A CHANCE!
text:
This inhaler does exactly what it is meant for...There are some that have mentioned a clay taste when first using it. Which it very well may be from the manufacturing process of the inhaler. There is an easy way to rectify that issue though, all you have to do is rinse it out with water before your first use and make sure that it is completely dry before adding your salt. It should be a good practice to rinse anything that you may be inhaling, eating, or applying on yourself anyways.

I purchased this for my fiance who has COPD and allergies. It has definitely helped his breathing, the hardest issue is just reminding him to use it since it is something new to him. The best times to get him to use it is in the morning when he is sitting watching the news. So he can just drink his coffee and use his inhaler. Then at night again right before bed when he is sitting in bed watching tv. I am hoping that the benefits will only get better, but they are definitely showing some promise.

Also don't expect this to work overnight! That is just not how this works, time before you notice any benefits can vary from person to person. So make sure you give it a chance to work. It is not an alternative to your Dr. ordered meds, but it has reduced my fiances use....I did not get this in trade for a review, I bought this and wanted to give an honest review ; )

Also key thing here when ordering salt either purchase refill from same company or order VERY COARSE SALT otherwise anything smaller will be too small. I made that mistake myself so I am making you aware of that, the medium coarse was even too small.

title: Great mask. Could use little improvement.
text:
The mask arrived two days late. This is not the biggest problem. However, when I order something with "Prime" I typically expect it on time.

The mask is very comfortable. The adjustable ear loops are great. Allowing you to adjust the fit makes this mask the best I have worn so far.

Improvements could be made. The mask has no nose bar. This means my glasses are steaming up. I feel they could very easily add a nose bar. I will probably buy and add a nose bar. I feel this would make the mask perfect.

The mask is big. I ordered the XL because I am a big man. It covers most of my face and looks a little odd. If I order again I am going to try a regular adult size.

Another improvement I would ask for is a break away clip on the strap. I saw they put one on their child's mask. I work in a factory that requires mask. However, I am affraid I will not be able to wear it because of strangulation risk around machinery.

I would recommend this mask 100% if the fact that it does not have a nose bar doesn't bother you.

The instructions pamphlet with the Back Knobber is a a little more complete. The device itself is easier for me to use. I can get better leverage. I like the way it comes apart for travel--I keep it at work where co-workers borrow it. The Theracane is also decent--the side knobs make for a more stable and gentle application to neck pressure points.

I figure I have already saved enough on chiropractic visits to pay for them both. Applying self pressure only works effectively with a tool such as either of these. I use the one at work when listening during an e-meeting, and the one at home during the evening news. Use of the devices is most effective during a regular relaxation time. I have also become very aware of my posture and am improving that so bad habits stop contributing to knots.

title: Easy to setup.  Simple and functional design
text:
[[VIDEOID:9607faec4f5f31e5ce2871d461dc97b2]] Bottom line ups front: This a great simple scale that looks great in my bathroom. The scale was easy to set up and works great. If you are looking for something that is simple and straightforward in a scale, this would be a good one to try.

I wanted to get a scale for the master bathroom that my husband and I could use. I had a lot of options to choose from but I didn’t want something that was complicated or confusing to use. Something that I could simply just step on and it would tell me my current weight. I saw this scale and decided to give it a try. The following are my thoughts regarding this product.

**Pros
1. Easy to use - All you essentially need to do is insert the batteries and that is it. The scale turns on and all you need to do then is step on the scale. There is an option in the back of the scale to choose the whether you want the display in pounds or kilograms.
2. Design - The design of the scale is very nice. The scale is made out of glass and has line print around the border of the scale. The design is simple enough that it would fit in a lot of different decor and its streamline design allows you to place the scale in your bathroom without taking up a lot of room. Another nice feature is the the LCD screen that displays your weight lights up to show you weight even in low light.

**Cons
1. I do not really have a con regarding this product. The only thing that you do have to keep in mind is that there is a weight limit to the scale so if you do weight 400+ pounds, this scale will not be able to register and provide you your weight.

Disclaimer: I did receive this product at a discount however this does not influence my review of this item in anyway. I do come back and update my review if the there is anything that I missed that was not identified in my initial review.

title: (Edit: Was) Accurate & cheap! / updated with two year retrospective
text:
This is a two/three year retrospective review, I original bought the product July 9, 2013. The scale was also $12 at the time so keep that in mind.

The scale has been used 2 ~ 3 times a week for the past couple years and has become more and more inaccurate. It's always around 5 pounds the right weight but will take 2~3 attempts to get an average weight. Ex. If you're 150 the scale will occasionally report 145 or 155, this is without touching the zeroing slider at the bottom. You can be at 0, get on the scale and get off and the zeroing will be changed to -2, 4, -5, 5, etc... Simply tapping the scale (either on the sides or top) will change the zeroing.

While the scale "works" for the most part, it was not built to last more then a year and a half. If this had started happening five years in I would have been disappointed but not mad due to the price. For $12 it's ok and I think 3 stars if fair for a product that was not desinged to last but you're better off buying something better (more expensive) that will last longer.

title: This stuff is amazing for magic noodles
text:
MAGIC SPAGHETTI NOODLES RECIPE: You can combine nearly any kind of protein (beef, chicken, protein powders, hard boiled eggs) (about 4 - 4.5oz of it. I used {drained} canned chicken, eggyolk powder, collagen hydrolysate, whey protein isolate, in various combinations, but mostly the canned chicken), optionally spices (I use a little bit of garlic/onion/paprika powders) -- anything that "can be liquified" is the key here -- in a high speed blender for about 2-3 minutes, then (while running) add 1/2 tsp xanthan gum blend another 30sec then (while running) add 1 Tbsp sodium alginate blend another 1 minute then pour into those 16oz condiment bottles, tap bottom on counter to inspire any air bubbles to rise, put in fridge for a little while. Cut the bottle spout so it's fatter.

When it's time to make the noodles: Put 1 to 1.5 Tbsp of calcium lactate into 7 cups water in biggest bowl you have and stir until dissolved. (If having issue with that, put in blender and run on high for a bit till dissolved -- the heat of agitation will help -- then pour in bowl. Be sure to wash out blender right after doing either of these things with it!!). Slowly spin the water (I used chopstick in center of bowl for this), then gently squeeze from your bottle, the batter into the water moving fast near sides of bowl. It forms into noodles. Get them thick enough to be spaghetti noodles. Squeeze evenly. Stop now and then (or cut later). Experience improves the result. :-) When you run out of room, put them in another bowl temporarily and keep going until you are out of batter. Then put all the noodles in the water, add lid and put in fridge for a few hours to fully finish firming up. These can then be stored either in that water or without it for about a week. This is just like regular spaghetti pasta, it's freaky magic (molecular gastronomy).

This sodium alginate is a key ingredient. Works great.

title: Jet Lag? Get Dohm! But be sure to get a power converter.
text:
I recently bought this because my wife wakes up at the slightest noise at night, I figured this would help her sleep. We just got back to Turkey from the US and I remembered that a steward recommended this to help you sleep when on international trips. Boy was she right. It is AMAZING.

I was completely unable to sleep before I turned this baby on--three nights of sleeplessness. Then all of a sudden I was sleeping like a baby. I couldn't recommend this more strongly. It's really amazing.

I have two other comments:
1) Don't buy the more expensive multi-speed, the device is made so you can adjust the volume by simply twisting the side. That is all you need.
2) It's recommended for international travellers, but it doesn't accept universal power input--it will not work with European voltage. What are they thinking? Is it that hard to make a special unit for the international traveller? They could slap another 30 bucks on the price and it would be worth it. Fortunately as an American living in Turkey I already had a converter, but if you don't have one you better get one before travelling.

So buy this now, and be sure to buy a converter as well. When I listen to the noise I would never believe it would work, but now both me and my wife are devotees--and not just because now I can go to the bathroom without waking my wife.
