Upon recommendation from a good friend I bought this solution immediately. I was really scared to use it initially because you have to follow the instructions exactly. If you put the contacts in your eye too early then you'll burn your eyeball and that doesn't sound like fun.

The first time I used it I left it in the solution for over 8 hours. It felt really good putting them in. I didn't have to wash them off or anything. They felt amazing the rest of the day.

I think the problem I must have been having is too much protein build up on the lenses. It was irritating my eye and the other cleaner was obviously not doing it's job.

This product has extended the life of my contacts by weeks. I don't have to throw them out in the middle of the day because I get frustrated with the feeling anymore.

The only sucky part is how fast you go through a bottle. You have to refill a large case every single time. This is going to be a bigger investment than I made in the past...but after weighing the options and realizing that my eye health is really, really, really important to me I can't really put a price tag on this stuff. It helps me to go about my day with comfort and I no longer feel like I actually have a foreign object stuck in there.

I highly recommend this. Do right by your eyes and switch over.

title: Love my Cove
text:
Before June 2021, I was a championship sleeper. I could sleep anywhere, anytime. That June, I lost my mother, whom I loved more than any person ever. The trauma didn’t really affect my sleep until a few months later (and obviously immediately after I had sleep issues).

Starting in September, I started having horrendous insomnia events, as well as horrible anxiety attacks right after my mom’s passing.

I tried every sleep aid known to man, including pills, but I had so much trouble turning my brain off. Finally, after finding Cove, despite the ridiculously expensive price, I took the plunge, I had to try it. Not being able to sleep was pushing me towards depression.

The crazy thing is, THE FIRST NIGHT, after the first use of my Cove, I slept through the night. Now, I don’t know if it was the lack of sleep from the other nights before using it catching up to me or a placebo effect. But I was shocked. Granted, I did not start low level like they suggest, I’ve had my Cove on level 8 since the day I got it.

That being said, every night that I use it, I’d say 90% of the time I’ve been using it since when I received it Late January 2022, I sleep through the night. I don’t understand how it works, and I’m sure it might not work that well for everyone, but it’s crazy how much Cove has helped me. When I feel like an anxiety attack might be coming on, I use it then as well, seems to calm me down somewhat.

The only negative for the Cove is the price, even if it was half the price it would still be a crazy price. But like I said, I was willing to try anything to try to get some sanity back into my life. And for ME, it’s working. What is somewhat getting your life back, worth to someone ? It works for ME, I can’t guarantee it’ll work for you. But as a $500 blind buy, it’s really helped me. I’m just amazed what it’s done for me.

title: "Cure" for Crohn's Disease!
text:
Well, there really isn't a cure yet, but Boost Plus helped my son go into (and stay in) remission from his Crohn's Disease. In Europe, and many parts of the world, Crohn's isn't treated with drugs as much as in the USA. Other countries prescribe "nutrition therapy," whereby solid foods are eliminated and a liquid sludge is mechanically pumped into the stomach via a nasal feeding tube. The sludge has all of the nutrients required by a person, including proteins and vitamins, etc. Unfortunately, the sludge is not palatable and many people report that they cannot stand the taste.

Hence, we tried a Boost Plus liquid regiment. Our son drank 7 of these per day for a couple of months, and the drugs were all eventually eliminated. We now continue the mostly-Boost diet, and only have added some safe foods for a rescue from the monotonous repetition of the liquid diet. The Boost has led to an accelerated growth rate (getting close to normal), and has allowed for healing of the GI track due to being gentle on the system. Our son also likes the taste better than alternative formulas (hence we buy these bulk Brikpaks).

We, of course, worked with our doctor and GI specialist, and have been on this plan for about six months now. If you or a family member are suffering from Crohn's or a similar GI condition, this therapy should be a consideration, as it is easy and effective.

I am not a doctor, so please do not consider this to be medical advice. I am simply a cautiously optimistic parent whose son is thankfully in remission from a nasty disease. Good luck, and please feel free to comment on this with your own experiences with similar conditions and/or treatments. RR

*** 2017 Update ***
After a year on the "mostly-Boost" regiment, our son did start to get some relapses of his Crohn's conditions (after trying to drop the percentage to 50% Boost). We now administer a bi-weekly immuno-suppressant but we continue the partial Boost diet for helping to keep his growth maximized. We are still happy we tried the all-Boost diet, but it became impractical after a while to keep him on an 80 to 100% diet.

text:
Disclaimer: I was offered a discount on ' Bitter Melon Capsules / Karela Capsules / Karela Jamun Capsules / Bitter Gourd Capsules / Momordica Charantia Capsules - 60 Capsules (500 Mg Each) - Apollo Pharmacy (1 Bottle - 60 Veg Capsules)' from Apollo in exchange for a fair and honest review. Disclaimer over, onward to the review:

Pros:

- Easy to swallow capsules

- Claims to be free from pesticides and heavy metals

- Vegetarian friendly

Cons:

- Manufactured in India

- Not manufactured in an FDA inspected facility

- Does not appear to be made to Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP)

First be clear this is manufactured in India, the factory address is right on the bottle. Now, Karela is alleged to be able to lower blood sugar, increase insulin sensitivity, boost immune system, aid with acne, prevent cancer, cause weight loss etc. Most of these are hard to test outside of a lab or over a short period so I just focused on the lowering of blood sugar. As my mother is diabetic I have easy access to a blood glucose meter and test strips so decided to experiment on myself a little. Ind the end after regular use, compared to a control period with similar dietary intake and activity levels, I did in fact notice a modest reduction in blood sugar levels which leads me to believe it would also eventually help with increasing insulin sensitivity.

If you are diabetic or pre diabetic it might be worth talking to your doctor about bitter melon / bitter gourd / karela and seeing if he or she would be willing to let you try it in combination with any other methods they are using to manage your blood sugar and insulin levels.

title: Deceptive snake oil.
text: If you read the instructions for another GermGuardian product, their mini wand, you will note they say the light must be in contact for 20 seconds to disinfect. With this GG1000, there is no way the air is staying in contact that long. At best, it's likely a second or two by time the air passes through. Also, look at the internal area. It's only cubic inches. A typical 10 x 12 room is 1,000 cubic feet. There is no way the air in your room is being circulated into this device at any noteworthy level. Put a piece of paper up to the air input on the device. Notice it doesn't suck it in much? How is it going to suck in some mold spore or bacteria on the other side of the room? Now, you could get lucky if you have a fan or air conditioning moving air around in the room. But still, this device doesn't have much power to suck in air. Anything that gets into the devicemust be within inches of it, and pure happenstance. I doubt once it's inside it is there long enough to be sanitized.... In theory, this device could work. But you would need it to be 1/3rd the size of your room.

The Pinnacle style was oddly shaped and made. It was rather wide due to added padding and material beyond the internal rigid support. The heel cup was wide and didn't provide a stable feel against supination (outward roll) like Sole inserts do, or allow my heel to feel securely nested in place -- almost like the insole wouldn't sit far enough back in my shoe. The padding and support were cosy, but not enough to override the negatives. I wish these had worked out.

These also appear to have been worn or tried previously. Will hope for a better result when I eventually manage to obtain the actual ProTech Full Length inserts I wanted.

If they offered more stability and allowed my heel to nest properly, I'd like these much more. Could be I need to try a larger size. The M 11/11.5 failed to fill my regular walking and hiking shoes, and my feet slipped forward (not comfy). These did fit into my Vasque hiking boots, which run on the smaller side for 11.5M, and haven't worked with ANY other arch supporting insole I've tried (and there have been many).

text:
Great product. Needed these for our safety compliance. Very handy. OSHA compliance can be a pain sometimes but this was easy and the kit is so thorough. The organized pocket system it uses makes it so easy to access, and should really be easy to use when (hopefully not) the time comes that I need to use this with an employee.
This kit is Hospital Grade and complete. It covers the needs of 25 people.

In case of an accident or emergency requiring first aid, you simply open your kit, fold out the clearly labeled pockets and at a glance you choose and open the one you need in the emergency at hand.
See the pictures below to see how clearly these bags are marked! They even have the items with expiration date separately bundled together with details so you can remember what you need to replace.

Did you know that the American National Standards Institute has delineated the exact requirements for a first aid kit to be what is needed in the workplace? This not only complies with their standards but also OSHA/ANSI/ISEA Z308.

I am going to get a second on for our Bug Out Bag in case of huge disaster I will use this when I rush out of town.
Purchasing it was a no-brainer with the 100% money-back guarantee!

title: Question validity
text:
Apparently I'm intolerant to Red Pepper but not intolerant to Bell Pepper (Red). You would think Red Pepper must mean something else, but in the description it says red bell pepper. No one QCed this? There is no consistency in the headers. Some foods are Capitalized Like This and others Like this, while some are all lower case. It said I'm mildly intolerant to egg whites and I eat 4 eggs a day. I don't understand how I'm intolerant to cheddar cheese but not every other cheese, and black tea but not green tea. I wouldn't take the food results too seriously.

It said I'm deficient in omega 3 and biotin. Omega 3 doesn't make sense. I take Nordic Naturals Ultimate Omega, krill oil, and eat a low-inflammatory diet. I cut out most seed oils. I have almost perfect skin and my nails are as hard as rocks. Biotin makes sense because I have white hair in my 20s. Everyone in my family started getting white hair as young as 12 (we're Asian)... When I take biotin my skin turns hard and my lips flake and peel off like nuts. One time I got a giant cyst on my face when I never get acne. I obviously have some genetic problem with biotin.

It said I'm intolerant to a few random species of mold and trees, and horse meat. It says no animal intolerances, which is true.

I think there's validity to bioresonance but I don't have much confidence in this test. I read articles where people tried multiple tests and they all got different results. I got suspicious when I asked customer service whether chemical hair dye and bleach will affect the results. They said it doesn't. I don't understand how it won't affect the mineral/heavy metal composition of your hair.

The only thing I learned is I have a biotin deficiency and intolerance to a bunch of chemicals put in processed foods. Almost everyone is intolerant to BHT, sodium nitrate, hydrochloric acid... I could've saved money by taking a heavy metal hair test.

title: Not the style I was looking for...
text:
**First I want to say that I received this product at a discounted price for my open and honest opinion.**

And here it is...

I love trying new products, especially for beauty and hair. My bathroom cabinets and bedroom containers probably contain more than a hair salon. I was lucky enough to be born with very "versatile" hair. I can get it super curly (naturally but with the right products, of course), it can go wavy like soft, like natural beach waves, it can go straight and full of body and volume or it can go pin straight and sleek. It all depends on what look I am in the mood for that day, how much time I have and what the weather is going to be that day.

I have mastered my routine for all of these looks and use the hair products and tools necessary to get my desired look. I typically use a large round brush and hair dryer, sectioning it as I dry. It comes out straight, but full of body. I also use a teasing brush to get more volume.

In order to give my honest opinion on how this brush worked, I knew I couldn't do my typical routine. I dried my hair without any brushes or products (only used serum). It had slight waves and frizz when it was fully dried. I used the brush starting with layers and temp around 300.degrees. I wasn't noticing much of.the "straight" look that I expected, so I turned up the heat to 400 and continued to brush in sections.

The thing that really bothered me as I was using it is the placement of the heat control buttons. They are right on the sides, where you would grip the handle. There is a button to "lock" the heat setting in place, but I kept hitting that too which would unlock it and the temperature would increase or decrease.  After finishing brushing my whole head, I was a little disappointed. My hair was straight, but not anywnere near how I would want it styled. No matter how close I got it to my scalp, it never gave my hair the smooth look that I'm used to.

More importantly, when I starting using the brush, I  noticed my hair started breaking off small peices. Talk about damaging! It almost looked like it started to fray and dry out. I also could not get the ends of my hair to be completely straight or curled into any sort of way - they were just dried out.

I tried it again several days later and came out with the same results.

Overall, I really like the concept of the brush, it arrived quickly and looked exactly as the pictures show. As for the brush itself and the results, I was dissapointed and unimpressed. I really did have high hopes because I thought it could be a big time saver. Unfortunately, I have to say, I wouldn't recommend this brush if you know how to style your hair with the tools you already have and use.  But, if you are not really comfortable with products, drying, styling, etc., then this might be perfect for you. I do think it might work better for someone with shorter hair - mine is about half way down my back.

I know this review was lengthy, but I hope it is helpful in making a decision on your purchase.

text:
I ordered these socks for my Wife as she tends to experience leg pains. I have already purchased the Kunto Calf Compression Sleeve and she loved it! So I figured lets see what these do for her.

She wasn't too thrilled. I ordered these based off the sizing chart provided in the item description pictures. I found it weird that it only bases the size off the foot and not a measurement of the calf area. Upon receiving them, she tried them on and they were VERY difficult to pull up past the lower calf area. She does not have huge legs, they are normal size so I was a little disappointed with this problem.

Overall she said they felt good, especially the foot area as the ball and heel areas are WELL padded! However, she said she would not be able to wear them for an extended period of time due to the tightness on her calf area.

I understand these are compression socks, but they shouldn't leave a large indent on the calf that causes pain.

I would recommend these to others BUT be sure to go up in size when ordering.

title: Strong (Practically Heavy-Duty) Nitrile Gloves
text:
I've used these for gardening - even digging in the soil and rocks with my fingers - as well as cleaning and scrubbing everything from dishes to bird cages, and not one has broken.

I do not re-use them to avoid spreading garden mites, among other biting vermin, and germs to my birds, although they are strong enough to last through two or three separate potting or mild dishwashing sessions. If you're going to do that, remove them by the wrist, allow the sweat to dry, and then turn them right side out and rinse if necessary, keeping the insides dry. Pulling them off by their fingertips practically guarantees they (or any disposable gloves) will break in half the time than would otherwise be the case.

I don't have large hands but have very long fingers, so I ordered the large to prevent breakage at the fingertips from over-stretching them. They fit and function as well as one could hope or expect disposable nitrile gloves to perform, certainly as well as any I've ever used before.

title: Cutest tub!
text: My baby had outgrown our hard plastic tub and was uncomfortable in it.  I got this tub as a replacement.  After reading another customer's review I also purchased a sponge for the bottom and have had no problems with him slipping under water.  It smelled VERY STRONGLY of plastic so I had to wait a couple of days to use it, I recommend airing it out.  But once it's blown up, it's ready to go.  It's a little difficult to fill since it's so puffy, I have trouble getting it under the tub faucet but since I need to test the water temperature anyway, I just cup my hands and let the water run into the tub like that.  If you had a tub hose or something it would be easier.  My son loves this tub.  He lays back and luxuriates in his bath and it's very cute to see him "relaxing".  (8 months old).  The suction cup on the back is awesome for hanging it up out of the way in the shower when we're done with it.  We keep it blown up and don't use the drain plug, we just tip it up to drain it because I read another review that the drain plug got warped and started to leak.  I'm avoiding that by just tipping it up to pour the water out.  Working perfectly so far!!  :)

title: Fun to use with beautiful pigments.
text:
I loved this product! A little background on me, I have usually just used regular nail polish. I have had dip nails done at salons but never at home. This was my first time trying the dip and after three weeks I can recommend this 100%.

If you don’t know what to do or this is your first time watching a solid tutorial is a must. It helps clarify a lot of questions and it can also help save your nails. Nail career education has a good tutorial especially for beginners.

To start the kit came with everything it said but as someone who has used the kit I would recommend three other things. First get a nail e file. It is an absolute must and your cuticles/ hands will thank you. Once you’ve applied the product, some areas will be lumpy and bumpy especially if you aren’t the best or don’t have a ton of practice so you will need to do a TON of filing. Filing is pretty much 60% of the process especially if you get tips. The second thing to get is acetone. You can totally file off the product but you could also compromise the integrity of your nail itself (plus it takes hours)so it’s better to get acetone and work from there. Lastly get a face mask. If you’re reading this during COVId. I’d recommend using a scarf and not wasting your face masks or getting a dust collector. This product along with the filing and dipping releases a LOT of powder and it can easily get into your lungs which if you’re like me and do your nails constantly, this could hurt you in the long term.

I would also recommend buying a separate clear powder as your base but if you’re tight on cash this could wait.

The colors:
White- your standard basic white. Very pigmented and probably needs two coats.

Pink- the pink is a bubble gum color. Not neon but and more bright pink. Two coats should do.

Blue- the blue is a light blue. Not dark but not very bright either. Two coats does the trick

Purple- this purple is a lavender purple. If you have the lavender iPhone, this is about the same color as that purple. One coat did the trick

Silver- this is a glitter not a silver color. Depending on how silver you want. One coat leaves some spots and you can see the nail itself. Two covers it all and leaves no nail visible.

Gold- I haven’t used this powder but it’s a similar powder to the silver just gold.

Red- this isn’t a true true red. It has some shimmer to it almost like a candy red. Two coats does the trick.

Some side notes.

The smells are pretty strong and they can make your eyes water so if you’re sensitive and have no mask and eye protection be warned because it makes it hard to put on the product. I didn’t mind because that’s part of the process and it’s normal but it could be a factor for you.

Step two and four are “glues” which help the product stay so if you leave them uncapped they will stick and make your life miserable if you aren’t careful. Also on a similar note be mindful when applying because you could apply some of the product on the cap making them stick and impossible to wipe off so try to use acetone to remove and scrape off the product after every use.

When applying step two make sure to cover ALL of the nail because if you don’t, product won’t stick and you’ll have spots missing. Again I’d recommend watching some tutorials which will help clarify a lot of what to do.

Overall I loved this product. It stays on perfectly and looks beautiful. I loved all the colors and have even ordered more. It is a little tough to use if you don’t know what you’re doing but if you have an idea it shouldn’t be too tough. I’ve had mine for about a month and a half and have had no issues with chipping or anything.

text: I’ve been using Blephaclean wipes for years since I discovered them in a Heathrow Airport gift shop. My eyes burn when I hike especially if I have sunscreen. When I saw Systane brand on Amazon I jumped at it as Blephaclean eyelid wipes are costly (Systane seemed cheaper). Alcon, the company that makes the Systane pads is well regarded in the eye medicine world and also makes Systane drops for dry eyes which I use. title: Great curling wand
text: This curling wand is very nice! I like that it is a 1 inch wand and can curl my hair fairly quickly. This is not a curling iron so there is no clip at the bottom to hold your hair. After using the curling wand my curls stay in my hair for a few days until I'm ready to wash my hair. The only product I use before curling and highly recommend is a thermal heat protectant spray to lessen the damage the heat causes to my hair. The wand heats up really fast. It would be great if it had a temperature control however it works just great and gives me the desired effect without one. I love the beautiful curls I get from using the wand. What works for me is to section out my hair before I curl. I take my hair and section it by pulling my sides up then clip the top section up. Then I do the same to the remainder pieces of my hair. I just pull my sides and clip. When I get to the last section that's where I start curling from the bottom of my hair up. I take about a 1 inch piece of hair at a time and wrap it around the wand for a few seconds and then release it. The heat glove that came with this is very useful it is too large for my hands but it works well enough to serve the main purpose and keeps me from burning myself while using the curling wand. I would highly recommend this curling wand.

title: This item is a little large but for what it does and I'm very pleased with it.
text:
When I saw that there was a new straightening brush I decided to order one on Amazon. I really like this item! This straightener has an LED display showing the temperature of the straightening brush. That means that I can heat up the brush as high or low as I would like. All of the bristles on this brush are very sturdy and I really don't show any concern of them coming out. The cord on the straightening brush is long. This was important to me because there's only one plug in my bathroom and I needed to extend across the sink. I was able to straighten my hair with this item and didn't burn my hands or my head. Now I know that that's pretty funny but I have burnt my fingers before using a straightening iron. When I finish straightening my hair I didn't find it to be frizzy but I did put some sheen in it. For my convenience I split my hair up into sections when I straightened it. This is exactly how I did my hair with a straightening iron and it worked well with the straightening brush. This item is a little large but for what it does and I'm very pleased with it.

title: What a pleasant surprise
text:
I have had mixed luck with various masks, both purchased and homemade, so I think I had low expectations for this product, especially at this price point. My first impression was that of disappointment. I took them out of the package and they seemed very small. Imagine my surprise when I put one on and it seemed to grow. I have a fairly fat head (as most of my friends will tell you) and this mask fits great. It covers my nose and goes under my chin. The sides go fairly high up near my ears and I feel pretty secure that I will not be sharing my germs with anyone when I put this on.

This other thing is this seemed like it was very light weight, but I checked it and it is indeed 2 layers. You may want to put it in the washer before wearing though. Mine definitely had a smell, which a friend of mine in the clothing industry has told me is antifungal, which all new clothes are treated with before they are sent off to warehouses before distribution, so you won't have to worry about getting nose fungus.

I washed mine and they now don't smell of anything and while they looked a bit shrunken when I took them out of the dryer, they stretched back out into shape. All in all a great price and a perfectly adequate product with enough masks to allow you to keep a clean one in rotation between washings.

Did I mention how easy these are to breath in? These are one of the most breathable masks I have tried.

title: Okay, but seems to leave the roots behind
text:
This is my first time using an epilator and generally use sugar wax or a razor. The epilator was charged straight out of the box and comes with a useful instruction booklet, a charger, a cleaning brush, and 2 separate heads for longer/ shorter hairs. The epilator has two different speeds depending on the type of hair. It also has a light on the epilator which is a nice touch.

I tried the epilator head on my legs. Surprisingly, it was not painful to use and would say the sugar wax method hurts more. It does not do as clean of a job and had to go over the same area several times to get the remaining hairs. I don't believe it is pulling all the hairs from the root as it should as I could feel stubble that wasn't there before. Shaving will probably give you a faster result. I used the foil shaver head for my underarms and the results were pretty much the same as shaving.

The good thing about the epilator is that it's meant to be used on dry skin. You don't need to use any shaving cream. It also didn't seem to irritate my skin afterwards. Overall, I think this product is just okay. It does the job for the most part, but I think there are other products that may do better.

title: Very satisfied with Nic-Out
text:
UPSIDE:
After using numerous boxes of these filters I've never came across a cracked one, as some reviewers have.
It's true, the filters DO NOT change the taste of the cigarette, and they catch most of the garbage that would be going into our system.
And for me, as a 30yr smoker, my cravings have fallen big time. I've gone from almost a pack a day habit to 4-5 smokes a day (consistantly for over a month). YEAH!!
When I look in the mirror, after brushing, my teeth are noticeably whiter (family and friends have told me so).

Now, for the DOWNSIDE:
Nic-Out claims that each filter is good for 5 smokes. For me, they're only good for 4. The 5th time I use it, the tar and nicotine slides back onto my lips making a pretty nasty taste, besides the fact there is no draw factor.
Sometimes, even on the 4th use, the draw factor is clogged and barely useful. This doesn't happen often and I have turned the filter around and blown the clog out, then it works.
Often, the yellow fiter (inside the unit) is all cockeyed so I have to use my tweezers to sit it in it's place.

The downsides might be kinda annoying but they're not a big problem that isn't easily fixed.
I hope you all have as good experience with these filter as I have had!

title: Positive Review by Someone Not Paid to Do It
text: I have used this product about 5 times over the past month.  I am over 55 and have always had wild curly, frizzy hair below shoulder length.  I am very impatient when it comes to taming my tresses.  So I normally wash it, put a little defrizzing cream on it (not that it helps much on humid summer days) and let it go natural.  But sometimes, I really want my hair to be straight and I don't have the patience to stand there with a flat iron because it takes forever to get through the layers.  I have tried flat irons, curling irons, heated curling brushes (now there's are snarl waiting to happen) and have tossed them all.  I decided to try this RoseMyst brush on a whim.  I am so glad I did.  I turn it on and it is ready to go in 90 seconds.  I make sure I have sprayed on some kind of thermal protectant.  I have been using the lowest heat levels of 355 and 375 and it works beautifully.  I run a brush through my hair to rid it of snarls and loose hairs (if you don't, the hair builds up on the RoseMyst brush and starts to smell as the loose hairs begin to singe).  Then I brush my hair just like normal and in less than 3 minutes, I have straight hair.  Sometimes I spray a little light setting mist on my hair to keep it from absorbing moisture when I go out.  But that's about it!  It does have a lock feature to keep you from accidentally changing settings while you work with it but I have never had any problem.  I wait until the brush has cooled and pull out some of the loose strands so they won't singe when I turn it on again.  I also like the swivel cord (it was a requirement for me before I bought it).  I Love this product.  I found it on eBay for $118.00 so the Amazon pricing is a much better deal.

title: Nice unit, with a couple of issues...
text:
The unit I got works well and feels good, especially on my lower back and between the shoulder blades. I like that it has different buttons for all it's different functions. That makes it easier to use than units that assign multiple functions to one button.

One issue I have with it though, is that, besides the rather quiet motor noise (that all these types of massagers make), it has an extra "swishing" /"rubbing against something" noise, every time the rollers go under the edge of the "frame" fabric. This is a new and different noise that my other, similar massagers, don't make. I think it's because the rollers actually go underneath the solid piece of "frame" material instead of staying under the mesh material during the whole rotation. And when they do it makes that noise. It's not that loud so I might be able to get used to it.

The other issue that I noticed upon unzipping the unit, when I was trying to figure out what was making that noise, is that the small circuit boards, with the contacts to the top buttons on them, are only taped into place and were dangling half-way off. I just re-taped them but I will have to find a way to secure them better or they will get loose and the buttons won't work. I noticed that some of the low starred reviews were because of buttons not working. So I guess theirs probably got completely untaped. I have made and attached a little info-graphic showing what I found when I unzipped it, and advising putting new tape, gluing or sewing the existing tape onto the fabric, after matching up the circuit board buttons to the backs of the buttons on the fabric. This should make the buttons work again. So that part is easily fixable, but I'm not sure about that swishing noise.

Other than those issues, the unit is very nice. It's comparable to others similar to it. It has no odor or smell to it. The price is lower than most others.

title: Very Well Made - Lots of Storage - Comes With Some Medical Supplies
text:
After one of volleyball players was injured during play recently I decided it was time to be a little more prepared and decided to get an emergency kit to always have on hand. I went to the local big box and drugstores but I wasn't impressed with the kits they had to offer so I decided to just make my own.

I went with this MT Tactical Pack as it appeared to have plenty of room for expansion, and it looked cool as well.

There were no unpleasant surprises once it arrived. The MT Tactical Pack is obviously well made and the multiple pockets, pouches, and MOLLE securing straps makes for plenty of storage options. And though I didn't see them listed in the pictures, included with the tactical pack was an emergency kit with supplies and an Emergency Trauma Bandage pack.

I'm just starting to load this tactical pack with various other medical emergency supplies. I hope I never need use more than a Band-Aid or two from the supplies, but I feel better knowing that if a real emergency arises I will have the emergency basics available.

You will see how to put the sock on the plastic guide then slip your foot into that plastic part and just pull up slowly enough to allow the sock to slip off and onto your foot and shin.

I wear dress socks, plain old white athletic socks and nice wool blended hiking or work socks; they all slide on like butter now. You will come to love this once you give it a chance. title: Now this I like!
text:
Before trying this I tried Suntue's heated percussion massager unit. It wasn't for me, but other people might enjoy it. See my review for that item for more details.
As for this massager, I am very happy with it! Suntue's reached out to me and wanted to make things right since I didn't like their other massager. I returned it and they sent me this unit instead, based on my preferences. Which was very nice of them.

Ive been very happy with this percussion massager so far. Its inexpensive, well built, it has a good strong 25 watt motor and some useful attachments! It feels really good!

I have suffered from chronic widespread pain from Fibromyalgia and nerve damage. I use a massager several times a day, EVERY DAY, to help keep my pain levels under control. I get sore muscles, stiff, achy joints, trigger points, knots, oh sooo many issues that cause me pain. My wife is massaging my back right now while Im typing this review and it...feels...great! Very similar to other percussion massagers I've been using over the years!

This may sound silly at first, but my favorite part of this massager is the cord! I'll explain why.
I use massagers ALOT, sometimes for several hours on and off throughout the day. So I have worn out many massagers over the years. And 9/10 times, the first thing to malfunction has been THE CORD! Companies use poorly designed cord protectors, or cheap, thin cords made with subpar quality brittle copper and plastic parts that wear and fray over time just through normal usage. The point where the cord comes out of the until is the area most succeptible to damage. The copper inside the cord frays and can suddenly (and sometimes very dangerously) cause an electrical arc and burn right through the cord! I've experienced this nearly life-threatening cord failure on dozens of massagers over the years! If it wasn't for the breaker tripping, I would have been electrocuted or something caught on fire!
It got to the point where I started using my electrical engineering skills to remove the awful cords and solder new, high quality utility cords onto my massagers to make them last longer and prevent such dangerous catastrophic failures!
Here's why Suntue's cord really impresses me! The design of the cord protector is brilliant! I'll include a photo so you all can see. It has a nice, thick double shielded cord, with a very long cord protector, and they included a stiff rubber arched spine on the top of the protector to allow the cord to still bend, but not easily bend too much to the point where regular usage will damage the cord! I applaud them for this design because it really seems they put alot of thought into preventing cord failure!
Some of my favorite percussion massagers have literally gone off the market and back to the R&D lab because of so many people complaining about these dangerous cord failures! So Bravo to Suntue for this smart cord design! That alone earns 5 stars from me!
I will update my review in the future after I use it for a few months and I'll let everyone know how its holding up! But as of now, I am very impressed! For the price of this massager and the quality of customer service, you can't really go wrong!

title: Product appears to be excellent, packaging not so much
text:
About 30 years ago, I cracked a tooth. The dentist told me it was from bruxism and said I needed to get a night guard. I got one of the standard wraparound type. A year or two later, I cracked another tooth. I had also chewed through a couple of night guards. This went on for several years with me cracking a tooth every 2-3 years, many resulting in root canals.

Finally, I did some research and found the NTI, a small bite guard that fits over the front teeth. The theory was that the wrap-around night guards actually made the bruxism worse because they sit between the morals, which are the brushing and teeth grinding. When they feels pressure, they tend to clamp down. This made some sense to me since I was chewing through the wraparound night guards.

The NTI had to be custom made by a dentist because, being small, they were a choking risk, so had to fit snugly over the teeth so they could not easily become loose and be aspirated. The going rate around here was about $500-$600 dollars. I decided to give it a try, because it was cheaper than crown and root canals.

I got my NTI about 20 years ago and have not had a cracked tooth since. However. about 7-8 years ago, the softer interior material started to wear and crack. The NTI no longer fit tightly against my teeth. I wasn’t too worried about aspiration because I never sleep on my back. But over the past year or two, almost all of the interior material has fallen out. The NTI is now so loose that it sometimes digs into the inside of my lip.

Before I spent about $600 for a new NTI, I did a little checking and discovered the Smart Guard. It looked like it might be the same job as the4 NTI and it cost a fraction of the cost. So I ordered one. It arrived today. I just completed the fitting procedure, so here’s my initial review. I’ll try to update it in a few weeks after I have used it for awhile.

The fitting instructions were pretty easy and I was able to complete them without a problem. It seems to fit fairly tightly – not as tight as the NTI, but I don’t think it will slip off. And it’s quite a bit larger than the NTI so much harder to aspirate. I give it an A- or B+ for instructions and fitting.

Here’s the bad news. This version, which is supposed to be “improved”, does not come with a case. This is a major problem, especially since I understand that previous version came with a case and two guards. This will cost it at least one full star. What am I supposed to do, just leave it out on the night stand? And what do I do when I travel, just toss it in the suitcase with the underwear?

Worse, the instructions say to keep the night guard in its “storage case”. I guess they just used the same instructions as for the previous version which did have a case. Deduct half a star.

The instructions are pretty good, but who keep paper instructions anymore? The folded instruction sheet is the wrong size for scanning and there is no downloadable PDF version on their website. Deduct another half star.

This is really too bad. With a little better follow through, this could have been a 5-star product. They appear to have done the hard part right. Pity.

I planned to start the Liver Detox on the weekend, since detoxing can produce a few undesirable side effects including any Herxheimmer reactions. I missed my first two days because I kept forgetting to take the pills 20-30 minutes before a meal.

title: Overall, I'm pretty happy I tried it...
text:
Okay, so at first I thought this was stupid and I refused to try it. I love my beauty blender and that's that. But then I saw a bunch of You Tube videos from various makeup artist channels that I follow and they all tested out similar products. They seemed to have mixed feelings, but they leaned toward the positive side. I figured it was time to give it a try.

I did have the issue with my beauty blender absorbing product. However, I used a cream foundation rather than a liquid, so it wasn't as bad as it could be. But at almost $50 for my foundation, I hate to see any of it wasted. This product seemed to resolve my only real issue with the beauty blender, so the real test was- does it otherwise perform the same? The answer is no. But that doesn't mean it performs poorly. It's just different.

I don't quite get the "airbrushed" look of my beauty blender, but it's also not caked on. It took a little getting used to (and about three days) to get the hang of it. But I think it looks pretty natural. I've figured out how to fold and bend the sponge to get under my eyes and around my nose. I have also figured out that a little goes a long way. Without absorption, I use a lot less product. So I start small and build up.

I have found that after I finish using it to spread out the foundation, I follow up with a damp beauty blender to finish blending it out the rest of the way. Because the foundation is already spread out and mostly soaked into my skin, it doesn't really absorb much if anything, but does a good job getting that airbrushed look I like.

Overall, I'm pretty happy I tried it and will continue using it, but following up with the beauty blender at the very end. Hopefully I'll get a lot more mileage out of my foundation this way.

title: Very Nice Results!
text:
Years ago, I got a medium scratch on one of my most beloved watches I own (A Citizen Eco-Drive that I purchased after I got hired at my first Big Boy job out of college). I wore it everyday, and eventually it got more scratches as the years passed. My watch collection has grown since then, and so has my distain for the scratches on the mineral crystal of this watch.

I saw mixed reviews of this product and it seems to be from folks using this to remove scratches from their Smart Phone Screens, so I figured I give it a try before I sent it off for a new mineral glass. If you've ever had a scratch on your cars paint and tried to buff it out yourself (or even professionally in some cases), you know that the scratch ends up looking way better, but in the right light you can still see it. So going into this, my expectation was that it would make the scratches on the glass look less severe.

After a few applications (and, a little bit of elbow grease), the scratches are barely noticeable on the wrist. Of course, if it catches the right lighting at the right angle, you will see the scratches on the glass. In my watch display case, the scratches are non-existent.

I am very pleased with this product. Yes, its a little tedious, but as with any repair that you want to come out correctly, patience is critical. If you are looking for the perfect repair, you should look into replacing the glass of your watch. If you are content with making the glass look better for a rarely worn timepiece, then this product is for you!

My glasses were this color. This is like a flat black.

As for the quality, the paint had a paint burr which I didn't like to see (bottom of magnet piece-right). Broke off easily however. It is a wonder how these people put this business together. Watched on the shark tank and then had my glasses almost once fall again out of my pocket, when bending over, then said, I should get that device. The other small defect is a small bump under the paint where the magnet part is but on the bent piece (flat circle). I assume a piece of metal or maybe dirt then painted over. Also the back of the clip isn't really painted. Has like an over spray paint effect. The back plate is not painted at all which is fine.

The magnets are very strong. I am amazed how it snaps together. Pulling it apart is easy with the grip of the bended part. I don't know if such a force is good for your body or not. Any health risks? You do or are supposed to have iron in your blood I don't know if it would collect there or turn you magnetic or what. Is such a charge healthy for you? Some people wear other devices for a healing effect. So who knows.

Also a concern is will this thing erase or corrupt the data of my credit cards, or flash drives? Also if near anything such as a laptop will it cause anything to be/become a magnet?

Curious what type of glue is on there. Seems pretty strong. Is it an epoxy? This guy took 5k for a patent and turned it into millions.

Totally amazed by this process of being in business for yourself. Gave away 65% I think. However Lorry made it a quick success.

Once people have so many patents though who can create a business without owing it to someone else, or not being able to do it? Curious how he found the patent that was already in place.

I thought of another thing as well. Maybe for a tie clip this would work too. The common tie clips either put a new hole in your tie or snag it with teeth.

Had a couple weeks and they're amazing. I'm one of the adults who always spill on my boobs when eating and it's embarrassing to have to go back into work with stains on my top. No better at home. I haven't actually tried washing them as, of course, I haven't really spilled much on myself since getting these. But I need one for my car and one for my office. (Have one currently in my kitchen for meals and one in my travel bag for day trips, but I like having many so I don't have to remember to bring one with me.)
My only disappointment in these so far, and it's minor, is they only come in these two patterns. I'm fine with them around the house, I like blue, but wish there were more attractive prints made by this company. Possibly some paisley (blue and purple and green are fine colors, no need for pinks or red or anything,) or midnight sky (with stars). Or maybe fall leaves or something fun like Halloween ghosts/bats/pumpkins (repeating pattern), as we're close to Halloween. Or polka dots. Basic polka dots - Navy blue background, white dots. Stripes. I dunno, just more variety. I'm all for the unisex look and simple patterns to disguise spills, and dark colors, but just more! Lol. I do really like the two I have, though. They're slightly "masculine" in colors/styles, which, again, is fine, but a little more variety for the ladies might be nice.
Regardless, these are great. LOVE the length! It's perfect, covers chest and lap, which is necessary! It's perfectly wide. The Velcro connector is perfect - thick, durable, well sewn, I like it's in the back. It's *extremely* comfortable. I love it! I'm ordering more, because I need them, and the patterns are fine, but I would like better color options.

title: Does not replace my traditional Straightener.
text:
It is just okay. I will say that for anyone with really curly hair, this is probably not going to be your favorite straightening tool. I have long,curly, fine hair and this brush seemed to make it more frizzy than I could handle. It does get super hot and comes to temperature very quickly. It is make very sturdy and heavy duty. I like that the temperature displays right on the top so you can easily see what temperature it it. I did not like the placement of the temperature controls, it felt like I was constantly bumping them while I was using the brush.

I first tried this after wearing my hair in a messy bun overnight, I took small pieces of hair and had to go over it several time before it took the waves out. It then left me with a lot of frizz. As anyone with curly hair can say, you DO NOT brush curly hair. I guess I should not have had such high hopes for this product just because I know that my hair does not do well with brushing.

The second time I tried it after towel drying my hair straight out of the shower. It was nice in that it did not burn my scalp, like my traditional straightener will if I use it on wet hair. However It seemed to give me about the same results if not a little more frizzy.

I think if you have shorter hair or almost straight hair that you just need a little extra to get it completely straight, and your hair likes to be brushed, then this would work well for you. If you have curly hair, I would say this will work well for getting the initial curl out of your hair, and maybe taking out the blow drying step before using a traditional straightener to get the glossy smooth finished look.

title: Good buy!
text:
I bought this as a movable computer work space I could use with my favorite reclining armchair in particular. I had some concerns after reading other reviews about putting this together and about the tabletop springing up sending my laptop and coffee flying every time I inadvertently bumped the underside with a misplaced hand or knee.I watched a Youtube video first, and read the instructions carefully. The table was well packed, the screws etc were packed in separate plastic container and clearly numbered, and the instructions seemed pretty straightforward. I'm guessing the company has made improvements here since some earlier reviews. I had an old all purpose Phillips head and some pliers and they did the job handily, Total time to put together was about 10 minutes, not counting watching the video and reading the instructions. I have mobility problems and am not very handy and it was definitely on the easy side for me.

Once together it was solid, large enough to hold my laptop and an extra ASUS 20 inch screen along with coffee, snack, pen papers, phone and 2 remotes. It fits easily over the chair when the foot rest is extended and rolls easily out and back as I get up and down. One thing I DIDN'T do.... Once assembled, I noticed the base table height, as is, was right where wanted it if not and inch or two higher. I couldn't imagine any reason I would want or need to raise it so I never removed the black screw that releases the mechanism that does so. This leaves me with a very steady laptop and coffee safe surface that I don't have to worry will rise suddenly if I brush the underside with my knee. I know some have complained of this and I can't comment as to how sensitive, or how much of a problem it might be. I admit to being a little curious but as it is with the screw left in, the table height is solid, safe and perfect for me. This table does everything I hoped it would, is much better made than what I would have expected for the price, and provides great value for the money. I am quite pleased with this purchase.

title: WORKS WELL, BUT PRICEY!
text:
I would have rated this product 3.5 had that been possible. My main gripes have to do with price. Gillette made its fortune selling razor blades, and they sold a gazillion blades my selling their razors dirt cheap. Emjoi have adopted that model, with a twist. The twist is that they charge a big fat price for their callus remover AND also charge more than enough for their 'blades.'

The system is simplicity itself. A piece of sandpaper, or equivalent, is wrapped around a 2-inch long cylinder made of wood (I think). This is the refill. When the device is turned on, the sandpaper-covered cylinder spins, and when held against hard skin on the heels, for example, white powder which seconds before had been skin, flies from the foot.

I decided that the battery operated model was almost certainly a bad choice because small devices with motors tend to eat batteries, and performance would decline as the batteries declined. Therefore I bought the AC model which cost just under $50.
My first impression was of something that cost a lot less, maybe $25. It is well designed, very comfortable to hold and to use, and it works well enough with the relatively gentle 'sandpaper' refills that came with it it. I just ordered coarser refills in the belief that they will work better on my very hard skin. The refills, which do not last very long, cost about $3 each in packets of 4, and slightly less in packs of 6, 8 and 12. If you have hard skin on your feet and have had enough of filing it by hand, try this.

title: Okay, but two issues for me....  The velcro and slippage.
text:
First of all, I'm an active tennis player (I have played 2-3 times per week for 25 years). I get tennis elbow more when I take a break from playing... so if you want to prevent injury, my advice is don't stop playing unless you have to.

I've used many braces. My issues with this one are: 1) The brace is neoprene (body glove) material on the inside. The plus of this is it warms up nice and keeps a consistent pressure. The bad thing is when you are playing active sports it slips down the arm when moisture hits it.... and you can't keep tightening it or it will make your arm hurt more. 2) The Velcro... While I love having an adjustable Velcro strap, the velcro on this one is sooo hard to peal off that it is frustrating while playing sports. I need to adjust it several times a match, and the Velcro just sticks too hard that I found myself yanking the thing off and throwing it at my tennis bag to not delay my opponent any more. The Velcro strap is also rigid and hard to grip with sweaty hands. Hate it.

Look for terrycloth style straps, where the Velcro isn't hard to manipulate. Also, a bit less width wouldn't hurt (prevents slipping). All you need is a little consistent pressure on the lateral epicondyle (outside elbow) for tennis, and the medial one for golf.

title: Good Stuff
text:
Glycerin is the key to great lotions. Some deny this because it's a petroleum by-product. But so is Vaseline. So is all forms of makeup.

I mix my lotion one third glycerin and two-thirds water. It's OK that way, but I like the lotion to be thicker than water, so I add any compatible drug compounding base I'll buy from a pharmacy. Unibase used to be the best compounding agent, but that's been years ago and the new ones are better.

Add the essential oil you like the most, mix, and the job is done...for months. (Be careful to date the containers; glycerin has a life span, after which it is no good.)

This particular brand of glycerin is very high grade. Read the bottle, and/or the approved methods of grading glycerins. I think you'll find this product well worth your money.

text: At first, I thought they were small because the nose to chin height looks short until you stretch it down over your chin. They are very stretchy. Then they felt too wide because the loops fit loosely over your ears but since they are very soft cotton blend and thin 2 ply, they will probably shrink after washing. In the ad photo, these look like they would prop up solidly on a table but they will not. They are like a thin handkerchief and will not provide much protection. That's okay for me because I will wear an n95 with a nose clip that fits and use these over it. There is no nose clip at all so your breath is going to fog up glasses and limit any protection for people around you without another mask underneath. That's why they are so cheap. These should NOT be the only mask you wear if you expect to protect yourself or those around you from a virus. They might shorten the distance of a sneeze.

title: Updated review: Being fair
text:
Original review: I suppose they have to have a very weak motor in these so they don't sand thru your face to the next layer but including the small massager head only points that out. I think if I ever replace it tho, I'll part with a few more bucks and look for higher quality.

UPDATE: I think I was a little unfair in my original review above. I should have mentioned that I am an over 60 male and my intent for this product was not for makeup or moisturizer but to try and reduce white head bumps and facial blemishes. My skin is not soft as a woman's (nor as leathery as Willie Nelson's) but I have actually had luck on high speed with filing down these bumps. I am rougher on my face in doing that than a woman or most men would want to be but it has helped me and I felt like I should add a couple more stars because of that. The construction is good and the production quality is good so if your need is along more normal lines such as the Proactive device advertised on tv, I recommend trying this. It is holding up well and I have had no troubles with it.
By the way, their customer service department is very good and they were concerned regarding my criticism. I did not ask to return it but I feel they will go out of their way to make sure you are satisfied. I would definitely do business with them again.

title: Initial Review - Instant Warmth and $$ Saver
text:
I have a chronic lower-back problem. I've been buying the air-activated chemical heat wraps, which are expensive, one-time use devices. They bunch up and can get itchy so I looked for an alternative. I was skeptical about this heating pad, but figured the good ratings and price would make it a worthy try. I'm glad I took the plunge! The pad is large enough to cover the entire back of my desk chair, it's comfortable, and the heat is adjustable and instant.

I was desperate. I was blowing through those chemical heat wraps quickly. I've been using this pad pretty much constantly for the past week. If you know how much those things cost it's not hard to calculate that this electric pad has come close to paying for itself already. It's really just about perfect. I don't need a back massager. I have a good portable one and sometimes those rollers just don't help or are uncomfortable in a desk chair. With this, I can sit in my desk chair without making any other adjustments, and can get through the day.

The heat is instant. I vary the heat between Level 2 and 4. In bed, Level 2 is enough. You know how your back can tighten up when you get in a cold bed? No more. Turn this on a minute before getting in bed and you're set. In my chair, I'm typically at Level 3 or 4, depending on what I'm wearing. The controller is easy to understand, and you have an auto-shut off option of either 2 or 6 hours.

I hope this review helps you. Trust me, I know when you are in pain, you'll try just about anything and that can be expensive. This won't fix your back, but it has helped me get relief.

Pros:
Relatively low cost
Portable and comfortable. Works on your existing chair or bed.

title: a portable hot stone massage
text:
I am a massage therapist, I enjoy working with hot stones, but traditional hot stones are not portable, nor are they suited for a clinic setting due to size, clean up, and weight. So this seemed to be a good portable way to bring hot stone into my every day practice.

It arrived quickly and in perfect shape, I took it out of the box and tested it out on low first. Low is actually luke warm and not much for therapeutic heat value unless you are using it on someone who really cannot tolerate heat. I then tried it out on high, which at first might seem a bit too hot, at least for placement directly on skin, but it cools off rather quickly to a good working temp.

It works good with a little lotion, oils would allow for more glide, but if you are using it for deep tissue it works well by itself or with a bit of lotion.

I only gave it 3 stars instead of 4 because the stones really do not retain their heat as long as traditional basalt stones do and it does take some time for them to heat up (they heat from the bottom up) so the advertising was a bit deceiving in that respect, however, there are enough stones that you can just switch stones when they do cool.

Easy to use, easy to clean, and easily portable for use in out calls, clinics, or even your home. So for the convenience and portability I would recommend this to others who like to work with hot stones. As a side note, if you do use hot stones in your professional practice make sure your liability insurance covers it.

title: Keep in mind, this is a shampoo brush, NOT a scalp massager
text:
Many of the reviews complain that the bristles are too soft for scalp massage, and that is by design! The intended purpose of this brush is to apply shampoo evenly, while using less product, with a gentle massaging effect to stimulate hair follicles. If the bristles were stiffer, you'd run the risk of breaking and damaging your hair considering hair stretches immensely when wet. Scalp massagers are entirely different products, usually made out of metal wires with soft tips.

This shampoo brush is a godsend for me. I wash my long hair only once or twice per week with sulfate-free shampoo, so when I do wash it, I need to really focus on my scalp to remove dirt and oil. Before using this brush, I would occasionally develop patches of eczema on my scalp near the nape of my neck, despite my chemical-free routine. I knew I needed to find a way to effectively cleanse my scalp without using my fingernails to scrub during the shampoo process, which is so bad for your skin.

I've been using this brush for a couple months and I've had no further eczema outbreaks on my scalp, and I've used significantly less shampoo as this brush distributes it more evenly. I suggest being very aware of HOW you use it, as it's possible to cause ridiculous tangles if used incorrectly. A circular motion is fine for each section of your head, just take it slow and try to comb through your hair with the brush as you're shampooing.

My wife and I rent out two bedrooms in our home to individuals who are new/newer to recovery (living a sober lifestyle - free from alcohol and drugs). We're known unofficially as a 3/4 sober-living home - as we have many rules that you would not have at a private bedroom rental (aka roommate situation). This means that we require those living here to submit to regular alcohol and/or drug testing.

Having an at-home breathalyzer is sooooo convenient AND has saved us money that we would normally spend at a local alcohol/drug testing facility. I think this also helps our tenants think twice about drinking, as they know we can immediately test without having to make an appointment here at the local testing facility (or run into the testing facility being closed or too busy given the COVID-19 pandemic).

So far, it appears to test accurately. We have used it regularly since we received it from Amazon.

Overall, I am thrilled (& relieved) to have this gadget now at our home. I would recommend to other 3/4 sober-living homes.

title: OHHH NOOOOO WAYYYY!! WHAT IN THE HOLY HEAVENS?! NOT MEEEE! NOT TODAAAYYYY!
text:
What in the actual??!! I tried to love these, I really did. But NOOO WAAYYYYYYY!
Firstly, I'll say this-
length=great.
Adhesive =great
Absorbency =great
Softness=great
Comfort=great
Shape=great
Price point=great
Scent=not so great
Plastic wrap= most definitely not so great
Sensation on the the v-jay, AWFUL!!!
What is supposed to be a cooling sensation turned into an uncomfortable, almost burning feeling within no time!
I read reviews for a considerable amount of time, and it seems I am not alone in this sentiment. The "burning" went on way longer then 1 or 2 minutes on my v-jay and never really stopped. It only be came less intense. I was well aware of my v-jay the entire time I wore this liner....YET I continued to wear these liners for 2 days....I digress 😑

Maybe cucumber instead of mint for the "cooling" effect? The scent from these liners from the essential oils was very strong and lingering. My bathroom was filled with it, and guess what else was scented by it as well? YEP- my v-jay! UGHHHHHHH! The combination of a scented v-jay and ESPECIALLY the constantly lit match stick in my undies was the the deal breaker! ( fire crotch comes to mind 🚫🆘️🔥☄)
On day 3, I threw in the towel....and the bag of liners- right in the bin! I can't do it!
For me, these liners smell awful and provide an over-the-top awareness of my v-jay, which I found awkward and unnecessary 😐 I love the whole mission behind The Honey Pot Company, and if these liners ever become available with a different combination of herbs/essential oils I will be right back. But that mint and yucky rose essential oil which I've never liked (unpleasant smell to me) well, they can keep it! 💯😕🙄
I really wanted to be one of the reviewers that could wear these and love the essential oil scent and the sensation that comes from them. Unfortunately, that was not the case for me. My v-jay can stay down there and not remind me constantly that it IS there 🤫 🤷‍♀️
You may have an entirely different experience with these liners, and 30 for 6 bucks and change isn't too hateful to give them a try. I ordered a few other brands of cotton/ organic liners, and I surely hope my holy grail will be found. These, however, are certainly not.

title: Best Solution Yet for Removing Calluses on Feet
text:
Emjoi Model: AP-3RPA
Made in P.R.C. (Peoples Republic of China)

I've tried several devices to get rid of the thick calluses on my feet and this works the best of any device I've tried. If the calluses are very thick, as was on my feet, it will be a slow process as it grinds the calluses away. And it may take more than one session to finish the job. If used properly, it won't be uncomfortable to use, nor will it produce any flesh wounds.

Overall quality seems to be much better than most other imports from China that we see. I have only used it one time so far, so this review is based on just a single usage. Though not overpowered, the motor is strong enough to get the job done if you don't try to force it to work harder than is probably safe (remember, the head is basically a grinder and you don't want to force it to take too much off at a time or you do risk injury to the area). So with that said, I consider the motor power to be just about right.

The only negative is that it uses a Plug-in Wall Adapter for it's power source with the cord end plugging into the bottom of the unit's handle. I would much rather it came with a flexible attached power cord with built-in strain relief at the handle of the unit and a small regular 2 Prong AC Power Plug at the other. The unit's power adapter is rated at 2.8V, 600ma (2.8V x .6A = 1.68 Watt). I'm sure the unit was intentionally designed for safety reasons to be very low powered to prevent use of it in an overly aggressive manner that could possibly result in personal injury.

title: Seem good to me, but potential issues are possible.
text: I got these and I liked the way they fit and feel. I bought one for a friend and he noticed a hole between two of the fingers, which was disappointing, especially for a gift. Although my pair did not have this defect. They are cut "resistant" which absolutely does not mean cut "proof". My buddy immediately took a kitchen knife to them while wearing them while I stood by and advised against it. They appeared to hold up to the test without noticeable damage to the gloves, or more importantly, the flesh. A heavy slash would be of concern, but they are better than bare skin. As for bites, pressure, and puncture, protection I wouldn't expect much. While they may guard against outer tissue damage, the pressure from a bite or the puncture of a bite, would hurt, bruise, and most likely get through the gaps in the fabric causing some injury. So I can see why other reviewers say that are not good for rough dog play or training. Since they are soft, you can still feel the pressure of a bite and the individual direct pressure of a tooth that may get through to the skin. Still they are better than nothing and would increase your body's protective armor rating, to an extent. The dexterity of the fingers and hands feels quite good and I feel that I could operate a variety of devices, contraptions and weaponry while wearing them. Wearing another pair of Kevlar gloves underneath them increases the intensity of the protective feel, obviously. I did buy more of them and there was a seam that stuck out from the side of the glove that went all the way down. I removed a star for the damage to one of the initial pairs and the weird protruding seam on the next pair that I purchased. I plan on using additional ones for gifts, but I am inspecting them for flaws/holes prior to gifting. For handling, cleaning, or practicing with swords, knives or other edge cutlery, they would increase my sense of safety. Overall, I like them and I am including them in my gear until I have something bad to say about them or find something better.

title: Comfortable, easily adjustable, very easy to put on.
text:
I have bursitis of the elbow and will be seeing a doctor in the near future. Appointments aren't immediate where I live.

I had been wearing an ACE bandage to try to protect my elbow. It wasn't padded, so it did a poor job of protection. It also caused some discomfort putting pressure on the swelling. It also tended to slip down my arm requiring constant adjustment.

This Corflex product had none of these issues.

It is amazingly easy to install using only one hand. There are two velcro straps which loop through two 'belt buckles'. Simply position the pad against the elbow, loop each strap through its buckle, and pull them back and engage the velcro.

What I like the most about this device is the velcro fastener(s). They are not only easy to apply but they are very easily adjusted for tension. Also, the two straps are above and below the elbow joint which makes it difficult for the pad to slide down your arm.

The pad itself is large enough to completely cover the swelling and is very comfortable. I can lean on the injured elbow without pain. I'm a large person and I would think this device would fit people ranging from Medium to X-Large, and possibly Small.

I expect this device to serve me adequately until I see the doctor. It would also be very, very helpful to those people who want to postpone seeing a doctor and try some home remedies first, like ice, heat, rest, NSAIDS, and a protective compression bandage, which are all typically recommended.

Good luck with your elbow and thanks for reading .... Sam

title: Print fades quickly, overpriced
text:
I love the zebra print because the zebra is part of the rare disorder awareness campaign. They tell doctors "When you hear hoof beats, think horses not zebras" to teach them to think of the more common causes of symptoms. But sometimes it is really a zebra causing the hoof beats and for that reason, lots of doctors are very reluctant to diagnose someone with a rare disorder. It took me 37 years before I did the research, found my disorder, and searched another 2 years before I found a doctor familiar with it enough to diagnose. So the zebra print has a very special meaning to many of those who need compression socks. I wish more offered this print in medical garments.

However, I don't normally end up choosing these out of the many compression socks I have. If they were more durable, I would probably be wearing my zebra print ones daily. I bought 2 pairs of these in both compression strengths and neither really is as effective as a brand I bought from a grocery store here or a pair of magenta colored sports compression/support socks I got through Amazon. I forget the name but they are bright purple with grey support patterns on the foot. They are not the most um, visually appealing socks but yet I choose those day after day when you would think I would prefer a zebra print. In addition to not being as effective for me, the print itself is slightly a dark almost purple color, for the stripes (see photo). They have only been washed a few times in cold water and have faded considerably. There is a seam going up the side of the sock where the print doesn't line up (see photo) and while that's a pretty minor thing, I paid a lot for these socks and expected more for the price.

title: Will work for some
text: This is one of those rare products I think where you just have to try it for yourself to see if it works for your particular circumstances.  When I first got the machine, I thought I was going to be disappointed.  It was smaller than I imagined, and not quite as loud as I imagined.  My particular problem involves rather loud noises in a neighboring room by someone who likes to scream late at night.  Putting the machine close to my head, the sound does indeed drown out for the most part that particular sound.  I do have to put it right above my head though in order for it to be loud enough to drown out other noises.  I have noticed however, it does not drown out all noises, particularly low bass sounds and things like footsteps and clicking sounds.  If your trying to drown out the noise of a TV... it might work fine whereas the sounds of someone playing lots of bass music it won't work.  In addition, whereas some people will find the sounds the machine makes to be soothing... others will find it more irritating than the noises they were trying to block.  It sounds almost exactly like one of those bathroom air vent fans.  So, in my particular case, while it drowned out the person who was screaming and I found the sounds relaxing, now the person who I was trying to drown out continuously screams about hearing my Sleepmate machine and so I'm forced to turn it off in the middle of the night and still get no sleep.

title: Best crutch tips ever- Hexagonal
text:
The cuffs are adjustable if you have someone strong squeeze them for you.
The best part about these forearm crutches is the “HEXAGONAL CRUTCH TIPS”....they last longer than ALL the others with SUPERIOR grip. I burn through crutch tips every two weeks, I have a crushed cinder driveway that eats them up so fast but these tips last for months and months.

Also, I have a Jack Russell pup that drinks out of his water bowl like crazy and leaves little water drops here and there on my tile, regular cane tips even when new have lost traction and I’ve fallen several times.

The Hexagonal tips grip so much better, have not slipped with them.

I usually replace the regular sized crutch tips with much more heavy duty ones but it kills my shoulders because of the added weight.

The crutch itself is adjustable for how tall you are or for your comfort level. I’m 5’8” and there is plenty of room to lengthen or shorten them.
The Medline crutches seem to be quieter than my last pair but with all of them it’s hard to sneak up on anything because of the squeakiness that occurs as the rivets, plastic and aluminum starts to wear down from so much pressure and stress put on them.

First off, if you're quitting smokeless tobacco, good for you! After 30 years, it was likely the best thing I have done for myself from a medical standpoint. Find yourself a support system and do all the stuff. Set a quit date, tell people about it, etc. GO to killthecan dot org for more.

Second, with regard to the product, the flavor is great. It's a full flavor, it lasts a good long time. I tend to toss it when the pepper overcomes the cinnamon.

It loses a star for price, occasional quality issues (the machine that cuts the pouches occasionally doesn't do so cleanly. You then have to be pretty careful in separating pouches or you'll open them and the pepper can burn). If you are quitting dipping for blood sugar reasons, as I did, you may have trouble finding info on whether teaza's ingredients cause an insulin spike. I never did, so I'm very careful about when I use these pouches.

text: I bought this product to spray my new car cover and immediate area to prevent my two outdoor fur-babies from climbing and clawing on what admittedly was an expensive purchase. So much so that the smell begins to ward off those applying the product as well. This would not be an issue if the spray cost less, but at its current price-point, I may have to find a different determent method. Daily sprays at the level necessary to keep fur, dirt and claw marks off my car cover for a small two-seater lasted just over 7 days. I have found that it apparently was not long enough to break habit, because they are now back at it while I think up another more cost-effective method.

text:
I have had an issue with stray cats coming on my back porch for months now. I have a camera set up so i can see any activity day or night, it started with 1, i didn't mind it, it was cute and furry. i was actually going to start feeding it until i saw another one, then it turned into 3. i even posted on my Ring neighborhood feed asking if anyone were the owners because they literally came every single night regularly. i just had to set up a barricade to keep them off so i can come up with a plan to keep them away for good since they were spraying all over the place.

I did my research, didn't want to harm them and read that coffee grounds would deter them so i scattered those around, i ordered something called a scat mat, (they jumped right over that ) and i was getting the grounds from the neighbor, i was sick of everything i was doing, not working. I was obsessed with getting rid of these cats, every single night i would see them on my camera and get more determined to find something that would work!

Finally i ordered this. it seemed like a good value for the money, it had a guarantee on it (you can't beat that) I followed the directions.....sprayed the entire area where they could enter my porch, the banisters and the sidewalk leading up to the porch and the next morning i looked at the camera and we did not have 1 visitor that night. for 1 week you have to spray each day, i probably over sprayed since i was sick of them so i ordered a lot more for future, but then after the first week, you only have to spray once a week or something like that.

The bottle is a good size, the nozzle is easy to use, comes out in stream or spray ( i love that feature ) super easy to use and i am 100 percent certain if you a similar issue as I do, you wont be disappointed.

This product actually does what it says it is going to do, i have not had 1 cat on my porch for 3 nights in a row! Not many products do what they claim to do or have that guarantee. i love this stuff!!
