text:
*UPDATE*

THIS STUFF IS AMAZING IN MY HAIR!
I like it as much or more than flaxseed gel and I may try combining the two in my next experiment! It has amazing hold (it even lays my 4A edges down) and is super healthy for my strands, especially my ends so they don't break when rubbing my clothes, etc. It also makes a really great detangler so I'm going to try it as a prepoo on my next wash day to stretch out my Nature's Little Secret Fenugreek Prepoo that I wish Amazon sold but doesn't.

So... Maybe this isn't the greatest, most organic brand for nutrition so value, IDK — but for this price, I can make enough gel for multiple hair uses for the rest of the year and buy another brand to put in my smoothies if necessary...so, sistahs stock up!
___________________

*ORIGINAL REVIEW*
I'm super confused by these reviews but this is the only brand I've ever purchased as I've been taking the ISM capsules and wanted to see if the gel in my smoothies was more effective and beneficial.

I followed the directions exactly except I cleaned and rinsed more times because I was concerned with debris. I watched a few YouTube videos and read other sets of instructions on Google, so, I'm fairly confident that I did it right. And, my gel turned out perfect! I only used a large handful and it produced way more gel than I expected so I'm going try it as a face mask and use it in my hair as it's supposed to be really healthy for both skin and hair.

I tried some in my smoothie and could not taste it which was a concern. My gel looked just like the authentic gel I saw online and in videos. I'm excited to use it in my DIY hair products.

Also, I think sea moss grows all over the world not just off the coasts of Ireland. I need to do some more research but I don't think the origins make a huge difference so long as it is wild grown (this says it is) and authentic.

If I try another brand and it is drastically different from this, I'll stand corrected. But, as of right now, I'm satisfied that I got what I paid for and I will update this if anything changes or if my skin or hair or body have any negative response.

title: Cheap but works ok
text:
[[VIDEOID:f316d6d406e3aa28d32cf35f48dd4a98]] This is an ok razor. It has some nice features such as USB C charging plug which means it uses the same charging cable that many smart phones use. This is really good because many of these shavers are using a special cable that may be hard to find, which is going to be a real problem if you lose it or break it while travelling. The two issues I have with it are 1) The trimmer which performs very poor 2) The pivoting platforms in the head part is sticky. It doesn't move freely. It could be affecting the shave quality which is just OK. It seems to be a sign of poor quality.

Positives
1) Standard USB C plug charging cable. Brilliant.
2) Uses a Toggle on/off switch which I prefer to a button that can be accidently turned on while travelling
3) Comfortable to hold.
4) Reasonably quiet.
5) Seems to use standard heads that many of these Chinese shavers use. The Flyco heads fit and replacement blades are available for purchase (really cheap too).
6) Cheap price.
7) Charging, Full charge and low battery indications. Nice.

Negatives.
1) Quality is suspect. Sticky heads.
2) Lousy trimmer. I would need a separate grooming device to do any trimming.
3) Shave is only OK. The Flyco shaves better.

I suspect the sticky heads is causing the so so shave. I ordered a replacement top head part ($6 on fasttech) so we will see if this improves the shave. For now it gets 3 stars.

UPDATE : Shaving performance has improved considerably. Now it's a great shave. I guess it needed to adjust to my face.

Another feature discovered. This is a cord/cordless shaver. When the battery is depleted the shaver stops running. No problem. you can simply plug it in and continue shaving. Very nice. Many cheap shavers are cordless only which means if the battery runs out in the middle of a shave you are rather stuck.

I’ve been trying on & off for YEARS to lose weight & get in shape. However, unfortunately except for 2 years from age of 18-20 when I was a normal size/weight (like I generally was throughout my childhood & adolescence), I’ve been struggling with obesity for pretty much my entire adult life. Now just for a little background, I am significantly (over 100 lbs) overweight, mainly due to the side effects of meds for several chronic medical conditions & disabilities (damn vaccines/Big pHARMa!🤬) — and even though I’ve been off all of the meds for a number of years, BOTH because the meds totally messed up with/screwed up my metabolism, appetite and sleep & energy levels, AND because I’m pretty sure I have insulin resistance (whether as a result of the other issues, or separately, I’m not sure!), I’ve been finding it difficult, if not IMPOSSIBLE to lose that weight ever since and I still weigh the same or maybe even somewhat MORE than I did when I first started trying to lose weight many years ago.

Now although, if I recall correctly, I only first found out the low-carb/keto diet in my mid-30s (in/around 2012), it is FAR from the first time I attempted to lose weight, and FAR from the first diet I've tried. Weight Watchers, Slim-Fast, low-fat diet and/or low-calorie diet, KISS diet, even cabbage-soup diet........I've tried ‘em all, and lost count of just how many!

Unfortunately, the problem is that, regardless of which diet it is/was, I inevitably always end up cheating due to feeling deprived, bitter & resentful. Especially since I gained all this weight through no real fault of my own — well, other than blind, naïve, and in retrospect, TOTALLY FOOLISH trust in doctors and the so-called  “modern medicine” system (damn Big pHARMa cartel/mafia!🤬) when I was barely out of my teens, literally starting only a couple months after my 20th birthday. Also, because, even during the time that I DID stick to those diets, I never even really LOST any weight anyway, I'd become disillusioned and start cheating. After which I'd usually end up going off the diet completely and binging on the foods/drinks previously prohibited/discouraged, with the inevitable result of gaining even MORE weight.

Yet, because, UNLIKE other diets (Weight Watchers, Slim-Fast, low-fat and/or low-calorie, KISS diet, cabbage-soup diet, etc.) when I HAVE been able to stay on the low-carb/keto diet, it HAS worked for me (I lost over 20 lbs when I stuck with it!) I don't want to go back to something that didn't work for me, like Weight Watchers or Slim-Fast and I don't want to try something new, that's basically the same thing like Jenny Craig, or Nutri-system. As such, I am always on the lookout for good low-carb/keto foods and particularly, “keto-friendly” equivalents for high(er) carb items to hopefully keep me from feeling deprived & resentful, and eventually cheating or even going off the low-carb/keto diet entirely.

So when I saw the [[ASIN:B07VHMSH3H Ketond KetoKarb — Keto Approved Low-Glycemic Carbohydrate Energy]] powder listed on my Amazon VINE products page, I knew I had to try it immediately ordered it, in Peach Mango (if I recall correctly, the only flavor available/offered through VINE) thinking that I could drink it if & whenever I had the craving for fresh fruit, which is NOT allowed on keto — and which is probably the food that I miss/crave the most (and which I usually end up first cheating for), and for which I’ve yet to find a decent keto substitute!

So I got this [[ASIN:B07VHMSH3H Ketond KetoKarb]] and then sometime after that (not exactly the next time, because it took me awhile to work up the courage to try it after a few bad experiences with other similar keto products like [[ASIN:B07H7PCX9Y KetoLogic KetoEnergy Grape BHB]]) when I was hungry and craving fresh fruit, I reached for this Peach-Mango [[ASIN:B07VHMSH3H Ketond KetoKarb]]. The directions say to mix 1 scoop of [[ASIN:B07VHMSH3H KetoKarb]] with 8-10 oz of water or “your favorite beverage” — and because carbonated beverages usually give me the feeling of being full, resulting in a kind of appetite control (by both extending the length of time before becoming hungry & wanting/needing to eat, AND reducing the amount of food needing to be eaten) I prefer carbonated beverages, though NOT conventional regular or diet sodas. Instead, I drink zero-carb/zero-calorie stevia-sweetened sodas (such as [[ASIN:B00ZK6H5HU Zevia Ginger Ale]] or other flavors) and unsweetened sparkling water (like [[ASIN:B078ZVL3V9 Bübly]] and [[ASIN:B07812QWNH LaCroix]]) when I’m starting to feel hungry to delay eating, and/or with meals to be filled up even with smaller portions of food.

As such, when I finally decided (admittedly, awhile after first getting it) to try this [[ASIN:B07VHMSH3H KetoKarb]] powder, since it was a Peach-Mango flavor, I mixed it with most of a 12 oz can of unsweetened [[ASIN:B078ZVMMF9 Bübly Mango Sparkling Water]]. Although the flavor was GREAT and I LOVED it, I was disappointed that the powder would NOT dissolve. I made the drink by pouring a scoop of the [[ASIN:B07VHMSH3H KetoKarb]] powder, into one of my [[ASIN:B07QQVHLZF Fountain Shoppe Classic 12-Ounce Clear Milkshake/Ice-Cream Soda Glasses]] and mixed in 8-10 oz of my favorite (well. not *exactly* favorite beverage, definitely in the top faves!) beverage, [[ASIN:B078ZVMMF9 Bübly Mango Sparkling Water]] as the directions say. But despite stirring it for ages and even using my [[ASIN:B00V3UGRAI Eparé Electric Whisk]] to try to blend it, the powder sank to the bottom of the glass and just sat there. I don’t know why, but no matter what I tried/used, this powder just WOULD. NOT. DISSOLVE!

It’s a shame really, since if it weren’t for that, I would’ve given this product 5 stars.

Because when Peach-Mango [[ASIN:B07VHMSH3H KetoKarb]] is mixed with Mango [[ASIN:B078ZVMMF9 Bübly Sparkling Water]] (and maybe Peach as well — I‘ve never tried it myself, so I don’t know, but it is another option) it makes a delicious and KETO-friendly fruity soda WITHOUT the sugar and carbs and other junk in regular sodas. But even though I LOVE the taste, I do NOT love the big lump/pile/clump of white powder that pools at the bottom of the glass — and this issue (and ONLY this issue!) has kept me from having/using this [[ASIN:B07VHMSH3H Ketond KetoKarb — Keto Approved Low-Glycemic Carbohydrate Energy]] powder more than once so far. Due to the fact that I’ve only had [[ASIN:B07VHMSH3H KetoKarb]] that one time, I cannot speak as to its energy-boosting ability, nor any other potential benefits.   That being said, assuming one can get past the mound of white powder at the bottom of the glass, and related cloudy-ish appearance of the drink itself, this [[ASIN:B07VHMSH3H Ketond KetoKarb — Keto Approved Low-Glycemic Carbohydrate Energy]] is a pretty good keto option for those looking to satisfy a craving for fruit. While its NOT the same as biting into a fresh, juicy peach or mango, and nobody/nothing can completely replicate it, especially when mixed with Mango [[ASIN:B078ZVMMF9 Bübly Sparkling Water]] it DOES come pretty close!

text:
I prefer glass files, because they last forever and you can even file painted nails and clean them up with acetone. Plus the grit is usually pretty gentle. My boyfriend put a pot down on my old favorite file, so I thought I should get this set with the carrying case.

I have mixed feelings about these files. I love the protective case and the fact that it comes with so many files. I put one in my car, one at work, and have backups in the little carrier in the living room with my nail polish. The files work really well, too. However I'm not sure what's going on with them! In my experience, glass files have a permanent etching. This doesn't really wear off because it is in the glass itself. These particular files seem to have some sort of abrasive coating instead of the etching. After moderate use, the filing part has sort of scraped off. It didn't photograph well unfortunately, but I can now see clear shiny glass in some areas. They no longer file in that spot!

Overall, these files are fine but won't last forever like normal glass files. I'll definitely be keeping the case after they all die, though.

title: Didn't fit waterpik holder and operates differently!
text:
This replacement water pik is pretty average in all regards. It installed easily, but the first thing you'll find out, likely by surprise, is that the valve is normally open, unlike the actual original water pik! What this means is that when you start the pump, water immediately flows out; you have to hold the button down to stop water! The button also gets stuck in the closed position quite often, and I've decided to dump mine after recently getting stuck again. The pik also doesn't fit the holder in the main water pik device. Also, given that the valve is normally open, after you're done, any water in the reservoir will keep flowing out. This means that you might end up with a puddle somewhere if you don't empty the tank after use, and it means that the pump will need some time to repressurize before working again.

Definitely stick to another manufacturer or the original.

title: Sweet cushion
text:
Let me first say, I was having numb leg issues from my home office chair. Let's be honest, prior to Mid-March I didn't use my home office chair much. Working from home forced me to rethink comfort. I use this cushion every day. It stays in my office chair.
I am a large woman. I needed something that was going to support my weight and give me a buffer between the chair and my body. I watched a lot of youtube video reviews to come to my choice. The reviews I paid attention to were people who spent their full-time jobs sitting (over the road haulers) and who were overweight. Two big things I took away from watching those: never ever leave your cushion in a hot vehicle and the nature of the materials (the purple) after time and body shifting your cushion can start to escape (you end up feeling like you might slide out). Easily fixed by tucking the back edges between the seat and the back of the chair. I ended up finding this configuration ends up relieving the pressure off my thighs that were previously causing numbness. About every third time I get up, I end up re-tucking the cornerback between the seat and the back of the chair. It does get annoying at times but is far better than what I was dealing with before.
Bottom line: get this cushion because your rear and your thighs will thank you.

title: Good storage, nice size
text:
I've used these containers for a while. First ones were from a supermarket chain. Only difference seems to be four little circular shapes on the corners of the lid. The containers are great. Just the right size for one or two servings of soup or chile or something similar. I have stacks of them in my freezer waiting to thaw and provide a meal on non cooking days.

Now for the downside of durability. The lids are a bit weak and they will split if not treated with care. The problem seems to be exacerbated by putting hot food in the fridge or freezer with the lid sealed. My fix for this is to let the food cool on the stove until it is warm. Put it in the containers and seal the lids on one side only and put them in the fridge overnight. The next day I seal the remaining sides of the lids and put the containers in the freezer or leave them in the fridge if they are to be used within a day or two. Similarly, I take the containers out of the freezer and let them unfreeze overnight in the fridge. Next day the lids come open with out trouble.

title: Great product, lightly scented
text:
I just received this product yesterday. I decided to use it right away because I'm starting a new yoga class tomorrow and wanted my mat to be fresh and clean since I can't recall the last time I've cleaned it, and it's also been a whole since I've used it. (Yikes. Lol)

I received my Asutra spray quickly, within the two day Prime window as promised. I noticed coming out of the package there was a faint scent, but the bottle didn't seem to be leaking. Probably just got jostled in transit.

After reading the label, I decided to go with the deep-cleaning option. Also, after seeing that other reviewers used a white towel on their first cleaning, I decided to try the same. Wow, I was impressed with the results.

So here's my take:

I shook up the bottle, as directed. I thoroughly sprayed down the "up" side of my mat, the side I usually face. It took a pretty decent amount of product to make sure the mat was covered, but not soaking wet. I let it sit for a few minutes (instead of just the recommended two, because I was doing other chores) and then took a damp, wet, cotton towel to the mat. I folded it in half, and rubbed in circles, starting at one end of the mat, and working my way to the other end. After the "up" side air dried, I flipped it over to clean the "bottom," the side that usually touches the floor, and repeated the process. I have not yet used the blue micro fiber cloth that came with it, but will likely carry that with me in my tote to clean after sessions.

Here are some pros:

•Pleasant, lightweight, quickly dissipating scent. I ordered the "uplifting eucalyptus," because I'm lavender-ed out. Lol
•The product is very lightweight, and did not leave any obvious residue on the mat, nor my hands. It didn't feel oily, and I didn't notice.
•After cleaning, my mat looked so fresh and so much better, and no longer looked dingy and old.
•I received my order in a timely manner, in new condition, and it was accurate.

Some cons:

•None, really. I did notice that if you don't shake the bottle well enough, the spritzer kind of "spits" droplets out, instead of a perfect mist, but this was easily and immediately remedied by shaking the bottle again. This would be the case with any bottle of this type.
•I read in other reviews that they experienced residue on their mats upon first using it after cleaning with this product. If I experience that, I'll be sure to update my review to include details.

Overall, I am pleased and would recommend this product!

text:
For the past 18 months I had been using the Contour Next monitor, and it was showing elevated fasting glucose readings. I had completely changed my lifestyle, and lost almost 80lbs, and STILL my fasting glucose would not go below 100. I was feeling frustrated and resigned to accepting the fact that I may indeed by dx with Type 2, regardless of diet and exercise. My husband suggesting getting a new meter to see if the readings were the same. So I decided to pick up the One Touch, since I was familiar with this brand (dx with gestational diabetes 14 years ago).

I have been testing with both the Contour and the One Touch. The Contour shows my fasting levels between 100-120. The One Touch has me consistently between 99-100. This morning, Contour read 118, One Touch read 100. So there appears to be an 18-point swing between the two meters. When you're watching your glucose, those points matter!

I will be getting lab work done soon, and will compare the lab results with the One Touch, and update my review.

Pros:

Cons to knock it down to 4 stars:

4) you can secretly monitor your roommates weight until they set themselves up on fitbit.com. All guest weights are shown to the fitbit authorized owner. Once you invite a friend, they sign up, and you point those guest weights to the friend, the friends weight is hidden for good.

Pretty slick device.

Wants:
network cable support
the timer when the scale goes dark to be longer or even configurable

title: Don't know why, but these help.
text: I ordered this product because I had done a little reading on probiotics and "learned" that you need a lot of them to be effective.  I found these on Amazon and decided to give them a try.  I have had stomach difficulties for years - had an endoscopy almost 4 years ago because I was having sharp pain shooting off to primarily the left side of my body at the top of my rib cage.  I have no acid reflux - just these sharp pains.  The endoscopy came out well - no Barrett's esophagus or other apparent stomach problems.  Was told by the gastroenterologist  to take 2 Prilosec per day.  Fast forward 3 years and the pains continued plus extreme bouts of belching.  A friend told me to start taking acidophilus which I did and I  started taking 2 probiotic gummy chews twice per day.  This seemed to help somewhat.  About 3 months ago I ordered these probiotics.  Almost immediately I saw a decline in the episodes of the pain I was having.  Three months later and I can count on both hands the number of episodes I have had.  The sharp pain and the belching have subsided tremendously.  I saw my gastro specialist just last week because I am concerned about any damage that might have been done from the pains, and told him that the episodes have decreased a lot after taking these capsules.  He was very reluctant to give any credence to my claims, which I understand, since he is not inclined to advise someone to take something that is not regulated.  I am scheduled for another endoscopy next month to make sure all is well.  All I can say is what I have personally experienced.  I just know that since I have been taking these probiotics I have been doing much better.

This case is just OK. A definite improvement over the old case and has a slimmer profile.
There are a couple of issues with this case:
1. It's not easy to pop the pump in and out of the case.
2. With so many cutouts for the charger, the reservoir and to pop out the reservoir, it seems the pump is still pretty exposed to being damaged if accidentally dropped.

I wish they would just develop a clip for the pump --without a case. I wore my Medtronic pump with the clip for years on end and never had a problem. title: Perfect cheap alternative to the Force of Nature appliance.
text:
This usb-C cable powered electrolyzer comes with a usb-A to usb-C cable. Plug it in to a newer cell phone charger for best results.
Its mist sprayer head is standard size so when it eventually fails any cheap Amazon-ed continuous spray bottle can be used to replace it!
I use this to make hypochlorous acid disinfectant. If you don't use vinegar, you end up with a bleaching solution.
I fill past the 250mL line to the line at the top, and with a funnel I add 1/4 tsp. non-iodized table salt, 1/2 tsp. white vinegar, mix, and electrolyze.
The run time is 5 minutes, which gets me to 200-250 ppm free chlorine, exactly where it needs to be! It chirps when it is finished, and the light turns off.
If you run it again by pressing the power button again, you get 500ppm-- a stronger disinfectant and cleaner for tougher messes.
My final pH is 5.3, also right where it needs to be.
I can confidently follow these steps over and over without weighing ingredients and get consistent results.

The disinfectant has a 2 week to 1 month shelf life, but I always use it up before then.

The only failing this product has is the lack of a silicone Usb-C port plug. I've accidentally gotten water in the port a few times. You can pick some up on Amazon for cheap.

All in all, the expensive Force of Nature machine will go to my mother because it is truly beautiful, and this amazing thing will stay with me.

title: Not enough stars!
text:
We have two of our four dogs crate trained. Their crates are in one of our extra guest bedrooms. Now before all of you PETA loving people have anything to say, our dogs love their crates. We’ve made it their homes, and they are never in for long periods of time.

One of the dogs in the crates is a labradoodle, the other is my giant baby, our English mastiff, Athena. Now Athena is my child from before me and my fiancé got together, so she is really really my baby, although before all you non-favoriting parents (we all know your lying and you really do have favorites) have anything to say, I treat them all equally. So Athena is flawless, but she does have something called excessive drool.

Her daily routine consists of shaking when I wake her up and when shaking, throwing her drool all over me, the walls, and anything else in a 10 foot radius. Needless to say, the walls now needed to be cleaned.

So I get this amazing idea that I’m going to surprise my fiancé and clean the base boards and the walls. Little did I know this was going to be a real project. I get super prepared, at least I thought so. I have rags, paper towels, 409, and anything other cleaning supply that isn’t supposed to be used on walls (they’ve got to be lying to me right? It just means it’s super powerful) with me ready to tackle this monster of a wall. Two hours later I haven’t even made a dent. But I’m determined and keep cleaning. Dried drool on the wall is a nightmare FYI.

So about 30 minutes later my fiancé comes in, and she’s laughing because I’m sweating my butt off, I’ve stripped to my boxers only, and I’m cleaning this stupid drool off this stupid wall, and I haven’t made any progress at all. She laughs more, I get mad, and well you know how bickering goes. So she comes back in the room and tells me to use this tool.

I mean it’s a freaking white sponge, I’ve used every dang chemical I could find in the house. I laugh laugh and say that’s never ever going to work. This dumb little baby sponge is not going to do the job. So just to show her up, I use this thing after putting some water on it. Much to my surprise it starts coming off, and not just a little, all of it is coming off super easy. So I pretend like it’s not working, sit in there another 2 hours (even though I was done after 30 mins and 3 magic erasers later) and then tell her I finally finished. I tell her how terrible the eraser was and blah blah blah how I had to tackle it like a man. Put some elbow grease on it, and got it done.

Well I messed up in my plans because I realized that I used the last 3 magic erasers in the house. She doesn’t typically clean until the weekend and this was late Sunday, so I’ve got about a week to sneak them in the house and pretend like nothing ever happened. I hop on amazon, and see they are pretty decently priced. Then I start to reminisce and remember how awesome they worked I get excited, forgetting about our argument, and how I had to be right, and I decide to order 5 boxes of 8 of these. Completely forgetting that they will be at the house in 2 days with amazon prime.

Well two days later here we are. I’m happy I received 40 magic erasers, but boy am I in some trouble. These are essential to any cleaning job. I don’t even care what it is. I’m going to be using one. I might even use it to clean a clean wall just because it’s so satisfying.

Thanks for reading and good luck cleaning. By the way, this is a true story.

P.S. Don’t feel bad for my fiancé, I’m the one always getting in trouble for nothing.

Product is still amazing, we keep tons of these at the house, and still recommend this product to everybody (yes, even you PETA lovers, isn’t that nice of me?).

title: Don't overlook Amazon's Solimo
text:
Chapped, dry, and bleeding hands are no joke and I have probably experienced the worst it can get while working in a machine shop (prior to CNC) and doing assorted mechanic work out in my garage. When really dry, it felt like my hands were going to fall off at the wrists, and I'll always remember the excruciating pain.

It was some time around the 1960's that specialty hand soaps for mechanics began appearing in the car parts stores. They were a bit of a miracle to watch as the gel just effortlessly lifted all that grease off the hands. But this new miracle solution worked so well it would also dry out the hands until years later when somebody thought to include lanolin in the mix. That finally changed everything for mechanics who no longer had to show up at the dinner table with grease still embedded in their dry, chapped, and bleeding hands.

Up until then there was LAVA soap (still in production today) but that's like scrubbing your hands with a brick. The highly abrasive mixture would sting and didn't work well on dry chapped hands, doing nothing to help heal them or diminish the pain involved. There were some special lotions like Corn Huskers and Vaseline Jelly (probably the oldest) for repairing dry, sick skin, but it would be used up too quickly and it might take weeks before remembering to buy more.

Now that I'm retired I haven't had dry skin or bleeding fingers for the past ten years, but it doesn't mean the hands still won't chap when neglected. Vaseline Medicated Intensive Care lotion was my favorite up until they took it out of production, nearly putting me into a panic. Vaseline introduced a replacement that worked even better, called Vaseline Deep Moisturizing lotion with 30% Petrolatum and had the same consistency as tooth paste. A little dab will do ya' on the back of the hands on a daily basis. But I quit buying it recently because Vaseline now contracts it out to other cosmetic companies, and the price is soaring to about $10 for 4.5 ounces while the quality continues to go south. So now I'm using Amazon's Solimo, likely made using Vaseline's own 100% White Petrolatum Jelly that has proven for a couple of centuries now to be better and Amazon has it priced lower than everything else.

There really is no need for anyone to suffer from dry, rough skin with the hundreds of lotions and treated soaps that are now available, all intended to remove that greasy feeling that women make very obvious how much they despise. Typically, most men couldn't care less how it feels provided it does what it claims. The best ones all seem to contain at least one ingredient of either lanolin, or petrolatum, or glycerin, and even menthol. There is a whole flock of ingredients listed in other products that have such long complicated names they can't even be pronounced. Oddly enough, those are the same ones that cost the most, whereas my little 7.5 ounce jar of Solimo that cost three bucks only contains just one ingredient: 100% White Petrolatum Jelly. A little dab on the back of the hand soaks into the skin quickly and the jar will last a couple of years positively keeping my hands absolutely free of dry, chapped, and bleeding fingers. And for that, I am very thankful. So there you go.

title: Wait a minute! It's good, but...
text:
"LED lights indicate charging.
There are three LED lights on the charger that indicate batteries have been correctly loaded and charging current is being delivered. The LEDs will shut off when charging is complete. Current will stop flowing to batteries at this time."

--------------------------------------

Above is an exerpt of the product description provided by Rayovac. It is somewhat misleading since two major gaffs are being made:
1. Only the LED for the channels that have batteries connected will light up. There are three separate channels.
2. Charging automatically stops after eight hours, and not before eight hours of charging has occured.

The model number of the charger I received is PS20A and a pdf with the same instructions I received with the charger appears when doing a google search for this charger. There is some discrepancy since the above comments from Rayovac might have you believing that once the batteries have a full charge the three LEDs on the charger will go out, and charging stops when a full charge is achieved prior to eight hours of charging.

Unfortunately, there is nothing stated in the directions that support that. Nor was any of that found to be true during actual use of the charger.

As such, I ran the charger for 8 hours on new batteries I received with the charger. It is stated on the packaging that rechargeable batteries will retain at least 80% of the full charge they were sent out with for 6 months. In actual use the charger went the full eight hours before the LEDs went out, only supporting the statement in the instructions that charging will automatically stop after eight hours.

Judging from the statements in the Rayovac ad, Rayovac would have us believing that charging should have stopped within just a few hours and the LEDs should have gone out at that time. Well, it doesn't happen that way.

The main gripe with all the other chargers is that there is no indication of how much charge the batteries actually have without purchasing additional testing equipment just for that purpose. So it looks like Rayovac is trying to convince buyers that their charger does more than the others when in actually, the full extent of its additional abilities is merely to shut itself off after eight hours of operation.

As in all the others, this charger will recharge the batteries, but there is no positive indication if the batteries have received a full charge within those eight hours while the charger remains in operation. That is a big difference from implying that charging will automatically stop when the batteries are fully charged. There is no indication this charger is capable of doing that.

Plug it in when you want to recharge your batteries, and in eight hours it will automatically shut iteself off. That's probably sufficient assurance for most that the batteries will be fully charged and there will be less possibility of burning out the charger or the batteries. However, in contrast to Rayovac's misleading statement, the possibilities of burnout still exist, so it's probably best to deplete the batteries as much as possible before connecting them for a boost in energy again.

Now, aren't you glad to know that!

title: Another option for straightening hair!
text:
I straighten my hair almost every day - it's pretty much a must for me - so when I had the opportunity to try this hair brush straightener, I jumped at the thought of finding an easier, more convenient way to straighten my hair. The upside? It definitely does straighten my hair! If I divide my hair into sections (like I would with the straightener) and brush the small sections at a time, my hair does get straight (almost) as well as it does with the straightener. The downside? I had hoped this would be a quicker, easier solution than my straightener...and it just wasn't. I got ALMOST the same results in about the same amount of time. For me, it wasn't enough of a difference to switch from the use of my straightener on a permanent basis.

My hair is medium thickness with a slight wave to it and I set the temperature at 450 degrees. I think I probably spent about 15 to 20 minutes with this brush straightener (the same amount of time I spend with my regular straightener). My hair has been difficult to straighten with some straighteners as well, so my hair could be part of the issue! If you are looking for a new way to straighten your hair and your hair is not difficult to straighten, I would definitely suggest giving it a try...maybe it'll work better than a straightener for you!

The hair brush straightener is well-made, high quality, and as described. I was surprised that I didn't burn my head with the straightener, but it does have protections in place for that (anti-scalding tips). I received this product for free in exchange for my honest review.

title: Go for the Lean 1, Skip the Chocolate Flavored and go for the Cookies and Cream!!!
text: I'm in love with the Cookies and Cream and the Lean 1 Shake quality. The taste of the chocolate however, is slightly bitter and bland. It's one that I felt like I had to keep adding more scoops or sweetened chocolate cashew milk. I always mix my shakes with milk (usually Horizon Organic, lactose free 1% milk (has a creamier texture and lower glycemic rate than other brands) or Silk Coconut Almond unsweetened milk with which we add frozen bananas for a great flavor .For a dessert for the family we might add some of the Silk Chocolate Cashew Milk (sweetened) I also have combined it with another chocolate flavored powder with plant nutrients for an extra boost. I'm buying some cocoa powder tomorrow to see if that helps it a bit. I always serve it blended with ice. In the morning I add a low acid instant coffee to make a frozen frappuccino type drink. My Dad and teenage son both love it. I really notice a difference in how we feel when we drink it. I haven't really used it for weightloss though I have lost some needed weight as a result of combined efforts. I have chronic nausea and this is something I can tolerate fairly well. I use 2+ scoops for the chocolate one but with the ice and milk it makes enough for 2-3 people to enjoy. The cookies and cream I might use 1 1/2. I do not like it with just water. It definitely needs something else to give it a shake like favor and consistency. It's pricey definitely but I look at the price of a good quality cup of coffee with creamer at home or a breakfast or lunch and I realize it's the initial sting that's tough (single mom on a fixed income) it all pans out to be a good deal, especially given the high quality ingredients. This is by far the best protein shakes I've ever had aside from slimfast (I know sounds like a crazy comparison but some of us have a decade of acquired taste for that horribly unhealthy but tasty and sugary powder!) I researched for over a year to find something of this quality and that agrees with my system as well as not tweak with my blood sugar levels and this is it! Warning...the cookies and cream does have higher sugars than the chocolate or possibly the others but nothing so significant that it affects me adversely. My advice- Skip the chocolate, buy the Cookies and Cream in the larger canister. It lasts longer than it seems and like I said, I find myself using less and getting more. ENJOY!

The gun I received has a handle that looks like a modern .357 or .44 revolver - not like the handle pictured. Although the gun looks modern, it has a thumb release door to allow one cylinder bore at a time for loading - like an old single action cowboy gun. title: small, easy fitting, easy to use, sound ok, battery life ok.
text:
I bought these for my mom. she lost one of her 3700$ fancy shmancy hearing aids, and with insurance they wanted 500$ as a deductible to replace one. Fortunately she found the missing hearing aid, so in the interim I found her these.

she uses them from time to time and with all the mask mandates, they are easier than the behind the ear fancy shmancy 3700 dollar ones she got from the ear doc. These work ok (I have tried them), but they are prone to get feedback (thus the reasonable price). You move them around a bit in your ear and they are good for a while. Sometimes for reasons unknown to me, they just start feeding back. I have good ears and can hear them feeding back from across the room. And watching my mom jump up in her seat is kinda funny too (ok maybe a little cruel of me, but still funny). Also I told my mom to cup her hand over the hearing aid and if it feeds back, then they are on. if they don't, then the battery is dead.

the only real draw back is the volume control is SOOO small and hard to turn, they are very difficult to adjust just right.

Overall for the price they are fine. if you need hearing aids and don't want to, or can't fork out thousands of dollars, these could do the trick for you.

title: Not for me...
text: I encountered two major problems with this product.  The first is that the taste is horrible and I can see why consumers are instructed to dilute the liquid in water.  But in my case no matter how much water I used it still had a terrible taste that was completely off putting.  The second issue, and probably most important of the two for me, is that this product set off pain in my esophagus area.  I've had problems like this when eating or drinking certain foods or beverages for quite awhile, but as long as I'm careful with what I choose to eat or drink I'm fine.  So this is something that applies to me personally and I'm not saying that I think this will be the result for everyone.  I just included this information for others who are considering trying this product and have issues with their esophagus or stomach to be vigilant.  I'm convinced that even lowering the amount of the product would not help and I don't want to try anyway and take a chance that I will get that burning pain.  I see in a response by a company representative that buyers can get a refund.  I will contact the company and find out how to go about getting a refund as this product is kind of pricey. (By the way, I purchased Dr. Dean's book and found it helpful although I don't recall seeing any warnings that told readers there could be a reaction like mine with pain in my esophagus.  I didn't read the book thoroughly, however, so I may have missed this if it is included.)  1/7/21 Just an addition to mention that I did get a full refund for the two containers that I ordered.  The refund was processed promptly which I appreciate.  Everyone reacts to medicinal products differently, so my issue may very well be rare.  I changed my rating to two stars from just one star because I can see that this company does care and wants to satisfy customers.  I still gave a low rating only to bring my situation to the attention of other readers in case they might see themselves running into the same issue that I did with my physical reaction to the liquid magnesium.

title: Short battery life, doesn't work on carpet
text: This thing is horrible. It just runs in circles over the same areas until you move it. It does not run in straight lines. The battery dies quickly. It stops with lights flashing and beeping, but there's no troubleshooting that I can find that matches the flashing and beeping pattern. The dirt tank is so small that you will be emptying it constantly. I have to disassemble the brushes at least three times during one cycle. IT DOES NOT WORK ON CARPET! I have low pile carpet in my living room and it gets stuck and starts beeping and flashing every time. I can only use this in two rooms, my dining room and my kitchen and both rooms have hard floors with no rugs or carpeting. This machine can not even handle those. Neither room is large. My dining room is only big enough to hold the 48" table and 4 dining chairs that are in it and my kitchen isn't even six feet wide. I have to move the chairs out of the room so that the vacuum will go under the table otherwise it just keeps banging into the same chair. The vacuum ignores the invisible wall that came with it; it goes into the living room even though the invisible wall is there to stop it. It doesn't matter if I put fresh batteries or if there are old batteries in the invisible wall. Yes, I have it facing the right way. Yes, I have dogs. However, I have to go through the two rooms and pick up any large pieces of dog hair and all pieces of dog food before I can run the vacuum. The app is a joke. It offers the ability to set a schedule so that the vacuum will run automatically, but that doesn't work. I set it up to run at 12:00 PM everyday, but it only worked once. You're supposed to be able to start and dock the vacuum with the app, but those features don't work, either. Honestly, it's faster if I just do the floors myself than if I let this thing run. I am so sorry I wasted my hard earned money on this vacuum. There were so many other things I could have done with it, but I thought it would save me time while I chased my toddler around the house. I was very wrong! Unfortunately, I can not return this because I missed the return window by one day. That's my own fault, but the fact that this is an AWFUL VACUUM is solely on Hoover!

title: ALLERGIC REACTION: HIVES ALL OVER BODY
text:
When I first got EOS lip balm at the convenience store, both in Summer fruit and Jojoba, I really loved the smells and texture. They made my lips feel great! And all was well and good UNTIL my boyfriend broke out in HIVES.

HIVES. all over his body. swollen lips, eyes, face, hands. It looked like the worst bug bite attack, ever. We were so scared that they would spread to his throat, but luckily the Benadryl brought them down after a few hours. We thought it might have been a food allergy. My boyfriend tells me that he has no food allergies, and has never had hives or any other kind of allergic reaction. And all was well and good UNTIL it happened again! The only similarity to his exposure to allergens was the EOS lip balm that I was using. This reaction was far worse and lasted far longer. Luckily, he had no breathing problems and is doing fine now. After a bit of research on google, it seems that allergic reactions to EOS lip balm are not unheard of, and are more prevalent when using Summer Fruit, Strawberry, or other mixed berry flavors.

I really liked the product. It made my lips feel amazing. But it's in the trash now, and I am telling everyone I know to pay attention in case of allergic reaction. EOS should figure out which ingredient is the allergen and put it on their label, because this is pretty serious.

title: They changed the recipe, its not the same as before
text:
This is not the same product I've been getting for the last year. They changed the formula, added stronger mint and lemon and it does not taste as good as the old product. I spoke with customer service at Silver Biotics, they said that these new drops have more silver in them, but the flavor is awful. The recipe used to be simply organic brown rice syrup, manuka honey, silver solution 60 ppm and organic mint flavor. Now its evaporated cane syrup, tapioca syrup, honey, the silver solution, a much stronger peppermint flavor, lemon flavor, citric acid, lactic acid...the flavor of the drop is not the same and I'm very disappointed in this new product and will no longer buy it. I've complained to Silver Biotics and I hope others who agree with me will do the same so maybe they'll go back to the old formulation. As far as I'm concerned they took a perfectly wonderful product and ruined it.
Update: I had an upper respiratory infection, tried several lozenges and these did seem to work the best. I added back one star. Funny, they taste better after using some of the others, which didn't taste very good at all. I really wish it was just mint and not lemon, this formula has a medicinal taste the old formula didn't. But, they do seem to work well.

title: Drink for breakfast
text:
I've never liked aojiru or green juice, it's just gross to me, but my diet this past summer was pretty bad so I thought I should try it in hopes to somewhat balance out my system. I found this "morning fruit aojiru" (translated name of product) from Yakult, the company famous for its probiotic yogurt drinks, and decided to try it. I usually don't eat breakfast (which I know is also bad), so I started to to drink this in place of of it. I figure it's better to have something in my stomach rather than nothing, and it's easy to fit into my mornings when I'm always running around. As for the taste, well, it's a mild fruity aojiru. The aojiru flavor is toned down by the fruits, which does make it easier to drink, but for me, I can still taste the aojiru and it's not something I'd savor. Since the amount is small enough, it's easy to drink up really fast though, lol. As for its effects, I don't have any numbers or evidence to show that this is working in any way, but my mind and body does feel more calm every morning since I started drinking it (I guzzle down extra water afterwards too). FYI, I am in no way suggesting that this can be used as a breakfast replacement, or that it has to be consumed in the morning. It's just an easy way to supplement your body with greens (and fruits, in this case), no matter the time of day.

Here is the translated info of the product, to the best of my knowledge, if it helps in any way:

Ingredients: barley grass extract powder (dextrin, barley grass extract), apple juice powder (dextrin, apple juice), banana powder, fructose, apple fibers, glucose, mango powder (dextrin, mango), acerola powder, flavoring agent, (part of the raw materials include apples and bananas)

The barley grass is grown with lots of labor and care, without pesticides and chemical fertilizers, by farmers in the Kunisaki Peninsula and surrounding areas of Oita Prefecture, Japan, who are contracted with Yakult.

Popular fruits such as bananas, mangos, apples, and acerola are blended in, which include the fibers derived from these fruits as well as vitamin C.

Suggested consumption: one packet a day, mixed with 1/4 cup of hot or cold water, milk, or other preferred drinks. Can also be mixed with various foods such as yogurt. (Japanese measurements are slightly different from the U.S., and their suggested amount of 75ml translates to about 1/4 cup -- I measured it using both Japanese and U.S. measuring cups)

Other notes: avoid making it ahead of time, and consume immediately once opened; there may be slight discoloration due processed plant material, but this does not affect the quality; consult with your physician before consuming if you are pregnant, breastfeeding, or on medication; check ingredients if you have any food allergies; although rare, stop consuming if it doesn't agree with your body; store this away from small children; be careful not to cut yourself on the edges of the packet

title: This is 99.99% water as admitted on the label
text:
I grabbed a spray bottle of this to do some kitchen counter cleanup. Sprayed it on and it looks, feels and acts like WATER. So I touched a small quantity of it to my tongue.... tastes like WATER. So I asked my wife if she had filled one of the bottles with water to use for some other purpose. "Nope, that's the product."

So I read the label. "Eco-friendly" --yep, just like water. "Natural" -- yep, just like water. And they say "produced with pure water, salt, and electricity" -- yep, just like reverse osmosis water you may have coming from your tap. "Neutral pH" - just like water though it supposedly contains hypochlorous acid.

Hypochlorous acid is one of the chlorine bleaches, though less harsh than your laundry bleach. You will get some surface disinfection from it, but I sure rather have something else to remove dirt, grime and grease.

Two ingredients in the whole bottle, one of which essentially makes it chlorinated water. I'm betting it costs next to nothing to make, but sold at close to a dollar an ounce! And sold to the gullible by appealing to their sense of environmental responsibility.

title: Big Mask For A Big Head.
text:
The Good:

Fits a big old head.

I've bought probably 12 different masks from a wide variety of sellers hoping one could fit my gigantic head. Most masks will either slip off my nose or slip off my chin when talking or, god forbid, laughing or yawning. This is the first mask that actually keeps good coverage over my nose and bottom of my chin even when stress testing contorted facial expressions. The adjustable ear straps are very comfortable and the well designed neck strap is a really nice touch you don't really notice you need until you have used it. Great for situations in parks or running errands when you need to take it on and off.

The (kind of) bad:

As some mentioned a nose wire would be helpful but easily found very cheaply on Amazon to add. Also the XL is so large that the filters I have don't fill the space completely. I try to position it to just around my mouth but will move around during the day. This isn't entirely their fault and if I could find filters made for this size it would be 100% my new goto mask.

Highly recommended for my big noggin' brother and sisters out there who have either dealt with ear pain or nose and chin "slippage". Love that they are US based and sourced and their story is pretty cool too. Started by a kid making buttons when he was ten years old and now run by his family and a union based workforce.

title: I used a newly purchased MagicEraser on an easy job - a mark on a smooth tile - ...
text:
This used to be my go-to product when nothing else worked for the toughest marks on walls, scratches on white cabinets, and just about anything one can think of (minus fabric). I've used them for years with incredible results. If the paint on a wall was one coat or a matte finish, an extremely gentle hand and lots of water in the "eraser" was a must, but always did the trick. Unfortunately, my last purchased box proved this product has been completely revamped. I used a newly purchased MagicEraser on an easy job - a mark on a smooth tile - and it didn't budge. It didn't even lighten. Yet, the Eraser began to completely crumble with barely any pressure. I grabbed another box in case it was a fluke, and the same thing occurred. A soft sponge with some Dawn (and no elbow grease) removed the mark with ease. Sadly, nothing now works on the tougher marks. Why did the manufacturer change a good thing?
If anyone finds a decent replacement, please share!

title: Ridiculously fragile
text:
I have been using these Magic Erasers since they came out. They are, hands down, excellent at cleaning almost anything you can imagine. One example of their cleaning power: I had a key fob for a car that originally had white words and pictographs on it. Over the years they had turned yellow from age and exposure to cigarette smoke. I tried several cleaning products on it and none of them could even begin to return them to their white color. I finally decided to try a magic eraser on it and it truly was like magic. With just a few quick wipes over it, they were sparkling white again.

Alas, I have to agree with many other reviews here on durability though. These are supposedly extra durable but they really are a joke. I've had them crumble in my hands even when using on smooth surfaces with little pressure (not much pressure is needed, by the way). While cleaning the walls in my pantry, I accidentally (but lightly) ran the eraser over a wire shelf. It instantly put a cut into it.

I found a different brand here on Amazon that claims to be more durable than the competition, so I just ordered some. They can't be much worse than these so-called extra durable Magic Erasers.

I keep this in our poorly ventilated bathroom to help air it out after use, and I do believe it genuinely helps.

The downsides are three fold. First, if you're sensitive to noises, stay clear of this or prepare to get used to it. I can hear it two rooms away when it's plugged in. I hated it for the first two weeks, then only sort of hated it, and eventually got used to it. I know I'm more sensitive to noise than most, though, so it may not bother you.

Second, the vents on the machine will clog frequently with dust and they are not easy to clean. I found a solution that works for me though - I use a doctor's toothpick and clean the vents with the frilly end. It works very well, and you know it's time to clean it when it's quiet enough that it doesn't bother you.

And third. I've had it just shy of a year and today the motor is making a constant "worn out" whine, so I think it's time to replace it. Not too bad for a whole year, but a shame I'll need a new one.

title: It is Okay, read all these comments before deciding.
text:
Some points:
Chair is very large, taller than any normal recliner and when it reclines back, it needs a good two feet open behind it... definitely not a wall hugger!
The documentation is pretty bad, barely English and in an odd order, like how to use it comes before how to assemble it
Assembly wasn't bad at all, but note that the chair is very heavy! You will need help moving it if any stairs at all are in play. Took two strong guys to lift it up two steps from garage to house.
The control panel is fixed on right side, and the keys are not lit, so I find it difficult to read the key labels in normal room lighting at night.
The controls are really kludgy... you really don't know what you are doing or what effect it really has. It runs these scenarios that you choose from... but then there are many controls for specific functions and I can't tell when I'm modifying a scenario or when I'm turning the scenario off and doing something else... the organization of the buttons is confusing at best
The startup procedure does a calibration, but you can't tell what you should be adjusting it to... no instructions on it ... it only says to sense your back and you adjust... but to what?
And the movable head or neck massaged: no instructions on how to adjust it properly... it seems that it should be obvious where to put the neck section, but it isn't ... shoulders? Neck? Lower skull? You can do any of these but I can't tell what is correct...
Chair is good for my 6'2" height... that was a big concern, but no problem... the foot section expands and I could definitely be even taller.
Oddly, my 5'2" wife is not tall enough for the chair to fit properly... her feet don't reach the foot rollers!
The massage: I'm finding it to be pretty good heat on my back, and the kneading of my back. The stretching modes do seem to work, but I think they could have more potential if the chair was programmed differently... it could stretch you more and better but it seems to have bugs in this area... for example, what it does is grab you laterally with airbags and then recline the chair which then stretches your spine in theory. What's old is that it doesn't activate the best shoulder bags, and the leg air bags grab you on the shins extremely tightly (actually hurts) but the shin bags don't let go until way after the other bags release, even as it goes back to upright, which feels a bit like it will break your legs... definitely do not wear jeans as the seam on the jeans digs in with the high air bag pressure.
It comes with headphones and will play MP3 from a USB stick... kinda cool, but note the controls are terrible... it tends to repeat songs and there is no mode to set that so I find I have to skip forward after every song. And most of the modes inflate the "stupid" air bags around your neck or head area making the headphones come off... you have to play with controls to find something that doesn't use those bags if you want to listen.
Othernthan the stretching, the airbags seem like they aren't worth that much for massaging.
I am finding I really just like the bag kneading and heat.. which I probably could have bought a chair at half or third of the price and gotten those features just as well. The extra money for this chair may not be worth it for some or many.
All said, I'm glad I have a massage chair, but honestly I wish I had bought a cheaper one with less features and a smaller chair that didn't use so much room.
But it does work....

title: Wrong Sounds are Amplified
text:
I've tried three different hearing aids, and this one comes in third place. My hearing is still good, but has been decreasing these past few years. I've been looking for inexpensive alternatives to spending $1,000 on professional hearing aids. This one does not work for me.

Likes:
- Stylish in-ear format matches the current trend.
- Compact rechargeable case, and the case can recharge the earpieces multiple times. Status indicator lights are visible on the outside of the case.

Dislikes:
- The amplified sounds are far too tinny. Some lower frequency sounds are barely audible at all.
- These hearing aids seem to only amplify two types of sound: loud clangs and high pitched sounds. I tried to watch TV with my wife baking in the kitchen. Every little clang from the kitchen was amplified immensely, but the TV was barely any louder than without the hearing aids. Even when my wife spoke to me, her voice was barely increased, but a dropped utensil was 4x as loud. Turning up the volume beyond my comfort zone made everything louder, but not clearer.
- Noise cancelling is insufficient. Background noises, like a fan, are still very noticeable, and since voices are barely increased, one still has a hard time hearing the person over the background. (Yes, I tried all three noise cancelling settings, including none.)
- The in-ear design has a large appendage that must go into the ear canal. The bend did not fit my ear well, and even with a smaller silicone attachment, the hard plastic crammed into my ear was uncomfortable.
- The in-ear design feels unstable. Since everything is one piece, earpiece is kinda big and always felt like they would fall out if I moved around too much.

Overall:
The lack of sound quality would make this a "No" for me; but adding the discomfort in my ears makes this a "Big No" for me. However, everyone's hearing situation is different, as are everyone's ears. This may work okay for you -- it just does not for me.

title: COMFORTABLE
text:
These graduated compression socks look so well designed I had to have them. I do have other compression socks that I have purchased previously through Amazon and from my Pharmacy. They don't breathe. My legs feel like they are being strangled (you have to wear them to notice). They make my legs itch. I have to remove them half way through the day. Sometimes they do not do the job they were designed for so my legs are compressed but my toes look like ten pudgy little cartoons toes and which are about to pop. First of all, I have never seen one designed the way this one is. I wanted to give it a whirl. The ones I received looked just like this picture.

These graduated compression socks are well designed. They are easy to put on and remove. They breathe when you wear them. I put them on at 6:30 a.m. and removed them at about 7:30 p.m. they were comfortable throughout the day. I did not feel the need to scratch or remove them. When I move the socks stayed and move with me. They didn't slide down my legs or moved around. The paddings on the sole of my feet felt comfortable and light. I can feel the pressure on my ankles which helps to keep my ankle steady. It does not work as an ankle brace. I am sure adding an ankle brace would increase their effectiveness, especially with a fused ankle. However, these socks will do in a pinch if I don't have access to the extra support provided by the brace.

I ordered the large size which is the men's ten and a half to eleven and a half. Usually, I am not very comfortable with women compression socks. This is just my opinion I prefer the men's compression socks they worked much better for me and are more comfortable. I want to wear a pair of compression socks and feel I can dance all day (which I don't). Anyone interested in purchasing a graduated compression should look into the Kunto Fitness Compression Socks by Kunto Fitness Product. They do have ankle and elbow support I was more interested in the compression socks. Summer is approaching and it is usually hard for me to tolerate any compression socks. The day I wore the new ones it was seventy-eight-degree Farenheight and the socks felt comfortable with perfect support and yes air circulation was great and adaptable. I am attaching a couple of pictures hopefully they will open so you can take a look at the design.

title: Decent heating pad, but has some flaws.
text:
UPDATE ON 2/28/2018 - The company sent me another pad to replace the one that kept shutting off. The same model, and it is working just fine and the heat seems to be more evenly distributed. The original one I received must have been defective. So GREAT customer service!

...................

First of all, I really like the feel of the fabric on this heating pad. The size is perfect for my back or my leg calves, depending on where I need it. Unlike a lot of pads I've had in the past, the innards do not bunch up or get soft and bent out of shape. The highest setting is not scalding like some other brands I've tried, which I am absolutely thrilled about.

But I have run into a few problems that I've been able to work around but may be of concern to others.

The most annoying problem for me is that while it claims to have a two-hour auto shut-off, it shuts off a lot sooner than that. I'm in the habit of using a heating pad at night while watching a movie, and when I have to turn it back on three times during a 90-minute film without commercial breaks, there's something wrong there.

There is also a notable design flaw. Unlike many pads that have their cords coming out from an edge seam, there is a large, hard plastic piece that is on the upper part of the pad (the soft part that you use against your body) that is incredibly uncomfortable if you happen to like to lean back in your chair while it's on your back. I realize that this is part of the removable power cord so you can wash the pad, but I wish it wasn't placed in such a way that makes using that corner of the pad uncomfortable.

Another thing I've noticed is that from time to time it does not feel like the heating element is distributing heat evenly throughout the length of the pad. This happens mainly after an hour of use.

None of these problems are so bad that I would wish to return it, but I do foresee looking for another model in the future.

title: Great bang for your buck!!
text:
After the horrible grooming experience I had for our cat, I needed a way to cut my cat’s hair myself. I was skeptical due to the price but read the reviews and hoped they were real.
Box came as many photos showed. Product neatly wrapped with many helpful gadgets as well. I thought I could use the clippers immediately out of the box and attempted to and was initially bummed about how they were cutting.
But, once fully charged (or attached to a charging box- which I think improves the performance), the cut was amazing. Everyone remarked how quiet they were and it didn’t appear to initially startle our cat (or dogs). They were fairly easy to hold and lightweight. I didn’t even use the attachments since I can adjust the clipper height directly on the clippers themselves. Initially, the clipper head was askew and I felt the cut was a little off, but they appeared to improve with use and the head straightened itself out. The instructions felt a little underwhelming, but they’re clippers for <$20!!! For the price, size, noise and end-product, I gave it a 5-star rating. The only reason I gave “easy to use” a 4-star is due to the grip- they slipped out of my hands more than I liked when I was trying to get closer cuts and sometimes I felt like they were a little too long for comfort/ease of holding.
Anyhow, great starter clippers and great value if you just need to figure it out for yourself. I love that they are cordless and I touched up the cut while completely cordless and i wonder how groomers even use those things with a cord!!!

title: Eh, Not As Revolutionary As I Was Led to Believe
text:
Purple comes up quite often when you look at ways to support the body, from bedding to cushions, you can usually see them come up when you are looking for relief. Having a chair with a pretty terribly designed seat pan, I wanted a way extend the use of the chair. Looking for options, this Purple cushion came up quite a bit and the marketing materials checked all my use boxes.

So did the cushion help, well, yes it did. I can definitely say it is much better than the cushioning the chair came with. However, after several weeks of use, I can say it really is not that much more of an improvement over just a normal style well built cushion made of foam or latex.

The design of this makes it breathe really well, but this design also causes some issues after a long period of use. There is a pretty good sweet spot where you have to have the cushion just right for it to support you correctly without creating pressure points.

What does it feel like to sit on after several hours? Have you ever sat on one of those drainage grates with the rectangular holes? There you go, it's not as harsh, but you can definitely feel a waffle effect after a while and you can tell that it is a grid that you are sitting on.

Would I recommend this cushion? Not at this price, I can see some people finding it very useful if they have a seat that can accommodate it well, but having it be that specific makes this something you can't just throw down an use everywhere. It isn't completely bad, but there are probably better options out there.

title: It works, but…..
text:
I liked that I did not have to ask my wife to shave my back for me. I liked that the extra wide blades shaved a wide path, and was a pretty close shave. I liked that the handle was long enough and was sturdy, but was still lightweight and easy to manage. What I did not like, and it’s at no fault of this razor, not being able to see what I was doing. I have only one small handheld mirror in my shower, which I use for shaving my face. I tried holding that mirror in a way that I could see where I was shaving my back, and found it quite difficult. What should have taken only a few minutes ended up taking about 20 minutes because I had to get out of the shower and check my back in the big mirror several times to she all the spots I missed with the razor.

I guess the one star that I am docking the razor for is its lack of practicality. For me, it’s either I get used to having a minimally hairy back, or catch my wife on a good day and hope she’ll shave my back for me. Granted, I am not the most flexible person, actually I am very far from it, but I don’t know of anyone that can turn around and look over their shoulder and down their back. Maybe it will work great for someone more limber who has a few large mirrors in the shower. I’m not judging.

I hope you found the review helpful.

title: Falls short of the OEM quality.
text:
Photo shows the OEM blades (my S9000 Prestige) in the upper right with the purple plastic drive pieces, and these replacement non-OEM blades in the lower left with the grey plastic drive pieces.

Not "bad", but had a couple of items I thought were noticably lower on the scale compared to the OEM blades. First, the "glide" over the skin as one moves the shaver around doesn't have the smooth, buttery, feel that the OEM blades do. These seem to "stick" a little bit. More friction from whatever the surface treatment is I guess (chrome, whatever). Second, I noticed about a half dozen times while shaving neck/face/head (I shave myself bald), a heavy "grind" noise. It was usually absent, but it popped up a few times.

The closeness of the shave wasn't terrible. I had to go over, and over, and over, spots multiple times to get the smoothness I think I want. But I have to do that with the OEM blades as well. But these took "just a little bit more" so are slightly less efficient.

If you're looking to squeeze pennies these are an option, otherwise, you'll get a better shave with the OEM blades.

title: Higher dosage than I usually get
text:
I am a firm believer in the power of black cumin seed oil to keep my lungs healthy. I try to keep capsules on hand, especially during cold and flu season, to ward off respiratory infections. My husband has noticed a decrease in the amount of times he needs an inhaler for asthma since we started taking black seed oil prophylactically.

These softgels are made with just four wholesome, natural ingredients: black seed oil, gelatin, vegetable glycerin and purified water. Since the packaging doesn’t tell whether the gelatin is plant or animal-based, I don’t know whether it’s vegan or not. They are, however, gluten-free, non-GMO and dairy-free. I especially appreciate that the company is American-owned and the product is packaged and tested in the USA.

These capsules are about twice the size and the dosage of what I usually take. It’s nice only having to take one a day, but they are harder to swallow, and I notice the strong cumin taste when the capsules dissolve in my tummy and make me burp. I don’t have that problem with smaller doses.

At about $13 for the 60-count bottle, these are just over 20 cents a capsule. That’s a really good deal—particularly when you consider that they may save you some trips to the doctor.

title: Odd quantities of nutrients
text:
I take supplements because you can never seem to get enough nutrients from food alone these days. I won’t take ones that are synthesized in a lab, though, because your body rejects the chemicals. It can only use what is natural (meaning plant- or animal-based). This supplement is all-natural, vegan and organic, which is good. However, I have some issues with it.

These tablets are entirely plant-based. You can immediately tell from the color and scent that beets are one of the major ingredients, since the vitamins are rose-colored. They’re also made of several berries, ashwagandha root, guava, mango, mustard and holy basil. They’re coated with carnauba wax.

The smell is strong, and the taste is bitter. The tablets are small enough, I haven’t had trouble swallowing them so far, but someone with issues swallowing may need to crush and add the vitamins to a beverage or breakfast food.

The manufacturer recommends taking three of these daily, preferably with meals. However, I can only take them once, because they make me so hungry! I’m not sure why, since the amounts of each nutrient are not as high as some supplements. The percentages are so random. When you take all three recommended, you may get as much as 500% of Vitamin B12 and as little as 9% of the amount of zinc your body needs. Those who cannot take iron or iodine should not use these, as they contain both.

I don’t want to have to take half a dozen pills to get the level of vitamins and minerals I should have. Nor do I want to feel ravenously hungry all the time. Therefore, this supplement is not a good choice for me. If taken as recommended, you’re paying almost $40 for a one month supply, which is about $1.33 per day. That’s more than I prefer to spend, especially with the aforementioned issues. There are a lot better plant-based supplements available that have more standard amounts of nutrients and don’t make me feel half-starved.

title: Funny looking but really helps relieve pressure!
text:
I got this after I learned that I had a damaged vertebrae in my neck that was pinching the nerves to my shoulders. After the chiropractor adjusted my cervical bones, he suggested that a neck traction device might be helpful for keeping the discs from being compressed and causing more pain. I researched dozens of neck traction devices--including ones that you hang over a door or bed and other, more expensive and complicated options. This seemed like the best value, most highly rated and easiest to use.

It really is simple to use. This comes with three pieces: an inflatable neck brace, a bulb and valve to blow it up, and a carrying bag. You attach the bulb to the tubing on the brace. Wrap the brace around your neck and fasten it in place, using the two Velcro straps. Then use the bulb to blow up the three sections to the desired height. Once you reach a comfortable level of inflation, there's a little bee-bee inside the tubing that you use to close off the hose.

The manufacturer advises using this for about 15 minutes or so, a few times a day, to start with. However, I was traveling about the time I was experiencing so much pain. I found that, by wearing this neck brace while driving, it made going over bumps on the road less jarring and painful. I actually wore it for several hours at a time this way. With the ball and valve, I could adjust the pressure up or down, as I experienced a change in altitude. It was easy to take off and put back on, whenever I stopped for food, fuel, etc.

I also find this device helpful when reading or working on the computer to keep from bending my neck forward and causing pain. I do NOT use it for sleeping, however!

The three inflatable chambers are covered with a soft, velveteen material that makes them quite comfortable to wear. It can get a bit hot, if the weather is warm and you wear it a long time. I recommend that you not only use this to take the pressure off your neck vertebrae, but also do some stretches to strengthen your neck muscles and consciously correct your posture to keep from slumping. When the device is not in use, you can simply set it aside, or deflate and store it in its drawstring pouch. It's very lightweight and portable, easily fitting into a purse, backpack or luggage to travel.

At less than $20, I felt like I got a really good deal. It sure beats the horrible pain I was experiencing before!

title: Great DHA source if you cannot swallow pills.  Drizzle over Chex Cereal before Adding Milk.
text:
I am a big baby who cannot swallow pills, so when I was pregnant I researched this fish oil.

I was really happy with my purchase and I found most of the reviews here ring true. It tastes (and more importantly..SMELLS) like Lemon. Not even a partially fishy smell (to me). Just smells/tastes like citrus oil.

The biggest tip I found among the reviews, that I am going to re-post here for the lazy is -- and I know this sounds weird...

- Pour yourself a bowl of Crispix or Rice Chex for breakfast
- Before adding the milk, drizzle on your 1-2 tsp's of the Lemon Oil.
- Add milk
- Eat
---- Tastes like Lemon Chex.

I suppose if you sprinkled some sugar on it also, it would be "lemon cake" chex.

Anyway, I know, I know..it sounds REALLY weird.. but this strange tip saved me. Taking a teaspoon of any type of oil, even if it tastes/smells like lemon.. is rough. It's still oil. After the first few weeks I decided to just try the Chex theory, and it worked. Towards the end of my pregnancy I was still having "Lemon Chex" for breakfast 3-4 times a week.

500 mg of DHA per TEASPOON - this is a wonderful, mercury-free DHA source.
To put it in perspective, you'd have to drink 14 8-oz glasses of 'DHA Milk' to get that amount.

I hope highlighting this strange tip helps someone else keep up the fish oil supplement throughout pregnancy, like it did me.

Good luck!

title: This stuff is AWESOME. Buy It!
text:
I love this stuff! I love the price. I love the results, the quality, the quantity in the tube. I even kinda love the tube itself. There’s a certain clinical elegance to it and I like the fact that the tube is recyclable metal instead of plastic!
I am far less enamored of being urged to include the adjectives Moisturizing, thickness and sheerness in my review; how something could be both thick and sheer beats me but I digress.
This is GREAT stuff. And It certainly IS moisturizing, though not oily. Hyaluronic Acid is a powerful humectant- it draws water to it so the moisture comes from the HA, not oil. I sometimes apply a pea sized amount of this followed by a dollop of my Clinique Dramatically different moisturizer. It’s certainly fine alone too. A little goes a long way. It has a nice texture, neither too thin or runny nor too thick. It is not greasy at all- either in the hand or on the face. It’s got sort of a soft matte finish. You can feel it slightly but you can’t see it. All you can see is a slightly nicer version of your totally naked face. I mostly use it at night but it’s not heavy or greasy like a lot of night creams. I’ve used day moisturizers far oiler than this. It’s a decent base for foundation. I’ve used this on my entire face/neck cleavage region including the eyes & lips. Any extra I rub into my hands. The Price has gone up slightly but the tube is huge and it lasts a long time. The price is incredibly reasonable in light of the concentration of Hyaluronic Acid which FAR exceeds that of any American product which contains HA- especially at THIS price-point! One could easily spend double or even triple this price for a cream containing less than 5% Hyaluronic Acid! I even sent a tube to my friend(whose skin is quite dry where mine is normal to oily) as a gift and she LOVES it too.
Bottom line- it’s great stuff! Good for any skin type, extremely High Quality with far more active ingredient than you’ll find in any other $20 moisturizer.
