title: I lost 5lbs in 45 seconds! AMAZING!
text:
Seriously, I have never had such a moody, unreliable scale in my life. I feel like I'm fighting with a petulant teenager every morning. It reads things two totally different ways (one way it shows me the shifting numbers as it wildly attempts to figure out my weight, the other way it just says "sensing" and then "step off" and then "thinking" and displays results), and the first one is almost always 2-5lbs heavier than the second one. Which is a few pounds more or less than the third one. And so on.

I basically have very little idea at this point of what I *actually* weigh. On the one hand, that's inane, given that IT'S A SCALE. On the other hand, it does help alleviate any minor obsession I'd develop about losing or gaining a few pounds, because I can't ever know if it's real or not! So who cares!

It gets three stars for being beautiful, for syncing to my FitBit dashboard flawlessly via wifi with nary an issue, and for if nothing else providing me with an overall weight tracking trend line... even if the trend it displays makes it look like I'm throwing a small pet in the air while standing on it.

title: The Good and the Bad
text:
I recently ordered this and my husband and I have been using it for almost a week, I wanted to be able to leave a fair review, not just based on one use. Our UPS delivery guy left our box in the rain, not taking the time to leave a plastic bag over it like in the past, so the box was thoroughly soaked, thank goodness the contents inside were wrapped in plastic or this probably would have been ruined. Right out of the box this looked and felt much more solid and expensive looking than I expected. Looks like leather, but I don't think it is. I liked that it came charged, and that the charging cord is detachable so that definitely gives you more freedom. It doesn't have alot of modes/buttons; on/off, reverse the direction of massager, and heat on/off. I have to say we both found that it does really give a great massage. And you are able to maneuver it around to massage that area that needs it. I personally have fibromyalgia and my neck ALWAYS hurts, ALWAYS. This massager was AMAZING for making my neck feel relieved, I really didn't know what to expect, but as far as how well it massaged, I would give it 5 stars! It was a slow deep massage. My husband moved it around from his neck, his shoulders, his back, and he was really impressed too!
The reason I give it 3 stars...
I deducted a star because the heat, I didn't notice any at all, just a red light?? So that is a non-existent advertised feature.
And I deducted one other star for value. I received this at a discount for my honest and unbiased review. At the time it was listed for over $100, which I felt was a little steep. Although it gives a great massage and looks like expensive leather, it is not. It only has one speed and one option to change the direction of the massagers. But I guess you could look at from this stand point, it does give a great massage and you would easily save the money from getting a massage elsewhere on this unit you could use over and over. Had the heat worked and maybe had a few other type of massaging features I would gladly pay the $100 asking price

title: These earplugs are my solution to cheerfully dealing with everyday outside life noise from living in an apartment!
text:
These earplugs have helped considerably with my ability to concentrate at work. I live in an apartment building, and frequently there are other apartment owners having construction work done in their homes during typical office hours when many people who live in the building are out of their homes at an office. That’s not the case for me!

Here these earplugs have helped me be a less irritable neighbor and more productive consultant; I haven’t had to compete with the noisy drilling and hammering – instead I put in my new earplugs and all the distracting noise just fades away. The design is excellent – these are simple to insert, easy to care for and clean, and the handy carrying case makes it possible to take these earplugs with you when you anticipate you may need them in other circumstances – like a loud venue/concert or in a noisy facility.

I find I use them as a way to increase my focus on a task even when there isn’t construction. These earplugs are my solution to cheerfully dealing with everyday outside life noise from living in an apartment (e.g. lawn care, fire engines, someone’s party in another apartment, a loud television – either in the same apartment or in someone else’s place), and this helps me get my work finished and provides me with an answer to getting to quiet when outside elements seem to get in the way.

There are four light weight, easy to use earplugs, a cord with an attachment at either end that makes it easy to place the cord with an earplug on either end around my neck so I can keep them close and also use and remove them conveniently as my need to use them shifts throughout the day or at any event.

The small, compact carrying case keeps the earplugs organized, clean, and simple to store in desk or bed table drawer. Someone could easily put their earplugs in this carrying case and into their pocket or purse for use during an outing, too. I am fortunate to have been able to purchase this product at a lesser cost in exchange for an unbiased, thoughtful review of my consumer experience using this product. I am pleased with this item and it earned a five star review.

text:
This worked really well for me, a guy in his fifties. The balance is pretty good, but the downside is there's a lot of caffeine so slightly overdosing might provide more caffeine than you really want.

Pre-workout powders are hard to judge. There's so much other stuff that goes into your stack that you potentially might miss all the benefits. However, having said that, I feel like this did help my performance.

The only real negative is the caffeine released seems to be almost instantaneous. I usually workout in the morning, so I've usually already had 1 or 2 cups of coffee, and the addition of this all at one time is a little too much for my body to handle and causes headaches. I've adjusted my regular coffee intake in the morning against the amount of caffeine in this pre-workout since I have them so close together. Even though I'm still rating this 5 stars, I feel like the caffeine release is something to be aware of.

Otherwise, I think the rest of the contributions are very good. As an older guy it's hard to sometimes find the right balance of performance enhancers, but this does a pretty good job. I'm really pleased with the way this has worked out.

I used this on several different types of pimples although I wasn't able to get pictures of all of them and saw very little different. If you use it on a specific pimple, it *will* suck that one pimple BUT that may not be what you actually want.

I had one of those hard, red, not-quite-a-pimple yet - this sucked the clear puss and blood to the surface.... but the white pimple never surfaced like it normally would have. Typically, the actual whitehead would have surfaced in a day or two, I could have popped that, and it would have gone away in another day or so.

Something about using the suction, has left me with a hard spot where I used it on that pimple over two weeks later, long after the pimple has healed.

To be fair, I did try it on my blackheads (tip of my nose) to no effect.

I also tried it on my larger looking pores (forehead). The forehead I tried running the end of the suction device over my skin. I did wind up with skin cells and oil collected on the edge but I think this was more what was on the surface and would have been collected with a wash cloth. The suction was pleasant but essentially useless.

title: Took red Sharpie out of off-white quartz countertop
text: Immediately after construction finished on the kitchen I’d been dreaming of for years, I discovered a line of red dots on my new off-white, honed quartz countertop. Someone had marked things off a checklist using a red Sharpie (!) that bled through the paper. The stains had been there at least a week. I contacted the people who supplied the countertop, and they recommended this product. Applied it per directions, let it dry completely, brushed it off, and followed up with a little of the ph neutral stone cleaner they recommended for daily cleaning. If I squint really hard and search for a while in very bright light, I can barely make out the tiny, very faded ghosts of two of the dots, and an extremely subtle texture difference where the cleaner was applied. It’s a vast improvement. Someone who didn’t know what happened would never notice the spots, and would likely have trouble finding them even if they were pointed out. Much better outcome than I could have hoped for.

title: ReliefBand 1.5 works better for me
text: I'm a longtime user of the original ReliefBand because it's the best solution I've found to my chronic motion sickness. And it really did change my life--I can now enjoy travel on small planes, long car trips, boats etc in a way I never could with anti-nausea medications that always made me drowsy and dopey. I was really looking forward to this 2.0 version with a cleaner-looking design and rechargeable battery. But sadly, it just doesn't work that well for me. The rigidity and size of the "watch" face and band make the device very uncomfortable, and it's difficult to position the contacts over the exact spot needed. I find I need to be pretty precise to hit the spot. I know I have it when I can feel the "buzzing" up through my palm, and my thumb contracts inward in time with the pulses. Getting the contacts on the spot with this new version is hard, and getting it to stay there is almost impossible. I have small wrists, and that could be part of my problem with this version. title: This Heating Pad is Wonderful
text:
I had a crappy old heating pad that was about twenty years old and was about a foot by a foot in size. I thought it was okay, but I discovered how very wrong I was when I bought this new heating pad.

I had some Christmas money and thought a bigger heating pad might be useful. Okay. Read a lot of reviews and decided this one was a good bet. Wasn't really excited but was hopeful that it would ease up a back problem.

Heating pad came in. Quite impressive. Nice size. Pleasant color. So very soft to the touch.

I've used my new heating pad almost every day or night since it came in. I have bulging disks and mild scoliosis. The back pain is pretty constant, but I did not know a heating pad could make much of a difference until I got the new one. No. It does not get rid of all the pain. That would be a flat our miracle. But, it does take the edge off and just flat feels nice.

One big plus with this heating pad is that it times off in two hours. I like to use the heating pad to go to sleep when my back is hurting, but I don't want it on all night. The auto shut off is something I would not have thought to look for, but I very much like the feature.

If you have pain that could be helped by heat, I would highly recommend this heating pad. I really can't say enough nice things about it and can't think of anything I would change about it.

title: My Feet Are So Happy They Want To Go Back For More, More, More
text:
I looked at this foot massager and then again and again. I'm not one to buy gimmick products, so I wasn't sure. I kept reading about the deep kneading foot action and relaxing it was, so I finally decided to order the massager. I hoped it was as good as it sounded.

Hallelujah. I really love this machine. It's super easy to use, and my feet are still tingling (in a good way) after 10 minutes and a little TV.

This is ready out of the box. You just get the power cord out and plug it in the side of the foot massager and then into a socket. There is a booklet, but I don't think I really needed it. All the buttons were labeled. There are two auto modes which may not be as obvious just looking.

There is a setting for time, and they recommend not over 10 minutes to start with and a max of 30 minutes. I am doing 10 minutes right now, since it's hard to squeeze in "me" time. The Shiatsu is Japanese and is a type of deep tissue massage. I love that. There is air pressure as well so that the Shiatsu is stronger with the air expansion and not as strong as it cycles. There is a setting for heat, but this is summer in NC, so I have not used the heat button. The pamphlet does say it may 10 minutes or so to warm up. The center button will shut the machine off if you set it too high for comfort or need to get up to do something.

I wish they had a full body model or at least one for the back and legs. The massage feels wonderful on my feet. You may notice the big scar on my leg which is a skin graft. While you aren't supposed to use the massager if you have a foot injury, my injury was higher and healed now. The massaging does make my leg feel better too. That was just a bonus for me.

I wear socks in my Shiatsu machine, but the foot parts come out with zippers and can be washed. I figure I'll not need to wash the feet parts (which fit women size 14 and men to size 12) very often with putting on clean socks right before using.

I did get a discount on the Shiatsu Deep Kneading Foot Massager in exchange for an honest review which is the only kind I write. I took quite a while to make the leap and get the massager, and now I'm wondering why I didn't get it straight away. It is a great luxury item to use at home especially after a long day at work.

title: Good blower w/little use and wrong photo
text:
The photo posted in this Amazon ad is the wrong one! The photo is of the Echo PB-500H which as a separate left hand throttle control grip while the PB-500T has the throttle grip on the blower tube handle with no handle/control on the left. The PB-500T makes a lot more sense since it leaves your left hand free.

I've only broke in/used my PB-500T for a couple hours and seems to work well. Only time will tell and hope I don't have the long-term use problems others mentioned.

The "cruise control" button for setting it on high seems to back off by itself which is a pain to keep moving it to the high setting again. Seems to have good power but doesn't have the anti-vibration you may get with a Stihil $500 backpack blower. But there again the vibration is mainly through the handle so a Stihl may be the same.

It's a shame Echo doesn't offer a curved blower tube extension to lengthen the tube while blowing leaves/grass away instead of almost straight down. Even with new power tools I alter them to fit my needs and make them more comfortable. I took the 30 degree curved extension tube end off of my old Homelite backpack blower and taped it to the end of the Echo tube which works a whole lot better. I'll probably also use good black electrical tape (Scotch 33) to tape a piece of 3/4" ID water pipe insulation foam to the handle to cut down on the vibration coming through the handle itself. I do this same foam install on my string-trimmers handles and don't need my nerves tingling or carpel tunnel.

Since I live in the woods I blow tons of leaves. Used the Echo blower to blow the leaves off my 800' steep/curvy gravel drive and part of my yard. Nice to have the curved blower tube extension tip on the end since it doesn't blow the gravel off of the drive like a straight one would.

I did use half a can of the TruFuel 50:1 mix and then used a good 50:1 2-cycle mix for topping the tank off. At about $20-$25/gal there is no way I'm going to use the TruFuel mix full time. Too bad I can't find any non-ethanol gas stations around here, E10 is bad enough, and don't ever use E15 fuel or you'll burn up the engine.

I'll update this review with continued use of my Echo PB-500T backpack blower and good luck!

title: Fancy looking but useless
text:
I own an old pair of eye massagers that rely on pneumatic pouches that inflate and deflate to simulate the massaging motions. I find it somehow good but not excellent, that's why I wanted to try these fancy looking ones hoping for a better performance. Not quite! These actually have no pneumatics but instead rely on the old school method of mechanical motors to simulate massaging motions. The issue with that is if you don't get the placement of those motors right then you get zero massaging and even end up hurting rather than relieving. This is the exact case here, there is no adjustments you can make to make these adapt to the shape and size of your eyes/skull. I put them on and it felt like I massaging my eye sockets rather than my eyes! One way to describe it is like you pay for a massage session on your sore muscles instead you get a massage for your bones!
The heat mode feels like a mirage, you feel something and you question yourself "is this really heat I'm feeling?!" You don't feel heat on your eye lids, you feel there's some source of heat but you're not sure where is it nor what's its purpose!
The sound mode is just useless to me and an unnecessary addon. I can use my phone for music if I want to, I don't need an extra device to pair for this, nor I plan on using these for an extended time that requires a music session.
5 stars for the looks 2 stars for functionality.

I love that you have total control over the pressure. You can go really deep or not at all.

I have no issue with it being two pieces, and in fact, I believe it's an advantage so that you can take it apart and travel with it if you're so inclined. It's so light and doesn't take up much space when apart, so I could easily shove this down along the side of my suitcase next time.

title: Pretty good, but do this....
text:
The carpet repair kit (purchased at Amazon.com) works well. However, here are a couple of suggestions that will make it easier for you.

1. If you're patching a carpet that's glued down to a concrete floor, take it easy when cutting out the bad part with this tool. Getting too aggressive will break the blades and the center point. I did that.

2. If you do break the blades there are two spares in the kit. If you break the point just file or grind a new point on it. It's adjustable in height so this fix will work OK.

3. The instructions and product description seem to say that the glue circles are sticky on both sides. They're not. This is apparently because the adhesive originally used would not stick all that well to the carpet. Instead, the circle now is sticky on just one side. This should be used to stick the circle to the sub floor, concrete, or whatever. After the circle is stuck to the floor spread some of the seam sealer adhesive on the top of it (brown paper side) and then place the patch. The sealer will stick the carpet patch to the brown paper.

4. The instructions say to wet the sticky side of the circle after peeling off the protective white sheet then work the circle under the edge of the carpet that is left after cutting out the damaged piece. This is pretty nearly impossible, at least on a glued down carpet. What I did, instead, was cut the circle into quarters yielding four pie shapes (before peeling off the white protective paper. This allows you to work each piece under the edge of the carpet placing the pointed end at the center of the cut out circle. Then do the same for each of the remaining sectors, aligning them against the previous one with their points together (re-assemble the pie). Wetting the adhesive is quite important because it is pretty aggressive stuff and you'll have a heck of a time placing it if you don't wet it first.

5. One more thing. If you're working with a glued down carpet be sure to work a putty knife, etc. under the edge of the carpet that remains after cutting out the damaged area, to allow enough space to slide the sticky circle under the edge. Then, after the adhesive circle is in place and before placing the carpet patch in the hole, spread a little of the seam sealer between the top of the adhesive circle and the bottom of the remaining carpet to glue it back down. Then spread a small bead of sealer along the edge of the remaining carpet and spread some on the brown paper side of the adhesive circle that you stuck down as pieces of pie. Then you can insert the patch and finish as in the instructions.

It makes a pretty nearly invisible patch.

I much prefer the latter type, and I wouldn't recommend this set to anyone except those who get stuck needing help to get it altogether in time.  Being in a jam, this year, I resorted to various forms of presentation, and, honestly, would recommend stocking up on all the holiday tissue you can, whenever you can -- just in case -- then, when in need, wrapping the kids' stuff in that and wrapping it all up in the biggest bag you can find.  Make it a trash bag with a great big bow, or use a cheap-o holiday tablecloth to bundle the parcels, and tie it all together with a jump rope, or clothesline, or boat-and-tow rope.  Even a bungie cord will do!  Children love ripping into the bag and quickly and easily unbundling each and every gift inside. title: Removed chili marks from white sweatshirt!
text: I have used this stain remover for a while and always thought it worked well- but I really put it to the test last night. My daughter was wearing a white sweatshirt and one thing led to another and I let her self feed with her bowl of chili which was smeared all over her high chair and got all over the sleeves and neckline of her sweatshirt. I thought, oh well if this doesn’t come out I never liked this sweatshirt that much anyway. My husband came in and said “oh wow you’re going to have to soak that in bleach”. And I said “we’ll see! I’m going to try the stain remover first”. So I sprayed the chili stained areas generously after dinner and let it sit for about 5-10 minutes while I got my daughters bath ready and then ran a load of laundry as normal. You can see in the pictures that ALL of the chili stains came out. I was actually surprised because I expected at least a hint of red but it all came out. I don’t know what would have happened if I let it sit for more time after dinner without spraying it, because we all know parents get busy and sometimes you can’t spray your clothes immediately after they are soiled. That will have to be my next experiment.

title: Not Exactly as Advertised.
text:
I have bought Kingpin products for a long time. These wraps specifically say they include the 'sticky lip' on them, which is the adhesive part you can lick and stick like an envelope. Being familiar with Kingpin products, I have used the sticky lip before. The adhesive is sugar-based and tastes sweet when you lick it. These wraps do not have any adhesive on the sticky lip. I had to use some reclaim resin to make it stick.

I would have given the wraps 5 stars if it had been my mistake buying 48 of these non-sticking wraps, but it's not my fault bc the product says it has the stick lip right on the back of the package. It doesn't, tho. That's not cool with me.

To reiterate-- Do NOT buy these wraps if you want the sticky lip. They don't have it. You'll have to glue the papers shut manually with your own adhesive. If you don't want to do that, don't buy these wraps. It also didn't come with a ES scoop card, as advertised.

title: Works Great With My Drive Medical Spitfire Scout 3 Wheel Mobility Scooter!
text: This Challenger basket will work perfectly on a Spitfire Scout mobility scooter. The basket fits right into the square tube just under the seat and it is kept in place with the knob with the screw in it and the two stainless pins that come with the basket. Even though the basket is 'heavy duty' in it's construction, it is easily removable when you want to take the basket off and put it in the trunk. The basket doesn't get in the way when you are maneuvering around tight places like the 'jumbo' basket does and it holds more items than you might think from looking at the photos in the listing. My new basket does not get in the way when I want or need to back up. It will hold two full gallon water bottles side by side in it and still have room for more smaller purchases around them. The front basket will hold one full gallon bottle of water and also have room for more items too. I found baby stroller hooks on Amazon and mounted them on to the underside of the armrests as you can see in the photos which make hanging shopping bags off of the arms a breeze. The last photo in my review shows the bags hanging off of the armrests with a 'Dollar-Tree' basket on the floorboard. The Challenger basket has replaced the cheap red basket I had between my feet and now I can shop till I drop. You can too! HIGHLY RECOMMENDED for anyone in my opinion. A+++ and a FIVE STAR purchase.

title: A must-have for a twin pregnancy -- skip the plain maternity support belt!
text:
I am 34 weeks pregnant with twins and have been suffering from constant back, hip, and round ligament pain for more than 2 weeks. I originally had a maternity support belt, but it didn't help much to begin with and I outgrew it a few weeks before the pain started. The only thing that has helped is warmth (warm baths, showers, and pools)--I have been miserable.

At my doula's continued suggestion, I purchased this maternity harness earlier this week, and I wish I had done it sooner. It isn't perfect, but it definitely alleviates the back pain. It does nothing for the hip or round lagament pain, but I didn't expect that.

The things I don't like about this product are:
- It is difficult to conceal under shirts because of the neckline.
- The straps are difficult to adjust while it is being worn.
- I wish the belly portion had more adjustability--they only give 3 options to fit it under the belly. I find that I need a set of hooks in between the smallest and medium setting. Had I purchased this sooner, I would have likely taking it to a seamstress to have a couple more hook rows added.
- They don't include instructions for putting the item on.

But overall I am glad I made this purchase because it takes away some of my discomfort. And at this point I am not going to purchase more maternity clothes, so I have accepted that part of the "V" portion of the shoulder straps is going to show. And I do wish I had purchased this sooner.

Oh, and shipping was incredibly fast through Amazon, and I don't have Prime. So I was so thankful for it to arrie when it did.

title: My Macbook Pro fits comfortably on the table with no fear of sliding off
text:
I got this table so that I could do homework/work on my bed. This was extremely helpful right after my car accident since I could no longer use my desk without severe pain. It honestly did take some adjusting to. The rim surrounding the tables can dig into your forearms if you're leaning your arms on it to do work/homework/etc. So I push my laptop up to the edge and that resolves the problem since I can rest my wrists/arms on the laptop. My Macbook Pro fits comfortably on the table with no fear of sliding off, the rim around the table takes care of that. It's also really convenient to have the small side table on the side for drinks/pens/phone.

I had two gripes about this desk. Even with the manual, it was terribly confusing to put together. There was one extra part in the manual that did not really exist so I spent so much time looking for it. Second, even though I tighten the tables all the way, they're still wobbly. So if I accidentally lean on the table too much, it will rotate the whole thing. I wish that it was sturdier because with my work on it, it's terribly inconvenient to maneuver around it to try and tighten and re-tighten.

title: Sturdy, Attractive, I Think Worth It
text:
Hello. The Zero arrived nearly all assembled. I simply slid it out of the box, surprised by how light it was. Beautifully and cleverly crafted and sturdy, and the quilted padded seat is super comfortable if a bit wide. Everyone wants to try sitting on the seat! Everyone says it's classy!

I am 5.2, weigh 120. This is my first rollator. I figured if I bought a really good one it could handle what I deal with. Rollator width looks as if it won't go through narrow house doors, but that was an optical illusion. Folds instantly by pulling a handle upward. Press handle downward to unfold. It will stand upright folded and an attached cord, very simple, keeps it folded. Photo shows it folded. Fits nicely in the car trunk if its chunky black wheels are all aligned and there's nothing else in the trunk.

Easy to raise and lower the handlebars. I like mine high so I can walk upright.

Took it for a spin on dusty gravel. Worked fine, and I hosed the dust off later. Excellent brakes and I love having no visible brake cables. Designed in Canada, assembled in USA. Mail your invoice with the registration card (to Canada) and in addition to the warrantees the manufacturer insures it (less $50) against theft or vandalism.

Included is a red metal pin that fits alongside one wheel, plus the bolt needed to install it. This step-on "curb climber" installed makes all the difference in the world. I didn't have the necessary socket wrench with the size 13 socket so had to buy them at the hardware store: $27. Maybe you can borrow one.

I called it "my rollator" and "the thing" until I realized it needed a name. I named it Bolt.

Took The Bolt to the art museum. Wonderful to be able to sit and look at paintings. Or sit beneath trees outside. One always has a seat.

My condition is called Primary Orthostatic Tremor. I walk and sit just fine, but cannot stay standing. Legs just shake, then fail. It looks like Angela Merkel has the same. Canes are useless to me. I needed a portable seat. Didn't want a cheap one or one with basket underneath that makes you look like you're sitting on a commode. Not a good look. The basket on this is placed forward. Wanted a seat high enough to sit at a dining table and so people didn't have to lean down to talk with me, so I bought the Regular size rather than Petite.

Hope my Bolt (Evolution Zero) is the only one I ever have to buy. I think it's worth the money.

title: Great for runners or people that have to walk miles everyday
text:
These CopperCare Knee sleeves are a thin stretchable compression sleeve that claims to help reduce knee injuries and help with recovery. Compression clothing has been around for ages and used in the medical field to increase blood circulation in your extremities. This is a proven fact but whether it helps athletes or not is unfounded. Some say the increase in blood flow will help improve your endurance. Others say that the compression reduces the impact shockwave your muscles receive from activities such as running; this in turn reduces muscle damage. I can’t tell you which, if any, theory is right. I was pretty skeptical at first but placebo or not I like how these compression knee sleeves feel.

These compression sleeves appear to be very well made; they are 88% nylon and 12% spandex. The seams are stitched flat so you won’t feel any pressure points or discomfort. There’s an elastic band on both ends to keep the sleeve in place, the top band also has a rubberized strip on the inside of the cuff to make sure it doesn’t move on you. The rubber strip is a very nice touch and I’m sure make a big difference.

I can definitely see how these knee sleeves could help people with minor knee/joint issues by holding everything in place. It definitely won’t replace a full on knee brace but for minor issues you want something that will fit under your clothing and won’t be too bulky. A sleeve also doesn’t restrict movement like a bulky knee brace would.

*I received this item at a discount so I could review it for you, 4 stars means that this item was as described and meets my expectations of quality and features.

title: Did not fit comfortably, hard to remove.  Little pieces can fall apart and get stuck in ear.
text:
I tried both the DownBeats and Etymotic ER20, both of which were actually PAINFUL to me. The DownBeats are so short they were very hard to remove. Some little pieces to these also, and they kind of fell apart easier than I am comfortable with. I would hope those little pieces would not be able to come off, since they face toward the inside of the ear canal, but they fell apart in my case, and I noticed one review on Amazon where they did fall inside someone's ear, and they had to be removed by a medic.

The Etymotic were so long I would not think I could sleep with them, even if they were comfortable.

I did find some plugs that work, as The LiveMus!c HearSafe Ear Plugs are very comfortable. They definitely cut the sound level. They go in easy, stay in, and are pretty easy to remove. The end of the plug is short enough to not interfere with hats, pillows... but long enough to grasp and remove. I can sleep in them very comfortably. The LiveMus!c plugs also come with 2 different sets of dB reduction levels, for a total of 4 plugs, an easily removable connecting string, and waterproof case.

I suspect I have small ear canals, as I prefer the softer and smaller poly foam disposable plugs rather than the standard, and seem to be sensitive to plugs that other people have no issues with.

title: Simple DIY Laundry Detergent for Seriously Sensitive Skin (read below)
text:
I make my own DIY laundry detergent with this brand of washing soda and just two other ingredients. I'm sharing the formula in this review. It's simple - just three ingredients, and cost effective. This is for folks with seriously sensitive skin, e.g. autoimmune issues etc. One proviso: this is not for laundry with heavy staining, e.g. motor oil, but for normal laundry with mild-to-medium staining. For heavy staining, I recommend treating the stains with vinegar first. Also note: never use borax or the two popular-brands of castile soap as these are likely to irritate sensitive skin. Also, when handling washing soda, throw a face-mask on to avoid breathing in any particulates.

Have a large plastic or glass container with a screw top to store your DIY laundry detergent in, a one-cup measuring utensil, and a cheese grater. If purchasing a 5lb bag of washing soda, also purchase 5lbs of pure baking soda (I use Arm & Hammer). If purchasing a 10lb bag of washing soda, purchase 10lbs of pure baking soda, i.e. always a 1-to-1 ratio. Scoop 3 cups of washing soda into your container (with your face-mark ON) then 3 cups of pure baking soda into your container. Use a cheese grater to then grate 1 bar of Cetaphil Gentle Cleansing "soap" into the container. Finish off by scooping 2 cups more washing soda and 2 cups more baking soda. Close the container tightly, turn upside down a few times to distribute the 3 ingredients around inside. Whether using a top-loader or front-loader washing machine, the process is the same. Use 1/2 cup of the DIY detergent per load. Load half the clothes, shake half the 1/2 cup in over the clothes. Load the rest of your clothes, then empty the remaining 1/2 cup in over the clothes. I hope my DIY laundry detergent serves you as well as it does me.

title: Effective
text:
The WP 70 is one of their best products. I've used waterpics for years and liked them. Never burnt out a motor but the plastic water hoses can break, the weak point. The old waterpic had a variable pressure dial on the motor housing, which I liked better but the adjustable pressure on the wand, itself, works well enough if you don't accidentally slide it to the high pressure mode. That kind of pressure can really hurt the gums if they are sensitive. Make sure to watch that setting. Does the product work? Yes. Very well at getting food particles out and toughening the gums, to keep them healthy and for good circulation. These devices have been around for a long time and are proven. For instance, I had issues with gingivitis about 20 years ago and my dentist warned me he would have to do a "root planing" which, he told me, is not comfortable. He advised me to get a good electric toothbrush. Either the Oral B, or Sonic Care. Either are good products and work well effectively cleaning at the gum line. It helped bring the distances down to 2 and 3 mm from 5 and 6. The higher the number, the more receding the gum line. This opens the door for disease and infection. I use it once per day.

If you're new to the waterpic, watch for the tenderness and gum bleeding. Do not use it on the hard pressure setting at first but, rather build up to that setting. You don't have to blow apart your gums to get a good cleaning and I would disagree with some dentists who recommend using the highest pressure setting over the course of use. The book says you don't need it but a good firm setting is recommended. The weak link is the water hose. The plastic can get brittle and break, as mentioned, as it did with mine but I was able to find a replacement hose and wand assembly. I like the 70, but if you want to go fancier, the 90 has some nice features for the extra cost. These products are tried and true and I give it a strong plus and recommendation for that reason as well as their effective cleaning. For dental health, it's a must. Be sure to look for coupons or ask your dentist if he/she has one.

I read glowing reviews on the internet about how it boosts testosterone and frankly I didn't believe them.

EDITED TO ADD: I'm finding you have to use this properly for it to work:

1. I take two capsules first thing in the morning a half hour before eating breakfast. This is key: it doesn't seem to work as well if taken with food.
2. Two capsules is a minute fraction of the bottle's recommended dose and it seems to boost my libido to what I consider "normal"--not specatular, but at about the level it should be. YMMV
3. I take it during the five-day work week and then cycle by staying off it on the weekends. This seems to be working and I don't feel I am becoming dependent on it.

title: Excellent companion to the fitbit!
text:
I've had this scale for the past two months or so-- I got it off of eBay used for slightly less than it's going for here and it's really great!!

Best for: Gadget geeks who already own a fitbit and are looking to get even more data. It's much more useful with a fitbit than without since this scale adds two pieces of data (weight and body fat) to the large amount of data the fitbit already provides. So, I'd suggest getting that first-- I have the Fitbit One ([[ASIN:B0095PZHPE Fitbit One Wireless Activity Plus Sleep Tracker, Black]]), but I've heard good things about the other new fitbit zip ([[ASIN:B0095PZHZE Fitbit Zip Wireless Activity Tracker, Black]]) or the older original fitbit ([[ASIN:B0031P3HY2 Fitbit Wireless Personal Trainer]]).

Pros:
- Syncs everything to the fitbit website automatically via wifi
- Setup is super easy! (took less than ten minutes)
- Battery life is good (haven't had to change batteries in the two months I've owned it)
- Appears to be pretty reliable-- I've weighed myself a few times over the past few weeks on a scale at the gym, and it's usually pretty close.
- Body fat calculation is useful and accurate (if you're trying to lose weight while gaining muscle, fat loss is more important than weight loss)
- Your whole family can use it-- it can tell who's on it by their weight (this probably isn't useful if you have twins that weight the same).

Cons:
- Makes you aware that you are gaining weight. Note: buying this will not actually make you lose weight come to find out.
- It's made out of the shiny Apple-esque plastic, so it can get grimy pretty easily in the bathroom. I clean it with my favorite Apple product cleaner ([[ASIN:B0023WU6OI Klear Screen IK-26K iKlear Complete Cleaning Kit]]) every now and then and it stays looking pretty shiny.
- You can't weigh animals on it. We tried.

title: Great quality budget air purifier that comes with physical remote control
text:
Pros
Light weight, Clean design, decent sealing, great air flow, quiet, physical remote control

Cons
User manual rather less informative, overwhelmed user interface, lack of options of filter replacement, filmy cover.

We have owned 3 blueair air purifiers around home and have been using those for over 3 years. Seeking for an additional one goes to the basement to help odor control. We decided to go for a more budget friendly options since the purifier would be using in the basement only.
Long story short, it works, and it actually works pretty well compares to our existing blueair classic given how much different in unit cost.
The removable filter has a foamed frame and it acted as a seal between the filter itself and the inner body of purifier, the sealing works really good and can feel very strong suction when covered by hand.
Odor were noticeably weaker after an hour of initial usage, and our basement is pretty much odor free by the time I am putting this together (1 week & 24/7 operation).
It is pretty quiet, it comes with physical remote control (I personally really like it over the in App Wi-fi control) and very light in weight, sometime way too light that it could be knock over easily if it has been placed at high traffic location with kids around.
I wish the user manual could provide more details on difference of modes (what exactly is Anion mode? Like Auto mode?) also explanation on air quality monitor value would be nice. Other minor stuff such as 3 levels of fan speed being indicated as 3 bars > 6bars > 8 bars bothers me a little.

Afterall, I would highly recommend Aiper as a quality budget air purifier for those who seek for a decent and effective purifier without the need of Wi-Fi control.

title: No perceptible change in air quality
text:
I do not understand the rave reviews I have seen on this product.

1. It is the size of a thermos. This may be a plus as I can see how you can easily travel with it if desired.
2. The fan does produce some white noise which does not seem to be noticeable on most days, especially when the A/C in the building is running.
3. The smell of the room is no different with it running or not.

I use this at work inside my small office (10' by 12') as I want to clean the air when my co-workers/clients come in with colds. The device may be working... however, there is NO perceptible change in the air quality and the smells of the office are no different even with it running 24/7.

Perhaps the UV is killing germs however, I cannot imagine that the device really can clean much air as the entire assembly is the size of a large coffee cup. I guess independent studies on the quality of the air before and after are the only way to truly know if this thing really makes a difference in the level of germs in the air?

Good luck with your decision to buy or not. I paid $40 for mine and do not feel it is really a great investment. I would suggest those with $40 to spend to invest in replacing the air filters in your house with high-end filters (i.e. 3M filtrete filters) instead if an improvement of air quality is the goal.

I purchased these lifts because of some third party websites that recommended them for crossfit. I appreciate that the bottoms have some small cleats to prevent the lifts from sliding. In testing the cleats seem to accomplish this pretty well. No issues with them sliding.

Note the bottom of these is a bit waffle pattern/hollow. When i tested these with 275 on bb squat, the lifts appear to bend a bit into more of a natural heel cup, which I actually prefer for increasing heel stability. The downside is you might loose a mm of the advertised lift. Again this is okay, because with regular weightlifting trainer shoes, too high a lift can lift you out of the heel box of the shoe.

In testing, I personally found these lifts helped my range of motion with squat and cleans. I plan to take them out for cardio and all other gym lifts besides squat, clean, and snatch.

title: This is a product fail for me
text:
I found that this product left lots to be desired especially when compared to old-time talcum powder. The very first use is a bit of a shock; it's cold and feels like Ben Gay on steroids. Intense menthol is not what I'm looking for in the more delicate body areas. With time the intensity of the "feel" decreased or I just got used to it. Use is more of a necessary evil than a pleasant refreshing experience.

The spray is somewhat intermittent more so when held upside down to use. Inverted use is a claim in their listing and does work some of the time. Keep pushing hard on that big red button to complete the job. This may be acceptable for some when coupled with this product's best feature as it doesn't make the mess that traditional powder does.

Lastly, although their formula does work the "feel" and "comfort" is not equal to talcum powder. Talc is on the market but very difficult to find. I did finally locate a brand available in a shake container that makes a little mess compared to traditional packaging, and has a really great smell.

title: Windows setup failed, Android worked
text:
Once it's running, this is a great device and works as promised. It saves us from the manual data logging we were doing before.

But setup? That wasn't nearly a complete disaster. I tried at least a dozen times using my Windows Phone and two different laptops running Windows 8.1. I tried it using the Windows software provided by Fitbit and the general web setup. Digging through the logs, I can see that the computer was able to connect to the Aria but was never able to communicate with it beyond that point. I saw others say that complicated Wi-Fi passwords could be a problem so I made the Aria it's own open network with a very simple SSID. Nothing worked. Finally I pulled an ancient Android device out of the closet, and bam, that worked on the first try.

I have very standard equipment (router is a WNDR3700) so I don't understand why the phones and the laptops didn't work. Surely they tested those platforms? Am I really the only person who ever had this problem? Seems unlikely. Yet tech support had no clue what to do about it when I called them.

I suddenly found myself unable to walk without support after having taken antibiotics that basically "killed" the tendons in my entire body. My knees were severely affected, and was unable to even move within the house. I got these to help me temporarily while my knees returned to normal.

I first found it difficult to change the length of them. I realised I needed to push the buttons in very well, and twist them at the same time. This enabled me to find the correct length for me. They are light, so they don't slow you back when walking. The arm holders are nice because they move, so they are easy to lean on when standing while working with the hands. I did find that one of them are tighter than the other. which caused some issues while out and about and wearing thick winter coats.

For my use, they were just perfect. I used both for about a week, when I was fortunate enough to get better. I used just one for another week, and now these crutches are in my closet in the hope that they will not be used again. I find it assuring to have them available for when I need support, if that should happen.

title: Too narrow and stiff ... and PLASTIC
text:
I should have paid more attention to the dimensions of this case before buying it; it's just barely 3/4" deep.

When I got it today, I realized it is too slim to let my eyeglasses slip in - I would have to force them in. Thinking I could maybe just flex it a little to make it easier to use, I pressed it on the narrow edges to open it up some, but heard this sharp crack.

I guess that's what they mean by semi-hard...the front and sides of this case have a hard plastic piece beneath the faux leather covering and it won't flex. So, now I've got a broken case and I'm out 13 bucks.

I don't have abnormally large eyeglasses. In fact, they are slim metal frames that fold very flat, so I don't think this case would fit many of the standard eyeglasses out there and definitely not a woman's fashion frame.

Make sure your glasses will easily fit in this narrow case before you buy it. Also, be aware that the clip is on the front of the case, not the back where I expected it to be.

title: Glad to sort only once every 14 days!
text:
I am horrible about remembering to take vitamins daily. I have been trying to find ways to help me remember, so that I can do much better this year than last. I’ve experimented with a variety of pill containers. The thing that attracted me to this particular container is that it allows you to sort out two weeks’ worth of pills at one time. This was a big plus for me, as one of the reasons I tend to “fall off” is having to re-sort the pills every 7 days. This may not be much of a task for some people, but my schedule as a working mom of a Kindergartener makes even that simple task a monumental one. I got the opportunity to purchase this pill container at a discount in exchange for my honest review, and I wanted to see if sorting pills for 2 weeks at a time would help me stay on point with my vitamins.

Yes, it takes twice as long to fill the container but that is because you are sorting twice as many days’ worth of pills. For me – THIS WAS WORTH IT! I was able to sort 14 days of pills, keep the container in my top desk drawer at work, and I remembered every single day to take them. This was primarily because that is the first drawer I open when I sit down at work in the morning, to pull out my glasses. The fact that I was not required to fill the container at the 7 day mark was tremendously helpful. I wound up replenishing week one at the 10 day mark, with no pressure. And this is why I saw success – because it was not a show stopper to fill the container at that point, I still had 4 days worth of pills sorted and ready to go.

The only con I noted was that the compartments are not as deep as other containers I have used. This is okay for now because I am not taking too many large pills at the moment. Once I add another fish oil pill to the mix, the compartments will be full.

This container is valuable to anyone who has lots of medication sorting to do; someone who does not have a time to sort one a week; someone who needs to remember if they took their medication for the day; or someone who is just lazy about this sort of thing. Being able to sort two weeks’ worth of pills at one time is helping me stay on course with my vitamins so far, and I am on my way to a much better vitamin-filled year.

title: Read this before you buy to prevent buying for the wrong reason
text:
I've read through the other dumb reviews so you don't have to. Most people clearly misunderstand what these are for! This is an excellent pair of earplugs for a very specific use:
*** Buy this when you WANT to hear the sound but at a REDUCED safer volume level!
That's it folks! Here is what it is NOT for:
* This is not for the gun range. If you thought that you clearly can't read.
* This is not for wearing at your workplace in place of OSHA approved hearing protection (Duh!)
* This is not intended to block ALL of the noise!!!
* Looking for an NRR rating? You clearly missed the point. Again. If you need a product for a purpose that requires an NRR rating, this is not for you. Probably an ESL course is more for you because you can't understand the point of this product.
* Airplane noise? This should help a little if you want to have a conversation with the person next to you. But they are not designed for that purpose.
* Concerned about dangerous noise levels? This is not for you. Go buy an NRR rated product designed for that purpose. Again, this is for people who WANT to hear the music.

SO THEN, WHAT ARE THEY FOR?
If you go to loud concerts and events, THIS IS FOR YOU! They will allow you to actually hear and enjoy the music, but at a reduced volume level that is safer. I have been to many concerts in my life, some that were so loud that I had to use the traditional orange squishy things in my ears, but then I could not enjoy the music because I felt like my head was under water and I just didn't enjoy myself as much. This product is a unique alternative that is specifically designed to reduce the sound volume AND still be able to hear the music. Heading to a rock concert? Coachella? Burning Man? Lightening in a Bottle? Tomorrowland? Now you're talking. Buy these and give them a try. They do help reduce the noise without muffling the sound. And, they come in a really nice metal screw-cap case with a key ring on it, so after you lose the earplugs in your drunken stupor you can still use the case to store other recreational consumables that you are probably bringing to the event.

title: Re-esterified nature identical fish oil molecules. Label error "free of fish".
text:
Label error "free of fish". Manufacturer should check the label for accuracy since they claim 21 CFR 111 current good manufacturing practices (cGMP). In addition, fish allergy warnings are required by law under "The Food Allergen Labeling and Consumer Protection Act (FALCPA)" and you must list the species of fish used in your product. Product contains both DAGs and TAGs. Better absorption under low and high fat meals than other products with more EPA and DHA as ethyl esters. It is not how much you take that counts, but how much gets absorbed. As a proxy for absorption, the short term phospholipid esterified EPA and DHA pools are measured and sometimes the total plasma concentrations. Some researchers have measured the TAG, free fatty acid, and the phospholipids concentrations in plasma to obtain a better understanding of the Pharmacokinetics (pk) of the dietary fish fat (oil) which is defined as TAGs. From this short term pool, the OM3s are then incorporated into the long term pool of the red blood cells (RBCs) which can be measured as a ratio to the total fatty acids in the RBCs to get the omega-3 index. If there is poor absorption such as the ethyl ester form, the short term pool is low and therefore the long term pool RBCs will also reflect the poor absorption. In my opinion, this product will produce a higher OM3 index than ethyl ester products of higher EPA and DHA content and at a higher price.

title: Personal experiences from 4 different people
text:
Recently my sister-in-law mentioned sitting with her Happy Lite in a joking email about our winter weather. I didn't have a clue what she was talking about, so decided to search Amazon just to see if anything would come up to help me understand what she meant. I started reading customer reviews, and two or three hours later I was both informed and intrigued. By the time I decided to try the Happy Lite, I knew a lot about the different kinds of disorders and complaints that people found it helpful for, the pros and cons for getting "low end" versus more expensive models, full spectrum versus "blue", etc. I also had an overview of the technology and theory behind it. Thank you to all of you who took the time to share your knowledge and experiences.
One of the things I'd learned from reviewers is that the light has to enter through your iris. But the main reason I was initially interested in the light was for my husband who's totally blind. He has no iris. His eyes are scarred shut. But isn't sunliight absorbed by the skin, too? I didn't know. But even knowing that it was a long shot, I took the chance and ordered this model because it was more powerful than others in the less expenive group of lights. And I thought if I was going to take a chance, I was't going to risk top dollar on it. I also thought that it might help ME be less angry at the 4 AM alarm clock, something I haven't adapted to in 25 years of having to get up in the dark to go to work. After the first week I was so excited by the results my husband and I were getting from the lamp, I got another one for my daughter for her birthday. My grandson decided he "liked" it, too, and started moving it to his desk. Now my 90 year old mother is about to be the recipient of the compact model, since she has more time to sit for the required 1-2 hrs it requires. Since all of us describe the benefits of sitting with this lamp in different ways, I'll try to do a brief individual summary of our experiences.
My sister-in-Law: She lives in northern Idaho, in a place that is overcast, cold, and dreary for much of the long winter. She started using the lamp for SAD. She says she had "instant results", feeling better after the first use. I don't know what model she uses, but the results are for her Happy Lite. She reports she's been able to totally get off the anti-depressants during the winter, and feels good year round. She's the one who inadvertantly started the rest of us down the Happy Lite path.
Me: My goal was to reset my internal clock to wake up willingly in the dark at 4 AM. I sit with the Happy Lite for half an hour right after getting up (and pouring that all-important first cup of coffee!). That's all the time I have to give it before having to get dressed and out the door. After two days with the light, I started waking up spontaneously at 4 AM. I continue to sit with the lamp every morning. I'm poping awake regularly between 3:30 and 4, unfortunately even on weekends! But I can roll over and go back to sleep within half an hour if I remind myself it's not a work day. When I do roll out of bed after sleeping in, I still sit with the lamp later in the morning. The later time on weekends doesn't seem to undo the earlier sessions with the light during the week. I hadn't thought ahead to what would happen on the weekends, but even with that slight inconvenience, I'm much more able to roll out of bed, and have decided it's a small price to pay for feeling more ready to face the day when I need to. I've also received an unexpected benefit that I don't think any reviewer I read mentioned, My eyes are becoming less light-sensitive. By that I mean that I'm no longer blinded by those awful blueish headlights on pickup trucks heading toward me in the dark on the drive to work, or by driver's who forget to dim their headlights on country roads, and I can drive in full sunlight without having to pop on my shades! I can't tell when this change took place, since it's one of those things that just sort of crept up on me and I suddenly became aware of the difference. This is a terrific help, especially when driving, both in the dark in the mornings, and "into the sun" in the late afternoons heading home.
Joe: My husband lost his eyes from a chemical burn in his early 20s. He has no iris, no optic nerve in one eye, and his eye lids are held shut by scar tissue. He can't even blink. He suffers from chronic depressions, that have gone untreated for the most part, because he's always assumed they were related to the frustrations of living blind in a sighted world. So how can this light help him? I don't know the answer to that, but I do know it does. He sits with the light 1-1 1/2 hours each morning. He warms a small siting room with a space heater, takes off his bathrobe and sits with just his tank-tee shirt. The light bathes his face, shoulders, arms, and to a lesser extent his thighs. In three days his depression started to lift. Now, after three weeks, he's better able to handle the life challenges, large and small, that come his way without feeling "in a fog" of depression. He's more outgoing and responsive. Yes, these are subjective assessments. But it's a huge change for the better, and he credits the light for lifting the depression he's struggled to overcome for over 40 years.
Terra: My daughter lives with DSPS. She works from home. I gave her the light hoping it would help her reset her own sleep clock. She's still trying to learn how to best go about that, but sits with the lamp when she does pull herself out of bed in the mornings. She calls it "instant energy" and is excited by how quickly she's ready to jump into work with enthusiasm she'd lost along the way. She was very skeptical about using the light...thought there was an element of "wishful thinking" on my sister-in-law's part, and was quite uncertain about my results. She had that "Yeh, yeh" attitude about it. I had to push her to try it, so her immediate response to it came as a surprise to everyone.
The bottom line for me is simple...the Happy Lite has worked wonders for each of us in different ways. We all love it and I'm sure that we'll each be passing it on to others in our lives who might need a boost. It hasn't fixed every problem, or changed the circumstances we live in, but it's improved the quality of life we experience and it's a worthy addition to our coping arsenal. It's definitely worth a try.

text: I bought the Ablware Hole in One key holder for an elderly friend to hold her house key.  She had the cheap plastic snap-together type of key holders before and they they didn't last long and tend to snap open after repeated uses on tight locks.  A simple screwdriver is all that is needed to attach the key (it will hold two keys).  The handle is made of heavy plastic and will hold the nut in place without the need of pliers or a wrench.  To use the holder, insert the key into thekey hole, bend the holder downward until it is also perpendicular to the key and lift the handle to the right or left to lock or unlock the door.  Very similar to lever handle door knobs.  This method can be done effortless without having to turn the wrist...great for those with arthritis in their hands and wrists.

title: Review by a strength athlete
text:
As I was looking at the reviews for this product, there were many reviews for post bariatric surgery patients and others, but very few for athletes. Bariatric surgery patients and others may be using dosing at 1 Tbs or one scoop at a time where strength athletes are using much more than that. I feel this makes a review more applicable to a demographic who may be interested in this product but have not seen many pertinent reviews on amazon.

I've tried the fuzzy navel, roadside lemonade, lemon tea, and kiwi strawberry so I'll review each individually.

The fuzzy navel was very good and a welcome change from the muscle milk that I have been using. I'm not a huge fan of peach flavored stuff, but this flavor was very good. It tastes exactly like the drink, to me, and mixes decently well.

The roadside lemonade tastes decent but definitely has a "creamy whey," flavor to it which I can really taste. The mixability was again only decent. I use a shaker cup for all of my protein drinks and the lemonade was definitely below average for mixing. I routinely got massive clumps in the drink that I'd have to break open with a spoon then shake it again.

The lemon tea was very good and mixed very well. I could definitely use this flavor routinely. It mixed with no clumps and tasted very much like real iced tea. I mixed some of the roadside lemonade in with the lemon tea (2 scoops lemon tea to 1 scoop of roadside lemonade in approx 16 oz of water) and it was probably my favorite protein drink.

The kiwi strawberry tastes like slightly watered down kiwi strawberry flavor (imagine that). It isn't overpowering by any means and isn't that sweet, but if you are expecting it to taste like a snapple then you'll be disappointed. It does mix very well and I would buy it again.

title: Hydra Killer!!
text:
I had hydra in my 49 gallon tank after purchasing a live Top Fin plant a few months ago. I tried hand-picking them out of the tank, but that's impossible. Using a syringe with hydrogen peroxide to squirt it right on the hydra works, but 99% of them are hiding, so you can't get at them!
At the time the tank became infested with hydra, I had a nursery tank full of dwarf blue neon rainbow fish fry - they all were eaten by the hydra. After watching one of the bigger fry get zapped by a hydra tentacle after swimming too close (he lived, but did a painful looking jerky dance for a few minutes afterwards), I decided the hydra had to die.
Dissolved 1 packet of fish bendazole in 100mL water - it goes into suspension, but doesn't all dissolve - and immediately added 50 mL of the suspension to the tank. I don't have charcoal filtration, but I temporarily removed the Purigen resin. Within a few hours, the hydra had shrunken into themselves a little bit, and their tentacles were no longer happily waving around looking for food. The next day they were shrunken into little stumps, and the day after that they were GONE! That was about a month ago, and I am still hydra free.
All of my fish were fine with the treatment. I have snails, and they didn't mind it, and my live plants were ok too.
Excellent product, fast shipping, and I have more packets for future infestations, so I am very pleased with this purchase.

title: Wonderful Invention
text:
My 83 yo mother has had several falls in the house. I have MS and am not strong enough to lift her off the floor. Therefore, we have to call EMS each time and feel guilty about using them for something so simple as lifting her into a chair. Of course, they are always most professional and kind to help us when this happens but I kept thinking there had to be a better way.
The ELK has saved the day! My mother had a fall two days ago and we tested it out on her for the first time. It worked exactly as specified and she was up off the floor in no time. As others have mentioned, it's topsy-turvy while inflating so you have to hold on to your person to keep them safe...or have them hold on to a chair for support. It's worse on Level 1 and 2..the bottom cushions. Once you get to the top two cushions, it becomes much more stable. Like others have said, keep the unit plugged in all the time. The battery goes flat pretty quickly if not plugged in. The unit is very mobile and easy to set up. Instruction booklet is excellent too.

title: Real pain and Wallet pain
text: Get ready for some pain!  This kit contains 2 urine cards..those were easy.  It's the blood sampling that's terrible.  You have to use a lancet to stab the end of your finger.  There is a card with 12 large circles on it.  The idea is to put one large drop of blood in the middle of each circle.  The auto-lancet stabbed my finger and it wasn't as painful as I anticipated.  The instructions say to "milk" your finger to get the blood to flow. Easier said than done!  I only got three drops on the card before my blood started clotting.  I kept pushing on my finger to try to get more blood out as the instructions say to do and was able to barely get one more circle done.  My finger is incredibly sore and bruised now.  I've also got this weird white bubble where the lancet pierced the skin.  I'm obviously not interested in trying to fill up the other eight circles with blood!  The entire kit just went in the garbage.  My finger is still aching as I'm typing this review.  What a waste of money.

title: Finally something that works well on my limestonee
text: I've tried several professional stone cleaners and this is by far the best so far for my limestone flooring in my bathrooms. I really wish I would have taken before and after photos because it blew me away. I used to pay $500 to $1200 to get my tile cleaned and resealed annually. in between it would get dirty again and look like crap. I was determined to find a way to do this myself more economically. after trying different things I finally found this method that works for me. I bought the Chapin home and garden sprayer (48 ounce) and use it to spray this cleaner liberally on my bathroom floor. I leave it for 10 minutes and then I go over it with my Hoover floor mate hard floor cleaner, which I fill with only hot water, using the deepest clean setting and doing it slow and over so the scrubbers do the work. I do this a few times because the Hoover sprays more water to rinse this product off. Then I use the dry setting on the floormate to suck up all the water. I got great results on the first pass when using as directed, And then did it again leaving the cleaner on a little bit longer to 10 min and it sucked up even more dirt. It's so satisfying to pour out the dirty water into the sink both times. The first time the water was almost as dark as mud, but even the second time it was very dirty. After this the floors look better than they ever have since I moved in- It's almost like I got new floors. Also, I'm not a fan of chemicals so I open the windows and wear a 3M particle respirator as I do this. Just wanted to share my methods since I'm so glad I finally found something that works And just came back to buy two more bottles!

title: Stay in experimentation mode
text:
My husband checked continuity across the surface with an ohm meter and this well-made pad functions as claimed. Results, however, depend on many variables. I would just like to caution people not to succumb to expectations that their own experience will be as dramatic as cases cited in the book EARTHING or associated videos. Likewise don't deny yourself the possible measure of success that could be yours because others...even 'science-minded' others... challenge its efficacy. There is a common bias against newer science that does not comport with old science. We don't know everything there is to know about anything, and we are so uncomfortable with not knowing it is easy to shut down our minds when we get to that borderland of what could be. You know your body best. Stay open-minded and work with safe modalities that you are drawn to and decide for yourself on direct personal experience .

My direct experience was after the 2nd or 3rd night of sleeping on this pad that the sore knots running down the outside of my thighs were only slightly tender by morning. They have been a chronic annoyance for years and they were sore again by the next evening but not quite as much as usual. I have lots of inflammatory issues... a collection I have accumulated over years. I expect reversals to take time and be measured rather than miraculous. The inflammation has to come down before the body's natural healing process has a chance. I'm giving it time and then I will add to my review.

There is definitely a side effect that needs more recognition. After several days I felt so amped and antsy after 2 or 3 hours I had to get off of it. THIS IS COMMON! I contacted the manufacturer and was counseled to just moderate my grounding while my body adjusts. In 10 days I was getting a healthy duration of restful sleep and now the energized sensation is welcome because I get up feeling like I can take on the day's activities. Previously my body was so uncomfortable it could not relax enough for me to get any restorative sleep until the sun was coming up. I would get up feeling that I had hardly slept. These results are enough to keep me working with Earthing options.

title: Fine drying power and range of settings; a bit larger and heavier than I prefer. Temp in °C only
text:
[[VIDEOID:ee380563321d6e9804db7abf6001d901]] I have a fairly utilitarian approach to hair dryers: I don't need fancy, as long as it gets the job done well and, preferably, fast. This one may be a bit more than sufficient with its degree-by-degree temperature range from 50° to 90°C (122°F to 194°F; however, temps are only given in °C on the display), hot and cool wind settings, and blower speeds from a light breeze to a light tempest.

Note that to turn the dryer on or off you have to hold down the power button for a couple of seconds; when on, a short press of that button switches the wind between hot and cold.

The slightly textured matte black surface feels good in the hand, although I found the uncontoured cylindrical handle wanting to rotate in my hand, with the weight of the head only somewhat balanced. It felt heavy enough that my arms would get tired holding it for as long as it takes to dry my long, thick hair.

The diffuser has nice smooth tips and the attachments seat securely; however, they could be a little easier to swap out—arrow indicators on the pieces to show when the locking tabs are aligned would be nice. I question, too, how long the plastic locking bits will hold up if heads are interchanged frequently.

The set comes with a storage bag and a round styling brush.

Bottom line: Out of the gate, a good, rather large hairdryer with highly customizable settings.

title: A person could get obsessed with this thing
text:
And that's what happened with my niece, who spied this unopened on my bathroom counter and pounced on it. She had been bothered by excessive wax in her ears and has been inspecting her ears nonstop since she commandeered it (washing the removable tips between uses, obviously).

She really did need help getting the wax out of her ears, apparently, as the camera revealed a veritable wall of wax blocking both of her eardrums, which would have taken her a lot longer to figure out without this handy thing.

In addition to the ear pick itself, the device comes with a small vial of reusable plastic tips and six long metal sticks with various scooped, spoonlike tips and even one that looks like a tiny whisk. These are also for cleaning your ears but they don’t attach to the device.

The ear pick came with a partial charge, so it was operable right out of the box. First you download the free app as instructed in the manual, then press the button to power on the ear camera. Turn on your phone's Bluetooth, go to wi-fi settings, and look for the network titled “Aisee” (this might be different for you; refer to your instruction manual for the name to look for).

I don’t really understand the technology behind it, but I guess the device is its own little hot spot? I say that because you connect your phone to it as if it were a wi-fi connection, and then you have direct access to the camera inside. The image is reasonably clear and there’s a very bright light at the tip to illuminate where you’re going inside your ear. You can dig around in your ear without any help, because you can see what you’re doing right from your phone.

My niece quickly determined that her ears needed professional care and went to the doctor to get them flushed out. Her doctor did not recommend she continue using this device due to its potential to scratch the ear canal or puncture the eardrum. However, it did prove extremely useful in revealing what was really going on with my niece's ears, and it seems safe enough to use if you’re careful not to explore too deep into your ear canal. But do be aware that this device could either save you a trip to the doctor or, if used incorrectly, cause you one.

All in all, I recommend this highly with a caveat to take proper care when using.

title: A little stiffer than the brand-name bristles, but great price
text:
I always try to make my Sonicare brush heads last as long as possible because they cost so much, but the price of this multipack makes it so reasonable to change them that I'll probably do it twice as often now.

Most importantly, the head seats securely on my Sonicare handle and the brush operates properly with it on. And the little protective caps for the heads actually click on more securely than the "real" ones do.

The bristles are slightly stiffer and that does matter to me for gum protection, but I can just lighten up the pressure a bit and the end result is about the same. I'm still on the first head, but after a few weeks none of its bristles have loosened or fallen out as seems to be common with inexpensive brush heads.

Overall, a good value for the price. However, if your gums are sensitive, perhaps consider looking for heads with softer bristles.

title: Maximizes benefit from topicals such as Retin A or glycolic peels
text:
First off, this is a serious facial steamer; and an excellent one at that. I'm surprised people ordered this and then seemed surprised that a spa steamer gets hot. That's kind of the whole point and there really isn't a way around this in terms of thermodynamics. To create a productive steam, hot water is required.

Now that we got that out of the way, you can touch the plastic container when at boiling, and it will not burn. Sure, it feels hot, but not "burning" hot. Furthermore, this does not appear easy to knock over because the components of the body are metal and the base is a decent weight (these are not cheap plastic parts).

USE APPLICATION: This amplifies the depth that skin creams penetrate. I cannot stress this enough. I learned this years ago when I accidentally gave myself a "peel" by applying everyday Retin-A right after a long/hot sauna. I use Retin-A daily and don't peel, but when COMBINED with a good steam... BLAM! With steam, the Retin-A packs a punch. The peeling creeps up a few days later as massive facial "dandruff" (during these times, wearing black is a very bad idea, unless you like the appearance of SNOW on your clothing).

This puts out an excellent amount of steam and pretty quickly. In about 3 or 4 minutes, it was steaming on full blast. Since I'm just treating myself, I only filled it 1/4 way and that was plenty. The head of this turns, so you can lay in one place and get your face, neck and chest without moving the machine at the base.

I'm not studied on the use of "ozone" for facials. And, after some internet research, this concept is still not clear. It seems that the ozone function on this machine accelerates the output of steam. So this would lead me to believe that this ozone function might input some ions or salt/sodium type accelerator for steam. However, I don't even faintly detect a salt like taste or residue. So that remains a mystery.

NOTE: Use distilled water. Hard water is likely to clog this over time.

Very happy with this. This is EXACTLY what I hoped it would be. Christmas came early and so did the facial snow (otherwise known as facial peel dandruff).
