title: Subtle, yet real
text:
I bought this in hopes that it would calm down my anxieties about school and work. My heart rate is typically about 100bpm, and whenever I go to the doctor my blood pressure is something like 140/90. I feel like I have a subconscious anxiety where I don't think or feel anxious, but the effects of anxiety are there in my body and the back of my mind.
Anyway, this arrived in my mailbox (get the larger size if you have prime) and I immediately mixed a shy half a tablespoonful with my hot chocolate. *Note: it doesn't mix with hot water. Only mix it with cold water or it'll lump up and you'll have to lick it off the spoon. It smells kinda sickly sweet, but also like juice at the same time. It does taste better than it smells. I did notice a mild numbing on the tip of my tongue, but as a redhead local/topical anesthetics don't work very well for us so it quickly subsided within 1 minute. I felt pretty ok, but not free of anxiety, and my muscles were still tense. I had another serving the same size a couple hours later. I felt the same with this serving as with the first one.
The next day (today) I had a whole spoonful of this stuff in some apple juice. I feel like the effects are so subtle that I've been dismissing them as placebo. The following are the effects I have noticed so far:
#1: I have difficulty after it kicks in to form mature adult-like thought patterns. Mostly I laugh as adult jokes when my parents are nearby, and I realize that "oh, I shouldn't be laughing at that right now, dad's right there", but at the same time I don't care. You hear that, dad, I just don't care. I also enjoy myself a lot more watching funny/strange videos. Look up "Berdthday boy" (note the spelling) on youtube and you'll know what I'm talking about.
#2: I've been thinking some really strange thoughts and sentences, even the day after I drink my tea. One word in my head leads to the next and then I've got this image in my head of a moocow propelling itself through space with her farts. I wish I could text these thoughts to my girlfriend, but she's been really busy at school.
#3: English words are strange and it's weird to type sentences.
#4: I'm feelink (see, I thought "g" makes close to a "k" so I accidentally typed a k) a slight level relaxation right now, 8 hours after I had my tea, and I'm feeling #3 very much right now. It's 2:30am, but I'm cool with that and my back muscles aren't really tense at all
#5: Vivid dreams. I normally just black out and wake up the next day for school, even on the weekend. I largely attribute this to the brain's ability to determine if it wants to conserve energy by reducing throughput. I had a vivid dream for the first time in ever. Though it was partially about anxiety about getting something done for another person I don't care about (sounds like grading papers for my boss), I could recall feelings I had, places I was, objects I saw, I even had a dream that there were corn chips in my kitchen and I was disappointed tonight when I realized we don't actually have fritos.
#6: Insomnia is a choice for me right now. Usually I get in bed and stare at my eyelids for an hour. I didn't have trouble falling asleep yesterday, and I really feel like I could fall asleep no problem right now, and I should really go to sleep but it's winter break so HA!.

I would imagine these effects would continue to build if I make tea tomorrow morning. Good thing I'm on winter break. I really needed this after an extremely stressful line of work I was trapped in for a year and a half there, and it's over now. I was going to drink to toast the end of it, but this is starting to feel like a much better alternative. I really feel like playing some great video games and just sprouting my couchpotato roots.

text:

I don't wake up with nasal congestion anymore. I checked the filter a few days ago and it had some dust in it. I also compared filter color to a new filter that I had purchased to have on hand when it is time to replace the original one. The unused filter is whiter than the one currently in the machine. I have noticed that some of the reviews are unhappy with the space that is advertised that the air purifier cleans. The specifications state under air changes per hour (circulates air 2x in rooms of 578 sq. ft/ 5x in rooms of 231 sq ft. It appears that air is being purified in rooms close to 600 sq.ft just not at the faster rate.

Update: August 8, 2022

The filter replacement blinking light just came on today. I purchased this air purifier in March of this year 2022. It has been running on high non stop and today is August 8, 2022. I have cleaned filter almost weekly to removed dust that had accumulated.. I have kept the purifier in my bedroom all summer with the A/C on and door closed. I honestly believe that it has kept dust to a minimal. I have almost no nasal congestion when I wake up in the morning, and far less dust on furniture in my room. I have no way to judge whether it is cleaning bacteria and virsus from the air but I haven't had any illnesses. I really like the simplicity of the product. I have noticed that the machine does change speed occasionally by itself but I don't have an issue with this. I just turn it back on high when I notice this happening. I noticed that it is out of stock on Amazon. I hope it comes back as I would like to purchase another one for other areas in my home. I guess I better order another filter to have on hand in another 6 months or so! Haven't checked to see if filter is available, I hope so!! I certainly feel I am getting my money's worth from this air purifier.

text:
This device is amazing, totally does what it says - I'm in my 30's, so I can't say that I have problems with wrinkles, but my skin is definitely looking "cleaner" and healthier (and younger). I use this as instructed once/day, before bedtime, because I don't have time in the morning before work, and it works great! Here is how I use it (after digging deep for english instructions and directions):
On the left side of the unit there are 4 lights:
1. Cleansing - the top one. I soak a regular round make-up pad in my toner
2. Micro-pat - the one under it - I apply my oil-based serum to my face, then use the device without a pad directly on my skin
3. Moisturize - the third one - I apply my moisturizer (oil-based) directly to my face and then use the device without a pad directly on my skin
4. Refresh (once a week) - this is for a sheet mask

On the right side of the device: the top light is the "high" setting and the bottom one is "low".

I hope this helps, this device definitely works if used at least once daily. You will not see much of a difference if you use it occasionally. It's definitely worth spending the time on, though.

title: Love these!
text:
These are exactly what I was looking for! I've used witch hazel before, but it was always out of the container with a seperate cotton pad. I think these are superior not only because they're super convenient, but the pre-soaked pads are also nicely waffle textured so it really feels like it cleans your skin more thoroughly. That's not to say they are too rough though, the formula is extremely gentle and soothing.

I have oily skin (very oily unfortunately) so I use toner or facial wipes many times a day to freshen my skin and keep pores clean. Therefore it's easy to over-dry my combo skin or, conversely, if the product is moisturizing it can sometimes break me out. I'm also in my 30's now, so I don't want anything too harsh. These pads are the perfect balance. They don't dry me out in the least. My skin is left super soft, soothed and yet it feels very fresh and cleansed at the same time. These also don't leave a film like some other witch hazel products I've tried.

As anyone who has used witch hazel before knows, it doesn't have the most lovely of odors, but it's certainly nothing intense or intolerable and it fades very quickly. It's also nice knowing that there aren't any unnecessary additives or scents. You are left with nothing but clean, fresh, soft skin.

I also think it's a great value for the number of pads/jars you get... and they don't skimp on product either... the pads are very heavily soaked in the solution which is exactly how I like this kind of product. Go ahead and give them a try... I think you'll probably love them too!

UPDATE: I've noticed my skin actually stays considerably less oily longer after each time I use these, more so than with other products of this type I've tried. Granted it doesn't stay perfectly matte, but it's certainly not the mirror that it usually becomes after an hour or so, which for me is impressive. I can only assume this is due to the fact that although it cleanses well, it doesn't strip your skin and dry it out causing it to respond by becoming more oily again. So this is a great option for my fellow oily/combo skin sufferers! PS -- I feel your pain. ;)

title: Surprisingly this does help!
text:
I was pretty impressed with this product. I am only 34, but I was diagnosed with essential tremor about 7 years ago. The doctors couldn't explain why, only that sometimes people in their mid to late 20's just wind up getting it (hooray for me). It's not *terrible,* but it gets pretty bad on certain days, especially if I haven't slept enough or I'm not feeling well. There are times when I can almost feel my whole body shake and can even hear it in my voice. Friends and family will notice my hands trembling sometimes and it's very embarrassing as I always worry someone will think I'm an alcoholic or something! Anyway, I didn't have super high hopes for any product to abate my tremor, but this one actually did make a difference! It doesn't make them completely go away (nor would I expect it too), but I do notice a marked difference on days when the tremor isn't super bad to start to with. When it's really bad it still helps a bit, but just not to the same degree of effectiveness as when it's a more mild day. If you're like me I'd highly recommend giving this a try!

As an additional tip for people like me, I recommend doing some research on supplementing with magnesium also (especially magnesium oil that you apply topically to your skin - it's far more absorbable by the body that way). Many, many people are deficient in that nutrient due to over depletion of our soils from commercial farming and other environmental/dietary factors in the modern world. It has an incredibly calming effect on your nervous system, so it's helped me a lot with my tremors and insomnia as well. Obviously you have to listen to your own body and do your homework on what's best for you, but I know it's worked well for me. Good luck!

title: Hand held cordless oral water pick works first time user
text:
First time user of any type of water flosser/pick. This has a slight learning curve to it so you don’t spray yourself with water or everything around. There are several different modes for personal preferences and I have been trying different modes. Turn/spin the attachment so the modes are viewable in mirror on the device and that helps you when first using it. It was pretty easy to learn the modes, as each one feels very different spraying the water and makes a different noise. The lowest setting has barely any water coming out and is a good mode to start with so you don’t spray yourself. The pulse mode helps if you have tight crowns to clean in between well.

Another thing to remember is to set it to the lowest mode (last light) when done. The device has a memory function that goes back to the last mode you used. Which is actually pretty funny if you don’t remember and it's on high mode when it first starts again. I suggest wearing old clothes when practicing that you don’t care if they get soaking wet.

The bowl that holds the water seems pretty big and the machine once put together is a good size but light enough to use easily. The first couple uses, I had to refill the bowl mid use to completely finish. This is partly a new user, as I am getting used to the machine. I would personally like a bit more water to not feel as rushed. Personal preference.

Easy to rinse out and place on a clean washcloth to dry. Button above the usb charger releases the attachment and it's easy to run hot water on and in it to clean out after use.

The device must be charged for four hours first time before using, with USB cord included. You will need a square plug in or strip with a usb port to actually charge. The usb port on the machine comes with a plastic cover to push into and cover plug area so water doesn’t get in. An extra cover is included in case you lose it or it breaks.

title: In my case "alleviate" not eliminate.
text:
My house built in the 80's was a squeek nightmare given the subfloor. The system did help, but because of the subpar building pratices and components used, still is not silent. I have construction experience and found that the average layman may find the system a bit tricky. I reccomend that after finding the floor joists (be sure that you do and keep checking), the use of a laser will dramatically help keep you in line and speed the process along. (i.e. find the joist on each side of the room, connect the screw points/heads using any laser that is sold at Depot/Lowe's for a few dollars and follow the light). Watch for lap splices when floor joist run over a bearing wall below, your layout will change by the thickness of the lumber used and you may find yourself screwing into air. Once you get the feel of the screw as it penetrates a framming member, you should know when you are off target and need to verify this from time to time using the joist finding screw (supplied). All in all, the system will help and it sure beats pulling up carpet, although that is next on my list of things to do to silence the squeeks for sure.

I would define subpar as 1 layer of 3/4 plywood with H clips betweeen the stud bays.

title: Cannot determine the value of this product under my circumstances so 3 stars not to knock it or rave about it.
text:
3 stars because I could not determine whether this would have any positive effect under different circumstances...........not to knock it or rave about it. Reviewing a product like this is extremely subjective. It depends on you in several ways of course as well as your ailment. I injured my shoulder and was in agony. It was a deep down tendon/muscle/joint/bone pain. I could not sleep. I could not move the arm. The pain drifted in and out but always was at its worst at night. Gravity alone was a constant antagonist whether awake or attempting to get some badly needed rest. I tried a number of products. The ones that were effective did more in the realm of distraction than reducing pain. Cooling was effective while heat made things more uncomfortable. Yet a hot shower also helped.

Now for my needs this product offered nothing beneficial in terms of surface effect. There is neither cooling nor warming. There is no tingling. A significant con is its oily consistency. It never blended into my skin and required wiping off. In my case the act of rubbing the skin was only worth it when the product provided a soothing quality. There was no noticeable effect with this gel. I endured the pain applying and removing it and was unable to detect a benefit. On the other hand Penetrex, Ben Gay and Biofreeze were worth using. I also used a TENS/Interferential device. I cannot say whether it had anything to do with healing but it was helpful as a distraction from the pain with its deep tingling sensations. Another device used successfully was an electric back massager. Unsuccessful was a heating pad.

Needless to say, I'm writing it -- but not for the one packet (although I do need to re-stock!) but because I truly think these are the best shoe liners I have used in years. I live in Baltimore, with 100-degree days, as well as sub-freezing days. Either way, I hate to wear nylons because my diabetic feet sweat, and my shoes were developing the familiar 'sour stink' thank simply cannot be cleaned out. I was, as others have mentioned, throwing out shoes that were not worn out because of the odor. Then, I found these. They are a shoe saver for me. I really do wear them in all my closed-toe, and peep toe shoes. I do not wear them with sandals, although I may try that this coming summer.

My only recommendations are that they make these a tad wider (make them for 'wide' sizes, and those of us who wear 'B' width can trim them if needed. Right now, they do not cover the width of my B-width shoes.) The second suggestion, along with other reviewers, is that they improve the 'sticky' material on the bottom. I have found that some stick like glue, while others move around -- and it does not matter if your shoe 'sockliner' is make of leather or vinyl. I have not used them in fur-lined shoes, so a merchandising line for that would also be nice. Nor have I used them in shoes with a 'Nubuck' sole, like my sandals have -- I will try that this summer.

I strongly recommend these liners. They really do help keep the odor down, and help to eliminate some of the 'stickiness' your toes feel after wearing shoes for an entire day at work. I'll be ordering more - and waiting to see if they start making them wider and tackier, too!

title: A perfect morning, every morning.
text:
This clock was purchased as a Christmas gift to my mother-in-law to replace her old noisy alarm clock. She has heart problems and has been trying to maintain her stress levels, and having an alarm that would jolt her out of bed with a grating buzzing sound was not conducive to a stress-free morning. We'd been looking for a quieter, more peaceful alarm for her when we came across this one.
We helped her set it up and showed her all the features; she loved the nature sounds and the sleep feature. She tried out the sleep feature that night and fell right asleep; but she noticed that the method for setting the sleep function was similar to the alarm method, and she ended up turning off her alarm. There are a ton of settings that she probably won't use, and actually getting all the settings right is a little tricky; but that might just take a little getting used to.
In all, we think it's a great product. It could be a little more user-friendly, but it's fantastic for the price.

title: ... only had the chair about 2 weeks but we love it. We placed the order on Thursday evening ...
text:
Update 2022. Chair is still working great about 4 years later . We were told by a chiropractor to use it 2-3 times a week and not every day. The shiatsu function is pretty strong. We havent had any problems with it.

2018.
We have only had the chair about 2 weeks but we love it. We placed the order on Thursday evening and it arrived on Tuesday morning of the next week. That was a very happy surprise since we didn't expect it for at least a week or 10 days. It is a little bulky so we had to have help to get it in the house. Once you get it on the rolling wheels, it is a lot easier to maneuver around the house. As for the actual massaging quality - it is great for someone that hasn't had a chair like this before (we have test tried some other chairs)! It takes a little getting used to because some sections of the rollers are pretty deep/hard on the back and feet. The airbags are pretty hard on your calfs too sometimes. So the first time make sure you have the remote in hand to press the pause button as needed. The foot massage is really deep too. I did not realize that I had areas on my feet/soles that I actually couldn't feel before we had the chair. With this foot massage function it seemed to rejuvenate my feet quite a bit. In the automatic massage modes the airbags actually keep your legs and feet pressed down so you cannot move your foot away from the rollers on the bottom and you really get a good deep massage there. If you are not ready for that you may want to try the manual mode first and see what works best for you. You can also move your feet in between the airbag squeezes and cover different areas of the feet/soles, which I really needed. It is also great that the main rollers go all the way down to the hip/bottom area and there are different modes for different sections of your body. If you have hip/sciatic nerve problems like I did it works on the areas you need and you can even stop it with the remote and work that area for a while. My husband has lower back issues so he likes that feature since he can pinpoint the area and use different methods on that specific area. The Kneading is my favorite but it also works well in the Shiatsu mode and I can also do the knocking and kneading together to work on the upper back and shoulders area. You can choose a whole body massage too or just a certain area. You just have to be careful and make sure you don't overdo it to start with. I didn't realize I had knots in my back, shoulders and feet until I sat on the chair and started a massage. The first day I was a little sore since my muscles were not used to actually being massaged. So I highly recommend to do a little the first day and gradually ease into it. You may be really excited, like we were, and try to do 30 min or more the first time and try to figure out all the functions but try to not do that much or your muscles will be sore the next day. I really hope the rest of the reviews are correct and we have this chair for a few years without having mechanical issues. It works really well for the cost of it. It seems to be put together quite well as well. It doesn't look or feel cheap at all. I was afraid the leather will be really thin and not last for too long but it feels like it will last a while. I would highly recommend this product to anybody. We also consulted with a Chiropractor before we bought a massage chair. He recommended the type where the roller goes up and down your spine, like this one and not the stationary type. He was absolutely correct since we enjoy the up and down rollers a lot! You cannot use this as a recliner as it does not have the padding and the rollers are not comfortable unless they are in motion and massaging you. We have tried the zero gravity position without the massaging but it only helps for a little bit. This chair is made for the medical benefits and massaging functions only and not as a regular chair.

title: Works Well, But Very Difficult to Assemble
text:
At first I wrote a negative 1-star review because I simply could not get this thing assembled. I am a petite woman (5'1", 120 lbs) and have small and somewhat weak hands from carpal tunnel surgery years ago. This thing takes a LOT of hand and upper body strength to bend the fairly rigid plastic into the slot it needs to lock into. (I even briefly considered putting it in the oven on a low temp to soften it, but quickly realized that that might ruin the back stretcher and/or my oven, and potentially end in disaster!) Instead, I kept working on it each day a little at a time, trying different approaches and bending it as far as I could by kneeling on it, pulling the ends upward and holding for as long as I could (usually about 30 seconds). After about a week, this actually made it pliable enough that I could FINALLY get it locked into place on the first level.

I was then able to use it for the first time and I must admit -- it really did help my back! I felt much better after only about 5 minutes the first time I used it. However, the raised bumps along the edge of the slot where your spine fits were somewhat uncomfortable. I really don't understand why those bumps are there -- the thing would work just as well without them and would be way more comfortable.

So now I'm glad I didn't return it as I was thinking about doing when I first got it and couldn't put it together. But because of how difficult it is to assemble (probably not too difficult for people with larger hands and better grip strength) and because of the uncomfortable raised bumps, I gave it 4 stars instead of 5.

title: Too small and therefore uncomfortable; pain worse after a weekend with this cushion
text:
I bought this for chronic piriformis pain. It does feel better under my butt, so for the piriformis area itself, it's great. However, as others have mentioned, it's too small. It doesn't reach the sides or front of my office chair, meaning it digs into the sides of my legs and the back of my thighs above the knees.

It's making my hip and thigh pain (some of which is related to the piriformis compression) worse. I tried wrapping a towel around the edges to create an even surface that covers my chair seat, but for the money, I'm not happy I have to do this, and it didn't really help.

Also, it doesn't stay put in my chair. After a few minutes of sitting here, without even changing position, it has slid forward, leaving a gap under my tailbone. Sigh.

I'm a small woman with a curvy backside--not tiny but not huge either. I can't imagine this working for a large man who needs it for something like a truck seat. It certainly wouldn't even cover my car seat. Was this designed by really thin people?

I don't get all the rave reviews, and I don't understand why no one can seem to make one of these cushions that actually covers an entire seat. It's no good spending the money for a better quality material when the dimensions of the cushion are inadequate. Purple, if you're listening, think about making an entire office chair, with this material integrated into the seat.

Something else I didn't think about--not the fault of the cushion but worth considering if you're short (5'3" or under). The cushion adds about 2 inches of height to my padded office chair. Now my feet barely sit flat on the floor, even with my seat adjusted to the lowest level. That's exacerbating the digging effect on my legs, as I have the cushion digging in on one spot and the back of my chair digging in a few inches further. I can't lower my seat any to relieve the pressure on the back of my thighs. So, now I have to get a footstool for under my feet? No.

I'm updating this review and subtracting stars because after a weekend of trying this cushion for a few hours at a stretch here and there, trying to give it the benefit of the doubt, my pain is worse than ever. Not only does the side I bought it for hurt worse, I now have sciatic pain on the other leg as well. It's going back, which is a huge inconvenience for me, but I can't afford to trash it for this price. Disappointed.

I didn't read it all the way through before using it and my feet were tender the next day. The instructions say to use it only 15 minutes the first time...I used it 30 minutes. I would also recommend using the shiatsu and the air compression separately until you get used to it. My feet are size 10 so using both, like I did the first time, really gave them a working over. I've been using it for a week now and I do the shiatsu for 10 minutes followed by air compression for 15 minutes most evenings.  My feet and ankles were very swollen by the end of the night before I started using this machine; I think it was from sitting around so much more since my retirement. Now there is almost no swelling so I think this is improving my circulation. I'm very satisfied and consider it money well spent.

title: Roasted feet, High current draw.
text:
They work as stated. However there are a few issues. First off there doesn't seem to be any temperature regulator in these things. They get uncomfortably warm after about 20 or 30 min. The description says 152 deg, and they are not kidding. The heating unit is a 7 in long by one inch wide strip that inserts in a zipper at the toe. It slips between the insole and out-sole of the slipper. you have to make sure it runs right down the middle or it will only warm one side or the other on your foot. The "Y" cable is kind of short so what ever your connecting it to has to be right next to your feet. and the "Y" itself is very short and limits how you can move your feet.

You can't just use any USB adapter. It draws so much current it got my IPad charger so warm it smelled like burning plastic and was very hot to the touch. They say you can plug it into a computer, but I would be afraid it would burn something out. It would definitely drain your laptop battery,

I will say it will get your feet warm after an evening of shoveling snow. So if you have VERY cold feet, this is what you need. Just don't fall asleep with them on.

title: works but...
text:
I get motion sickness easily, from long car rides to 3D games, that often escalate into severe headaches. Unfortunately I don't have a road trip to test these on but I had two solid tests for the gaming issue: Portal and a certain game that features a man with an awfully shaky camera. So good news, I actually felt fine!

What didn't feel fine, however, was my nose. Maybe it's the shape of my nose, maybe my glasses are bigger than what they had intended to accommodate. But the nose pads press into the sides of my nose to the point where I feel like I'm in some weird situation where someone is pinching my nostrils halfway shut. Because they are literally being pinched halfway shut. I think you can kind of see it happening with the guy in the example photo. It's really uncomfortable and the feeling stays for several minutes after I take them off.

Maybe they could've use the fact that these are made for glasses wearers, so that these bulky things to be supported by the top of my glasses' frames. Or even just the bridge. Instead of my weak little nose. I don't know, I'm not a product creator but I wish there were just pieces of plastic that could just rest on top of my glasses.

So yes you'll look like a fool and yes these will work for motion sickness. They will fit on top of your glasses. But now I have a new dilemma of feeling discomfort from my nose that's honestly a little sickening in itself. I think I'm going to return these and get one of those pressure point wristbands.

Edit: Nevermind! Nonreturnable! Guess I'll just keep these to have something to take funny selfies with. And also deduct a star from my review.

title: Buyer beware
text:
I purchased the Aria scale using my Mileage Plus Rewards on United (not an Amazon purchase).

Scale was purchased 5/15/17. In April/May of this year after “a firmware upgrade” the scale has not functioned. FitBit support is, in my opinion, laughably useless and asks its customers to go through a ritual troubleshooting process that is equally as effective.

It is my opinion that this is a planned obsolescence of the product to push users to the Aria 2.

The result is a $129 scale that is a non-functional paperweight and, again in my opinion, not worth the money spent. I would recommend using a ‘dumb’ scale or finding a smart scale alternative. I recommend going to the FitBit Aria forums and taking a peak at the complaints and the ‘support’ responses.

Candidly, I was a huge FitBit fan (and have multiple products). This review is just to state my sincere disappointment in FitBit support of their products and their customer service. Once my HR2 is dead, I will never purchase a FitBit product again. And, after my experience, I would not recommend purchase of the Aria scale(s).

title: Great lightweight coverup + towel
text:
I am a disabled old lady who is very limited with the kind of exercise I can do, but I can swim, which I do 5 days a week at an senior center.

I bought a couple of approximately 35X60 inch microfiber backpacking towels for over $20 each, because they were extremely lightweight and absorbent. Weight is as important to me as it is to a mountain climber, I can carry only so much.

I was hoping that this was made out of the same material as the towels, and was disappointed to find that it was different, having a sight nap. Also it was the same size as the towels, but was heavier, 11.2 ounces as opposed to 6.8 each for the towels, of course I believe most of the difference in weight has to do with the weight of the 8 inch velcro strips and elastic band.

It turned out to be perfect for my needs. The elastic strip around the top is very good with a lot of stretch, and thus I believe anyone who can wrap a 60" towel around themselves will find it fits them.

And the best thing is this wrap is super absorbent, as absorbent as the towels of the same size that were over twice the price.

I hated having to change in fount of all the women in the locker room. Now, after my shower, I wrap myself in this and by the time I dry the parts of myself that were not covered, the parts that were are dry. I just put my lower clothes on without even removing the wrap, thus a lot of my modesty is maintained.

I read a couple of other reviews, where people were complaining the velcro stuck to other things, and yes, that is the nature of velcro, but I do not find it a difficult chore to always close the velcro scripts together when not wearing it.

Also, this wrap dries very quickly, in less then a forth of the time as terrycloth. After hanging it up after use, I find it is completely dry only 4 or 5 hours later.

title: Elevate your wet-shaving experience
text:
This is, perhaps, one of my better purchases for wet shaving! It is true that this item has a musky scent, but it is not over-powering, and it has seemingly faded with use. Initially, I rinsed the brush in flowing warm water while moving it in circles in the palm of my hand. That seemed to be a smart thing to do as it released some sort of darkly colored dye and a few bristles (less than 10, I'd say). Afterward I hung it, bristles down, and allowed it to dry.

My first shave with it was surprisingly easy, despite the presumed learning curve I expected to experience. For harder soaps like Mitchell's Wool Fat, it lathered quickly (and yes, I have softer water). For softer creams, it thinned it out more than I'd have liked, but then the brush is designed to retain water, so after a second attempt with a much dryer brush, I got better lathering results, but less "stored" lather in the bristles. I think the less "stored" later aspect had more to do with the shave cream and less to do with the brush, itself.

I recommend this product!

My last batch, 9 of the caps fell off as I was filling them. When they did fill properly, I had a tremendously difficult time getting the material out of the mold when I wanted to . If I stored in the freezer, too hard - I had to use a chopstick to push them out usually leaving about 1/2 the material in the mold and bashing my hand in the process.
Does anyone have any alternatives to this??? I would like to try something else.

Update: All things work for good. If these molds hadn't failed I would still be struggling with their usage. I switched to silicon gummy bear molds - www.amazon.com/gp/product/B078HL4QR7 - at 1/4 the cost, and couldn't be happier!!! They are 1000 times easier to fill - you have the whole length and width of the bear to drop your material onto instead of the small opening - no more wasted essential oils. They are a breeze to pop out of the mold, completely intact - couldn't be easier. And best of all, no parts that separate and wear out. title: Too much going on here. I'm looking for a hair, skin and nail supplement.
text:
Wasn't impressed with this “HSN” formula. I didn't see any results in the form of hair or nail growth. My skin didn't appear any different and I didn't notice any changes in my hair's strength or shine.

I have tried hair skin and nail support supplements in the past and have had decent results. I have found the ones that work the best are the most simple in recipe. This formula has ingredients I never heard of such as Plant Squalene and bamboo. The amount of Biotin (3000mcg) is disappointing.

This formula seems to have too much going on. It's claims sound more like those of a multivitamin. A lot of the mentioned benefits (cardiovascular, vision, energy increase and memory improvement) I expect from a multivitamin or other benefit specific supplement. When looking for a Hair, Skin and Nail supplement I want it to focus on just that. I think this company was trying to capture too much here.

Three capsules daily can be tiring. The price isn't too bad, but I have used HSN products in the past that cost around the same or less and work loads better. On the positive side, the capsules are quite easy to swallow and don't give off any bad smell or aftertaste.

I received this product at a discount in exchange for my honest and unbiased review. Always be cautious of “free or deeply discounted” product reviews, but DON'T discount every reviewer. Click on the reviewer's name and check their other reviews. Honest reviewers won't give every product a 5 star review and will typically write more than a few sentences.

I bought this Chlorella because I am having my Mercury filling removed and many sources suggest taking Chlorella before and after; additionally, it comes from Taiwan. I researched the location of the source of Chlorella extensively and Taiwan appeared to be the cleanest.
I have been taking it for almost a week and at the moment I do not feel anything specific, however, as I mentioned for me it is because I want to have Mercury filling removed. The thing I was not so happy about was: on picture 5 it says the ingredients are Organic Chlorella, on the ACTUAL product is says there is beta-carotene and folic acid. Now, I take a folate supplement and do not want to take folic acid due to its synthetic nature. If the 'folic acid' is not added but derived from the Chlorella, it should be called folate (the organic version in folic acid). I will continue to take this for the next month until my fillings are removed and replaced.

title: Four Channels Are Handy, Modes Don't Make Sense
text:
I like the fact that you can use four channels at a time, even more with the double lead they include. Device is mostly easy to use, except even after reading the minimal (and tiny) instruction booklet I still can't figure out how to sync all channels, so it's kind of annoying when you have electrodes on complementary body parts doing different things.

The 30 levels are fine for EMS but the TENS I wish I could go a bit higher. For the money though it does just fine. And the 24 modes are split up 12 modes each for TENS and EMS. A way to customize modes/any customization options besides intensity/duration would be nice but isn't a deal breaker.

Time can only be increased in increments of 10 minutes but you can turn it off whenever so it's not a big deal.

The instruction booklet (which as mentioned before) is very short and, seriously, incredibly tiny, so the pictures showing where to place electrodes are as good as useless. However this isn't a big deal since Google exists. Still would be nice to have a handy reference you could actually use.

The only things keeping this a 4 star review instead of 5 is the modes are very confusing. The modes are chosen based on choosing a picture of either a massage (TENS) or activity/sport (EMS) but the pictures don't make a lot of sense in regards to what they device is actually doing. There's not really a rhyme or reason to it that I can find. It makes it really hard to decide what mode to actually use. That along with the impossibility of getting channels to actually sync dropped it down a star.

Cost/benefit of the device though is still very much worth it, especially with the 4 channels, 30 intensity levels, 12 TENS + 12 EMS modes, and quality build of the device. You can definitely feel it working and it seems to be helping, at least short term. I suggest giving it a shot.

title: Saving my nips & my bfing journey
text:
I bought these following a work trip where I pumped exclusively vs my regular 3x/day. My nips were sore for weeks after, I wasn’t expressing as much milk as my LO needed, and I was so distraught. It took a couple weeks of experimenting, but these have been so wonderful! Pros/cons/tips:

Pros:
- I like that they came in a set cuz I do use diff sizes sometimes. 90% of the time it’s the blue XS ones, but it took a couple weeks to settle on that size.
- The silicone (S & XS) is a lot nicer than the rigid plastic IMO
- The downward angle means less pooling around the breast, so I don’t need to “scrape” the flange up at the end to ensure I get all the milk. I also think it better replicates the angle LO nurses from, which my breasts are used to, but this may be feeling vs fact.

Cons (reflected in Clean & Use stars):
- It took a couple weeks of trying sizes to settle on the XS—evaluating comfort at EOD/EOW and average milk expression.
- It took a couple weeks to get the hang of centering them well—and it still takes a couple tries
- The additional collar pieces for the silicone flanges are unfortunate. 2 more pieces to clean and keep track of! :( And they trap milk between collar and the Medela tubing/bottle/flange connector piece. I wish the silicone was simply thicker at the end.
- I do wish they were sold as 1-offs cuz I’d buy additional XS ones for home

Tips:
- Takes a bit of practice to get the hang of folding back the silicone to get the nipple both in the “tunnel” and centered well. Keep practicing!
- My IBCLC always made a big point of not letting the nipple rub the flange sides, so when this happened with the XS ones I worried. But again, after experimenting for a couple weeks, I found that the rubbing didn’t bother them at all! After a little condensation and milk gets in there there’s sufficient lubrication. YMMV here, but it’s working for me. (To be clear: the nipples still move freely, but they rub a bit at full suction/extension. If the flange isn’t centered it compresses the nipple and it doesn’t move freely, which isn’t what I’m describing here.)
- I haven’t had any issues with massaging my breasts and pumping with these at the same time. (There was another reviewer who had issues with this and I was worried about it.)

Heading into month 8 of breastfeeding and still going strong thanks to the comfort this product brought to my journey. Thank you!

title: Amazing value! Low mid-range chair at low end price.
text:
We've had the chair for about a month now. I'm 5'9" 230lbs and my girlfriend is 5'1" 110. The chair is perfect for her size, but I barely fit comfortably in it. I had my 6'4" cousin try it and that was fun to watch.

Pros:

1) At $769 dollars, this chair is a steal! Bought Amazon's extended warranty with it.
2) The chair looks great, very happy with the materials.
3) The remote functions are easy to use.
4) Massage presets range from torture to gentle bliss. This chair can really dig into your kidneys on some settings, no bueno!
5) The foot massage roller with the airbags is perfect, wearing socks is a must.
6) Bluetooth sounds decent, not for movies or games, just some background sound.

Cons:

1) The functions are a little simplistic, not much adjusting the auto massage programs. There should be a delay to let you get settled in, because once you start it, it goes immediately. A 5 second delay to get your arms setup would be ideal.

2) I barely fit into the chair comfortably. The shoulder massage does little more than crunch me. I should have researched this more, my bad.

3) There's no way to manually operate the calve's air bags. You can do feet and isolate every other area but the calves. My favorite auto function is the "sleep" mode and the calves don't inflate at all!!!

4) Some settings could bruise your kidneys if you don't know it's coming, but some people like it rough...

5) The arms are very underwhelming, I don't even use them about half the time. My GF uses the arms everytime.

This is the perfect entry level chair at an amazing price. Highly recommend!

title: Girlfriend-Approved
text:
It's been about a year since I tried Nora, and I'm still not murdered in my sleep. So, yeah, it works for me. I had been tested and approved for a CPAP device, but I knew from the testing alone that I would never use it. Like others, I had tried nasal spray, nose strips, mouth appliances and different pillows. So when a Nora ad popped up I gave it a try. Not because I had snoring-related issues like tiredness the next day, but because my significant other did. She very quickly responded favorably to this new woman in my life.
Regarding the device itself, it is pretty simple to use. The "egg" charges with a USB cable you connect to Nora. It has different sensitivity settings to account for background noise, etc. It also has a delay setting, so you can set it and still watch TV or talk for about 30 minutes before it starts to respond. The main body charges with a wall plug and generously long cord. I find it lasts through the night on a charge, but not all the way through two in my case. The egg lasts much longer per charge. The tube connecting the case and insert is also quite long.
The only problem I ever had was the bladder separating from the vinyl insert. Once I figured out that it was just velcro'd in, it was easy to fix.
I think that with the 30 day guarantee, it's a no-brainer. I wish I had known about the snore app others have referred to, as I would have tried it sooner.

title: It really is a nice way of consuming calories
text:
I've only had Soylent twice, one pre-bottled that tasted like cardboard (I'm assuming an old version) and now this v1.8 powder which has ended up becoming a staple of my weekly diet. There's not much to really say other than it's got a nice mild flavor and blends well with just about anything but cacao baking powder (that was a mistake on my part).

Because of the overhead cost on Amazon I happened to get a tub on sale and have been refilling it with monthly shipments from Soylent directly. It's a very friendly subscription service, add to it, subtract from it, skip a month, double up on a month, or cancel altogether. There's no hoops to jump through (this isn't a newspaper subscription) so it feels very risk free which I was afraid wouldn't be the case.

My base recipe is:
8 oz - Water
4 oz - Half-and-Half
1 scoop - the-chai-latte-formerly-known-as-big-train-chai from Costco
2 scoops - Soylent

It tastes great on it's own, but watermelon and blueberries add a nice flavor. I wasn't too impressed with raspberries, and apple is way too fibrous to be pleasant to drink. I haven't gotten around to getting in on blackberry or cherry action yet. At one point I went for a blackberry, blueberry, strawberry frozen mix but it was light on strawberries and the blackberries left a million seeds at the bottom.

text: I have been using Downunder footbeds for a long time.  I bought this pair to go into some new inline skates.  I use a pair in my work boots and in other pairs of inline skates.  I have also tried Superfeet, but find Downunder to have a better performance cupping the heel and supporting the arch.  They will add volume of material under the heel, which can push the top of the foot up against the laces or the metatarsal guard.  If the shoe doesn't have enough room, this will create a pressure point on the top of the foot.  On the flip side, adding this footbed can absorb some of the extra room in the heel if the boot has more padding on the ankle than it should, which tends to pinch the back of my foot or squeeze my ankle uncomfortably.  This footbed helped remove that problem in several skates and in my work boots.

Since I was afraid to use this product , I made my own concoction. May I say that it even tastes good. I used 1 Tbsp. of organic apple cider vinegar. 1/4 tsp. of organic ginger powder with 1 clove of grated fresh organic garlic . ( works great with a micro plane ) in a cup of filtered water , added some honey, let it sit for a while and voila\ a very tasty drink ! So good and so inexpensive. It sounds complicated but it is not. Took me just 5 minutes ! I drank it with the garlic , swirling often and not biting on it ,(the garlic)
My plan now is to make it in greater quantity (the vinegar will keep it from spoiling ) and strain it after a few days.
No more doling out so much money for a product in a cheap plastic bottle !

title: I REALLY wanted to like this.....
text:
I purchased this tongue scraper with high hopes, considering all the gleaming reviews, could you really blame me? Well, it wasn't a complete failure, but I was very disappointed considering this thing has one primary use. It does a good job. If you've NEVER cleaned your tongue, even with a toothbrush, then this might be a game changer. However, I normally brush my tongue with my toothbrush after I'm done brushing my teeth, and my toothbrush did a nearly complete job of removing that nasty white residue off my tongue. The tongue scraper scraped about 90% of my tongue clean. Even when I focused on the missed spots, I still couldn't completely clean my tongue. I really feel like I'm missing that scrubbing to really lift that white residue from in between my taste buds and other little crevices that are on my tongue.

If you never clean your tongue, this will definitely help you. If you already brush your tongue with your toothbrush, this will, at best, match what your toothbrush can already do. You definitely won't be blown away.

I ended up returning this item. They did ask for it back knowing I used it. I really hope they thoroughly clean these before they resell them! Otherwise multiple Amazon customers have gotten to know each other really well without even knowing it! haha.

title: Easy-to-use, simple blood pressure monitor
text:
I ordered the Blood Pressure Monitor by Antrolife to help keep tabs on my blood pressure at home. It is a small, lightweight device that comes with a bag for easy storage.

When you first turn on the device, it will walk you through an initial setup of inputting the date and time and then selecting if you’d like the device to speak to you or run silently, as well as the measurement units of kPa or mmHg.

The arm cuff was a bit difficult to set to the right size on my own arm at first. However, after a few days of use, I got the hang of it, and it became much easier.

After you’ve set it all up, taking a blood pressure reading is as easy as putting on the cuff and pressing start. Around a minute later, you’ll see your blood pressure rate in large, easy-to-read numbers on the device’s screen.

The readings have been in line with the readings I get at my doctor’s office, and I am happy with the device overall.

My only complaint is that when setting the date, there is no indication of what part of the date you are setting on the device or in the manual (DD/MM/YYYY or YYYY/MM/DD) as you set two numbers in groups of two on each screen. And on the time setting, I guessed it wanted time in a 24-hour format, but there wasn’t any mention of which it wanted in the manual (12-hour or 24-hour). That said, I don’t know that it really matters as there isn’t any date displayed on the screen during the reading or in the recorded memory function that I can find.

title: case should be smaller and shorter; hollow construction makes it hard to clean
text:
Normally these tools come in a case that is barely bigger than the tool, making it very portable and stowable. The suction cup sticks firmly to the inside of the cap, making it easy to remove from the case. The case is normally closed with a sliding cork cap. And normally the tool itself is solid.

This product, though, is hollow, which means you can never really get it clean. The tool is always loose inside the case rather than stuck to the inside of the cap, which makes it easier to drop on the floor or down the drain and lose when desperately fumbling for a way to retrieve a wandering lens.

I also don't like the fact that the lid screws on. I use this tool primarily in emergencies, where a very dry contact has slid up under my eyelid and I can barely keep my composure due to pain and blindness. So it's literally too much work and precision to have to unscrew the lid. I need rapid-fire action when I'm wincing in pain! :)

It does work, though. If I drop my contact in the sink concave side down, I can easily pick it up with this too. So it's an ok product. But I wouldn't buy it again.

title: I'm Impressed, Did A Great Job in My Shower
text:
I've been using green and natural cleaning products for years, and this one has definitely impressed me with its performance. It has a decent citrus smell that is not too overbearing unless you have to use quite a bit of it, then the smell can get pretty strong where you need to ventilate the area. I have been using it at full strength and that seems to work best for me and what I need to clean.

The first thing I tried this in was my garbage disposal. I poured 2 quarter cups down the drain in the first week and it definitely presented a better and more pleasant smell from the drain. After the first week of using there was no bad smell coming from the drain after that. I have used this on my laminate flooring and tile in my bathroom and it did a great job cleaning them up with no damage whatsoever.

The thing that impressed me the most about this cleaner was how well it cleaned my shower and the grout in there. I have tried other cleaners and none have been able to clean the grout and tile in there better than this one. I just sprayed it full strength, let it sit for a few minutes, then took an old toothbrush and scrubbed everything clean.

If you have some tough to clean areas, I definitely recommend giving this a try, it works.

title: Literally saved my backside
text:
I had a big work project that meant more and more hours in my old desk chair in front of the computer. It was getting to the point that I was so sore when I stood up, that I could hardly move. I started looking at other chair options, but I couldn't find anything I really liked (adjustable arms like my chair has, seem to be hard to find). It occurred to me one day that maybe I just needed a cushion. I had run across the Purple brand randomly out on the internet before, and I reviewed all the cushion options on their site and here on Amazon. Admittedly when I finally made the purchase here on Amazon, I was desperately uncomfortable sitting here at the computer. But I figured I needed to go for this Ultimate one due to the size being about the same as the seat of my chair. When it arrived a couple days later, I literally was opening it up during a conference call. It was a perfect fit, and has made all the difference in the world! The culmination of the big work project was that in 7 days I worked 95 hours. This cushion literally made that possible.

My chair is entirely cloth covered and the seat is fairly flat. The Ultimate Purple cushion comes already in the black cover, which has rubbery nubbins on the underside. If I get up and down a few times, it starts to slide forward a little. No big deal to me, I just quickly adjust it back into place and sit down.

Since I started using this, I'm able to get up out of my chair, even after many hours (which we all know we shouldn't sit so long, but we all have a lot of demands on our time, and the hours fly by) with not even a thought to being sore or uncomfortable. It literally and truly saved my backside!

I got them for five and a half bucks through Amazon Prime, with free shipping, half-way through last year. I see the price has gone up, AND it's now an "add-on" item that I'd have to spend so much to get free shipping- while wording it in such a way to make you think that the item wouldn't have been available otherwise. It was. I get that it's expensive to ship small and cheap things, and it cuts a couple bucks off the profit on a cheap item, but to me, this sort of defeats the purpose of Prime- when Amazon has pretty much always had a cut-off to get free shipping UNLESS you were Prime. Other sellers have it for less than five bucks now, with free shipping. Yes, it cuts into the profits to ship "free," but by taking away the option, you cut back the amount of business by driving people to more competitively priced sellers which are on the right side of the screen. Not that Amazon cares about getting my business over an extra buck or two over a few replacement toothbrush heads, but that buck they save by not shipping it free will now probably go to someone else the next order... Amazon will still get a cut, but it won't be as big. Just a thought.

The shaving sheets sounded like a promising idea. I had visions of the little sheets foaming into masses of lather. No, not so. title: There is SO much that I love about this straightening brush
text:
There is SO much that I love about this straightening brush. I have tried others and they had flaws that caused them to be a styling tool that I would not use on a daily basis. I love the "idea" of the straightening brush and I knew that one designed well would be such a fantastic tool for daily styling.

This one is the one I was waiting for. My hair is fine, medium in thickness, has quite a bit of curl, and tends to frizz when I don't straighten it with a straightening iron. Because my hair isn't very thick, though, a straightening iron tends to leave my hair very flat with absolutely no body or fullness.

I feel like the Gisala Metal Ceramic Hair Straightening Brush straightens my hair without removing all of the volume. It looks softer and natural, but it still removes all the frizz and curl. The straightening brush reaches the same high levels of heat as my straightening iron does so the smooth styling has the same staying power.

There are several features that set this straightening brush apart from the others on the market right now. It has a long power cord that swivels 360 degrees at the base. This is a feature you find on almost all professional styling tools because it makes them SO much easier and less awkward to use. It prevents the cord from tangling while you use it.

It is lightweight with a handle that fits very comfortably in your hand while you use it. The buttons used to operate the straightening brush are located on the very front of the handle instead of on the side. On the other brushes with the buttons on the side, it is impossible not to push the buttons while you use the brush. The Gisala Hair Straightening Brush has the added protection of a "Lock" feature so that you can't accidentally push the buttons to change the temperature or turn the brush on and off while styling.

A digital display flashes until the desired heat setting is reached, then it remains solid.

The heated brush plates are close together so that they easily come into contact with all strands of your hair. The heated base and brush bristle plates are super smooth. They are bordered and topped with equally smooth teeth that remain cool to the touch. Because all parts of the brush are super smooth the brush easily glides through your hair, not pulling or breaking it.

Other brushes have rubbery tips on top of the brush plates that make them hard to pull through your hair so that you could tangle and damage your hair.

I know it isn't the most important thing, but I adore the Cyan color and design of this brush. It also comes in a Gold color that looks like it would be beautiful, too.

This comes beautifully packaged in a box with a magnetic closure. Included in the box are the straightening brush, a cleaning brush tool, a heat protection glove, a pretty black drawstring bag to store the straightening brush and accessories in, and a warranty card. The operating instructions are printed on the inside of the top of the box. They are complete and very easy to understand.'

title: cooling and heating effect with anti-inflammation Boswellia. Spray applicator is convenient.
text:
When I review a pain relief item, I am interested in the mechanism for pain relief whether it 1) absorbs deep into the pain source such as high quality Emu oil does, or 2) whether it masks pain through a cooling and/or heating sensation. The latter type of pain relief can relax muscles and thus, potentially free joints-- thus both mechanisms are useful. This particular product works primarily according to the second route. That is, it contains a menthol (called methyl salicylate) that first cools the injury sight, then leaves a lasting feeling of heat. In addition to this primary ingredient however, they include Indian frankincense (from the plant, Boswellia) as an anti-inflammation agent. So this product is trying to be the best of both approaches. For about two weeks I have been comparing this pain medicine to other pain relief creams and lotions. I love the spray applicator so my hands do not get messy or greasy. It makes it more convenient to use when in public for instance, or at bedtime when one simply wants to turn out the lights and not run to the washroom to scour hands clean. The spray has a feint menthol + rubbing alcohol smell and a few seconds after spraying it will leave a cool feeling, a minute later the cool becomes hotter. Feels like icy hot in a spray. However, I sleep better knowing that unlike pure icy hot creams, this also has boswellia to lower inflammation. So it is supposed to mask and speed healing. I cannot tell you if the inflammation is actually going down, but I do get relief. Though not as much relief as my emu oil. As an added bonus, the product evaporates my sweat (there must be alcohol in the product) adding an additional layer of cooling and keeps me dryer.

Overall, This product ranks #2 among 6 types of pain relief I have been using off and on. My favorite product however (a cream with high quality hemp and menthol and emu oil) is 4 times more expensive than this spray. Given the $10 per bottle price, which seems more than reasonable for what you get, I will happily give it 5 stars. I hope this helps with your pain and please give this a thumbs up if my review has helped you with your decision to purchase (or not)

Others have complained about the plate scratching the shower arm during installation. It will if you install the arm first and then slide the plate on the long way. Then, push this new plate on to the new arm starting at the end that will be installed in the wall up to the same distance OR less. THEN screw in the new arm. This was a replacement for an older shower kit I had and I found that the wall pole on this new one was too long for the holes that were already drilled. title: Going with another brand until the price comes down
text:
This review has been edited since its first publication:

Sequel Vega Optimizer mixes a smoothie recipe of flax, hemp, brown rice, chlorella and pea powder together so you don't have to do it yourself. Vega isn't the only product to do this with smoothie ingredients, but it's arguably the best.

Vega charges a whopping 37 to 45 dollars a pound. Organic or not, vegan or not, that's just incredibly expensive. Am I being unfair? I think not. Most of these ingredients by themselves, even at full retail price, cost an average of 15 dollars a pound. We're talking about grains, seeds and green algae here, which in bulk should be reasonably priced for consumption.

Maybe it's because Whole Foods carries and markets it, maybe it's because of the fancy logo and the celebrity endorsement. Considering the actual costs of mixing these ingredients together and selling them in a plastic tub, Vega has made its R&D investment back many times over already.

When the price is down around 40 dollars a tub, I purchase a vanilla chai or chocolate flavor tub. Otherwise, when the price of Vega shoots up seasonally to the 60 dollar region, I buy the Tru-Foods brand, which offers virtually the same mix for about 32 dollars a tub. That's half the price, and closer to the fair market price for these ingredients. I use this product every day for weeks at a time, so I'm saving significant coin by going with Tru-Foods. I'm hoping that other well known nutrition brands make a similar product to force the Vega price down to reasonable levels.

title: Nerdwax - it just doesn't work
text:
I am unsure why there are so many positive reviews. As usual, any product works on only a distribution of customers, and in this case, Nerdwax did nothing for me at all. Slippage is influenced by several factors, namely, the oiliness of the skin surface, the friction of the nose pad, the tightness of the pad arms, temples and temple tips, the weight of the frames, and the activity of the wearer. My nose pad is a non-slip variant that is offers decent grip. The pad arms and the temples are not especially tight as that would be uncomfortable but they were fitted by an optometrist and so they are not abnormally lose. The spectacles are made of titanium and are frameless. The lens are ultra-thin high-index lenses which weight very little. I tend to spend my time working at the office computer. The only factor left unaddressed is the oiliness of the skin. I do tend to have oily skin but not terribly oily. So despite all this, my glasses tends to slip, not by a whole lot, but enough to be annoying. Therefore, the only thing I could address is the oily skin, which led me to try Nerdwax.

Well, it didn't work at all. More does not always result in better performance, so I experimented with various amounts, from just a quick application of the wax on the pads, to prolonged waxing. I even tried to apply the wax directly to my nose (after washing my face of course). No matter what amount of wax I used, my glasses would slowly inch down my nose about 2 minutes later. In fact I didn't notice any difference whether I used Nerdwax or not.

I am glad others have been having success with it, but as far as I am concerned, it doesn't work at all.

title: Not too bad
text:
I have two tubs...the new kind and an older porcelain tub. Will not stick to either tub!! The best I can do is put about one inch of water in bottom of tub, then put mat in to tub and try to suction it to tub as best as possible. Then I sit in tub carefully covering mat with my body. Last, I turn water on and fill tub then turn machine on when tub level is good. If you put on bottom of tub then fill with water before getting in tub....it will just float to top of water. Try my directions and it will work fairly well. You will have to use your body to keep mat on bottom of tub. I just get comfortable with my bath pillow and a book and I do not move. I see most of the reviews have the same complaint. Either make it work for you like I did, or send it back for a refund.

The noise people complain about is no problem. First...most whirlpools and hot tubs, even the kind at the gym, make noise. I think most people forget instead of being in a large room where the sound can dissipate, you are in a bathroom. Of course it will be loud!! However, I find that with a nice book or magazine or just shutting my eyes and resting.....sound is no problem. I kinda melt in to the sound:)

When you are spending less than $100 for a bubble experience do not expect the same kind of results you would get with an actual bubble tub, whirlpool. This is the poor ladies spa. However, it can be a nice experience if you make a few adjustments and I am sorry to say stop complaining about silly things like some people have in these reviews. Honestly; the complaints about the noise is so silly. Some people act they are going crazy or it is the worse sound they have heard. Hey folks....a machine in a small bathroom....yes it is going to be a little loud. The last time I stayed at a hotel with a large whirlpool hotel in my room...when I turned that thing on I could not hear my Husband talk unless he was within about 7 or 8 feet of tub! Try using the sound to block out the rest of the world! It works!

title: Gave it 3 days of 8-hour a day use and still didn't like it
text:
I purchased this seat cushion because I work from home most of the time and sometimes spend long periods sitting during phone calls and web conferences. I had been using the [[ASIN:B01B23UM74 Comfy Cure Coccyx Memory Foam Seat Cushion - Top Doctor Recommended Premium Grade Orthopedic Cushion for Back/Tailbone Pain Relief - Office Chair and Car Seat Cushion]] and wondered if one of these would be more comfortable.

After 3 days of using The Royal Purple seat cushion 8-hours a day, I have went back to the Sleep Restoration Comfy Cure seat cushion.

Things I didn't like about The Royal Purple:
- It somehow manages to be too thick and not thick enough at the same time. Too thick where my thighs meet my butt. Too thin where my butt cheeks meet the seat. It creates a ridge where my thighs are that is uncomfortable. And my tailbone is achy at the end of the day from not enough cushion.

- Not wide enough or long enough. I'm not a huge guy - a size 38 - but my entire butt does not fit on this cushion. I hang over the sides of it by ~2" on each side. And I was constantly trying to push it back further in my chair to get more coverage on my tailbone. The size is just wrong for me all around.

- Moves around in my chair whenever I move. The grippy bottom on this does not grip my chair like the Sleep Restoration Comfy Cure one does - which is strange because they both have similar grip dots. I guess the ones on The Royal Purple aren't as grippy. Either way, The Royal Purple required constant repositioning because it never stayed where I put it.

title: Honestly, these taste pretty awful.
text:
I was thrilled to find this gummy supplement on Amazon last week, especially because the price was awesome and it contains Omega 3s, 6s, and 9s. I looked at a lot of different products, being careful to weed out the ones with labels stating they are made with fish oil powder (because "fish burps" are so unpleasant). My kiddo has high cholesterol, and I read many different reviews of this product that said it tastes great, so I had high hopes. However, I can only assume other reviewers must have received a different product than what I got, because these things taste just disgusting. Disclaimer: This was my first experience with an Omega-3 gummy supplement; maybe they all taste this bad, or worse? Anyway, reviews that say these gummies taste like "lemon curd" or "candy" are INCREDIBLY misleading, at best. The worst lemon curd or candy I've ever tasted was tons better-tasting than this stuff. These gummies taste, well, like fish oil, which is precisely what I was trying to avoid by purchasing a gummy supplement.

I'd like to say that these are a good value for the money, but I can't even do that because there's no way I can even chew these without wanting to retch - much less give them to my teenage daughter - and they aren't eligible for return (I'll be more careful to check that little detail on future purchases). So even though the price was right, I still lost money - meaning they weren't a good value for me personally. I was looking forward to seeing if these would help to lower cholesterol/triglycerides, and I hope they do (but I won't be finding out for myself). Best of luck to anyone else who purchases these!

title: True 60w replacement at only 10.5w, here are the details...
text:
Two of my outdoor 14 watt CFLs burned out. So I replaced them with these Phillips LED bulbs. I was not sure how well they would work, but they ended up working great and have the same brightness as my 14w CFLs.

Phillips usually puts accurate information on their lighting products (unlike many other bulb manufacturers). These are 3000k color temperature. Don't confuse color temperature (kelvin) with brightness (lumen). Incandescent bulbs are usually about 2700k, where daylight is 5000-5500k which is a true white light. That spaceship blue light you typically see with LEDs is about 6000k and above. 6000k is not anywhere near a natural light color.

A 60 watt incandescent bulb relates to the brightness (lumen) of a 14w CFL bulb. LED wattage does not have a direct lumen comparison to incandescent or CFL bulbs because the light emitting diodes in LED bulbs come in many different variations. The lumen scale is the proper way to judge brightness between all of them. Here is a chart for comparison:
40 watt incandescent = about 450 lumens
60 watt incandescent = about 800 lumens
75 watt incandescent = about 1,100 lumens
14 watt CFL = about 800 lumens
15 watt CFL = about 830 lumens
This Phillips (424895) 10.5 watt LED bulb = 800 lumens (180 degree light spread)
Phillips (409904) 12.5 watt LED bulb = 800 lumens (330 degree light spread)
Phillips (423244) 10.5 watt L-Prize LED bulb = 940 lumens (330 degree light spread, close to 70 watt incandescent equivalent)

At the time of this writing, a 10.5 watt LED that puts out 800 lumens, like this bulb does, is pretty darn good.

I am not sure if these bulbs are rated for outdoor use, but I have them installed outdoors where my non-outdoor rated compact florescent light (CFL) bulbs were installed. Both the CFLs and this LED light have worked great in our northern temperature ranges of 90 degrees to -3 degrees Fahrenheit. We also have high humidity.

I have these bulbs set up on an automatic timer switch. It leaves the lights on for about 9 hours a night for 7 days a week. Even in the cold, they light-up instantaneously; where the CFLs needed about 15 minutes to get at full brightness. My CFLs lasted for 4 years in this environment, so I hope these LED bulbs will last for 6 to 7 years.

The size of this LED bulb is perfect as an incandescent replacement because it is the same size.

The only negative I have about these bulbs is the narrow spread of light. Because of the long base, it leaves only half of a dome to disperse light to only about a 180 degree angle. I would prefer a 300 degree spread to shed more light around the area. If you want a greater dispersion of light, then get the other kind of Phillips bulbs since they are designed with more rounded domes:
[[ASIN:B007RKVT4C Philips 423244 10-Watt 60-Watt L-Prize Award Winning LED Light Bulb]]
[[ASIN:B00APTS030 Philips 425264 12-watt A19 LED Household Daylight Light Bulb, Dimmable]]

I bought these on sale for about $27 a pair, so I am very happy with them for the price. I really like their performance in my outdoor setting, so I will buy more for the other fixtures.

I would have given it five stars if it had a wider spread of light. 4.5 stars is more appropriate.

text:

This is one fantastic product at a very low price.

I'l like to post an addendum to the original post: Although the product did work, I found the itching would always return, so evidently it was only a temporary fix and I found I was scratching just like I was before using the product. What I just tried and it seems even better than Miracell was just putting a few drops of "Scalpicin" which I had in the cabinet for scalp itch, I put some on the Q-Tip and rolled it around inside the ear, and I think it's actually better than the Miracell. I think once you can break the itch - scratch cycle, it may be cured.

title: Worked great at first, but then started broadcasting my weight to my boyfriend
text:
My love-hate relationship with my Aria in three acts:

Act I
Set-up was a nightmare. I downloaded the setup.exe to my laptop and after an hour of trying to get it set-up, even though the set-up executable never said that it was set-up correctly, it seemed to be working. It was connected to my wifi anyway and updating my fitbit account correctly.

Act II
While it was working, it was amazing! Loved it!

Act III
Shortly after receiving it, I invited my boyfriend to use it. It worked fine for awhile, until maybe a week ago. All of a sudden, I was showing up as guest on the scale and my Fitbit account wasn't updating. I tried taking out the batteries and starting the whole nightmare-ish installation process again but nothing worked.

Found out yesterday that my scale has been shooting out my weight to my boyfriend's account for the last week! It seems to think that he owns the scale and it's updating his account with my weight! My worst nightmare!

Even worse is that there was no way to remove the scale from his account. He had to un-invite himself from the scale but I'm not sure how that is going to work since the scale seems to think it belongs to him now.

And aside from the obvious humiliation of having my weight bandied about indiscriminately, the worst part is that I love that scale. I want it back working properly. Now I'll have to call Customer Care (if they even have one) and try to get it working again, which I hate more than anything. (And I won't be inviting ANYONE to use the scale again!)

Fitbit, please please please fix the installation and privacy problems! It's such a great product.

I can have flare ups from vibration (driving in a car was always bad) or holding a cold cup or gripping something too tight. In one week's time, I have been able to, without incident, drive, hold cold cups, put my hands in frozen fruit to make my smoothie and not have to warm my hands up. Unless it works on me for my issues I am skeptical, however, I am a skeptic no longer and am a believer that yes, with the right natural products you can help your body without the use of pharmaceuticals.

text:
I am a protein powder conniseure as well as partners in a supplement company that we make our own protein powder so I am extremely picky when it comes to make a smoothie or shake with anyone's protein powder. I read up on the benefits of Collagen Whey and decided as I fight the wrinkles that I'd rather put something natural in my body that helps with collagen than all these gimmick creams and serums you read about out there. I pretty much ordered three different variations of Vital Proteins Collagens proteins and will be trying all 3 and reviewing them but so far making a Strawberry Banana Smoothie with this one TAKES THE CAKE!!!!
Recipe
1 cup unsweetened almond or coconut milk
1/4 cup creamy peanut butter
1/2 teaspoon vanilla
1 cup frozen strawberries
3/4 cup ice (if not using frozen bananas)
Blend all above, then add.....
2 scoops of Vital Proteins Banana, Cinnamon and Vanilla Collagen (add last to blender)
2 frozen bananas (or regular) I just like mine frozen-- if not frozen add ice
Finish Blending....Makes 2 full 8 ozs of smoothies

The bristles are very soft and I use a homemade tooth powder that can be quite abrasive, so the soft head is perfect for that. I've only used it a few times but so far it's holding together well. The head is narrower than the typical toothbrush, so that was a little strange to get used to, but I don't think it really takes away from the performance of the brush. By buying the 12 pack I ended up spending just over a dollar a brush, so it was a great deal. I used a marker to write my name on the handle on case my husband decides to switch over too. Would buy again.

title: More for Less
text:
I injured my back earlier this summer. While undergoing physical therapy, it was recommended that I get a pair of Lofstrand crutches to help me get around. At first I was shocked at the cost from the local Walgreen's or CVS. Even on-line (Amazon) you can spend $140.00 for a pair. And the cost of renting a pair from a medical supply firm wasn't much better. Then I discovered everything is in a name. Instead of using the word Lofstrand I searched for forearm crutches and got more hits for much less expensive crutches than I'd been looking at previously. [Does anyone know if there is something special about Lofstrand crutches versus forearm crutches that would cause them to be more expensive?]

I ordered a pair of forearm crutches for about 1/3 the cost of the Lofstrands. When I got them I couldn't really tell the difference between them and the Lofstarnds I'd looked at at Walgreen's.
