I have really enjoyed using the Celleanser Vegan Clean Toner, and my skin seems to like it too. I also tried the Celleanser Clean Serum, and the Celleanser Clean Cream. They all worked nicely for my dry, sensitive skin, and they worked nicely together.

This toner mist is a very fine, soothing liquid mist that provides an extra layer of hydration, moisture, and antioxidants on the skin. It is applied immediately after cleansing, or as a soothing refresher throughout the day. It soaks into the skin nicely, and prepares the skin to absorb the next steps of the skincare routine. It is not sticky, and it layers perfectly with other products. The scent is incredibly light, and it disappears immediately.

I will say that the finish of this line of products isn't my go-to. It isn't really dewy or glowy. But I wouldn't call it extremely matte either. Maybe somewhere in-between, but more toward the matte side. I typically like to use dewy, glowy skincare, so I would probably use this product at night for that reason.

The packaging is very nice with a unique-looking, tall plastic bottle with a very functional mister. It seems to produce short, fine bursts of mist. At $19.99 for 120ml / 4.05 fl. oz., it's a pretty good deal. Especially because the ingredient list is nice.

I haven't been using it long enough to speak on the long-term results, but I do like this toner mist so far, and I will definitely continue to use it. I would recommend this to anyone who likes the ingredient list and wants to give it a try.

title: Good Brush for applying beard oil.
text:
I was looking for a way to apply my beard oil everyday without using to much or getting covering my hands in oil. I bought this brush and poured about a quarter of my beard oil into the can so I could apply as needed.

Pros:
1. Absorbs and applies oil well. I poured a fourth of my beard oil into this container. The boars hair fibers absorbed it very quickly. But it will applies the perfect amount to my beard. Not to much, not to little. Does the job I bought it for 100%!
2. Prevents wasted oil. This is the main reason I bought it. I was either using to much, or to little oil. Now I pour my oil into the bottom of the tin, put the brush in there and apply every morning after my shower. Does exactly what I need it to!

Cons:
1. There was a strong odor on the bristles before they were used. At first I thought it was mold, but it wasn't a bad smell... Hard to describe.
2. Lots of loose hairs. As I use this product, I find random long boar hairs in my beard. As I have used it, it has become less common. So just expect it to lose a bunch of hairs in the beginning.
3. The can it comes in is very flimsy. The second time I closed the tin it comes in, I bent the tin. Not so badly that it cannot close, but bad enough that it will never be the same. So word of advice, close the tin from the edges and not from the center. haha

Bottom Line:
If you need a way to apply beard oil effectively without wasting copious amounts... This product will help!

UPDATE 2-28-20
I finally got a new one of these and it works so I put it in the fridge and it operates as the manual said it would BUT this unit produces the cleaning version of Ozone. Yes, it will sanitize the fridge and freezer at the 50ppm it produces in the sealed sections but once you OPEN the door to the fridge you will INHALE that Ozone while loading or unloading the fridge. THAT is NOT healthy for you or me.
HOWEVER, I give it 4 stars because of how I am going to use it safely. Nothing cleans a fridge better than ozone because generally air is usually shared with the freezer. So, a few times a month I will put this in the fridge overnight while nobody is opening the fridge to let it sanitize and then remove it in the morning and take the batteries out so I put it back in it’s box to store until the next sanitizing date I choose. For this particular use only I would consider it safe to use and earns 4 starts. But I would never use it 24/7 as advertised on the box because every time you opened the fridge or freezer you would inhale a blast of ozone which is not a good thing. You can clean the inside messes spilled in your fridge and then use this overnight only to sanitize and you will have the most sanitary fridge start up for the week! title: Although marketed for men's beards, this comb is equally great for women's hair!
text:
Very happy with this brush/comb. It's well built and fits nicely in my hand. I found it much easier to use than my longer more expensive hot comb. Simply press button once for blue light (350 degrees), twice for green light (410 degrees) and hold button to turn off. In less than a minute, the light stops blinking and the comb is ready for use. The green setting worked great to straighten my super curly hair. It's important to read the operating instructions before using as there are helpful tips in there on the best way to use this product.

The unit does get hot after about 10 minutes but the company provides a nice glove to protect your hands, which I didn't need to use because I was finished before it got uncomfortable. The only complaint I have is that it is easy to press the button and change the setting during use, but that's really a minor issue.

Overall, this is a great product that I plan to take with me on vacation (it comes with a carry bag) and will now use it at home instead of my larger hot brush.

title: This is real pain relief--from the laboratory of neuroscientists.
text:
It has been 25 years since I have experienced a pain-free day. I have extra bone growth throughout my body, severe arthritis in several joints and Parkinsonism--which contributes electric-shock pains several times a day to a random part of my body.

I have been totally disabled since 2002--I was 45 years old at the time. I have become quite discerning about the types, flavors and intensities of various types of pains.

Overnight, Ted's Pain Creme eliminated 70% of all of my pain.

This is not like other topical pain creams, so don't mutter "everyone knows that topical treatments don't work." Instead of trying to mask or distract from the pain, Ted's takes a novel approach to block certain pain signals from reaching the brain.

Ted's research team (focused on pain in mammals) discovered a key difference in the way that new, legitimate pain is transmitted. So they set out to disrupt the communication of previous illegitimate pain. After all, pain from an injury I received three hours, or three days, or thirty years ago does nothing to help me avoid additional harm to my body. I want to know when something is supposed to hurt, but not to be nagged by old news.

It works like the sustain feature of the piano. Think of striking the key as the onset of new pain. Something has changed, perhaps suddenly. But with the sustain pedal, the sound doesn't quickly go away; it goes on and on and on. Ted's Cream does nothing to cure anything--the reason for the initial key strike, nor does it prevent additional keys from being struck. It does cut the effects of most pain short, so that you can clearly hear additional notes, instead of one awful discordant mess of indistinguishable notes.

Everyone is different. Chances are your Aunt's best friend's former son-in-law experienced some miracle pain relief by wrapping their head in dirty socks. There is no reason to believe this will work for me.

Ted's seems to work best for relatively surface pain--it is great for my elbows, ankles, knees, feet and hands. It is somewhat less effective on deep shoulder pain, and doesn't seem to help much for the deep hip pains.

Carpal Tunnel: was headed to surgery and this eliminated the pain, which allowed the inflammation to heal and the problem went away. Now if I stop whatever I am doing when the tweaks start, I will experience no pain.

Severe knee osteoarthritis: both knees, wrists, shoulders, elbows. Ted's reduces pain by probably 90%, once the initial applications take effect (several times a day for a few days). Now I reapply when something starts to hurt again, about every 4-8 weeks.

Organ pain: no change.

bone pain: for bones relatively close to the skin, it can eliminate 70%- 90% of the pain. Again, reapply only when it starts to hurt again.

wound pain: extremely effective, applied not to the wound, but liberally around the wound. It worked wonders on road rash I sustained when my wheelchair tipped over, trapping me underneath (after extraction and application a couple of times). A colleague said it worked on sunburn pain, although I have not had a sunburn in many years. . .and I am not going to be stupid in order to test this account.

muscle pain: sprains, bruises and painfully tight muscles all respond well, although with muscle lock, the new pain keeps continuing, so it will bring only brief relief. Brief enough I can work on some stretches in the reduced-pain window.

migraine pain: some people report wonderful results but I don't have this particular problem (thank God)

This is not an exhaustive list, but it gives a flavor of the type of pain most likely to be relieved. At $25 a tube, which will last for months, now that you know if you are tied up in pain it's probably on you for not trying this product.

The gel is like a roll-on deodorant plastic-ball thing. It has almost no smell. The creme is laced with Wintergreen oil and other herbs so it is quite minty for hours. The professional strength (new product) is more effective than the original, but not 4x as much.

Apply it liberally, rubbing it in like sunscreen to help the skin absorb it (it works transdermally). Re-apply 2 or 3 times a day until you notice a large reduction in your pain. Then re-apply when it starts to hurt again.

Look, folks, this is not a fly-by-night nutritional supplement scam. It is produced by neuro-scientists in scientific labs as a serendipitous discovery from a different experiment. The NIH (National Institutes of Health) believe in its effectiveness enough to fund the development of a related treatment for post-operative eye pain (don't rub Ben-Gay into your eyes, really).

I refused to try absolutely everything pushed at me. I tried products that had some reasonable explanation that stood up to scrutiny (why should I believe this will work?) Just try it, please. Pain is not our friend.

title: used it to make an ice pack
text:
Put 80% water and 20% glycerin (by volume) into an ice pack, and voila, you now have an ice-pack that you can re-freeze. No need to put cubes in there every time. Just throw it right back in the freezer. The glycerin acts as anti-freeze. It will get semi-solid, in the freezer, but still remains pliable, kind of like firmly packed snow. You then massage it a bit, so that it becomes soft again, and voila, you have a very cold ice pack. (Even colder than regular ice.)

The product is non-toxic, and I do not believe that it goes stale or spoils. Basically, should last forever. Preferably, use purified water, so that it won't spoil.

If you want it softer, try 75% water, and 25% glycerin ratio. That should work well. If it gets too hard, then let it thaw, pour out some of the mixture, and add in a bit more glycerin. If it is not thick enough, then add in more water instead. Let it re-freeze, and there you go.

title: Excellent VG for DIY e-liquids
text: Excellent, non GMO, kosher USP food grade VG. I use it for making my own  e-liquid (heretofore referred to simply as juice) and I couldn't ask for a better product. It's much less expensive than buying from a B&M vape shop (if they'll even sell it to you) or an online vape shop. I quit smoking cigarettes back in 2012 after I bought a cig-a-like from 7-11, it didn't produce much vapor, but it got me off the tobacco. I vape a lot and I've gone through a liter of VG every 3-4 months for use in my juice and that's only for my personal use. This VG is clear, slightly sweet, and highly viscous compared to propolyne glycol (PG), the other main component of most juices. PG is closer in viscosity to water, therefore it is used to thin out the mixture of your juice and give it more throat hit (TH makes juice comparable to a real cigarette). I personally don't use any PG in my e-liquid, because I don't care for any throat hit, I prefer a max VG juice because it's the ingredient that produces lots of vapor. If you are a vaper thinking of making your own juice I wouldn't hesitate to start because you'll save a lot of money and you can learn to make flavors that are specific to your preferred needs and taste. If you consider the low price of this VG, around $13.00 for a liter, plus the cost of flavoring, (and another necessary ingredient which is highly addictive), you'll be at about ¢35 for a 30ml bottle. Compare that to how much you pay for high quality (high percentage VG usually 80%) juice from a vape shop which on average is about $22.00 for 30ml bottle, and you'll see the savings on juice alone. Vaping is not cheap. Not for me anyway, however using products like this VG will definitely help you keep more money in your wallet and you'll feel the health benefits from quitting smoking 🚬. I was a pack a day smoker for thirty years. I only wish vaping would have been an option a long time ago. Now I have COPD and require oxygen. That's why I'm such a proponant of vaping or e-cigarettes (if you want to call it that) I don't like the term, it is too misleading but it's very recognizable. I will definitely recommend you buy your VG from this seller. It's a high quality product and I will be buying more in the near future. I hope this review is helpful and informative.

title: A Home Necessity
text: Okay you guys, listen up. I can not even express how glad I am to have purchased glycerin. I bought this specific bottle for $11.47 in September, 2013 and I swear I saw it;s price drop to $8.99 earlier in December. Nonetheless, I got the most bang for my buck from this seller than any others on amazon. My original intention when purchasing this bottle was to make alcohol-free herbal extracts. I've found many uses for it since then. It makes the perfect facial scrub; a great alternative for those of us who cringe at the thought of rubbing a scrub made of oil into our faces, no matter how many times they say it's hypoallergenic or won't cause a breakout. Instead of sugar I add pure epsom salt because I don't like sticky. It makes the skin soft, smooth, and moisturized. I also use glycerin as a hair serum for a shiny and soft effect. Add a small amount after towel drying and brush or comb hair when fully dry. Really, it makes hair incredibly soft, particularly the next day. It's a great moisturizer too, though I would not advise applying it undiluted near your eyes as it make make them feel puffed. Hell, I could use it in beverages and meals. I suppose I should stop here, and say that I still have more than half the bottle left. Glycerin goes a long way for small uses. Now, my only recommendation, for my own convenience sake, is that the bottle come with a waterproof label. The ink has completely diminished because of water contact. But hey, I still love the stuff. Just look at how many personal care products list glycerin as an ingredient. It's a necessity for health care. If only it were like $1 a gallon... (Yes, I'm that cheap.)

title: Excellent for 26650 batteries
text:
I love these things. I use them for my custom ecigarette mod boxes, and these springs work great for 26650 battery contacts. They are perfect for snapping right on to bare circuit board, which I use for the battery end supports in my mods. On the back of these, not shown in the pictures, there is a solder ring which "almost" fits 24 gauge solid copper wire. By very carefully prying on the solder ring with a small microscrewdriver, I can spread the ring just enough to allow the 24 gauge to slide right in. Buy some extra springs though if you need to modify them like this, as the solder tab will break off if pried too hard.

I get ZERO voltage drop through my circuit when using these, so they're fantastic for unregulated mods. For 18650's, get the AAA springs instead, as they are narrower.

title: VG review by an e-Juice DIYer
text:
I purchased this product because I am an e-Juice DIYer. For individuals who comparison shop, you won't find a better deal on this product in this quantity on any other site.

This product arrived promptly and works perfect for my e-juices. My only complaint for this item is that when I received it the label was dirty and you could tell it had been sitting on a warehouse shelf somewhere.

For complete e-juice novices or people who are interested about learning more about it, please continue reading below.

32 oz (1 quart) is a perfect starting quantity for DIYers. There are about 30 mls in 1 oz and precisely 946 mls in 32 ozs. This item is typically purchased in conjunction with propylene glycol and nicotine concentrate to form a base for e-juices. PG is available on Amazon whereas nicotine concentrate is not. Within this base, VG typically constitutes anywhere from 20% to 100%. VG is a much more viscous liquid than PG and the purpose of VG is to produce vapor whereas the purpose of PG is to produce 'throat hit.' Some people are allergic to PG while almost everyone is not allergic to VG.

title: Sustainable is a total lie
text:
Please use vegetable glycerine... There is no sustainable palm oil, it is a lie. Globally, 193 critically endangered, threatened and vulnerable species are threatened by palm oil production.

Palm oil is used in all sorts of everyday products from shampoo to chocolate, but it’s been disastrous for the world’s forests. Here are five not-so-fun facts about ‘certified sustainable’ palm oil, which is often anything but.

1. Palm oil is cheap – and we’re using way too much of it
Palm oil is a vegetable oil – like sunflower or olive oil. It’s made from the fruit of oil palm trees – Elaeis guineensis – which come from West Africa but were taken to Southeast Asia in the 1960s. Palm oil can be produced sustainably – but a lot of it isn’t.

Palm oil is great for big food and cosmetics companies, because it’s cheap and versatile. It’s used in many of the things we use or eat every day: shampoo, bread, toothpaste, detergent and even snacks and chocolate bars.
Not only do roughly half of the processed goods in the supermarket contain palm oil, but millions of tonnes of palm oil are going into the tanks of people’s cars. More than 50% of palm oil coming into Europe (but not the UK) is for biofuel.

2. Palm oil is a major cause of forest destruction
The palm oil industry has been a disaster for the world’s forests, wildlife and climate. Palm oil is mostly grown in Indonesia and Malaysia, two tropical countries with large areas of rainforest home to tigers, orangutans and other species that are found nowhere else on earth.

Palm oil companies have been destroying these rainforests because they want more land to grow oil palm trees.
Around 24 million hectares of rainforest were destroyed in Indonesia between 1990 and 2015, according to official figures from the Indonesian government. That’s an area the size of the UK. Palm oil and paper companies are the main causes of this destruction.

3. Palm oil is devastating the world’s wildlife
Destroying forests and replacing them with palm oil plantations wipes out critical habitat for animals that have nowhere else to go. Half of the Bornean orangutan population has been wiped out in just 16 years.
More than three-quarters of Indonesia’s Tesso Nilo national park, home to tigers, orangutans and elephants, has been converted into illegal palm oil plantations.

4. ‘Certified sustainable’ palm oil is a con
In 2004, the palm oil industry set up the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil (RSPO). RSPO members have their palm oil ‘certified sustainable’ and brands using this palm oil get to claim that their palm oil is ‘sustainable’.
Most supermarkets in the UK and many consumer brands like Nestlé and Mondelez use RSPO palm oil in their products.

The RSPO took 14 years to ban its members from destroying forests – which it finally did in November 2018. It still hasn’t enforced this new rule – and RSPO members are still destroying forests and getting away with it.
RSPO members were right at the centre of Indonesia’s 2015 forest fires crisis. This year, the fires returned – and roughly three-quarters of the fires linked to palm oil companies were on RSPO members’ land. This means that so-called ‘sustainable’ palm oil growers are – in some cases – at the forefront of Indonesia’s environmental crisis.

5. Brands have broken their promise to end deforestation for palm oil
Back in 2010, some of the world’s biggest brands promised to protect forests and clean up the palm oil industry by 2020. That’s less than two months away – and companies are miles away from ending deforestation for palm oil.
Many still don’t even know where their palm oil comes from. In fact, there’s no way for brands to tell how much forest is being destroyed to supply them with cheap palm oil.

Brands have broken their promise to clean up the palm oil industry. To save Indonesia’s rainforests brands have to use less palm oil – and any palm oil they do use must come from suppliers that are 100% deforestation-free.

title: E-Liquid usage WARNING
text:
As an experienced vaping industrialist/enthusiast, I'm always vigilant for economical, yet superior methods and resources to produce an optimal experience.
I gave Essential Depot's Vegetable Glycerin an opportunity to prove its practical applications to that in our community. Although it be economic, it is very misleading with its "USP-Kosher-Food Grade" claim and left me questioning their latest manufacturing standards, any quality control protocols and marketing strategies in practice.

My experience using this liquid was very uncomfortable; resulting with nausea, a numbed-mouth sensation, and "foggy" mentality after a few "draws" from quality testing my initial trial batch.
The only deviation from my formula and chemical synthesis was substituting this vegetable glycerin to which I would normally utilize.
This naturally lead me to believe the allowed tolerance of arsenic, chlorides, sulphates, etc. have increased or some form of contamination occurred during the manufacturing process.

Although this may be favorable for other applications other than vaping, I COULD NOT RECOMMEND this vegetable glycerin for DIY electronic liquid manufacturing. I ask that Essential Depot update the Certificate of Analysis / Spec Sheet for this product (last certified 2012) and suggest you proceed with EXTREME CAUTION should you disregard this warning.

title: This stuff changed my life for the better! If you have ichthyosis, try this!
text:
I was diagnosed with ichthyosis vulgaris by Dr. Amy Paller in March of 2017.

I've tried all kinds of lotions and body washes. My least favorite was Amlactin. I hated the ammonia smell. I used to use Eucerin Skin Calming body wash, but that really didn't make a huge difference (and cost a lot more than regular soap).

In August of 2019, I read in the ichthyosis subreddit that some people mix glycerin with lotion. I tried this for the first time on August 15, 2019, and for me, it has made a huge difference.

I use 16oz jars of Cetaphil and quarts of this glycerin. I mix it with a lotion-to-glycerin ratio of 2 to 1, so in a typical 16oz Cetaphil jar, I mix 320 grams of lotion with 160 grams of glycerin. I use an OXO Good Grips 11-lb food scale (also on Amazon for around $40 US) but you can use whatever scale you like. I use a plastic fork to mix it up, which helps to get all the lumps, and put it in a Ziploc bag for storage.

I shower daily, usually in the evenings, using regular Irish Spring (which used to dry my skin out in the winter) and 75g Loofah Bath Sponges (a 4-pack, again from Amazon, for around $13 US).

I rarely use more than 15 grams of lotion on my face, neck, arms, torso, and legs, and use even less in the summer. I'm very happy to say I've been flake-and-scale free for over a year, and I hope this information helps someone.

title: Awesome!
text:
Glycerin is a well known moisturizer and used in most personal care and beauty products. If you search for some scholastic papers, it has healing properties too, while other moisturizers do not.

I brought one bottle last year but didn't figure out how to use it - how to get enough on the skin without breaking the bank. I was on the wrong track of trying to make body/face wash or body lotion. Then I realized the best and simplest way is to dilute and then spray with a fine "atomizer" on dry skin. I must have came across that many times but since they always add something to it like rose water, I wonder what they were trying to achieve. And that I wasn't comfortable leaving some chemicals on my skin, until I know it has healing properties.

For this product, I use 1 part glycerin to 9 part filtered water. It is by volume, teaspoons or buckets. You can apply like cologne or spray with a fine mist. After drying you will feel that your palm is slightly coated with a smooth, comfortable but not sticky layer. The exact concentration doesn't matter that much as the drying process is self adjusting. I bet this level of concentration beats the content in even the most moisturizing body wash or shampoo.

You can use up to 2 part glycerin to 8 part purified water without feeling sticky, but the presence of glycerin on the skin will be felt.

My hands wouldn't heal easily. I have to wear gloves when doing house work. But even washing hands after going to the bathroom will interrupt the healing. Nothing OTC can really stop the deterioration, until I have to go to the doctors for prescription steroid. I use Dove for body wash and Vaseline for body lotion. That won't stop the next cycle of outbreak - steroid.

Then I discovered corn huskers lotion. It worked miracles. It's $2 a bottle. But I am fed up to go to the only store that stock it. It was so simply that I made my own. Replace 4 part of water above with vodka (standard 40%) ! That is 1 part glycerin, 4 part vodka and 5 part of purified water. I think the alcohol in corn huskers lotion did the job. You can use 70% rubbing alcohol for first-aid but vodka is obviously food grade so I can handle anything without drying my hands completely first or wash them. Also, some people add vodka to make beauty products, so I'm not worried. You can vary the concentration to see if it works faster.

Other than my hands, I also have an occasionally outbreak that made my whole body extremely itchy. I have to see the doctor urgently and receive shots. Because it's the whole body or the whole legs, he can't give me potent steroids so I have a few days of can't do anything because of the itch, using the useless creams that he gave me. Dermatologists are only interested in plastic surgery so he wasn't keen on finding the cause of my problems. I think it's dryness on a small part of the limbs that caused it. For years I was afraid to go swimming, and banned myself from the hot tub. Dove body wash and the like won't work. I have to top it up with body lotion. If I was lazy a little bit, some minor skin problems will come up somewhere.

Now I just spray (1:9 glycerin) after bath after towel dry. It's almost free compared to lotions. But the effortless application is priceless.

There's more. I have dry feet. At the heel some dry skin peeled off but remained attached. I cannot grind it off with beauty stones. Lotions make it feel better but the dead skin are still there. But after just a few days of spraying glycerin, the problem vaporized. My feet were smoother than I can remember.

I sprayed my hair after towel dry too.

Nowadays I look for glycerin in shampoo and body wash. The ingredients are listed in the order of concentration I think. I look for pure soap made from vegetable oil and preferably olive, as they were for the royals. The difference is the amount of glycerin in it. The liquid form is made of potassium salt suitable for shampoo and body wash. The solid soap bar is made of sodium salt. But they are selling like gold, approaching $20 for a quad and $10 for a bar. Even if I use them, I still need to spray glycerin from time to time, or if just to feel soft, smooth and good. I may also find cheaper ones with less glycerin because I have plenty.

Just don't apply neat. High enough concentration can absorb moisture from your skin. Also, be sensible reading things from the Internet like this. My brain almost blew up. One person conjectured that if the atmosphere is dry enough, the glycerin will lost moisture to the air, and get moisture from your skin instead. Other than that it is totally wishful thinking, if that make any sense products containing glycerin would have carried a warning label - don't go to California after application.

title: Comparison to vintage 1389 tube/etc
text:
-This tube is identical to the tube on my circa 1996 1389 Backpacker...except...my Backpacker tube does not have the 1" (or so) opening for the hammer pin. The front breech screw location/theads/etc are exactly the same.

-The plastic piston, pump linkage, pivot/handle/clevis pins are exactly the same parts.

-The barrel band is not tall enough for use with my Backpacker breech (the swing-out type loader with the bung for the pellet) and holds the muzzle end of the barrel pointing downward...well over 1/8" drop from breech end of barell to muzzle end (14" barrel).

-The pump cup is slightly different on this newer model. My Backpacker pump cup has a small dimple in the center that "seats" into the intake port of the valve. This new pump cup does not have the dimple.

-The valve is aluminum of course, my Backpacker being brass. Of note about this new valve from AllianceHobby...this is the US version, it does not have the relief hole in the back end of the valve.
That said, web resources will tell you the difference between vintage and current valves. ie: no dimple on pump cup works well, I hope, with the 1/32" taken off the tip of this current-production valve-cone.

-Yes, the hammer assembly is included. However, I may attempt to continue using the rear-cocker system from my Backpacker, which fits the tube perfectly.

-Thank you AllianceHobby for having this available.
Value of money and moisture

title: DO NOT VAPE THIS!  Get your VG elsewhere if you plan to consume it.
text:
Something is dangerously off with this brand of VG; I normally get my VG only from my favorite e-cig vendor, in large orders with other things, but a few months ago I just wanted to order only VG and get it fast without paying for shipping, so I came to find some VG I could get with my Amazon Prime membership, and this is the one I ended up ordering.

Big mistake. HUGE mistake. I've been vaping my own juice mixes for about 2 years, and a year ago I switched to 100% VG-based juice, using only VG from either one of two trusted online vendors (I don't want to say which ones because I don't want this to look like an insidious form of advertising). I'm a creature of habit and have been cycling the same recipes, same concentrated flavorings, same concentrated nic solution, same hardware (Aspire Triton and Triton II); the only thing that changed in the last few months is using this VG.

I am very sick right now. I have constant breathlessness, lightheadedness, chest heaviness, pounding heart sensation, soul-crushing fatigue. It's not a problem with nicotine since I've been doing 3mg for almost a year and lately have gone through a few 0%. For a while I did not even suspect it was my e-juice because my husband picked up a nasty respiratory infection from someone at his job, so I thought I had caught it from him, but that was weeks ago and our symptoms aren't remotely similar.

I do notice that when I vape this VG more (I have a bad habit of chain vaping when studying, something that rolled over from my smoking days, but these sessions didn't use to wipe me out and make me think about calling for an ambulance). A few days ago when I started getting suspicious about this VG and made some 50/50 PG/VG juices to see if something changed -- and yes, it did change. Diluting this VG with PG made me thirstier but I could breathe a little easier. Unfortunately I can't just go to 100% PG because 100% PG is the reason I switched to 100% VG in the first place.

Something is suspect about this VG. I don't know if it has to do with manufacture methods that meet Kosher requirements, or if this simply is not 100% VG as claimed (actually, we KNOW this is not 100% VG because this is something that you just don't see on the market at all, the highest quality USP grade VG is still about 99.7% pure - there will always be at least a tiny bit of water in it - HOWEVER, a truly safe-for-consumption high grade VG will NEVER claim 100% purity, you will see 99.7% somewhere on a label or lab result), or if it's contaminated, or bad batch, or whatever, I don't know.

All I know is-lesson learned-do not buy cheap VG from anyone claiming it is 100% if you plan to inhale it. Get it from an e-juice vendor since that is the surest way to get proper VG for putting in your lungs because if something's wrong with a vendor's VG, the online vaping communities will get the news out to protect each other in no time at all and the vendor will suffer serious financial losses very quickly.

Using it to make soaps and lotions and whatnot: I'm sure this particular VG is just fine for making all that other stuff. That's why I gave it three stars although I feel that is being too generous since the 100% claim is a lie (so I wonder what else is a lie...).

But DO NOT VAPE THIS VG.

title: Excellent!  Cleared up dry and flakey skin!
text:
I have very dry, flakey skin and as I get older it seems to get drier. I have used all the expensive creams and lotions (Chanel, Dior, Prevage, etc.). However, I got the best results from this glycerin. Yes, it is sticky, but I mix it with distilled water (1/3 glycerin and 2/3 H20). I put it in a spritzing bottle and it makes a great face spray. In two days the flakes on my forehead disappeared and I had a bit of a glow. This may not seem like a big deal, but given my skin and travel schedule it is!

I thought it was maybe a short term effect though so I kept using it. The true test was when I went on a long international flight. Usually, I'm so dehydrated that I'm itchy. On this flight I put my 'spritz' in small bottle and carried it on with me. After a ten hour flight, I was dewy and my skin didn't feel tight at all. In fact, it was velvety smooth. The only thing I used was this and water. In the past, I have used Evian in a spray bottle and that made no difference. Therefore, it had to be the glycerin.

Since this experiment worked so well, I used it to make my own foundation. I swear it works just as well as Chanel's Vita Lumiere. I just used the same formulae for the spritz (in 1 part glycerin to 2 parts water). Then I mixed that with mineral foundation (I used E.L.F with great results and it was cheap!). The ratio I used for that was 1/3 foundation and 2/3 of the mixing medium of glycerin + H20. I sponge it on and it works great. Also, you might want to put some stainless steel ball bearings in the bottle that you use to help with the mixing.

title: Where has this product been all my life?
text:
Ok, I have owned this little guy for a little over a week now and cant comment on its longevity, but... it certainly seems to work well. I am a pack a day smoker and like clockwork I catch any cold my significant other gets within a day or two. She came down with something last week when I bought this plug in unit and she is now finally starting to get over her cold or whatever. I have yet to get sick! I am sure there could be other reasons for this but let me assure you that a robust immune system is not one of them! :)

Some people complain about these units.. saying there is low airflow through them. I'll let you in on a little secret.. it takes some time in contact with light to kill germs in the air. If the air moved too fast the germs would not have enough contact time with the light to die. Put the unit in an area where the air moves around it. Perhaps near a door or in a room with a ceiling fan that normally runs. If you put it in the corner of a room with dead air.. its going to purify the heck out of that corner.. :)

I placed the unit on a kill-a-watt meter tonight and it registered a constant draw of 9 watts. Thats pretty great as far as air purifiers are concerned. I have electronics that draw more than that when they are off. Costco has them 2 for $67 and Lowes has them for $39 ea (then you find one of the MANY coupons for Lowes like $10 off a $25 purchase.. exc).

The technology behind the units is a little questionable and I was not able to find links to the documented evidence of their effectiveness. They claim Harvard did test this product.. hope thats true but I would like to see the source of that claim posted somewhere. UV-C bulbs have been around for a long time, but for some reason they are just now showing up in this kind of a product with no real description as to why that is.

The bulbs only last one year and I cant find replacements locally (yet) so minus one star for that.. otherwise.. good job. Hope its for real. I went back to Lowes today to get another one and they were sold out.

UPDATE: Year and a half later, first bulb replacement (should have been done at the one year mark.. I guess). I took the opportunity to use a duster can and blow out all the dust that had built up in the units over 18 months of continuous use. Wiped down the outsides with Windex. Back in business.

Each daily pillbox has 4 compartments to cover all times of the day (Morn, Noon, Eve, Bed)
Individual days compartments open separately to avoid spilling

The quality of the pill box is not all that great and it's a little "random". The pill boxes don't all open in the same direction. Sunday, Tuesday and Friday all open on the left side while Monday, Tuesday, Friday and Saturday all open on the right side. Each days tray is held in the box by a little piece of plastic that sticks out on both sides. Some days pop out too easily while other require a bit of force. This has created small plastic shavings and tiny chips in the plastic box container.

I would suggest people find a better pill container that's better quality even though it is difficult to find pill boxes that have four different containers for each time of the day.

title: Kid Friendly Thermometer....see why
text:
I have several thermometers in my possession. I have the traditional stick thermometer and even one that takes temperature by ear. The stick thermometer is too hard and uncomfortable. The one by ear has been a life saver as its accurate and not uncomfortable like the stick thermometer. However, it's a little big to carry around in a purse or diaper bag. So, when I saw this one I jumped at the opportunity to give it a try.

This digital thermometer is pretty darn cool. There are several things that I like about it. First, i like that its a flexible tip. This makes it especially easy to use under the tongue, under the arm and helpful for a rectal reading on a baby. I have two young kids (4 yr old and 10 month old) so any way that I can provide comfort to them while they're sick and under duress is a win for me. In addition, it provides a pretty fast readout that gets displayed on a large LCD screen. Took about 10-15 seconds for the reading. This is a plus when your child is already irritable.

When I first opened the package, I was pleasantly surprised that it came with its own protective case and included the protective sleeves so that no germs are transferred between family members. Also, the thermometer is waterproof so it can be easily washed. And when it is no longer in use, it will shut off automatically.

I really enjoyed this thermometer and will get great use out of it for years.

I received this product at a discount in exchange for an honest and unbiased review.

title: Life changing!!!
text:
My oldest child has been horribly motion sick in cars since he was 6 months old. Nothing we did helped. If he was in the car for more than 10 minutes, he'd lose it. When he turned 2, we started him on Dramamine. The Dramamine has worked for years, but it's not exactly convenient. It takes an hour to kick in for him before he can get in the car, or he'll throw it up. And he needs it every 3.5-4 hours, instead of the usual 4-6 hours, so he hits his daily limit faster than normal. And they are DISGUSTING, so it can be a battle to even get him to take them.

He's now 9 and that's been our routine for 7 years. I saw these things and figured they were worth a shot since we've tried everything else.

Today we took a 1.5 hour drive to a nearby lake for a day in the sun. He put these glasses on (along with a pair of Seabands on his wrists) and we hit the road. By the 30 minute mark, I became cautiously optimistic. By the hour mark, I became hopeful. And when we pulled into the park, I was in shock. He hasn't made a trip like that without puking unmedicated since he was 6 months old!!

For the trip home, I feared it was a fluke. I spent the first half hour expecting his usual "uhoh, I need to throw up" followed by instantaneous vomit. But no, he was drifting in and out of consciousness due to exhaustion from swimming for hours. At the hour mark, I got excited. He was awake at that point and calmly staring out the window. And when we rolled into the garage, I could have cried with joy. 3 hours of driving within 12 hours, completely unmedicated, and not even a funny tummy.

I don't honestly know if it was the Seabands, these glasses, or a combination of the two, but I know I'll be buying more sets so there is a "kit" in every vehicle.

This changes how we live our lives. We can be spontaneous and just go places. I don't need alarms to remind me to give him his next dose. I don't need to worry about forgetting to buy more when he's running low. And he doesn't need to stomach those nasty pills anymore.

We are planning an 8 hour drive to Disney World this winter and I was incredibly worried about how it was going to work with him. Plus the rides! Now I'll just put a band on these glasses so they don't fly off and he can wear them on the rides that could cause him to get sick. The relief I feel is unbelievable.

TRY THESE!! I know they don't work for everyone, but for our family, they are a blessing.

I will say, my ONE criticism is that they come in that case that is pictured, but they are shoved in there so tightly that the frames are bent at a wonky angle and can pinch the nose a bit. They are more concave then straight. I've been trying to bend them back and the kid says he can do the same when they start to feel pinchy and it helps for awhile, but I do wish it wasn't an issue because these things are a godsend. This issue isn't bad enough to stop me from buying more though!!

title: Very detailed water analysis
text:
I was looking for a test that did more than the typical dipstick which provides a yes/no answer to whether a contaminant is present. Being a toxicologist, I understand that dose is of utmost importance (meaning, it is not just about whether a contaminant is present, but at what concentration, that determines health impacts). This company offers various kits, and I chose the 'ultimate', which tests just about every conceivable parameter. The instructions are simple; fill some bottles with water and return in the included package. It took about 2 days for my sample to make it to the testing facility, and 16 days until I received my results by email (the company keeps you abreast of progress with texts in the interim). The analysis was thorough and detailed, and provided levels in the mg/L (or appropriate unit, depending on substance). For a person with little background in reading these types of analyses, the results may seem a bit overwhelming initially, but they are also color coded to rapidly grasp any areas of concern (green means your water is ok, yellow if a compound is present but not at dangerous levels, red if contaminants are present outside of safe levels, etc). The cost of this product is hefty, but it provided precisely what I was looking for, and I like knowing exactly what I (and my kids) am drinking.
Note: I was not paid for this review, nor am I affiliated with the company in any way. I am just a person who is passionate about water quality.

title: Helping with my allergy!
text: I've had this lying around unused for 5 or more years.  I bought it because I'm immune-compromised and had chemo and worried about germs while traveling.  I ended up not using it much but recently, with COVID-19, decided to plug it into our family room, the room we go through and are in the most.  I have had allergies and over the past 10 or so years have had to blow my nose frequently even when I'm inside.  I have no way of knowing whether this device will help against the virus, but, to my surprise and delight, I realized recently that I have hardly ever had a runny hose anymore when I'm in the family room.  It has really helped relieve the inconvenience of my allergy.  The noise is very white -- just a steady sound of air blowing, and it's not at all obtrusive.  We'll see how long it lasts before a bulb or something else wears out, but for now I'm delighted.

title: Most comfortable mask ever!
text: My husband and I have about eight or nine of these masks each.  This is so far the only mask that does not fog my glasses, does not touch your mouth or nostrils, so you can talk and breathe freely.  It never slides down over your nose (like many mask do).  It’s quite comfortable, stays in place, and there are three ways to wear it, which is unique from most mask.  It comes with its own filter, but I also added an additional filter.  Although the directions suggest hand washing, I have washed ours numerous times in the washer on Delicate cycle, cold water, inside a lingerie bag.  After, I lay them on a towel to air dry (I wouldn’t take a chance putting them in the dryer), and they have maintained their shape.  If you don’t have a lingerie bag, any mesh bag or inside a pillow case.  Of course hand washing is always an option.  I first saw several Hollywood stars and professional athletes wearing these mask last year (2020), read all the positive reviews, and found them on Henry website, and I purchased several from Nordstrom.  Very happy that Amazon now has them too, because each site has different styles and I ordered two more from Amazon.  We probably have 10 or 15 other basic style mask that we will never wear again, because we love our Henry Mask!

title: Love these! Good-bye clogged drains!
text:
Love these! Not as pretty as the more decorative sink/tub strainers, but much, much better at keeping hair and debris from going down the drain while still allowing water through. Since dropping these into the shower/tub drains, we've stopped having those constant hair drain-clogging problems that we'd been regularly dealing with. The mesh is fine and traps everything. Easy to clean by tapping upside down on the edge of a waste basket or wiping out with a bit of tissue.
Before these, I had purchased some stainless steel strainers with very small round holes for our bathroom sinks (from Amazon) only to find that their design created a kind of surface tension that caused the sink to drain so slowly that the sink filled with water, even when there was no debris or hair in the strainer. That was a waste.
So I like these mesh strainers much better! Their mesh design doesn't seem to create surface tension--they drain water almost as it they weren't there! Even with hair in them, they drain well! They have a deeper center where debris collects, still leaving lots of mesh surface around the sides and top for the water to pass freely through. I have one in the kitchen sink, too!

So, I can use it for both my dad and myself. It was super easy to set up. Turn it on, set the time and date, pick a user and press start. It comes with the case, an instruction booklet and card, two sets of batteries, a USB cord and the monitor.

The blood pressure cuff is perfect size for both of us. It monitors the heart rate. It also comes with a little card that tells you the proper way to take a blood pressure, which none of the ones I've had before ever included. For instance, I didn't know that whether you've eaten or not could affect your blood pressure.

The instructions are very thorough! Sometimes you buy a product and the instructions assume you already know how to use the product. This instruction booklet tells you how to use the monitor, where to use it, how to read the blood pressure, how to care for the monitor, along with all the specifications of the monitor (25 pages).

I rated this monitor 5 stars! I would highly recommend it to others. Accurate, easy to use and great instructions!

title: Cleans Engine Bay Pretty Good, Low Oder Smell.
text:
{ WARNING }
Clean your car's engine with caution. ALWAYS cover major parts like the Alternator, Mass Flow Sensor (connected to air intake), Distributor (if your car has one) and Air Intake (if easily exposed to water, can cause damage to engine as air is sucked into the engine and water in the engine will bring bad results). You can use Plastic bags to cover these parts.

{ REVIEW }
I'm sure everyone like myself pop up the hood in our cars and then say "Wow, that's pretty dirty in there, doesn't look like it when I 1st bought my car anymore". I spent a good amount of time looking at YouTube videos on how to Engine Clean. There are a few choice in terms of products, such as GUNK Engine Degreaser, B33, Purple, etc. Many of those product have good results but leaves a pretty strong chemical type of a smell.

I read the reviews that stated this is one of the best at removing those heavy grease, dirt and is also safe. I purchase the 1 Gallon bottle and also went to Home Depot and purchase a Spray bottle for $1.78. I mix it to 4:1 ration (4 parts water to 1 part solution) by following the guidelines on the side of the spray bottle. What surprise me is that this Grand Slam Engine Degreaser doesn't have a strong smell and has a soapy like feeling to it.

First I cover up the Alternator (some people don't, but I do), then I cover up the Mass Air Flow Sensor. All with plastic bags. Make sure your car's engine is cool and not hot. I don't pre-wash the engine, I just spray the engine with the solution and make sure NOT to spray the belts. I then use a brush (you can buy at the dollar store) and start scrubbing away. This helps the solution do it's job. After a few minutes, I use a regular Garden Hose to hose it off, then I use a LEAF BLOWER to dry the Engine bay out. You can use a towel, I just happen to have a Leaf Blower to make it faster.

Once it is all dried out. It's time to give the engine the new car look. I don't like those super shinny spray. I like a nice clean smooth spray that doesn't leave those crazy shine. I use Meguiar's G4016 Supreme Shine Protectant [[ASIN:B001O7LX6S Meguiar's G4016 Supreme Shine Protectant - 16 oz.]]. This give it a new car look without the crazy oily shine.

{ CONCLUSION }
This Grand Slam Engine Degreaser does it's job at cleaning the Engine bay very well. Now if your car's engine is super dirty with heavy oil build-up, you might have to do this process multiple times. I prefer this Grand Slam Engine Degreaser because of the low oder, so it doesn't leave any oder behind when you are done washing it away. Others on the market does. I still have plenty left for maybe 10-15 cars of cleaning.

title: Sugar Free Energy!
text:
Usually when I see “sugar free”, I move right on to the next one, and it doesn’t really matter what we are talking about. Going against better judgement, I decided to give this one (Glytch Gaming Energy Supplement) a try, and I am sure glad that I did.
Despite being sugar free, Glytch actually has a good flavor to it. The label says it tastes like “Rainbow Magic”, though I’m not sure what magic tastes like, so I will say that it has a berry flavor that is not overpowering and is actually really easy to get down, unlike many energy supplements.
Within 20 minutes of drinking a single serving, I feel a noticeable increase in energy and motivation . It makes me feel ready to do whatever it is that I have planned, either gaming, going to the gym, or going on a run. It is a physical as well as mental effect which makes it really easy to focus completely on whatever it is that I am doing and even makes me feel excited to be doing it. This energy supplement by Glytch really does work.

title: Expensive For a Creatine Product
text:
I was always under the belief that creative monohydrate was the best and most effective creatine available, in fact, until this supplement, I had not ever seen other forms of creatine. I figured I’d give it a try to see if I noticed a difference.
The first thing I noticed was how well this mixes. I mixed it with about 12 oz water and it fully dissolved within 20 or so seconds. The flavor, “Lions Blood”, actually tastes good and was easy to drink.
After about 3 weeks of usage, I decided that I could not determine any noticeable difference between this and plain creatine monohydrate.
My one complaint here is the price. Creatine is generally inexpensive, however, this is just under $40 for a 60 day supply, which is simply too much.

title: Basic Creatine
text:
This product is exactly as advertised, regular old creatine monohydrate. This is unflavored, as plain creatine is, so in terms of flavor, it is exactly what one would expect. I have been stirring it into a cup of iced tea, which has worked perfectly.
This creatine does mix well, though I will stir it a few times as I drink it to make sure it is fully dissolved. Stirring 3-4 times for 15-20 seconds each time will completely dissolve 2 scoops into 1 glass of the drink of your choice.
After a month of use, I can tell a difference in my lifts as well. Definitely a slight increase in the amount of weight that I am lifting across the board on all lifts.
This is a great value for the money. Creatine actually works, and this jar has 60 servings, for less than $15, that is a really good deal!

title: Strong Stim Preworkout!
text:
One of my New Years resolutions this year is to get in better shape, which I am sure is the same for many people. As a result, I have been searching for supplements to help me make the most of my workouts, to help me get results.
In this time, I have tried several different pre workout drinks and can tell a huge difference in effectiveness, with some helping me to have incredible workouts while others essentially did nothing for me.
This pre workout works well. When you take
2 scoops, as recommended for the “strong” dose, it can even be a bit too much, especially if you are not used to strong preworkouts.
If you are caffeine sensitive, this is NOT the drink for you. This pre workout is high in caffeine and not for caffeine sensitive people.
Aside from a high dose of caffeine, this pre workout has a pretty good ingredient profile, including the staple of any pre workout drink, creatine.
The “Berry” flavor is pretty good, not great, as it has a bit of a chemical aftertaste.
Overall, this is strong pre workout drink.

With this priced much lower than other 300ml duffusers and since it functions as well, if not better (even full I get more mist than with one of the other brands), it's well worth you while to save the few dollars and buy this one. As the article says, it's definitely the leader in the "the thing tastes like the thing" category. This is definitely like real shrimp soup that you would get in the local area. I have never been to Penang but I have traveled China.

I love hot foods but I found this to be almost a little too hot for me to enjoy. It creeps up on you. I use half the packet of chili paste and a bit more water.

The price tag is a bit high. The local Asian market (which is actually mostly Korean) doesn't stock this. I was willing to pay a bit more just for the convenience of trying it from Amazon. However, I would not buy it again unless I can find it for $1/pack or less.

Overall, it's an interesting experience. If you like ramen, noodles, or soup, check it out.

title: I am astonished at my Pruvin  results
text:
To begin, I believe in science, not hype. I've finished my second week. I've tried not to change anything about my life (food, activity). My diet is ok, nothing special, I don't "work out". I cannot explain why I have lost 6#s, and BP has dropped from upper 120s to upper teens since starting Pruvin two weeks ago. When I was in my 20s and 30s I was active in tennis, running, weight lifting. Weight was so stable at 185 I didn't own a scale.
I quit smoking and gained 30 lbs. I instantly went on a starvation Slim Fast diet, and lost 10 lbs. So 205 w/HBP(140+/-,90+/-) and "middle age gut" for 20 years. In 2012 I retired, and weight came down another 10 lbs to 195. Still HBP, but borderline high. I was not able to get below 195# for 20 yrs after quitting smoking until 2 days ago using Pruvin. Since starting Pruvin, I've eaten potato chips, Triscuits, some TV dinners, lots of apples, oranges, bananas, broccoli, and Greek yogurt. Just the kind of stuff I normally eat. My BP this morning was 114/72 P75. It was 125/89 P92 when I started Pruvin. (I'm still using the Rx diuretic started in the '90s). What I am reporting here is totally 100% anecdotal, no claims about Pruvin; just statistics for you to decide.
Pruvin's taste needs improvement. I add only 3oz of water, stir for 2 minutes to get most of the CO2 out, take a good breath, and breathe out while swallowing. . Because it's mildly acidic, I swish around and swallow some alkaline Essentia water (Amazon) to neutralize the acid. Baking Soda works for that, too (don't swallow). So the taste part is over in about 2 minutes.
Since starting proven I've lost 6 lbs in 2 weeks, my BP has dropped enough that I could stop my BP Rx today, but I will wait on that until I drop 4 more lbs to finally reach the weight I was way back in my mid-20s.

title: Good Mask for dust, dirt, & allergens
text:
I work at a farm stand that I've spent the winter & spring renovating. It's an open air stand with a huge road construction project taking place out front. I've spent the last several months sawing, sanding, & refinishing displays which has produced an enormous amount of dust & dirt - plus there is the constant dirt being shifted around by the construction crew. As an asthmatic, either of those is bad news. These masks have helped keep my asthma in check for all that plus has helped my allergies a ton!

These are comfortable for all-day wear and fit my face well. They're so-so when it comes to my glasses fogging up but most dust-type masks are. I bought some anti-fog clothes which do the trick.

These are currently $15.99 for 20 masks which is a bit on the pricey side. I reuse them for several days but at $0.80 a mask, it's a bit outside a farm worker's budget hence the 4 stars. Otherwise, I definitely recommend them.

title: Covered in sugar
text:
Overall, these aren't bad but every single gummy is covered in sugar. I'm sure there have to be ways to keep them from sticking together without sugar. I've tried many other gummy vitamins & supplements and these are the only ones that are sugar-coated. The flavor is technically strawberry but the sugar makes it mostly sugar-flavored.

If you have small kids that might find your vitamins, hide these very well. They are literally gummy bears coated in sugar, in appearance and taste. I know adults who've made themselves sick by eating too many gummy vitamins - but a kid is going to think these are actual candy if they see them.

As of this writing, they are no longer available for purchase, which is probably a good thing. No one needs more sugar in their life so I wouldn't buy these no matter how inexpensive they were.

title: You really should consider this
text:
This review is about the Kent soft bristle toothbrushes
I'm in my seventies, age-wise. As time passes I have less real teeth and gums that "get angry" more often. I have used salted water, electric toothbrushes, flosses, mouthwash varieties, "manual" toothbrushes of all kinds and bristles, toothpastes aplenty, and other devices and ways to soothe and clean my mouth. I'm not unique in trying to find relief, just stating that my experiences qualify me to recommend these Kent toothbrushes.
I bought a Kent comb a few years back and was pleased with it, so I bought another (different size and style) and was pleased by it, too. My two Kent experiences made me believe the Kent name indicates products to seriously consider. I was browsing Amazon when up popped Kent toothbrushes. I bought two.
The "mouth feel" of the toothbrushes is good, soft but substantial. The bristles feel like they clean well and they do (things which were between or adhering to teeth and gums show up when rinsing & spitting). The brush handles are solid and easy to hold (I have carpal tunnel syndrome, ulnar nerve damage, and arthritis).
Not meaning to insult anyone, I want to add that brushing teeth and gums isn't all I do for mouth care, so I don't expect toothbrushes to be the end-all and be-all. For brushing teeth and gum stimulation these are the best I've ever used.
I'll be buying more of these toothbrushes as I need them and I urge other people to try them.

title: Works exactly like it should
text:
I really needed one of these. I've been using a regular shaped hot water bottle on my neck and shoulders and it just doesn't sit right or cover the area that aches. I also have one of those neck pillows you can stick in the microwave to warm, but they don't stay hot for very long, so they're a waste of time.

This U-shaped hot water bottle does exactly what it's supposed to do. Just fill it about two thirds of the way with hot (not boiling!) water—I heat my water to 175°F or 185°F and that is definitely hot enough. Then carefully squeeze out excess air before closing the bottle. You will probably want to have a layer of fabric between the bottle and your skin until it has cooled down, then you can place it directly on the skin. The bottle doesn't have any smell, which is good.

text:
I’ve wrestled with whether to give the product 4 or 5 stars and here’s why: it cleaned almost all surfaces I tried it on exceptionally well! This alone would not have bothered me enough to take a whole star away, but one of the spray bottles stopped working after first use. There was appeal in purchasing a two pack as I was planning to keep one bottle on the first floor and one on the second for convenient and quick clean up. I’m also pregnant with small children so I prefer not to have to run up and down the stairs every time I want to clean something up. So, for those two things, I removed a star.

Having said all that, this is my new favorite all-purpose cleaner and I love the fact that I don’t have to rinse countertops or toys with water after use. The smell is a bit different, and I agree with other reviewers that it’s reminiscent of orange or some sort of citrus, but I don’t find it to be unpleasant and it doesn’t linger once the cleaned surface is dry (unlike Clorox wipes or vinegar for example).

All in all, love the product and will continue to purchase.

title: I love this thing
text:
I love this thing.

I have terrible insomnia. Sometimes I can't sleep without complete silence. I live in the city and there's so much outside noise. And my housemates have a completely different sleeping schedule than me. I tolerated it for a few years before I was so sleepy all the time that I couldn't take it anymore. That's when I found this. I first saw it in a counseling center at my school. I didn't know what it was because I thought most white noise machines were tracks being played. But this is better. I slept with a fan on my nightstand in the summer and I found out that this drowns out the noise. So I use this in the other months when it's too cold to use a fan. It has helped me sleep soundly. It blocks out enough noise that if someone were to call me from outside, I wouldn't hear a thing. I can't hear cars passing by or people talking on the street. I can't hear things through the walls. I have this thing on the floor right near my head. I think the placement matters.

The only bad thing about this thing is that the motor is making noises now. It used to smell the first few times I used it too. It was this plastic smell as the machine heated from overnight use. It disappeared after a week and the machine doesn't get nearly as hot anymore. I'm a bit disappointed that the motor is kind of dying but I think it has to do with dust. For my next one, I'm going to be careful with the dusty on the floor. I tried to open my current one up but I haven't been able to unsnapped certain parts to get the hood to pop off. I've had mine for almost two years now. I see that some people have had theirs for much longer. I guess the quality has diminished or there was a bad batch. But it's so essential to my sound sleep that I just don't care about paying $40ish every two years.

If you're debating whether or not to buy it, go for it. But be aware that it literally sounds like a fan without the wind. If you can't stand that type of white noise, then don't get it. I find it soothing.

I was new to the process of tube feeding my dog and was horrified by the single-use tubes - considering that I needed 12 a day! It's true that some of the food gets stuck under the tip, but it's not a problem. I bought enough for a days' feeding and I put them in the dishwasher each night and am confident they are sterilized. When re-inserting the plunger, I find it helps to wiggle the plunger at a few different angles to get it in - rather than trying to plunge straight in - and then it glides in easily. You can also try running medium-hot water in the capsule to soften it before inserting the plunger. You can refer to my short video to see how I do it.  Best of luck. Tube feeding my dog was a steep learning curve, but it was so worth it. She is doing so much better now and starting to eat on her own again. I no longer have to fight with her to take her pills - I just crush them and put them through the tube, and if she doesn't want to eat a meal, no big deal, I feed her myself through the tube. She has learned to ask for meals by standing by the Breville Boss (after trying NutriBullet and every competing product, the Breville is truly the best).  I call her tube (or "snorkel) the "nutrition line" which has taken all of the stress out of getting her the nutrition she needs to stay healthy and happy and I will hopefully have her for many more years to come!!  Good luck!!

title: YUM! Taste like a healthy version of Starburst Candy!
text:
I drink the Mother's Milk Tea and vouch that (when I take a moment to make a cup of tea) it does help my milk supply. I found myself needing more tea (and making a cup of tea isn't always the easiest) and stumbled upon these chews. The reviews were all over the place. Some people loved them while some people could not swallow it down. But I wasn't too worried over that. No what worried me was that the reviews noted the taste to be like a combination of licorice and lemon.
I can not stand licorice (the black traditional yuckiness -WHY is that even made into candy??). Ever since I was little I would rather go without candy than eat licorice candy. To me, the black jelly bean is pretty close to being near sacrilege.

So now that you know my background of despising licorice...you can see why I was so worried to try these but the ease of a chew made a compelling case for me to at least try it.
I took a breath and ordered it.
It arrived today and as I ripped open the package- I stared at the contents contemplating if I had wasted money.
I took another breath and ate one.
Immediately a pleasant lemon flavor. Upon chewing is, yes I can sense the licorice flavor undertones (but the lemon flavor was always there). For one who despises licorice- this chew was utterly delightful and tasty.
On a fun note, It's square shape, wrapper and chew consistency reminded me of healthy version of a Starburst candy.

If you want to try these, one thing that might be helpful is if you first try the tea. The tea has a distinct flavor and I wonder if it was advantageous that my taste buds knew what they were in for.

title: I've always slept better during storms and it's nice to be able to hear one anytime I'd like...
text:
I like this sound machine but it doesn't have as many sounds to choose from as others I've used in the past. For the price, I feel it should have more than 8 choices. The 8 choices it offers are White Noise, Rain, Bird, Brook, Lullaby 1, Lullaby 2, Ocean and Thunderstorm. I like the choices, but since 2 of them are lullabies, that means only 6 are what I would call white noises. The thunderstorm choice is my favorite, followed by the rain. I've always slept better during storms and it's nice to be able to hear one anytime I'd like. The ocean is also very pleasant and it does remind me of a day at the beach and I also like the brook, but have to admit that it makes me have to go to the bathroom more often. (Just a heads up lol) I'm not sure I could sleep to the birds, I associate birds more with waking up I guess, but I do like the sound. As far as the lullabies go, they are nice but they are not my cup of tea, although I can see how they might be a good choice for an infant. The sounds are all very clear and it's easy to tell what they are supposed to be, and the volume can be turned up much louder than I expected. It actually gets quite loud. If this was priced a little lower, I would have easily given it 5 stars, but for the price they are asking, I just don't think it competes since it has too few choices compared to others in that price range.

title: Best and easiest Linux distro to use
text:
I started my journey with Linux when my old Core i3 Windows 7 laptop started freezing when I went on the internet. I didn't matter which browser I used. So, instead of going to the friendly local neighborhood office supply store that begins with an S or and O and paying $150 to fix it, I decided to install Linux Mint 16 32-bit. I explored other distros such as Ubuntu 15.04 32-bit, but when Google decided not to support the Chrome browser for all 32-bit Linux distros, I got another disc from a competitor to LinuxDiscOnline, which was 64-bit Ubuntu 15.10. The problem with this install was that even though it could recognize my Hotspot, it could not recognize my Wifi router. Since this was a total deal kill, I purposely searched another vendor and found that this particular product had one 5-star review, and I decided to purchase it.

My install experience, since I had already installed 3 different Linux distros, was a breeze. After updating successfully from the Update Manager, I immediately installed the Google Chrome browser for 64-bit Debian, then installed Dropbox. All of this was done within one hour from inserting the CD into the laptop. All of my settings and add-ins in Chrome automatically were installed. Now I have an all around computer to use at home to browse the internet and check up on my email. Thank you, LinuxDiscOnline!!

title: Great little unit with many different uses
text: Years ago, my husband suffered a back injury at work. He was unable to perform his regular job and spent years on L&I. It was obvious that this was a life changing injury and that his back would never be the same. He saw several different doctors, underwent many different treatments, took tons of medication, endured tons of different tests and even attended a pain management clinic. Throughout this lengthy process, He was given a medical grade tens unit. It was the most effective tool he had to combat the pain. My husband went thru vocational training, attended the local community college and got himself a CDA and became a long haul truck driver rather than live on disability for the remainder of his life. Because he decided to better himself and not live on a government disability check, once his L&I case was closed, he had to return the tens unit. Of course a medical grade tens unit is ridiculously expensive and we simply cannot afford one. He has tried a few different cheap ones, but none has really done the job he's needed from it. I came across this one while browsing one day and figured it couldn't hurt to try given the fact it wasn't too costly. While it definitely doesn't work like the medical grade one, this little guy actually does a fairly decent job. Given that my husband is using this to relieve back pain and it helps, anyone looking to use this as a massager or fat burner should be extremely pleased. The unit requires two AAA batteries to work which are not included. Included with the unit a single cord that splits into four pieces, four pads that attach to the end off the cords and stick onto the body and an instruction manual. One simply plugs the cord into the unit, attaches the pads to the cord, place the pads where on the body they want massaged, pain relief or fat burner and then turn it on. It is much simpler than it looks. The unit has several different levels of intensity depending on what you are using the unit for and what your tolerance to the eletrical currents. Overall, this is a fantastic little unit that works great and has many different uses.

title: Love this stuff.  Use half-doses.
text:
I've bought this stuff probably ten times now. They used to have it at the health food store around the corner in San Francisco, but we've moved and now I have to get it online. I don't take it every day because the amount some of the minerals and vitamins is so high I'm worried about toxicity, but I do like it first thing in the morning.

If you take 5 hour energy, what you've got there is basically a B vitamin and a bit of caffeine. This has just as much B vitamin in it (and I only take one scoop instead of the recommended 2), and with a half a cup of coffee, you've got the same effect, but you also have a lot of other vitamins, minerals, and some protein. And it's less expensive and tastes better.

Tip: On the label, it says you can mix it with milk or juice. DO NOT mix it with juice. It's horrible. If you don't drink milk, I've used almond milk and soy milk with comparable results. Also, put the liquid in your shaker cup before you put the powder in or you will be scraping green putty out of the bottom corners.

You can control what SPF is in your products by following recipes found online. You can use it on skin wounds and it aids in healing. I know when I worked as a nurse, I would see Zinc oxide as an ingredient in creams/ointments and unna boot wraps. There is Zinc oxide in many more products than most realize.

In researching the benefits and uses of Zinc oxide powder, I learned Zinc oxide can be used on energy saving and as a heat protectant on windows! Hello lower electric bill in the summer! Applying a coating to Windows helps keep heat inside rooms, let's visible light in and reflects infrared radiation.

Can be used as a skin astringent. Zinc can act as a skin drying agent, help relieve inflammation/irritation/reduce rashes. Likewise, it can be used for dandruff, dry/itchy scalp (intact is in many commercial brands of anti-dandrruff products). Likewise, Zinc is in many kinds of make up also. It just has a wide array of uses!

With all that being said, and I know I'm leaving a LOT of other things that could be mentioned, I am over all satisfied with this Zinc oxide bulk package from Plant Guru, but would be nice to include some instructions, as not everyone will know to research how to use this.

title: Bye-bye scaly ugly feet.
text:
As I age the body is doing surprising things. While I've always had callouses on my feet since I am barefoot as often as I can, they were supple and caused no troubles. Now they are hard, cracking and look like I took a cheese grater to the sides. The ones on my large toes come out at the side making my toe look huge and those callouses on the balls of my feet hurt even at rest.Trying to keep these under control using lotions, pumice stones, foot baths, etc., was not working. The Ped Egg worked somewhat, but was scary in that you don't want to dig too deep and even when you're done with the metal part you have to use something to sand what's left smooth.

I bought the battery operated device like this one locally at a drug store, and it worked, but would bog down and ran through batteries. Okay for smaller callouses on my feet it would have cost a small fortune. So I ordered this one here and wow! what a difference. I had to use it twice to get a good result, I used it initially and then let my foot skin rest a day then applied it again. My feet feel good and all pain from the callouses is gone. Device didn't bog down once since it's corded and using it only took about 5-7 minutes for each foot.

The only thing I wish I had done was buy the extra coarse stones since that may have cut the time down the first time. Will recommend this product to others.

title: Great idea, but body fat % is wildly unreliable and FitBit email support appears mediocre
text:
Syncing, setup, and lbs seem to be great. Really, I wouldn't change what it does or how it does it. I just used the Android app to set it up. It was a pretty slick way to do a setup! The scale also looks good and, though the display is simple, it does its job well.
I was so excited to see my own data so gracefully charted that I got fitbit flex bands for my wife and myself. The synergy between the products is mediocre currently, but they are neat separately that I'm not concerned by it. I'd love if it told me how the measures of weight, fat, sleep, and activity relate to one another!

The fat% readings are horribly unreliable. I should mention that I'm 6 ft tall and 175 lbs--as a guess, I'm 15-20% body fat.
On the Aria, I go between 15% and 38% (5 readings of one then 7 of the other...it's not an occasional inaccuracy--these are across multiple days and times of day).

Fitbit support was only able to tell me to switch to "lean" mode (which would be inappropriate for me, I'm pretty physically average).

I think I will return and replace through Amazon and hope that I just got a bummer.
