title: Making a huge difference in my life
text:
This review is for the blue cloud tri-core pillow. I am an average-sized woman with a largish head and shortish neck, which I mention in case that helps someone else choose a pillow size.

I was always a stomach-sleeper, which was so cozy and comfortable for me for 38 years, but I believe it contributed to my current neck problems. A few months ago, I began to have debilitating pain in my neck that made it impossible to even turn my head. I saw an orthopedist, who told me that my neck vertebrae were on the verge of rupture. She recommended a cylindrical neck pillow from a big box and beyond store, so I bought one.

I found it really impossible to sleep on that cylindrical thing. First of all, it rolled out from under my neck a hundred times a night. And it made me snore -- the angle of my head caused my mouth to fall open while I was sleeping, so I would wake with a sore throat. Also, staying on my back was the only option; if I tried to roll to my side, it caused intense pain. I went back to sleeping on my regular pillow, but on my side. (I can no longer sleep on my stomach, which vexes me.) My neck pain was still horrible every morning when I awoke.

I saw this pretty cloud pillow online and hoped it would be the answer to my prayers. So far, it is! I've had it for a couple of weeks, and by the third day, I was used to sleeping on it, and my neck pain is absent for the first time in months. I start out sleeping on my back, but rolling onto my right side or left side no longer causes problems because the pillow is firm enough to support side-sleeping. I have also stopped waking up with a sore throat, so I think this pillow isn't causing me to snore even when I have to be on my back.

title: DO NOT BUY!
text: I have not ever given a product such a warning before.  I bought these (not from Amazon)and even got the bonus because it sounded like the best idea for those of us who sew and are past our 40's (and we know what that means).  Well The first one to use it was my son (in his 20's-great eyesight)to replace a button on his shirt, and boy did it ruin the shirt by snagging the threads of the material.  I thought he just wasn't doing it right because after all he's not a person who sews.  My other son tried to sew something onto his jeans, and it snagged those too!  Still not believing these 'amateurs' and not wanting to believe this product was a dud, today I took my youngest son's suitcoat and tried to sew on a button that popped off.  Threading was great!  Stitching was HORRIBLE!  It snagged the suit material and it took me two minutes of finagling the needle not to destroy the jacket where it was pulling the material thread.  Even then I thought maybe it's a certain way to hold it or pull it through faster.  No such deal.  It snagged again and this time pulled the thread out of the suit. Thankfully it was behind the button.  I had to work the gather out of the material without exposing the pulled thread. The section of the needle that you 'slip' the thread on making it easy to thread the needle also is too sharp to go through material cleanly, but acts like a second needle and pulls on the material.  The needle is also not very sharp and leaves holes when you push it through.  I feel sorry for someone who uses this on a more expensive piece of material.  I definitely wasted my money, but maybe not yours.

title: Stopped working and drains batteries in a week
text:
I purchased an Aria scale a few years ago (Nov 2013). It worked fine for several years, only had to replace the batteries once or twice in that entire time period. In the last few weeks I replaced the batteries 3 times, and started to wonder what was going on.

I can see now there are a ton of other negative reviews on this product, and everyone is saying the same thing. The device is defective. At some point, it will start malfunctioning and the sensor that detects whether or not someone has stepped onto it will fail. This will cause a few things:

* Throughout the day, it'll ask you to Step On and it'll loop between Step On and Thinking randomly all day, burning through the batteries
* It will have issues registering when you Step Off of the device, and go into a Step Off/Thinking loop
* It will use up a fresh set of AA batteries due to the above two issues within a week

I contacted customer support for Fitbit, and they had me walk through normal troubleshooting. But after we exhausted the normal stuff (remove batteries to reset, reset with a paper clip, etc) they asked me about replacement. Because the device was out of the 1 year warranty, they basically told me I was out of luck and my option was to purchase a completely new scale at that point.

This is a manufacturing defect, and should be treated as such. I know there is only a 1 year warranty on these (and many other) electronic devices, but the usual thing is that most devices work for years and years, and the warranties are there to fix things that are out of the ordinary that fail in the warranty period.

Forcing customers to buy a new scale every 2 to 3 years is a ridiculous obsolescence policy. I would not recommend anyone purchase Fitbit merchandise as they seem to have systemic quality issues and poor customer support. Buyer beware.

text: I bought the Tropical Mojito flavor and let me tell you it’s delicious! One of my favorite cocktails of all time is a mojito and this tastes as described, like a mojito with tropical fruit. This is top 2 best flavors I have ever had and I have tried MANY products. Now, let’s move on to performance and feel. I can actually tell this product helps with pumps, I definitely feel and look more vascular, I’m sure it would be way better/more amplified if I was leaner. I also believe that this product is a quality product because it doesn’t taste at all processed like some of your cheaper powders may taste and I actually still feel good when I take this. If you have tried many products, you know some make you ultra dehydrated, make you feel sick, headache etc but this product does not make me fill that way at all or jittery. This product does not have any creatine in it as well, or any that I could find. This is a huge plus for me because let’s just say if I didn’t want to take creatine, this product would be off limits. I would much rather have my preworkout creatine free and have the option for me to add creatine as needed separately. I also think creatine can contribute to the above effects. Beware of the amount of caffeine in this product though! It has 360mgs per scoop which is a lot for just one scoop. For reference, a lot of products have 100-130mgs of caffeine per scoop. So I just take a half scoop of this and the taste is not at all watered down and it’s the perfect amount to give me great energy without feeling over amped and limits the effects of any big crash later in the day. Lastly, the price is RIGHT where it needs to be. If it was any more expensive I probably wouldn’t buy,if it was cheaper it would be of tremendous value. All in all, this is a great product and I do believe you are getting exactly what you pay for. And once again, the flavor is unbelievable. I look forward to trying other flavors.

title: Caution: Burns hand easily
text: I ventured off of my MIracomb replacement curling brush, that I absolutely love, when I got caught up in this one with the disappearing bristles. This Sylkia brush does not have enough bristles to keep your hand & fingers from touching the hot barrel when guiding your hair around the brush.  Maybe with thick ,long hair this would not be a problem but for me and my medium length hair it was a disaster with no way to guide my hair onto the short and far apart bristles without getting burned.  There was not enough bristles to create holding power.  I could also see, right away out of the box, that this could tangle your hair. The bristles are short , far apart with little nubs at the end.  I could see how hair could wrap around and get caught getting pulled into the barrel when you retract the bristles.  This did not happen to me but only that I could see the potential there.  To retract the bristles you push a lever and have to hold it there.  The lever does not lock to keep bristles in thus allowing for a smooth barrel styling if you would choose.  This was a bit hard and awkward for me to do with arthritic fingers.  I managed it but could see days it would be tougher to do.  Big kudos to the maker for the thought in the On and Off switch and heat level buttons. They are inset so you won't be accidentally turning the wand off.  That was well noticed by me.  Swivel cord worked  nice... not real thick and is pliable. Length of cord is ok but could be longer for some people.

title: The best set for the price, with another completely satisfied customer!
text:
I belong to a Fasciablasting group on Facebook, and I saw someone post this as a recommended item along with the Face Blaster, a healthy diet, drinking plenty of water, clean eating, etc. I do all of those other things so I thought I would give this a try. I was optimistic in the idea but skeptical that it would work so quickly and be so easy to use! I did a LOT of comparison shopping before deciding on these: let me tell you what I found.

First of all, you get four cups with this set: two identical larger cups and two identical smaller cups. The idea is to use the same size cups simultaneously over symmetrical areas of the face. I haven't found myself to be that coordinated yet, but here's what I do: my main concern/area of need was between my eyes on my forehead. I've heard people refer to this as the 11s - the two lines you get in between your eyebrows from squinting. Well, I've been an avid squinter all my life. I live in Florida, the Sunshine State, so there's that aspect, and then my close-up vision has gotten bad so I squint to read small print up close. This has taken a toll on my forehead. I find that I can apply [[ASIN:B00FZPTL7S Trader Joe's Vitamin Oil E, 4 Ounce]] after the shower and then use one of the larger cups between my eyebrows, moving it gently up and across both sides of my forehead, kind of making a circular triangle, if you will.

I kid you not - I did this two nights in a row, then took a day off, then did it another night ... maybe I've done it every other night for about 10 days now. I went for a run today and got out of the shower and I can't believe how smooth my forehead looks! These silicone cups are fantastic! The directions are really easy to follow, and this set is truly the best price-point out there. You want the clear silicone so you can make sure you're not capturing a wrinkle and/or giving yourself a hickie. You want to be able to see increased blood flow to the area and I'm not sure how you can gauge that when using a pink or purple-tinted cup.

The soft scrubber is great for facewashing or even just facial massage. I honestly have no complaints with this set at all. As a first-time user, I'm thrilled. The company reached out after purchase just to make sure I was happy with the product. Shipping was quick and Prime. Packaging was great. If you're considering facial cupping, this is the way to go. It blows my mind that there are sets out there that cost upward of $60 - I'm not sure what those would do that this doesn't, other than you're paying for that company to advertise. Look here - no advertising, a great company with great customer service providing a great product at a great price. What's not to love? :-)

title: Do not buy this watch and do not get it from Maxi-Aids they don't stand behind the product
text:
This review is as much about the seller Maxi-Aids as the watch, It's hard to review something when it only works a few days. What I want to impress on you, the next possible buyer of a talking watch is that most of these watches are not going to be of high quality so what you need to be sure of is that the seller will stand behind the product when it possibly quits working in a few months or less.

I bought this Reizen watch for my dad who turned 85 on Christmas. I previously bought my dad a talking watch and he loved it and wanted a different one as a back up, his vision is very bad and he has really come to depend on it for the time. I thought I would try this watch out since it gives not just the time but the date with one button (much less confusing then the multi button alternatives). The watch has sat on a shelf since Christmas and only been used twice, this third time the voice was garbled and only spoke about 10% of the message, it does this if you touch the watch anywhere.... not just the trigger button.
Maxi-Aids refuses to issue a refund and only offers to repair it... Their excuse is that it has passed the 30 day refund period, it's been between 45 - 50 days. I have no confidence in a watch that only worked for 2 days, repaired or not, and I will never support a seller who hides behind policy rather then stand behind it's products and it's customers best interest.

As a result of Maxi-Aids's non functioning watch I bought an Avalon XXL Series Low Vision 1- Button Talking Watch from: Watchvalues, to replace this one that doesn't work, it's the second one I bought from them, the first was almost 2 years ago and still works, good loud voice quality, the hands are a bit loose and don't always keep the time but my dad can't really see that anyway.
The main reason I bought another is while the watch is alright... It's the seller that makes the watch great. When the first one I bought quit working after a few months, I called Watchvalues they immediatly gave me a refund and sent me a replacement for FREE... thats a seller I want to buy from, I want to have confidence that if what I buy turns out to be junk the seller will be there for me and not themselves.

title: Mediocre
text:
As far as disposable liners go, I have tried many and these are not my favorite.

Here's why:

-thick and rough like an industrial paper towel. I wouldn't flush these, even though they claim to be flushable, because I wouldn't flush a paper towel.

-wet feel. These absorb a small amount of moisture, so unlike the more porous bamboo and viscose liners that stay completely dry, I suspect having this in a diaper may be like putting a wet paper towel in there and probably feels wet. Some kids may not mind.

-leaves debris on baby. They pill quickly.

-can't reuse. Ok, I'll admit that I reuse a liner a few times if several diapers in a row are wet. A poopy liner, no, that goes into the trash. These get wet, cold, and clammy, so you really are just using one per diaper change.

But they have some good points:

-pop up dispenser. No tearing one off a roll while the baby squirms away.

-perfect size for fitting in a diaper. I wish all liners were these dimensions.

If someone gives you a partially used box, great. Take it and use it, but if you have to buy these, look around for a different product.

title: These bluetooth hearing aids were very disappointing.  Buy the lower priced Earrck instead.
text:
This is NOT as good as the lower-priced non-bluetooth Earrck set, and here is why:

•1. On my cell phone, although my voice was crystal clear to the caller, each caller was distorted through the hearing aid.

•2. It had no noise-cancellation. Callers could hear TV in the background no matter how my head was rotated.

•3. Amplification of distant origin was not good nearly as good as up close. I had to keep the TV volume much higher, but with the less expensive Earrck I could have the TV at half the volume.

•4. It completely blocked my voice. I could not hear myself speak.

Further, the added controls on the cell phone did not prove valuable, you cannot answer the cell phone by any button on the hearing aid, and there's no button for last number redial. Further yet, caller ID was not announced, and the cell ringing through the earpieces was louder than the caller's voice.

title: So far I like it just fine!
text:
(Updated after using the product for three weeks.)

First off, I should mention that just about all flavors of toothpaste (e.g., mint or cinnamon) have always made my mouth "burn". There are very few brands / flavors that I find at all comfortable to use.

I had been using this company's toothpaste for years and really liked it till they added the nano silver. (They simultaneously made the wintergreen stronger, leaving lemon as the only flavor that didn't hurt my mouth.) After reading up on nano silver, I decided that since it's a fairly new additive and is now being added to quite a variety of products, I'd rather wait and see whether "they" find that it causes problems down the line. So I switched to the powder.

The jar is surprisingly small (compared to how it looks on my laptop), only 2-1/4 " in diameter -- but that means it fits very nicely in my medicine cabinet. Besides, it's sold by net weight, not by the size of the jar! At the three-week mark, I've used nearly half the jar, so I estimate it'll last 6 to 8 weeks.

I like spearmint flavor in moderation, and several reviews said this product has a mild flavor, so that's what I ordered. I wasn't sure I'd like it unsweetened, but it's nice -- like chewing on a mint leaf (rather than mint chewing gum). It does burn just a little, but far less than the vast majority of toothpastes. I may try the citrus flavor next, or could try mixing the two.

One review said that dipping a wet toothbrush into the powder was fine at first, but eventually made the powder get all clumpy. Also, I found that dipping my wet brush into the jar picks up more powder than necessary, so I give my toothbrush a shake after wetting it, before dipping it, and I put a tiny bit of water in my mouth. With the right water-to-powder ratio, it's pretty much like brushing with paste.

Another review mentioned needing to brush again with just water after rinsing, in order to get all the powder off their teeth. I suspect that they were using it like scouring powder, rather than using enough water to make a soft paste. Just a regular rinse works fine for me.

I've been using the powder for three weeks now, and so far I like it just fine -- though I still wish they hadn't added the nano silver to the paste, which I find a bit easier to use. On the other hand, the jar is recyclable and the tube isn't. And I should easily be able to get every last bit of powder out of the jar.

title: Extra insulation + extra padding = year-round comfort
text:
I bought one pair of these insoles over a year ago, and liked them so much that I recently bought a package of two more pairs. In winter they do a good job of insulating my feet from cold floors and cold ground. They're comfortable in summer too -- they don't make my feet too warm, and they provide an extra layer of resilient padding that's very comfortable to walk on. They're also durable -- I've been wearing the first pair in my tennis shoes for over a year, winter and summer, and they're still nice and cushiony.

Of course they do take up a bit of room inside the shoes. I removed the gel insoles that I had been wearing in my tennis shoes and replaced them with these when the weather got cold fall before last -- and they've been there ever since. They provide enough extra padding that I don't miss the gels -- and my feet don't get sweaty like they did with the gels. I had to get a new pair of my long-time favorite Haflinger Grizzly wool clogs, one size larger, because there wasn't quite enough room for the extra insoles in my old ones. The new combination is so comfortable and cozy that I may be loathe to revert to my old pair (sans insoles) in the spring!

Considering the fact that human beings are outnumbered by something like 200 million to one (a very rough estimate I read somewhere) and many of those critters love to feast on our blood as well as carrying dangerous infections, we need something to fight back. UPDATE, It's now October and the amplifiers are still working well. Have ordered more Banglijian Wax Guards from Amazon and also memory foam tips for the devices. One of the pluses to using these Amplifiers during the Pandemic is they don't fall off when you are wearing a mask, the over the ear Amplifiers do. UPDATE. January 4, 2023. title: It's really worth ZERO stars!!
text:
If I could have given 0 (zero) stars I would have. I played around with this piece of junk for almost 2 hours trying to do a chignon. When you put your hair into the clip, as you pull it down to the ends of your hair, it turns and flips on you so you are fighting to keep the miniscule teeth of the clip on your hair the entire time. IF (and that's a big IF), you finally get it into position so you can roll it back down towards your head, as you start rolling, your hair starts sticking out of the clip and by the time you are down and ready to twist it closed, you have very little hair in the chignon and most of it sticking out (assuming you did not get it tangled in your hair).

I tried wetting my hair, applying a light gel, everything to keep my hair together, but nothing worked. I wear my hair bone-straight, same length all around (even cut, like a bob), thick and falls about 4 inches below my shoulders. I even tried sliding it down to the end, but leaving about 3 inches of hair beyond the clip, and tat still didn't work, the clip still did not roll the hair down properly. These were my personal experiences with the clip, other issues I had with the product:

1) Instructions are ONLY written in Kanji (Chinese) letters. The least the product vendor can do it slip in an English (or even Spanish) translation when selling the product to US purchasers. I should not have to have my laptop running the video while I am trying to do my hair.

2) The clip really is made of a cheap, flimsy plastic, so it has absolutely no ability to stay straight on the hair and not bend/flip. If you have thick hair, avoid it, since you will have trouble getting in position to even start the roll down.

Overall, the clips (I ordered two of them) went back very quickly to Amazon (and yes, is there a reason why Amazon ships two flat pieces of plastic in a box designed to hold a book? They could have been shipped in a manila envelope...thereby saving the customer shipping charges). This product has absolutely no quality and considering the pirce paid, iyou would be better off going to a "dollar store" and getting something for 99 cents!

title: Amazing considering the benefits I’m reaping!
text:
[[VIDEOID:4653a56f6da747e835066a1080daad41]] I am a first time mom in my mid 30s. Postpartum hit me hard with depression, anxiety, severe insomnia, and leg cramps that sent me to the hospital at one point. I had been on antipsychotic meds to help with my sleep and anxiety. My baby is now over a year old and I am ready to get off the meds. It is not easy, until my therapist told me about Magnesium Glycinate. Unfortunately I have gagging issues that makes swallowing pills extremely stressful. Most Mg Glycinate came in capsules form. I was thankful to find this product in powder form. Magnesium Glycinate and vitamin B6 are supplements that are not meant to be tasty when taken as food. Yes, it has an off taste but nothing too offensive that I cannot chuck it down in one gulp. I discovered that it dissolved fairly easily in lukewarm water. I tried it in my hot coffee, it took a bit more effort to dissolve the clumps - though i did not need to use anything other than a spoon. I found it more tolerable in coffee when I added cream and sugar, coffee is naturally bitter so it masks off the taste of the supplements.
Benefits: i have been using this supplement religiously for over 2 weeks and felt many obvious effects on my mood, sleep, and the frequency of leg cramps. I have cut down to half my dose of the meds but waking up feeling more rested than ever every morning, I power through the day with a calm and cool demeanor. I am hopeful that i will be able to completely get off the meds in a near future.

title: This Extremely Colorful Set of 12 Silicone Cupcake Liners by V & I Accessories is both Practical and Fun to Bake With!
text:
This Extremely Colorful Set of 12 Silicone Cupcake Liners by V & I Accessories is both Practical and Fun to Bake With!
Not only do they replace the cost of paper liners, the color combinations will delight both children and adults alike.
There are 2 of Each Color Combination in the set, with Each Silicone Cupcake Liner measuring 2 7/8" across the top, 1 7/8" across the bottom and 1 1/2" deep.
For the purpose of my review, I wanted to actually bake something in them so I could post photos, however, all I had on hand was a Brownie mix, so that is what I used.
In fairness to V & I Accessories, unlike cupcakes or muffins, brownies tend to be sticky in consistency by nature.
For this reason I did Not expect the cupcake liners to be clean when I removed the brownies and I proceeded to bake them without greasing the liners before adding the batter.
What I was curious to learn was how baking my brownies in these Silicone Liners would compare to when I have used paper liners in the past and if the taste of my brownies would be affected by the silicone.
I appreciated that I could set the cupcake liners directly on top of a cookie sheet and didn't need to dig out my cupcake pan from the back of the cupboard. They were easy to fill and the brownie batter leveled itself without issue.
I am extremely pleased to report that there was absolutely No Difference in the taste or the amount of time it took to bake them using these adorable Silicone Liners. They baked evenly and tasted delicious!
As I had expected, there was some brownie residue left inside the cupcake liners, but no more so than if I had used paper liners.
For the most part, my brownies came out of the liners unscathed and I was able to proudly share them with my neighbors.
What really surprised me was how easy they were to clean by hand!
I do not own a dishwasher and was especially concerned that it would be next to impossible to completely remove the sticky brownie residue from the tiny grooves inside the liners.
I was delighted to find that I could turn these sturdy, but flexible silicone liners inside out without damaging them and after soaking them in some hot soapy water for a few minutes, they were quickly restored to like new condition.
I will be grocery shopping over the weekend and plan to pick up some cake mixes so I can see how cleanly the cupcakes release from these silicone liners. Should I find that my expectations of them coming out of the liners without sticking is Not met, I will come back and update my review accordingly.
In the meanwhile, I am very pleased I agreed to purchase mine at a reduced cost in exchange for my honest, unbiased opinion and would highly recommend them!

title: A+++ Non Porous Stoneware Bake and Serve Bowls with Spill Guards!!
text:
I love to cook, but as I live alone, I usually don't bake my favorite recipes because the standard sized bake ware I own meant there would be too many leftovers.
Sure I could freeze some, but food never tastes quite the same when reheated, so when I was offered the opportunity to receive these Wholeness Home Bake and Serve Bowls with Spill Guards in exchange for testing and review, I was happy to accept.
These 3.5" w x 2.5" deep Bake Ware Bowls are the perfect size for an Individual Serving of Mac & Cheese, Casserole, Soup, Bread Pudding or anything else you can think of!
The are made of Non Porous Stoneware, which means they won't absorb food odors, flavors or stains.
The feature I love the most is the Silicone Spill Guard!
All too often, the foods I love to bake the most end up dripping down the sides of the bowls an onto the cookie sheet, leaving me with a big mess to clean up.
For testing purposes I decided to treat myself to my Homemade Baked Mac & Cheese.
I removed the bowls from the Attractive, Easy to Gift Wrap Box and Styrofoam Inner Packaging.
As suggested by Uniware in the easy to understand instructions that came in the box, I gave the Bowls, Lids and Spill Guards a quick wash before using them.
Then I par cooked my noodles in a saucepan, mixed them together with my milk, butter and favorite cheeses and filled the Bake and Serve Bowls with Spill Guards in place.
I topped them off by sprinkling some crushed up garlic and butter flavored croutons over the top and set the Lids in place.
Into the oven they went and I sat down to read while I waited for my Mac and Cheese to cook, stomach growing the entire time.
When the stove timer told me it was time to remove them from the oven, I was very pleased to find that my Mac and Cheese had cooked evenly, retained it's moisture and the croutons even had a bit of a crunchy brown texture from the heat generated by the Stoneware Lids.
Best of all, the Spill Guards had protected my cookie sheet from sticky melted cheese drips!
I removed the Spill Guards and was pleased to find that they had performed exactly as described. My Homemade Mac and Cheese looked like it had been prepared in a fine restaurant and it tasted delicious!
Clean up was a breeze with some soapy water, a sponge and a hot water rinse. No scrubbing needed! These Bake and Serve Bowls are also Dishwasher Safe for those who are fortunate enough to own one.
As I could only eat one, I put the other in the refrigerator and warmed it up in the microwave the next day for my lunch. The Stoneware kept the mac & cheese moist and tasting as good as it did the night before.
Uniware shipped quickly and offered excellent follow up to my order. I found them to be a very pleasant company to do business with.
I am extremely satisfied with these Wholeness Home Bake and Serve Bowls and will be purchasing another set come Holiday time to gift to my
sister for her and her daughter.
Well deserving of the A+++ Recommendation I am giving them!!

title: Best Plugs Of The Few I've Tried
text:
These work very well. Just used them at a Zeds Dead show and I can hear fine and no ringing so they did their job. I like that people can't see them in your ear unless they are actually looking into your ear from the side. They are probably the most comfortable plugs I've used so far.

I'll compare them to other similar plugs that I've tried at festivals the past year:

Downbeats vs. Hearos (confident they're made in the same Chinese factory as the Etymotics):

Sound quality - Slight edge to the Hearos. Though, that may be due to the fact that the downbeats have a slightly higher dB reduction so the Hearos are louder. My ears slightly ring after using Hearos at a loud show.
Comfort - Definitely the downbeats. Hearos/Ety can get uncomfortable after a couple hours, but the downbeats don't annoy me.
Style - Definitely the downbeats. Almost invisible, while the Hearos stick out.

Downbeats vs. Dubs:

Sound Quality - Very slight edge to the downbeats. To me, they have almost the exact same quality, but the Dubs reduce the decibels maybe slightly more. If you're sensitive to noise levels the Dubs could be slightly better here.
Comfort - Tie. These are both very comfortable plugs and I've never had a problem wearing them for long periods. Though it always feels kinda good taking them out every couple hours for a break.
Style - Slight edge to the downbeats. They are both pretty discrete, but the dubs are more noticeable from the side.

Overall, great plugs and the best I've tried so far.

title: Does WONDERS for plaque/tartar removal!
text:
I am so happy to FINALLY have the tools I need to get nasty plaque and tartar off of my teeth between visits to the dentist. I have always been disgusted by the plaque buildup that seems to evade even the best dental floss, and eventually turns into tartar. (Plaque is the colorless, soft, sticky film of bacteria that is made of food particles and saliva, and if it is not completely brushed or flossed away each day, it can harden and turn into tartar, which can be very difficult to remove.)

This kit came with 7 individual instruments, three having a different tip on each end. The sharp tips came protected with a clear rubber segment over them, which I'll likely keep so that I can put them back on after each use (for safety's sake). The pieces in this kit include 2 dental picks, an anti-fog mouth mirror, Jacquette scaler, tartar scraper, burnisher, and a sickle scaler. The carrying case is zippered and compact, so it's easy to store in a small space or take with you for travel.

After my first try with these instruments, I was able to remove tartar behind my bottom front teeth that had been bothering me for a while, and it feels so wonderful to have that gone! Do be careful when using these instruments, and don't scrape too much against your teeth. It is possible to damage the enamel and gums, so be gentle and go slowly! I'm VERY happy with this dental kit, and I would recommend it for those who want to keep their teeth extra clean between visits to the dentist.

title: Really works for volume relief, but caused slight pressure in my ears
text:
I bought these earplugs both for use at the occasional concert I attend, and for my daily apartment life with a roommate who always has our TV volume up very loud. These plugs come with a useful metal case that can be attached to a key ring. The ear plugs themselves are a soft silicon material. After reading the directions on how to place these plugs safely and comfortably (you must pull the top of your ear up and outward to straighten out the ear canal for plug insertion), I put them in. I had to adjust them a few times, as they did not feel like they were far enough in. When they were firmly in place, I felt a decent amount of suction pressure, which wasn't very pleasant, but that sensation lessened a little bit after wiggling the plugs around some more. The plugs are not the most comfortable things to have in your ears, so I might suggest wearing them for short-term events, or at least taking breaks from having them in your ears. They began to give me a small headache after having them in for a few minutes, but this could just be because I'm not accustomed to wearing this type of ear plug.

These do help immensely with lowering the volume of sounds around you, while not completely muffling them. While my roommate had his TV show volume waaaaay, way up, I put the plugs in my ears and it made things much more manageable. I was able to hear my roommate speaking to me at a normal volume, and he didn't sound muffled. These ear plugs are definitely superior to foam plugs when needing to wear them out, as they sit securely in place and do not move or feel like they will fall out. I would certainly recommend these for concert-goers or those who live in loud environments, but do be aware that they can cause a sensation of pressure inside of the ear.

title: Really nifty
text:
I’m thoroughly impressed with this little device. Lots of pros: I especially like the waterproof feature. I specifically got it for use in the shower, as using something like this at the sink can leave a mess. And it works really well. Charging is good, the three mode options are practical, and I like that it came with three replacement nozzles. I have a molar who’s filling fell off a few years ago and has left a hole that’s traps food. My toothbrush doesn’t help with removing that effectively. This water pick helps clean it out really well, at least until I can get to the dentist for repair.

There are a couple of cons: The jets are such that the water tank empties too quickly. Not that big of a deal. Just means you have to refill often. It does have a 2 minute timer shutoff (like most electric toothbrushes) but I never reach the 2 minute limit cuz I always have to stop to refill. Again, no biggy. But it is unfortunate that the fun is usually interrupted haha. The only other con is placement of the power button; it’s exactly where my fingers are for holding the device during use, so I accidentally end up turning it off and on at random times during use. Again, no big deal, but relocating this button (and the mode button too) a little lower would make sense.

Overall, I really dig it. It helps a lot. And it reminds me of childhood haha.

Otherwise, the 'fix' is to get some 220 wet-or-dry paper on either a random orbit or a finish belt and (with ONLY LIGHT PRESSURE) put the TOP (don't put the bottom or you'll remove the index tab) onto the sanding surface and remove a very small amount of material - about the time you notice a lot of white dust you'll probably have done enough. I have been a hairstylist for 15 years and tend to be very particular about the tools that I use. That said...I'm extremely impressed with this Curling Wand.

When I received the package; it was very apparent that this was a high-end device .The wand arrived packaged in a high quality box that is durable enough to store the curling wand in for however long i'll have it. I find that to be a valuable feature that most brands don't care about or provide these days. There was a black glove included in the box that protects you from burning your fingers. The glove is quite large for my hand but it still served it's purpose without affecting my ability to curl my daughters hair.

The Curling Wand itself works extremely well! It has a smooth surface and generates an even, intense heat that doesn't increase the longer I have it turned on. I use it mainly to curl my daughters really long, thick hair. She has a difficult time sitting still for long periods of time so I loved that I was able to achieve tight curls even though I was curling large chunks of hair at a time. title: Let us now praise a great musical
text:
What makes a great movie musical? Plot? Well, it can help, but that isn't as important as one with no music at all. The ability to take us to new worlds? By it's nature, yes, as ordinary life doesn't break out into song at the drop of a hat. It can fail, as I think "Moulin Rouge" did, but "Oklahoma" presents the real world as well as any musical can and does succeed.
How about number of memorable musical numbers? Now there's something. The musical "Showboat" is considered one of the greats, and has a moving plot. But aside from "Old Man River", how many memorable songs can you count off from that production?
With all that in mind, I believe that "The Rocky Horror Picture Snow" is one of the great movie musicals of all time, and I've seen quite a few. Of the three criteria above, pure plot may be the weakest, but even there I think there is something. First, it is a comedy, and at times is very funny. But the subtle (and not so subtle) reminders of 1950's science fiction films make it in it's own way a touching tribute.
It succeeds much, much more in taking us to new worlds. I just got done reviewing "Guys and Dolls", a musical as far removed from this as you can get. But that one succeeds partially because it creates an underworld that is real only in our dreams. "Rocky Horror" goes way beyond that, creating something truly unique in the area of cinematic story-telling. There is nothing quite like it.
But the songs. Richard O'Brian evidently hit lightening in a bottle with this one, as shown by the fact that he hasn't really done anything else of note since then. But much better to get all the good stuff in one work than a career of one or two-hit song albums. From the hauntingly beautiful opener "Science Fiction/Double Feature", the soundtrack doesn't have a clunker in it. Yes, it's primarily rock and roll, and "Whatever Happened to Saturday Night?" would have fit right into Meatloaf's "Bat out of Hell" album. But the comedic "Toucha Toucha..." does advance the plot, and "The Time Warp" is as good as any musical production number.
I saw it about thirty times back in college, and was apprehensive about getting it for home viewing. Could the experience be the same? Well, not exactly, but it's well worth getting it for home viewing.

title: It doesn't provide a stable temperature
text:
I bought this thermometer to use on our grandbabies since they are way too wiggly to hold them down for long! It comes with a simple set of instructions on the back of the box, but there are more complete instructions inside the box. One push turns it on, you wait a second and it displays the last temperature taken and then starts flashing, which shows it's ready. I used it under my armpit six times and got different readings each time, ranging from 95.9 to 96.9. Then I tried it under my tongue exactly where the doctor's office always takes it. The first time it read 97.0 degrees. The next three times, it dropped one-tenth of a degree successively. Then the next three stayed consistent. The next one was another one-tenth of a degree lower. Now I don't know whether I can really trust it or not. It took between 9 and 16 seconds to read the temperatures and then started sounding a tone so I knew it was done. Each of these temperatures were low compared to my usual temperature. To test for accuracy, I compared it to a temporal scanner infrared thermometer, which read my temperate exactly the same at 98.3 four times in a row and was within two-tenths of a degree of my usual temperature. I don't believe I can trust this thermometer, especially for our grandbabies since a difference of 2.5 degrees can be serious in a child.

Even though I bought this thermometer on sale, I still expect it to work correctly. I rated it one star because it doesn't provide a stable temperature. I contacted the company, who said they would send me a replacement. One month later I still haven't received it.

text:
So where to begin? Oh yes, I have BAD breath!!! There, I said it and I am not ashamed to say that. The first step is admitting you have a problem, and I am WELL aware of this one!

According to my dentist, my bad breath is not because of "bad" oral hygiene - I have no cavities and brush regularly; instead my bad breath stems from bacteria and "gunk" (dead tongue cells, etc.) that gets stuck to my tongue. So no matter how often I brush or use mouth rinse, my breath still seems to Reek!

Reek no more! I bought a cheap little plastic tongue scraper and it seemed to work (for a bit) until the plastic started to get "funky" so I threw that one out! Then i started looking at more "permanent" devices such as this one. There are a few metal tongue scrapers out there, but this one seemed to be the best value and look the most professional, so I bought it.

It works AWESOME! I have a big tongue, and this bad-boy covers it with one "foul" swoop (Pun Intended) AND when I am done, I can clean it over and over again without it getting funky = AND i don't ever need to throw it away!

I HIGHLY RECCOMMEND THIS TONGUE SCRAPER!!!!

title: Beware of hidden mold
text:
I purchased this brush at WFM and only used it several times before cleaning it and putting it away, forgotten, under the sink.

The bristles weren't stiff enough to wash root vegetables and I found the ring design a bit awkward to use. The narrow design of the bristles also meant a smaller contact space which meant scrubbing something wide like potatoes takes longer. Scrubbing and preparing potatoes already takes a significant amount of time, last thing I need is to double the scrubbing time, lol!

I went back to my plastic Oxo with its short, firm bristles and wide profile that fits nicely in the palm of my hand. (I have no connection to that product.)

I came across this brush again in my gadget tub and pulled it out, hoping I'd like it better this time. I used it occasionally for some lighter scrubbing for a couple weeks. I like to clean my brushes and upon a closer inspection I noticed black mold at the base of the holes where the bristles are anchored into the bamboo. Our climate is very dry here and my Oxo, which was quite a bit older, was fine. I think the wood base verses the plastic base in the Oxo creates an environment for mold growth. I normally try to avoid plastic, but mold as the alternative is a deal breaker.

I have several natural bristle bottle brushes that have never molded so it's not a problem with the bristles, it's a problem with water not being able to air dry properly in the tight spaces where they are anchored into the bamboo. Cleaning vegetables with a moldy brush is not safe, even when the mold isn't obvious. Spores are microscopic and it doesn't take much to contaminate food, your hands, or the air. This is especially important for anyone sensitive to mycotoxins.

title: Warning, smelled like chemical perfumes
text:
The bag I received arrived with a nice carry case, but it had a chemical perfume odor. The kit inside was in a sealed cellophane bag so I wasn't too concerned - I decided to try washing the carry bag to remove the perfume. But when I opened the enema cellophane bag the entire enema kit had yet another type of odor, one that was very fruity and clearly another chemical perfume.

The manufacturer must be attempting to mask the chemical smell of the silicone with perfumed chemicals. This is becoming more and more common with Chinese made items and usually an indication of the use of more toxic chemicals in the production process that need to be masked. High grade silicone should never smell - not of chemicals and not of masking perfumes.

I will return this and look for a silicone bag that is made of silicone graded to EU or US standards for food grade silicone.

Chemical perfumes are among the most toxic chemicals in use today - there is no oversight and none have been tested for toxicity as individual chemicals much less when combined with dozens, sometimes hundreds, of other chemicals, as is the case with the manufacturing of perfumes.

I'm not willing to risk the acid in the coffee leaching whatever chemical perfumes have been added to this bag - not to mention the chemicals in the low grade silicone that required masking with perfume in the first place.

Very disappointed. The other reviews seemed promising. Some even mentioned "no chemical smell". Did they not smell chemicals because they were simply covered up by perfume? And did they not realized that these too are chemicals?

title: Best wax for car or boat
text:
I have used Collinite Paste Fleetwax # 885 for years on my sailboat, and have used on my car too. Gives a good hard coat of wax that last a long time. A single application on my boat in the spring will last the entire boating season. On the car I have used on the entire car give a good shine and water beads up especially in the door wells, helps keep the areas free of dirt and snow. I have also used on the wheel rims where brushes don't reach keeps most of the dirt build up and road junk from building up.

One important Item. When you are waxing an area do not wax an entire side of the car or boat and let it dry to a haze. Which you would do with regular car wax. If you do it's going to take three men and a boy to rub the haze off. Take a one of two foot area at a time to wax and as soon as you cover the area start wiping the wax off. You will get a nice shine and a smooth finish.

title: It WORKS for us but with some TWEAKING!
text:
This stuff works amazing for my seven year old that has a hard time with pill taking. He has a pretty sensitive gag reflex and gets anxiety over thinking about throwing up, etc. Unfortunately the medicine he takes tastes horrible when opened or mixed with food so we really had to get this pill taking thing down pat! This stuff DOES work but there are a few things that should be noted. First, the texture is like a thick, sticky, melted gummy bear. It's hard to get it onto a spoon or in the right place in the mouth for my son because it sticks to everything. I thought it was more jelly like but it is not. For us we put a bit into a spoon and then I spray it with another 'pill glide' liquid substance and mix it so it has more of a fluid texture. I also have done this with a tiny bit of water before I found the pill glide spray and it has worked well too. I have my son hold the spoonful of swallow aid in his mouth and count to 15 and swallow. Then we repeat the process one more time. I then take his pill and cover it with a spoonful of applesauce and he swallows. Most days this does the trick but some days his gag reflex still kicks in although it definitely is not that bad. I definitely think it is worth it but don't be afraid to mix it up to make it work for you!

*****UPDATE******
We followed the exact routine I described above for about three weeks. One day my son asked if he could try to take his pill without the 'gooey stuff'. I am proud to report that he took his pill like a champ with applesauce only! He no longer needs to use this swallow aid. Woo hoo!

title: Sustainability is important -- and this one has it covered.
text: I have tried a lot of different fish oils.  This one is a good one, without the "fish burps" or acidity you catch from some types of fish oil.  One big concern for me recently is sustainability -- if we are screwing up the ecosystem for our fish oils.  A lot of fish oils come from a type of Haddock -- Menhaden - which is frequently called "the most important fish in the sea."  It is the fish that any fish-eating fish loves to eat.  We are driving them to extinction, which will have a domino effect on the larger fish we eat, like tuna.  This company uses sustainable Krill, which is one of the better options. (I am a member of the Monterey Aquarium and sustainability is something they drum into your head!)  I like this one.  I got a discount for reviewing this product, but I bought it and I am using it.  If it were not effective I would not take it.  Happy to answer questions if I can.  I do suggest though that you should add sustainability to your standard on this product -- it is of great importance.

title: NOT AS ADVERTISED
text: Read closely and scroll through because you're not getting what you think you are! I was excited to find a set of gel socks that fit men, as my husband has terribly dry rough feet, and like most men, he doesn't care for his feet like he should.  I love the fabulous soft results I get from my gel socks, and thought these would be the perfect gift for my husband. I was sooooooo disappointed when these were delivered. I thought for sure they had delivered the wrong product. THE GEL PIECE IS SMALL MAYBE 2 AND 1/2 INCHES ROUND AND ONLY IN THE HEEL!!! The amount of the gel used in the heel is small and super thin as well. The gel portion is not even thick enough to cause a measurable amount of thickness to the heel of the sock. I would describe it as more of a thin gel skin. These socks are so thin that the fabric is see through, and that is before being stretched and put on a foot!  The socks are way to small to fit a man comfortably, unless he has very small feet. I wear a ladies 8 1/2, and they would need to stretch to fit my foot, but I believe they would fit comfortably. To add the width and length of a man's foot would make these extremely uncomfortable. If the fabric could withstand the stretch, which I'm not convinced it could, these socks would crumple my husband's toe's and cut off his circulation lol! The fabric quality is what I would expect to find in a dollar store pair of socks, where you would buy them in a pinch, but know they are never going to survive one wash. Gel socks are supposed to be thick luxurious and comfy, for me at least. I want them to make the person wearing them feel like they are being pampered, and receiving a spa like treatment in the comfort of their home. These Gel spa socks just don't make the cut. The picture on the front of the packaging also shows ladies feet, which only adds to my suspicions that thes are designed for women, and not what you would want to try to squish a man's foot in. They are a hard pass.

title: Truth or coincidence?
text: After having this item in my cart and debating for a while, I decided just to go for it.  What was one more posture support?  I really didn’t have too much expectation but hoped for the best anyway. All I can say is...incredible! There is no need for instructions on how to put it on. I took it right out of the box and put it on just like you would a garment..just slip your arms in and pull it together in the front. IMMEDIATELY after securing it in the front, my posture was, what I would consider, in the perfect position. I didn’t want to take it off; however, it does say start with one hour a day for two weeks. The next day, I wore it again, and it felt so weird having my back and shoulders aligned that I kept it on for two hours. Third try, I overwore it and realized  there is a reason why they say wear it one hour a day for a time..my underarms were sore-that could have been aggravated by surgery many years ago- I did not wear it for two days and it felt amazing when I put it back on yesterday.  I have had the worst posture for many years.  It has led to back pain and hip and leg pain.  I cannot believe what an improvement I have had just wearing it a few times. If it is coincidence, then let it be.  I did try to wear it up against my skin, and it is not going to be comfortable doing that in the summertime, but I will not go without it even at this early date. Another plus is that not once did I have to pull up one of my bra straps.  Sorry guys,  I know these are not just for women.  My husband tried it on, at my suggestion, and it just will not fit him at all. I did buy the large size  because I measured between a medium and a large.  I am of average height and 165 pounds and it is a most perfect fit with more room to tighten it if I need to and plenty of room to let it out, but it did not fit his  average height, at almost 200 pounds.  In truth, even though it has only been a few days, I really would like to buy another one just to have for backup! I am very surprised that they offer a lifetime, unlimited refund guarantee on this item. It must be their confidence in the quality.  Sorry to be so long-winded. I Hope I can leave another review in a few weeks time. Thank you for carrying such a quality product Amazon.

title: Sticky zippers and uncomfortable full carry
text: I bought this bag first and foremost for the looks and second for the back and forth toting of my breast pump to work and home. I just wanted one bag, so wanted to use as a purse for the same purpose. I admire the quality and heavy duty material. I also loved how many pockets were available and that it came with a dust bag and additional smaller bag for things that are wet/soiled/etc. However, I am displeased with enough things that I decided to return it and resume my search for the perfect bag. First off, the zippers would constantly get stuck either with the interior beautiful satin blue fabric, or just within its own teeth track. I had to fiddle with it more times than not and was especially careful not to damage the fabric, so sometimes it took awhile to zip/unzip. You shouldn't have to think about this! Another con was that while it indeed fit my Spectra S1, it was a tight enough squeeze that it was a pain to get in and out when I needed to charge it. There was no way I could fit anything else in that side pocket. While the handles were again, nice quality and heavy duty, it just didn't fit comfortable on my shoulder if I had much else on it other than the pump and a few other small things like a wallet, checkbox, etc,. I had to keep my medela bottles and cooler on the top of the inside, which had me needing to zip up the top piece that normally can fold over. This made it almost impossible to keep on my shoulder and it hurt after awhile. Not very efficient to carry while full. I'm 5'9" with a long torso so I can't imagine this working for someone short and stout. To boot, it was heavy. Not sure on the weight, but I suppose that's what you get for buying a bag with a heavier material (normally I wouldn't think this to be good, but not combined with the handle comfort). And last but not least, I agree with another reviewer that for the price of this bag, you shouldn't be finding random strings, etc.! There was a piece of the insulation of the handle sticking off to the side. Not very neat/proper.

title: Not perfect, but so much better than anything else it warrants 5 stars.
text:
Update after 18 months of use:

Still the best callus remover I have ever found. Absolutely 100% recommend. Before purchasing this I had nearly constant foot pain, and nothing I found could adequately deal with my calluses. Since I bought this, my problem has been solved.

The few negative reviews all site the same basic complaint: It is not powerful enough. That is due to the power supply that they chose to include. It has ample power at full speed, but the power drops off as you slow it down, and even slightly below full speed it becomes unusable. To me that is not an issue. I prefer it at full speed anyway, but for others it might be an issue.

They claim the new version addresses the problem. I don't know if that is true or not, but I would still not hesitate to recommend this.

--- Original Review ---
By far the best callous remover I have found. Mechanically, it is very simple and should be reliable. The consumables are dirt cheap and easy to use. And it just works. My feet are in better shape than they have been in in years.

The not quite perfect:

* Having the power switch and speed control on the cord is annoying. It works, but it is a pain to use. Personally,.I only use it at full speed, so it is not a huge deal. The bigger issue is that if the wall wart fails, you just replace it with a standard power supply. Integrating the speed controller into the device would make it far more reliable.
* For most parts of my foot, the design is great, but it would be nice if it had a sort of pistol grip handle to reach the callouses on the bottom of my foot.

Neither of these issues are deal breakers. I've tried the Emjoi and similar callous removers and different manual tools, but this works far better.

text:
I bought these to go with my [[ASIN:B01HJBN4SW Dansko Women's Sam Flat Sandal, Sand Dollar Full Grain, 36 EU/5.5-6 M US]] shoes. I dislike the feeling of the inside of shoes for too long so I was in the market for some weird socks.

If you're not used to wearing 'toe socks' like I am, it'll take an hour or so to get used to the feeling of fabric between your toes, but after that it was fine. I think the toes are an integral part of these staying on your feet, actually. I've purchased regular socks at this size and they just want to come off, so I was perfectly fine with the feeling as long as they stayed on. I also liked the little pad/support bit on the bottom of the foot. I also felt this inside the shoe, but it was a comfort knowing that if my feet sweat, it'd be mostly absorbed by that part. Seemed to have worked too. My shoes felt dry inside and didn't have any gross odors after wearing these (they were new shoes).

I've only hand-washed them so far and they seem to be holding up okay. The probably won't last as long as any normal sock, but these aren't too expensive to just buy more when they do - as long as you're taking care of them as per the directions. I'd expect them to to last at least 3-6 months. If they last longer, that'll just be a bonus. I mean they're not German engineering, c'mon now.

title: Best dental floss ever!
text: Let me say first I did not purchase this product on Amazon, but directly from dentallace.com. First, the dental floss. It's amazing! I have very tight space in between my back molars, but this slides through with just enough resistance to pick up what has got to without hurting my gums. What I found ingenious, and I am not sure if this was done on purpose or if it is the inevitable result of producing silk floss, is that the floss is not completely smooth. I don't mean to say it is rough. The intertwined strands of silk create a larger surface area and thus are much more efficient in removing deposits in between teeth! My mouth feels truly clean and refreshed after flossing!  When I think of the other brands of dental floss out there I wonder how come they are all so smooth! But the main reason for purchasing this is that I am actively trying to get my house rid of plastics. Just by making some small changes, we noticed that our waste has decreased tremendously. I have always been worried about the environment and always tried making the best decisions when purchasing anything, but I must say that companies like Dental Lace have made this process of diminishing waste easier these days. This brings me to the only negative observation I made on this product. All wrappings are biodegradable and seem to be made of post-consumer recycling, but the refills come in a small plastic wrapping. If this is made of recycled plastic, of course it is better than using new plastics, but it would have been better if there were no plastic at all.  Plastic can only be recycled a few times to which point it is not viable to be used any longer, as far as I understand. So, in the end, it goes to the land fill, rivers and oceans. The best is to avoid plastics altogether. This is the only reason why I did not give 5 stars to this product. I do hope Dental Lace will consider an environmentally friendly solution to the use of plastic in this case. Perhaps biodegradable plastic or waxed paper to protect the floss from contamination? I imagine contamination would be the worry here. Thank you for this wonderful product!

title: Does a great job but it is a bit messy
text:
I really wish that I could give this Wellness Oral Care High Powered toothbrush a 4.5 instead of 4 stars. It is a really nice toothbrush and it does a really good job. But, it is the messiest toothbrush I think I have ever used.
First, I will tell you the things I like about it. The brush is very sleek looking. It is powerful and leaves my teeth feeling shiny and polished. It has reduced the old smoking stains on my front teeth by leaps and bounds, without adding any whitening agents. I like that the brush is on a 2 minute timer and gives you a pause after each 30 second interval to let you know to switch areas of your mouth. I like that there is a sensitve teeth function and have found this very helpful since I do have sensitive teeth. The handle is comfortable and almost ergonomic. I love that this set came with multiple heads in different colors for the whole family to use.
Things I don't particularly like. The brush head is a little small for my liking. My fiancee and I have both missed the feeling of our gums being massaged by a larger brush head. I am used to using a battery operated toothbrush and it even has a larger head. With both of us using it, we have to take the heads off in between brushings and there is no resting spot for the heads when not in use. The charging station is nice and small whichis great for my counterspace... but it leaves me with brush heads that can be knocked off the counter, get dirty or not dry properly. I have taken to storing them in a little finger bowl from the kitchen. Lastly, the brush is so messy. Both of use have to hold our chins over the sink because it gets really drippy even if you try to hold your lips tight. The drips run down and get into the grooves on the brush head. When this happens, due to vibration, the moisture bubbles and "spits" from the band where the head twists onto the base. I can't wear my glasses or I get little droplets of toothpaste on them.
Overall, I do feel like this is a high quality toothbrush that does a great job of cleaning. There are a few things I would change about it if I got to redesign it myself, but it is a great value option at this price, especially if you have multiple people using it.
I ordered this product for free or at a discount in exchange for my honest and unbiased review. When I make purchases on Amazon, I depend on the reviews of others so I personally try to leave helpful and informative reviews.

title: I have a really bad ear infection and the past week has been horrible
text:
This little pillow of therapeutic therapy has been a godsend this past week. I have a really bad ear infection and the past week has been horrible. This hot & cold therapy pack has really helped with the excruciating pain I have been in.

I put it in the microwave for 2 to 2 ½ minutes and it last from 20 minutes to 45 minutes depending on where and how I’m using it and the temperature of the environment. For instance, if I lay in bed with my head on it and I’m bundled up in blankets it doesn’t cool down as fast as if I have it laying on my head or body and it is exposed to the air.

It’s also wonderful for menstrual cramps, back aches, headaches, and when my knee is hurting. I had reconstructive knee surgery a few years ago and I have to use hot and cold therapy in addition to my tens unit.

The pack is rectangular in shape and measure 11.5 inches by 6 inches and is a great size and shape for a variety of uses and body parts. It has two sides, one side fleece for hot and the other side is cotton and smooth for cold. But to be honest I used both side for heat. Because it is soft and fill with rice it is moldable to the body part you are using It on so you get more contact.

I put it in the microwave for 2 to 2 ½ minutes to heat it up and put it in for 1 ½ to 2 minutes to reheat it back up to temp when needed. To chill, I throw it in the freezer for an hour or two.

I got the unscented hot and therapy pack but if you want you can add a couple of drops of essential oils to the pack.

I love that everything about this pack is natural and handmade. From the material to the ingredients which is rice, you know what you are getting. There is no hot plastic chemical unpleasant smell like with traditional heating pads. It does smell like toasted rice but it wasn’t unpleasant because it smells natural and earthy. Also since it’s not electrical there is no risk of fire and it’s safer to use with kids. Still be careful about the heat though, use something between you and the pack. I use a bamboo wash cloth or towel or put it in a pillowcase.

I received my hot and cold therapy pack at no cost in exchange for my honest and unbiased review.

title: Love at first wearing? :)
text:
Note: I received these at a discount in exchange for being encouraged to write a review. And I just now received and put these on. Normally I wait a bit before I review a product, but my initial impressions are strong enough that I wanted to rave/post about this product already, about how much I like it so far.

I am a nurse (currently working part-time while in grad school). And for one thing, I love the look of this product. The socks look sleek and rather classy overall. And stylistically, they actually LOOK like they could be for athletics but don't have to be used only for sports participation.

Second, putting them on, they are helping my feet to feel better currently already. I don't have a work day today but did work most of the weekend, and my feet were hurting quite a bit last night soon after I finished working, when I was just starting to relax (or try to relax). They felt better by the morning, but I think that it still happens to be good timing that these socks arrived today.

On another note, regarding price: So many socks these days seem expensive, whether they are compression socks or not. For most of them out there, I don't think that the full, regular retail prices tend to be worth the prices (not for the potential of getting a second pair for oneself or another, at least). To some degree, to be honest, that may be slightly the case with some other Kunto products out there. (Maybe. I'm not sure, mind you, because personally I haven't had as much need of some of the other types of Kunto products out there.) But for me and probably many others, these compression socks do feel worth paying a bit extra compared to non-compression socks at least, for sure. Truly.

So while it is early to say, I am loving these socks so far. I guess that one thing for people to bear in mind is that the socks are pretty warm. So I could imagine some individuals not realizing that when ordering them and then complaining about it. But if compression socks being warm is okay or even good for you/others (I personally like warm socks sometimes on days that I'm not working and/or during cold seasons)...Then these could be socks that would be of benefit for you/your others.

Oh, the socks definitely do extend up to the knees, by the way. Fyi for any person/s unsure of the length based on the photo or something.

title: Great tasting creatine + L-Glutamine supplement
text:
I am a competitive triathlete and have taken creatine as well as L-Glutamine to help improve athletic performance. I like that this product combines both supplements in an easy-to-eat pouch. I don't normally take creatine monohydrate very often, as it makes me bloated. Apparently, this company has developed a highly bioavailable and easily digestible and trademarked Creatine called CreaBev. I have not had any digestive issues after eating this creatine/L-Glutamine supplement, which is great.

On the their website, this company suggests taking these pouches for 5 days and then taking 2 days off so your body continues to respond to the supplement. I took this suggestion. Although I feel like it's too early to really tell if taking this improves my performance in any way, I have felt good taking it. I like the flavor too. It's a bit sweet, but overall the taste is better than many other supplements I've tried. I don't think this is something I'd use all the time, but I would use it regularly during periods of high training volume. However, with this dosage strategy, a box of 20 pouches would only last 4 loading cycles. At $50 for 20 pouches, this product is much more expensive than, say, buying a creatine supplement and L-Glutamine supplement separately.

Overall, I appreciate this company's commitment to quality, and I think this is a good product. However, it is very expensive, so I am deducting one star for the high price.

title: Basic post-workout mix w/ electrolytes, BCAAs, pricey
text:
I had never tried any products from Sports Illustrated (I didn't even know until ordering that they made supplements). I was almost out of my recovery drink mix and decided to order this one and try it out. In terms of flavor, it is pretty good and tastes as you might expect 'fruit punch' to taste. The flavor is better compared to other brands I've tried. In terms of ingredients, this contains very similar ingredients to my favorite post-workout drink. I use post-workout drinks to replenish whatever electrolytes I may not have been able to replace with an intra-workout formula, and I find that supplementing with BCAAs after workouts helps me recover.

I use post-workout formulas mostly during the triathlon racing season, when I usually have 3 workouts a day and sweat a lot. I would not use this during the off-season or when I am not training as intensely. The addition of tart cherry in this formula is also nice, but given that the ingredients and taste are not substantially better than other formulas I've tried, I think this product is a bit overpriced. There are comparable supplements out there available for a lower price.

title: Antioxidant powder in handy little packets!
text: I had never heard of the maqui berry, but after a little bit of research, it does appear to be more of a superfruit than goji or acai berries! As the package claims, it contains a high concentration of potent antioxidants. Several studies (including test tube studies and clinical studies) show that maqui berry (or extract thereof) may reduce inflammation, reduce LDL cholesterol levels, and improve blood sugar. I am a competitive triathlete, and during the racing season, I try to increase my intake of antioxidant-rich foods to help offset any free radicals that may be released during intense exercise. I don't use these packets every day--more like 2 times a week or so. As the packaging suggests, the maqui powder in these packets is best when mixed with yogurt or a smoothie. It has very little flavor itself (although it does have a beautiful purple color) . I like that the powder comes in these handy packets. I can easily put them in a pocket or purse or gym bag. As for price, these maqui powder packets cost about $1.40 each, which I feel is reasonable.

The main ingredients are vitamins C, E and B plus 'performance' , 'energy', 'ocular', and 'antioxidant' blends, which consist of various fruit powders and vitamin blends. Each serving contains 175 mg of caffeine (1 cup of coffee has about 95 mg), so I rarely take more than 1 serving of this per day (the package says never to take more than 2). Overall, this is a good-tasting energy drink that works well for any activity that requires concentration, stamina, and focus.

title: I wish I could give this product more stars
text:
I have had a host of issues for over 10 years now; autonomic neuropathy manifesting with symptoms of chronic and often debilitating nausea, moderate to severe IBS, and atrial tachycardia (rapid heart rate) with accompanying heat/activity intolerance. There is no cure and conventional medicines have done very little in the way of symptom management. After trying just about anything and everything, I had all but given up on leading a normal life. In one last ditch effort, I tried this against my better judgement, especially considering I'd fallen for many other "miracle" products in my search for something to ease my suffering and nothing had made enough of a significant difference to justify the price-tag that accompanied it. The only two things that even seemed to help at all were ginger caplets for the nausea and coconut oil for overall health. Still, these alone were not making enough of an impact and I was desperate so I researched Panaseeda long and hard and found it promising enough to pay the price and give it a try.

This stuff has changed my life!!!

I put that on its own line because I wanted to signify the profound importance and impact of that statement. When I say that, I'm not exaggerating or sensationalizing. I have no vested interest in the company that manufactures this product, nor am I getting paid to say it or even to leave a favorable review. Plain and simple, if even one person can get the same results that I have and ease the pain and suffering they're going through, then I would be shamefully remiss if I didn't relate what this has meant for me. It hasn't just eased my issues, it has given me my life back! In the span of 2 months, I went from feeling permanently ill and debilitated to only having occasional but very manageable complaints. Heck, I was experiencing improvement the first week! My digestive problems have vastly improved to just minor upsets and my heart rate has come down enough that mere daily activity doesn't leave me feeling utterly wiped out. I'm now finally able to move forward in my life, a possibility that was a distant fantasy for me just a year ago.

So are there any negatives? I'm not gonna lie, it smells like pine tar and tastes what I imagine pine tar would taste like. I pinch my nose to take it and wash it down with several mouthfuls of water, swishing each one to get the residual oil out of my mouth. It's gross, but that's a very, very, very infinitesimal unpleasantness compared with the benefits and healing that comes with it.

This together with a continued daily regiment of coconut oil and ginger capsules has given me back control over my life, and I pray they will continue to make it for the rest of my lifetime!

title: Great Pool. Horrible third party seller.
text:
The three stars is not for the pool itself, which is pretty awesome, but since the company that sells it, Plumstruck, deserves zero stars, I compromised and used three. Other reviews have mentioned the ladder issue, but since the description specifically mentions a ladder, I thought the problem was fixed. When Amazon and I both contacted Plumstruck about the fact that there was no ladder included with the pool, Plumstruck repeated ignored my comments about their false advertising and just sent me the same letter again saying that they were sorry but the ladder is not included. Since the pool is useless, even dangerous without the ladder, this issue must be addressed by the ad. That being said, Amazon does have comparable ladders available for a reasonable price so if the company would just change their wording, people could figure all of this out in advance. Amazon is investigating the company, so hopefully all of this will change.

Some people mentioned a heater, but there is no heater with the pool and it is not mentioned in the description. I was actually worried it would only work with the heater and I didn't want to have to use a 220 outlet, so I was relieved that it doesn't have one. If I decide I need a heater later, I will go to my local pool supply and show them a picture of the pool and get their recommendation. I will never order anything through Plumstuck again. They are a horrible company. If you can find this pool through someone else, I recommend it. It is small enough to fit comfortably in the garage, but deep enough to get in a full aerobic workout.

I also want to add that Amazon sells a salt water conversion system that my local pool store also sells (for a lot more money) that the pool representative says will work with this pool so I will soon be able to convert it to salt water.

text:
