Fitbit has the exact approach that I am looking for in fitness devices: worry free. I embraced the fitbit pedometer philosophy of set up and then update a journal wirelessly. It works for me.

So when the FitBit Aria was introduced and I got past the sticker shock, I realized it was a necessary addition for me given my lifestyle and infinite fitness procrastination. Rather than manually entering weight numbers (what a chore!) this gadget inputs it for me.

Yes, it makes a difference. It also helps that it is very sleek looking and sexy (for a scale). And it seems to work from a quite a distance (dependent on your wifi network strength) and does not require any other antennas.

Why four stars? Because it galls me to admit that the simple action of input weight numbers manually is often too much for me. But for that e-link, there are lower cost options like "Eatsmart Precision Plus Digital Bathroom Scale" ($36.95) or the fancier "Ozeri Touch 440 lb Digital Bath Scale" ($48.95); both are well reviewed. That is over a $70 premium for an e-link.

Setup is very easy, I don't understand what problems other reviewers are having. The issue may be that getting to the actual download site is not as intuitive as it should be. You can use any of these options listed at this link (I hope this link gets thru the Amazon link police. If not, simply google "Aria Scale Set-up Questions" and select the fitbit link).

help.fitbit.
com
[...]

I think that the link above is far more useful than the "manual". I used the PC zip file and there was no issue.

There are a couple of things that are not intuitive but still easy:

1. If you have multiple users you have to set up on one account and then send emails to invite the others. Up to eight fitbit users can hook up to it. The steps are as follows:

(i) Administrator is the first person set up
(ii) Administrator has to send an email invite from the dashboard
(iii) The new person has to accept email invite
(iv) The new person has to go on the scale and take a measurement - it will log as "guest" on the web log
(v) then the administrator has to go into the measurements on their FitBit account and assign that new "guest" weight measurement to the new person (there is a pull-down menu option). Maybe the person can self-assign at the scale but if that option was available we missed it and had to go back to the admin's account.
(vi) After that, all future weight measurements go just to that person.
(vii) Note that the person's privacy settings do apply but only after the administrator has assigned that measurement to that person.

2. The scale figures out who is on the scale and confirms by displaying the initials after it gives you the weight and body fat in percent.

3. If the scale can't figure out who you are then it asks you to choose from options. so far it easily identifies everyone so I have not seen this actually in use.

4. if you are not one of the registered people then it will assume you are a guest and simply mark you as such.

5. you can't see the other's weights unless they share it (guests do not have that option).

6. it seems to have a great wi-fi range so I have not had issues with that.

7. it is not intuitive how you get to the scale from the dashboard. under devices (right hand side under "app gallery - learn more" icon), there is a "Devices" panel. In rather light letters you will see that "Scale" has been added to the right of "Tracker" (if you have a FitBit pedometer). That is how the administrator (the first person to set up) can get to the scale settings.

8. Fat Percentage is a little gimmicky in my opinion. Consumer Reports will not even rate Fat Percentage scales because the technology is inherently inaccurate (google "why CR doesn't test body fat scales"). Even the best bathroom scales have a 5% error margin or more in body fat readings. I don't know the Aria's accuracy but after using it for nearly two weeks I would say that I have seen a 5% fluctuation that I cannot entirely explain. Now that I am following the tips below, it seems to be giving a steady and more consistent reading. Consistent does not mean accurate. If someone has more data on Aria fat percentage accuracy then please do add your comments.

TIPS FOR BEST FAT PERCENTAGE READINGS

a. Best to use fat percentage to measure progress as the readings are not entirely accurate. Reviews on other scales have linked fat percentage accuracy to price, so maybe Aria is more accurate than most.

b. Measure yourself at the same time of day and under the same conditions. Some advise to drink the same amount of water one hour before each measurement and most advise to not do it when dehydrated (like after exercising). I just do it first thing in the morning.

c. If you are so inclined, try the gold standard "DEXA Scanning" or "hydrodensitometry" (water immersion). I am not that fanatical. Honestly, for me, even 5% accuracy is just fine. Those other tests go for $40 - $75 and can be done at health clubs and doctors' offices.

title: Just buy it, you can thank me later worth every cent.
text:
Huh? What? Huh? What? Are you tired of hearing that? I sure as heck did as my 11yo child kept asking us to repeat ourselves multiple times a day. We thought he was testing us. Well, last week the 11tr old went in for a regular check up. Lo and bold: the Dr. could not get in there and see anything as my son’s ears were full of wax.

We came home and did debrox for 2-3 days in each ear to loosen and soften the wax.

And then it was time; time for me to step up and clean out these ears using the elephant ear system.

I filled the bottle in thirds: 1/3 lukewarm water, another 1/3 with room temp hydrogen peroxide, and rubbing alcohol for the last 1/3. I did not measure.

When you do to start squeezing the sprayer, You do need to prime it a few times. I did this into the basin so that my son would not feel air blown into his ear. Once the solution was spraying, I put the very flexible tube into his ear, nor far at first.

Two squeezes and wax was flowing. I did this a few times and then started to place the flexible tip into his ear at different angles to make sure we got most of it. I thought we were finished with my sons ear as he said “I can hear!” I said let’s do one more squeeze to make sure. I’m so glad I did the one more squeeze, as more came out.

Since this happened everyone has had their ears cleaned.

I think there are some key factors as to why it worked for us:

1. We used slightly warm water and hydrogen peroxide to soften the wax and I believe the alcohol helps prevent swimmers ear.

2 we prepped each ear for 2-3 days by using debrox.

3. I changed the angle of the plastic tubing in the ear while squirting, so that the different angles would dislodge more gunk

This has saved me money by not having to see the dr. It’s also one last place we moms have to taxi to for the week.

Buy it, don’t give up too soon; IT WORKS!

title: Forearm Crutches are Way More Convenient
text:
I'm a physical therapist who recently underwent hip surgery. As a result I have to be off my leg for 3 weeks (4 more days as of writing this) and I discovered after two days of clunky, hospital-issued crutches weren't worth my time or money. They were clunky and loud, woke up the whole family any time I walked anywhere, always managed to fall when I leaned them on something, and left my ribs raw and bruised, no matter how I adjusted them.

As a result, I've come to the conclusion that if you're going to be on crutches longer than a few days and you don't get forearm (Lofstrand) crutches, you're a chump! Why?

Well, first of all this design has a (relatively) closed cuff that is completely adjustable. That means that I could reach up and grab something while the crutch hung from my forearm (in a long sleeve shirt) or I could quickly slide my arms through them further so they hung on my upper arm (at my side really) while I reached up overhead.

The cuffs also allow them to lean more easily on things, and because they are rubber coated, they have more friction. These crutches are pretty heavy-duty. Aluminum, with locking screws that prevent clunking and clacking, but I did have to get a wrench to loosen the cuff bolt slightly, so that they would swing a little easier.

The tips are very grippy and soft. I've started to wear one side of them out, so I rotated the bottom of the crutch by pushing in the adjustment buttons and rotating. I walk extremely fast, and I've been hard on these crutches - standing and walking for 7 hours a day so far, with a 12 minute walk to and from my car - so I'm not surprised that the tips are showing a bit of wear already. The crutches overall are steady, safe, and designed well. I wish that the cuff width could be adjusted somewhat (although metal, they bend but do not stay) more for a more precise fit.

Overall a really good, inexpensive, highly reliable product.

text: People swear by these supplements.  I tried this when I had my first daughter three years ago, and again with my second.  Both times my milk failed to increase a drop.  If anything, my supply dropped.  My milk did go back up after I stopped taking this, so thankfully no harm was done.  I did a little research, and most experts say that yes, these herbs can boost your supply, but the amount you would have to take to see any results is astronomical.  Far more than you're going to get from any capsule.  The only true way to boost milk to to express as often as possible. That, plus a good night's sleep and lots of water is what does it for me.  It's my guess that when women say these pills work, they want them to work, and are also doing everything else they can.  Then they give the credit to the pills, but it's really just a coincidence.  Either way, it doesn't hurt to try.  If these pills don't work, you can always increase milk the old fashioned way.

title: Overpriced
text: I developed an eczema on my eye lids as a result of sun exposure.  My usual eye creams do not work for me anymore as they irritate my extremely sensitive skin and cause new flare-ups.  While I found a few eye products that do not sting or cause more irritation, I am constantly searching for more and kind of obsessed right now to get more relief from itching and redness.  So among other eye products I ordered Body Tonique Repair and Replenish Facial and Body Oil.  It arrived promptly in a sealed 4 ounce plastic bottle.  The twist on and off lid is convenient for precise dispensing.  The oil is a mixture of several carrier oils with mostly oils that are found in the kitchen.  It also has a blend of essential oils that is kept a secret by manufacturer.  I was able to recognize lemon and lavender oils in it.  I applied this oil under my eyes only where I have eczema.  It was absorbed some but left a very noticeable greasy residue.  It felt okay on the lower lids but the oil got on my eye lashes and into my eyes and caused some eye irritation and blurred vision.  It made me blink constantly.  I should put less oil and even lower next time to prevent this from happening.  I already used jojoba, argan, moringa seed, rose hip and sea buckthorn oils and found them to work better and not leave so much greasy residue on my lids.  It is probably better to use it on the body than on the face, and definitely away from the eyes.  However, the biggest issue I have with the price.  While I was offered a promotional discount in exchange for my honest and unbiased review, I think the regular price is extremely high for what it is and I will not repurchase this product in the future.

title: Huge bombs
text:
By now I tried so many different bath bombs, and repurchased my favorites multiple times. While I prefer bath bombs to other bath products like bath salts, seaweeds and herbal baths due to their moisturizing and skin conditioning properties, I discovered that the quality of bath bombs on Amazon varies greatly. Most of the sellers claim their bath bombs to be natural, however, some are artificially perfumed or just lose the scent when dissolved in water.

Beauty by Earth Bath bombs arrived promptly, and were packaged in a carboard boxes with cutouts, so you can smelled them right after the opening of the shipping box. I ordered both energizing and relaxing collection and all of them smell great! And they are scented with essential oil blends, not artificial perfumes. The scents do not disappear after the bombs do, so I had wonderful aromatherapy sessions during my baths. These bombs are very large, 6.5 ounces a piece. Some bombs on the market are only 2 ounces which is the size of golf ball, while Beauty by Earth bombs are the size of an orange. They contain Dead Sea salts and Epsome salts that sooth tired muscles, as well as clays for detox. These bombs do not contain dyes that leave a ring on your bath tub. I do not need a visual show that some bombs offer, what is important to me are skin moisturizing and aromatherapy. So I enjoyed these bath bombs. I received them at a discounted price in exchange for my honest and unbiased review.

It's wonderful that as Hypnobabies experiences rapid growth there are doulas taking the time to become Hypno-doulas, so they are better able to meet the needs of their clients. It's a great opportunity for us doulas to differentiate ourselves in our local market. As Hypnobabies continues it's explosive growth, we Hypno-doulas will have a built in customer base.

The training manual is fantastic, informative, concise, and great to refer to as needed. The CDs included are fantastic, I've used them personally as well as with clients, and they work amazingly well! Great bargain for everything that is included.

title: Surprisingly simple and surprisingly effective
text:
Im a grown a** woman, yet no matter how many bottles I buy, or how many fruit infusions I make, or whether I carry a water bottle around all day or not, and regardless if i have a straw or dont, I will still go several days without drinking water. Its ridiculous, really. I know that water is good for your hair! And Skin! And Headaches! and probably a million other things, but somehow I just never get around to taking a sip of water.
Enter this incredibly simple little gadget. I almost didnt buy it, because in addition to not drinking water, Im also incredibly frugal (and by that I mean stupidly cheap). But, i gave it a shot, and Im glad. it works right out of the box. No instructions, no weird buttons to press or start up. Literally just slip it on your water bottle. It lights up when I get to the office to remind me to fill my bottle, and then annoyingly blinks throughout the day until I pick it up to take a drink. I actually rolled my eyes at it today because I felt like Ive spent the entire morning in the bathroom, but alas, the eye roll didnt stop the annoying blinking so I took another drink. Which is the whole point. So all that to say it works. A simple reminder that I should be able to give myself, but dont and wont, so this little diddy makes it happen.

I can only conclude that it's cheaply made and certainly not worth a fraction of the premium price tag. Shoddy, very shoddy.

My original (very positive) review is below. I wrote this after 3 shaves:

(original title: Very nice - albeit expensive - shaving brush) - I've been a mug-and-brush guy most of my life. I've occasionally dabbled with aerosols etc, but always come back to the mug and brush for a nice, thick, warm, rich lather than makes shaving a breeze. I got this one as a replacement/supplement to my 20-year-old Old Spice brush (left in the photo) which has served me well for many thousands of shaves. The bristles on the Prof Fuzzworthy are finer and hold more water, so I quickly learned to shake it out before making lather or the lather comes out too thin and watery. The Sassafras wood handle is nice and gives it good visual appeal. But I must confess that it feels more than a bit extravagant to spend almost 50 bucks on a shaving brush. I can't help but think that there are many out there that would give a great mug of lather for a fraction of that cost. But that said, it's a great brush and I'm completely satisfied.

Then you partially lift it out and move it sideways so it can rest on some little plastic things while you squeeze the excess water out.  When you are through washing one area, you either have to repeat the above process, which adds dirt to your clean water, or you have to take it to your sink to wring it out.  Problem is, there is no mechanism to wring it out except the one in the bucket.  You can do it by hand, but it's a bid tricky and not very handy.  One thing I do like about it is that it does not leave your floor soaking wet, so it dries pretty quickly.  Also, I love the size and shape of the bucket--who needs a round bucket? title: Miyarisan is well worth the long shipment time from Japan. Research confirms its many benefits.
text:
I have some specific health needs involving long-term use of antibiotics and antibiotic resistance. I've done some rather extensive research to understand which product would most effectively help rebuild my gut microbiome: Miyarisan or the Canadian product, Advanced Orthomolecular Research (AOR), Amazon's Choice. If you have real health concerns, the detail provided here may be helpful. Otherwise, you might want to skip or skim this review.
There are instructions in English on the Miyarisan box, but not much else. It indicates Clostridium Butyricum as the probiotic, but it does not give a count of Colony Forming Units (CFU) per dose. This missing information makes a straight comparison between the two products difficult. However, based on dosage guidelines, nine of these small pills are taken each day, so this bottle of 330 tablets will last about 36 days. The Advanced Orthomolecular Research product is a 30 day supply. Doing the math, it ends up about 9 cents more per day for Miyarisan or $2.70 more for a month's supply. Not much.
Miyarsan contains, in addition to lactose hydrate (which is in both formulations), cornstarch, talc, MICROCRYSTALLINE CELLULOSE (a refined wood pulp, which some holistic practitioners warn causes inflammation), MAGNESIUM STEARATE (a synthetic fat, which many holistic practitioners are up in arms about), and sucrose. Cornstarch, talc, and sucrose, all common pharmaceutical fillers, each has their critics among holistic practitioners in North America. In contrast, the AOR probiotic has, in addition to lactose and potato starch, two synthetic polymers: polyvinyl alcohol and providone. Both are used in eye care products and thought to be safe, but who knows? These synthetics appear to have been on the market since 1996. When they've been around as long as talc and sucrose, there may well be concerns raised about the safety of them. The AOR capsule is vegetarian hypromellose, essentially a dissolvable synthetic.

The real concern about the Advanced Orthomolecular Research product is that its primary probiotic is Enterococcus Faecium which is provided as a whopping 54 million CFU's per dose compared to 1.8 million for Clostridium Butyricum. While non-toxic strains of the latter are safe and very valuable probiotics which contribute to the formation of butyrate in the large intestine, there are some concerns that Enterococcus Faecium could contribute to antimicrobial resistance (AMR). A 2001 study on Clinical Infectious Diseases presents evidence for this; it can be found on the internet @ Oxford Academic, under the title, Probiotic Enterococcus faecium Strain Is a Possible Recipient of the vanA Gene Cluster,
Moreover, a recent (2018) scientific article reiterates that concern, It states, "Concerns over the safety of E. faecium for use as a probiotic food supplement have been raised due to the propensity of this microbe to develop and acquire AMR, especially to vancomycin and ampicillin." This article is on the site, Pen & Tec and is entitled, "Enterococcus faecium as probiotic – is it safe? Views from Taiwan, USA and EU"
Given my history and the rise of antimicrobial resistance worldwide, this last is more than enough to lead me to choose Miyarisan over AOR. I found another study specific to Miyarisan, which confirms this decision. It’s on the site, Science Direct, under Clinical Microbiology and Infection. It is entitled, Clostridium Butyricum: from beneficial to a new emerging pathogen
In part, it reads, "A recent study found that the C. butyricum strain MIYAIRI 588 (CBM588) promoted regulatory T-cell generation in the intestine through induction of transforming growth factor-β1 from lamina propria dendritic cells… with a suggested role of fermentation metabolites such as butyrate. This C. butyricum strain also induced interleukin-10-producing macrophages in inflamed mucosa to prevent acute experimental colitis in mice… Other experimental studies have shown the capacity of this strain to improve non-alcoholic fatty liver disease and prevent C. difficile infection, enterohaemorrhagic Escherichia coli O157:H7 infection, and gastric ulcers. In clinical practice, the administration of CBM588 was effective for both the treatment and the prophylaxis of antibiotic-associated diarrhea in children. It increased the level of anaerobes and prevented the decrease in the level of Bifidobacterium species in subjects who received antibiotics."

text:
I was a little worried from reading peoples reviews but I really like this product. I'm not sure why people are so undecided on this product or worried about the creator of this product but this product works as advertised. The first time I used this product I was outside drilling 48 holes with an auger for a fence I was building. It took me all day (9 a.m.-8 p.m), at about 1-2 p.m. I took this product and didn't even stop for a lunch. The drink was filling, not in an over bloated way but a satisfying way. As if I had eaten something for lunch. It also gave me a boost of energy. The feeling wasn't like drinking two cups of coffee (jittery on the inside while blah on the outside) but a natural energy (upbeat/not tired) without a crash. Like I said I took this drink at about 1-2 p.m. and didn't finish until about 8 p.m. By 7 p.m I was getting tired but it wasn't a crash feeling.

If I had to change something about this product, it would be its taste. The taste is not intolerable, not like some whey protein drinks, but the smell definitely is better than the taste. It taste like water with a slight hint of flavor with your taste buds searching for more flavor. Hopefully that makes sense. I was expecting a sweeter taste. Since my first time taking this product I was sold. I take it to help boost my immune and curb my appetite. I have been taking this product for two months now and have lost 17 lbs.

What I really like about this product is that it isn't a chemical based product. It has multiple vitamins and nutrients and is a natural alternative to other chemical based immune, diet, and health products. It picks me up without a crash and helps me feel full with a light meal.

title: Took less than 2 months.
text:
Our child was almost done with Kindergarten and was still wearing pull-ups. Without them, every night (at random times) they would pee the bed. It was frustrating. They were so out-of-it when they peed that I could be standing next to them talking loudly and shaking them, and they wouldn't wake up.

The child is VERY into horses, so we told them this was a special thing for horsies, and the sound from the alarm (that this plugs into) is from the start of a horse race. That got them super excited, they were telling friends and grandparents, and showing it off.

The first month was frustrating, I was up every night with absolutely no progress. Random times, and at first, the loud sounds and vibrations weren't enough to wake them up. So I pushed the vibrater back against the bed-post. Now when it goes off it bangs (from vibrating). That helped a bit, but it would still take a while to rouse them.

Then halfway into the second month, they just stopped peeing in bed. They weren't getting up and going to the bathroom in the middle of the night...just not peeing. I thought maybe I was just getting lucky and they weren't drinking water or something. But it's now been half a year about....and they have only had one accident! (well...we have some problems when they sleep in a different environment, like a sleeping bag, so we still do pull-ups if we travel)

This was such a relief!

title: Disappointed, They Smell Soapy
text:
I was really excited to try these out. After all, who wouldn't like some aromatherapy while showering? The first scent I tried was the mint one. I was disappointed that I did not get any trace of mint. It smelled soapy, as in similar to some hand soaps I have had. The same thing happened with the ocean breeze, spruce, and mango.

Finally, I got to the rose. This one smelled slightly like roses. However, from the description, it says a potent smell. The smell was weak and barely noticeable. The same thing with the lavender. I got slight floral notes, but again, an overpowering soapy smell.

For all of them, I put them in the corner of my tub and let the steam activate them, sometimes adding a few drops of water. You can see the colors go down the drain, so you know it is working. I will say to rinse your tub thoroughly after use, otherwise the color will stay and you have to scrub it out. It does not stain the tub, the color will come out.

title: Don't stick them in too deep ... OR--!!
text:
Okay, these are great. They block the damaging sound but remain "loud enough" where you are experiencing a live concert and it feels great and loud and "live" -- without the ringing afterward and beyond. After a few minutes, you forget they're in your ears, and the level of sounds becomes "normalized" in your head -- so you don't feel like any filteration is happening. Live music just sounds more clear. It really works and I'd absolutely recommend it. I used these at a punk rock concert (standing right next to the speakers!) and also at a country concert (sitting near them.) Both were loud and both I walked away from pain-free and ring-free, while enjoying the music thoroughly.

Only criticism/warning: DO NOT PUT THEM TOO DEEP IN YOUR EAR. They're extremely easy to "bury" into your ear canal, where you'll need a friend with tweezers to work them out. This is an extremely frightening experience. The first time I put them in to "test" them, I got one stuck. My friend only accidentally pushed it deeper, rather than pulling it out. I took some nail clippers and levered it out myself. Jeez...

To properly insert, just lightly push into ear. Don't allow it to go any deeper than a few mm's. You may even feel like they're going to fall out. But they don't. Maybe they need longer "extraction knobs" or something -- but the company is trying to make them subtle, so you don't look like you're going hunting or something, with big, honkin' orange foam plugs. haha

title: The relief of the hot water bottle
text:
This is a nice hot /cold water bottle. I like the transparency of the bottle makes it easy for me to see how much liquid I have in it or the status of that liquid. Et If I fill it with ice for a twisted ankle, I can see how much of it is melted without removing the bottle from its perch. The sweater works as a nice insulator to keep the water hot or cold for a longer period. It also makes it soft to the touch, no longer a need to wrap a towel around it. Which makes it more effective I believe because you're not constantly having to rewrap it.
I used this the day we got it because my little fur baby had an upset tummy and hadn't been feeling well, likely because she ate too fast, so I put some warm water in it and placed it so she could lay on it. She laid right on it, fell asleep and did not move until it had started to get cool. There is a wide mouth which makes it so much easier to get ice in it and/ or safer for pouring hot water in it, and when it is necessary, easier to clean.
I like the colors of it and the sweater gives a nice cozy feel/ look giving it a nice calming effect for the one not feeling well.

title: VERY comfortable and gentle, easy to pump a lot of milk!
text:
I have come full circle with this pump. When I first started using this pump, I found it was much more comfortable than the one I had been using at the hospital. However, having flat nipples, it became increasingly difficult to pump. I assumed it was because of the type of pump, but now (11 months later) I know that pumping just takes some getting used to! I switched to a different pump (the Philips Avent Comfort Double Electric Pump) and used it for 10 months, not realizing that pain during pumping is actually NOT normal. The Avent was a great pump for most of the time I used it, but over time my nipples became traumatized from the hard suction and incorrectly sized breast cups. Pumping started out being awkward-feeling and uncomfortable, to being extremely painful. My nipples were constantly swollen and red, and super enlarged. Because of the pain, I really couldn't pump more than 2-3 ounces at a time (dropping down from 5-8 ounces at a time!), so in desperation I switched back to the Simplisse breast pump. At first, my nipples had become so engorged I had to use nipple cream to be able to comfortably use this Simplisse as there are no larger sized breast cups available, but over time the cream (which was olive oil-based) started to degrade the silicone parts. (Never use any oil-based lubricants on any silicone. It melts the silicone!)

The Simplisse was fantastic, much more comfortable than the Avent Comfort pump, but the nipple oil I had been using ruined the pump parts! I contacted the company directly to replace 2 parts, and they sent me an entire collection kit (everything but the pump) for free! I received the kit within 2 days, and I am so glad! By this time my nipples had returned to their normal size, so I was able to comfortably use the Simplisse without any nipple cream.

It has been a couple of weeks, and I am LOVING the Simplisse pump. I pump for less time, less often, and am pumping more milk than I ever did with the pinch-y Avent! The SImplisse pump has a different suction that more closely mimics a baby's suction, and offers flow and speed controls. It's a little louder than the Avent pump, but the silicone breastcups and gentle suction make this SO much more comfortable to use -- no pain! Just be sure to follow the directions EXACTLY when putting it together -- and in removing them! My husband accidentally snapped a piece off the top lid holding the valve because he didn't realize the trick to removing!

PROS: gentle suction makes this a more comfortable pump; fast let-down; different controls for speed and flow; easy to clean the parts (BUT be gentle with the white valves - dish brushes can scratch them!); pump a lot

CONS: a little loud; sensation takes some getting used to if you are accustomed to a hard suction pump; parts are a little tricky at first to put together (BUT once you know how it is easy!)

title: My skin looks beautiful!  Works amazingly well.
text:
After only one week on the product, here are the positive benefits I have noticed so far:
Lowered appetite (Will this lead to weight loss? Too soon to say)
Less desire for sweets
Beautiful skin!!! (It took about 5 days until I really started to see the skin benefits.)
Healing of acne and skin issues (even on parts of the body that I don't put the cream on.)
Sleep very well at night
Waking up refreshed in the morning often before my alarm clock with no tiredness.
Greatly lowered anxiety.
Mood more stable and relaxed
Been in a good mood all week.
Slight improvement to concentration
Slight improvement to vision
Dried cracked feet are healing
I see a few new hairs coming in on my scalp (dark and thick) - too soon to say but hoping this will help with my thinning hair issues.
Reduced PMS symptoms
My neck, shoulders, back, and knee joints feel more flexible and I have more range of movement. (Haven't felt this pain-free and relaxed since I was a teenager.)

Negative side effects:
My thyroid swelled up so it felt uncomfortable to swallow. (Taking Selenium stopped this side effect.)
Mild runny nose. (This went away after day 2.)
Increased need to drink water. If I don't drink water when needed, it makes me cough.
Increased trips to the bathroom to get rid of water. (Averaging about once every 1-2 hours)
Some mild headaches (Had about 3 this week. Pretty mild and did not last long so did not have to take pain relievers.)

I looked up other experiences online of people who take Iodine and those mild negative side effects are normal. That's where I found out how important it is to ensure you're getting some Selenium also while taking this product if your diet is not naturally high in selenium. The side effects have been mild and the positive benefits have been way beyond what I expected so I plan to keep taking this product. Please do your own research. If you already have a diet high in Iodine (which is rare but possible) then this would not be a beneficial product for you to take. Iodine and Selenium are needed in your diet but they can be overdosed on which has bad health effects so do your research and never take more than the recommended amounts on the product containers. Be careful and discuss it with your medical professional.

I've been using this Iodine cream per directions on the label for 1 week now. This is powerful stuff so do not use more than recommended. I also take it with 100 mcg of Selenium (L-selenomethionine) which for me stopped a couple of negative side effects at the beginning so if you have any side effects consider adding a little Selenium. I also take a very expensive high-quality multi-vitamin with minimum RDA of Iodine and Selenium however I've taken those for years so am sure they are unrelated to the positive benefits I've seen on this product. Nothing else has changed in my life other than taking this Iodine cream and some added Selenium so all the good effects are from taking this product.

I paid for this product with my own money. Haven't received any free products from the sellers. If I continue to see more positive effects or any negative effects, I'll try to remember to come back to update this review.

title: Hold button on side to toggle on/off. Cute, simple, pretty lights
text: [[VIDEOID:7544b561180586d17c25e76615acb26b]] This is a pretty cute item, I think it's great if you have a baby and need some sort of ambient noise to help them sleep. If you're using this for yourself, you could probably find something very similar in your appstore or YouTube for free, but if you don't want to rely on your phone or a video for that, this is a nice alternative. The sound quality is okay, and pretty loud if you want it to be, you can also use something else like headphones since there's an auxiliary port. You toggle it ON and OFF from a small button on the side by holding for 3 seconds. It charges via micro usb, which is included. Every button on top is touch sensitive and cycles through your options, except for volume which has 2, one to increase the other to decrease. There's 3 categories of sounds/music(32 total), I counted 3 for Yoga, 3 for Alpha Music, and 26 for White Noise. There's a nice optional ambient light feature, 7 colors, 3 levels of brightness, and an option to toggle the light to "breath" which gently goes between dim and bright. There's also a timer, but the maximum is 1 hour. The only complaints I have is the timer may be too short for some, and if you have a favorite song/sound, you'll have to cycle to it. I'm sure you can make a soundtrack list to make cycling easier, so it's mostly a minor issue.

Should've used a 2x4 instead of 1x4 to keep the rail off the floor when initially installing, because it dropped too far later. Used a hand winch to pull the track uphill after assembly. text:
This is (IMO) an outstanding product . . .

I returned to the states in August of 2015 after having lived in Germany for the past couple years . . . and during our stay, we picked up a number of antique items (some, like this stove, needed a little finishing TLC). So, to that end, I attempted to find a stove polish similar to that used in Germany . . . after checking the big-box stores, all I could really find were versions of spray paints (not what I was looking for; for reasons beyond the scope of this review). Anyway, after speaking w/ some friends back in Germany (one guy, Lothar, was a professional restorer of antique cast iron stoves, takenplattens, irons, etc.) . . . this was the product that I ended up with . . . as it was recommended to me by Lothar.

Initially, it was difficult to determine the 'end color' of this product as I was looking for a 'silver-black' finish & this one came as close as saying "graphite". So, I thought I'd give it a try . . .the picture I'm attaching is being provided so that readers/viewers may appreciate the before & after effects. The doors are the 'after' applying & buffing the polish; whereas the area immediately around the doors (both sets of doors) have not been buffed. As you can see, the contrast between the 'pre & post' buffing is pretty dramatic . . . it goes from a flat black to a glossy-ish silver-black. (Note: ignore the crown as it's not been addressed yet & ignore the firebox, below, as it's been buffed). So, for purposes of this review, check out the doors & the immediate areas around the doors.

If you're going to use this polish on a stove (or any iron item w /much detail), then I'd recommend using the following:

1) Application Brushes: both sponge & bristle brushes have a purpose in this restoration
2) Buffing: I used both cotton rags & a horse hair brush.
3) Dremmel: I used my dremmel (w/ appropriate attachments) for some buffing in the very tight spaces.

After applying the polish & waiting a minimum of 4 hours, it requires a bit of 'elbow grease'; but the end product is well worth it.

Anyway, I hope this is helpful.

Regards,

Shek

We have two cats. One is half Ragdoll, which means she has medium to longer length fur. Not to mention, my own hair, which is long and always shedding. I use lint rollers before I leave my home. I use them on furniture-for what the vacuum doesn’t pick up. And, I can’t stand loose fur on my pj’s before crawling into bed. So, I again lint roll my clothes right before bed. I’m using a lot of lint roller sheets. In our home, they are always on hand.

Given the bargain price, I didn’t have high hopes. If you go to your local Walmart or Target, you can pay six or seven dollars for a single roller. Six lint rollers for this price is unheard of here-locally. I didn’t know what to expect, but I didn’t expect much. I was pleasantly surprised. Not only am I stocked up for awhile (you get two refillable handles and six rolls of sheets), these actually grab debris well. When I use them on my son’s sofa in his domain in the basement, they pick up crumbs and fur with ease. I have no regrets with this purchase. I’d purchase them again. Whether you have pets, or are just looking to leave work lintless, I’d give these a try.

title: Objectively? Don't waste your money.
text:
First, my order was very very late. That seems to be an issue with this seller as the reviews say.

As a mask goes?
PRO's-
It looks better than a paper mask.
CON's-
1- Runs a bit small. You'll have to keep adjusting the fit as you go about. That does NOT help keep your hands away from your face and compromising it's fit.
2- Adjustment wire in the bridge is very weak and will lose whatever contour/shape you form it to fit your nasal bridge. Hands-Face issue again and compromising masks fit.
3- Breathability;
A- You may have issues with this product if you're asthmatic, have COPD or ARD's. It is difficult to breath (I have moderate asthma/COPD at my age of 54) and it's a task to draw a breath through the mask.
B- The "Valve" does nothing to aid in exhalation, it's decorative. My two masks literally open up at the sides for my breath to escape around the sides of the material, not through the valve.
C- Elastic ear bands, again they run small and pull your ears forward. Distracting and uncomfortable (not to mention they make you look like one of the "Little Rascals" from old black and white television. Sure dated myself didn't I?

I am certified in SCBA's marine firefighting from the oilfield (13 years) and have eight years training for Nuclear, Chemical, Biological Warfare from the infantry (M17 Protective Mask) and feel I am more than qualified to say this is a fail in all regards.

If you are prior service, the best comparison I can make is figure it's like trying to breath through an M17 Protective Mask that has wet filters. You can do it, but it's a fight.

Caveat Emptor, folks. Buyer beware.

title: Really good value toothbrushes for the environmentally conscious!
text:
I’ve been on an environmental kick and wanted to be conscious of the waste I’ve been producing. That’s when I saw these bamboo toothbrushes that are said to be biodegradable (note not the bristles!).

I bought these at around $14 for four with two travel cases. I find that quality toothbrushes usually cost between $3 to $5 on average. When you add on the cases and the unique bamboo material, I personally thought it was a FANATASTIC deal! The handle even widens at the end so it’s easy to hold.

The only thing that I’m not sure is a negative or a positive yet is that I’ve noticed there’s a wood taste when using the brush. I might update the review later with my assessment but something to note if that’s a deal breaker for you. I didn’t think about it when purchasing so I assume others haven’t either.

In summary, great price, great value, and environmentally friendly!

title: Love it - one of the better meal replacements i've tried - try it with cold brew coffee!!
text:
So far so good,

I really don't like the chocolate flavored meal replacements, and this one although not exactly cereal milk flavored like I've heard so many rave about is pretty good. It has a neutral flavor profile, You can definitely taste the rice.

I did try it by itself, and it went down pretty smooth, as usual with meal replacements, the colder the better.

Getting the consistency down isn't easy for me because i'm an idiot and i don't measure things.

There, I said it...I think If I were to do that, I would know what the consistency actually should be since Ive never tried the bottled stuff, but in my 24 oz shaker bottle this morning, I put in three scoops and filled it to the brim with my cold brew coffee.

Like I said it has a neutral flavor profile, so you throw this in a mixer with bananas, its just gonna taste like bananas, strawberries, its gonna taste like strawberries, so no surprise, with the coffee, it tasted like, well...coffee.

A bit more latte-ish - you get the mouthfeel of the fat in the Soylent, which kind of reminds me of the bulletproof coffee I used to drink... if you haven't heard of the concept, you make your coffee, pour it HOT into a blender, mix in some grass-fed butter and coconut oil (this is the homespun recipe - you don't have to go buy the bulletproof brand MCT oil, coffee and such) - blend it up and you supposedly have a drink that will make you razor sharp, and satiate your hunger - all this is true, it is delicious, and goes down smooth as all get out, but you're a mess, greasy lips, shiny face, your coffee cup is a mess, spills leave fat stains on your shirt, no bueno...and jeez, who has time to do all that mess first thing in the morning.

So I gave that up, and I gotta say, trying Soylent with cold brew coffee brought back some of those same sensations, it will satiate your hunger (without clogging your arteries), and has close to the same mouthfeel, although nothing tops pure grass-fed butter and coconut oil...

All in all, I'm a fan, been drinking it for a while now, and almost time to reorder - I have heard it was cheaper to order from the website, but I know for a fact it's easier for me to order from Amazon...

For reference, this is the shaker bottle I used,
[[ASIN:B07DHS4N8J Contigo Shaker Bottles Black Mixer 28 Ounce (2 pack)]]

title: Sharp style with sharp edge
text:
Stainless steel- I've been so in love with them for a long time, and after a lot of thought, I've decided that it's time to share it with the world. The carbon-steel knife you see pictured above? Well, I'd like to introduce you to the love of my knife. I am so glad I purchased this. Yup, that's my baby right there a long time, I lived in denial of how strong my feelings were. People would ask me what knives they should buy, and, unless they were professionals, I'd always steer them towards stainless steel. I figured I was giving good advice, since stainless steel is more forgiving, and most home cooks are looking for ease.
Bu a long time, I lived in denial of how strong my feelings were. People would ask me what knives they should buy, and, unless they were professionals, I'd always steer them towards stainless steel. I figured I was giving good advice, since stainless steel is more forgiving, and most home cooks are looking for ease.
But now I'm going to tell you what I really think, if you take cooking seriously, if you're ready to invest a little bit of time and a lot more care, and if you're willing to sharpen your own knives, then carbon steel is where it's at. It pays off in dividends.
If you just want to get dinner on the table, not think about your knives beyond whether they're just barely sharp enough to blunder their way through an onion, and not worry if you mistreat them to no end, then yeah, stick with stainless.t now I'm going to tell you what I really think: if you take cooking seriously, if you're ready to invest a little bit of time and a lot more care, and—this is a big one—if you're willing to sharpen your own knives, then carbon steel is where it's at. It pays off in dividends.
If you just want to get dinner on the table, not think about your knives beyond whether they're just barely sharp enough to blunder their way through an onion, and not worry if you mistreat them to no end, then yeah, stick with stainlessI'm not an expert when it comes to the finer points of metallurgy, but for our purposes, what's important to know is that the difference between carbon steel and stainless steel is that stainless has chromium added to carbon steel's basic iron-and-carbon mix. The metal bestows upon stainless its resistance to corrosion and rust.
That rust resistance of stainless, though, comes at a price. First, stainless tends to be a softer form of steel, which means it often won't hold an edge as well as carbon steel. That's right: carbon steel stays sharper longer than stainless.
Second, and this is really important, carbon steel, despite being harder than stainless steel, is way easier to sharpen than stainless.This is critical because, in my experience, knives that are used frequently simply don't stay very sharp for long. Sure, they stay sharp enough to do their job reasonably well, and certainly sharp enough to cut you if you slip, but not high-performance, precision sharp. Great quality knife and cuts meat and veggies with super style. Will recommend this to other. Glad to be given a discount to review this.

title: Works on course facial hair
text:
What I like:
1) It’s a great price.
2) It gets the coarse facial hair leaving my face smooth as silk. (#1 reason for this purchase).
3) Bonus items, like the face brush cleanser attachment. Used it twice so far & liked it.
4) Battery life is long and it shows me how many of the 90 minutes of a full charge I have left.

What I don’t like:
1) It definitely takes more passes than anticipated to get the hair. It has 5 blades…you’d think one and done, but it’s more like 5 or more slow, circular passes over each area to finish the job.
2) It is not discreet. As a woman embarrassed about problematic course facial hair, it’s hard to hide from the family when it’s in use because it’s loud, like a hair buzzer, & large.
3) It’s somewhat tricky to wake it up to turn it on. I press around the base and hold the button for several seconds and eventually it recognizes the action & comes to life suddenly. Not a problem, just not my favorite feature.

Good to know:
I haven’t tried it in the shower but I tried using it dry on my lower legs and, as I mentioned before, takes quite a few passes to get the area
smooth & regular shaving with a razor is much faster. Definitely not my first choice for legs.

There is a rubbery scrubber looking attachment included but nowhere on the box or in the instructions does it say what it’s for. Maybe it’s in the product description on the product page here and will go back and look.

For all the reasons above I give it 5 stars mainly because you get what you pay for & for $20 the cons were minor in comparison to the pros.

title: Are you ready to become somebody who matters?
text:
I am new to the world of nootropics, Optimind is the first product I try that claims to boost your mental health and give you laser focus. Before I write my opinion, I have to say that the power of placebo cannot be underestimated. Yet, I don't think it was placebo that made me recall my forgotten French language skills, because I cannot explain how I started talking in French half an hour after my first pill! My mood was lifted above the clouds, and I could multitask effeciently, without giving second thoughts to what I was doing or stopping halfway to refocus. Honestly, it was like my mental abilities were trapped and suddenly after I took my first pill they were freed! I actually had a class in college on the same day after I took my first dose, and during that class I was having an engaging, and sophisticated conversations with my professor, I could even point out his mistakes, and saw the flaws to his arguments as clear as the sun. Under regular circumstances, I wouldn't participate in long conversations. but on that day I felt like saying what I wanted to say, without worry or fear of being judged, it became clear to me that this drug can do things I never thought any drug could acheive. I felt like a God for a day. It *did* give me laser focus. However, I feel that it also raised my blood pressure, and I had a feverish feeling, like my brain was on Speed. Thankfully, that worrying effect didn't last long. The thing I noticed the most after taking this drug is that I had a tenfold increase in my multitaking skills, I was reading something and listening to something else entirely and I noticed that I could actually focus on both without having second thoughts. I could apprehend both. If I could attribute the biggest benefit this drug had on me, it's the noticable increase in my multitasking skills. The second day was not as good as the first. While I took my first pill in the evening, my second dose was taken the morning after, I felt all the bad side effects from the drug. I could still feel that my multitasking skills were improved, but I had a slight headache and I felt feverish again and I also felt jittery. I have Hashimoto thyroiditis. I believe I didn't feel as good as the first time because I took my second dose in the morning, closer to my daily thyroid prescription. Since I noticed that the best effects of Optimind happened to me during the evening, I think I'll revert to the same time I took my first pill, and see how it goes. I'll continue taking 1 pill a day at least for 10-15 days to assess my tolerance, and from there I'll increase the dosage to 2 pills a day.
To everyone who is reading my review. Go ahead and try this drug. Honestly, I would never tell anyone around me about this, unless it's someone I truly care about. This is truly the limitless pill you've been waiting for. I hope in the future caffeine is removed from this drug and replaced with something better. Maybe something to help with the noticeable increase in blood pressure and stomach bloating. To conclude my argument for this drug, I have to ask you –dear reader– this, If one pill did that for me, imagine what it can do for you? *Set your goals!*

title: definitely helpful
text:
I am not hard of hearing, so I can't speak to the usefulness of this device for those folks, but this device worked well in all the areas in which I tried it out.

I wore it around a grocery store and out in the woods, and found that it gave me considerable control over volume and assisted in hearing certain things.

In the store, I could easily get it loud enough to be uncomfortable, and could hear softer sounds amplified with greater clarity. The use of some form(s) of sound processing was obvious, and anyone used to the "breathing" of poorly adjusted audio compression will know what I mean.

Again, not being impaired (I actually test about 10db better than average for my age, except at one narrow frequency band, despite years of loud music and guitar playing in my youth), the effects were more annoying than useful to me, but I can easily see that this could be quite handy for people with certain kinds of hearing problems.

The processing did seem able to help separate near field conversation from background noise, especially in the woods.

As a wireless headset for media playback, I was quite pleased with the quality of the sound. The included earbuds were comfortable (different sized fittings for the earbuds are included), and the sound quality quite good for this kind of headset. (I have been spoiled by recording studio quality headsets, and Koss Pro4AAs were my headset of choice even for casual listening for a long time.)

The earbuds provided quite good sound, and I watched many, many hours of video from YouTube and Amazon without fatigue or discomfort. It was nice to wander around the living room and even the kitchen without losing any audio quality or volume.

I had no problems with signal or linking (the wireless is Bluetooth), and connections to the bas unit were easy and clear.

I could get quite used to this system. If you are in the market for something to use for wireless audio and audio assistance in conversation or public places, I would definitely give this a shot. I think it could be very useful.

title: Surprisingly effective anti-inflammatory
text:
I had a spider bite on my finger bad enough to warrant the use of a steroid cream, and the itchiness and swelling from fingertip to knuckle was driving me crazy. The steroid helped a bit, but I couldn't use it more than twice a day, so I tried "silver shield," which came highly recommended at a holistic-remedy-type shop. Wow! Several uses and half a day later, the swelling was almost completely gone.

Silver's usefulness as an anti-fungal/anti-bacterial agent in topical creams is pretty well documented, but I didn't expect it to do so much good against my own immune system's swelling response. Knowing that I'd want to keep using it to treat future bug bites, scrapes, and scars, I did some internet research on silver's toxicity. (MAN are there some crazy claims out there - AIDS cures and such) but I was reassured by the following statement on wikipedia:

"The reference dose, published by the United States Environmental Protection Agency in 1991, which recommends the estimated daily exposure that is unlikely to incur a appreciable risk of deleterious effects during a lifetime, is 5 µg/kg/d; meaning 5 microgram of silver per kilo of weight per person each day - about 1 liter of 10 ppm colloidal silver per month for a 66kg person."

Since the cream contains 24 ppm silver and since 1 liter is about 11 times as big as this 3 oz, container, you'd have to use up 4.6 of these 3 oz containers per month to reach that EPA recommended-safe exposure.

So I'm gonna keep on using this gel. Mosquitos, come and get me!

Edited to add: I now use this cream instead of moisterizer on my face, both morning and evening. The redness on my cheeks and a burst blood vessel (rosacea, I think) have faded quite a bit - the blood vessel in particular is completely invisible now. Who knew? I thought you could get those kind of results only with a laser!

title: Case cap is too loose - it opens up on its own, picks spill out. Not good. ** DO NOT BUY!!! **
text:
I strongly suggest that you DO NOT BUY THIS PRODUCT (unless you don't plan to go anywhere and don't mind just keeping it in one location as transporting it often allows it to come open on its own).
Although I love the picks themselves and have been buying them for years, it always has been a bit of a hassle figuring out how to stash a few. Couldn't really find a sanitary method, so when I came across this cute little Brushpick container I was excited to get one (or three as in my case). They came very quickly (I am a Prime member) and was anxious to try one of them out. The top of the case swivels and the holes line up and you can shake out a pick - good concept for pick delivery. Unfortunately, however, the thing did not want to stay in the closed position (it just turns and turns, going past the closed and then to the open and past the open positions, etc.). But, hoping that it was tight enough to attach to my key chain (one of the product's key selling points) I did just that - making sure that the top was turned to the closed position. To my dismay, however, I soon discovered that several picks had fallen out of the case onto my driveway - ugh. Later in the day, I received a text letting me know that three picks were found on the rug that morning.
So - in spite of its great concept, I had to return the product, virtually unused, due to the fact that it truly is a defective item.
*** I'll give you One Star - for product concept and quick delivery only. **

Maybe for a larger open area this would fit the bill, but for me it was a disappointment.

text:

First thing I noticed is that it does NOT come with the cleaning tool or moisturizing disk shown. Since I already had the cleaning tool, I didn't raise a stink over it.

The exterior of the pouch is well made for the price but the interior is a very cheap vinyl liner, I suspect it will tear at the upper seam at some point but that is just a guess. The storage compartment for the pipe itself is very small so you cannot really put the pipe and the cleaning tool in the compartment at the same time.

All in all, for the price it will work for me till I find a permanent replacement for my pouch that has more room for the pipe or better yet a separate spot to store the tool. But for now, 3 stars since it was about what I expected for the price.

title: They Laughed, But Who's Laughing Now?
text:
So, I splurged. On nail clippers. Mind you, I didn't get the $70 option, but I did spend far more than I ever had previously. On nail clippers. My wife scowled at me increduously, chuckled, rolled her eyes, and turned away dismissively.

I'm not a professional nail tech. I don't have any medical conditions that require special needs or infections for power tools to saw through. I'm just a guy who likes his nails to not scare small children and cause strangers to recoil in horror. And to impress people with my hygiene, like my beautiful wife who once appreciated how sharp I am but now clowns me for researching expensive nail clippers.

Yes, I did research. For nail clippers. Apparently, Japan does their typically excessive, impeccable work on personal hygiene products that involve cutting edges, like little katanas. These are Japanese, and are highly recommended by the review sites.

They're pretty, satin finish and curves and all, but the engineering is where it's at. Solid feel. Good weight. Great tension. And the cutting. Wow. There's something to this offset feathered edge technology. On regular drug store clippers that just means poor quality control and uneven, misaligned edges. Not here. This is some space age, intentional, genius-level paradigm shift in nail clipping. The included file is quite impressive, but you don't need it. Because it cuts so well.

And the little clipping catcher actually works, which boggles my mind because clippings usually shoot across the room *away from you* but it captures them inside, in the opposite direction.

One note (not a complaint): The research I did stated that this was best in class for larger clippers, which is what I was looking for. The type you can use on fingers and/or toes. Not the tiny ones for itty bitty baby nails or those giant, club-like toe nail clippers you could cut hedges with. That's what the M in the name is for, I assumed: Medium.

Well, these are large. Not unwieldy, two-handed monsters that look like a car jack, but larger than I'd expected (these replaced--and are larger than--some Revlon Sure Grips I had for a decade that were larger than most).

Maybe I'll let her use them. Or, maybe I'll be petty, roll my eyes, and chuckle. Nah, then I'd miss a chance to sing their praises and spread the nail clipping gospel...and justify my efforts.

title: Kidney stones are painful and this product is a little difficult to use when you're in pain
text: I developed a severe pain in my back a month ago. The pain was so bad that my spouse took me to the ER.  I've never felt such pain. After several hours of waiting which involved various levels of crying, moaning and pacing around the hospital room, I was sent for a CT scan. Subsequently,  the doctor diagnosed two 3mm kidney stones in my left ureter. The doctor gave me narcotics and sent me home. I ordered the SPECIAL PACK OF 3-Calculi Strainer Kidney Stone Collector so I could collect the stones when they passed.  Anyway, they come in a three pack. They are small, around 8" in diameter. You need to hold the collector in one hand and hold your business in the other hand. It is awkward, particularly when you're writhing in pain. Anyway, they work. The screen catches the stone. I would prefer a product, though, that fits or rests on the toilet rim, obviously a bigger product that I don't have to hold in my hand, a product that can stay put i.e. which I don't have to have handy and carry with me to the bathroom whenever the need to pee arises.

title: Excellent customer service and excellent product!
text:
Update: This company has excellent customer service and goes above and beyond to keep their customers happy. I had an issue with the first eyelash curler I recieved. The company reached out to me and quickly fixed the issue without any run around and made things right.

I have long natural eyelashes that don't like to stay up and I won't risk damaging them with traditional eyelash curlers that in the past have cut the tips off. The heated eyelash curler gets my eyelashes up there and they actually stay put for the entire day without damaging them or crimping them funny. I don't have to use as much mascara either. I have tried it with and without mascara. It works both ways but works much, much faster with a coat or 2 of mascara. In just 2-3 passes with mascara my eyelashes are up where I want them to be. It is a little unsettling having heat that close to my eyes and their is a slight learning curve but it's pretty self explanatory and you could get the results you want with a little patience. It heats up to full temperature in 1 minute or less so I don't turn it on until my eyelashes are dry and I'm ready to use it to try and save the battery.

My only complaint is that I wish the battery lasted longer. I can realistically get 3 uses out of it, but it does charge quickly so it's not a problem. The product absolutely does what it says it will do and functions the way the company describes it to so I would definitely recommend this product.

title: Carlsons Fish oil not what it used to be !!!
text:
I purchased this bottle of Carlsons Liquid Fish Oil recently. We have used it for years. Sadly the quality seems to have gone downhill. Why do they add sunflower oil as a stabilizer? That's not the biggest problem. They have changed the bottle cap several times. Instead of sticking with the plastic type cap they went to a cheap, flimsy metal cap that strips threads and is hard to remove from the metal seal. I've seen where people have cut themselves on the cap or can't remove it at all.

This particular bottle we were using caught my eye after I had been using it for a week or so. I'd been taking my regular amount and never looking too closely at the liquid. But one evening I notice something shiny and reflective inside the cap and in the liquid when the light hit it. I put it directly under bright lights and could see there were very small metallic shavings inside the cap. I have enclosed pictures so you can see what I'm referring to. The inside of the lid was disgusting! It looked like something off of the engine in my car. It was black grimy sludge with metal shavings.

I sent the pictures and my concern to Carlsons Laboratory directly. I have to say the customer service was a joke. They down played everything. Insisted it was nothing and refused to believe it contained metallic shavings. The pictures speak for themselves. It IS metallic inside the lid. To be treated like a person doesn't know what they are talking about and to patronize them is awful. I've been a nutritionist for years. I wont be recommending Carlson's Fish Oil anymore. Especially when customer service is insulting, and doesn't take concerns seriously. Yet they expected me to send the bottle back to them. They didn't seem overly concerned about anything I explained to them. At $40 a bottle, there are a lot of other fish oils on the market to consider using. I'm seeing lots of other complaints about the lid. Metal shavings and black grime in a product that customers are putting into their bodies is unacceptable.

Use at your own risk.

title: It is a good footrest but not great
text:
This is a good footrest. The massage balls are fun to play with. Assembly was not terrible -- it took maybe 15-20 minutes or so.

My major complaint with this footrest is that there is no way to make any of the positions "stationary." You cannot set a mode (say, completely horizontal) or at a partial degree without constantly balancing it with your feet. The footrest can only go completely to the bottom of one side or completely to the bottom of the other, and at such a steep angle it actually isn't very relaxing to use. I used one of the pins that came with it to stick inside of a loop that that created a kind of locking mechanism so I could get it to sit at a 45 degree angle down instead of full to the ground. That was helpful, but it was a kind of ad hoc measure to get it to a comfortable enough setting. I do wish you could "lock" it in at the horizontal level too.

Overall, it is a decent but not amazing footrest. The massage balls are nice, but it needs mechanisms to lock it into place when you find your perfect spot.

title: Great size for traveling, fits great in your bag!
text:
This sample tub of Alpha Lion is absolutely *perfect* for traveling. It's small size means it wont risk weighing your luggage down at the airport (I put it in checked bag) and assuming you're using 2 scoops per session it gives you about 7 days of preworkout, which is more than enough for a week or longer (depending how many days you workout) trip. Very great sizing and useful for short stints for work or vacation.

In terms of ingredient profile, its pretty run of the mill standard ingredients. I will say their citrulline malate 2:1 combo is slightly higher than most (7g instead of 6), but still a bit underdosed based on the 6-10g of pure l-citrulline effective min-max effective dosage. The rest of the ingredients are fairly common. AstraGin is a nice addition to this preworkout, which claims to boost absorption.

Hulk Juice as a FLAVOR was great. It's a kind of green apple flavor. If you like "green" flavors you'll enjoy this one. Not the most cost effective for bulk buying, but GREAT for travel. Would definitely buy in a pinch.

title: Tasty but not AS good as oatmeal cookie flavor
text:
I've become a major supporter of JYM protein after getting a tub of the plant-based oatmeal cookie flavor. Hats off to the team for being a little more creative with their plant-based flavoring profiles.

The pros:
1) tastes good
2) simple, clean ingredient profile
3) mixes easily in blender
4) look forward to drinking after a workout!

The cons:
1) moderately priced (not the cheapest on the market)
2) not AS tasty as the oatmeal cookie flavor (but still tasty!)

In short, I would highly recommend JYM's plant-based protein line to anyone escaping the clutches of dairy!

title: For a non-stim product, I like this a lot!
text:
This is a non-stim product, but despite the fact that you're not going to get any caffeine jitters (for those lacking the proper enzyme to metabolize caffeine the way I do!) it really does have a solid ingredient profile. I very much like the inclusion of Agmatine Sulfate, Norvaline, Nattokinase, and Stearoyl Vannillyamide. The green tea extract and Nitrosigine are nice boosts. The inclusion I could do without is the sodium -- in fact given how many of us have electrolyte imbalances and favor sodium over potassium, I'd prefer the latter if any were to be included. Very few of us need MORE sodium intake in our diets...

That said, the capsules are GOLD in color. My hunch is this isn't super healthy for us, but it certainly feels and looks cool downing 8 golden capsules! Really makes you feel like royalty before you tuck yourself in under the barbell on the bench press!

I generally cut the dosage in half and use alongside my main preworkout. It's a nice little booster.

title: Good multivitamin, but reeks and leaves a smell on your hand
text: This is a GOOD (not great, but GOOD) multivitamin with a strong ingredient profile. In general, I am conservative with multivitamins, given that my diet is pretty strong and diverse. I break these in half, and only use a half a pill per day (but you will still see a strong change in urine color an hour or so after using!). You can check the ingredient profile and compare with other multivitamins, and you'll see this one exceeds some of the other cheap multis on the market. That said, the SMELL is pretty atrocious, and if you leave it in your hand for even a second or two you'll have a smell on your hand that is pretty annoying -- I have to wash my hands every time I take one. The pill itself is fine and easy to swallow, but the smell is the only reason I couldn't award this 5 stars. It's a good value for the price, but the smell is a real drag!

title: Honestly the BEST tasting plant protein I've ever had
text: I don't often RAVE about the flavor of a protein powder, but the oatmeal cookie flavor protein is by far the single best tasting plant protein powder I've ever had. The industry has had many years to perfect whey protein flavoring schemes, but the plant protein genre has been suffering a bit in this regard. I don't know how JYM managed to make this plant protein taste so good, but they really accomplished something here. I might have trouble going back to anything else after this. THAT SAID, it is a bare bones plant protein -- you're not getting all the greens and random bells and whistles that other plant proteins try to jam in. But honestly, it is perfect as is. I don't begrudgingly down this shake after a workout, I look forward to it. It's a real treat.

As usual with puremedics, they have a solid product from their packing to the additional features that appeal to me being diary free, vegan friendly, nut free (for those that have allergies) and a few other things.

I can’t attest to if it actually boosted my immune system without a doctors test being done but I know quite a few if not all of the mushroom blends in this offer a wide range of things to boost your immune system among other things. I had no adverse reactions to it and took it daily with all my other pills with orange juice. Although it’s suggest to take water. I’d highly recommend this product if your immune compromised like myself or even if you struggle with some common cold or other issues. You have literally nothing to lose and puremedics customer support is great. Looking forward to whatever else puremedics puts out there. The suggested use was 1-2 times a day but I only took it once a day. If it was me, I’d take 1 a day to see how you fair with it before going to 2 a day.

I bought these to replace the insoles in my slippers. One side had a really rough texture which I assumed was intended to go on the bottom to prevent sliding. The otherside has slightly slippery texture. The foam doesn't reach all the way to the edge which I found rather annoying, and uncomfortable since my flat feet don't conform to the standard foot shape. I ended up turning them upside-down (rough side up) and putting the left in the right, and the right in the left, before putting my old flattened out insoles back on top. Made the slippers a bit snug, but much more comfortable for me this way.

UPDATE: a little over two weeks and these have gone completely flat and no longer provide any cushion. Keep looking folks, these aren't worth it.

title: Poor interface - Difficult to program
text:
We've had this scale for over a year now. This Aria scale (made by Fitbit) is designed t interact with your Fitbit device and log your weight into your Fitbit app automatically. Then it's supposed to keep your stats and help you achieve your weight goals.

Long story short, this device has the worst, most unnecessarily complicated interface I have ever encountered in my life. I am an IT guy, so it's not like I am unfamiliar with tech stuff.
When my wife and I finally got it programmed last year after at least an hour and a half, it did work.

Last night, my daughter decided to get on the Fitbit bandwagon. My wife and I got new Charge 2's so I gave my daughter my Fitbit Charge HR. When I tried to set up her Fitbit on the scale, it took an hour.

I have "connection unsuccessful" literally burned into my brain I've seen it so many times.
When we did get her setup (or so we thought) it recognized her and we thought all was well in Fitbit land. Wrong!

Now, my wife and I show up as "Guests" on the scale and my daughter shows up as me. She weighs a good 20 lbs less than I do so when she showed up on the scale as me, the app thought I had lost 20 lbs and sent me a congratulatory message. Threw my weight goals and planning right out the window.

Following me so far?

To setup a Fitbit to interact with the Aria scale, you have to remove a battery in the scale for 10 seconds to get to the setup menu. Then, you have a slim window of opportunity to make the connection. Since it takes so long to make the connection, the scale times out and you have to repeat the process all over again. After about an hour,I really, really wanted to throw the scale against the wall, but remembering how much is cost ($130.00), I decided I would refrain from this idea.

You are required to connect your device to the Aria wifi (it has its own) and upon doing this, you are then required to switch back to your regular wifi. Ridiculous interface.

If I had it to do over again, I would NEVER have purchased this overly and unnecessarily complicated device. Putting your weight into the Fitbit app manually is far easier than fighting with this Aria scale. This you can do with ANY scale.

Unless Fitbit and Aria get their act together, I suggest you do NOT buy this scale. It is just not worth the hassle.

I loved that it had multiple methods of whitening your teeth. The directions are simple: almost too simple at times. However, the product really works. I can see a difference in just these few days (though admittedly that difference is slight; it's a 14-day treatment). The strips are quite large, with the larger one for your top teeth and the smaller one for the bottom. The desensitizing gel works well; be sure to use it if you have somewhat sensitive teeth. The strips treatment doesn't hurt, but when I rinsed my mouth the first time I could feel it a little. Not so when I used the desensitizing gel.

The bamboo toothbrush is fun, with a soft head of bristles. The thing you get the most of is the whitening powder, which so far I am using whenever I brush my teeth. They don't quite tell you how do it: toothpaste first or second? I tried it both ways, and it's better for me to place a small amount of toothpaste on my toothbrush, then lightly dip (not scoop) it into the whitening powder. I expect that is at least a month's worth of powder or more, and it is great. Note: no matter what you do, when you first place it in your mouth, there will be a very fine powdery mist. Do not be alarmed. :). I'd recommend this product!

title: Fire Hazard?
text:
After about three and a half years of almost nightly use, this thing finally bit the dust in a big way. I always thought this machine ran a little warm, but seeing as how it is purely a mechanical device it didn't worry me much. As a side point, I now find it a little odd that nowhere can I find a power consumption rating for this, not even on the company website. What is this thing costing to run each night??

Anyway, a couple nights ago as my wife and I were going to sleep, the Dohm just stopped working, and shortly thereafter a cloud of stinky smoke started coming from it. Thankfully we were awake, unplugged it and removed it from the premises. What would have happened if we were sound asleep when this happened? I don't know, but I'm glad to not have found out.

I took it apart to see what happened, and I think it was the power supply that went bad. There was a black material surrounding it that was all melted so that must have been where the smoke was coming from.

Doesn't look like the one year warranty is going to cover this one! Now I'm hesitant about buying another one after this experience. While we very much enjoyed the soothing sound of the Dohm, I'm not sure I want to risk burning the house down with us inside of it while we are sound asleep thanks to said machine. It's a dilemma for sure. I think I'm going to look into other options.

Update: Just ordered the [[ASIN:B00E6D6LQY LectroFan - Fan Sound and White Noise Machine]] This is a lot of money to spend on a noise maker but I see a lot of positive reviews on it and compares favorably to the Dohm. And hopefully the fact that it does not having moving parts, presumably will require less power, and not threaten our lives, will be a plus.

title: mg per dropperful - calculation - for those wondering
text:
Just wanted to leave a note for those wondering because it's a little unclear on the bottle - a 2 oz. bottle typically has 59 droppersful - each dropper full is 1 ml (this is a 59 ml bottle so this would appear to be true for this bottle as well). In the answered questions, a seller stated there was approximately 30 g per bottle. If each dropperful is 1 mL, this would mean each dropperful contains approx. 508 mg, Hope that helps.

30g = 30,000mg
30,000mg/59mL = 508.4 mg/ 1 mL
1mL = 1 dropper
