title: Defies basic ergonomics for such an expensive product
text:
I am a person with rather severe arthritis and pain issues in my lower back and hips/pelvis. For some time, I had been looking for a seat cushion and a lumbar support - particularly to be used in the car because driving for any distance causes my quite a bit of pain in my lower back and bottom. When I saw Purple's products, I thought this was what I needed!

Unfortunately, I'm not particularly impressed with the seat cushion at all. I didn't cheap out and get the smallest: I chose the second largest one they had. But, it has no contours; it's just a square egg-crate seat cushion. Furthermore, the front edge of the cushion (with only the slightest attempt to taper the edges) is very uncomfortable on the back of my legs. The Purple cushion even takes AWAY the natural benefits of the contour of the seat below it. The whole cushion is just... strangely uncomfortable. Overall, I consider it a poor design and quite a waste of money. I have yet to find a purpose or place for it - but I do keep trying.

At the same time, I also ordered a lumbar pillow, with which I've had a bit more success. Ergonomically, It's too aggressive (meaning has too much material between the seat and your back) but it does seem to help some when I'm driving. Again, though, it being too thick on top of any lumbar support that is already part of the seat on which you are using it shows, I think, some lack of awareness of body ergonomics. I sincerely wish that The Lumbar pillow had receive just a bit more attention to design since it is a product for which I had a real need.

For both products, I do not believe that Purple lived up to it's own advertising or claims. I truly wish it had though. In retrospect, I should have returned the seat cushion at the very least. However, I missed that 30 day window, so my task now is to find a use for it only to keep it out of a landfill.

title: Nice oil for the price.
text:
Started doing aromatherapy mid April. Took two courses at a reputable aromatherapy school. Spend a lot of time reading and learning about essential oils and their uses. While I'm still a novice, I feel that I'm getting more knowledgeable every day. When I originally started to receive essential oils at a discount for an honest review from Amazon, I'd write about "red flags" and information one should know when looking for a company from which to buy oils. At this point, the major companies have started to have a lot of the information on the bottles and in the product descriptions--Latin name, safety information, method of extraction, where the plant material was grown, what it's used for, date of expiration. You no longer have to hunt for it. The only information I couldn't find is what part of the plant is distilled. I know that with all the Frankincense species, it's the gum resin.

I belong to several essential oil Facebook groups. Many of these groups rate essential oil companies--cream of the crop, very good and not worth your time or money. Much of the information is determined by the availability of information on the individual oils that can help determine the quality (whether or not they have the chemical constituents they are supposed to have at certain levels.) I buy most of my oils from two companies that are rated "very good." Have recently treated myself to oils from two of the "cream of the crop" companies. What I've started to do to evaluate some of these less expensive oils is to compare them to the oils from the "very good" companies.

There are three species of Boswellia essential oils--carteri, fereana and serrata, all of which own. I have one other Boswellia serrata. It's from one of the "very good" companies. At the time I purchased, they didn't have an organic Boswellia serrata, now they do. For me, I'm not sure that organic makes a big difference. The cold pressed citrus oils are the ones that I've read that you should buy organic. The US Organic Frankincense serrata smells identical to my other Frankincense serrata. I wouldn't hesitate to use this oil for any "safe" purpose--diffusing, appropriately diluted for topical use and in my cosmetics. (I don't ingest oils.)

I received this product at a discount for an honest review.

title: We tested it over a period of an hour and took several readings which were pretty consistent. It is also very accurate as to ...
text:
I purchased this BP monitor for my father-in-law who has CHF. The automatic cuff he has now fits over his upper arm and rarely produces a consistent report. This one is much easier for him to use and the fact that he just has to slip it over his wrist and hit a single button makes it practically fool proof. We tested it over a period of an hour and took several readings which were pretty consistent. It is also very accurate as to pulse rate. I also like the fact that it keeps an easy to use record of the last several readings. However, it really is designed for single user since there is no way to keep a record if it is being used by multiple users (of course wildly different readings can become obvious that two persons are being monitored). All in all a good machine and worthwhile for persons concerned about blood pressure.

It comes in a hard plastic case which looks like it will do a good job of protecting the device.

title: I don't believe this is fresh, active Moringa Powder and the company believes it is.
text: I bought my first bottle last month and was very excited to begin using it. The capsules I have contain light brown powder. The pictures in the ad on Amazon Prime are bright green powder. I have been taking it every day but haven't noticed any effects at all. I have arthritis and always seem to have low energy. I'd hoped it would help one of them. However I did more research online and found out that Moringa leaf powder has to be processed correctly so that it stays a bright green color. If it's brown, or light brown, it hasn't been processed correctly and is either contaminated or "dead". So I contacted the company but they said, "the moringa is absolutly fresh. The color is a little bit lighter because of the veggie capsule around. All nutrients are good"-direct quote. I don't believe them at all. So I am going to try to get my money back according to their policy. I am continuing to do more research and ask more questions about Moringa's freshness and what it should be like. But all the places I've researched so far have all stated that the powder must be green in order to be effective. I would caution people to do more research and not spend money until they really know more about it. I won't be purchasing from this company again though.

title: Great Concept But Misses The Mark (Literally)!
text:
First off my family really enjoys the Comfier brand. We have a few pieces of massage equipment from them that works great. That being said let’s talk about this Eye Massager.

The eye massager has some good qualities. This massager has four different modes that can easily be changed by its single button control. You can long press to turn on and off, with a short press to change modes, a double press to turn the heating option on or off and finally a triple press to stop the annoying music. It’s only display tells everything about the massager. It’s very easy to tell what mode, heating and charging display all on one display. The strap is very easy to use and adjust. Lastly the massager is a good build and is very easy to charge with the included charging cable.

Now let’s talk about it’s negatives. The massager massages my nose and not my eyes. Not sure who engineered this massager but it misses the whole point of being an eye massager. The music that’s preinstalled is very annoying. I would recommend turning that off immediately. Lastly my massager was making an annoying sound while on. This massager needs to be revamped to work like it should.

If your looking for a nose massager than this is the one for you. But if your looking for an eye massager then look elsewhere. We were very disappointed with this massager especially having other massagers by Comfier that work great.

title: Thrilled how well this is working for my dog!
text:
I bought this for my lab who in early February was already showing signs of environmental allergies. After seeing how miserable she was last year (the entire year) despite giving her regular treatment baths and increasing her allergy pills, I decided to try the bee pollen, which I had researched as a possible treatment.

I'm very happy to report that within a day of starting the bee pollen, she was not scratching at all. It's now been about two weeks and she is still doing great as I slowly increase her dosage.

I know vets suggest benadryl and all kinds of other non-natural treatments for allergies, but having killed a dog using conventional medicine prescribed by a vet, I choose to always look for safer, more natural ways to treat things.

If you do decide to try this for your dog, please do your homework. You should start out with just one granule at first, and slowly increase daily to make sure your dog doesn't have a negative reaction. Even with a very, very small dosage, I immediately noticed positive results in my 100 lb.+ lab.

If anything changes, I will update my review, but as of right now, before using dangerous drugs or prescription meds, I recommend anyone who has a dog with outdoor allergies to give this a try first.

I have a son who has undergone a Bone Marrow Transplant and is still on Immune Suppressors. His immune system is still not functioning at 100%, therefore, it is vital for my family to stay healthy. I am constantly on the search for decent and tasty immune support. And these NEW chewables from Emergen-C definitely hit the mark. The tablets are roughly the size of a quarter and the instructions are to take 2 per day (ages 14 and up). They are tangy and sweet. I was strongly reminded of the taste and texture of Sweet Tarts (except these are way better for you). These are also very convenient, you can take them anywhere and pop a couple in your mouth wherever you are. Overall, I LOVE the taste and highly prefer the chewables to the fizzy drink. And I can rest easy, knowing that my immune system has decent support.

I received a free sample of Emergen-C Immune+ with Vitamin D Chewables from Smiley360 in exchange for my honest review. All opinions expressed are mine alone.

title: Warm Hands at Last!
text:
I live in the North East, so winters can get quite chilly! For the last few months, my hands and feet have gotten *ice cold* indoors--even if the room temperature was quite warm. My husband would warm up a large homemade aromatherapy product intended for the neck and I would use that to warm my hands. It was awkward because it didn't fully surround my hands.

Well, I was THRILLED to receive the Bed Buddy Warming Mittens with Aromatherapy for Christmas from my dear hubby! They work fantastic! There are two fabric pouches that you remove from a pocket on the underside of the mittens. (The mittens are reversible, so you could conceivably put the warming side UP). After microwaving both for about a minute or so, you just re-insert the warm pouches and ouila! Warm hands!

The first time I used these warming mittens, I was surprised at how damp the insertable pouches made them feel. I wanted to be warm...not wet! So although they do say "moist heat", I noticed that the mittens stayed relatively drier for subsequent uses (so I didn't feel like my hands were covered by a hot, wet washcloth!)

The product information says that the aromatherapy ingredients that are within the warming pouches are eucalyptus, clove and cinnamon. To me, it smells more like a lemony cinnamon scent.

I am so pleased with the Bed Buddy Warming Mittens (which are a nice navy blue color) that I plan on ordering the slippers now! I bought a pair of down-filled slippers before Christmas (for $35!) to keep my feet warm and, although they do the job, I don't think they'd keep my feet nearly as warm as a product from Bed Buddy!

title: Installation
text: The installation is done with no written instructions.  The on line process for me failed at the last step too many times to count.  It seemed so easy.  Download an install program, run it and enjoy the results.  It was so frustrating to get to the last step that required fitbit contact on line and have the process stop dead.  I knew I was missing something, so I went back and read everything carefully without actually physically following the instructions.  What I missed was a poorly placed note to disconnect the Ethernet connection.  Counter intuitive when you are doing an on line install.  The install continued to fail until I noticed a small hole on the bottom of the scale.  There is no documentation on this, but I figured it might be a reset port.  Once reset, with the Ethernet connection removed the process via wireless Internet was smooth and fast.  Once set up the scale function is fun, but don't count on getting within a pound of your actual weight.  My Doctor's scale shows me 1.3 pounds heavier.  As long as the relative weight stays constant, I can live with applying 1.3 pounds to the Aria.  It is very modern looking and has a nice backlit digital display.  The input into the fitbit program works great on my MAC desktop, iPad, and iPhone.  After a delay, I did hear from tech support with a boilerplate response.  They never mentioned anything about the Ethernet disconnect or the reset port. I was really on my own.

Moreover, when mixed in after heating the oatmeal, it coats the oatmeal and prevents it from turning into organic concrete. I never need more than 1 teaspoonful with my breakfast. Not this version of yacon. It is too liquidy to coat anything and adds nothing - neither sweetness nor taste nor coating. It is absolutely awful.

Well, there is one advantage. When buying the other yacon syrups, I can pour the liquid contents into the nice glass jars, cut open the others' plastic bottles, dig out the hardened materials, and can mix the contents to my hearts content in this glass jar.

Biggest waste of $20 yet.

title: Excellent snipping ability.  Excellent value.  Not bulky.
text:
These clippers are a great value at about $4 for both finger and toe nail clippers. They are not bulky and are easy to grip. The small file area works better than I expected.

The key to a good nail clipper is:

1) A prominent 'triangle' area that forms the fulcrum of the lever that causes the clipping action.

2) A stiff pressure bar lever that you press on to clip nails. If the pressure bar flexes, you have to press much harder to clip a nail.

These clippers have stiff levers that efficiently transfer your finger pressure to the clipper cutting edges which makes clipping nails very easy. Some other more expensive clippers have pressure levers that flex and as a result do not trim nails properly.

These excellent clippers are comparable to some I have paid more for on Amazon.

title: Butyric acid really stinks--literally.  And yes, it is supposed to smell like vomit.
text:
This butyric acid by Ecological Formulas appears to have a great formulation. I learned that Butyric acid, also known as butter acid or valeric acid, is a chemical that has an odor smell of vomit. I was afraid that my tablets were rancid but was happy to learn they are supposed to smell like puke. Butyric acid, to me at least, smells very similar to Valerian root. They both really do stink.

When you take a butyric acid capsule out of the bottle, the smell even lingers on your hand. So, you probably do not want to put a couple of them in your pocket to take at lunch time. (Unless you want the people you work with to give you a wide berth.)
According to PubMed, this noxious smell is quite normal for butyric acid.
From PubMed website: "(PMID: 16460475) Butyric acid is a carboxylic acid found in rancid butter, Parmesan cheese, and vomit, and has an unpleasant odor and acrid taste, with a sweetish aftertaste (similar to ether)." Well, that sure explains a lot.

Edited on June 3, 2015:

I have tried so hard to love these bottles, but after months of use I am completely fed up with them. The price and the look is spot on - the functionality is AWFUL. The plastic is thin; after approximately 4 or 5 pumps the bottles begin to "suck in". Another Amazon reviewer stated it perfectly:

Also, the plastic ring between the tube and the pump top wrinkles, tears and gets mashed up after multiple threadings and un-threadings of the top. I really didn't want to spend a ton of money on foaming soap dispensers as I have five sinks in my house that need them, but this product was NOT the way to go. The saying is, "You get what you pay for." It's true.

I'm very disappointed with the long-term performance of these foaming soap dispensers.

title: Save Your Dollars!
text:
Shame on me rather than the maker of this cold remedy. I am stupid for buying into the hype.

I have used Sambucol (elderberry extract) in the past for colds with zero results and find that the added ingredients in the Sprouts Cold Remedy have no efficacy at all in stopping or lessening the discomfort of a common cold. Green tea leaf, myrrh gum or thyme (all ingredients listed in this 'remedy') have their uses but they are not anti-virals, expectorants or decongestants. Red root is supposed to soothe sore throats and aid in 'damp' conditions, but I doubt there is enough in the bottle to do that. Red clover herb is used for hot flashes. Why would it be in a cold remedy?!

While the taste is not unpleasant, the effects on my symptoms are nil and this 2 oz. bottle is seriously and exorbitantly over priced at almost $30. Maybe the placebo effect which I talk about in other product reviews is strong or maybe a lot of the reviewers, who got this for free or with a steep discount, feel they must falsely sing praises for something that will not hinder, but will also not help a cold sufferer.

title: Overrated
text:
I have been a huge fan of the FitBit since I got my first FitBit in 2009. So I was super psyched about the Aria and pre-ordered one from FitBit. Unfortunately, the Aria has left much to be desired.

First, the positives. It looks very cool and seems to be an accurate weight scale. After an initial bit of confusion, it synchronizes wirelessly fine for both users of the scale. And the online charts on the FitBit site are nice.

Now for the negatives. The body fat measuring portion scale is far from accurate. Even using the "lean" setting (since I am very active), the scale measures my body fat percentage 4-10% higher than reality. And the body fat percentage varies greatly, jumping 2-4% from day to day. It even varies this much if one steps off and then immediately steps back on. I realize that this scale is not to be compared with the types of equipment that professionals use to measure body fat, but I thought that this would give me a bit more accurate readings.

The bottom line is that it is a fine weight scale, but not a very good body fat scale. And if all that you want is a fine weight scale, save some money and buy the [[ASIN:B003XHVSBC Biggest Loser 7544bl Cal-max by Talor Wide Body Scale, 440-Pound]] for $40. The Taylor is a quality, accurate scale.

I wished I would have known this before I bought the Aria.

title: Easy to customize and effective!
text: I have been a grinder since I was a child. I have had 2 expensive, dentist made mouthpieces for this purpose: one where my bite changed and they needed to make a new one. The second one got thrown out by accident. So it's been a couple years now since I have used one, and a recent trip to the dentist informed me that I have grinded myself into 5k of damage, cracking teeth, loosening fillings, and completely flattening my back teeth now requiring a total bite adjustment. The mouth guard was going to be $900 and not covered by my insurance. I put it off until I woke up the other morning and the one side of my face extending past my ear and covering the whole side of my head was in excruciating pain. I could not even touch my skin or brush that side of my hair without wincing in pain. I found this mouthpiece on Amazon and I decided to give it a shot. I have seen several that appear to be nothing more than repurposed soft mouth whitening trays, and I chose this because it looked like a real mouth guard.  The product arrived containing two blue and white mouth guards, two storage cases, and what looked like a large, empty teabag (for dipping the mouth piece in hot water during the molding process). To mold the trays, you first heat water in a cup or bowl and submerge the mouthpiece in the water for about 12 seconds. You can use the teabag to easily dip it in and pull it out or you can just scoop it out with a spoon. As soon as you remove it from the hot water, quickly dry it and place it in your mouth against your top teeth and then bite down for 15 seconds. Then remove mouth guard and dip in cold water for 20 seconds to lock in the impression. The trays can be remolded again by repeating this process if necessary. They can also be trimmed or shortened with scissors to achieve a better fit. I found this process very easy and the product is very effective for me. I find as with any mouth guard, it takes some getting used to but it is doing its job and no more pain! Would definitely recommend to all of my fellow grinders out there! Disclaimer: I received this product for free or at a discount in exchange for an honest review.

It's true that this charger doesn't come with instructions, but it isn't hard at all to figure out on your own how it works so I didn't feel the need to knock stars off like some other reviewers. It's not super sturdy but not super flimsy either, and really how sturdy does it need to be when it is plugged into the wall all the time? title: Great product and lightning fast delivery.
text:
I have a 100 year old bungalow in Chicago, with a 50-60 year old slab patio next to the house. 25 years ago we added a semi-circular concrete slab to the older one, expanding the patio. Been loving it all this time but finally made the mistake of really looking at the patio. Pretty much green with algae . Since May and June of 2020 gave me lots of free time, I scrubbed both patios with 30 second cleaner (also a fine product), wire brushed the many spots where the algae was "barnacled" to the concrete and finished the whole thing with a power wash. Looked really good so I decided to seal it. Researched online and decided to go with a water based siliconate penetrating sealer. Foundation Armor SC25 was frequently recommended online so I bought 5 gallons.
IT WAS DELIVERED IN 2 DAYS! But the best parts were yet to come. Used a paint roller for super easy application. Panicked briefly when all manner of imperfections in the patio popped out when wetted.
Within a few hours, the patio zits all disappeared and the color normalized between the two patio surfaces.
(amazing since they are at least 25 years apart in age)
This morning my wife spilled a bucket of water on the deck and it ran off like it was a ducks back!
Great product, great service. Happy to write this review.

text:
I used this to apply self tanner to my back thinking it would be more efficient than using a towel (which I had been using). Turns out the towel method (the "free" method) is infinitely better. For starters, the foam pad does a horrible job at smoothing out the lotion. It is WAY too smooth and the lack of a frictional surface causes you to have to apply an intense amount of pressure just to be able to rub the lotion. Secondly, and by far the deal breaker in my eyes, the sides of the pads have a tough ridge. When rubbing the lotion along your back you will likely at some point use it at the wrong angle which causes the ridges of the pad to stab areas of your back. This is now only painful but also will leave your back covered in scratches. The handle is sturdy but because it is slightly arched you can't get any pressure on the pad when applying the lotion.

Overall this is a horrible product and I wouldn't recommend it to anyone trying to find a tool to apply lotion to their back with. You are much better off with the tried and true "towel method". Save yourself the pain, the frustration, and the money and avoid this product at all costs.

title: Life changing
text: This cream is INCREDIBLE!!! Literally life changing! I have been having issues with extreme dry skin on my face not just due to the occasional retinol use but in general. I was using another brand's HA serum for the last year and it wasn't helping despite also using squalane oil and another moisturizer. (HA should not be your sole moisturizer because while it does draw water from the air to your skin, it can also go the opposite way and dry you out if you don't use something to help seal it in.) So I found this cream thanks to a blogger and I will be a loyal user of this for the rest of my life. The consistency is perfect, you don't need a lot (I use a pea size), no smell/fragrance, it's affordable, and IT WORKS. It checks off every box for me. The price has gone up since I purchased it but I know a tube will last me months even if I use it 2-3 times a day so I'm not worried. I have heard to be careful because there are sellers that sell counterfeit but I believe mine is legit and will be sure to verify for my next order (a long time from now!). Seriously BUY THIS CREAM!!! The French definitely know what they are doing when it comes to skincare.

title: Works for UTIs as well as D-Mannose and a lot cheaper
text:
Yes, Mannitol does work to treat and keep away chronic UTIs, as well as D-Mannose, and is a lot cheaper, mainly because Mannitol has been used in the food industry for a long time as a sugar substitute, and is readily available in bulk quantities.

The original paper that described how and why both D-Mannose and D-Mannitol work was "Effect of Carbohydrates on Adherence of Escherichia coli to Human Urinary Tract Epithelial Cells" published in Infection and Immunity, Nov. 1980, p. 531-537. You can Google it and read it. Basically, most UTIs are caused by E. Coli, and E. Coli cause chronic UTIs that are hard to wipe out with antibiotics by adhering to the epithelial cells of the bladder. But, most E.Coli also readily bind both Mannose and Mannitol and this make them less adherent to the epithelial cells, and the E. Coli can then be washed away by drinking lots of fluids and emptying your bladder frequently.

Both Mannose and Mannitol are not absorbed as well as glucose/sucrose/fructose and both are also not metabolized to any extent. So they don't make you gain weight or make your diabetes worse.

The bad news is that some UTIs are not caused by E. Coli, and some strains of E. Coli do not bind either Mannose or Mannitol, so it doesn't always work for everybody.

Plus, ingesting a lot of sugars into your gut that don't get absorbed into your body leaves these sugars in your gut where the gut bacteria start digesting them, and this may cause loose stools or diarrhea, as well as lots and lots of gas. This does seem to improve with time, though, if you persist and let your gut flora adjust to it.

title: Didn't work for me
text:
I just tried out my bedfan today, and it didn't seem to work for me. I suspect part of the problem may be my foam mattress, though, so I'm not going to totally discount it as not working.

The design is dirt-simple, especially for a $80 piece of equipment. 2 x 10watt small fans which blow air up a plastic baffle. It comes out and gets deflected forward by a crossbar (the handle-looking thing on top). I have to admit that I was disappointed in paying $80 for 2 tiny fans with a plastic guide for the airflow, when I can get a $30 fan by Lasko with far, far more power and sturdiness.

Perhaps I'm asking a lot from it, but its 10 watt dual small fans were not powerful enough for me. They definitely puffed my sheets up - you could see that there was definitely air movement under the sheets, but I found that my apt is sufficiently hot that even when I laid directly on the puffed sheets adjacent to the fan, I didn't get any cooler at all. Again, it's possible that with my foam mattress, I sank so much that the air conduction simply went around me instead of under me, so this product may work very well for others who don't have Posturpedic-type foam mattresses.

On my defense however, I cranked the Bedfan up to max setting, and aimed it straight at me, with no sheets in the way. Much better than under the sheets for me, but still too weak for me to consider it for use.

There are a lot of positive testimonials on the vendor website and I couldn't find any negatives, so I may be the outlier here, but I did expect it to work a bit better than it did for me. Product will be mailed back to the vendor.

title: Good enough to do the job
text:
This set of a water flosser and electric toothbrush are good enough to do the job, but they aren't great.

It's 2023 and small devices like these should all use standardized charging connections. Why is there are barrel connector on the toothbrush and a weird proprietary connector on the flosser? Especially when the included charging cords connect to USB-A on the other end and chargers aren't included, this makes them seem really cheap. The charging connectors ought to be some USB format, or if they are going to be proprietary then at least make them magnetic so that the device can remain sealed and waterproof.

The brush works well and has different settings, but I think it's louder than others my family uses and has used in the past. Also, I think the bristles are too soft, as they are much softer than the standard ones that our Sonicare brushes use. This brings me to another point, which is that I don't know where one would get replacement heads. This toothbrush doesn't use heads that would fit a Sonicare, so once the included heads wear out, I'm not sure how to order replacements that I know would fit it.

The water flosser works okay. The user really needs to try to keep it upright in order to keep the water flowing, which makes it a pain, but that is just a result of the physical form factor where the water reservoir is built in to the wand. It doesn't put out the same amount of pressure as our Waterpik brand flossers always have, but that's only an issue if you want higher pressure. The nozzles aren't compatible with our Waterpik ones, or with any of the other generic ones that we have used in the past. So, like the toothbrush, once the nozzles all need to be replaced, then it probably means buying an entirely new unit as compatible replacement parts might be frustrating to locate.

For the combined price, these are still a decent value and do the job well enough, but for a little bit more you can get something that is designed better and uses standard and easily available replacement parts.

title: Amazing insole to provide good arch support
text:
Whatever I'll write in this review will not capture how impressed, overwhelmed and satisfied to have this memory shoe insole. I have back problems that all stems from my foot and I cannot wear any shoes I'd like unless they have special insole. I purchase this one as I do not want to be limited to shoes that have the appropriate insole rather I would like to use any shoes I want and just move the insole from one pair to another. I purchase this item for that purpose and I was so satisfied with the convenience of it. I order the 8.5-10 US size and there is a line to cut them to your appropriate side. It was very easy to follow the curvature of the cut for the right size of your shoes although I had to use a precision scissors for that. It fit the shoe properly and I put my leg into it and the feeling was so much different and better even more than the built in insole I use to purchase on my Nike snickers. The insole is made from soft memory foam and gel on the heels which absorb the foot strikes while walking and for me personally it relives back pains by walking properly. I wouldn’t say I can fly with this shoes or jump 20 feet in the air but this is the best insole I've ever used and I feel the absorption on every foot step I make. I would highly recommend this product even if you don’t have any back or leg problems as this upgrade any shoe you wear.

Disclaimer: I received the product from the seller at a discount in exchange for my honest and unbiased review of this product. I do believe that giving the most honest and reliable review may help other customers like me meet their expectations apriori and helps sellers improve their designs to meet the needs of their customers.

title: pro musician. prefers the longer stem.
text:
Middle aged pro musician.
Very good plugs. I have larger ear canal, and typically find triple flange plugs go in to far and become irritating and uncomfortable. I had used ER 20 and alpine plugs, as well as custom molded with etymotic filter. I prefer the long stem. The longer stem is not so long that you couldn't wear this under a helmet. The shorter stem is rather short. I have big bass playing fingers, and the longer stem helps me get a grip.

about custom plugs-
The custom ones are good - perhaps the best- BUT: I have had at least 5 custom plugs with mostly poor result considering the price. Sometimes they are cast poorly and don't seal in the canal; sometimes they are cut poorly for the filter, and the filter pops out or leaks. Sometimes there's a problem with the molds made at the lab. Not one pair of custom plugs have I had both a good seal in the canal and reliable filter seal/retention. And what happens when you lose one? You spend hundreds of dollars to do it all over again...
So I choose to save $100+ and buy these, replacing as necessary.

compared to comparable plugs- the ER20 and Alpine Musicsafe
The other plugs wear out faster than these. They also fit a little smaller. They all attenuate about the same, but I prefer the downbeat. The good case low price fur and durability stand out. I keep these on my keys. I can't do that with the others. The cases for the others don't hold up stay closed, etc.

The ER-20 and its siblings are triple flange, which I avoid for comfort reasons, but they are good. The Alpine are also good. I find them to be quite comfortable, but the tips wear out quickly, and require more frequent replacement than these downbeats. The Alpine case is similar, but made of plastic- it does not stay closed/on the keyring. Then they are gone. boo. Downbeats win.

Plus, here's a bonus for me- these buds fit perfectly on my etymotic earphones. I love those earphones- highly recommend*- but the tips wear out over time. I keep a pair of downbeats and my headphones in the same pack. Win.

title: Outstanding Bath Bombs bundle!
text:
Outstanding Bath Bombs bundle! I absolutely LOVE bath bombs. They make the bathing experience a million times more enjoyable, and they work wonders for my family's skin concerns. My son especially suffers from severe eczema, and bath bombs tend to make the water less harsh on his sensitive skin.

This bundle came with 50 bath bombs, so it definitely lasts a VERY good amount of time. Even in a household like mine where we have four frequent bath bomb users, this 50 pack is an extremely generous size especially at such an affordable price.

Speaking of price, these are more than worth the cost. I frequent high end bath bomb sellers like LUSH, as well as lesser quality substitutes you can find at convenience stores, and these are definitely closer to higher end quality. They float and fizz perfectly, and let off an amazing array of unique aromas that satisfy the soul and relax the mind.

They haven't caused us any irritation whatsoever as a result of use, and have actually really improved my son's eczema. They seem to let off a light oil that hydrates the skin very nicely. My favorite are the lavender and the coconut. My son prefers the blues and the greens, while my daughter adores all the pinks with their light rose and yummy cotton candy-like scents. My youngest just seems to like that they fizzle about and giggles at the show they make. I'm very pleased with the quality, and love the amazing assortment this bundle provides. I would absolutely buy again. Highly recommend them. (I received this product for free in exchange for an honest and unbiased review.)

title: Happier Feet After a Day in Heals
text:
I am not an everyday heel wearer but I do love wearing heels when the opportunity arrives. The problem is that my feet usually hurt after wearing them for a long time or I get blisters because I do not wear them all the time. I have used other products in the past but they always end up moving or not lasting so I have been looking for a long lasting solution. This is a heal kit that includes a toe cushion and a blister protector.

Pros:
-Thick pads
-Toe pads have a ridge for fitting
-Blister pad is thick and cover the whole shoe edge
-Very sticky backs
-Don't move once in place

Cons:
-A bit difficult to get into place
-Blister pad pushes foot slightly forward

These pads are thicker and have a more satin finish than others I have tried and that makes them more comfortable to wear. They have very sticky backs which is good for staying power but does make it a little bit difficult to get into place. The toe cushion with the ridge makes wearing the highest of heals comfortable. The blister cushion which is comfortable to wear and does work to prevent blisters after a long day of wearing your shoes, however the cushion pad does push your foot a bit forward so if your shoes are already tight these may not work. My feet are happier after wearing my heels with the pads in them.

I received this heal kit at a discount for my honest and unbiased review and opinion. Opinions expressed are mine and mine alone and may differ form yours.

Since that first interaction, we give it to her every night. Out of curiosity, I decided to try a drop myself, and found that it tastes great too. As far as the longer lasting effects of the vitamin D3 drops, I cannot quite say with absolute certainty. text:
The bandaids themselves are actually great bandaids. A little big but they're some of the better ones I've bought and delivery was pretty darn quick.. Looking at the pictures, however, I was under the impression that each box came with ALL FOUR types of bandaids.. not just one type per box. Now I HATE leaving anything but positive reviews unless west I got was really bad or not corrected if my order was messed up but I mean who buys character/designed bandaids to only get one style. Not to mention my kids mostly wanted the ghost and spider web one and we got a box of ONLY pumpkin ones. Description did state something along the lines of "style may vary" except looking at the pictures, I thought it meant the boxes were different. The box we got and the boxes in the pictured on amazon even has pictures of all the other designs which is why I'm a little frustrated because I believe these are being falsely advertised. And if you're only going to include one style band-aid, at least let the customer choose which one! Bought these because we just found out that my 7 year old has type 1 diabetes and now needs lots of finger pokes and insulin. He likes bandaids after the finger pokes so after he was discharged from the hospital I went and ordered like 5 different boxes and was excited for him to get them but am now disappointed. If somebody is reading this and decided to order some, either buy 4 boxes or just know that you're only getting one style per box.

I don't want a refund or to return the product because the bandaids are just fine and I would certainly change my review to 4 or 5 stars if this seller/store either mentioned in the description that each box only has one style or if they changed their boxes and included all four designs in each box so that nobody else is disappointed expecting variety and only getting one style.

title: Unacceptably Inaccurate
text:
I was really looking forward to using this product as I really like the concept.
But I find the flaws of this product unacceptable.
After using it for some time, I am very disappointed. The first thing I noticed was that my weight was always off by one or ~3 lbs versus the very good old scale I'd been using. I decided this wasn't that critical, and continued using it. Over the next few weight ins that the gap was inconsistent--sometimes I weighed more on the old scale, sometimes on the new scale, sometimes they were close to one another. More importantly, my weight changed by 2-4 lbs from one day to the next. As a longtime dieter, I attributed this to water gain and the like. What really got me, was when I tried to weigh myself multiple times within a minute or so. I tried this a few times, and the scale consistently showed different weights. Now this should NEVER happend to any decent scale. Even one that you can get for $20. This should certainly not ever happen to a scale that is sold for over $100. Importantly, this is not only a matter or principle (that expensive products should work right). Rather, any dieter knows that the motivation to continue depends strongly on seeing results. If one's results are all over the place even though I am being good about watching my food intake, exercising, etc., this really hurts my motivation.
I am very disappointed. This firm really needs to get its act together!

title: Pleasantly surprised that I like them so much!
text:
I was tired of the mesh loofah balls that I have been using for years. My skin is more sensitive and I have a rare skin condition that causes me to feel uncomfortable very easy. I also have arthritis and neurological conditions that make it challenging to hold a regular wash cloth. So, I ordered a variety of products to see which one I prefer best. After trying different sponges and loofahs, I ordered more of these. Here’s why:
Pros…1. Even though it’s silicone, the long bristles allow the body wash to lather and it holds the soap as you move to different parts of your body. Note that I tried a different silicone loofah sponge with shorter bristles and it did not lather up the same. Since the long bristles hold the soap, I use less soap than I did with the mesh loofah balls.
2. The bristles are very soft on my skin and don’t irritate it at all. The flip side is good to use when I have an area of skin that needs a little more elbow grease to clean. It’s actually good to remove the remnants of barrier cream and other medications, dry skin, etc.
3. These are so easy to keep clean. After my shower, I just put them on the 3rd rack of my dishwasher. It has a sanitizer cycle. The bristles don’t get completely dry, so I just let them finish drying on the drying rack. With the mesh loofah balls, I had to put in a mesh bag after each use, wash with my laundry, and hang to dry. With these, I know they are completely clean.
Cons…1 They don’t have a loop to hang up on a hook or to hold on your hand. It would make it easier to hold on to if there was a strap on the back to hold it on. It would also be easier to hang dry if there was a string to hold it up. I have cute decorative soap dishes that I put it on to dry in the shower, so I make it work.

title: Good vibrations
text:
I have been using this everyday for almost a week before I go to bed to help relax my tense neck and shoulder muscles. I work at a stressful office hunched over a keyboard all day so I got this to help remedy the tightness in my neck every night. There are some pros and cons but overall, I think it is effective and I will continue to use because it does help alleviate some of the soreness.
Here are some of the pros:
-It is simple to use and comes with clear instructions
-It is rechargeable so it is portable
-The battery life lasts long enough that I have used it once a week without recharging
-It is fairly small so it doesn't take up a lot of space
-It does help relax the neck muscles
-Each session is 15 minutes and is timed
Here are some of the cons:
-I didn't find the voice control to be useful
-If I use it without getting my neck a little moist, it will pinch a little (but that was me not following the instructions)

This massager does have a strong vibration, which can be adjusted according to the comfort level of the user. For me, because my muscles are so tight, I have to use the low level or it is uncomfortable. At first I didn't want to wet my neck as the instructions suggest. I am sure there is a good reason to do it, but a side benefit is that it keeps some of the wispy hair on my neck from getting pinched because it keeps it out of the way.

title: So many uses and great to have on hand
text:
This stuff is awesome. I have been using charcoal and coconut for different things, so it is nice to find a product that combines the two into one for more benefits. Usually I have charcoal capsules on hand to take in times of tummy upset and if I needed to, I could encapsulate this powder with veggie caps I keep on hand. There are such a wide array of uses for this versatile product and someday I will get to trying most of them. But for now, my family uses it for teeth brushing and as a detox/tummy soothing drink. There are some recipes right on the bag that explain how to use as a facial mask, detox lemonade, and simply adding teaspoon to a glass of water to help with stomach upset, bloating, and other digestive issues. We have been maxing the detox lemonade and to my surprise, my eleven and fourteen year old boys will drink it because they know it is good for them. We make it about once a week, sometimes two. The recipe is simple and we had everything on hand including fresh lemons. The drink looks almost black in color, but is more palatable than it looks. It has a little bit of grittiness, but not too bad. Another way we use it, is as a tooth powder. That is pretty self-explanatory, but the best advice I could give is to put a small amount in the tiniest plastic container and keep near your toothbrush, so when you are brushing your teeth, you aren't having to fiddle with the big bag, risking a messy spill. Wet the toothbrush and dip it in the powder. As others have suggested, you may want to brush with water and floss after brushing with the charcoal powder.
I received this item at a discount for an honest and impartial review. The observations and opinions expressed are solely my own.

text: Since I visited the Styrian region of Austria, I've been trying to find good pumpkin seed oil online.  I've found two brands that are sometimes great, sometimes not; they're from farming co-ops in Austria, and this is probably part of natural variation in seeds and seasons.  Still, I'm always looking for a good, consistent brand.  I must say this brand is one of the worst of the 8 that I've tried.  It should have a dark green color in the bottle (red only when more thinly dispersed), which it does not, and the flavor is not good--there's actually almost no flavor and what there is tastes "dusty" and "heavy/oily".  Good pumpkin seed oil is heavenly--such a warm, nutty flavor I cannot describe.  I'm debating whether to make myself use the bottle or, sadly, just pour it down the drain. But to my surprise this little rig does a very nice job although not unexpectedly it takes multiple passes. No nicks or irritaion either. :) For my purposes it fits the bill nicely. I certainly didn't need an upscale foil shaver from Braun or other major manufacturer.

So why just 4 stars and not 5? The little manual states that replacements accessories (e.g. foil head and cutter blades) should be replaced when worn and to "go to the designated service point for" them. There are NO service centers listed in the pamphlet NOR have my two requests here on Amazon to identify where replacements could be purchased been answered. I suppose that simply means that when the blades dull or foil rips this shaver is disposable. I find that unacceptable.

title: Like a Vacation for your Vagina
text:
Ladies. I'm not a huge menstrual pad fan in general. Overall, they make me feel sticky, hot and decidedly unclean in my nether region, during a week when I'm generally already not loving life. Nevertheless, I don't like wearing tampons all night long, so I've always viewed them as a necessary evil for nighttime.

Enter Honey Pot's Menstrual Pads. I got these as part of a BirchBox subscription, and chose them because they were both organic and from a black owned business, which are both big wins as far as I'm concerned. When I saw that they were mint infused, I thought that was an unexpected bonus, but I had NO IDEA what was coming my way.

It's like a mojito for your vagina. Calming, refreshing, and unexpectedly gooooooood. Like, so good you almost don't want to tell people how good they are because they might look at you askance. But you do anyway - because HOLY CRAP THESE FEEL AMAZING. And now you are the person that tells random women about how great your vagina feels after using a specific brand of pads.

Of course, vaginas are like fingerprints - no two are the same. So I hear those women who are saying that this minty sensation makes them feel like their vagina is on fire - but I'm not here for it. Maybe it's because my blessed ladyparts have seen their share of war (two kids, yo) but this mint is nothing but bliss to me. I've told everyone I know that still menstruates (and several people who don't even have a vagina) of how amazing this product is and I will continue to do so.

title: Works well, Setup HORRIBLE (Mac)
text:
Listen to the other reviews that talk about the awful setup method. If you don't mind doing something over and over 3-5 times, then get this, otherwise look for other wifi scale alternatives.

In a nutshell they require an APP to run to setup the scale (at least on a Mac they do) which tries to change your wifi network from home to scale and back. Well either the app is really poorly written, or well... or it's poorly written because it is able to make the Mac drop a network but not to connect to the scale.

You can try this and maybe you'll have better luck than I did, but using all recent (within 6 mo old) hardware there was just no way that this software would recognize the scale (although I could connect to the scale manually on wifi)

In the end I gave up, and used their web based wizard from an iPhone - which did work the first time through - probably becasue it wasn't trying to connect or disconnect the iPhone wifi, but rather gave instructions like "now change the network to the scale" waiting for you to manually do this.

Save yourself the trouble, and use a mobile browser - or just get a different scale.

Once I had it setup it seemed to work fine with measurements reasonably close to other scales I have.

title: Almost five stars - with a caveat
text:
First, the caveat: if you're looking for a perfect protein bar replacement that walks like a Quest bar, talks like a Quest bar, and tastes like a Quest bar... while ALSO demanding it be paleo, non-dairy, low carb, and grain-free, you're just not going to find it. Science isn't there yet. If you don't want the fillers and blood sugar rush and everything else that comes with mainstream whey protein bars you're just going to have to suck it up and accept it's going to be a different experience. That said, these are decently tasty for what they are.

Texture: Julian Bakery could probably get fewer negative reactions if they advertised from the get-go that these are taffy-ish in consistency, rather than insisting on calling them "cake like." Taffy's pretty good. Trying to soften the blow and appeal to the Quest bar crowd will get you nowhere, they are what they are. So they lose a star for willfully bad advertising.

Flavor: I wouldn't call this a truly convincing caramel flavor, it's a bit more like sugar-free caramel syrup flavoring... but asking a non-dairy/low carb bar to taste exactly like something that's literally heated milk/sugars is a pretty tall order. If you're sensitive to whey products or on a dairy-free keto diet you could do a lot worse than these.

title: If you need "123" batteries, be sure to shop around to find the best price for the quantity you need
text:
Hey, they're batteries! We needed to replace the "123" lithium battery for a weather station. Since that was the last one we had, we immediately shopped to buy some more. This was the best deal at the moment for a reasonable quantity. Six batteries should last us for about a year or two; we don't have too many devices that use the "123" size. It didn't make sense to buy more and have them sit around.

We like the Energizer "123" batteries, because they last a long time. We are consistently satisfied with Energizer.

Hint: Be sure to shop around on Amazon every time you buy these! So many sellers offer Energizer "123" batteries at an incredible range of prices. There's no rhyme or reason to it. Be sure to look at the whole price, including the batteries, shipping, and tax, because some sellers offer a low per-battery price and then nail you on shipping.

title: [Updated] NOT GOOD for SIDE SLEEPERS
text:
March 23, 2015 Update:

I had to purchase another one because the original pillow lost volume over the years (the millet probably crushed into powder). The new version of this pillow has MUCH LESS MILLET inside, making it a lighter and flatter pillow than before that is NOT GOOD FOR SIDE SLEEPERS.

You cannot change the volume of the millet yourself because the pillow sealed the millet seed compartment. You have to be handy as a tailor and have a sewing machine to undo the seams and later repair the hole.

As a side sleeper, I buy several pillows every year since all the pillows I buy start too high then flattens out over time. My search is over: the Serenity Pillow has left me without neck pain since I've used it. The wool/cotton cover over the millet softens the firmness of the grain so it's not uncomfortable. There is a faint millet/grain smell but it doesn't bother me.

The only concern I have is the wool/cotton cover is fairly warm -- good during the winter months -- but I wonder if it will be too hot during the summer. Only time will tell.

UPDATE February 11, 2012:

It's still a great pillow, BUT the pillow case has stretched out so the grain has more room to move and the pillow will flatten out a little. This pillow does not flatten out like normal poly-fill/foam pillows because the pillow is still very firm.

I may try to sew the end of the casing shorter to make the pillow full again.

The grainy smell went away (for any of you who are interested).

When I opened up the bag it had a very strong aroma of campfire, the smell is so strong that they have been airing out for 5 days and the smell is still there just as strong as it was before. The pair I put on my shoes made my whole closet smell like campfire within a day and the smell started coming out making my bedroom smell like campfire. Those shoes even though I took this anti slip pads off 3 days ago still smell like fresh campfire very strong. If you like the smell of campfire and don't mind it on your shoes and permeating your clothes in your closet (if you keep your shoes in your closet) then these would work OK for you if you glued them onto your shoes, if you don't like the smell of campfire I'd avoid them.

title: Good scale, effortless uploads, user recognition okay
text:
I am a new owner of a Fitbit Aria, and I love it, for the most part.

It has all of the standard accuracy of other scales I've tried with the same weight and body fat capabilities, with little-to-no fluctuation of weight if I step off the scale and measure again five minutes later.

It is beautiful, and it cleans easily. It is heavier than it looks, and it feels like it will last a long time.

WiFi setup was very easy, and all of the data has been available on the Fitbit site immediately.

For users with very different weights, the user recognition is excellent. However, my husband and I are about 6 lbs apart, and it gets us mixed up (easily fixed from the dashboard for recording purposes). It would be nice if it could take a little more into account in determining the user. For example, if we weigh at the same time each day, chances are good that we each match with the one that we were closest to the day before, not the one 5+ lbs different. Additionally, our body fat percentages are very different, so I don't think it is using that to help determine user.

That being said, our daughter and my best friend are about 100 lbs lighter/heavier than we are, and it recognizes them with no trouble, so this shouldn't be an issue in households with more varied weight. I will update again as to whether users are still confused around 10 lbs of weight difference.

Bottom line: The scale is worth it, with just one flaw that takes about 10 seconds to fix via the Fitbit website.

title: Smart...doorstop?
text:
Nothing makes a fat guy more angry than when his network smart scale doesn't work. It connected fairly easily, however when attempting to weigh myself I was getting "Sensing....Step....Sensing....Step" I diligently read through blogs and reviews that this issue does occur. I tried the recommendations, pull the battery...wait, reset button, reconnect to the network but nothing worked. Pretty much the end game to this issue appears to be "contact customer service". Yahh right... Sent it back to Amazon.

One comment I read was that the weight cell can get out of calibration during shipping. Made me wonder why there wasn't a lock out to prevent damage/calibration issues in shipping.

Other than the above issues, it really is a fine scale. Appears to be made well and looks great, better than i expected. But, if it doesn't work, its not much more than a door stop.

Update: returned device. Already got a new one.... Yeah AMAZON !!!!!!!!! Went through the wireless link up and it works beautifully !!! My hypothesis ??? .... Weight cell suceptable to damage... Packaging has no foam impact protection or sensor damage protection aka lock out device to prevent platter from hammering the sensors. If you get the above error I would return it. Don't waste your time with their customer service . I read a lot of comments about the above issue and Fitbit has never as far as I've read admitted that it is their device that may be defective. So sorry to say I'm keeping my review at 2 stars . I'm sure the Fitbit allergy issue was expensive for them. If I was the ceo I would not want to go through that headache again. LOL

Ok... Ok. Fitbit threatened my family and so I have changed my review to 4 stars. I'm totally kidding about that. After using it for a day I am impressed. It really is a great scale, well built and if you read the directions it is very easy to set up. I realized I was frustrated with the scale error issue and still am dubious about the fragility of the sensor so I made my review one star short of perfect. Fitbit really needs to address packaging. What changed my mind are two things:

1) If you can't set this thing up you are:(based on me reading other reviews)
a) A complete moron
b) Are having an issue with your network
c) Don't read directions (like most of us)
2) Fitbit really did go out of their way to email me back quickly regarding fixing the issue. I just chose not to spend the time with their customer service

title: Perfect light for the Kindle 2
text:
This light is the perfect size and shape and weight for the Kindle 2. We have two of these lights. It has just the right amount of light at the high setting, and a perfect, non-glare pattern on the page.

The batteries need replacing or recharging every few days. We use rechargable batteries, so we just plug in every few days to recharge.

We travel frequently, so the small size and provided carrying bag is very nice. We use a small footprint Phillips surge protector/plug in specially sized for traveling (available at Wal Mart for $22) with 3 standard AC plugs and 2 usb recharge plugs, because we find that sometimes where we travel good plugs are hard to find. This way we can plug in two lights and 2 kindles and 1 phone to recharge all at one time.

Contrary to some reports, we find that the Verilux book light is quite sturdy, as these types of lights go. The only improvement we can think of would be to put a little led light on the light (similar to the Kindle 2) , so that one knows when fully recharged.

We have used our light for about a month now, and are still quite pleased with this product.

This product is made in Barcelona, Spain with all natural ingredients, Paraben free, Animal cruelty free, Consciously sourced. On sale for twenty bucks it is worth a try. Being the scaredy cat I am the first time I tried this was after shaving but before my shower so I could rinse it off if needed. I was extremely pleased. The scent is mainly peppermint and eucalyptus and not over powering which was also important to me sense I am using it in my moustache which is a tad bit closer to the nose than a beard. The consistency was slightly thinner than the Avida lotion I typically use but not so thin as to feel oily. The balm quickly absorbed into my skin and moustache and left a smooth feel that was in no way oily. There is no alcohol to sting or dry your skin. I am very pleased with this product and will continue to use it so long as it is in the twenty to twenty-five dollar range. At forty bucks I would likely revert back to my lotion. All in all, I really like this brush, and am happy that I can straighten my hair in just minutes! We were running late one morning, so I spent about five minutes with it and had much smoother hair. Typically, I'd spend more time, but happy to have a styling tool that works for super quick touch ups. Busy moms can always use that!!

title: Binchotan works pretty well. Dallas water without any carbon filtration is ...
text: I've ordered three of these.  Each time, you get a big piece and a small piece.  Binchotan works pretty well.  Dallas water without any carbon filtration is a bit icky-- not horrible, but certainly not a pristine mountain stream (and I *have* tasted pristine mountain streams, so I know whereof I speak).  By allowing these to soak for 2 to 6 hours, the water that you get is indistinguishable in taste from a more traditional plastic-based carbon filter.  So, it's not as fast, but if you hate the chemical and environmental and endocrine-harming properties of plastic like I do, the trade-off in speed is more than acceptable.  The calculus you have to engage in is that because of the slower throughput, the longer soak time, if you're using this to retire a 70-ounce plastic filter carafe, you should plan on having at least 140 ounces of glass/stainless steel bottles (and a corresponding # of carbon sticks) so that one can be soaking at all times.  So, it's a 2x trade-off.  But again, well worth it.

title: Easy to use, right size, best of 3 arm slings tried for this average sized man
text:
I picked up the Walmart branded arm sling the day I got hurt. It was massively too big with the arm pocket extending to my fingertips and the strap around my shoulder was so long, doubled over it was still too long. This is not to mention the contortions required to attach the strap with a painful shoulder. I think you would need to be 7 feet tall with a chest the size of a giant for this arm sling to be an appropriate size.

The second one was an Amazon SLR Products model. Overall this one is a good arm sling with the only little nit being the arm strap being a tad long without enough adjustment to get my arm to a "level" position or slightly higher to take the stress of my shoulder joint. The strap attachment at the wrist was easy to use unlike the option above from the big box store.

This Copper Compression arm sling is just right for this Medium size T-shirt/Polo wearing man of average build and height. It has by far the best adjustment system and range of adjustment. I cannot speak to the Pro's and Con's of the copper aspect other than to say it seems to be anti-microbial and has not picked up any weird smells or odors after nearly a week of use. Whether copper is doing anything else is an unknown to me at this time so I will defer to people more knowledgable than I regarding the benefits of copper in injury recovery. The strap adjustment system is easy to use and sized reasonably. The strap is split at the neck and relieves any pressure and, it lets the skin breathe so it doesn't get sweaty there. It is super easy to put on and take off using one hand and is as good as it gets with shoulder pain.

**--**--** Update after recovery December 31, 2019

The Copper Compression Arm Sling is the best arm sling I used. The runner up, SLR Products model was nearly as good but, to be honest after using the Copper Compression Arm Sling I never put it back on. The Copper Compression Arm Sling just worked better for my body size and profile. For the price, quality, and performance I can honestly say this was the best one I tried and it helped me heal faster with less discomfort and pain. Highly recommended!

title: These chinstraps work for me!
text: These are very nice well made chip straps. I have used cpap for years, so I am picky about my chin straps. They have to be comfortable, of course, but also made to fit at the correct angle to provide secure closure of your jaw. The velco adjustment needs to be flexible with a lot of adjustment. These two straps work very well and accomplish the desired result. Both are made of neoprene which can be a little on the warm side, but neoprene is more forgiving in the fit to your head and jaw closure success. Chin straps made of cotton work well at first, but over time become stretched out and wear out a lot faster. The main thing to pay attention to with all chinstraps is how secure it closes your jaw. If the closure is not secure, you will snore or if using cpap, there will be leaks. I like these straps and will be buying more in the future. The price is good and the quality is good. I received this product at a discount for an honest review. A product reviewed by me is not swayed by a discount. Some products, in my opinion, are good and some not worth the money. I will always be honest. I also rely on product reviews for items I purchase and believe that a good, honest review is a valuable tool to ensure I get my money’s worth from products that I purchase.

title: Superior product helps save money.
text:
We can't be without our cling wrap by Kirkland! This is my third roll which I expect to last about 2 &1/2 to 3 years. I buy meat in bulk and break it down to serving sizes, wrapping each individually. Large roasts are broken down to smaller ones (there is just two of us) bulk hamburger is broken down to make patties and half lb portion then all put into a large heavy zip lock bag and into the freezer.. Bulk chicken is portioned out, some breasts pounded down for cutlets others cut in strips for other dishes, each wrapped separately and again stored in large heavy duty zip lock freezer bags. It sound like a lot of trouble, but it goes quite quickly and your all set to pull out just what you need to make a quick meal for as many people you'll be serving. AND you save money buying bulk meat.

The product is thicker than usual and really stretches to make a very tight seal. Should it tangle a bit, it's pretty easy to untangle. Not like that flimsy stuff you're probably balling up and angerly throwing away.

The box IS big and bulky so I camouflage it. First one I painted white. Second one I wallpapered. Use your imagination. Maybe you can match your cabinets, find interesting design paper or fronts from seed packets. My daughter-in-law is fortunate enough to have a deep top drawer so she stations the box in the front of the drawer and only need to pull the drawer open, remove what she need and close the drawer.

Pretty much the only thing I like about this mask is the size. I am large (6'4"), so I have a hard time finding masks that cover and are comfortable. This mask fits that bill. Now the down side:
It's hot. This is by far the hottest mask I own. I sweat profusely under it.
It is not easy breathing. I find myself actually pulling for air when I breathe in this mask.
The filter pocket is a joke. The pocket goes across the whole mask, but is too big for the standard PM2 filter, so the filter slips and you don't have total filtration, if any. This is something they conveniently leave off the advertisement.
There is no nose clip, so my glasses were constantly fogging.
The quality is not great. Mine is kind of lop-sided, so when I try to get it comfortable, the ear loops pull off my ears.

I'm not going to be using this mask very much. I can't recommend it to other people.

title: Kind of Big for Smaller People
text: I  like the idea of this traction device. It helps take the pressure off of my neck. However, the sticky side of the velcro straps isn't long enough to hold it in place around my neck. The sticky side of the velcro is only a few inches long on the neck straps, whereas the soft side of the velcro runs very long. What happens is the velcro doesn't have a strong enough hold, because the sticky side isn't long enough to get full adhesion, so the straps pop open while the device is around my neck and fully inflated. The other size issue is that the brace slides up over my chin, so that the rim of the brace, which holds the neck up, suddenly loses it grip. It's uncomfortable to say the least. I've tried turning the brace sideways, which helped with the neck tension, but aggravated my TMJ. So that is not a viable option for more than very occasional use. Had the manufacturer made the velcro strips the same size, smaller people like me might find this product more helpful.

title: Mismatched case with loose top slider
text:
I was disappointed upon receipt of this case for 3 reasons:1) The top slider tab was loose, creating a problem of tobacco and cigarettes falling into my purse, making a mess and breaking cigarettes jumbling around in my purse. 2) The top and bottom also fitted together too loosely and the patterns did not match. 3) The seller told me "that's the way they come (for the mismatched pattern between top and bottom)we'll be happy to exchange it for another product for you if you ship it back."
I guess that is OK...except who wants to waste their time and money on shipping and packaging returning a low quality product, possibly only to obtain another low quality product? As a business person, I would have replaced the item at no charge to the buyer without making them go through all of the hassle of re-packaging and returning. It just makes better marketing and business sense because the customer has already lost faith in the seller and his/her products. I am a creative artist so I made my own solutions: I glued an attractive drawing (made on business card stock thick paper) to tighten the fit between top and bottom and bent the top loose slider a bit upward to make it stop leaking out all of my smokes. If you are a guy that just keeps your smokes in your top shirt pocket, this item will probably work out for you. It did not work for me until I modified it. That's what we get for all of these made in China low prices.

text: Very easy to do and the results were better than expected. I did a 2012 Sienna & 2013 Tundra using a foam lance and I was able to do both in no time at all. title: Great stuff.  Goes down easy and helps lower cholesterol levels!
text: This stuff is great.  It has a light lemony taste and it goes down surprisingly easy for liquid fish oil.  Two tablespoons a day have significantly lowered my triglycerides and LDL (the bad cholesterol).  The one thing it doesn't appear to do is raise the HDL or good cholesterol.  But I'm very satisfied with it.  I tried this over the course of a year by using only this fish oil and no other supplements other than a multivitamin.  The first cholesterol check at the beginning of the year was my baseline measurement.  After six months of one tablespoon per day, the triglycerides and LDL levels went down some but not as much as I would have liked.  At the end of one year I went back to the doctor for another set of tests.  From the six months to one year test I increased my oil intake to two tablespoons per day (with meals) and my triglycerides dropped to a nearly normal range while the LDL went down as well.  Of course, this is only an aid to good cholesterol health and not a cure all.  Diet and exercise are always the two main staples of good health, but this fish oil can greatly assist you along the way.  Good luck and good health!

My first 45 years I lived in the quiet suburbs, Mayberry type quiet. I then moved to downtown Seattle, one block off of Pike Place Market. Bad move. I've since moved back to the burbs for a few years now but the sleep issue unexpectedly followed me. Fall asleep around 11 pm and wake up at 3. At least it was one continuous block of time. My body became accustomed to the sleeping pills and they were no longer effective. Nothing worked. Then I found this Tryptophan and all I can say is it is awesome, awesome, awesome! I'm getting at least eight hours of sleep a night and there is absolutely no grogginess when I wake up. I wake up alert and well rested. This is the thing that finally works for me.

title: tattoo machine review
text:
I was quite impressed with this kit. the four machines it came with are all set up for different things such as lining and shading and what not. I have had no problems with the power source so far. the ink like everyone says sucks its good for practicing on grapefruit or pork skin, but I recommend purchasing some ink wen you move to tattooing on people. the video that comes with the kit is pretty funny, especially the sweet cat tattoo he does.(you can find helpful videos youtube) the practice skin is a joke in my opinion, if you use it make sure you have vasiline on it or the ink will just smudge on it permanently, it still will though anyway. color didn't really work well on it either. but it is good for practicing you line work it has some flash art already on it. I'd maybe use it without ink just to get a feel for the machines.

please keep in mind that nothing in this kit is sterile except for the needles in the packages. so you need to sterilize the tips and tubes, even the disposable tips and tubes.

I'd also recommend getting better parts for the machines in the future like springs and coils, but they do the job for now.

you also need to get lots of other stuff like green soap and more gloves and what not.

I've done a few tattoo's on myself and friends and so far so good.

just keep in mind you need to learn how to keep things sterile to protect yourself and others, as well as setting your needle depths so your not giving people blood poisoning or bad tatts.

title: Huge fan! Works and save a ton of money in between drycleaner visits! Read my review for tips.
text: Huge fan! Just started trying this at a coworker's suggestion. She's been using it and told me how much she saves in between drycleaning visits. I have an expensive Ellen Tracy dress that is white, black, green and blue fabrics sewn together. My regular drycleaner wouldn't clean it because she said the fabric colors might run because it said to use hydrocarbon dryclean only. I had worn it a dozen times and it needed to be freshened up so I took a chance and used one of these cloths on medium heat for 15 minutes in the dryer with just the dress by itself. It didn't run the colors and came out smelling so much fresher. There were still some faint stains around the inside of the top collar. I might try the pre-treat on the inside of the lining next time to see if it will remove the stains without discoloring the fabric. Tip: Try cleaning multiple garments of the same color family at one time but don't do more than 4 or 5 at once. I also used it with four items that were khaki color (3 pants and one blouse) for 20 minutes and they came out freshened up nicely. I also tried it on a business jacket, jeans, and thin sweater for 20 minutes. I love drycleaning my jeans because then they don't shrink and get out of shape. This product will not press your clothes. You can however use an iron on the lowest setting possible without steam and a sheet in between to avoid the shiny effect when ironing a dryclean only item. Just don't get a garment marked dryclean only wet. If it's a cotton dress shirt or garment that you can wash like jeans, then you can definitely iron it on low setting without any issues at all to get out the wrinkles. Another tip - don't try to press seams at the same time, do them each separately. Love this product and will be buying it in between the drycleaner visits to save money! It's easy too - just throw in the dryer on medium heat with the cloth and that's all there is to it.
