title: Seems to Work Well, wish it had less scent.
text: We are in the midst of a sunny and hot holiday weekend (4th of July) in hot and VERY BUGGY Minnesota. We participated in numerous outdoor activities with our friends, from kayaking the chain of beautiful lakes inside Minneapolis, to spending a day on a pontoon on a private lake with other groups. We used this lotion at the onset of each day's activities and it seemed to work well for very many hours without a need to re-apply, even though we were playing on or in water all day, every day. I neglected to apply it to my shins for the kayaking event, and I was sunburned below the knees (my bad planning, as I was expecting a different kayak design than we rented and the opening exposed my lower legs to the sun). I did not have sunburn anywhere that I applied the lotion. The next day and night, when playing at a private lake outside the Twin Cities, the bugs were more plentiful than I have (almost) ever seen, probably due to an excessively wet season here in the Land of 10,000 Lakes. Bug deterrant is a #1 conversation here, where the mosquitoes can strip you of at least 10 pounds of unwanted (along with your essential) flesh per hour if you are not slathered in DEET and gasping for breath and dying along with the bugs you hope to deter. Anyway, after several days and evening in the great outdoors, after using this Avon lotion, I came away with only TWO bug bites, and I think my partner (who also used this Avon lotion), had none.  Our friends and companions, who did not use this lotion, were ravaged by bugs early and had to run, screaming and swatting, to the house in retreat as soon as the sun set. The lotion was easy to carry and did not come unopened when tossed about. A smaller 'hole' design in the bottle that could be clipped on with a small caribeaner (spelling??) would have been nice.  You have to shake the bottle to mix the ingredients before applying. It rubs on smoothly and seems to absorb and stay on without a mess, although you will be able to feel it on your skin until you shower it off. We were not aware of any side effects of using it, although we are both somewhat have a sensitivity to strong odors or scents, and we would give this a 5 if it had much less odor. That said, the smell of this lotion is much less offensive than other bug sprays that have made me sick in my lifetime. Another advantage is being able to carry just one bottle instead of two or three on your outdoor excursions. THAT is probably why we made it through the weekend with less sunburn and bug bites than our friends. They were applying lotions, one or the other, throughout the day. I am thinking that this might be a good gift to buy for our friends. Most importantly, combining lotion functions into fewer lotions uses less planetary resources and creates less pollution than producing only one-function lotions.  If the packaging was made from renewable resources and used renewable energy for manufacturing, plus if the bottle was 100% bio-degradable, I would rate the product a 10 and would buy stock in the company. Is anybody listening?

title: This Has Proven to be Quite Effective for Us
text:
My wife and I are in our seventies. We live in a 112 year old Victorian home in northern Illinois which, along with its ambience and charm, comes complete with over a century of accumulated dust, dander, pollen and whatever else has wafted its way. We also have two long-haired dogs - a Sheltie and a Golden Retriever. I will warn you up front that I really appreciate those reviewers who actually tell me something about their experience with a product so I always try to do the same. This means I tend to write detailed and lengthy reviews, so if you expect to learn about our experience strap in and get comfortable.

My wife has developed a problem that seems to worsen when the weather gets cold and we find ourselves spending more time indoors during the winter: she tends to suffer from nasal and sinus congestion which seems to be particularly acute in the mornings. Over the counter congestion remedies help, but the condition is chronic and quite frustrating.

As we entered another winter I began thinking about things I may be able to do to help alleviate the problem and I came upon the idea of trying an air ionizer in our bedroom. I had a passing familiarity with ionizers and the reviews for this particular product were good so I ordered one. I didn't tell her about it - I just got it and plugged it in. Within two days I noticed - and she did as well - that she was no longer waking up congested.

Now, understand that I am a lifelong skeptic. I am prone to approach any "new" or "Improved" development - especially when it happens to be involved in the process of trying to sell me something - with more than a little bit of a jaundiced eye. I want to be able to understand it. If you're trying to sell me something, I want you to be able to prove to me that it works. So when this seemed to have a rather dramatic positive effect I did what I should have, by nature, done in the first place: I conducted a bit of research.

And I discovered something fairly rare. The information on air ionizers is muddy at best. The best I can do to illustrate this is to reference two points offered in the Wikipedia entry for air ionizers. Air ionizers work by producing negative ions (anions) which are electrostatically attracted to particles in the air. These charged particles are then attracted to a nearby grounding surface such as a filter, a wall or a floor, removing them from the air we breathe. A portion of the Wikipedia article states:

"The frequency of nosocomial infections in British hospitals prompted the National Health Service (NHS) to research the effectiveness of anions for air purification, finding that repeated airborne acinetobacter infections in a ward were eliminated by the installation of a negative air ioniser—the infection rate fell to zero, an unexpected result."

Unexpected to say the least! A 100% success rate is rare...and remarkable. But the problem here is that, as good as this news is, it is anecdotal. It is not a properly conducted scientific test and therefore must be taken with a large grain of salt. Could other factors have been involved? Certainly. So we can't conclude with complete confidence that this instance "proves" anything.

On the flip side, the very next portion of the Wikipedia entry states:

"However, a 2013 comprehensive review of 80 years of research into air ions and respiratory function outcomes found that there was no clear support for any beneficial role in respiratory function, nor evidence for significant detrimental effect. In conclusion, 'exposure to negative or positive air ions does not appear to play an appreciable role in respiratory function.'"

But read that again carefully. The people who make air ionizers do not actually claim that their product provides any direct "beneficial role in respiratory function" - they claim that it knocks gunk out of the air. Which it does. It is not the exposure to negative ions that makes a difference; it is the demonstrable fact that those negative ions reduce the presence of potentially harmful particles in the air that produces the beneficial outcome.

As a result, though the science is admittedly murky, I come down on the side of believing that this ionizer is producing a beneficial effect that has demonstrably - and positively - affected my wife's health. And for that reason I should give this device five stars.

Except...

Several other reviewers have commented that they found the operating instructions for this device to be either insufficient or confusing. I am going to disagree. The device has three settings and they are clearly described in the accompanying paper. They are:
Position 1 - Night light is on, air ionizer is off.
Position 2 - Night light is on, air ionizer operates on a motion detector which turns it on for 30 minutes whenever motion is detected.
Position 3 - Night light is off, air ionizer is on constantly.

These instructions are neither insufficient or confusing - they are STUPID! They describe a major flaw in the basic design of this product: I would guess that a significant percentage of the consumers who purchase this device assume that when the night light is on the ionizer is working and when the night light is off the ionizer is also off. But their assumptions are wrong both ways. When the night light is on, the ionizer MAY be off...or it MAY be in motion sensor mode. The only thing you can know for sure is that if the night light is OFF - the ionizer is ON! And that is a mind-numbingly idiotic design.

First off, why in the world would you want the night light ON and the ionizer OFF? The only reason for that is that you just want a night light - and if you paid this kind of money for a night light then - excuse me - but you're an idiot. And conversely, if you want an ionizer but you don't want another glowing doohickey in your room, why not provide a setting on the device where the ionizer is ON while the night light is OFF? I hope the manufacturer is paying attention to the reviews of this device because they need to rethink the fundamental design. A good number of their customers are quite likely using their product thinking that it is functioning because the night light is on and getting no actual benefit from ionization whatsoever. Of course they're not going to think it works...because it isn't working!

So our rating is four stars - because while the functional design is weirdly and majorly flawed, it still seems to be doing what we had hoped it would do. I realize that our experience is purely anecdotal and should have little impact on your decision to purchase as it is entirely possible we are experiencing a placebo effect. But given that my wife did not know about the purchase and did not know I had installed the device in our bedroom, the chances of a placebo effect are greatly diminished. Still, coincidental factors could be involved - we did a bit of housecleaning in preparation for the holidays and gave both our dogs a bath recently - but neither would have had a profound effect on our bedroom. In the end, all I can say is that we experienced a desired positive effect from the installation of this device and recommend it. We would recommend it even more highly if the functional design made sense.

By the way, if you found this review helpful and/or informative I'd really appreciate it if you'd leave a comment or at least hit the little button that says it was worthwhile. It would be nice to know whether the time I spend doing this is proving to be beneficial to anyone out there. Thanks!

title: Great Machine but only lasted 18 months
text:
I really like this distiller. I has more stainless steel than my previous distillers from Sears. The bottom of the top half is stainless, (it was plastic in my Sears distiller), the spout is stainless and the fan blades are stainless. Nice. The point of failure in my first Sears distiller was the rubber gasket, this machine has a silicone gasket which I expect will last longer and seal better. The company includes a cute little tool (also stainless) that positions the spout over the receiving bottle. I had never seen one before, but I enjoy using it, and it keeps dust out of the bottle as it fills. I really can't complain about my Sears distillers. I bought two and they have given me 23 years of service. Over the years various parts have failed, but I was able to swap them with each other. The only criticism I have of the Tinton is I wish it had a knob on the top so it could easily be lifted off.
Also I received the distiller one week after ordering it, Amazon had estimated a much longer delivery time.
Update: It is now Jan 31, 2016 and the machine no longer works. It did not come with a contact number or trouble shooting guide. The past few weeks it was cycling on and off every 5 minutes, as if it was too hot and automatically turning itself off. There are small burn/melt marks next to the 'ON' button. It will stop working after a small amount of water is distilled--maybe a cup. Since my prior Sears distillers lasted for years, I am disappointed that this machine has died after a year and a half.

title: Tired of Alkalines?
text: If you find yourself going through Alkaline batteries and spending a fortune, it is time to convert to Hybrid NiMH. Eneloop batteries are kind of a combination of Alkaline and Nickel Metal Hydride (NiMH). If you have used regular NiMH (not hybrid) in the past, you might have asked yourself why did I waste my money because they discharge so fast when not being used. Hybrid NiMH are completely different: they will hold a charge when not in use, so you can have spares ready to go into a device when you need them. These do not have memory effect like NiCd. All in all a good battery. Check out Imedion's for a lower price point and more power. BE CAREFUL: there are some devices that require the full power of an Alkaline battery and won't work with these.

title: It's good, but not PROFESSIONAL
text:
Firstly, I want to address something:

The listing here says this is a professional ceramic flat-iron. Although it has many of the same components as a professional flat-iron, I don't feel that it is the same quality as a professional one. One of my best friends is a hair stylist and she cuts and styles my hair for me. While her work flat iron isn't pretty at all, it does the job quicker and better than this one does.

That being said, I do think this is a good product for at-home use.

I have naturally curly hair-- although I'm firmly in the 3A or "Curly Twirly" territory ([...]), and I used to just wear my hair curly. Since I cut it shorter though I like the way it looks straightened, so I've been using this iron almost daily for the last few months before writing my review.

First, lets talk about the cons. 1. This thing is HEAVY. It's heavy guys. It's not heavy like a 2-lb dumbell, but it does have some weight to it. I was used to a cheaper iron before, which didn't work as quickly, but was a little bit easier to use because it was lighter.
2. This says that it has a safety switch which turns it off after 40 mins-- but reality determined that was a lie. I have left this thing on more times than I can count (I'm not the most responsible human adult) and every time I've come back to this being as hot as when it first reached temp. It's not been a problem for me because I keep it on the little protective mat that came with it, so nothing has been damaged, but I don't have children so.
3. Finally as I said before, I don't feel this is a professional salon quality item.

Okay, so lets talk pros:
1. It's cute as heck. I don't really mind leaving it out on my dresser because it's almost like decoration.
2. It comes in a super nice package with a comb (for different part designs and for easier separation for ironing) and a safety pad to wrap it in to cool down. I've obviously gotten a lot of use out of that.
3. It works, guys. It works better than my $25 Revlon one that I got a few years ago, and it works the same every time I've used it since I got it a few months ago.
4. Finally, it's a reasonable price. It may not be AS good as a CHI hair straightener, but it is solidly $30 cheaper than the cheapest CHI, and it works plenty well enough for daily use.

I purchased this item at a slight discount in exchange for my unbiased trial and honest review, but after using it for 3 months, and knowing how it works, I would have paid the full price for it.

title: Update, a year later...
text:
This was definitely a great purchase. We used it for several months without any issues of mold or mildew, funny smells, or any quality issues. It provided a great platform for my kiddo to play. Looking at current reviews, I don't see how anyone has a problem with this not supporting their baby, unless they are using it on a baby who isn't sitting upright yet. It is assistance to keep a baby who can sit up from flopping over. Regarding buoyancy issues - it fills with water which weights it down and keeps it from bobbing around and throwing an unstable little one off balance. Using a few inches of water in the tub - all I still use with my toddler - works perfectly. He was able to sit, reach, play, splash, and enjoy his bath in comfort. It was much safer than me trying to hold on to a slippery baby in the tub, and softly supportive. I figured out an easier way of draining the water from it - I would let the tub drain while drying and dressing baby, then jump in and walk on it to get the excess water out. Then, put the hook through, give it a hoist and hang it from a hook in the shower. Worked great. It may not be everyone's cup of tea, but I think this was exactly what my precocious little one would have picked for himself.

Old Review: We have been using this for a couple of months now and I love it. We got it before my son had perfectly mastered sitting by himself (around 5.5 months) and it provided the perfect amount of support. Now that he can sit well and is confident, the bottom of the hug tub keeps him from sliding around and provides a nice platform for him to explore. This is also great for combining bath times with an older sibling. Pay attention to care instructions which say not to use washes with lotions or oils because they will prevent the hug tub from drying completely. We hang it over the tub to dry and occasionally throw it in the dryer on low to get it dry and have had no problems with odor or anything. Hanging it outside to finish drying is an even better option. It is really heavy when wet (fresh from the bath, but you can squeeze most of the water out by squishing it in the tub, and it drains quickly and becomes easier to move much faster). When it is nearly dry (several hours or overnight) I put it in the dryer for a few minutes to finish it off if I need to (I live in higher humidity). Also some other reviews mentioned that the front is open and the risk to your baby, but this is a bath aide, not a safety device. I sit right by the tub and I have never had a problem preventing him from falling into the water when he gets excited, but this is so much better for dealing with a squirmy slippery baby than a lot of the other things I've tried. Not to mention that it is soft, comfortable, and grants him a little more freedom. The tummy option, letting him play with the water while propped over the back of it, is nice, too, but my kiddo loves being able to sit up and play in the tub. I highly recommend this.

title: Wonderful, comfortable, reliable alternative to cannula
text:
These masks are comfortable, durable, cute, and provide consistent flow my daughter’s doctors and I appreciate. The added humidification that occurs helps keep her nose from drying out, especially when she’s requiring higher flow rates -we also use a humidifier bottle.

When she is an especially active sleeper it can get loose if not taped. We use kind tape to tape it on when she’s ill or already has low saturations - just to save us all being woken regularly by pulse ox alarms.

I’m so glad I found these a few years ago, for my (then 2yo) daughter. She has been using them daily for years. She has NEHI & for nearly 4yrs has been on oxygen anytime she sleeps, during illnesses, & times of poor air quality. We (inpatient nurses, respiratory therapists, physicians and I) struggled to get her to put or keep on the cannula. Even if she’d comply awake, she was constantly ripping off the cannula in her sleep. The only solution were these padded arm braces that kept her from being able to reach her face. She despised the “wind in ‘her’ nose”. We tried so many variations and setups, but either she wouldn’t keep them on, they wouldn’t stay on, or the blow-by options couldn’t consistently/reliably keep her SATs up. There wasn’t a cannula or mask we could find that she’d keep on, until these.

I am so late in reviewing them. Recently, we were traveling & she decided to chew on the tubing while we were driving through a mountain pass. I had to switch her back to a cannula for a few days until I could get more of these. We were all ready to hug the delivery man when they arrived. These have made a world of positive difference in her (our) live(s). They’ve literally saved my girl.

text:
Very easy to use home test. Whilst you can't be 100% certain that there are no problems if you get a negative result, it does allow you to get immediate confirmation as to whether there is blood in the stool.

Easy to use, just have to watch how you use it, but that would be the case of anything that has to be used in this manner. If you read the whole of the instructions first, you will have a good idea as to where you are going - wipe, close off the wiping area, drip a couple of drops of fluid, and KEEP YOUR EYES ON IT for a couple of minutes. Do not walk away and come back a while later as the results may find and leave you thinking you have a negative result when you are actually positive. Follow the instructions and it will work perfectly. You don't need a very large sample for this to work.

I tested to make sure a positive would have shown up by pricking my finger and dripping a droplet of blood onto a tissue and then using the testing fluid - you shouldn't rely on a negative test result, without ensuring your test is effective!

title: Straightening your hair is as easy as brushing it!
text:
I want to start out by saying I'm lazy. lol I'm in night school taking nursing classes so I'm up until the wee hours finishing up my weekly reports or trying to wind down from my clinical days at the hospital. On days when I need to run errands it's easier for me to just throw my hair up in a bun and wear a bandanna. Until now...

I have long-ish thick wavy hair that's kind of frizzy. With my regular flat iron I have to divide my hair into sections AND layers to make sure I get it all done. It takes forever! It takes so long that I only do it on days when I need to be at the hospital (they won't let me have my bandanna lol) and special occasions.

I was skeptical when I first received my WonderBrush Straightener. I quickly became a fan. No sections. No layers. Straightening my hair is now as easy as running a brush through it.

I used a blow dryer on my hair before I used the WonderBrush so I had more volume then I usually do when I use my flat iron. I plan on trying it out on air dried hair tomorrow (I'll update afterwards).

The WonderBrush heated up quickly and remained hot the entire time. Sometimes with my flat iron I'll have to turn it off and then turn it back on to get the heat back up to the proper temperature. The rubber bristles spread my hair out in an even layer and kept the heating element away from my scalp.

All in all it took about 10 to 15 minutes to straighten all of my hair. I brushed the top first and then did the underside just to be sure. That's only a fraction of the time it would have taken my flat iron to get the job done. I'm impressed!

I love this straightener!

text: This product was recommended to me by a friend who told me it took care of her Stye in only two days.  Due to underlying health issues, I have a stye in one eye more often than I would like.  I have tried all the home remedies, including warm compresses, and none of them work as well as this product.  You can put it right on the stye itself and it does not hurt your eye at all (in my case I had an external and very large internal).  While I could not reach the internal, some of the oil did drip down onto it, thankfully, as it helped the pain subside very quickly.  I cannot attest to whether or not it shortened the healing time, I believe it did but have not timed my other stye eruptions to say definitively.  Either way, rubbing this oil on the stye helped take the pressure, pain, burning and redness away for me.  I am going to order again just to have extra on hand should I run into anyone else who may have a problem.

title: pedaler
text:
this is a good product. the only problem is the plastic they used for the shell creaks when pedaling, and the more resistance, the more creaking. someone took it apart and lined the area where the two halves meet with electrical tape, and no more creaks. I plan to do that soon. once the creaks are gone, it will be almost silent.

UPDATE: i just added the tape, and the creaking is gone. totally worth a few minutes' effort. I used black electrical tape so it is not really even visible. i just unscrewed all the screws on the one side, and put the tape along the smooth seams, on the side with the lip. Wrapped it around the lip so half the tape strip is outside, half inside. I didn't bother putting it on the parts of the seam where there are ridges in the plastic--just on the smooth parts was enough to take care of the noise. It was not necessary to remove the pedal cranks in order to accomplish this--there is enough space after you unscrew the one side to get the tape put on. Much more pleasant without the creaking. The quality of the mechanics looked solid while I had it open.

title: Excellent, simple, and effective product.
text:
The product is what is seen in the photo: a bucket. This very simplicity makes it excellent. You put hot water, put your feet in, after 3 or 4 minutes add some hot water. Repeat one more time, and after 10 or 15 minutes, just turn it upside down and ... done! No hassle, no whistles, no bells, no cords, no lights, no sound, no bubbles, no massage, no wi-fi, no leaks. Perfect.

Prior to this, I had bought (for twice its price) a "foot spa" from a different maker. It had an electric cord, made bubbles, had a thermostat. None of these were really useful and I used it about two times, plugged off, because the little thermostat was useless, the bubbles were annoyingly noisy, the thing was bulky and was heavy. I could have lived wih all these inconveniences, had I not noticed, in my 3rd usage, that the water level got to about half its initial level in about 15 minutes. I had not noticed before because I was using it on the bathtub's floor to avoid spilling on to the bathroom's laminate. Thanks god I did iso: it was leaking!! I returned it to walgreens immediately, and at the same moment I ordered this one from amazon. How happy I am now!

title: Useful Item for one of life's daily chores
text: Nice little pill container, though I would advise against using it for travel.  As with many daily pill organizers it seems, the compartment tops could stand to stay closed a little more securely.  If it might be tossed around at all (as in a carry on bag, or loosely packed in even checked baggage), there's a good possibility that one or more of the compartments will spill their contents.  Usually not the end of the world, but annoying.  The labeling on the covers is printed (as opposed to embossed into the plastic), so perhaps in time it will wear off, but I don't see that happening anytime soon.  It's a reasonable size considering it does provide 14 compartments.  I might recommend it, and would consider buying it again.

title: Functions as Advertised
text: Though using two 7 compartment pill organizers (for AM and PM) was getting old, I had them, so it made sense.  It was a hassle while traveling though, so that's what prompted me to buy something like this.  The organizer itself is very heavy duty and feels like it could survive being thrown from a moving car (though I have no idea why you would do that).  I'm not sure that extends to the compartment covers though.  I'm convinced that that's the Achilles's heel of all pill organizers.  Not being hinged, regardless of the plastic's quality, the repetitive motion has to eventually take its toll (which I get, and at around $10, I'm willing to replace it as necessary).  These covers close securely, and as important while traveling, so far, have stayed closed.  The compartments are large enough to hold any variety of pill shapes, sizes, and quantity (all of which seem to change and grow as we get older).  I would recommend it and would buy it again.

text:
I have a large face and a beard. I dislike masks because they NEVER fit. I decided to try this one and was pleasantly surprised how well it fit.

Reasons why this earned the five star rating:
1) The XL fits my large face.
2) I love that it is adjustable. The ear loops are adjustable, so you can make it as tight or loose as you want.
3) The neck strap is ingenious! Not only does it facilitate the ear loop adjustment, it acts as a keeper to hang the mask from your neck when you don't have to wear a it, keeping it always available and not having to pull it out of a pocket.
4) The material is soft T-Shirt material making it comfortable.

Overall it is well worth the little extra in cost! I ordered one to try and am ordering the four pack, to save a little money overall, especially since I have to wear them at work. I think a nose wire would improve this mask; however, most masks with the permanent wire in them the first thing to go is the the wire due to metal fatigue form constantly bending and unbending. I like the fix of using the self adhesive metal strips that can be ordered on Amazon. This way the strips can be easily replaced and you still have an awesome, intact mask.

title: A Perfect Face-mask for a Bearded Man
text: As a man with a beard of medium-length, having the right kind of mask to wear -- on a daily-basis -- is very important. The first few masks I tried were somewhat serviceable, however, they were all designed with elastic ear-loops. These elastic bands caused three main issues for me: 1) since these masks were frequently worn, the elastic slowly weakened over time, leading to a fit that was too loose to be effective; 2) the elastic bands caused my ears to feel sore and tender after extended-use; 3) these type of ear-loops caused each mask to tug and pull at my beard, which was, at best, mildly uncomfortable. ENTER BUTTONSMITH, which offers a mask that is PERFECT for a guy like me. First off, they've designed a mask crafted from a light-weight, breathable material that's easy to wear for extended periods of time(in my case, up to eight or more hours per day). Secondly, they offer an "XL" size that allows me to cover the entirety of my beard WITHOUT tugging or pulling at it. And finally, the ear-loops are ADJUSTABLE via a strip of material that allows a CUSTOM FIT while doubling as neck-chord, which prevents the mask from accidentally falling to the floor. It truly is an INGENIOUS design. For all my bearded brethren out there, I can't recommend this mask enough!!!

text:
I'm a big dude (6'4, 300 lbs, average head size for my body I guess?). This thing fits well and has held up in the washer and dryer. I really like it, but I have two complaints that might keep me from ordering multiples. First, it's VERY hot. I find myself sweating quite a bit while I'm making groceries with this thing on. Not just under the mask, but my whole head feels hot. Might be okay when the weather cools, but right now it's kinda miserable. The other thing is that there is nothing along the top to cinch for form to your nose. I wear glasses so my lenses will fog constantly. I've taken to pushing the mask up my nose and putting my glasses over the fabric, which works but isn't comfortable and my glasses won't stay put. If it had something to prevent glasses fogging, I'd give it five stars.

As for the good, as I said, it feels sturdy. It's been through the washer and dryer a bunch. Still looks good, still in good shape. There is a pocket for a filter, but I haven't bothered with that. It's already pretty thick. I like the strap around the back because you can pull it off and let it hang like a bib, which I do as soon as I exit the grocery. Feels good to feel the air in my sweaty beard as I walk to the car. I also appreciate being able to easily tighten or loosen the mask by pulling the string under your ears. Get perfect comfort, except for the heat. Very soft. If you're in a cooler climate, this is perfect. Here in NOLA, it's a bit rough. We'll see when winter gets here.

title: Just what the doctor ordered
text:
I HATE having to wear a mask. But if this is how things are going to be for a while I wanted to find the most comfortable and well-designed mask out there. After considering the available options I ordered a Buttonsmith mask. The mask arrived in the mail today (a day earlier than expected!). As soon as I opened the package I was sure I made the right choice. The fabric is extremely breathable and soft against my face.

The adjustable straps are cleverly designed and extremely handy. They allow the use of ear loops (which are the most secure way to keep the mask in position), but there is also a strap that allows the mask to hang around the neck if you need to take it off of your face for a few minutes.

At $15 apiece these masks are far from inexpensive, but they are nowhere near the most expensive option. This is certainly not the time for me to skimp on a quality. These mass are worth every penny. I would have bought a few of these masks if they weren't quite so expensive. Having actually received the mask I may go ahead and order another anyway.

My only other issue with the mask is the color. For these first several months of the pandemic I realize that the number one priority was to get masks onto everyone's faces, and that the most efficient way to do that was to produce just the one color. But now it looks like we're all going to be wearing masks for quite a while, At some point it would be nice to have a choice of colors (especially some light colors which would be even cooler still in the summer).

Aside from these few minor issues I recommend that you spend a bit of extra money and buy the Buttonsmith masks with the adjustable straps. They're just what the doctor ordered.

The idea of being able to adjust the mask by pulling the strap through an "eye" with the rest of the strap around your neck is a great one. But the engineering is awful. The "eye" is so large that it doesn't hold the strap in place.
You'll have to adjust the mask every single time you put it on, and then it will probably get loose as you wear it.
It would have been so easy to design the "eye" to be a real choke point requiring effort to pull the strap through. You can do it with needle and thread, but it shouldn't be necessary. Also the straps are way to thick (which tends to cause your ears to stick out and and fold forward).

title: Best Mask So Far
text: I have tried face masks from multiple sources this year.  Some have been too small.  Some have been made of material that was hard to breath through.  Many do not conform to the contours of the face.  This one, however, is pretty good.  I like that they have multiple sizes:  child, youth, adult, and adult XL.  Too many masks by other makers are one-size fits all (really meaning one size fits a few people well and most people poorly).  Buttonsmith actually gives you a range of sizes!  These masks are made of cotton jersey which is a very breathable material.  That is important for all day use, but is really just a facial covering for low risk situations.  There is, however, a pocket inside the mask for an additional filter which could boost the level of protection provided.  I like that this mask is contoured to fit one's face.  I love the adjustable ear loops!  Too many masks have either tiny ear loops that bend my ears forward or loops that are so big that the mask sags.  These are adjustable so you can make them fit just right!  I also like the neck loop.  This allows me to drop the mask away from my face when I am not around people without having to worry about laying the mask down & losing it.  One drawback was that there was a fairly strong dye scent at first, but that went away after a couple of trips through the washer.  I purchased the black masks.  Buttonsmith also offers a white option.  Perhaps the white masks wouldn't have the same issue?  At any rate, it was easy to get rid of the odor.  I agree with another reviewer who said that these masks need a wire nose bridge.  I purchased some stick-on aluminum nose wires which work ok, but it would be nice if the nose pieces were sewn in.  I also thought the price was a little high for what they are, but these are the most comfortable masks I have tried so far.  I guess that is what I am paying for.  I will probably buy some more, maybe in white.  It would be nice if there were a few other color options.

CONS: And, in my opinion these con’s ARE SIGNIFICANT.

1. THERE IS NO metal or plastic strip at the top of the mask to make it conform to the bridge of the nose.

2. Without disassembling a mask, it appears THERE ARE NOT 3 layers of fabric forming the face mask. THERE APPEARS to be only TWO layers of fabric used in the mask assembly

I believe that the available guidance from Dr. Fauci and CDC calls for 3 layers of material in the body of the mask.

3. The interior pocket for a filter covers the entire interior surface of the mask. The here is no notification what size filter to use with the mask. I am concerned that the PM2.5 filters would migrate within the pocket to a position where they would be ineffective.

This final statement is going to sound snarky, for which I apologize in advance if is not called for, but I choose to wear face masks to protect myself as well as those whom I come into contact. I DO NOT CHOOSE TO WEAR MASKS AS A FASHION STATEMENT.

title: Take my word for it as a black car owner; Not all spray detailer is created the same.
text:
I own a gloss black car, so I'm constantly washing it. Realistically I wash it 2 days a week, but I digress.

I hate how cliche this will sound: "I've tried other brands, and this is the only one I keep coming back to!" Yeah. But it's true. And here's why.

I don't always use detail spray in the best conditions. Sometimes its muggy. Sometimes its exceptionally sunny. Sometimes its both. What tends to happen for me with other detailers is the 'gum-up' on the car for lack of a better word, and start catching small fibers of whatever you're wiping. Tough to explain. It's almost like instead of applying a smooth drying shine you're spreading a microfilm of wax/oil around on your finish. And in certain light that's exactly how it looks - especially on a black car.

I really wanted to like other brand options after I started running out of Eagle One. I was sold on catchy slogans and bottle art showing impossible glassy finishes, but none of them were without problems.

Eagle One is always in my trunk now. It wipes off clean without residue, which is important to me.

title: Perfect for kids going to school!!
text:
I love these masks for my family for several reasons. I also have a couple of cons, which I will list below. But even with the cons I can’t find any masks that work as well and are made in the USA. I will continue to use and purchase these!

Pros
1. Made in the USA.
2. Neck strap!! My boys are going to school and I like knowing they won’t be setting their masks down random places.
3. Easy for my kids to put on! No ties or anything like or previous masks that hung from our necks. Schools won’t be able to help students with their masks so I had to make sure my boys could put the mask on and off alone.
4. Thick, can’t feel my breath on the other side; even without an additional filter.
5. Super soft and doesn’t bother or pull on our ears.
6. Washable!! We wash ours at the end of each day and have had no problem after many weeks of doing this.

Cons
1. We had one (out of 16 masks) that had a seam separate. Not that big a deal since it was just one out of the 16 I purchased. I can fix it myself.
2. Thick, we live in the south and it gets very hot in these masks!!
3. Only two solid colors to choose from. My son would like to wear some of the cooler looking masks he sees other kids wear but he understands these are best for where they are made and with the neck strap.
4. No nose piece to form the mask to your nose. We all wear glasses and when you walk out the door in the south and are hit with humidity a mask that doesn’t block the breath well makes it worse. I’ve gotten to where I don’t wear my glasses when I have my mask on.

title: Finally, a mask that fits!
text:
I have a larger head and facial hair which means that most masks, which were apparently designed for smooth faced mannequins, won't fit. When I say they won't fit, I mean they barely cover from the tip of my nose to just above my chin. Fortunately, this one fits from the bridge of my nose all the way under my chin. To be honest, it almost borders on being too large, however, once I adjust the rear loops, it snugs up just fine.

The material is as advertised; some type of cotton, t- shirt type cloth which is very soft and comfortable. The ear loop adjustments work as advertised and it has a filter pocket for added protection. I haven't tried washing it yet so I couldn't speak to whether it holds up just yet, however, the stitching seems to be decent so I'm hoping I won't have any trouble.

Overall I'm pleased with mask. It's nice to finally have one that's comfortable to wear.

Once I've washed it a few times, I'll try update this review on how it went.

title: Comfortable, breathable and BIG in a good way
text:
I have now purchased 7 of these! After trying and returning many, many different masks, these are above and beyond my expectations. For a while my wife was making our masks from home, but as she put it, "You have a very large face", so getting the sizing right on both the material and the ear loops was driving her crazy.

I also found that several different types of elastic gave the back of my ears a rash. And then I found these masks, that are big enough to cover both my face and beard. The adjustable ear loops means I can perfectly fix it to my face. And the material is super soft, but I also feel very safe while wearing it due to the double layer. It is also very breathable.

The one downside is that it does muffle my voice a little, and I have a job where I have to talk a lot while also projecting (teacher), but the benefits to this mask far outweigh that minor inconvenience.

TLDR: Big enough for my very large face shape and beard, extremely comfortable and breathable. Slightly muffles my voice.

I don't usually submit reviews, but with face masks being a critical wardrobe feature these days I thought it might be helpful. For starters, the mask arrived very quickly; a day earlier than expected even. Although I've only worn the mask for 1 day so far, I have to say it is very comfortable. The fabric is soft. It barely makes my glasses fog up (which I cannot say of the other masks I've tried). I do not have a filter in it at the moment, but there is a pocket for one. The quality is excellent. I love the neck strap and adjustable ear loops. I highly recommend this mask.

title: Best mask I’ve ever had, but still searching for better
text: What sold me on this mask was the neck loop so it stays on your person even when you’re not wearing it on your face. Very convenient if you’re going in and out of stores and want a better system than putting the mask in your center console or hanging it on your rear view mirror. It’s soft and lightweight. It’s about as comfortable as a mask can be. It can feel too heavy and clingy if you’ve been sweating. For glasses wearers, yes, it steams up. My trick is to put the mask on first and wear it very high up on my nose, so that it covers my cheeks from my jaw all the way up to just shy of my lower eyelid. Then I put my glasses on and wear them a bit lower on the bridge of my nose than I normally do. When I wear it like this, I can be steam free unless I am exerting myself and breathing more heavily/ sweating.

title: SKALD Works
text:
I tried SKALD to see if it would work, and I am impressed. Please note, I have not been reimbursed for this review nor have I been sent this product for free. I simply purchased this on impulse from an Amazon deal.

Long story short, you MUST use this with exercise to see the results. This is a thermogenic, so the more you put into your workout, the more you will get from this product.

I've used Hydroxycut (original) back in the day, as well as Oxy Elite Pro (Original) and SKALD comes VERY close to these original formulas.

In my personal experience, I had a plateau. Most of you out there know how difficult it is to get out of it when you're losing weight and on a disciplined diet plan. You're thinking to yourself, "What else can I do? I'm doing all I can!"

As to hunger suppression, it does better than most products I've used. When taken about 30-minutes before you eat lunch (I do not take it every single time I eat), it does seem to keep me feeling full, longer. I then take another pill later in the afternoon to curb later cravings. This does seem to work. However, don't think that this is going to put a Ball & Chain on your brain activity for craving potato chips, tortilla chips, chocolate, or whatever else you may want. It won't. It just makes it easier. And when it's easier...YOU CONTROL WHAT YOU EAT. Not that bag of chips in the pantry. For example, I have better concentration on my eating habits and I simply grab a banana and/or yogurt later in the evening.

I give this product 4 stars because I want to see some improvements in the increase in thermogenic potential as well as making an even more aggressive hunger avoidance formula. I'd give this a 4.5 stars if I could.

In any case, I highly recommend it. Remember, you MUST exert your body to get the full benefits of this product.

For a stack, I'd recommend the Animal Paks (yes, those 9 or so horse pills). If you're taking additional caffeine pills (200mg per pill), you might want to hold off until you get an idea of how SKALD interacts with your own stacks. And this brings up another important point: SKALD doesn't have any major side effects, even with mixing with other aggressive stacks. This is from my own experience, so it could vary for you, and this is why I say take it easy on the caffeine.

Just a word of advice. Stacks are most beneficial and less dangerous on the body when you are working out. This is because the body is using the supplements versus sitting on a couch, expecting a miracle, and letting the supplements just sit there...wreaking havoc on your system because your body isn't moving.

In conclusion, you have a product that does not have major side effects (in my case...none), a product that increases your metabolism during workouts, a product that more than likely will stack and integrate just fine into your current supplement cocktails, and a product that will curb your hunger cravings and allow you to choose a more healthy snack if really needed.

title: The best solution to the demise of the photo album
text:
It has occurred to me that there is a real problem in digital photography, one not generally acknowledged. Image quality has gotten better and better due to advances in sensor technology, but easy means for displaying all these great images haven’t really kept up. We are all struggling in a sense with the demise of the photo album, and with the (mostly unacknowledged) severe limitations of phones and tablets as display media. Photo albums have passed almost completely out of current usage (everyone I see still dutifully printing at photo kiosks in drugstores is over 65!), and photo albums are now resting quietly with the Sony Walkman, VHS, and ‘carbon copies’ as technologies in the historical graveyard.

Currently, roughly 95 to 98% of all digital images are viewed on small screens, often times barely HD, and oftentimes, no bigger than 5 inches. Tablets are now the second most common viewing surface for digital photos, followed by laptops, but these are also small, and although higher resolution is now readily available, the eight megapixel display on my Android phone with its 5” screen is clearly overkill. So we really do not have commonly available high-quality display options, unless we have 4K or above monitors, which tend to be used as workstations for image processing but not for image viewing in the home. And 4k TVs are also a cumbersome display media – I’ve used them, and they are a pain, and you can’t just hit a button and have a slideshow. For our very best images, photography enthusiasts have gravitated towards large prints, but at some point, we simply run out of wall space . . or frames. And large prints have their issues too – principally the cost of all those frames, and significant cost for the print itself, if we are printing past 13 x 19. Frustrated with a huge library of high quality images but no great, easy way to view them, I decided on a bit of a whim to try a rather expensive Memento 25 inch 4K display – thinking that if I didn't like it, I could easily send it back. Well, to my surprise, it's had a transformative effect, in terms of how I approach image display, and has made a huge photographic library all of a sudden much more accessible – and I bought its bigger brother, the 35 inch version, which even my wife, our queen of anti-technology, loves. And indeed we like the images on this screen even more than any of our high resolution prints, even though those printed images legitimately might have a bit more theoretical detail (more on that later).

It's proved to be a stunning way to display an enormous amount of photography (the frame will hold up to 3000 images – these appear to be stored in the frame, but I suspect they get compacted down to the 4k max resolution to save memory space). The frame has changed radically the way I look at my own photographic work, and it has rendered large prints virtually obsolete. Although the very best larger prints may have a little bit more detail than any 4K frame is capable of displaying, the panel has a luminous image quality that makes the very best images even more appealing, and remarkable per pixel sharpness and definition. And of course when you display a large print, that’s just one image, while this display medium gives it the ability to display 3000 of them on a rotating basis.

Pros:

1) Luminous image quality – they have done an excellent job of tuning this panel so that image quality exceeds both of our larger 4K TVs, even though the panel is clearly smaller and has no more resolution. Terrific contrast, and dynamic range and color, without notable oversaturation. Best viewing surface I've seen yet for a 4K panel displaying high-resolution images. Does not appear to be OLED but gets close to that in dynamic range and color.
2) Excellent per pixel sharpness
3) Basic image parameters such as color, saturation, contrast and of course overall panel brightness are easily modifiable. I find that default settings are just about right.
4) Capacity for holding 3000 images organized into almost any number of playlists (not sure what the maximum number might be but I haven't hit yet).
5) Excellent smart phone app (but see Con #1) which allows full remote control of the panel (controlling everything from cycle times to playlists to screen color and contrast tuning to simple on/off functions), as long as you are on the panel Wi-Fi network.
6) Excellent program on the PC side and decent Android and iPhone software for control of the panel and for image uploading (but see con #4).

Cons:

1) Somewhat buggy operating system issues, suggesting that this needs more OS refinement. One frustration is that you can't simply load images by attaching a flash drive or SD card. Indeed there is not even an SD card reader, and the apparent USB flash drive slots on the rear of the panel are there for 'diagnostic purposes only' according to their technical support, and have no utility as a port for reading or loading images. WUWT???
2) This means that you are totally dependent on a Wi-Fi network and Wi-Fi connection to upload images into the panel's memory. This is very slow when you're talking about uploading hundreds and even thousands of images – way slower than even USB 2.0.
3) The panel’s total memory capacity is unspecified so I suspect that the 3000 image limit might be exceeded long before you get to 3000 images if you're uploading very large files. This may change and re-incentivize where you set your JPEG quality slider in your postprocessing program!
4) User handbook is a bit of a joke, and does not adequately clarify that your best interface for uploading is unquestionably through your PC (or Mac) – where typically we have most if not virtually all of our digital images. Someone not doing a deep dive here might readily conclude that they could only upload images from their phone, grow frustrated with the process of having to transfer everything into their phone, and give up.
5) Cost – this is a pricey item, with even just the smaller 25” panel going for $600, and the larger 35” one (which might be more appropriate in living rooms and other larger rooms), going for $999 – up from $900 just one year ago.

This is the best digital frame on the market right now. So why am I giving it 4.5/5 stars? Good question. It's just a bit overpriced and needs further work and refinement of its operating system – both of these are likely a function of the near total absence of real competition In what appears to be a still immature and developing marketplace niche. It's as though nothing has really yet filled the gap of the now totally antiquated picture albums, and while tablets and phone have taken over, those aren’t the way to make your images more ‘viewable’. Perhaps the ‘meme’ of a dedicated high-resolution display (and your phone, TV or tablet cannot be dedicated by definition) just hasn't quite caught on, as people have not yet experienced and appreciated the virtues of this approach. There are for sure many other digital frame products (the idea has been around for quite some time and I think the first of these appeared 15 years ago or more), but none that I have seen anyway that offer 4k. And several of the barely HD options aren't even that much less expensive than this. Given that even your typical android cell phone and iPhone take 12 to 14 megapixel images, it's amazing that the marketplace is so far behind the potential demand for a technological solution to fill the gaps between the dead photo album and the limitations and restrictions of phones and tablets. In any case, this is clearly the best way to display your images, whether they are from a cell phone or from a high-end professional full frame camera . . or anything in between. But it does have some minor issues – and it ain’t cheap.

Still, overall, Highly Recommended, with the above caveats. Given that the cost of 4k displays have come down rather dramatically, I was hoping that we'd see a more competitive and less expensive product in the last year, and one with OLED, or a price drop on this, but instead the price has gone up! For now, this is the best option on the market for both mid-size and large digital frames. It will potentially transform how you feel about your digital image library, making it far more accessible to both you, and your family. Worth a try?

title: Unsure of the effectiveness
text:
Let's start with first impressions. Very simple label design, not a lot of frills or intricate design. Simple is good. Always remember K.I.S.S. (Keep It Simple, Stupid)! But what is ENZOPLEX? From looking at the label, I wouldn't have a clue what this supplement is taken for. Lets turn the bottle.

Serving size is 2 capsules and has Serrapeptase, which comes from an enzyme that occurs naturally in the intestines of silk worms (yuck)! Serrapeptase is used to treat a variety of ailments including carpal tunnel, back pain and migraines, to name a few. Papain is a digestive enzyme that comes from Papaya, this aids in protein synthesis. Papain is all in all a digestion booster and is great for people like me who eat a high protein diet. Enzoplex boasts that it's a healthy alternative to pain relievers. But lets look at the other side of the label.

I'm still not seeing ANYTHING that would tell me what this is used for, aside from looking up the product on the internet or the individual ingredients. I would hope that if I found this in my medicine cabinet I could read the bottle and know what it's used for. That to me is the one HUGE, MAJOR downfall of this product. The good new is, it's just a packaging issue.

The product itself is small and easy to swallow. As far as effectiveness I took this product for a full 30 days I didn't notice an improvement. Enzoplex asks that you give them 60 days to see if you're satisfied so I am hoping with continued use I can see/feel that I'm reaping the benefits of a Kosher/Vegan all natural product.

title: Amazing! Refreshing.Great addition to wet shave.
text:
I am relatively new to DE Razor wet shaving, and have been experimenting with a lot of products. Intitially shaving with no preshave, trying hair conditioner, Musco real Glycerin soap as recommended in Leisureguy's book and now the Edwin Jagger pre shave lotion. I have yet to try the pre-shave oils but when I do I will add to review.

First I must say that any pre-shave prep is better than none. I found the glycerin soap was a great improvement to the shave over the moisturizing hair conditioner. The Edwin Jagger pre-shave lotion though is amazing, astounding difference over the glycerin soap. Virtually eliminating razor burn and allowing for a really good close shave. Smooth through all three passes. My new favorite, again I still plan on trying some oils, but so far I am very satisfied.

Caution! This product is very mentholated. If you have sensitive skin or don't like the menthol feel on your face this product is not for you.
On the other hand I awoke this morning somewhat congested, and the pre-shave completely cleared my sinuses.

Summary: I love this product. Great pre-shave. Don't buy if you don't like menthol shaving products.

Update: As I am one that loves trying new items and combinations, I have recently tried [[ASIN:B001G371IY The Art of Shaving Pre-Shave Oil - Lemon - 2 fl. oz.]], which worked well, but I didn't feel the slickness that I expected considering the thickness of the oil. I then applied the Edwin Jagger Pre-shave lotion on top of the AOS oil and had a very amazing shave with little to no friction on any of my three passes. Given many out there won't want to take the time, or spend the money, but as this is a review of products, I hope this is helpful. If even for the occasional treat this combo is really nice. If I have to use one or the other, at this point I like the pre-shave lotion a bit better.

text: I am always hesitant when trying new supplements. The main nutrient is Omega-3, a fatty acid that your body can not produce on its own and must be ingested through the food we eat. Though I love fish and a diet high in sea foods does replenish this, it is not very efficient and too much fish could lead to mercury poisoning… which can be a very serious problem. Krill Oil is the oil harvested from Krill, a shrimp like crustacean that lives at the bottom of the ocean. In this case, it is from the Antarctic Ocean, located in one of the coldest and cleanest places available. By taking Krill Oil, it’s been said that you can find amazing health benefits including a healthier heart, a boost to your brain, an easier menstruation and more. For me, I can’t really speak to each specifically as they are hard to judge subjectively, but I can tell you that I’ve never felt better. The added CoQ10 makes this product over the top for me, I love being able to get that heart specific extra love in my diet. I did receive this product at a discount in order for my honest review, and that's what you got. By no means do I ever promise a good review, and by no means do I give them out every time. title: Nice But Barely Fits a Skinny Person
text:
The Rinkmo Rollator Upright Walker was easy to put together; however, I am a skinny disabled senior citizen who is 5' 9" tall, weighs only 145 lbs; and I barely fit between the handle bars when I sit on the Rollator seat (which is comfortable). I also wish the arm rests were 2" taller for a more comfortable fit. It is important to be very careful when rolling over any cracks on the sidewalk that is more than a 1/3 inch tall, as the Rollator tends to easily tip forward. The Rollator is very light (wish it was a little heavier and studier), and a little wobbly that can roll fast on sidewalks, so be sure to tap the brakes to slow down, otherwise an accidental fall can happen. I do like the two side handles by the seat, and I do use them to lift myself up to stand; this is a great unique feature that other upright walkers do not have, and the main reason for me to purchase the Rinkmo Rollator. So if you are my physical size or smaller, the Rinkmo Rollator will fit you. After using this walker for a few months, I've updated my rating from a 3.5 star 4 stars because I've learned how to use it safely. I've been using it everyday but with caution, and now I can walk a mile

Very Important:
Be sure to rest your elbows firmly on the pads to add stability when using the Rinkmo Rollator; when I first tried using it, I almost fell before realizing I have to rest my elbows firmly on the pads to keep the Rollator from leaning (falling) forward. This is especially important when you apply the brakes or when you hit a small crack on the sidewalk, otherwise you will fall forward. It does take a bit of a learning curve to be able to safely use this Rinkmo Rollator.

title: Perfect brush for those of us who feel the need to scour their teeth
text:
I don't know why, but I tend to brush my teeth as hard as possible when I brush. This is a bad thing - even my dentist commented on how I was wearing away my gums from brushing so hard. I found this brush by chance at a dollar store and when I saw that it was described as a soft-bristled brush, I got it immediately. Wow, I love this brush! The bristles are so soft and dense and I can grind away at my teeth with it and not damage them.

I wanted another one when my first one got too worn out, but of course, the store I got my original one from no longer had them, so I took to Google and found them here. I had no idea it was a children's toothbrush! The tiny brush end should have been a dead giveaway, but I don't care! I was glad to be able to buy these in bulk and I will never go back to using a normal stiff-bristled toothbrush when this one lets me continue my bad dental habits without the damage I was doing before.

I'm sure this is a great brush for kids, but if you're any age and have a tendency to scrub your teeth as hard as possible, I highly recommend this brush. My teeth are just as clean as before and not nearly as sore.

title: Dark Chocolate Almond & Double Dark Chocolate Review
text:
It seems like the same reviews are linked into the pages for different flavors, so I am mainly commenting about the Dark Chocolate Almond and the Double Dark Chocolate bars. Personally, I love the Dark Chocolate Almond. It is really tasty and easy to eat and tastes more like a treat than a protein bar. I tried the double dark chocolate and unfortunately bought a whole box of them only to realize that they are way too chocolatey for me. The double dark chocolate is really rich and usually I have trouble finishing it. I have to force myself to eat it, whereas I look forward to the Dark Chocolate Almond bars.

If you are a choco-holic, then you'll like the double dark, otherwise, get one of the flavors where the dark chocolate is mixed with something else: almond, strawberry, raspberry, etc. For me, the almond really balances out the taste. I have tried the chocolate peanut butter, which is okay. Not as tasty as the almond, but decent.

Overall, the zone bars are pretty good and for the most part don't have that really nasty soy protein bar taste that a lot of power bars and protein bars have.

title: I also got ripped off by MedSuperStore
text: MY 92 year old mother recently fell and needed 15 stitches to sew up her wound. The hospital used a Tegaderm bandage which is flexible, beathes, and did not tear her skin when the bandage was removed. I was impressed and thought that we needed a few of these excellent bandages on hand. Now, I am very impressed with the product. My rating is really of the MedSuperStore company that has the advertisement listed on Amazon, and secondarily with Amazon who has done nothing to resolve my complaint. Here is the issue, the advertisement for this product says (and I quote) "3M Tegaderm Transparent dressings. Picture Frame Style Transparent dressing, 4 x 4 1/2 with/label, 50/box, 4 bx/cs". The unit cost was $8.88. Now, I could not believe I was going to get 200 of these bandages for $8.88, but I thought that I would at least be getting 50 bandages for $8.88. Shipping was $8.00. So I ordered it and to my amazement, what arrived in the mail over night was a cardboard box (medium size) which had a single Tegaderm bandage in it. ONE BANDAGE for $16.00  !!!!  WOW, what a rip !  The probelm here is not the bandage, but the problem is with the MedSuperStore which appears to be using a standard photo and product description without every clearly indicating that actual price is "per each". Worse, I have complained through Amazon's specified conflict resolution process and my complaint has been ignored by MedSuperStore (I bought two different sized bandages and spent a total of $32.00 for them, and at that price, would like to return them). No response or follow up from either MedSuperStore or Amazon. At this point, I have written this event off as a $32.00 learning experience for me. However, the rest of you that may see this review and the other one on here, be aware. You are not getting what you think you are going to get. And Amazon, you should be ashamed for letting this kind of misleading advertisement continue on your otherwise excellent web site.

title: Overall a very good keychain pill carrier. A close to perfect balance of capacity and compactness. Some issues.
text:
There are a lot of keychain pill carriers for sale on Amazon. The reason I picked this one over the others is that it is not too big to easily carry on my keychain AND not too small to carry some bigger pills. It also looked durable.

Pros:
This thing is about half an inch longer and around 1/5 of in inch wider diameter than the keychain pill container you can pick up at CVS. And that is a very good size for those of us who have to carry around larger pills. I can now carry four or five of the larger pills with me instead of two, and there's still room left over for about four or six medium sized pills or even more small pills.

The slightly larger diameter is great too. My old CVS pill carrier lid happened to be the exact perfect inner diameter to sometimes get an average sized gel capsule stuck inside it. The pill would often be stuck so tight I would have to dig it with my keys, which would occasionally break the capsule, causing tiny spheres of medication to go everywhere. Yuck!

But that's not the case with this pill carrier! No capsules or pills stuck in the lid, at least no pills that I take.

It also feels nice and solid. I have dunked it in the sink enough times to be confident it is waterproof.

So, why only four stars?

Cons:

The main issue: the way the top is threaded is a bit subpar, at least with the one I got, which I don't know is typical.

When screwing the lid back on it's a little bit of a hassle to line the lid up perfectly with the body to get the threads started. Also, the threads squeak and sometimes bind, making me paranoid I'm cross threading the lid. A little olive oil on the threads mostly took care of the squeaking and binding. I'm not sure how often I'll have to re-apply to keep the threads feeling kinda-sorta smooth with only a few squeaks.

***** BTW, if you lube the threads like me DO NOT use WD-40 or some other oil not safe for consumption. Non food oils will no doubt "work" better, but no matter how carefully you apply that oil some if it is going to end up on your pills, and then in you. *****

Overall, I'm concerned that sooner or later I'm going to screw up this pill carrier by cross threading the lid.

Maybe the lid thread issue has to do with the titanium metal-- though I doubt it.

Maybe I just got one with improperly machined threads.

Also, the lid's O-ring looks really thin. It could be fine and last a good long while, or it could end up tearing after a few months of regular use. I don't know, having had the canister for only a couple of weeks. I'll probably post a follow-up review six months or so from or this posting. If the O-ring does tear, I hope I can find another at a hardware store.

Finally, I wish this pill container was just a tiny bit larger still-- say 5 or 6 mm longer and maybe an extra 2 or 3 mm in diameter. That would be make it enough to make it even more useful while still not so large it would be a hassle to keep on my keychain. With the current size I can ALMOST-- but not quite-- fit six of my large pills along with six of my medium capsules in it. If I could do that it would be perfect for me as I have to take two of both kinds of pill with my meals, and sometimes I have to be on the go all day.

title: Pros and Cons
text:
I bought this powder because I haven't been eating my vegetables regularly. I've also dramatically reduced my intake of beer and find that guzzling a tall glass of water with powdered greens fills my tummy the way my favorite beverage does.
Pros and Cons. This powder is made up of a wide variety of ingredients, so you're more likely to get at least a bit of a lot of things that are good for you and are unlikely to get too much of something that's not (like men getting too much iron by ingesting a lot of moringa leaf powder). The flip side is that some of the ingredients are in such small quantities that they may not really be adding much of value. Compared to other superfood powders available on Amazon, Country Farms Super Greens powder costs less. Unfortunately, it's still really expensive compared to, say, fresh vegetables at the supermarket (I can justify buying the stuff, because it's a lot less expensive than all that beer I used to drink).

A final note: I bought the natural flavor. It doesn't taste very good when mixed with plain water. It's not bad with a squeeze of lemon or lime and a packet of stevia or sucralose. I have the berry flavor of one of Country Farms other powders (Super Reds Energizing Polyphenol Superfood). It's really tasty, so - the next time I buy Country Farms Super Greens powder - I'll try the berry flavor.

Update: I bought the berry flavor. How disappointing! While it smells like berries, it tastes like the smell of humus soil. Gross!

title: Very satisfied with my purchase. Legit pictured.
text: So I ordered this a few days ago and just now used it to cut my hair. I will say it right now, that I love it! I was sketchy like I sometimes am with a lot of ads, but I can attest that this is a legit order. Everything you see in the ad, is what you get. Was planning to go to the salon because my hair getting so thick, prior to the pandemic, but of course, everything shut down. I honestly hate going to the salon, so rarely went anyway because it feels like a hassle. But my hair was getting too thick, I couldn't stand it, I needed to go to the salon. Once everything shut down, I just shrugged and decided to order some professional scissors with the thinning shears. I couldn't wait. My hair got so thick, it was hard to run my brush through it. This came pretty quick and the package was small. Left on my doorstep. I believe it could just fit in the mailbox, but I'm sure it won't be delivered that way.---So the hair cutting process was so easy. I really honestly wished I'd ordered it sooner. Not saying you'll get a "perfect" haircut doing it yourself, but if you're careful, it doesn't really seem that bad. It's really quite easy. I wear my hair in a ponytail most days and a bun at work because I'm actually required since it's food service. I just needed to get rid of bulkiness, and thinning shears does the trick. It's all about the thinning shears. I can't express enough how much better I feel after taking out the bulk. I took out a LOT of hair! And it feels great! Feels just like a fresh cut from the salon. They are very sharp and pretty. No snag. They came a blue and silver color. Not sure what the 'white-3' option was...? The accessories were a little cheap feeling, but can't complain, they're still nice. The apron has a logo on the front, not pictured in the ad. But that shouldn't stop you from achieving a desired cut. I cannot wait to cut my husband's hair. So yes, I do recommend these if you're looking for something you can trust. I took a chance and I'm pleased.

title: Good, but could be better.
text:
While I like this gel pack, it has a couple issues for me too.

Pros:
Nice large size for large issues, like sore thigh muscles or aching backs.
Material seems nice and durable
Given it isn't frozen too long, easily folds in half or molds around body part if needed

Cons:
There is a large area for the gel and seems it could use a bit more gel in it than it has.
The large area is not partitioned off at all within meaning it can all gravitate to one part of the pack leaving the rest empty
It can freeze too solid making it no longer pliable and easy to use

It is still a good gel pack, but I do feel it is lacking enough gel and could have been made more efficient by not letting all the gel squeeze too much into any one part of the pack and be more evenly distributed. Smaller packs don't have to worry about this so much, but its a big problem when you have a big pack and gel that can take up less than half of it when it moves. If it freezes too solid like that, then almost impossible to be used effectively in any manner.

I kept seeing commercials for the pedi soft and, as I am obsessed with the aesthetics of my feet, I was very intrigued, so I did my research. Of the three most popular electronic foot buffers on the market this one received the best reviews, although the others were not too far behind. So I ordered it, and I can't say I disagree! Although I have not used the other two so I cannot say that this one is the better of the three, I can say that this one works very well and does everything it promises to do.
The product arrived fairly quickly. Packaged well, and in brand new condition. when I opened the box everything was in place. I took the unit out immediately and turned it on and was delighted to find that it was charged and worked right out of the box. I emphatically went right to work and lo and behold it did everything all the reviewers claimed it would do. There was a large amount of "dead skin dust" just piling up under where I was using it. Immediately I noticed a difference. My feet were softer and smoother within seconds. To be honest, it's a little addicting! It is actually fun to use! Be careful though, as overuse can leave your feet cracked if you thin the skin too much. Also, if you leave the unit on one spot for more than a few seconds without moving it it can feel like it's burning. It doesn't take much to notice a difference but because it is so enjoyable it is easy to overdo it.
Furthermore I was contacted by the company three times. Once when I initially received it I got an email with basic instruction on how to use the product. Over the next month I received two more emails with further instructions and FAQ's about the product, as well as an offer of eager customer service on hand if I have any problems at all. Personally I think customer service is just as important as the product so I do appreciate this attention, however i am hoping this won't be a constant occurrence as I can definitely get annoyed at an overbearing overabundance of constant correspondence asking if I like the product. YES I like the product! THANK YOU for the wonderful customer service! Cheers!

text: Okay......the reason why I bought this massage ball is for the fascia at the bottom of my feet.  Our fascia surrounds our muscles and organs. It's a thin sheath of fibrous tissue enclosing a muscle or other organ.  I would use this at the gym I went to in Middletown, CT.  My trainer was Kevin Dean and he is the best!  He would explain why it is important to roll out your legs with a roller to break up the fascia, and a part of warming up the body.  Fascia hardens and can cause problems.  It needs to stay supple.  I found that when I arose from bed it was difficult to walk.  It was like they were stiff.  I thought it was weird because I am not old enough to have this problem.  It was going on for a year!  So, I decided to buy the ball and start using it because the feet are so neglected.  I have moved from CT so I no longer attend the gym with Kevin as my trainer.  I also take my toes and push them towards me which also helps with the fascia.  Anyway,  this ball is addicting to use.  It's like massaging your feet.  I no longer have any problems with my feet!!!!!!!!!!  My husband also loves this ball!!!  I am going to buy him one.  I don't want to fight over this.  LOL.  I recommend this for everyone and the price is great!
