title: Perfectly happy (initial impression)
text:
I have had this scale for just one day, so this is just an initial impression.

Pros:

1. EASY SETUP. After reading so many reviews about problems in wifi setup I was a little apprehensive. I used my MacPro to download the software and it took all of about 2 minutes to set up. Just follow the instructions which is quite simple. (I will be looking out for any problems in the future.)

2. LOOKS: People who like design of Apple products will loke this scale (white). Next to it my old scale [[ASIN:B0020MMCDE Omron HBF-514C Full Body Composition Sensing Monitor and Scale]] it looks so futuristic. I was happy with my Omron but Aria steals the show.

3. CAN'T CHEAT: All readings are stored on the server. No need to write down weights, it records date, time and measurement. (Readings can be manually deleted on the web site if needed.)

4. ACCURATE WEIGHING: I compared a couple of readings with the Omron HBF-514C ones and both were within 0.2 pounds. Omron was calibrated with a previous Tanita scale and found to be accurate. Reading seem good enough for me.

Cons:

1. PRICE: At $130 it is a (fit)bit expensive. However, on Amazon the prices varies. I started tracking its price about 3 weeks ago and the white one which always showed $127-130, one day had new one for $108.xx and I grabbed it. The black one varies often and I have seen it go down to $111.xx on two different days. So if you are patient you can save some. Still it is expensive but for the convenience it is worth it in my view.

2. RECORDS ALL: Sometimes I just want to test my scale but everthing is recorded. It can be deleted by going online but wish there was some option not to record a reading in the first place. Just a small inconvenience though.

3. BODYFAT: Most expensive scales give out this measurement but the accuracy is highly suspect. Best will be to look for trend and for those who are obsessed with bodyfat measurement, best idea will be to get theirs measured at professional locations at about $60-70 every six months or so. For example I hae seen underwater measurement (most accurate one) offered at local climbing gyms at $70.

SUMMARY: I am very happy with this scale. I also own a [[ASIN:B00BGO0Q9O Fitbit Flex Wireless Activity + Sleep Wristband, Black]] and I think my activity and weight measurements, while still not perfect, have reached a new stage keeping up the latest advances. I will use this scale and will report if something changes. Thanks for reading my review.

title: I'm glad these work!
text:
I bought these for my daughters who lately have been complaining about getting car sick. They liked that there were multiple colors to choose from so they could be different from one another. This is a great size for their wrists (ages 7 and 4). It does seem to work best when put on a few minutes before actually getting in the car. They aren't effective if the motion sickness has already set in.
My daughters enjoy wearing them, pretending they are a cool fashion accessory for trips to Grandma and Papa's house.
I think using pressure points actually does help, and while it's not a magic fix, it certainly helps the girls mentally prepare for the trip ahead and believe they are wearing their magic bracelets. The difference between wearing them and not wearing them on long trips has been quite noticeable. If we lose this pair we will definitely purchase another.

Others have posted they have experience the same thing, so I wanted to test it for myself. I would step on, get a reading, step off, repeat, and never get the same result. Fitbit claims that there is 2% error in the body fat reading, so each time your reading could be off by that amount. This might not sound significant, but it is. The weight readings seem to be consistent, but a $10 scale could have told me that information.

title: Great lumbar cushion, but don't leave it in a hot car exposed to the sun
text:
This cushion is great for lumbar support; the gel structure is cooler and more resilient than a fiber-fill or memory-foam based product. I will likely buy another when I have extra income for other applications.

I bought this with Purple's "Portable" cushion as their website suggests that cushion is good for tall people in small cars, though I didn't find that to be true. This back cushion however is a godsend for my Chevy Cobalt's poorly designed driver seat.

Criticisms:
My advice to purple: Please document what the loops on the back of the cover are for. There is no indication or documentation I could find that describes what to use them for or how to use them, although I found some generic text referencing a "handle" on this cover, which seems to be left over from another cushion. Logic tells me these loops are to secure the cushion to the seat with elastic bands or straps.

While this was sold as "New" direct from Purple's Prime store, it did not come in a box like the Portable Cushion. This bothered me because I hadn't selected "no-hassle" shipping and the other cushion came with information about it. The cushion isn't affected by this shipping decision, but I would have appreciated a heads up. Receiving it without the packaging made it feel incomplete, especially when shipped next to the portable cushion. I felt like it was missing important information such as "Don't leave this in a 'superheated' car because it will deform if pressure is applied when heated above 105ºF" and perhaps straps to keep it in place on a seat-back.

title: Why is this an Academic Year and NOT a Calendar Year planner?
text:
Why is this an Academic Year and NOT a Calendar Year planner?

I must have had blurry eyes when I ordered this planner. I swear it said it was an 18-month calendar through December 2015. If it had been, it would have been just what I wanted. IT IS NOT thru 12-31-15. I would have returned it had I not written in it before I noticed. Not sure why they would make this planner on a school year when they also make others that way. You would think they would want to appeal to those not on school year schedules as well.

That being said, I will use this for the six months left in this year. I ripped out the July-December calendars, but left the Notes sections for each month. I used double sided tape to tape together the pages that were not notes so when I flipped the pages, it went from note to note. I used those pages to journal my "To Do" lists for 2015.

Things I like on the weekly calendar:
Each day has a "check off" list with boxes to check off what you have done.
The abbreviated appointment calendar underneath the check off list.
A list for "While I'm Out" and a "Shopping List" for each week.

Other things I like:
Monthly Calendar
Notes section for each month
Christmas Card list
Other Card list

Things I don't care for:
Monthly Budget - I wouldn't use this in case it was lost, too personal
Not on a Calendar Year
Yearly Calendars of months is on Academic Year

Since this company/person makes other Academic year calendars, I would like them to make a Calendar Year planner for us NON-School Year people.

Loss of stars: 1 for only being Academic Year, 1 for printing errors (I found appointment times wrong on some pages)

title: Questionable support on the body
text: I bought the purple royal seat cushion for my 95 year old Mother. She is bed bound, wheel chair bound, and incontinent bowel/bladder.  I get her up every morning and allow her to sit on the sofa for approximately four to five hours.  I thought the purple royal cushion would ensure that she would not get any sores on her bottom.  Well, when I used it, the first time and changed her diaper after the four hours, she had deep red indentations on her bottom from the honey comb shapes of the purple royal cushion.  I was a little upset about it, because she gets sores on her bottom if she has these red marks.  So, I treated her bottom with ointments and creams and the next day the red indentations were gone.  I wanted to give the purple royal cushion another chance. So the next day I used one of my quilted hospital pads on top of the purple royal cushion and sat the purple royal cushion on top of a memory foam pillow.  I did this because, when I sat my Mom on the purple royal cushion the previous day it went flat.  This time the purple royal cushion was supported from the bottom.  This made a big difference and she did not have the honey comb indentations on her bottom.  So, now no red indentations on her bottom and it works. So, I am semi satisfied now, but it took a lot of modification to get here.

title: Mixing In The Methox?
text:
As a mature powerlifter, I've found that less is more as far as my routine goes. I can get by with fewer exercises and more rest than I could a decade ago. Unfortunately, I'm less responsive to designer products, and even 'legal steroids' is money down the toilet.

As a result, I'm mixing and matching all the higher-rated enhancement products available on Amazon, and Methox Power happens to be one of them. Most of the young lifters have written positive reviews about it, and I have no reason to report otherwise. I've worked back up from a 315-lb/20 rep squat routine to 405x20 over the past six months and including Methox in the mix hasn't cost me anything. I take five during the routine (squats followed by bench presses) along with a whey protein shake and it carries me through just fine.

Probably the best way to determine what works is using the product by itself for a couple of weeks and see what it does. I don't have that luxury, but always look for something recommended by other lifters. I'm counting myself among others who have no complaints about Methox Power.

title: Needs the power drill brush to work —but it DOES WORK!!
text: I am writing a review because I read about 59 reviews before I bought this product and I want to help someone else out.  We have a bathroom with a glass shower door and wall which hasn’t been properly cleaned for 17 years.  We washed it but never concerned ourselves with getting rid of the hard water stains.  Finally during COVID-19 I have had tons of extra time and got a bee in my bonnet that I needed to get that shower looking fresh and new. I started with CLR, then Lime-a-way.  Each evening for about 2 weeks I spent about 20-30 min of hard scrubbing on that glass shower every day to try to make some effort. Most of the buildup was gone after all that scrubbing,  but the etched in hard water stains remained, no matter what I did, no matter how hard I scrubbed. Next I moved onto a razor blade and scraped and scraped but it made absolutely no difference.  I got a ceramic oven cleaner and tried that. Nothing would work.  I was scared to buy this product because some reviews gave it low marks. Also, I wanted to get the set with the power drill brush, but several people said that it left scratches on their glass.  So I finally gave in and bought a bottle of this product, and I also bought a WHITE power drill brush (not the stiffer yellow one) and tested it out on a small spot in the shower on the glass.  I had to drill at high speed for a few minutes, but afterwords I was flabbergasted! It actually worked! All the etched in hard water stains were gone in that spot! I couldn’t believe it!  It did take 3-4 attempts to completely remove all the hard water etching from my glass.  And I had to rinse with tons of water, and then I used windex to remove any residue.  My glass looks brand new! It is amazing!  I must say that there is a very slight  (and hard to notice) clouding of the glass now, but the glass looks so clean and new that it is like we just bought the house! The slight (very very slight) clouding is much preferable to the hard water etched-in hard water stains.  It looks so amazing now!!!  I gave this 4 out of 5 stars because it was so expensive!! And because of the very slight clouding.  But I honestly don’t know if it is the product or just the power drill brush that made the difference, but the combination of the two did the trick! I wish I would have used this first rather than getting all the chemical burns on my hands from the lime-a-way that I tried in the beginning!!!

title: Keeps consistent humidity level.
text:
I am not a ‘cigar guy’ but I have a few cigars and needed a legit humidor to store them. I smoke maybe 2-3 cigars in a year so budget long term storage is what I am going for. This humidor was easy to setup and had instructions on how to season the box and test the hygrometer. I like the window on the top of the box because it lets me read the hygrometer without opening the lid and letting the humidity out. The rest of the box feels solid and well built, the outer finish is polished and shiny so if you’re into a more traditional look it might be a little too much. The cedar interior is also well built and thought out, there’s one included separator for the top shelf to help organize your cigars. The lid creates a good seal. Wood (especially cedar) can have the tendency to warp or change its shape but they have done a really good job machining the lid to have a perfect fit and seal.

The hygrometer included is digital and can’t be calibrated. I checked it using the salt on a spoon method and after 6 hours it read 73% which is pretty close to 75% and within the margin of error +/- 2% in the instructions. The temp reading takes awhile to adjust but after an hour it was reading the exact room temperature.

The included humidor puck and hygrometer are loose and each have some 3M double sided tape to attach them to the interior of the box. This was one feature I was not a fan of. The box has a premium feel and does a really good job of holding a consistent temp and humidity levels so it was surprising they went with cheaper components. The hygrometer looks like it was added to the kit last minute and doesn’t fit the rest of the theme. I can’t bring myself to slap it with some 3M double sided tape to the nice cedar finish on the inside so I just set it under the window frame. I may upgrade to a nice looking analog hygrometer in the future.

If you are a cigar newbie like me this kit has everything you need minus the humidor fluid and cigars. The strongest feature of this box is well it can keep a consistent humidity level which is fundamentally what you need a humidor to do.

title: responsive company
text:
I'm shopping for a FIR pad for my knees and felt I needed more info about this product before I could decide whether or not to buy it. I wrote to the company, asking several questions and I very much appreciate their thorough response. I haven't decided or purchased a product yet, so my 5 stars are for their responsiveness. Here's my Q and their A :

1. Q: How many temperature settings?
A: There is only an " On and Off" switch. There are no heat settings. All of our products only go to mid-40 degrees. So not very hot more-so warm to the touch. Our products have been proven to penetrate 2.36 inches so 6cm through the body. Normal heating pads usually only heat the surface of the skin where as Thermotex products go deep and penetrate through muscles and issues in the body.

2. Q: What are the 2 far infrared inserts made of?
A: Our inserts are - A patented carbon impregnated fibreglass mat. So when electricity is applied it produces far infrared energy.
3. Q: Does it shut off automatically?
A: No, none of our products shut off by themselves. You have to turn off the heating pad if you don't want it on anymore.
They do not use a lot of electricity - it's only 4 cents a day.
Therefore they are not very expensive to keep on if you chose to use it all day or forget to turn it off after you're done using it. Very cost efficient.

4. Q: How is it powered?
A: All of our products are powered by an electrical wall outlet that you plug the product into. If you wanted to use it in your vehicle for traveling you could do so -- just would need a converter.
Our plugs are made for the north American market so depending on your location you may need a converter if your plug in outlets are different then in north America or Canada.
5. Q: Is any part of it washable?
A: Yes you can wash the covers of all our products.
You can't wash any of the products with the inserts still inside as water might damage and wreck them.
There's a velcro strip at the very bottom of the knee where the electrical cord comes out of. You would just open the velcro and remove the inserts before washing.
The covers can be washed in the washer and then in your dryer on the low tumble setting.
6. Q: Can I bend my knee when wearing it?
A: Yes you can bend your knee while wearing the knee pad. You do need to be by a wall outlet and keep the product plugged in in order for it to continue to work. You can bend and move with it on though.
7. Q: What kind of fabric is it?
A: The fabric covers are made of polyester, nylon and cotton.

title: A solid purchase without reservation
text:
I liked the idea of a Wi-Fi scale and we have Fitbit devices so this was an easy sell. The setup is unlike anything I have set up. I was curious how it would be done. I wanted to live with the scale then write my review.

The first person in the family who is setup on the scale becomes the primary person in charge of adding other family members. That first person then emails up to 7 additional family members and gives them permission and instructions via an auto-email from the Fitbit site. The scale gives you 3 letters to identify each member of the family (they pick and this can be changed easily). If a "guest" uses the scale it says "Guest" while weighing, gives the weight and then the light goes out.

Each individual's weight is assigned to them. If you are within 8 pounds of another person the scale will display both of your ID's until it can decide who is the person on the scale. When your initials (or 3 letter name) shows step off the scale and you will be assigned that weight. A big check mark appears when the scale is finished. You can step off then.

The real nice feature is you can step on the scale and simply wait for the light to go off. Once the light is off you step off the scale and go about your day. When you feel you can handle seeing the numbers you can check your Fitbit Dashboard online. So nothing to write down. No forgetting. Easy recall and graphs of your weight online. BMI (body mass index) is given on the scale too as the weight, BMI and 3 letter ID rotates on the display. BMI is also logged online along with the weight.

Scale can be moved around for dusting under it, etc. Put it back or relocate keeping it within range of your Wi-Fi.
350 pound maximum weight and scale weighs to the nearest Tenth of a pound. Scale uses 4 AA batteries

Each person sets up their own privacy settings for where and who sees their numbers. Family members will not see your weight unless you set it up that way. There are several setting for your weight alone. So everyone can be happy

title: Surprisingly strong, and CERTAINLY clear enough to see what's inside
text:
One of my uses for these is to protect stuff in storage against dampness. So, I put a vintage reel-to-reel tape deck in one of these bags, wrapped the top of the bag into one hand, and lifted up the whole thing -- 49 pounds and the bag held up fine. Nice!

But I am also writing this partly in response to reviewers complaining that the bags aren't 100% crystal clear. True, but you can easily see what's inside anyway. They're about 90% clear. I don't see the problem. You could get a slightly larger, thinner, perfectly clear Husky bag for twice as much per bag.

Others have complained about the packaging, saying that the bags are just "dumped" into a box. Different product? My bags were packaged as 10 rolls in a box, with each roll holding bags separated by perforation. Just pull and tear off a bag. Again, what's the problem?

My only dislike (thus 4 stars) is that these are the kind of bags that are welded at the bottom seam in a kind of "pinched" fashion -- it's like a giant hand came up under it and pinched it closed with all five fingers. (Other brands will have a single-line seam at the bottom, or no seam at all. This makes the bottom spread out more so it can hold more.) This doesn't seem to affect the strength, though. The 1.2 mil thickness seems just right -- holding 49 pounds for this size bag is impressive.

Good deal at a good price. And probably the only review I'll ever write for a garbage bag!

text:
Taking a bath is my way of unwinding each evening. Generally I just enjoy a soak in nice hot water or water with Epsom salts and essential oils. Using these bath bombs took my bath to a whole new level!

When I took the first one out of the box to use, I made the mistake of unwrapping the clear plastic, that surrounded the bomb, by my vanity sink rather than the bathtub. Even though the bomb was completely intact, there were “crumbs” in the package that spilled out onto the bathroom floor. Lesson learned! Always unwrap directly over the bath tub.

The bombs had a very pleasing light citrus smell. I am somewhat fragrance sensitive but these had an aroma that were pleasing to me. Once I dropped the bomb into the tub, it fizzed and dissolved very quickly leaving the nice aroma in the air. I was surprised how soft the bomb made my skin feel. Not over oily, but enough to feel like there was a little oil in the water. It felt luxurious on my skin and did not irritate it one bit.

Perhaps I would buy these for a gift, but at the very expensive price, I would not be able to justify buying them for everyday use for myself again. The product is a 5 star product for sure, but it loses a star due to price.

title: Best Soapstone Treatment for Show Areas
text:
It's been about 2.5 years since we installed soapstone countertops in our kitchen. At first, we left it natural to see how it would age, but switched to Dorado wax because of splotchy darkening and our Kitchen is pretty open.

It goes on easy, dries well enough to buff out guickly, and hand buffing leaves a low sheen easily. There's no waxy or oily feel once it's buffed.

It does pick up water marks--as all waxes do. We've learned to wipe surfaces as we work. Also, they easily buff out after cleaning. You also lose the ability to set hot pans directly on the countertop. But that's not exactly a ding.

We touch up as we go and reapply every 9 to 12 months

title: I've seen a few posts suggesting this app and I would highly recommend it. The free version is fine
text:
I have snored for my years and tried a number of devices. Nasal strips, nasal sprays, Zyppah, a custom fitted dental mouthpiece, different size pillows, etc. None of them resolved the issue. The Zyppah was also very invasive and uncomfortable. I also had a sleep study and the result was "no sleep apnea, but yes you snore very loudly." I was skeptical of the SleepNora device, but figured I would give it a try as the snoring was very disruptive to my wife.

Prior to using the SmartNora, I started monitoring my sleep with the SnoreLab app on my iPhone. I've seen a few posts suggesting this app and I would highly recommend it. The free version is fine, but the premium ($8) is worth the upgrade. I used this to benchmark my sleep and snoring before SmartNora. I had very high snore scores and lots of "Epic" and "Loud" snoring.

The first couple nights were a little awkward as I had to get used to the pillow insert inflating, but it did work. I've been using it for about two months now and my snoring has drastically been reduced. It is definitely the best anti-snoring device I've used and I would recommend it. I almost never have any Epic or Loud snoring any more as the SmartNora device activates and stops my snoring.

My one wish -- -- I wish it had a monitor to measure how many times the device activated in a night.

title: Ice Cubes Work With Different Cup
text:
So I never usually write review but I felt the need with this product. I bought it as a present for someone who loves Slurpees. (I figured it would be great to make healthier versions with juice etc.) Only to be horribly disappointed when we first tried to use them.
On the first try the cup leaked all over and it barely froze anything. Tried again later this time making sure to wipe around the edge of the glass and tighten like crazy. Didn't leak this time but still barely froze. On the THIRD try it finally began to slightly freeze. HOWEVER it took a good 6/7 minutes of shaking and after taking out the cubes we were left with barely half a cup of juice.

I decided the problem is that the cups themselves are not cold and do not really keep any of the cold in (your hands holding it to shake it don't help either.) So on my FOURTH try I used frozen drink glasses I recently bought from CVS and what do you know IT WORKED PERFECTLY! Still not worth paying 15 bucks just to get the ice cubes but I was happy to figure out how to use something I was unable to return instead of being stuck with 30 bucks worth of garbage.

title: Perfect for my 6 year old... great customer support!!!
text:
These glasses are the perfect size for my 6 year old. She's almost 7 now and has been using them for over a year. They work as advertised. Looking through the lenses reveals a clear and crisp image. No warping at all when looking through the glasses. Very nice product. The only issue, and not that big of a deal, is that the glasses tend to slide down when she looks down at her iPad when bounding around in my truck or if she decides to lay on her belly to look down on her iPad. But that, I'm sure it's just because the bridge of her nose may be a little small for now. I'm sure she'll grow into them. Now for the best part.....
We had an issue with both the hinges getting loose. But we were only able to tighten one of the screws. The other screw would not even catch. I contacted Swanwick and they got back to me right away. Even though the purchase was about 1 or 2 weeks shy of a year, they came through with flying colors. They were not only able to, but more importantly, they were WILLING to resolve my issue even almost a year after purchase. This is the type of business I like supporting. They don't advertise a warranty... at least I couldn't find one. But they absolutely backed their product. I will be purchasing from Swanwick again soon. Our daughter has her Swannies, and now it's time for Mommy and Daddy to get theirs. I only wish they made daytime Swannies in kid sizes. For now, our daughter uses her nighttime Swannies whenever she's on her iPad.

title: Works OK with a few caveats.
text: Using this device to help an elderly relative with pill reminders. It works OK most of the time. It has a few minor issues that are fairly easy to deal with. First, it does not seem to be possible to set a reminder for more than a week ahead. Second, sometimes it seems to hear someone talking loud and asks for a command. You can stop it from talking back by pushing down on it or issuing a specific command to it at that point. One of the drawbacks of voice activation I suppose. Last, it takes a while to get used to the commands to set up the clock initially. But, after that, it does seem to work well most of the time. My relative now takes his pills on time, most of the time with the help of this device. ** Update: After using this clock for a while I do have one issue with it. When I go to visit my parents the clock has been unplugged from the wall. Seems the time has changed. I suspect that my father has done something while I was gone to reset the clock and he does not remember how to reset the time. Think I have him trained finally. Time will tell. The clock seems overly sensative, at times, to voice commands. I seems to respond when someone is fairly close and speaks even when they are not trying to communicate with the clock.

title: Put an end to glasses sliding off your nose when working up a sweat.  Great natural product works.
text:
I have to wear glasses. Contacts don't work for me. The bridge of my nose is shaped such that I almost always buy glasses frames with nose pads that stick out, rather than frames with just the molded plastic that bridges over, well, the bridge of my nose. I also sweat. So frames without nose pads often slide right off my face when I get some sweat on my brow that drips down my nose. I once had a friend who is an ophthalmologist dose me up with Botox on the bridge of my nose and above it, since Botox stops your sweat glands from producing sweat. (Who knew?) But he wimped out and gave me the lowest dose.

Then I discovered Nerd Wax! It's really just beeswax that you spread lightly on your glasses where they make contact with your nose. it works like magic. I only have to apply it once a week, since it generally stays a bit tacky for that long, preventing my glasses from sliding off my nose into the muddy pool of water, the desert sand, the pile of sawdust, or wherever I happen to be working up a sweat. Two thumbs up and five stars. The only slight ding is the price -- it's just beeswax, after all. But that's not going to stop me from buying a new tube in 5 years when I run out! (Or sooner, if I lose it! Lol)

title: True Mass - Reviewed From My Experience
text:
UPDATE FOR MAY 03 IS UP!

UPDATE FOR SECOND CONTAINER FOR JUNE 06 IS UP!!

This is a review based on my experience. I am a real person and I am not paid by no company to review this, so everything is told as how it is.

I got this product extremely quickly from AMAZON. After it was shipped, it usually comes to me in a day or two with the free shipping method, which I'm very happy and satisfied with. UPS handling it is a whole 'nother thing since they more often than not tend to use my package as a basketball.

I got the chocolate milk shake and so far I would like to note a few pros and cons and extra side notes to whoever is interested.

MY PURPOSE FOR TAKING THIS:
1. Weight gaining
2. Working out like mad afterward to turn it into muscle since I tend to retain muscle a bit better than fat.

I have a super high metabolism, not to mention my family tends to eat healthy (leaning to vegetarian style) so that just makes it even harder to gain. I'm 125 lbs and am trying to get to 140-150.

Pros:
1. The taste of the chocolate milk shake is pretty decent! I avoid vanilla like the plague because it'll remind me of ensure which after a day to a week of drinking just makes me sick to my stomach even to think about it. The chocolate taste actually tastes pretty decent even though it does get to me if I drink it more than twice a day.

2. Scoops are moderately sized and I calculated the calorie and find that this container contains a total of more calories. Don't be fooled by other gainers that have more calories per serving. This is so because their scoops are bigger and they also have less servings per container. This container gives you 18x630 = 11,340 calories. Mix it with milk and you get even more nutrition and calorie.

Cons:
1. Well it is not too much of a con but if you want to mix this with a liquid, the best way to get uniform mixture is with a blender. I've tried mixing with a spoon and just adding the powder with milk and all you end up with a bunch of chunks you have to break down which is time consuming. I also tried putting the mixture with milk into a large bottle and giving it a good shake. You'll still end up with chunks. So a blender is almost a must if you really want to drink it and enjoy the full quality of the taste.

UPDATE: You can mix it pretty well with method #2 in which you put the powder and liquid into a bottle and give it a good shake. However, you must shake it for awhile. Let it sit for a bit and give it another good shake. If you find that you're still getting some undissolved bits, adding a bit more liquid should help. This method makes it a bit more convenient than setting up a blender.

2. It makes me gassy. Some people here say it doesn't give them much gas, but think about it. You have to shake this up a lot meaning there's a lot of bubbles in the water. You gulping it down means you'll also be gulping down the tiny air bubbles that'll eventually build up in your stomach. There's really no way around it. So for someone to tell you that stuff like this doesn't give you any gas leaves a big question mark, guess it's just them.

Too much of even a good thing could make it a bad thing if you know what I mean. 4 servings a day? Yeah.....right. I was thinking about taking less liquid and making a more condense mixture of it to accomplish 2 servings a day, but this think is $31-38! Can't afford it even if I could drink it fast.

Even with all the cons I still would take this and I'm pretty decent with it. So far I bought two containers and will try it out for two months or until the two containers end. So far I've had this for a few days only. I got this on the 15th of April and so far I've drank this for 5 days straight.

My weight was 125LBs and I am now 128-130LBs, however, I wouldn't jump for joy yet because I think it is because of the weight of all the food I have in my stomach. I weight lift and do workouts quite a bit, but have lately become a bit lazier. My muscles seemed a bit more pump, but I really need to gain more weight for it to really show. I will give you more updates after I finish my first container. This review is mainly my personal opinion in terms of taking the stuff.

If this indeed helps me gain weight, then I should be hitting 135lbs, if I stay at 130lbs that means its just food weight...

This little wonderment has saved me about $30K because I did not have to purchase a new vehicle. Let me explain. I have a 2012 Honda Accord Coupe that I really love; it has currently a little less than. 30,000 miles. The only problem with the car is that the driver's seat is uncomfortable. As a last ditch effort, I purchased the Tush Cush with the hope that it would solve my problem. Well, "mission accomplished."

First, the product takes the pressure off of your tail bone by allowing it to float ... The hole in the back of the product that you see in the photo is the key here, and it is quite effective at reducing pain. Second, the product is a wedge that forces your body into a correct seating posture. Again, this helps to reduce or eliminate pain. Also, I found that moving my seat back a bit so that my knees were not bent excessively helped a lot, and changing the angle of my seat from a vertical 90 degrees to a small incline of between 100 and 110 degrees provided much more comfort. Of course, I had tried these methods previously to no avail, but when they were implemented in conjunction with the Tush Cush, the result was quite effective.

This product really works and I am thankful I found it ...my bank account is ecstatic as well. So, if you are at your wits end because of back pain from driving, and are considering getting rid of your vehicle because of it, I recommend that you try the Tush Cush before taking such drastic action. You may just save yourself a huge chunk of change. Also, make sure you get the 16"x13" version as it fits most bucket seats perfectly; it's almost as if the product was made specifically for my car.

title: Incorrect calculations, had to "trick" scale
text:
I've never reviewed a product on Amazon. This scale worked for a month and then gave out.. Just after the return period. Wonderful. First off, it won't calculate a "low" amount of weights. I tried placing my 5lb dumbbell on there and it flashed to 5.6 or so and then the number disappeared. This happened with anything that weighed just a few pounds. It weighed me and my boyfriend fairly well for the first few days. I had just gotten back from the doctor so I knew how much I weighed give or take.

Last week, that's when it got funky. We have both been eating better and working out (cardio and minor lifting) and I could tell the different in my clothes and measurements but it was stuck on the same number.. Even down to the decimal! For instance, if I got on, for days it would stay at 125.4. So anything around 125.4 it would give me that number. If he got on. It would stay at whatever he weighed.. 205.2 and keep flashing at that. But if I got on, then he got on, then I did again, it would change! So say, I got on and it was 125.4 then his was 205.2 then I got on, it would be 123. It's like you had to trick it with a very different weight to get an accurate weight!

I even tried to stand on it with one leg up. It dropped a few pounds and the next 5 times I got in it (2 feet firmly planted on the base) it would give me the number that I had when I was testing it with 1 foot up. This was super strange. I was excited to get a digital scale but it doesn't seem to work right.

Other than that, it looks really nice and has a slim, sleek design. Affordable too! Wish it worked past the return period but that seems to be his lots of products work.

text: I am going to start this review by saying that it is clear to me that people who gave this product  good 5 star reviews here clearly do not know anything about whey protein and what it's supposed to look and taste like. This product is total GARBAGE! I should've known better by the price they were selling it for, but as always, I try to support new products and I promote competition which benefits us the consumers. When I opened this bag of TruProteins whey I immediately noticed something was wrong with the texture of the powder, it looked highly processed and "grainy" like sand. Real whey protein IS NOT GRAINY looking, quite the contrary actually and the powder is very thin to the point that it sticks to your skin. Then I took a small spoon of it and tried it on my mouth, the taste was off as well and tasted like something I had never had in my life. I have been using concentrated whey proteins for years and I know good whey protein when I see one, TRUProteins whey is just not it. I also have a degree in Nutrition, and part of my daily job is to identify real foods and recommend the best products for my clients. Anyway, I hope this review discourages everyone out there to buy this product because it is not worth the money they charge for it nor your health. God, I I hate to be deceived by false advertisement... Again, this product simply does not look like what undenatured whey protein is supposed to look and taste like. I am returning this product and getting my money back. Now, to end this on a positive note, the only good thing about this product is actually the bag, which has a laminated interior which protects the highly light sensitive whey protein from degradation when exposed to light, but in this case the product inside doesn't look like real whey protein anyway so it  does not matter...

title: 3 days in I noticed a difference. 3.5 weeks in and I ordered tihs suite of supplements again.
text:
First I would like to tell people to beware of buying this suite of supplements (Colitis Care Pack) from independent e-commerce shops. At the start of COVID Amazon showed me there were 7 of these available to purchase. By the time I was ready to give it a go there were none. I ordered off an independent seller site and received only 4 bottles.

When I ordered it from Planet Ayurveda's Amazon store (which I just received today... hence why I'm writing this review) I received 6 bottles, which makes sense. I'm finishing up the pack I purchased from the independent seller and I ran out of capsules in one of the bottles, and the loose powder bottle is almost empty. These things are supposed to last 2 more weeks.

Buying experience aside, I'm a Gluten Free/Vegan who eats a primarily Paleo diet. I don't restrict myself to this diet it's just the easiest way to eat without feeling like I'm dying for weeks at a time without a break. I also don't eat much sugar, although I don't actively deny myself, it's just not in a lot of my food choices.

I wrote that part about my diet so I can get across the point that this Ayurvedic Remedy isn't magic. It won't work by itself. If the person taking these supplements doesn't follow a diet to support their healing then they're actively choosing to continue to damage their intestines. I think anyone would be hard pressed to find a supplement or medication that can heal a person's body faster than that person can continue damaging it by putting things their body finds toxic directly into their gut. I say so because after I purchased this Colitis Care Pack the first time I read unending numbers of reviews stating that Ayurvedic Supplements are a hack, bogus, a lie, fake, and the person who sells them is a con artist or scammer or whatever. It made me nervous. However, the supplements arrived a day later and I spent the money on them with the intention of trying them, so that's what I did.

I noticed nothing for 2 days. I was glad about that because in my research on the supplements I read that people were sometimes experiencing constipation, and I didn't really want that experience.

I started out on the high end of dosing recommendations because I've been in this flare for an extensive period of time. Day 3 I noticed a minor bit of relief. From that day, on through today - I'm 3.5 weeks in - it's been improving and staying somewhat stable.

I went from having to remain in a reclined position - which reduces my pain level - for a very very long time (weeks+) to being able to sit up, stand up, walk without issue, carry things, do chores, run errands...

I also have to note that I ate something I am reactive to, by accident, in the middle of this 3.5 week journey and I was out of commission for 3 straight days. But I kept taking these supplements throughout the flare and I'm extremely positive the supplements are why my resulting flare didn't last for weeks on end. The last time I ate something I was reactive to I lived in agony for over 4 straight weeks.

All I can say to the people who write that this pack doesn't help and it like throwing money away... is that you can't eat a Western Diet and expect this suite of supplements is going to fly in and save the day. It's not likely to work that way. IMHO the best way to use these supplements is to eat a modified/restrictive diet and to let these plant medicines get to work.

I started taking my doses after breakfast and lunch, because the powder is so strong I didn't want to risk going to bed with the taste in my mouth. I figured I'd take it as soon as I could and get it out of the way.

But, one day I missed a dose so I took my final dose after dinner. It was late when we ate so I went to bed almost directly after taking the supplements.

The following day I felt SO much better. I had been improving before that point, when taking them after breakfast and lunch. But when I took it after dinner, the following day was like I had taken a giant leap forward in the healing process. My gut felt SO much better.

I'm a real purchaser of this care pack. This is a legit review by a legit user of these supplements, in case you're wondering how real this is. Check out my other reviews to see for yourself that I'm a real person. I know that was my biggest worry when I was prepping to order this. It's pricey so I wanted to make sure I wasn't being scammed. There were limited reviews here on Amazon, and even less anywhere else. I ran into a general Planet Ayurveda Facebook Page which shows a ton of reviews, many not entirely flattering, but they weren't for this specific care pack most of the time, so I went in with an open mind.

title: Shouldn't have waited so long.
text:
I hemmed and hawed for many months before purchasing this item. I thought it was a bit spendy, but mainly I didn't know if it would work with my bed. I have a Select Comfort bed, top of the line, which is a tall mattress with a pillow top. I also have an adjustable frame that can raise the feet and the head. I was afraid that the weight of the mattress (which is air, really) would be insufficient to hold this cradle in place.

My fears were unfounded. The part of the cradle that slips between the mattress and foundation is very long (you can't see that here). Even when I raise the foot of the bed, the cradle just goes right along with it. The height of the cradle is adjustable, and there is more height available than even I needed with my tall mattress.

I had reached a point where I would have spasms in my feet if I lay on my back and had the weight of the covers on my feet. Even with light comforters. I was so pleased with the relief I got after putting this cradle in place. I do have to keep socks on my feet, and you have to have sheets and blankets that will reach down to the mattress when hung over the cradle, but one would expect that.

For the extra sleep I've been getting, this cradle was well worth the price.

title: Used it for regular laundry; did not clean well.
text:
I had really high hopes for this product. After the first few washes, I thought I liked it a lot. The smell (raspberry) is not overwhelming, and it doesn't leave any powder detergent residue on my clothes.

However, after about three weeks of using this product, I began to notice that it did not remove sweat smells from my clothes. I started using Rockin' Green in the summer, and I have a half mile walk to the subway each day. By the time I would get to the subway and had sweat in my clothes, the clothes started to release a really annoying sweat odor. I wear deodorant every day, and I'd never had this problem until I started washing with Rockin' Green. I also don't sweat THAT much. But I thought maybe it was the clothes that were the problem, so I soaked them in white vinegar to try to neutralize any sweat odor, then washed twice with Rockin' Green on the heavy setting with pre-wash. But I still had the same issue. So finally, I bought Febreze Sport spray and loaded the clothes up with that spray. Then I washed the clothes in Tide with Febreze Sport scent, and within two washes, the clothes were fine and I didn't have the same problem. Since I switched back to Tide, I have not had this issue at all, which leads me to believe that the Rockin' Green was not working. I was really disappointed because it is pretty expensive.

After losing a lot of weight in the past year, the amount of cellulite on my thighs and legs has become much more noticeable and I have been trying everything under the sun to reduce it. Unfortunately, there is no true way to get rid of cellulite for good but I have found that massaging the area regularly can make the skin appear a bit smoother temporarily, which is good enough for me.

I really like the fact that this kit has 2 different types of massagers included. There is a very nice mitt style round one, and one that has a pair of rollers on a handle. I've been using the roller style massager dry in the evenings and the round mitt style massager with some anti cellulite lotion after I take my shower in the mornings, and that seems to be working out fairly well.

So far, out of the two types, the one with the rollers has quickly become my favorite. It's really easy for me to use it and roll up and down my leg and I can also reach the backs of my legs without any problems. To me it also feels nice and I find it to be kind of a relaxing ritual when I use it in the evenings as I am getting ready for bed.

The rollers on both of them are relatively stiff, so be careful not to press to hard the first time you use it. I expected them to have some flex, and was surprised that they did not bend at all under pressure. Now that I have gotten use to them, I am glad that they are stiff because it seems that is necessary in order to help smooth out the cellulite deposits under the skin.

While I will still have to deal with cellulite for the rest of my life, I can say that my skin does appear somewhat smoother after I use these. I received the massager kit to review and I can say that I am very happy with the results and will continue to use them. Obviously, there is no miracle cure for cellulite, but I can definitely say that my legs are less dimpled and my skin looks much nicer from all of the increased circulation after using these.

title: Avoid Rugby brand of guaifenesin
text: Guaifenesin is an ingredient of various products which help to thin mucus which is a help to people who have allergies or respiratory infections, chest congestion, etc. I have used Guaifenesin for decades and have always found this ingredient to be helpful. However, when I could not find any of my usual brands, I tried this and once was more than enough. This has way too many unwanted ingredients. Normally, I avoid artificial sweeteners, and this is "sugar free" with sucralose as the sweetener. It seems to have THREE preservatives none of which I am pleased about - methylparaben, propylparaben, and propylene glycol, then both artificial and natural cherry flavor, red food coloring #40, plus menthol, and a couple other ingredients in addition to Guaifenesin. All in all, it seems like too many additives, and it tastes VILE. I see others have mentioned the flavor, not liking the flavor - but - what is causing the bad taste is all the various garbage additives, and it's not the normal cherry syrup used in other brands of this product, whether the original Robitussin, or Waltussin. This is very watery and thin, not the usual consistency, and certainly not the usual taste - but I think the taste is coming from some of the additives. The bottle that I opened and used once - big 16 oz. bottle - is going in the garbage. It's not simply bad flavor, but I'm assuming all these various additional ingredients are what is causing the bad taste, and I'm not going to take it again. Unfortunately, I ordered TWO of the bottles. Just now, I looked at the site on Amazon where I ordered this product - AND - the list of all ingredients is entirely different on the website compared to what is on the label of this bottle. I just made a screen shot of it, perhaps to share with customer service, since the preservatives and sweetener and the syrup itself are NOT the same in the listing at the website as they are on the bottle - totally different. In any case, I recommend getting some brand other than Rugby brand of this product. I see currently this product is out of stock on Amazon, but that's a good thing - order something that is not this. Unless you have already used the brand and like it. I won't use it again, ever. I don't know if I've ever given a negative review of anything before - usually if something is mildly not what I wanted, I still don't want to be negative, but in my opnion there is no reason to buy this brand.

title: Heating area is only 12"x19". The rest is a border that doesn't have any heating properties.
text:
While this heating pad is touted as being 28” x 17.3”, that measurement is only for the entire unit. The heating area where the stones are is only 12"x19". This is also the only area of the pad that has any heating properties. This makes it rather bulky for providing such a small actual heated area.

The User Guide and Instruction Manual that comes with the pad states, "This Far Infrared Heating Pad works a little differently than your standard coiled heating pad. Please allow 5 to 10 minutes for the far infrared energy in the stones to build up and for the pad to heat up."

Well, I've had my pad plugged in and heating for over 25 minutes & it still hasn't reached the 150° temp I set it for. My house's temp is 62° & so far the best my new heating pad's controller has been able to read is 140°.

Perhaps these tourmaline & jade stones will radiate the heat more deeply into tissues, but so far I'm not convinced that this pad will be useful for any areas smaller than those mentioned in the description - back, neck & shoulder. It seems to me that attempting to use this pad in anyway other than flat out won't be easy.

title: Portable, rechargeable slippers. My icy feet can finally endure winter in comfort.
text:
These heated slippers are so great! They are wonderful to settle back & relax in the warmth they provide

But that's also where one of their drawbacks becomes apparent. When my slippers arrived I made sure to fully charge their battery packs & then settled down to enjoy their heat. Turning on the TV, I tilted back in my recliner to enjoy the evening. Now, I don't know about you, but when I lie back in the recliner I often cross my legs at the ankles. Doing that, the on/off button that is normally on the outside of each foot ends up pressed against the other slipper's on/off button. And yes, I didn't even notice it until I felt like my toasty toes weren't being toasted so much anymore. The slight shifting I'd done in my chair had turned my 'high' setting down to 'medium' on one foot & to 'low' on the other. It's a minor thing, but I wish there was some way to set the on/off button switch so it can't accidentally be changed by such a minor bumping.

My other minor quibble is with the relative 'run' time of the batteries. I like toasty feet and at the highest heat setting the instructions say I shouldn't really expect more than 2-2½ hours of use. If I'm in front of the TV for a marathon binge I can certainly spend more than 2½ hours in one evening.

Now, with that info, I explored Amazon to see if there were any questions about ordering replacement or supplemental battery packs. No questions, but a search for 'Kamlif battery' brought up just the 2-pack spare batteries that I was hoping for. As I write this they sell for $26.99. I ordered a set just so I can relax knowing that if/when one set runs down, I can replace them immediately with the back-up set.

With those slight drawbacks known, I can wholeheartedly recommend these slippers if you suffer from chronic cold feet.

title: Poor design
text:
There are three main components to this device: the foggy-clear plastic case, the cartridge with 3 interchangeable barrels, and the handle. The plastic case shields the cartridge and is placed using notches at the widest ends to snap on. However, the notches are triangle-shaped, so you have to be exact with lining it up, and it is resistant to bending, making it a hassle to put on or remove.

Changing barrels is even worse. It's not impossible but the "wings" of the handle are so resistant to bending. The alignment of the notches has to be spot-on and there isn't a comfortable way to grip the "wings" as you try to pry them apart to remove the barrel. I had to dig in with the tips of my fingers and was honestly worried about breaking my nails or accidentally punching myself in the face as I wrestled the darned device.

I need to admit that I have not tried using this item as I wanted to return it in a better condition. The sticky material does seem like it would work well. Additionally, the barrel does roll quite freely once it's on.

I purchased this with the intent of using a barrel, washing and removing it, using another barrel, etc and rotating through barrels as used ones dried off. However, the inability to comfortably exchange barrels makes this prohibitively difficult to use.

title: Heats up well but difficult to position
text:
Generally, I really like heating pads with jade and tourmaline. Although they're slower to heat up because they need to heat stones and not just wires, they hold the heat well and disperse it to ease you into and out of the heating session. That prevents any cramping from a too-fast cool-down, which I really appreciate. When it comes to that, this heating pad is no different from the other stone pads I've used. I love the way it provides heat. And it's larger than other similar pads I've used, which I really like; it can cover my whole back and not just my lower back.

However, the material is stiffer than in similar pads I've used. At first, I thought that would be a good thing and help hold it in place. However, it's not quite stiff enough to hold up to the weight of the stones, so it still needs to be held in place, and it does not come with a belt to help with that. At the same time, it's too stiff to drape and fold around my curves properly. And it gives off a chemical/plastic smell, especially once it heats up.

For those reasons, this is not my favorite jade and tourmaline heating pad. However, it also costs less than others I've used, and the heating is very good, so I consider it a decent deal.

title: App requires location permission, and belt only partially works without the app
text:
Cons:
The app does not connect with Bluetooth alone; it also requires GPS access, which I refuse to give it. Without the app, I can turn the pad on and adjust the intensity, but I cannot set the timer function. Also, although the website does not mention one way or another, the instructions included explain that there is a pulse mode. They do not explain how to turn that on, even with app. The app's links to maintenance and user manual do not go anywhere, at least with the app disconnected from GPS.

Pros:
The pad is softer than similar ones I've used. Most use a clear plastic overlay against the skin; this one is cloth, which has a nicer texture. It may make it more difficult to sanitize, but if you're the only one using it, that shouldn't be a problem. It does have multiple intensities to choose from, which allows you to choose your own comfort level. And the included battery pack means that it's portable—that's not common among such devices, but I do appreciate it a lot.

Overall, this device is OK; it's neither fantastic nor horrible, and it gets the job done.

title: Nice and powerful, but unclear instructions, only three modes
text:
As far as I can tell, there are only three modes, not six: steady red light, pulsing red light, and pulsing mixed red/infrared. Hitting the power button again after those modes turns the device off, and then it cycles through the same three modes again.

There are five intensity levels for each mode; the up and down buttons on the left control these. The buttons on the right allow you to choose the amount of time before the automatic shutoff. There is also an adapter with a power dial to vary the wattage. I cannot tell exactly how that interacts with the power levels on the controller, so that makes figuring out dosage a little difficult. It's hard to tell exactly how many watts I'm getting. Also, the adapter does start to get hot after about thirty minutes.

That said, this red-light pad is nice and powerful, and I love that it provides full-body coverage (for me; I'm 5 feet 2 inches, and the pad is 5 feet 3 inches; if you're larger, it may not work as well). Lying on it feels like lying in the sun on a moderately warm day; it's nice and energizing, and I find it provides a great boost in mood. It's also working well for my psoriasis. And it came with a carrying case for storage and goggles to protect the eyes.

So overall, I am pretty happy with it. I just wish the directions were a little clearer and the device a little cheaper.

title: Cuts Well And Easy To Use
text:
This is the first set of clippers I've owned and I am very pleased. The clippers are easy to hold and they work well. When I opened the box, the manual said to charge them although it didn't say how long it takes to charge them. They were already at 60% out of the box, so I charged them fot approximately two hours and it was not fully charged but it was pretty close. The LED indicated 80% for a lengthy time, so I knew it had to be getting close to being fully charged.

I experimented with the various sizes of cutter guards, and the lowest guard still didn't help me achieve the results I wanted for my cat. She's a domestic medium hair, so her hair isn't that long. Once I took off the guard I was able to get a better cut. Since I removed the guard I made sure to be careful not to cut too much off because I didn't want to give her a buzz cut. Thankfully it turned out well.

It was easy to disassemble the cutter for cleaning, and it quickly snapped back into place. The set includes a small brush to help clear away the loose hair around the blade, etc.

The only thing I don't particularly like is the fact that it charges through a USB port. It's more convenient to just plug things into an electrical outlet as opposed to having to use the laptop, plus I feel like USB charging takes longer. Despite the inconvenience of charging through USB, I am pleased with the clippers and the results achieved.

title: Works with remote control switches. High quality ballast.
text:
If you use remote controlled switches like X-10. You will find other brands of Full Spectrum lighting tend to use a more efficient ballast. That doesn't make them better. When you use X-10 switches there is a slight energy leak through like 1/4 watt of power. With other brand bulbs the ballast tries to be super efficient and attempt to light up the light, which results in the light flickering to no end after you shut off the light. It will eventually stop as the gas inside is no longer excited.

This product puts out good quality light. I've used them for years for just around the house.

--- Update
They have a new factory making their product. The old factory had a Hex shaped ballast. The new ones have a Round base as the one in the picture now. They don't work with X-10 switches anymore as they moved to the fast start efficient base. It flickers a bunch when turned off when plugged into a X-10 controller.

title: Unintended use
text:
This is supposed to be a dietary supplement. [Lion's mane, in case this review crosses over to other products.] I however love mushrooms and their flavor. I love mushroom umami flavor in my soups, fried taters, and eggs. This fits the bill. It may not work well for you if you want to use it primarily as a supplement. It does have a pronounced flavor. It looks and initially smells like cocoa. However, once put in anything hot (or take a GOOD whiff), the more the mushroom becomes apparent. It's easily covered up in a strong cocoa or coffee (but, it's still there). You need to double it up to use it in a serving of good soup, though.

The powder is so fine (it's just dried powdered mushrooms) and it doesn't per se "dissolve". It can be whipped into a suspension, and that's as good as it gets (if you were to drink it). In soups, it takes a lot of whisking to get it to suspend there as well.

The flavor is hard to describe. Very nice. Not as pronounced as shiitake, but, there is no salt added, so you can add as much as you need to get as much of that great flavor as you want. Chocolatey, but still mushroom.

I haven't been able to hear colors, smell sounds, or have my ability to read auras enhanced at all - but it's a GREAT addition to my spice collection. My soups, taters, and eggs thank you. Unintended use, but it works in my particular application.

This product works completely and will effectively help you out in the weight room. The big problem is that this particular form of creatine tastes much worse than others that do the same exact job. You can put unflavored creatine monohydrate into your protein shake and barely taste the difference. This ethyl ester form however will make your entire shake taste like crushed up pills. Absolutely disgusting. I question if anyone giving this product a positive review has tried another form. The flavor is at least 5 times as strong as monohydrate with the same performance, and you can even find that form for a little bit cheaper than this one.
Creatine makes me feel a little weird for a half hour so I wanted to give alternative forms like this one a try. I still feel the same weirdness from this but now I understand why this form is not common: it tastes horrible. Will throw this into the garbage where it belongs and continue on with regular creatine.

title: CEE for a NEWBIE with Stomach issues....
text:
This is not my first attempt with Creatine from Nutricost. The first was the Nutricost Creatine Micronized however due to digestion issues I couldn't make it past the first week with that stuff, it sat like a rock and was just awful. When I started GVT training, the trainer said to use Creatine along with my Protein. After explaining I couldn't handle it, CEE was suggested. I was skeptical due to the reviews on CEE from almost every body building site, as I am a "NEWBIE" at working out I didn't want to purchase something that I would waste, or worse yet not work.

I am writing this review on week 2, and so far I have had NO issues with digestions like I did with the Micro. I have tired to mix the CEE in everything from water to juice, though I feel the taste is still gross ( like metal from a battery). I mix it with the required water, hold my nose and down it like a Champ (than chase it with something else 1 or 2 sips). For people with stomach/intestine issues Crones, IBS etc... like me this might be the stuff for you. As for the size it's only week two, so I do feel stronger but that could also be a placebo effect.

The pros:
No loading time
Doesn't kill your stomach/intestines
Cheaper than other brands
Great customer service when I had questions about the product.

Cons:
Taste like metal from a battery
You do loose a bit more of the Creatine than you would with the micronized, due to how it breaks down.

Final:
I would recommend giving this a try as the NO Load times, easy on intestine and reasonably priced make this a great alternative. The only down side is you must take this first thing in the morning on no work out days, and as I keep saying oh that taste.

title: Not a good buy
text:
I bought this unit in the hopes that it would replace the other units I use for weight and fat loss. Unfortunately, it is incredibly inaccurate. I currently use two other units to determine body fat %, a scale with similar tech and a handheld unit. When I purchased this unit I used all three together as a test. The first two were consistent with what I have seen over the past few years, 16%, and the Aria came in at 25%. Way off. I did the test three times and the result was the same. Next, I tracked the change in body fat over a 3 week period. The other two showed the same change in body fat from week to week (2% over 3 weeks). The Aria only registered a .2% change in body fat over the 3 weeks (1/10th of what both the other units measured). Finally, the Aria connected to my fitbit app on my iphone the first time I used it, but wouldn't connect again after that, so I had to manually enter the weight and body fat into my app for the second and third week of use.
All in all, I plan to return the Aria. For over $100 this is unacceptable​.

Hi received a sample of this in an Amazon sample box which included household cleaning products. I have had hard water stains on the very BOTTOM of my toilet for years. Two days ago I received this sample box of cleaners and it contained a small packet of a small packet of Brite & Clean. I had never heard of it before but when I read that it took care of hard water stains, I couldn't wait to give it a shot.

I flushed the toilet and just let a few inches of water come back into the bowl and then I shut the water off from the main valve behind the toilet. I poured the entire packet right into the small area of water and went out for the day. I came home seven hours later and could not believe my eyes. Without scrubbing, my toilet was pure white again!!!! I was amazed. I wish everything worked this easily. Take it from me people, I scraped and scrubbed and used tons of chemicals and nothing worked. title: So far no data on battery life, but otherwise, 5 *****
text:
Very impressive at handling background noise. I have been buying these in this price range for a long time, and was never fully satisfied. I am NOT going to deal with a $3,000+ hearing aid salesman, because I fear my temper will land me in prison. Intense advertising budgets for these imply "WAY too much markup."
For me, the fatal flaw in all the ones I have tried is handling competing signals. I would get in the car, my wife would be talking, and as soon as she turned on the radio, I would remove the hearing aid, and put it away. It seems they all gave the entire sound spectrum the same priority in setting the gain. I don't know how this does it, but with the three programs, it was possible for me to select the best one for my particular problem. Tonight for the first time, I was able to converse with my wife while the AC was running and the TV was on. OK, I just ordered one for the other ear.
All I really question is how many charge/discharge cycles the battery is good for. That will be the limit on the lifetime of these. I am SO glad to be rid of those tiny batteries the others took, especially on the units where you open the battery door to turn them off. The battery falls out, of course, and is generally lost. It is a horrible nuisance.
The ONLY question or issue I have is the expected lifetime of the unitHow long have these been out? I'll see if anyone started a discussion about it. Otherwise at present it's 100% 5 Stars.

title: ... in the mountains where I was having too much fun and forgot to refuel
text:
This stuff has really saved me on a few occasions out in the mountains where I was having too much fun and forgot to refuel. It pushed me away from the wall faster than anything else I've tried.

Pros:
1. It works fast, faster than the GU Roctane that I will also use from time to time. In fact, after taking this stuff in, I can literally feel the surge of relief and boosted endurance in my muscles within ~10-15 minutes. Nothing else I've tried gives me such a noticeable boost.
2. The unflavored version doesn't have any flavor (or rather it has a neutral bland flavor). It is what it is.. that's a big pro for me.
3. Using a blender, I can make a calorie dense liquid that will last for hours and hours. I like to do (3) scoops in 20 ounces with 80 calories of electrolytes for 500 calories.
4. It's relatively cheap. As of this posting, this stuff is 111 calories per dollar. But you'll need to mix in your own BCAA'a and electrolytes to make it a more complete intra fuel. That could get expensive. By comparison, GU Roctane is 50 calories per dollar so it's more than twice as expensive (for the variety pack), but it has electrolytes, BCAA's and OKG to make it a more complete fuel. Maybe blend (2) scoops Vitargo and (2) GU Roctane together to make a 500 calorie super fuel?

Cons:
1. It doesn't mix that well on the go. Drinking a clumpy energy drink is distracting and I don't like it.

2. The high absorption rate causes brief stomach distress directly after ingesting. I've almost upchucked this stuff a few times, I had to slow down and walk a few minutes until the nausea passed. I think I can experiment with taking smaller sips more often to fix this, but for now I am calling it a con.

title: Great for Heartburn!
text: This stuff is amazing. I have had asthma since I was 3 years old, and started getting acid reflux symptoms when I was about 15 or so (I'm 30 now). I got fed up with taking both advair and whatever heartburn med I was on at the time (most recently, prevacid). The meds worked, but I was worried about long term side effects, so I bought the book "why stomach acid is good for you" by Jonathan Wright. He suggests increasing your stomach acid to reduce heartburn symptoms (counter intuative, I know, but brilliant) and argues why turning off your acid production is a bad solution. Anyway, one of the first recommendations he makes on how to treat yourself is bitters. They don't taste great, but it's doable. I mix about a teaspoon or so in a couple tablespoons of water and sip slowly, really making sure to taste it (that's the whole point - this is the signal to your stomach). I've quit prevacid cold turkey before and after a few days had a lot of heartburn pain/burping/hiccups and waking up in the middle of the night. This time, I quit cold turkey, but also added bitters into the mix. The heartburn totally went away. I even went to france right after and ate lots of cheese and drank coffee, along with all sorts of other bad habits. The other good news is that I am off my asthma meds too, and symptom free! I think bitters is a huge part of my success in quitting medication. I dont have to take bitters all the time anymore, maybe once every couple days if I feel a relapse coming on(mostly from drinking too much coffee!) It ends up being cheaper, and in my opinion, healthier, than the pharmaceutical option.

title: First impressions:  Ahhhhhhh....ooohhhh....relief!
text:
I just received this day before yesterday so this is an initial impressions review. I'll follow up in a few weeks.

First, I bought this for my office chair, which is an excellent chair with lots of adjustment knobs and levers that I bought (lightly used) for home use 12 years ago. I've now been working from home for almost 5 years, and the seat recently just seemed to turn to concrete. For weeks I've been unwilling to get on an exercise bike after sitting all day because my tush hurt so much, and it finally got to the point that two hours in this chair had me squirming in pain, my whole lower back hurting. Replacing the whole chair seemed ridiculous: everything is in great shape except the seat cushion, and getting a chair with a similar set of adjustments would be well over $300 (this chair retailed for $330 in the late '90s.) So, for weeks I used various cushions from around the house (including memory foam), a borrowed wheel chair cushion with gel, 3 layers of an excellent closed-cell foam exercise mat: nothing helped.

I used this WonderGel Extreme Orthopedic Seat Cushion yesterday for the first time, and sat 6 straight hours with no problems at all. I worked a couple of more hours in the evening, no problems. This truly feels heaven-sent. I highly recommend it for any use - office chair, wheel chair, full-time driving, etc. It has a good cover on it; one side has a no-slip texture to prevent the cushion from slip-sliding when in use, and a sturdy carrying handle. This version is not light: it seems to weigh about 5 or 6 lbs, or as I told one friend, "think laptop not netbook" if you're thinking of lugging it around. They do seem to have lighter models, including the Orthopedic Wondergel (Intelli-gel) Roll & Go - Gel Seat Cushion, which at 1 inch would be half the depth and less than half the weight (the dimensions are slightly smaller). The original model is 1.5 inches, same dimensions as this model, and comes in at 3.9 pounds, so my guess on the weight of this one is about right. (http://www.amazon.com/Wondergel-Original-Gel-Seat-Cushion/dp/B004EMXZKW/ref=pd_bxgy_hpc_text_b) For occasional use (driving, stadium, church or theater seats, etc) I would have gone with the one of the lighter models, but for full-time use I'm guessing this is the better choice, though it might be more than is needed for a petite woman.

Overall, remarkable set of products, highly recommended.

title: Worth every penny if you suffer from neck pain, arthritis, fibromyalgia, etc.
text:
For someone with neck pain or other physical challenges that make reading difficult or painful, this product is excellent!! Setup was easy and it functions as advertised. Despite the heavily weighted base, it rolls around easily, even on carpet. Works well on hardbacks or paperbacks. Although my focus is on its use for those of us with physical challenges, it has also occured to me that I could now take up knitting while reading, if I were so inclined!

What you don't see in the picture are the straps holding the book. The metal plate that holds the book has two sturdy velcro straps that run through holes on the top and bottom of the plate and which are threaded through plastic plates that look similar to the weight-distribution pads found on a luggage shoulder strap. You place the front and back of the book under these plastic plates and pull the straps tight. (At this point the pages are free floating.) You then use the arms seen in the picture to hold the pages in place.

Why this and not a simple table top book holder? If you are simply trying to free up your hands for note taking, or looking for a cookbook holder, etc., you don't neeed this. Get a $5 (wire) - $20 tabletop book holder. If, however, you need a book holder with adjustable height in order to avoid extended periods of neck flexion while reading with a book in your lap (or even on a table top), this is the only solution I've found. And yes, if you need full neck support while reading you can use it as shown: lying back and using a neck roll, etc.

Overall, great product, excellent vendor, HIGHLY recommended for those with special needs.

title: Not ultrasonic as advertised
text:
The ad and the package both state it is an "ultrasonic" sound device. It is not! It is a sonic sound device.
What is the difference between sonic and ultrasonic?
Ultrasonic "sound" waves are not audible to human hearing, whereas, you can actually hear the sounds produced by sonic sound units.
You can hear the buzzing sound produced by these units, hence they ARE NOT ultrasonic. That being said, might they still actually work to keep the moles at bay? Maybe; only time will tell since I don't expect feedback from the moles.
However, because I also treat the invaded area with the caster oil/detergent/mint solution, I may never know if these truly ran them off or if it was the caster oil treatment or a combination of the two. But the devices are more-or-less a set-it-and-forget-it device, I figured I can't go wrong with just leaving it in place until it either stops functioning or I smash it with the lawnmower wheel, whichever comes first.

UPDATE: Not only is it not ultrasonic as previously mentioned, (for whatever good that would do, even if), it is woefully ineffective. Look at the photo taken on 12/15. The mole/vole/giant earthworm/prairie dog, whatever it is, dug a new tunnel within about 18 inches of this device that was emitting its "uh, ultrasonic" audible sound every 20 seconds. Now, they never showed up again in the area where I soaked the soil with the caster oil/Dawn/mint mixture. I had not sprayed this area because, well, I guess I'm a sucker for a gimmick and I was cautiously optimistic that this just might show some promise. Well, now I'm playing hardball with a more "permanent" means of eradication.

title: NOT a placebo, these things work!
text:
I used to dread taking drives because it was a given my son would get carsick and vomit on any drive more than 5 minutes.

I was at a point that I was going to turn him forward facing to see if that helps, since every other recommendation was unsuccessful. He is within the weight to safely do so, but keeping them rear facing as long as possible is statistically safer overall in the event of a crash.

As a last resort, I bought a pair of these. Since wearing these he has not vomited on ANY car ride and his carseat remains rear facing.

Some people say these are a placebo and don’t work. I don’t know how the placebo effect would apply to a toddler who has no idea what the intended purpose of these are.

Proper placement I believe is critical for these to be effective. Luckily, my son does not mess with them at all.

There are cheaper alternatives available that will probably work the same, but this particular brand may be more durable and better quality stitching/materials overall; I’ll stick with these!

To sum up, it’s worth a shot giving these type of
wristbands a try before resorting to medications or in conjunction with. I’ve recommended these to all our friends who are in the same situation.
