title: Don't waste your money
text:
I have never regretted a purchase this bad before. I have owned this unit for 5 months now and I am buying the Silver lungs generator to replace it.

I don't know where to start with this. My first impression was that someone made this with a trip to home depot and $20 bucks. It leaked from day one and one of the 9 volt batteries that were sealed in the cap where almost dead. Yes, I said sealed in the cap, with glue!

The ionic silver made from this machine is so weak it is practically useless. It failed the milk test. I also gave some to a friend for her daughter for her acne to spray on her face. She was using a 10 ppm spray from Silver Wings and having great results. When she ran out, I gave her some of the stuff I made with this. She might as well have been spraying distilled water on her face. All of her acne started coming back immediately.

According to Silver lungs these guys have no idea of what they are talking about and the size of ion particles is more like .23nm not 10 nm. NO PARTCILES are created whatsoever in a colloidal silver generator. ONLY (ions) are dissolved from the electrodes. So what is this 10nm thing all about? TEM analysis creates particles that weren't originally there after you evaporate the water so it is not the correct way to test for particle size.

This product claims 10 ppm after 35 minutes. What they don't tell you is that to them, 4 ppm is 10 ppm and they have an equation they use to justify it. Every other generator on the market uses a 10 ppm reading on TDS meters. The standard that people have been using and is effective is 10 ppm on a TDS meter. Even if that is really more than 10 ppm when converted, it is the measurement everyone uses and compares to. I have tried to make 10 ppm with a TDS meter on this unit and it took me over a hour. It was a pain because I had to clean the silver 4 times. The quality was poor with debris in the water.

This is a very poorly made product. Even the silver they give you is cut in a way that the ends of the wires have sharp edges that promote silver oxidation build up. The Silver lungs generator has 7 guage silver rods that are smooth all over and polished.

I have an idea. Instead of posting tests showing the size of your particles, why not test your solution to see if it really works?

P.S. the company itself has downvoted my review so that it had less effect on the overall score. How else can my review get downvoted within an hour of posting. I also don't believe all of these reviews are real.

title: Worth getting addicted to...especially if you like really Dark Chocolate
text:
I saw the words "Dark Chocolate" and I lit up. For years now we have been enjoying the lower sugar and positive effects of dark chocolate, braving all the way up to a smooth and cool 90% cocoa -- That's right up there with baking chocolate. I didn't let myself expect much from a commercially made probiotic, and maybe that has to do with my happy surprise. But let me start with the fact that the chocolate is 64% cocoa! Not bad, not bad at all for dark chocolate lovers.

They are the size of a rounded quarter and have a firmness that allows them to be savored - they melt just like a piece of chocolate would. If you are a dark chocolate lover you will appreciate the slight tang and less syrupy sweetness that accompanies milk chocolate. These are really pleasing and they tout that their flora survives our stomach acid 100X better! It took me 4 days, to notice the shift. My roommate took 10 but we both commented on the absence of feeling bloated after dinner and the regularity that ensued (Okay I have to confess that I would often take one at lunch AND dinner)!

These are NOT laxatives but candy bites that are packed with Probiotics or "good bacteria" the stomach needs to help digest our food and maintain a healthy balance of energy and fuel. So rather than feeling that your food takes hours to digest there is really a sense that things are more efficiently being broken down in the intestines. It's not an uncomfortable feeling at all (but could be if you over do them).

They don't taste like they smell, so don't dig your nose in and take a big whiff anticipating a nice rich chocolate smell...You won't. What matters is the flavor and the results both of which you will get.

title: Having used Woolite with cold water on clothing and towels, I would never go back to detergents.
text:
We have been using Woolite in cold water for all of our clothes and towels for over 3 years. Previous to this, we used the usual name brand laundry detergents and either warm water for colors or hot water for whites. In time, colors faded, tee-shirts became shorter, towels were less absorbent, etc. This was all accepted as the result of aging fabrics. Woolite was only for hand washing delicates in cold water, right? We thought clothes just wouldn't get clean if we didn't use either hot or warm water washes.

I read an article about using cold water for laundering clothes that stated hot or warm water was not necessary. The article suggested Woolite for a laundry detergent and white vinegar for softening. Having used standard laundry detergents and fabric softener for over 40 years, this was a totally new concept for me, but I decided to try it.

As mentioned earlier, I have been using Woolite in cold water for all of our clothes and towels for over 3 years. What I have noticed is t-shirts I have bought since have not shrunk, faded, or become misshapen. Towels I bought over 2 years ago still look like new and are just as absorbent, if not more so. By using white vinegar as a softener, everything seems even softer than it did when I used fabric softer, and nothing holds wrinkles or creases.

In addition to all of the benefits mentioned, washing in cold water saves energy since the water does not to be heated, and vinegar is much less expensive than fabric softener. Personally, I would never go back to the old way of laundering clothes and towels.

I hope this review was helpful for you. If so, please click the helpful button.

Since I am a first-time user of this type of product, I decided to read the user instructions so that I didn't damage my skin. The first problem that I encountered was that the user instructions are microscopic. I couldn't read them even with a magnifying glass. I tried scanning them into my computer to enlarge them, but they still were not legible. After contacting the seller about this problem, they did send me a .PDF that still needed to be enlarged to be legible. Prior to getting the legible instructions, I tried winging it, and ended up with a big red mark on my face that took two weeks to go away.

After the red marks healed, I tried it again per the instructions, and was able to remove the couple of blackheads that I had. The other problems that I had with the instructions is that they mention the supplied filters should be changed periodically, but they don't say where they go or how to install them. I found out how to do this from the reviews of a similar product. There are also rubber gaskets included, but I still don't know where these go or how they are used. Although the instructions describe the four suction cones, they do not offer suggested uses for each. This information would also be very useful for the user.

Other than the user instructions that leave much to be desired, I would give this product a 5 star rating, but I feel the poor and tiny user instructions may cause someone to do damage to their skin as I did.

text: I have a busy lifestyle. I have 2 kids under 5, a full time job AND I squeeze a workout in almost every week day. So a QUICK and EASY energy bar is my JAM. I like this one but I am trying to watch what I eat(especially my sugar intake) and I don't workout more than 30 min a day which means I am not able to justify all the extra carbs this bar provides. BUT - if you need a quick and easy pick me up after a hard day at work and before a quick 30 min workout in the evening, a couple of these cubes will give you the energy you need. I split the bar with my husband on days I need the energy and i am able to complete my workout without stopping in between. I wont have this as a pre workout every time i workout though. The sugar and calorie are super high for my lifestyle. This may be OK for a very active,athletic teenager. 4 stars.

title: We just finished our last packet..
text: We don't give this to my daughter everyday but every other day. It has 30 packets of powder you can pour directly onto tongue if they are 3 years and older.My little one does not like that so we mix with water or juice. It is supposed to help improve with your child's immunity and respiratory system on top of the probiotic benefits. We haven't really seen a difference or improvement per say (its only 1 box had over 2 month frame) but I'm sure this will help in the long run if had regularly. Its convenient and the water/ juice is sweetened which isn't ideal but its not bad for your child's teeth. I still feel like the price in on the expensive side especially if you want to give this to them everyday. I will stick to every other month for now and continue giving her a multi vitamin and yogurt.

title: Great Tasting, But Only 1 Strain
text: I love a vegan gummy. No need to use animal byproducts anymore! These taste really good, but they do stick in your teeth a little bit. No big deal, in my opinion. My major complaint is that for the price and quantity, these should contain more than 1 strain of probiotic.

title: Great for Many Uses!
text: I like pure luffa for many uses. Two of my favorite uses are exfoliating dead skin and cleaning my cast iron pans. For the pans, you can slice these luffa into 3 pieces so you get more uses out of them. You can Google 20 more uses for these around the house! These are definitely genuine luffa and I'm pleased with this purchase.

title: Great value!
text: These vitamin D gummies are easy to chew, they taste great, and they keep my levels high enough. For some reason my body doesn't maintain vitamin D levels on its own even though I live in the south and get a lot of sunlight. The last time I had it tested, my level was 1 and should have been above 13 to be considered "low," so I was "critically low." After repeated tests over the course of 2 years, my doctor said I would need to supplement forever. I started off with RX vitamin D and then weaned to daily supplements. My levels are better and I am not so exhausted all the time. I was retested last week and have maintained my levels using these gummies and as a bonus, I don't have to swallow a horse pill!

title: I have two large dogs
text: I have 2 large dogs and my vet recommends giving them glucosamine and chondroitin with MSM. When I had the chance to try these supplements, I jumped at the opportunity. My dogs didn't get any tummy upset from the switch and they're running around like usual on their old bones! Only time and consistency will tell if these hip supplements really do what they claim, but for now I'm happy.

title: Smells right
text: Sometimes you order lavender essential oil and it has an off-smell, but this one has the perfect balance of earthy and floral, just as a lavender EO should smell. The size of the bottle is large, so it will last you forever, and it came with a glass dropper that screws on. The bottle arrived with a plastic plug under the screw cap to prevent leakage during shipping and it worked! I would buy this again.

title: Increasing my neck flexibilty
text: The directions say to start with 2 minutes and gradually increase to 10 minutes per day. The first night, my head wouldn't reach bend back enough to reach the bed underneath, so I knew I would need to spend some time stretching with this device. By the end of the first week, my head easily reached the bed as I was able to increase my time on the device. This means I can turn it around and use it in the other direction to increase my flexibility even more. The material is on the harder side, but has give to it. The first couple times I used it, I thought it was a little unpleasant, but after that, it felt perfectly fine. I can feel a good stretch happening right at the base of my skull where my neck starts. I'm hoping to recreate the natural curvature in my neck that I've lost as I've aged and treated my body poorly.

title: Lightened my stains
text: This stain remover smells AMAZING! I tried it on a splatter of spaghetti sauce and on an ink stain. It didn't fully remove either one when used as the instructions say, but it DID lighten the stains. I'm thinking this will be a good product to take when I travel (because of its small size) as a pre-treatment so when I get home I can better treat the harder to remove stains like ink or red sauce. This stain remover would probably work really well for kid's markers and other common/ easy to remove stains. I'm just happy to have fewer toxins in my life, so this product is a keeper.

title: Deliciously sweet/tart
text: Perfect flavor balance between sweet and tart with no strange aftertaste. Will be my new go-to.

title: Odd thumb placement
text: These gloves arrived nicely packaged and they're thick, soft inside, and durable. My only complaint is that they fit weird because of where the thumb is placed. Otherwise, the fingers fit well, if not a little big, but the thumb needed to be placed more to the outside edge of the palm section in order to fit properly. I think for $15 for 4 pairs, it's a fair deal, but I'd like to find a pair that fits better.

title: PRETTY FEET IN THE BLINK OF AN EYE...
text:
I have to say that within a matter of a minute or two of using this callous remover, I had pretty feet. Gone were the rough, scaly patches of dry, dead skin on my feet and heels. Instead, my feet and heels were smooth to the touch. This callous remover gently buffs away hard, dry, dead scaly skin quickly and effortlessly. It comes with an extra buffing roller and may be used on wet or dry skin.

This callous remover, for which I paid a discounted price in exchange for an impartial review, is comfortable to hold and easy to use. It is certainly easier and less tiring to use than a pumice stone, which requires endless rubbing. The callous remover does, however, require two AA batteries, which the buyer must supply. It is definitely worth it, as the results are terrific.

title: Does Freshen Up Bathroom
text: No bathroom is complete without something designed to freshen up after “business” is conducted. This product gets things back on track…it smells fresh but not like “cover up” sprays. I try to spritz one shot into the toilet first, then a shot into the air afterwards. It works well.

title: Could Use Better Design
text: While I like the concept of this product, it has some issues. First, it's not USB chargeable. Most similar products are. Second, the various functions are indicated on the face of the product with non illuminated symbols. So if it's dark in the room, as is often the case with a sleeping child's room, you can't see the symbols to see what you're trying to turn on. Lastly, the light is too bright, in my opinion, to be used as a nightlight. I would pass on this and look for something with better function.

title: Nice, But Not Very soft
text: These are nice brushes but, contrary to the description, they are not soft. They are pretty firm, actually. But they are well made and I like that they have wooden, not plastic, handles. I keep them on hand for overnight guests who might have forgotten to bring a toothbrush.

title: Nice Glasses, But Heavy
text: These lenses are very well made. They are quite clear and the magnification is true out to the very edges of the lens. They are genuinely spring hinged, not like some of the cheap "spring hinge" frames which aren't "springy" at all and will break if you apply any pressure. I actually stepped on these and didn't ruin them. My biggest complaint is that they are heavy. They hurt the bridge of my nose if I wear them for long periods of time. Other than that, I think they are very good.

title: Floss breaks way too easy.
text: As a lifelong flosser I was excited to try this floss.  I like the feel of it, its thin and seems to dig in to any buildup on my teeth.  Thats where the good review ends.  The box and metal cutter are pretty flimsy and I am always in danger of loosing the end of the floss back into the box.  The biggest concern I have is the weakness of the thread.  My first floss lasted a few seconds and the floss broke.  A second peace broke in the same spot. After four breaks I pulled out a different brand and flossed that tooth with no breakage.  I tried going back to my original floss and broke it twice before a successful round could be completed.  One break or two I can understand but this was too much.  The slightest sharp edge on a tooth renders this worthless.

title: Good Lotion But Strong Smell
text: This is a good lotion that absorbs well and leaves skin feeling soft. The fragrance is similar to Jergens original; a cherry-almond scent. I think this is a bit stronger smelling than the Jergens, though. I deducted a star simply because the fragrance is overpowering to me.  Other than that, the performance of the lotion is good.

title: Excellent value.
text: The plains of northern central Montana are so dry in the winter! With frigid temps bringing constant heating and icy winds tearing at your nostrils many a nose bleed happens this time of year. While I don't suffer from the frequent nose bleeds my family and friends do, I'll get so dry it gives me headaches. This saline works wonders at slowing the misery down and works just as well as the name brand I was buying at the local big box store.

title: Manufactured in the US too!
text: I was really pleased with these. Easy to take and didn't upset my stomach as long as I took it before bed. If you're sensitive to iron like I am you will want to watch out for that as the iron dosage is high.

title: Dunno if it works or doesn't work
text: These little sticks slide into the drain. I don't know if they work or not, but they cause no harm. The scent is negligible; nothing to notice after taking it out of the bag.  Maybe after I use the whole package I'll notice the difference when I no longer use them.  No complaints.

title: I don't wear heels often
text: I don't often wear heels -- like just a few times a year, when I have to.  These pads on the balls of my feet help take the edge off.  Feel like running shoes? No.  But its something!  I don't wear them everyday, but for when I need those heels, these fit the bill.

title: Not For Me
text: I did not find these to suit.  Too soft is a big thing to me.  I guess for some it will be just fine.

title: I Shampooed A Dirty Nubuck Leather Boot Using This & It Delivered
text: Knowing that peroxide is akin to bleach I decided to take a chance and generously spray a light tan colored nubuck western boot with this.  The boot had some dirt and water stains and I was curious if this would do something better than Lincoln Easy Cleaner for suede and nubuck leathers.  Importantly I did not leave it on longer than five minutes and then doused it again and used a brass brush (the right abrasiveness because brass is softer than steel and has finer tines).  Brushing with the brass brush quite aggressively seemed to get results but I wouldn't know until the leather dried and lightened up (anything wet makes nubuck darker).  I am glad to say it did a good job removing dirt and water spotting.  I rinsed the boot thoroughly to wash away both the dirt and the peroxide.  Then I dried overnight on the famous PEET BOOT DRYER.  Come morning it looked good but a little dry.  I was please because it looked clean and even if a bit dry.  To finish it I gave it a good finishing treatment of delicate cream which is something that replinishes moisture but when it dries to the touch the leather comes back lighter as  in this  case the original color.  After I was sure it was dry it looked perfect and I sealed it with Scotchgard for suede.  This delivered for me in this use.  You just need to remember this can change the color of some leathers just like bleach on fabric.  I wouldn't advise leaving it on to dry.  Nope, apply it, agitate according to the leather,  wash off, and dry very slowly.  Treat leather with appropriate conditioning then seal the deal with invisible Scotchgard.

title: Using In Stain Removals For Suede
text: I was looking for a magic bullet to clean suede at my shoe repair shop.  I'm still experimenting but so far have not been overly impressed by the lifting or elimination of stubbord stains in taupe suede for instance.  Not that it has done any damage as it did not change the color of the Taupe Suede Birkenstocks and Clarks Desert Boots which are medium light suede.  I will mix it with Lincoln EZ cleaner ( a decent suede cleaning product you mix with water) and it may only slightly increase the efficacy of the Lincoln product's cleaning ability.  I've been threatening to get some club soda to use instead of water and see if that does anything special???  If I figure out a good mix of this and anything I'll report back.

title: One Of The Better Made Low-Cost Multi-Pair Sets
text: I love having reading glasses all over the place so I'm able to grab a pair whenever needed.  Of course I've keyed on lower cost ones with this shotgun approach.  Many cheap glasses only last a few weeks to months and either I break them or lose them.  These are a definite cut above.  Made to a higher standard I anticipate having these a long time and actually having some pride of ownership where I'll be a bit more careful because they look great as well.  The 1.5 strength was accurate and they get the job done well.

title: Works well but isn’t non toxic
text: It is great for its scent and washing ability however it is not non toxic for our bodies so I can’t wait for them to make an organic line but for now we use this on stains and large items like blankets.

Made in China.

title: Interesting, Fun, But Not Without Issues - The Quest Doesn't Work So Well For My Needs
text:
The Hoover BH70700 Quest 700 Bluetooth robotic floor vacuum is easy to setup, including the Bluetooth connection to your phone. The box has basic instructions in the inside flap and is pretty much all that is needed to have the Quest 700 doing its job.

The Quest isn't noisy at all. It is actually quiet compared to other units on the market. It does okay on our ceramic floors and moves around at a surprising pace. There are a few areas I had trouble. I have a plush carpet. The Quest has a harder time maneuvering on this thick carpet. It travels at less than half speed compared to the hard ceramic floor and the worst part, it gets stuck easily on anything on this carpet. I don't understand why, but the speaker stands for my surround sound system seem to attract the Quest. The stands have a base that is about 1/2 inch high and the Quest always gets hung up on the base. I have to physically get up and move the Quest off of the base to allow it to continue.

The Bluetooth phone connection works better compared to the IR remote that also came with the Quest. The IR remote is only line of sight, meaning the remote has to be pointed at the vacuum to work. If the Quest is behind something, the IR remote will not work. The Bluetooth remote works even if the Quest is behind furniture or walls with in about 15 to 20 feet. With this Bluetooth app you can steer the vacuum away from trouble areas, command it to spot clean, go home to charge, and a number of other functions. The Bluetooth also allows you to program a schedule for the Quest. This is convent, but it would be nicer if the unit could just navigate on its own without my intervention.

Run time varies depending on the floor type. On the ceramic flooring it will run a good 35 to 45 minutes. On the carpet this time is reduced to about 20 to 30 minutes before it starts looking for the charging station.

The collection chamber is easy to remove, open and clean out. The volume of the container is rather small requiring frequent emptying.

In our bedroom we also have plush carpet. The Quest would make its way under our dresser. The dresser has a wood skirt around its base. Once Quest is under the dresser, no matter how hard it tries it can't find its way back out. This is a major pain as it always stops way in the back near the wall making it very difficult to retrieve. Because of these issue I can only give it 3 stars.

All in all it is on par with others in the market place and might be what you need or looking for. If not for our carpeted areas my star rating would have been higher. The carpet and hang ups are my issues.

title: Great Supplement But Only a 20 Day Supply
text:
This is a 20 day supply. You are supposed to eat three gummies per day.

They taste okay but not great. Still, it's an easy way to get the omegas into my diet. There are lots of nutritional benefits to these supplements. I especially like that they reduce inflammation.

I do find it a bit pricey for only a 20 day supply.

title: Good Toothpaste That Tastes Good and Works Great
text:
This toothpaste tastes very good and does a good job of cleaning my teeth.

I was particularly looking for a whitening toothpaste with fluoride. I also wanted a product that had few chemicals.

I like that the toothpaste was developed by dentists.

title: Highly Recommend This Sleep Mask
text:
I have worn a sleep mask every night for many years. They help me attain excellent sleep, and I highly recommend them.

This particular mask has made me very happy. It successfully blocks out all light. It helps me go to sleep quickly and sleep soundly.

It is a 3D style mask which means it provides a concave kind of shell over your eyes. I prefer this kind because it prevents any scratches on the eyes if I open my eyes during the night.

It fits snugly, and I've had no problem with it slipping off during sleep. I highly recommend this sleep mask.

title: good in my tool kit
text: I had a friend who was a dentist and he gave me old tools when he was replacing them. These are not close to the quality of real tools. But I used them for various projects around the house and these are good enough for that. The most frequent tool I used was what I called the poky think - the sharp, curved tool that  is used for scraping off plaque and other junk. The set will continue to help me get into small areas, push release levers, etc. I would run of I saw my dentist using a set of this quality, but for home use it is fine.

title: work, but really small
text: These are definitely made for keeping in a pocket/purse for reading menus or other short-term reading. They are too small to read more than that. They really do fit in a small space and are great for back-up use. But not for reading a novel.

title: No. Just no.
text:
There were no instructions, but there was tape on the screen and a slot in the frame, so I figured I would just remove the tape backing and put it in the frame. It does not fit.

The packaging gave their web site so I thought that would help me put it on correctly. Unfortunately it is only in Korean with no "english" option and Google can't translate the page.

The plastic is very thin - the same weight as used for school report covers.

It does not wrap around, so it does nothing to protect from the side.

I got this thinking it would be great for an upcoming (necessary) flight. I am not going to bother. It is flimsy, looks like the screen will fall off right away, and does nothing to protect me from anyone in my row. I will stick with double masking.

I am very disappointed.

title: Good, but wish the velcro matched and was reversed
text:
This is lightweight, which is good as it does not drag down. The only complaint I have is that I wish they had used black Velcro for my black item. The wide white tape just doesn't cut it for me. I know from experience it will also get filled with black junk, either from this or other darks I wash it with shedding. I have closed the velcro completely before washing, but I know fuzz happens. Other than that I like it a lot. I appreciate the addition of a hanging loop (white again, but that makes it easy to find). I can keep it on a hook next to the shower to prevent the "whoops" factor.

When I wear it so the velcro does not totally meet it is uncomfortable. The scratchy side of the velcro is on the side that touches my skin. I don't know why they did it that way. It hurts and the problem could have been avoided if they put the soft side on the outer section and the scratchy side on the side that never touches your body.

I was concerned about it saying "plus sized" as I am not there (yet!), but it fits me, normally a medium, just fine. I think it would fit even a size small adult, it just might not overlap the whole way across the top if the user's bust was smaller.

title: way too fine a powder
text: This is way too fine a powder.  Its like trying to eat baby powder.  This makes it hard to measure and mix.  The taste is ok but I'd rather just use fresh spinach - it makes less mess.

title: I love the texture
text:
These vibrating sensory balls were a bigger hit than I expected. As an adult, I love the texture -without the vibrations. There is a little vibrating machine that is inside the pillow that works only when squeezing. I found it to be more annoying than massaging. Fortunately, it is easily removed.

My kids, on the other hand, both love the pillow and the vibrating function. An argument immediately ensued over who would get the pillow etc

If you have more than 1 child, make sure you get more than 1 pillow. Or, just keep it for yourself to soothe away the kids' arguments ;)

title: Make sure you buy one for each kid
text:
These vibrating sensory balls were a bigger hit than I expected. I like the texture without the vibrations. There is a little vibrating machine that is inside the pillow that works when squeezing which I personally found to be more buzzing than massaging and therefore annoying. My kids, on the other hand, both love it. An argument immediately ensued over who would get the pillow.

If you have more than 1 child, make sure you get more than 1 pillow ;)

title: Great light duty mop
text: This is the perfect mop for hardwood and laminate floors.  It is made of a lightweight plastic and using it on tile or very dirty surfaces might be a bit tough.  The pads are slightly oversized which helps protect the floor from scratches.  The reservoir is what I consider midsized.  It is smaller than my curent mop but larger than others that I have seen.  To insert it, simply apply firm pressure until it pops in.  To remove, just pull.  The pads are easy to launder - just do not use any sort of fabric softener or dryer sheets on them.

title: Great gag gift
text: This is a great gag gift. The roll is smaller than a normal TP roll.  The graphics are cute and colorful.  It is also perfect to use as a streamer etc.  I would not use it as actual toilet paper lest it clog our plumbing.

title: Horrible instructions
text:
A friend recommended getting a facial steamer so I jumped at the opportunity to try this. The instructions are awful. I actually thought I'd missed a page. The angle of the steam piece is weird. The reservoir gets put in upside down so I end up spilling water on the floor. And there is a mystery basket piece that I can not figure out what to do with.

Its small and lightweight are perhaps the best I can say. For $40, I expected better.

title: Wish the handle were longer
text: I wish the handle on this were longer.  While I can appreciate that the intent is to have something portable, having it be so short renders it almost unusable on my neck/back.  If you can manage to use it (or have someone else use it on you) it feels great and definitely helps to loosen those deep knots.

title: Dont love the taste but they work well
text:
I dont love the taste on these flossers. They are minty but there is a bit of an aftertaste that is a little unpleasant.

They work very well. The floss thickness is perfect and the pick works well. It comes divided into 4 plastic storage cases which I like better than just having loose flossers in a bag that gets knocked off the counter and some fall out.

title: NO Instructions!
text:
I requested this because I remember seeing that red wave light is good for acne prone skin. I was surprised to find the box on my doorstep - with just a label on it. No wrapping, instructions or any other info of any other sort. The lights are super bright but I have no idea how I'm supposed to use them. Honestly, they remind me of grow lights I ordered a bit ago.

With no safety info or instructions, I'm certainly not going to have my teen use this to 'see' if it improves her acne!

title: Assembly required
text: This is a decent banner but you have to put it together yourself.  I wish there were blanks that could go between the words rather than smooshing everything together.  The material is fairly decent - if you are careful, you might get to reuse it for future grads (minus the dated ones).

title: Cute set
text:
This is a cute set that will entertain the tween set for a bit. The creating part is fun - I could see getting a few sets and using them at a slumber party and sending the guests home for their baths. I'm not quite sold on the 'stem' portion. Sure, they'll get some science out of it but depending on how the parent presents it, it may or may not stick so to speak.

Still, a decent fun set at an affordable price.

title: WHY isnt a Wall charger included???
text:
I'm so tired of companies selling things that run on electricity but not including a wall charger. This is even worse - it does not run on a reg usb charger - it has its own sort of plug but you need to plug it into your own wall charger!

There are a number of different sounds that are available on this machine - pretty much something for just about everyone. The on/off switch is a bit odd - not the conventional symbol, but I'll get used to it.

title: Confusing
text:
So, this is a confusing item. The listing says "Instant dissolving: Compared with traditional laundry tablets, Ohuhu laundry tablets have no residue and fast dissolving effect" Based on that, I requested it. But they're laundry sheets. Even better since I have to go the laundromat to wash bulky items occasionally. I figured this would be great to have for then.

But the back of the product says "Place the color & dirt catcher sheet and clothes into the washing machine adding laundry detergent as normal." Huh? You also need to add extra sheets per 6kg worth of laundry. (Who weights their laundry?)

I used it as I thought it was supposed to .... as a laundry sheet but now I'm confused as to what this is.

title: Not my favorite but pretty good
text: These are not my favorite elderberry chews but they are pretty good.  I like that I only need take  1 vs the 2 I need with my other brand.  I also like that they are a little less sticky than other brands.  On the negative side the taste is not as great as my favorite brand (though better than others I've tried!)  Packaging is also excessive.  It comes in a big jar that could easily hold 3x as much as it does.  That makes it wasteful and it takes up far more space than it needs to in my cabinets.

title: Its huge
text:
I have 2 of these already and this one is HUGE - think family sized. So if everyone in your family is out and about, this might be the one for you. In our family, my husband and I are the only one who go out and never at the same time so this size is overkill for us. I'm also confused why the light portion of the top is separate and has to be connected separately. Yes, it does make it fold smaller but it also is a bit confusing.

The rack included is nice and IMO a necessity. Having a rack means both sides of your items get disinfected at the same time.

Overall, this is a nice unit for those who require a bigger disinfecting station.

title: Measure carefully
text:
I'm not sure what size trashcan this is supposed to fit but it clearly isnt mine. Its wide and short rather than the skinny tall bags I've always seen.

The bags seem thick and sturdy - definitely more so than regular bags I've used. Sadly they wont work in my trashcan

title: Distinctly different sizes
text:
I got these because my daughter is already tired of plain masks. Out of the package, it was clear that the 2 masks are different sizes. No idea how/why. The black mask fits me reasonably well and is comfortable. The red mask is far too small but fits my 10yo well.

They're pretty and one fits each of us well but I was expecting 2 masks that fit the same.

text:
I am disappointed with this mask holder. The slots are very small - really do not work with cloth masks. These WILL work with the thin cords of disposable masks - but nothing is said in the listing.

text:
This has just about everything I want in a supplement. Vit C, Elderberry, garlic, vit B.... if it had calcium, it would be perfect!

I also appreciate that you only have to take 2 capsules a day and that at $15.00 it is reasonably priced.

title: I like it
text:

title: This Cat Ball Traumatized My Parents' Cat, Angel; She is Now Afraid of My Parents' House!
text:
I must be honest and say that my parents' adopted stray cat, Angel, never did like plastic balls of any size. I think it is because they are too hard for her to sink her claws and teeth into them. Normally, Angel will attack tiny plush animals that have feathers and fur sticking out of them and hollowed bellies carefully stuffed full of catnip. However, I thought she might like Coubon's Interactive Cat Ball because it has lights and sounds. Unfortunately, instead of attacking the ball, like I thought she would, she ran from it in terror. We had her in the kitchen of my parent's home. Normally, Angel isn't allowed unsupervised in the main floor of their home because she sheds too much; instead, she lives in my dad's basement workshop.

When Angel saw the ball's lights and heard its sounds, she ran in terror to the basement door, crying to be let out so she could return to her bed. My parents have tried several times to get her to like the Interactive Cat Ball but she is too terrified of it. Now, whenever she walks into the kitchen from the outdoor patio, she becomes scared, thinking that ball might still be around, and darts to the basement door, where she cries to be let out. She can't forget that horrible ball. This ball might make a great toy for dogs and children (of which I have neither), but I requested it for a cat. Cats are like people; each one is different. Some cats might like Coubon's Interactive Cat Ball, which seems like a great concept, but Angel isn't one of them.

title: Blood Pressure Supplement
text:
I've listened to western medicos like Dr. Dean Edell put down supplements and vitamins (and go ballistic over homeopathic remedies) for thirty years. Chinese meds are rarely mentioned, and when they are it's usually to say they're old and useless.

Well, Chinese remedies are old: they have a couple thousand years on modern medicine. And from experience, I think they have their place. They certainly do for me.

I first came upon Chinese remedies seven years ago. My then six-year-old cat had chronic irritable bowel symptoms and my usual vet - open-minded as he was - could offer nothing but prednisone, a steroid. Cats tolerate it much better than humans or dogs, but I knew it would shorten his life. That was when I found a DVM who also uses holistic methods. Ricky the cat was put on a tea pill regimen (not the pill being reviewed) and has been on them ever since, with only an occasional change. Ricky is extremely active and far healthier at thirteen than he was at six.

So, I'd been taking Inderol for mild high blood pressure for many years and I had avoided reading about the side effects for most of that time. A couple years into Ricky's Chinese pills, I consulted a practitioner and began using Six Flavor Tea Pills as recommended. After a couple weeks to give the pills time to begin working, I began lowering the amount of Inderol I was taking. Within a month, I was off the prescription drug and my blood pressure was lower than the drug-induced norm. It's stayed that way since then. (And one of the side effects of Inderol, tiredness, suddenly abated in the first couple months -- I was so used to the side effect that I didn't know I had it until it was gone.

This is a remedy. It may work for you, it may not. Once my western MD commented on my better-than-ever blood pressure (at least six months after I'd switched), I was pretty convinced this is good stuff. For me. Please consult a good practitioner -- these simple pills are complicated and a practitioner prescribes or suggests OTC like this based on a whole body approach. Their goal is to restore balance to the body, and a good one knows what they're doing.

Meanwhile, Ricky and I are very happy.

Note that both practitioners (human and animal) only use Plum Flower Brand. Neither recommends any other brand.

text:

This not only has Huperzine, but also other well-known cognitive enhancers such as L Tyrosine, Bacopa, Ginkgo Biloba, Alpha GPC, GABA, etc. He seems to like it, but it's hard to determine if it has helped his particular issues given that it's summer right now.

So I love the ingredients, but one hang-up I have is that the Cogni Xtend uses a "proprietary blend" and the label doesn't indicate how much of each ingredient is present. One star deducted for that, for sure.

The price for this ($24.95) is highly competitive with other so-called brain boosters, but again, an apples to apples comparison isn't possible because of the label issue. Overall, I think this is worth trying - my son likes it, the price is good, but consider the lack of ingredient transparency.

title: A Very Handy Item With a Caution or Two.
text:
This is a very handy, well-made stool. It is indeed heavy duty. There are two problems that need to be addressed.

1) The Amazon description stated that the weight limit is 500 pounds. The tag included with the stool stated 300 pounds. Which is it? That is a 200 pound variation. I contacted the company via email to ask that question and they did not answer me. So, that is something to consider—making me wonder if the company backs up its product. At this point I can’t say.

2) Being a heavy person, beware that you do not put your hand on the handle and use it as support to step up because before your weight is on the stool—your hand on the handle can cause the stool to tip since your weight is on the handle but not yet on the stool securing it to the ground.

With those things in mind, this stool is hearty, well-made and very handy.

title: Slight Aftertaste
text:
Ah, I love Julian Bakery's protein bars. Usually. They honestly make my all time favorite protein bar, their primal thin sweet cream...which if you're reading this, you may not want to try because you may be vegan, which I am not, just vegetarian with vegan leanings, and that bar has whey in it. So, of their vegan bars, I've tried three. This was my least favorite, I actually liked the cinnamon twist the best.

So, what was interesting to me about this bar was the protein source...watermelon seeds. I was super curious about how that would work out in terms of flavor, so curious I didn't pay attention to the fat content on the nutritional label when I ordered it, and it is generally higher then I want in a protein bar because I have some fat restrictions on my diet, so to eat these I have to make adjustments elsewhere. And honestly the watermelon seeds were probably what gave it the slightly bitter aftertaste that I wasn't so sold on.

These bars are high in fiber, which I think is great, but not as high as their ginger snap cookie protein bars, which use pumpkin seeds. I do really like that they use more natural ingredients. I can not say enough how big of a fan of that I am. I do like that these have a bit of iron, because I tend to save their pegan or vegan bars for my period because I generally need a boost of that nature then, but this bar doesn't have as much iron as either cinnamon twist or ginger snap.

The texture is a bit dryer then their egg white sunbutter bar which I love the taste of ...my apologies for offending any vegan sensibilities on that one :) So for me, the texture wasn't an issue, I kind of like that it doesn't stick to my teeth as bad as the egg white sunbutter one, but the star came off for the bit of an aftertaste. I think the all natural ingredients thing totally trumps the slightly bitter aftertaste, but because they have bars I like better that work better for both my fat content preferences/needs, I doubt I'll be ordering this one again. I do think it's a solid enough bar, and probably if you like a little bit of the flavor of watermelon seeds you'll do just fine with this one.

title: Working Well for Our Kiddo's Oral Stimulation Protocols
text:
I purchased these at the recommendation of the fabulous Miss W, who is a good friend and valued member of our son's therapy team. Our little man has a laundry list of diagnoses at this point, and he does a lot of chewing and oral stemming as part of all of that. So she had recommended these as part of a protocol to increase stimulation to the mouth in a manner that might decrease his desire to chew on everything he touches. (We swab the insides of his cheeks, the top of his palate, and the sides of his tongue...I also provide a firm but gentle press to the bottoms of his front teeth).

These arrived without any condition issues, and we haven't had any of them break thus far. I must confess that because of what we are using them for, I tend to wash them out and reuse each one a few times, as he's the only one we're using them on. I also must confess because I was having a rather crummy month right after she recommended it, I was not as diligent about it as I should have been ;) But I've been better in the past week, and you know what? It does seem to be helping some! But the rating is based on the lack of condition issues and that they are holding up, not their helpfulness in this area.

title: Aptly Named, Super Tasty, and Nutritionally Sound
text:
Julian Bakery flat out makes my favorite protein bars, so when this popped up as a recommendation on my Amazon page, I felt pretty safe in giving it a try. I'm starting to loose track of the ones I've tried, so we'll just leave it as the only two I didn't love were their glazed donut and their coconut cream. The glazed donut I felt was too hard, and the coconut cream reminded me too much of coconut nougat candy, which I'm not really fond of. Unlike some of their bars, I actually think this one is well named. Super well named. It really does taste like a cinnamon twist roll, I was actually pleasantly surprised on that. Thumbs up, guys :)

Like all of their bars I've tried, these do have a thin sheen of oil coating them, I'm guessing to keep them from sticking to the wrapper. Easily wiped off, and I totally think it's worth putting up with because of the naturalness of the ingredients they use. I love that about their bars in general. I also love that they don't use artificial sweeteners, but rather use monk fruit, which has a glycemic index of zero and comes with zero calories. The artificial sweeteners many brands use come with a host of undesirable side effects that vary depending on the type, and some brands load their bars up with so much sugar or corn syrup it may as well be a candy bar. If you have any sort of reason medical or otherwise for wanting or needing to be careful of your sugar intakes, their products are a great choice, because monks fruit doesn't have any sort of bitter taste, and it doesn't have any of the side effects that come with the other artificial stuff.

Now since this is a vegan friendly product, it is worth noting that they do list the amino acids and the quantities on the bottom of the box and I didn't really have any problems with what I saw there, it looks like the bases are well enough covered. For me, I'm not vegan, I'm not paleo, I'm just generally a vegetarian, but I think their bars flat out rock because they're not loaded up with unnecessary crud, they use healthier sweetening alternatives, they use natural ingredients, and most of the ones I've tried taste awesome. This is honestly one of the better ones, my other two favorites though are not in their vegan line so I'm guessing they're not as relevant to you (but in case you're not strictly vegan, the sunflower butter ones and the primal thin sweet cream are also super awesome).

So I did enjoy these, would actually buy them again, and have no problem recommending them. And since I'm starting to sound like a spokeswoman for their company, I should say...I buy everything I review for my own use, I don't review free samples of anything, and I'm not in any way affiliated with anybody or anything I've ever reviewed. I just genuinely love their protein bars and think they are overall a superior product.

title: Office Sunlight Lamp
text:
This lamp has an interesting balance of pros and cons. I think perhaps if I were using it in an office, or even a craft workspace, I would see a higher value in it.

1) When I pulled the lamp out of the box, the pieces looked pretty straightforward. I put the lamp together without needing to look at the instructions. However, when I tried to put the main straight pole into the base, I ran into an issue. While it fits over the top of a protruding metal piece in the base, it wouldn't go all the way down into the groove that was made for it. Essentially, this meant that I couldn't screw it into the base.

After looking at it for a while, I realized that it was because either the straight pole or the base was just slightly off. One of them was cut incorrectly, preventing them from fitting together. Because I can't get the screw in if I can't get the hole to line up, I will never be able to lift the lamp up by the straight part of the neck. This isn't a huge deal to me, but I know it may really irritate others. =)

My guess is that this issue was specific to my lamp rather than a normal design flaw.

2) During the day, this lamp brings a nice natural light to your workspace. It appears to make every item in the room have the correct coloring rather than the yellow/orange hue you get from incandescent lights. When looking at some jewelry I've made in the past, I realized this would be incredibly helpful to have over the desk while trying to match colors.

3) I would not use this lamp at night. This is mostly because your body gets thrown off by the bright sunlight after the sun has set. During the day, it didn't really bother me, but in trying to use it to light my bedroom in the evening, I quickly turned it off. If I had left it on much longer, I would suspect it would give me a headache and some painful eye strain.

4) This lamp makes a buzzing noise a little like fluorescent lights. If you get annoyed by small noises like this, it's something to take note of.

5) The top of the neck (darker grey) is quite flexible. You can bend the lamp slightly backwards towards the ceiling if you like.

6) The light from this lamp is pretty direct. I believe it's intended to be used over a desk, providing a small focused area of light.

7) It's a little ugly, as you can see in the picture. I'd say it's more suited for a basic work or home office that is focused on function over design.

So in summary - this lamp is most useful in an office, over a desk, during the day, when your purpose is to see colors for what they really are and to eliminate the fake feeling of yellow lighting. This lamp is not really for lighting a room.

title: A white noise machine that doesn't make white noise?
text:
I've got tinnitus and use white noise or relaxing sounds to help distract from the constant ringing in the ears. I recently got a fan-based white noise generator that lets you adjust the tone and volume and have been using that in the bedroom to help sleep. I had been curious about some of the electronic white noise generators and thought to give this one a try, thinking I would use it in my office.

Probably the best thing going for this device is that it looks nice. It's about the size of an Echo Dot, looks sleek, has a nice speaker on top, and a great looking screen. First impressions were very good. Actually operating the device is another story. There are 6 touch buttons on it (no tactile feedback) - power, volume, timer, lock, category, sound. Operating this should be easy, but it is really not pleasant. For instance, to adjust the volume, you can't simply press volume up or down, there are no such buttons. There is just a single volume button. You can hold it, and the volume will change in 1 direction. I guess it cycles to the loudest sound, and then back down to the quietest sound? Strange.

Then there are the scenes/music you can cycle through. There's a category button, and a sound button. You can press category to cycle through categories, and within each category you can press the sound button to cycle through the sounds in that category. There's no indicator on the screen of which category or sound you are in. So you can cycle through things like nature, animals, life, etc. Some of the options are very strange, like there is an ASMR category which contains sounds like eating potato chips, or drinking water. There are some genuinely good sounds in here, but I find it very strange to navigate around. I wish there was some visual indicator of the category or sound, because I have to look at the instruction manual to try and figure out which category I am in. I suppose if you find a favorite sound and don't want to switch to others it would be fine, but I still don't like the process of navigating the sounds on this.

The thing that is most baffling to me is that this is called a white noise machine, the manual calls it a white noise machine, but there are actually no white noise options to choose from on it.

Pros:
- Looks nice
- Decent speaker
- Screen is good quality
- Displays temperature/humidity on screen
- Battery powered
- Can work OK if you find a sound you like and don't want to navigate around

Cons:
- Single button for volume control is bad
- Navigating scenes/sounds is not intuitive, it's hard to tell where you are and where you're going without referencing the manual
- It's called a white noise machine but doesn't actually have any white noise option

For all it gets right, the stuff it gets wrong is enough for me to not recommend it.

title: This scale is old and expensive, newer scales are cheaper and measure more things while being friendlier with Apple Health.
text:
I bought this scale almost 4 years ago and am just now writing a review. The reason I am writing the review is because it recently started flaking out which prompted me to buy a new (different) scale, so I figure it's worth sharing my experience with the Fitbit Aria scale now.

The things I like about the Fitbit scale are that it looks gorgeous, seems to be made of high quality materials. Really, never thought I'd be so impressed with how a scale looks, but it just looks and feels premium. It seems to provide pretty accurate and consistent measurements, but -- it only measures weight, body fat, and BMI.

After daily use for nearly 4 years it has started acting up -- and this has happened occasionally in the past also -- while the scale is sitting undisturbed, it'll just keep acting like someone is standing on it and will say "Step Off" or "Thinking" over and over and over. Sometimes it'll do that in a loop for hours. I'm surprised the batteries last as long as they do, but the battery life is surprisingly good.

Besides the scale becoming possessed and going into these seemingly endless cycles of thinking someone's standing on it, the biggest thing that bugs me about it has to do with Fitbit as a company not embracing popular health platforms like Apple Health. Your $100+ smart scale suddenly feels not-so-smart when it doesn't sync with Apple Health, when it seems like just about every other modern smart device or app out there that measures anything fitness/health related does sync with Apple Health. Apple Health wasn't around when this scale came out, but it's still irritating that they don't support it now. You can go on the iOS app store and get a paid app that will sync your Fitbit data with apple health, but it's a manual process to do that.

When I started searching for a replacement scale I found that many newer scales are cheaper and measure lots of different things that the Fitbit scale doesn't. I bought a new smart scale that tracks weight, BMI and body fat % (the only 3 things fitbit tracks) as well as muscle %, bone %, water %, and BMR (things the fitbit doesn't track).

If I could go back in time, I'd still have bought the Fitbit scale because I liked having it and it was the best option when it came out, but at this point in time I have a hard time recommending it to anyone because there are many alternatives to this scale that are newer, have more features / track more things, and cost less. The Fitbit hasn't gained any new features in the many years it's been out, it hasn't dropped in price, but loads of smart scales from other companies have come out that are more competitively priced and measure/track more things, all while being more friendly with platforms like Apple Health. I guess the only reason I'd recommend this is if you want to track your weight and only do it within the Fitbit ecosystem. For me, I've moved on from the Fitbit ecosystem and like to track lots of different stuff within Apple Health so I may be a bit biased.

Pros:
- Premium look/feel/build quality
- Has served me well for several years of daily use
- Surprisingly great battery life. Batteries seem to last for months at a time of daily use, even when it goes in to these bizarre loops of measuring over and over while nobody is standing on it.

Cons:
- Started flaking out occasionally and going into loops for hours at a time where it thinks it is sensing someone standing on it. While I'm happy to get nearly 4 years of daily use out of ANY electronic gadget, it feels like a scale is something that, especially for the premium price tag, should last even longer than this did.
- Fitbit as a company refuses to embrace Apple Health, requiring you to jump through extra hoops if you want to sync your scale data with Apple Health
- Expensive - has been out for years but still has the same premium price tag
- Newer scales measure more things than this and cost less, while embracing platforms like Apple Health

text:
[[VIDEOID:f4dc4c038460254b3c6d84f812c5d24e]] My wife's feet are always hurting and, therefore, she's always asking for foot rubs. In order to ease her pain and my sanity, I thought I'd give this product a try. Before I even got home from work on the day it was delivered, I got a text from her, "the foot massager rocks!" Putting it into manual, you can select between 3 different speeds and then select if it moves forward or reverse. The remote is useful if you are like me and have a little belly that makes it hard to reach down and touch your toes when seated. You have to point it really close and sometimes press the button more than once, but it works.

I could see how, if you had wider feet, this might be a little too tight.

As far as long term reliability, the jury is still out. If you search around Amazon, you can find this exact unit badged under many different names. The 3 with the most reviews are [[ASIN:B00F7SC2K6 Kendal]], [[ASIN:B000C1KUHA Tripact]] and [[ASIN:B004EXOFVY Carepeutic]]. Looking through those reviews, the average rating is about 4-stars, but you'll find where some had issues with reliability. The problem with a unit like this breaking is expensive return shipping costs due to size and weight. Have a read through some of those reviews and decide if its worth the risk. If you really need a product like this and can't afford the ones at Sharper Image, it might be worth the gamble.

However, it does say it is standardized to 5% thymoquinone so I'm guessing it is balanced in some way. In terms of usability, this is easy to swallow and I tolerated it well when taking it with food (no stomach distress). It smells vaguely herb-like, but it doesn't have any taste. I also did have any unpleasant burbs after taking it. I can't speak to the efficacy of it as a supplement because this isn't the sort of thing that you take and have immediate results with. It's a long-term dietary addition which is supposed to contribute to overall health (as does eating leafy greens or other nutritious food). I believe it is helpful, but I can't prove it. This is only a one-month supply and on the pricier side, but it's hard to rate value when it's impossible to compare this extract to the more common oil supplements.

title: versatile, easy to use
text:
I have a few white noise machines of various types including mechanical and recorded. This is one of the better ones in several ways. First, I didn't notice any looping in the sounds, though I can't say that I listened carefully after falling asleep. It also has the widest variety of noises among all of the machines that I have had experiences with. I liked that it has buttons for each type of sound so I didn't have to cycle through too many options to get to the one I wanted. The animal sounds are soothing in particular, but I was a big fan of the types of white noise and the fan noise for aiding in falling asleep.

The light on this is pretty versatile. The first white light is very faint and works well as a night light without being too bright. The second one is more of an actual light then the rest are just atmospheric for color effects. One of the most impressive points is the volume. One of my white noise machines which uses recorded sound is pretty good, but it can't be made especially loud. That means it's hard to drown out louder noises with it. This gets super loud and I was happy with the range of volume options.

The only minor quibble I have with this is that the power cord connects to USB. I don't have a USB connector in my bedroom so I had to use my own adapter as this did not come with one. This is a small thing, but worth keeping in mind if you don't have a lot of spare adapters lying around or a USB connector on your power strip or wall.

title: pretty good basic filter
text: I got these filters mainly to use with homemade cloth masks and ordered a "large" and it seems to be just about enough to cover my nose and mouth without concerns about slipping down. The filter is not very thick, but it is tightly woven. As an addition to a mask that is already 2-3 layers, I found it to be satisfactory without making it too hard to breath through. The only down side to these was that they have slits across the bottom and top to make them fit your face more accurate by angling. I would have preferred to cut them myself because they are cut a bit longer than I need and that increases the likelihood of gaps. However, with a good pocket, I think they should work very well.

title: seem helpful in reducing bloating
text:
I've been trying a variety of probiotics to help with digestive issues and this one has the shortest range of shelf stability (about 4 months). Since one bottle is a one-month supply, this isn't a big problem. I think the short expiration date is probably a good thing since it means that the manufacturer may be more accurately estimated the viability of the cultures in it.

This is supposed to have a special formulation to help the probiotics survive stomach acids and reach the intestines to assist with gut flora there. I have no way of knowing if it is working. I can only say that I have had considerably less stomach discomfort and bloating since taking this. I tolerated it well, didn't have any issues digesting it or having it feel "stuck". The capsules aren't too big to take, though they are less slender than some. They have a slightly sour milk smell, but they have not taste.

title: good fit and feel, thick enough
text: When I ordered these gloves, I expected something akin to what you see people wearing in fast food places - baggy, thin, crinkly food handling gloves. These are much more like nitrile gloves or exam gloves. They have a good fit (my hands are generally between a medium and a large and these large ones fit nearly perfectly with just a little extra room above my fingers). They have good "touch" (aka, you can feel things through them). They're stretchy and are easy to put on and take off. They aren't powdered inside, but they glide on easily anyway. They are pretty strong for thing disposable gloves as well. The only small point is that they are very short at the cuffs and don't expend much past the top of the wrist. I'm also not sure that they are good value compared to similar gloves, but they are high quality.

title: like chewing on coffee beans in a tootsie roll
text: I realize that this bar is "espresso" flavored, but I expected a little more depth and complexity than something which tasted like chewing coffee beans. The ingredients list includes other flavors, including chocolate, but I couldn't taste them at all. I also wasn't a fan of the texture, which was on the gooey side with little crispy bits scattered throughout. I liked the crunch, but was less a fan of the gooey parts. I ate this during hot weather so it might be better if it's refrigerated. The caffeine portion is on point though. It's less enjoyable than a cup of coffee, but more portable.

title: thicker than average, long lasting
text:
I mainly use these gloves for common household cleaning like doing dishes and cleaning household surfaces. I haven't used them for more heavy duty purposes or with very abrasive cleaning materials (like steel wool). For my purposes, they have worked very well in terms of durability. I would put them as being at least on par with Playtex living gloves in terms of quality, possibly a bit longer lasting. They have about the same tactile qualities as those gloves which means they are good for medium-duty work, but not finer work as you can't feel a lot through them.

I liked the fit and found them easy to put on and take off. I'll note that I generally experience chafing and dryness in my hands from wearing gloves like these, but haven't had that experience with these gloves. The lining seems to "stick" less to my skin which I really like.

title: quite durable, and don't leak
text:
I use gloves mainly for household cleaning (toilet, tub, etc.) and dishwashing so I can only speak to how these gloves perform when repeatedly doing such tasks. They worked well for me in terms of not developing rips or tears for over a month. When one glove had a tear in one finger, it still didn't leak (oddly). I've been using that same pair with the tear for going on two weeks without leakage. The durability is better than average.

The fit is what I'd expect for the large size. I think they may run just a big small since my hands are probably between a medium and large and these fit well with enough play to easily put them on and take them off. There was no chemical smell from the gloves when I took them out of the package and the packaging was easy to open. They don't have great tactile qualities, but they are about the same as similar household gloves (no more or less sensitive). Overall, I'm quite satisfied with them.

title: a bit sticky, but effective
text: I used this for a variety of purposes including on my hands and feet to "seal" moisture in. It worked well for this. I also used it on drawers that were difficult to open and close and it made them move more smoothly. The main difference between this and other petroleum jelly products that I've tried is that it seems a bit stickier/tackier. Also, I'm not a fan of the scent which smells very chemical-like to me.

title: absorbs well and not greasy
text:
I usually use Lubriderm (though I sometimes use cheap no-brands as well) so I'll be comparing this to those brands. The first thing you notice about this is that the cherry scent is really quite potent when you first apply it. To me, this was the greatest weak point as it smells not of the flesh of cherries, but of a pit which is going off a bit. The almond scent isn't present at all. However, the scent doesn't linger after application and you really only smell it when you first rub it in.

I used this as an all-over body lotion after showering given that it's economical and in a large bottle so I used it on my legs, arms, neck, and hands. I did find that it did a solid job keeping my legs from getting flaky, dry skin on them (which I'm prone to) as well as my arms. It didn't go the distance on my hands, but I do wash them a lot and wear rubber gloves about a dozen times a day (stripping them on and off dries out the skin). I don't think this is potent for hands, but it's certainly decent for more average use.

As someone else said, it's hard to get the top to pop up when you first open it (very hard). I guess this is supposed to help it not leak during shipping, but the truth is that mine leaked a little into the bag it was in anyway (I don't know how). The lotion goes on smoothly and isn't greasy. It absorbs well. For me, I found this to be a good “all around” type of lotion.

Pros: absorbs well and not greasy, economical, moisturizes well over the long run
Cons: cherry smell is off-putting, hard to open pump
